Evo Calls Claure Crazy for Suggesting a Reward for Capturing Him Former President Evo Morales called businessman Marcelo Claure crazy and foolish on Sunday, after Claure said he could offer a $1 million reward for the ex-president, who is under an arrest warrant for aggravated human trafficking charges. Morales, on his Sunday program on the coca radio station Kawsachun Coca, likened Claure's proposal to an empire and recalled that the United States had also requested the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro for between $5 to $20 million. I'm starting with a million (laughs). These people are crazy or foolish, I don't understand, he questioned. Marcelo Claure, who resides in the United States and is also president and main investor of the Bolívar football club, suggested the retribution through a post on X, accompanied by an image of Evo Morales with the announcement "Wanted Pedophile. Evo Morales Violator of the Chapare." If you give $1 million in reward, I'll think about it. The LuchoXBolivia government is shaking in its boots, wrote Claure on social media. In January, a judge declared Morales in contempt for not showing up to two hearings that were meant to resolve the charge of aggravated human trafficking against him, for supposedly having a relationship with a minor with whom he later had a child, while he was president of Bolivia in 2016. Morales has been in hiding in the Tropic of Cochabamba (center), his main political and union stronghold, since last October, where his supporters have set up vigilance in anticipation of the possibility that the police might execute the arrest warrant. Claure, close to Morales while he was president, recently took on a political role by promoting a couple of opinion polls for this year's presidential elections, which, in his opinion, revealed that Bolivians are demanding a deep change. He also proposed a super-delegate to define the opposition candidate, with main figures being former President Jorge Tuto Quiroga (2001-2002), businessman Samuel Doria Medina, and Cochabamba Mayor Manfred Reyes Villa. Last week, the businessman openly acknowledged being against the ruling Movement for Socialism (MAS), the party from which Morales was recently leader for nearly three decades and is now in the hands of social sectors aligned with President Luis Arce, due to differences between them. In an interview with a local medium from the United States, Claure stated that if the MAS continues to govern Bolivia, he will withdraw from Bolivia and the Bolívar. Who asks him to stay, it's his right, was Morales' response to the millionaire's warning. Morales said that Claure is behind Bolivia's lithium, a country with one of the world's largest reserves of the mineral with 23 million tons, and claimed that the businessman has not invested anything in the country and has even privatized Bolívar's heritage. Governor Sáenz and Minister Bullrich to Open a Site for Victims of Trafficking in Aguas Blancas Politics 10 February 2025 Salta Governor Gustavo Sáenz and National Security Minister Patricia Bullrich will open a refuge for victims of trafficking in the border town of Aguas Blancas. The site will operate out of the Puerto Chalanas Migration Office. Salta Province continues its policy of security and the fight against organized crime. Following her recent praise from National Security Minister Patricia Bullrich for her efforts in the fight against narcotics trafficking, the official will visit the north of the country next week to carry out a series of official activities. One of the central acts of her visit will be the inauguration of the Safe Site for Trafficking Victims, which will operate within the Migration Office in Puerto Chalanas, Aguas Blancas. During the event, a traditional ribbon-cutting ceremony will take place, and the Presentation of the Action Protocol for the use of the new space will be presented, whose objective is to provide protection and assistance to people rescued from human trafficking networks. This site will serve as a first point of refuge before victims are transferred to suitable containment spaces. In addition to the inauguration, Bullrich will also participate in the delivery of equipment to the National Gendarmerie, within the framework of strengthening operations against narcotics trafficking and organized crime on the border with Bolivia. The minister will visit the 28 de Julio Post of the federal force in Aguas Blancas, where she will oversee progress on infrastructure projects aimed at optimizing security in the region. The presence of the official in Salta reinforces the commitment of the National Government to security in border areas, where efforts are made to combat crimes such as drug trafficking and human trafficking, problems that directly affect the province.

In a recent human trafficking case, three Thai women were rescued after being deceived into participating in an illegal egg harvesting scheme operated by a Chinese gang in Georgia. The rescue was prompted by Pavena Hongsakula, founder of the Pavena Foundation for Children and Women, who was alerted to the situation by a victim who managed to escape from the network. Crucial information from a victim A victim, who returned to Thailand in September 2024, informed Pavena about other Thai women who were still trapped in a large egg harvesting farm in Georgia. After paying approximately 70,000 baht (equivalent to 42,490 Mexican pesos) to the criminals for their release, the woman revealed details about the illegal operation that allowed Thai authorities, in collaboration with Interpol, to launch an operation to liberate the other women. After that, on January 30, 2025, three more women were rescued and returned to Thailand. During a live broadcast on the Facebook page of the Pavena Foundation, one of the victims recounted how she was deceived into being involved in the criminal scheme. How they deceived the victims The victim explained that she saw an advertisement on Facebook offering a job with a salary of between 400,000 and 600,000 baht. Upon contacting the advertisers, they assured her that the job involved being a surrogate mother for couples who were unable to have children in Georgia and that the process was completely legal in that country. In August 2024, the woman and ten other Thai women traveled to Georgia, where they were supervised by a Thai woman suspected of being involved with the criminal gang. Upon arrival, the women were taken to a rural area where they discovered that at least 100 other Thai women were already living in similar conditions. Immediately, they realized it was not a job as surrogate mothers, but the criminal network subjected them to hormone treatments to stimulate ovule production, and extracted the ovules under anesthesia once a month. The women did not receive any payment for their participation in the process, and it is suspected that the collected ovules were trafficked and sold to other countries to be used in in vitro fertilization (IVF). According to the Pavena Foundation's records, in 2024, a total of 257 Thais were victims of human trafficking, of which 53 were found in Thailand and 204 in other countries. The foundation has managed to rescue 152 of these people, becoming a fundamental pillar in the fight against human trafficking in the region.

Horror in Libya: Mass grave with 28 migrant bodies discovered The bodies are of people from sub-Saharan Africa who were found near an illegal detention center. The remains were found in a mass grave in the desert, north of Kufra, according to Libya's Attorney General. This discovery occurred days after 19 more bodies were found on a farm in the same city. The discovery was made possible by an operation targeting human trafficking. In the same operation, 76 migrants were freed from detention and torture. There was a gang whose members deliberately held the illegal immigrants captive, tortured them, and subjected them to cruel, humiliating, and inhumane treatment, according to the Attorney General's office on social media. A Libyan national and two foreigners were arrested in the operation. The recovered bodies were taken to a morgue for autopsies by experts. It is suspected that the incident is linked to human trafficking networks. The search in Kufra continues and more bodies are expected to be found, meanwhile, authorities are documenting the testimonies of the survivors.

Thieves steal money from vehicle with signal jammer. A group of delinquents managed to steal G. 5.5 million and several documents from a vehicle parked in the courtyard of a restaurant, located in Capiatá. According to closed-circuit images, the thieves allegedly used a signal jammer to prevent the doors from locking. The incident occurred when a family got out of their pickup truck and headed to the restaurant. At that moment, a Toyota Funcargo vehicle parked near the victims' vehicle. In the images, a man is seen getting out of the car, easily opening the door of the pickup truck, and stealing a wallet containing cash and personal documents. Subcomisary Jorge Báez, who intervened in the case, confirmed that the pickup truck showed no signs of forced entry on the lock or windows, which reinforces the hypothesis of the use of a signal-blocking device. The victims claimed to have closed the vehicle, but upon returning, they found it open and without their wallet, the officer explained. The National Police are already analyzing the security recordings to identify the perpetrators and obtain details about the license plate of the vehicle used in the robbery. In addition, citizens are recommended to manually check the closure of their vehicles after activating the locking system, especially in public places, to prevent this type of crime. The Chilean town of Alto Hospicio was the scene between 1999 and 2001 of a series of crimes that shocked the country. It was 14 young and adolescent women who disappeared in that period without a trace, causing great fear in the community. Initially, the authorities thought they had been voluntary escapes, which delayed the investigations and allowed the perpetrator to continue with his atrocious acts. The lack of responses and the growing concern of the families led to media and social pressure that demanded clarification of the facts. However, the truth came to light when his last victim managed to escape and reveal his identity. A taxi driver and a series of mysterious disappearances Silva was born on July 15, 1963, in the commune of Puchuncaví, Chile, and before establishing himself in Alto Hospicio, he had led an apparently normal life. However, after his capture, shocking details about his personality and background emerged that indicated violent tendencies. He worked as an informal taxi driver and was not the type of person to arouse suspicion in the community That is why his modus operandi consisted of gaining the trust of women who did not have money to pay for a taxi, offering them a safe ride, and once in the vehicle, diverting to desert areas where he would carry out his crimes. This strategy was what allowed him to act with impunity for years. The first crime occurred on November 24, 1999, when he kidnapped Macarena Sánchez, a 14-year-old student whom Silva took to the depths of the desert. After sexually abusing her, he forced her to walk tied to his own ropes and pushed her off a 220-meter cliff. The following year, in February, he tortured and murdered Sara Gómez, 18 years old, and Angélica Lay, 22, whom he buried in a clandestine landfill. A month later, he massacred Laura Zola, a 15-year-old teenager, and discarded her body by throwing her off. The crimes of the psychopath of Alto Hospicio in the newspapers of the time. (Photo Guioteca) As uncertainty grew over the disappearances of these young women, the police had the theory that they were voluntary escapes. According to that hypothesis, the young women were escaping to Peru to engage in prostitution. However, this allowed the taxi driver to continue the crimes with total impunity. On April 5, 16-year-old Katherine Arce got into the man's car, as she knew him from a distance and offered to let him take her to school. Hours later, the killer hid her body in the trash. In the months that followed, 17-year-old Patricia Palma, 15-year-old Macarena Montesinos, and 16-year-old Viviana Garay suffered the same fate. But everything changed when the father of the last teenager, Orlando Garay, discovered that there was a connection between all the disappearances. In this way, along with the other families who were desperately searching for their daughters, he proposed making the case visible so that the police would start acting with greater speed. Despite this, the investigators insisted that the girls had escaped from their homes voluntarily. During two attacks he carried out in 2001, Silva had lapses that led the authorities to discover his identity. In April, he kidnapped 16-year-old Maritza and abused her. She managed to escape because she chased him away with her screams. Upon arriving at her home, she told her parents and they took her to a hospital in the city of Iquique, where they were able to extract DNA from the aggressor. After that incident, Silva waited several months to attack again. It wasn't until October that he chose his next victim. Although he attempted to use the same modus operandi with 13-year-old Barbara, he made a mistake after raping her, hitting her on the head with a stone and leaving her by the precipice, because he believed she was dead. The arrest of Julio Pérez Silva, the psychopath from Alto Hospicio. (Photo Guioteca). However, the reality was that the girl had managed to survive and even remembered what her attacker had told her. He told her that he was the psychopath from Alto Hospicio, that he had killed the other girls and that she wouldn't escape this. Suddenly he comes and throws the stone at me. I said I wouldn't escape. The stone fell on my head and he kept shouting. He picked up another stone, threw it at me, and that's when I fainted, the victim recounted in a television interview. Barbara, accompanied by her parents, provided all the detailed information about Silva to the police, as well as a particular detail: a stuffed animal from the children's series Bananas in Pajamas hung in the rearview mirror. It was just the toy in his car that gave him away. That same night, in the police station, the killer confessed to the murders of the 14 women and gave the exact location of where their bodies were. Three years after his arrest, he was sentenced to 20 years in prison for 14 counts of qualified murder, 20 for sexual abuse, and 10 for attempted homicide. Accused of abusing his step-daughter from the age of seven to 17, in the trial against him at the Provincial Court. Europa Press The Supreme Court has confirmed the 11-year prison sentence for a man who abused the daughter of his partner over the course of a decade, from when the minor was seven years old until she turned 17. The High Court has not admitted the cassation appeal filed by the man against the sentence imposed on him by the Cantabria Provincial Court in January 2024 and confirmed in April of the same year by the Cantabria Superior Justice Court (TSJC), which dismissed his appeal. The defendant's defense filed a cassation appeal with the Supreme Court based solely on the consideration that his right to the presumption of innocence had been violated and, for this purpose, referred to the lack of rationality of the ruling and that the victim's statement, his step-daughter, was lacking in persistence and sufficient concreteness. They are the same arguments on which he based his appeal before the TSJC, which dismissed the appeal and did so, according to the Supreme Court, with an accurate assessment in which it assured that no violation of his constitutional rights had occurred and that the sentence of the Audiencia had counted with sufficient evidence, constituted essentially in the testimony of the victim, who enjoyed persistence with regard to the nuclear facts. Facts that the victim, insists the Court, recounted with sufficient concreteness, detailing the progression of said acts from the initial touches above the clothing and escalating to concrete sexual relations, both through vaginal and anal routes. There has been sufficient evidence, adds the Supreme Court, which, in addition, recalls that the victim's declaration can constitute sufficient evidence when practiced with the necessary procedural guarantees, as, it defends, has been in this case. The Supreme Court considers that there is no grounds for the cassation appeal because in this review process, only the rational coherence of the court's evaluation and the witnesses' statements can be reviewed, which in this case presents no defects whatsoever. Moreover, the High Court also does not observe any deficits in the probative and evaluative aspects of the condemnatory ruling. ELEVEN YEARS' CONVICTION The Provincial Court of Cantabria, in a January 2024 sentence later confirmed by the TSJC, convicted this man to eleven years in prison for abusing his partner's daughter over the course of a decade. The young woman lodged a complaint when she turned 18, and both at that time and in the trial held in December 2023, she stated that she had suffered touchings, vaginal penetrations from the age of nine, and anal penetrations from the age of eleven. The Third Section of the Court fully credited his account and considered the accused to be the perpetrator of a continued crime of sexual abuse with carnal access to a minor under 16 years old. In addition to the sentence of 11 years in prison, he was prohibited from approaching the young woman for a period of eight years, he was disqualified from any role that would involve contact with minors for 16 years, and he was imposed a measure of supervised liberty after a period of six years of deprivation of liberty. Furthermore, in a civil liability sense, he was condemned to pay 24,000 euros to the woman, who presented post-traumatic stress and social damage with negative repercussions on her personal, family, social, and affective-sexual life. According to the proven facts that were recounted in the sentence, the convicted person acted with a libidinous intent and to satisfy his sexual desires by taking advantage of the fact that he was with the minor in the family home. Thus, from the time she was seven until she was 17 years old, on numerous occasions, he performed unwanted touching on her body, eventually penetrating her vaginally when she turned nine years old, and from the time she turned eleven, also anally. The court arrived at a full and absolute conviction that the events took place after analyzing the evidence presented in the trial, as the victim's statement was sufficient to undermine the accused's right to the presumption of innocence, who denied the events and argued that the young woman filed the complaint at the moment when he and her mother set boundaries when she wanted to emancipate with her boyfriend. For the court, her account was clear, coherent, and convincing, with full credibility and verisimilitude, and no ulterior motive was observed. Furthermore, no manipulation or influence from third parties was observed in her statements. Additionally, this account was corroborated by the documentary medical evidence, which established anal fissure, alterations in behavior during childhood, and depression. Along with this, the expert testimony also supported the young woman's version of events. Therefore, despite the exhaustive and meticulous technical work developed by the defense to justify acquittal, it is a fact that there is sufficient evidence to prove the facts declared proven, the court added. The evidence presented in defense consisted of the accused's statement, in which they categorically denied the facts, and the testimony of the young woman's mother and wife, who said she did not believe her daughter because she considered her version to be implausible and unbelievable. However, the young woman's statements, corroborated by objective, external, and peripheral elements, have completely convinced the court of the credibility and truthfulness of her declaration, the Audiencia concluded.

Many grains of sand can stop human trafficking Stefano Leszczynski Vatican City Human trafficking is like a perverse mechanism that catches and crushes people, but many grains of sand can make its gears jam. This is the image used by Sister Maria Rosa Venturelli, Comboni missionary and coordinator of the USMI network against human trafficking, the Union of Superior Women of Italy in the diocese of Rome, to explain the importance of the week of prayer and awareness that preceded the February 8th event convened by Pope Francis in 2015.Human trafficking statistics The United Nations estimates that 50 million people are victims of human trafficking worldwide. The most affected are women, children, immigrants, and refugees. One in three victims is a child, while 79% of victims of sexual exploitation worldwide are women and girls. Wars, conflicts, violence, poverty, and environmental disasters around the world force people to leave their homes, making them especially vulnerable to trafficking and exploitation, as they often turn to traffickers or the black market to travel from one country to another. Added to this is another form of trafficking: online exploitation. People as merchandise Combatting the indifference that makes different forms of trafficking invisible is a priority, explains Sister Venturelli, who coordinates the USMI network in Rome with 22 other sisters and laypeople. It is essential to act at all social, economic, and even ecclesiastical levels, I would say. The phenomenon of trafficking is terrifying, notes the Comboni missionary, and we often have the temptation to look the other way and not get involved. The condition of slavery that characterizes all forms of trafficking is dominated by the awareness of evil, which explains why a religious approach is a very harsh reality to face, and the risks to the safety of victims and those who attempt to oppose it are real. The strategy of evil The exploiters only know one strategy, that of terror. This is how they nullify the will to resist of a person who is no longer able to say enough is enough to life on the street, because with fear it is difficult to make positive decisions. The law does not always help to face these situations, partly because it always requires a complaint from the victim, and not all those involved in this trade have the courage to do so. They have too much fear of the violence they expose themselves to if they are caught by their exploiters after fleeing. Many stories of hope. But there are also many stories of rescue and hope that show how it's possible to free oneself from exploiters, sometimes just by becoming aware that there's another way of life possible. A young woman from El Salvador, whom Sister Maria Rosa recalls, found a way to escape her enslavers while being detained and locked up for two months in Ponte Galeria CIE. From a young age, she had lived in a context of degradation marked by continuous violence, and had ended up believing there was no other life for her. It's often a form of resurrection that girls and women who have survived trafficking experience. Along their path of rebirth, these women demonstrate exceptional will and determination, and they can accomplish great things. What's important is never judging, but being solidary, pouring out a drop of humanity every day on the most vulnerable sisters and brothers. Thank you for reading this article. Peru's Ministry of the Interior confirmed on Sunday, February 9, 2025, the dismantling of an international organization allegedly responsible for human trafficking linked to the Aragua Train. In the operation, 23 people were arrested and a large number of human trafficking victims were released, including three minors. Twenty-three members of this transnational mafia were detained in Lima, three minor victims were rescued, and firearms were confiscated. We continue to hunt for the perpetrators, the Ministry of the Interior stated in a report published on social media. The operation was carried out in the country's capital, Lima, with the participation of the United States Embassy in Peru. The branch, called Los Hijos de Dios, has ties with the Tren de Aragua. You may be interested in Paramilitary groups in Venezuela: an analysis of their sociopolitical influence What is the Tren de Aragua The Tren de Aragua is a transnational megacrime organization originating from the state of Aragua, Venezuela. Founded between 2007 and 2010, it emerged from the construction union of the train in the aforementioned state and evolved into a criminal organization with multiple functions. With its base of operations in the Tocorón prison, the group is led by Héctor Niño Guerrero and has approximately 2,700 members. Its illicit activities encompass a broad spectrum, including extortion, kidnapping, migrant trafficking, human trafficking, narcotics trafficking, and illegal mining. Additionally, the Aragua Train has expanded its presence beyond Venezuelan borders, establishing cells in countries such as Peru, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Brazil. This organization is characterized by its franchise structure linked to a central command, its use of extreme violence, and its ability to exercise territorial control through a dual system of co-optation and coercion. The incidents were reported to the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Family and Gender Violence, which initiated the investigation, and Luis Alberto N was presented to the Control Judge via summons. In court, the judicial body decided to link him to the process, imposing an official preventive prison sentence as a precautionary measure and setting a one-month deadline for the closure of the complementary investigation. The FGE reaffirms its institutional commitment to addressing any act that threatens the integrity and well-being of Michoacán's children.

Leticia Fuentes February 10, 2025 11:02 AM Still impacted by the Pelicot case, which resulted in a 20-year prison sentence for Dominique Pelicot for drugging and raping his wife Gisèle with over 50 men, France is preparing to face another major trial for sexual violence. In this case, it will be the largest judicial process for pedophilia. The defendant is surgeon Joël Le Scouarnec, accused of abusing nearly 300 children, mostly patients who were asleep at the time of the incidents, between 1989 and 2014. The trial will begin on February 24 and last until June. Given its importance, complexity, and number of victims, this procedure has been described as extraordinary by the judiciary management of the Ministry of Justice, said Lorient's prosecutor, Stéphane Kellenberger, who provided details of the indictment, over 700 pages long, of a case that will become the largest child molestation trial in France in recent years. Le Scouarnec, 73 years old, who is currently serving a 15-year sentence for abusing four minors, worked for years in various French hospitals where he came into contact with hundreds of victims, mostly 11-year-old children. In this new case, he is being prosecuted for raping 158 boys and 141 girls, 256 of whom were under 15 years old. 30 years of impunity Despite several complaints from colleagues and a first conviction in 2005 for possession of child pornography, for almost 30 years the surgeon remained off the radar of justice, as many of the victims did not have documentation of the rapes, as they were abused under the effects of the sedatives provided by the doctor. The accused benefited from the impunity of silence, this must stop, said the lawyer of one of Scouarnec's victims, Francesca Satta, in Telegram. According to the authorities, during months of interrogations, the accused acknowledged his involvement in all the facts he is accused of. He explained his methods of operation, the determination of his actions, as well as the precautions he took to avoid being discovered, the prosecutor explained on Monday in front of the press. Minors under 11 years old. In 2004, the FBI contacted French authorities after detecting that the surgeon had used his credit card to purchase child pornography on a Russian website based in the US. As a result, he was briefly taken into police custody. A year later, he was sentenced to four months in prison for these charges, but without a suspended sentence. Following this incident, his wife distanced herself from him, but neither divorced him nor, if she knew about it, reported him to the police. In the notes found on Le Scouarnec's computer, which he documented everything on, he himself wrote in 1996: "She knows." According to the French media outlet FranceBleu, in 2006, just a year after being convicted of possession of pedophilic material, one of his colleagues reported him to the regional council of doctors in Finistère. This agency received the doctor's criminal record and, despite this, no measures were taken to keep him away from the minor patients he treated. For years, the doctor continued working in hospitals and living a normal life until 2017, when a neighbor reported him for attacking his 6-year-old daughter through the garden fence. It was then that the case was uncovered. In the doctor's home, the police found thousands of files of rapes and sexual assaults, as well as 300,000 photographs and videos of child pornography. In Joel Le Scouarnec's home, notebooks were found that describe absolutely abhorrent things, explained the prosecutor. The detainee, like in the case of Dominique Pelicot, documented everything in notebooks, leaving a trail of the abuses he committed while working as a surgeon. On December 3, 2020, he was sentenced to 15 years in prison for rape and sexual assault of four minors. Among them, her two nieces, whom she abused in 1980. Following this conviction, the authorities continued with the investigation, which lasted seven years and led to nearly 300 victims of rapes.

The dry wind of April 2024 was blowing strongly in Taganga, when a 13-year-old Wayúu girl went missing. While she was being searched for, a Canadian citizen was torturing her harshly in the room of a hostel he owned in that municipality of Magdalena. The news barely leaked beyond the community. There were no headlines or urgent calls from the authorities. A year later, the foreigner, identified as Andy Asselin, was captured, but the path to impunity was already clear. The Prosecution only charged him with aggravated kidnapping, despite the map of scars on his skin telling the story of the torment and the heartbreaking account of the minor. Cornered by poverty and fear, the victim and her family lost themselves in anonymity, and that has been, precisely, the biggest obstacle for Wayúu lawyer and activist Estercilia Simanca, who decided to act as an agent of record, taking on the representation of the family, even without having found them. Simanca took care of setting off the alarms as soon as she found out what had happened. She immediately demanded a rigorous follow-up of the case from the authorities. However, her greatest frustration is having arrived late, she did not have news of the crime until ten months later, when she found out about the capture of the alleged perpetrator. The Canadian was detained on January 12th in the Rafael Núñez airport, in Cartagena, when trying to flee to his country. Then, Estercilia Simanca embarked on an tireless fight to guarantee justice and reparation. In that mission, recently, Simanca sent a letter to the Attorney General's Office requesting that the foreigner be charged with the crime of torture abroad. In it, she affirms that the minor was a victim of physical and cultural aggression and the evidence supports this. That case has 10 months and I only found out in January. The Constitutional Court and the ICBF must follow up because it involves a Wayúu minor and indigenous children and girls are special subjects of attention. I am starting to understand that Wayúu children who are outside the department are part of that unconstitutional state of affairs. I will be vigilant through petition rights. I do not know if the girl has lawyers, I do not know if she is protected, I do not know who her family members are, nor what her community is, but I do know that she must be protected in light of the Court's sentence, said the activist and lawyer. Simanca refers to the T-302 sentence of 2017 of the Constitutional Court, which recognizes Wayúu children as subjects of priority attention. Her greatest fear is that this man will go free. Before his capture, Andy Asselin moved between Santa Marta and Cartagena offering tourist packages with which he attracted clients to his hostel in Taganga. It's lamentable that in Colombia, there is no protection for individuals recognized as being under special protection, such as the Wayúu children, but Canada does protect its citizens, and that is the fear, he added. And with reason, he seeks justice. Although before a judge the foreigner declared himself innocent, the Prosecutor's Office points him out as being responsible for the torture to which the indigenous girl was subjected on April 26, 2024, after being accused of having taken belongings from the hostel. The punishment was as brutal as inhumane. They dragged her to a room and there subjected her to a merciless torment. She was beaten. With a hot machete, they branded her skin. They shaved her head and eyebrows. The minor was found by workers at the scene tied by feet and hands to a bed in poor health. Immediately, the Police initiated an investigation and the search for Asselin as a presumed responsible individual. Months later, he was captured by the Cartagena Tourism Police after verifying that there was a blue circular warrant and an arrest order issued by Interpol against him. The hostel where the incidents occurred, Chill Inn Spot, is under investigation. The authorities are seeking to verify whether the allegations are true or not, according to which the foreigner used the facilities for the possible sexual exploitation of minors and the so-called sex tourism. On social media, the man offered various tourist packages. We have many contacts in the city to organize your next excursion in Taganga, whether you are interested in hiking, exploring rivers and waterfalls, enjoying dinners in restaurants, going out at night, practicing water sports, snorkeling, renting a motorcycle or a boat to explore the impressive Taganga area, it reads on the website. In this case, Aselin, it appears, did not act alone. According to the authorities, it was reported that he collaborated with another person, whose identity remains under reserve while the investigations continue. Preliminary information suggests that this person would be an employee of the same hostel. For now, Simanca is waiting for a response from the Prosecutor's Office and the Colombian Institute of Family Welfare. He trusts that these entities will take on the case firmly and facilitate contact with his family. The lawyer affirms that she will not rest until justice is done and this case does not remain in impunity.

Sanchinarro and Rejas are the hideouts of the great drug lords. The Albanian from the Balkan clan who moves the most cocaine in the world, Niko Kreshnik, has his residence here. I will never leave the narco world, I love it. 20 years hunting pedophiles, murderers, and drug traffickers around the world. The real story of La infiltrada, the movie by Arantxa Echevarría about the undercover police who ended up in an ETA commando. Although Madrid is not as plagued by foreign corruption and the score-settling characteristic of the more affluent areas of the Costa del Sol, the great international drug cartels are indeed settled in the capital of Spain. The Balkan clan is, at present, the most powerful on the planet, competing with the Mocro Maffia (with a special presence in Sweden and the Netherlands, and also in the Malaga coast), and having even displaced the great organized crime groups from Colombia and Mexico. Traditionally, these were the strongest worldwide. Where do these criminals stop in Madrid? Sources of all credibility point to three specific hotspots. The two most important ones are the Sanchinarro neighborhood (Hortaleza district), a stone's throw from La Moraleja, and the other is in Rejas (San Blas-Canillejas), in the vicinity of the Plenilunio shopping center and next to the A2 (Barcelona highway). At a lower level, the A6 (La Coruña) axis is where the towns of Majadahonda and Las Rozas are ideal for those narco-traffickers who want to have their children close to exclusive bilingual schools. They move a lot around the Plenilunio short-term rental apartment zone. Specifically, there are eight blocks where people from Eastern European countries and Colombians are housed. Many of those type of houses have been built there, which we all know what they are, where they can pay in cash and ask for few guarantees to rent, a national police officer affirms, highlighting the ease of using false documentation in some of those establishments. It's no coincidence that the Rejas neighborhood, the Mercedes industrial estate, and the shopping center itself are scenes of some drug trafficking and also police operations. One of them was the Peregrina operation, in which Ismael García Navarro, a 41-year-old Spaniard, was caught. The Central Udyco considers him, allegedly, one of the leaders of hashish trafficking on the Levantine coast. Very well-known on the beach of San Juan de Alicante, the man known as Linterna wanted to switch to cocaine and established ties with Galician narco-traffickers who have worked with the Charlines clan, which has a powerful logistics network. The main suspects were held at the Eurostars Plaza de Castilla and Compostela Suites, with the latter establishment located in the Rejas area. They were finally apprehended when attempting to distribute 70 kilograms of cocaine. The Queen of Ronda was also caught at the shopping center parking lot. María del Mar Mellado Blanco, a 41-year-old Malaga native and expert in luring mules for drug trafficking, was caught when investigators were tracking another woman, who arrived on a hot flight from Colombia. She disembarked at Barajas Airport and was used as bait by the agents. From there, she went to a hostel in Canillas, where she spent over an hour and a half with two suitcases, before leaving in a taxi for the Plenilunio shopping center. There, she met a man and a woman at the parking lot of the complex. She got into a car and drove only a few meters before entering a community garage in the Mercedes polígono. The FARC's cocaine was found when they opened the two suitcases. The second woman was the Queen of Ronda. In the co-pilot's airbag compartment, 23,500 euros and six encrypted phones were found. In the luggage, there were 11 kilograms of quite pure cocaine. At another shopping mall's parking lot, Montecarmelo, businessman and Congolese influencer Eric Mandala Kinzenga, 48 years old and owner of a television, was arrested a few days ago. He was caught in the act of transporting 171 kilograms of cocaine with two partners. Officially, he is involved in diamond trading and international transportation. A plot between narco groups that wanted to sell seized cocaine from the FARC to a group of DEAy Udyco police infiltrators took place in a café at the mentioned shopping mall. They would meet there in the mornings to negotiate the sale, previously agreed upon using a code in the form of a series of numbers from euro bill serial numbers. I want to pick up the cocaine tomorrow. We will be traveling in two vehicles, the drivers are trusted individuals, as we have been working together for more than ten years. The most dangerous are the Albanians. A very important part of the cocaine passes through Madrid, which is why there are so many citizens of that country in the capital. They like Sanchinarro very much because it has very wide streets and, in some way, remind them of neighborhoods in America, according to police sources. This is the case of Nikolai Kreshnik Budlla, a 50-year-old Albanian and considered a major target for investigators. Alias Niko, has his official address on José Donoso Street in Sanchinarro. Currently, he is in Albania, where he has a pending case, as well as another in Italy. He is probably the one who moves the most cocaine in Madrid, Spain, and Europe, as indicated. Do not take him lightly, as the Balkan clans have all the infrastructure, they no longer depend on the Galicians, and they have a lot of money. It's tons and tons that also end up in the Netherlands. The trail of Niko in the capital began to emerge in 2007, when he was investigated for the break-in at José Luis Moreno's mansion in Boadilla del Monte. He was also under scrutiny for the shooting murder of his subordinate Mendzici Nurarel in El Molar in 2008 and the shootout with heavy firearms at the Telémaco street roundabout on January 21, 2010, where his boss died. He was arrested in May with 20 kilograms of cocaine, but escaped from prison in 2014. In 2019, he was caught at a hotel near the Castellana.Enemy of the Mocro Maffia, Niko has ten distinct false identities and is also known as Kreshnik Farruku within his family faction, which introduced 10 tons of cocaine and the same amount of hashish into Spain. In the 2023 Operation Proper, the Civil Guard found identification vests from the Armed Institute (with which he took photos) in his Sanchinarro residence, but he also posed as an inspector from his country's police. But Niko was not among the 17 detainees. A large part of his guilt is that Spain is full of cocaine. There is an overproduction in Colombia since Gustavo Petro's arrival as president, who said a few days ago, "Cocaine is illegal because it is made in Latin America, not because it is worse than whiskey." The elimination of aerial fumigation with glyphosate is key and usually comes from Ecuador to our country. A few months ago, Niko was arrested by the Central Udyco, but he was released. His surroundings have also been investigated as Hernando Mauricio Vergara Castillo, alias the Doctorcito, who was Maradona's doctor and the mastermind behind the diet that made him change his figure for a time. This Colombian doctor, who was given the role of alleged mediator with the leader of the Albanians from Farruku, has a clinic on Santiago Bernabéu street that investigators located as one of the operation centers not only for aesthetic purposes, but also for a drug cartel with which Edwin Congo, former Real Madrid player, was also linked. The athlete was seen in surveillance with Niko on a rooftop in the El Carmen neighborhood (Ciudad Lineal) and was detained, but was released a few hours later. The Albanian has Colombians working for him and also moves in Dubai. I will never stop being a narcotics trafficker, I love it. Word of Farruku.

data.text: Current Events 30 years and a half in prison for raping his two minor granddaughters under the age of 10 The convicted man is a 64-year-old man who raped his two granddaughters since they were 6 and 10 years old respectively, for 4 years Extra Photo Jaén The convicted man during the trial The Third Section of the Jaén Court has sentenced a 64-year-old man to 30 years and a half in prison for raping his two minor granddaughters under the age of 10 for four years. The sentence, accessed by Europa Press, condemns this man to 30 years in prison as the author of two continued sex aggression crimes with intimidation and family relationship exploitation. To this, he adds three months in prison for a maltreatment crime and three more months for a child pornography possession crime. On the other hand, he is acquitted of two continued threats crimes, two psychological injuries crimes, and a minor physical injuries crime for which he was also being accused in this cause. As an accessory, the sentence imposes a 10-year ban on communicating or approaching the girls, in addition to the prison sentence once served, as well as 10 years of supervised liberty and one year of deprivation of the right to possess and carry firearms. In terms of civil liability, he must indemnify each of the minors 50,000 euros for the moral damages and harm caused to the two girls. The facts date back to May 2018 and extended until January 2023. To achieve the girls' silence, the grandfather would tell them that if they told anything, he would kill the two girls, their mother, and his wife, which caused an absolute state of fear in the minors, who did not dare to tell until February 1, 2023. In addition to the sexual aggressions, the sentence convicts him for an episode of mistreatment against one of the girls, whom he grabbed forcefully by the shoulders in the middle of the street and pushed against a wall. The additional evidence against the defendant includes the seizure of his mobile phone, which, upon analysis, revealed pornographic images of a minor and a video of his four-year-old grandson naked, in which the defendant is seen asking him to dance. Although the defendant claimed his innocence during the trial held in January, the verdict confirms that the defendant repeatedly abused and subjected his two granddaughters to various forms of sexual practices, taking advantage of their familial relationship and the numerous occasions he was left alone with them, as their parents worked. The verdict also states that the defendant used intimidation and threats to overcome the resistance the girls may have shown to the sexual acts, to the point of threatening to kill their mother and grandmother if they told anyone. The defendant defended himself in the trial, saying that everything was a lie, but the court establishes that the testimony of the two minors, with all the details about the practices to which their grandfather subjected them, allows a degree of certainty that constitutes sufficient evidence to dictate a condemnatory sentence. The minors' statement was carried out in the trial with the reproduction of the statement they made under preconstituted testimony. The minors detailed with their words numerous alleged violations and physical aggressions perpetrated by their own grandfather, the person who, from time to time, after violating them, gave them money. He gave us five euros or bought us clothes, the girls pointed out. The older sister said, "He did it to me a thousand times." She pointed out that she and her younger sister made a pact not to tell until their grandfather died because he threatened to kill their parents and their grandmother if they told anything about what was happening. The eldest sister, who was 12 years old, was the one who told her friends from school what her grandfather was doing to her, and they in turn told a teacher who was the one who sounded the alarm and brought the case to the attention of the family, which the girls had never spoken to before. The mother of the younger girls, who testified behind a screen that separated her from the accused, said that the girls would often stay with the accused. Who would have thought, she said, emphasizing that she loved her father with all her heart and that it never crossed her mind what her daughters were going through. As a mother and as a daughter, this situation was horrible, it was a disappointment, it was a person I wanted because he was my father, and as a mother I felt terrible because they were my daughters, the accused testified in court, while denying that there were family conflicts as argued by the accused. The prosecutor's attorney, Francisco Navea, maintained that the evidence against the accused was overwhelming and gave full credibility to the girls. That is why the family has sought justice, that the facts suffered by these girls at the hands of their grandfather, whom the lawyer defined as a monster, be repaired. OTHER SENTENCES The sentence imposed on this grandfather is one of the highest imposed by the Jaén Court for this type of crime, taking into account that there are two minor victims. Another similar sentence was the one dictated by the Jaén Court in 2007 when it sentenced a 49-year-old father to eight years in prison for violating his daughter over eight years and sexually abusing another of his daughters, both minors. In this case, the sentence was 33 years in prison for a habitual family abuse crime, two continued sex aggression crimes, and one sex abuse crime. In this case, the compensation fixed was 140,000 euros for the two daughters.

This text, originally published in Ideas de Izquierda México before Donald Trump's presidency, examines the anti-immigration, xenophobic, and racist policies of the United States during the recent period, aimed at exacerbating the exploitation and criminalization of migrants. Influenced by the slow growth of the international economy, these policies use the situation of migrants as a tool for social control, exposing the vulnerability of migrants to capitalist exploitation. They are a clear reflection of the subordination of countries like those in Latin America with regards to North American imperialism. Migrants are often forced to leave their places of origin due to a lack of opportunities, an increase in violence, the dispossession by organized crime groups, among other causes, compelling them to seek sustenance in other countries in search of better living conditions, with the hope of finding a better future for themselves and their families. However, from the very heart of imperialism, they are now facing restrictive policies that criminalize their situation, and soon they will be forced to comply with anti-migration orders in the face of the massive deportations announced by Donald Trump, who will take power on January 20. Migration has historically been a phenomenon deeply linked to economic and political power structures, and currently remains a key axis in global dynamics. In this context, this article aims to address the living conditions of migrants, as well as the structures that drive and perpetuate migratory flows inherent to control and management policies imposed by the dominant classes, imperialist powers, and transnational corporations at the international level. Moreover, these dynamics, from Mexico's internal policies, its current relationship with the US, and the pressures of the USMCA (the free trade agreement between Mexico, the US, and Canada that replaced NAFTA during the previous Trump administration), must be understood within the framework of a global unequal system, anchored in dependence, that favors imperialist powers. Migration as a tool of social and political control The migratory flow from Mexico to the US is a clear example of how imperialist countries use migration as a tool of social and political control. Through policies of criminalization, the US (Note: The translation is strictly in English, without any additional explanations or comments.) This has generated an environment in which migrants are presented as a threat to national stability and, at the same time, as a source of cheap labor. The Trump administration's policies, followed in many aspects by the Biden government, have turned migration into a national security issue. The border wall, mass detentions, and deportation of thousands of migrants are examples of how migration is used to strengthen imperialist control over borders, while also reinforcing the division between the working classes of both countries and the region. This security approach has been supported by Mexico's policies, whose governments from the Morena party, both López Obrador's and the current one, although presenting themselves as defenders of migrants' rights in their discourse, in practice submit to the pressures of the United States. The Mexican migration policy, just over 100 days into Claudia Sheinbaum's term, has been characterized by a submission to US demands, evidencing cooperation in the detention and deportation of migrants, as seen in the past two months' Trumpist threats. According to data from the National Migration Institute (INM), 1 in 2023, 211,980 compatriots deported from the US were received and assisted, many of whom were sent to resource-poor countries without support, in a context of growing violence and discrimination towards these groups. Socioeconomic Conditions in Latin America and the Causes of MigrationThe migrant caravans that have left Central America for the United States via Mexico in recent years are a direct response to capitalist exploitation, resulting from a complex interaction of socioeconomic, political, and historical factors, including imperialist interventions, the imposition of free market economic policies by major powers, and the plundering of natural resources by foreign companies, which have stripped Latin America and the Caribbean of their resources, deepening violence in the region and leaving broad segments of the population in conditions of structural poverty.According to World Bank data (2020), approximately 30% of the population of Latin America lives in extreme poverty, prompting migration as a response to the lack of economic opportunities. In addition, Latin America and the Caribbean is one of the most unequal regions in the world, with a Gini index of 3 of 0.49 according to the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) 4. This means that there is an uneven distribution of wealth, which affects large sectors of the population, that is, a significant proportion of resources and income is concentrated in the hands of a small elite, representing the dominant class and the so-called upper classes, while a large part of the population has limited or no access to these resources, particularly the working class, peasants, indigenous peoples, and urban poor. Although it is not the maximum value, 0.49 is relatively high compared to other regions of the world, which is characteristic of economies with high levels of poverty and social exclusion. On the other hand, countries such as El Salvador, Honduras, and Guatemala are facing extremely high levels of violence, with homicide rates among the highest in the world. Although Salvadoran authorities indicate that in 2024, homicides decreased by 26%, 40 fewer than in 2023, The Graphic Press mentions that it has an approximate homicide rate of 52 per 100,000 inhabitants 5. Furthermore, in Honduras, Guatemala, and Nicaragua, foreign companies have taken control of large extensions of land, often with the help of organized crime, displacing entire communities, which previously relied on these resources to survive, and is directly linked to capitalist powers and the State. According to the Mesoamerican Alliance of Peoples and Forests (AMPB) 6, it is estimated that more than 100,000 people have been displaced from their lands due to mining and the exploitation of natural resources. It is essential to highlight the importance of US imperialist interventions in Latin America and the Caribbean, as seen in Haiti, for instance, as well as through policies like Plan Colombia or the funding of governments and paramilitary forces, which have exacerbated violence and instability in the region. These processes have been responsible for creating unsustainable living conditions that force people to migrate, whose conflicts and violence generated 533,000 displacements, with Colombia being the majority of the total, followed by Mexico and Haiti, according to IOM figures. By 2023, the number of internally displaced people in the Americas increased to 6.7 million, all of which causes genuine humanitarian disasters. The impact of the TMEC and external pressures The TMEC, as well as its predecessor the TLCAN, has played a crucial role in shaping Mexico's migratory policies. This agreement, which prioritizes the free flow of goods and capitals and the interests and profits of large transnationals, has conditioned Mexico to adopt migration policies that favor the control of human flows over the protection of their rights. The current governing administration in Mexico, a defender of capitalist interests beyond its progressive discourse and a status quo where the country maintains a subordinate and dependent situation vis-à-vis imperialism, in a situation where it must comply with the demands of the United States and maintain some type of rhetoric to respond to popular sectors, has adopted policies that align with the demands of the White House and the interests of large corporations, not with the working class, and least of all with the poorer migrant workers who, due to their vulnerability to the criminalization of foreign people, face even harsher conditions of exploitation. And that is why the TMEC reinforces capitalist policies by maintaining and expanding an economic model that favors the exploitation of migrant workers, mostly employed in northern Mexico's maquiladoras. This agreement, in its current form, continues to push an economic structure that prioritizes the profits of large corporations while keeping workers in conditions of vulnerability and precariousness. Firstly, the TMEC grants advantages to transnational companies, allowing them to operate under minimal labor standards, which favors the labor exploitation of migrants. In the maquilas where most employees come from migrant communities, labor conditions are usually extremely harsh, with low wages, long working hours, unsanitary conditions, and lack of access to labor benefits such as public healthcare, retirement, etc. In addition, the treaty does not guarantee the effective protection of workers' labor rights, allowing corporations to take advantage of this situation without facing significant consequences. The treaty also limits the ability of governments in subordinate countries to properly regulate employment and decent working conditions, as labor and economic policies in the TMEC are geared towards maximizing competitiveness rather than protecting workers' rights. In this way, this competitive model at the cost of labor rights loss deepens the inequality among workers, promoting the idea of second-class workers, generally migrant, keeping them in a state of precariousness, while large companies reap enormous profits. Instead of an economic integration between equals, which could only be achieved on socialist bases as we explain in our Declaration, let's face Trump's anti-immigrant offensive. Down with the imperialist policies over Latin America and the Caribbean, the treaty promotes an economic model that deepens inequalities and increases Mexico's dependence on the United States, creating an economic pressure that pushes many people to emigrate in search of the American dream for better working conditions. The migration crisis and criminalization The migration phenomenon has triggered a humanitarian crisis in the region. The mass deportation of migrants and the violent treatment by both Mexican and U.S. immigration authorities have exposed the precariousness and vulnerability of migrant workers. Complaints of mistreatment and abuse by the INM and the Border Patrol, combined with the lack of an effective support system for deportees, illustrate how migration has become a tool for social control and show the disdain of governments such as Mexico and Guatemala for the lives of migrants. This criminalization is intersected by another phenomenon linked to security, as while the authorities on both sides of the border implement restrictive and severe anti-migration policies, migrants are forced to cross this treacherous border, facing truly complex and harsh scenarios, one of the main dynamics that fuels this crisis being the relationship between migration and organized crime groups. These groups, which operate both in Mexico and other regions of Central and South America with the tacit approval of the authorities, have established a de facto control over migrant routes to the United States, turning migrants into victims of extortion, kidnapping, and disappearances, among other crimes. Over the past few years, organized crime groups and human trafficking rings have identified migrants as a source of income, exploiting their vulnerability to obtain illicit gains. The testimonies of migrants who manage to cross the border are alarming and recount a crushing reality: they are handed over to criminal groups operating at the borders, who force them to perform forced labor or threaten them with violence if they fail to meet the payments demanded of them. This situation worsens with the complicity of authorities and armed forces on both sides of the border, who in many cases not only allow but coordinate, direct, or collaborate with these criminal groups. As a result, organized crime groups also benefit from anti-migrant policies and a real protection protocol for migrants, which has left a void that criminal gangs have filled, ensuring control of migrant flows. This phenomenon is not isolated; it responds to international inequality dynamics that allow the interests of narcotics trafficking, human trafficking, and migrant trafficking to flourish without major obstacles. Moreover, the criminalization of the migratory phenomenon, driven by xenophobic U.S. and Mexican border control migration policies, contributes to migrants being viewed as criminals simply for attempting to cross a border in search of better living conditions. This vision is intensified when, in the collective imagination, migrants are associated with illegal activities, as Donald Trump is saying, and with the media stigmatization that ranges from social media publications, insensitive films that treat the subject, among others. This stigma allows migrant workers to be treated with hostility and violence by society, which acts as a kind of law enforcement, showing indifference to the exploitation they suffer as an impoverished international working class and also fuels division and confrontation with their brothers and sisters workers in the US. The return of Donald Trump and anti-immigrant rhetoric Since Trump took office in the US in 2017, immigration policies have become increasingly restrictive. During his first term, severe and even cruel measures were implemented that made it difficult for migrants seeking to dissuade and criminalize migration from AL to access their rights. This is the case of the zero tolerance policy, which involved the separation of migrant families and the detention of thousands of people in inhumane conditions. According to Humanium's webpage, it was reported in February 2019 that under this xenophobic policy, 4,300 unaccompanied minors were detained between 2017 and 2018 after crossing the Mexico-US border. During Biden's government, there were nearly 60,000 deportations in the first two years of his term, whereas in 2023, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) carried out 225,483 deportations and returns, an increase over the figure of 170,896 during the same period of the previous year. However, there were many more during the pandemic under Title 42 to quickly expel migrants for sanitary reasons. In the years leading up to this, we had seen the actions of another Democrat, Barack Obama, dubbed the "great deporter" by pro-immigrant organizations in the United States. Now, in 2025, Donald Trump's return to the political scene has revived anti-immigrant rhetoric that, to a large extent, has shaped both U.S. and Mexican migration policies. Trump has repeatedly claimed that the open border of the Biden administration has allowed the entry of supposed terrorists and dangerous individuals, deliberately ignoring the structural causes that force millions of people to migrate. In fact, the Biden administration, although more moderate in its discourse, has continued to implement harsh policies against migrants to divide the working class between natives and migrants, hindering labor unity. Claudia Sheinbaum questioned former Morelos prosecutor Uriel Carmona, who requested the lifting of immunity for former Morelos governor Cuauhtémoc Blanco, as he faces a complaint for alleged attempted sexual abuse. Mexico City, February 10 (SinEmbargo). President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo stated on Monday that her government will not cover up for anyone, following questioning over the case of former Morelos governor and current Deputy Cuauhtémoc Blanco, who has been accused of the alleged attempted sexual abuse of his half-sister in 2019. We will not cover up for anyone. Investigations must always be conducted in all cases. That is the responsibility of the Attorney General's Office and state prosecutors, but it does draw my attention that the Morelos prosecutor, after being in office for seven years, in the last four days, I don't know how many investigation files against the former governor he pulled out, the Mexican head of state said. In a press conference from Palacio Nacional, Sheinbaum Pardo reiterated that it does not seem strange that after seven years in office, four days before he knew he was going to be removed, a large number of investigation files suddenly appeared against the former governor and that he be investigated. On February 6, the Morelos Congress decided on the definitive separation of Uriel Carmona Gándara, until then the State Attorney General, with 16 votes in favor and four against. Hours before, Carmona revealed, in an interview with Azucena Uresti, that he had requested the Cámara de Diputados to lift the immunity of the former governor Cuauhtémoc Blanco, due to the denunciation of attempted rape that weighed against him. It is a constitutional requirement, for the Public Ministry to proceed penalmente against the federal public servant, that the Chamber itself withdraw the immunity so that judicial investigations can continue. That was presented today. Official communications have already been sent requesting that, on this occasion, the ex-governor be subjected to a constitutional procedure so that they can respond to a penal judge here in Morelos, the prosecutor reported during the news broadcast by journalist for Grupo Fórmula. The prosecutor detailed to the medium that the complaint was filed by the ex-governor's half-sister, identified as Fabiola N, due to a presumed sexual assault attempt committed in December 2023 and ruled out that it is a political matter. Headlines Services We Highlight Francisco José Fajardo Las Palmas de Gran Canaria Tuesday, February 11, 2025, 1046 The First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has just dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Raúl Asencio, one of the four young players from Real Madrid who are being investigated for their alleged involvement in the recording and dissemination of a video with sexual content featuring a 16-year-old minor. This decision confirms the ruling of the Instruction Court number 3 of San Bartolomé de Tirajana, which had ordered the identification of the members of messaging groups where the material may have been shared, as well as their declaration as witnesses or suspects if deemed necessary. The case originated from an investigation by the Civil Guard initiated on September 6, 2023, following a complaint filed by the minor's mother in Santa María de Guía. According to this part, on June 15, 2023, three of the soccer players allegedly engaged in consensual sex with a minor and another 18-year-old girl at a private area of a well-known beach club in Amadores (Mogán). However, these relationships were recorded without the consent of the young women, and the video was allegedly shared through messaging apps afterwards. The investigated players are Gran Canaria's Raúl Asencio, who was a member of Castilla's squad at the time and is now a starter for Carlo Ancelotti's first team, Catalan Ferrán Ruiz, Galician Juan Rodríguez, and Balearic Andrés García, all of them between 20 and 21 years old, from Real Madrid C. The arrests took place at Real Madrid's Ciudad Deportiva in Valdebebas, and after making a statement to the Guardia Civil, they were released. The club issued a statement in which it stated that, once it had knowledge of the facts, it would take the necessary measures. The head of the Investigating Court number 3 of San Bartolomé de Tirajana, Julio Wood Rodríguez, summoned the four footballers investigated for a presumed crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, in relation to the recording without consent and the subsequent distribution of the images. The statements were scheduled for November 8, 2023. During the investigation, dumps of the mobile phones of the investigated were made, revealing conversations in which the players commented on the recording and showed concern for the possible legal consequences. One of them even consulted the Internet about the crime of distributing intimate images or recordings without consent. Additionally, Ruiz, Rodríguez, and García allegedly made humiliating comments about the 18-year-old woman from Gran Canaria who filed the complaint. The three Real Madrid C players appear in the investigated sexual recording, where they also find the 18-year-old woman who joined the complaint after learning, through a witness, that the file had not been deleted and was being shared by other team members. In this procedure, Asencio's defense argued that the investigations ordered by the investigating judge were prospective and that there were not enough indications of the commission of the crime, since the video had not been recovered. They also claimed that the legal deadline for the case instruction had expired, according to Canarias 7. However, the Provincial Court, in a ruling dated January 28, presented by Magistrate Secundino Alemán Almeida, rejected these arguments, pointing out that the investigation has sufficient circumstantial evidence to continue. The ruling emphasizes that the disappearance of the video does not imply the non-existence of the crime, as the criminal conduct would have been consummated at the time of its dissemination and exhibition. Moreover, the Chamber clarified that the instruction period has been fulfilled and that the agreed proceedings are valid even if their results are obtained subsequently. The case is framed in the possible commission of crimes of discovery and revelation of secrets, as well as child pornography. The sexual relations with the two 16- and 18-year-old women were allegedly consensual, but what the investigation is looking into is whether the video was recorded without permission and disseminated to third parties. On the day of the incident, the four players were on vacation in Gran Canaria and had agreed to meet three women at the beach club. At one point, Asencio and the third girl left to take a swim in the pool while the other three soccer players were left alone with the two women, allegedly filming the sexual encounter without the young women's consent. The court's resolution highlighted that the penal investigation is a dynamic process, where new lines of investigation or implications for other possible perpetrators may arise. In this sense, it noted that it is not possible to speak of prospective investigation when the proceedings aim to identify people who may have played a role in the chain of distribution of the material. With this decision, it confirms the validity of the instruction that is proceeding towards the possible celebration of a trial, where the four investigated soccer players could be seated in the dock. Two Teenagers Found Dead in Florencio Varela; Double Homicide Investigation Underway, Other Theories Not Ruled OutTwo adolescents who had been missing since last Thursday were found dead in the last few hours in the Florencio Varela partido in the province of Buenos Aires. According to police sources, the victims are Paloma Gallardo, 16 years old, and Josué Salvatierra, 14 years old, classmates from the Secondary School No. 63 in the area. The two teenagers were found dead under a bridge near the Champion battery factory, close to the town square in Bosques. While some sources reported that the bodies were bound, this detail was not confirmed by the police. It is not yet confirmed whether the case was a double homicide or a homicide followed by a suicide. Last Thursday, the parents of Salvatierra, a 9th-grade student, alarmed by the prolonged absence of the young man, went to his residence and, out of concern, filed a report with 911. On the other hand, Omar Gallardo, Paloma's father, who was in 5th grade, stated that his daughter was last seen on the same day when she headed to the gym, located about seven blocks from the square, around 6:00 PM. The girl did not return home, and by 9:00 PM, they began to worry and think that something bad might have happened. The man made a telephone report through the 145 line. I am concerned that behind the disappearance of these young people there may be a case of human trafficking, he said at the time, although this hypothesis has not yet been validated by the authorities. Both teenagers had a cell phone, which initially generated hopes of being able to track their locations. However, after intense searches, their remains were discovered under the bridge. Officers from the local police station and forensic experts from the Buenos Aires police force worked for several hours at the crime scene, and up to this point, the most solid hypothesis suggests a double homicide.

The Andalusia High Court of Justice has confirmed a five-year and six-month prison sentence for a man who sexually abused his 11-year-old cousin, a girl. The abuse lasted almost four years, taking advantage of moments when they were alone to touch her and show her pornographic material. The high court's sentence imposes five years and one day in prison on the accused for continued sexual abuse, as well as an additional six months for showing pornography to a minor. It also establishes a 15-year order of separation and isolation from the minor, as well as 14 additional years under supervised liberty. According to the proven facts, the accused, who was 37 years old at the time of the abuse, took advantage of the visits the minor made to his home in El Ejido (Almería) to commit the crimes. The girl did not inform her father, who is the accused's brother, due to fear of generating family conflicts, as they both lived with the accused's parents and siblings. The abuses occurred at least until 2022 and occurred in various circumstances. On some occasions, the accused attempted to bribe his niece by offering her money to touch her genitals or maintain intimate relationships, to which she refused. Additionally, when the girl was 12 years old, the accused showed her a pornographic video from his mobile phone and then attempted to force her to touch him. Psychological consequences These acts caused the minor symptoms of depression, as well as physical discomfort and intrusive thoughts related to the suffering caused. The Appeals Chamber has supported the minor's version, considering her testimony as credible, plausible, and persistent, supported by an expert report on her.

A U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer was arrested in El Paso on charges related to his alleged involvement in a conspiracy to smuggle undocumented non-citizens for financial gain and alleged narcotics trafficking activity. Between December 21, 2023, and February 5, 2025, Manuel Pérez Jr. allegedly attempted to smuggle undocumented non-citizens into the United States for commercial advantage and private financial gain. The indictment alleges that, in multiple instances, Pérez Jr. admitted a vehicle driven by an undocumented non-citizen at the Paso Del Norte port of entry as part of the human smuggling operations. Additionally, Pérez Jr. Apparently, Pérez Jr. conspired to possess a substance containing at least five kilograms of cocaine from November 1, 2019, to February 5, 2025, to distribute it across Texas, Louisiana, North Carolina, and other places. Pérez Jr. is charged with one count of conspiracy to bring aliens into the United States for financial gain, three counts of bringing aliens into the United States for financial gain, and one count of conspiracy to possess a controlled substance with the intent to distribute. If convicted, he faces a maximum of five years in a federal prison for the human trafficking conspiracy charge, three to 10 years in prison for each of the three additional human trafficking charges, and 10 years to life in prison for the drug trafficking charge. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the United States Sentencing Guidelines and other legal factors.

The Aragua Train is a criminal organization originated in 2005 in the Venezuelan Tocorón prison, expanding its illicit activities to several countries in the Americas. Peru has been one of the countries most affected by this group, considered by President Donald Trump as a threat to the security of the United States.
