The Constitutional Court declared the provision that allowed girls and boys over 14 years old to get married in the Civil Code to be unconstitutional. This supports the bill that prohibits child marriage and was approved by Congress last year. The Constitutional Court set a precedent in Colombia against child marriage. Through Sentence C039 of 2025, it was considered that marriage and de facto marital unions between or with people under 18 years old are contrary to the Constitution. In this way, the Court sentenced that the minimum age for getting married is now 18 years old, not 14 years old, changing what was established by a provision of the Civil Code, which has been in effect since 1887, and allowed marriage for those over 14 years old with parental permission. This court ruling aligns with the Project of Law 297, which was approved by Congress last year, with the aim of eliminating child marriage, de facto marital unions, and early unions (MIUT) in which one or both of the contracting parties or permanent partners are minors. Additionally, it creates the National Program for Comprehensive Attention to Life Projects for children, girls, and adolescents and issues other provisions. The previous congressional approval and now this court ruling mark another step in the comprehensive protection of the rights of girls, boys, and adolescents. However, the law is still pending presidential sanction. We celebrate this court ruling, which reinforces and supports the actions of civil society and all allies who have pushed for the elimination of child marriage in Colombia, to continue promoting legal frameworks and genuine commitments in the protection of girls, boys, and adolescents, said Daniela Esguerra, national advocacy leader at World Vision Colombia.Context The Committee on the Rights of the Child and the Universal Human Rights Committee had recommended to Colombia to eradicate marriages before the age of 18, repeatedly emphasizing that it is a harmful practice that carries severe consequences for children. According to the 2015 National Demography and Health Survey, in urban areas, 21% of women aged 10 to 19 years old were married before the age of 18, while in rural areas, this figure rises to 37%, showing a 16-point percentage difference. Additionally, more than 2.5 million women between the ages of 20 and 49 entered into marriage or initiated a union before the age of 18. With the law, national authorities have more tools to protect the integrity of girls, boys, and adolescents, as it had been evidenced that child marriage and early unions generated violence such as sexual exploitation and forced labor, which constitutes an aggravating factor of all physical, psychological, and economic damages. Furthermore, girls and adolescents who marry prematurely are exposed to suffering violence, abuse, and sexual relations that result in forced high-risk pregnancies, and even being exposed to situations of human trafficking for the purpose of sexual exploitation and forced labor, leading to a severe impact on their development and integrity. Early marriages and child unions unfortunately have become normalized in our society. In 2020, more than half of girls aged 10 to 14, 52% (2,229), and 75% (82,778) of adolescents aged 15 to 19 who had given birth, were in unions, according to data from the Observatorio Contando lo Invisible based on data from the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, Sispro data warehouse. From World Vision Colombia, along with all civil society organizations and with special articulation with Alianza por la Niñez, we celebrate this important milestone and applaud society for continuing to do responsible work to protect the rights of girls and children. With this decision, Colombia is getting closer to achieving a sufficient legal framework that protects the rights of childhood and would also join the group of 12 countries in the region that have prohibited child marriages.

Peruvian Police assert that the Aragua Train is completely dismantled. The Peruvian National Police (PNP) stated on Monday that the transnational criminal gang known as the Aragua Train is completely dismantled in the country, and highlighted that its main leaders are detained in Challapalca maximum security prison. At the moment, we have the Aragua Train dismantled. As a criminal organization, the Aragua Train in Peru is completely dismantled. All leaders have fallen () are serving their sentence in Challapalca, said PNP General Aldo Ávila Novoa to RPP radio. He explained that the Aragua Train has a very special behavior and an undefined structure, and they are studying it together with the Government of the United States how it is organized. In this regard, he indicated that its structure is not pyramidal nor collegiate and the hypothesis is that it is a differentiated organization with higher levels and others distributed in countries such as Peru, Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Spain, Brazil, Panama, the United States, and Costa Rica. The Aragua Train has two main characteristics, adaptability and negotiation capacity. In Peru, we mapped them in 2017, and when the migration came in 2018, they began to occupy territories of human trafficking, Ávila stated. He said they fight against separate groups of the gang like the Sons of God and Los Gallegos, but he cannot give the exact number of the different remnants located in different points of the country. Ávila referred to the mega-police operation carried out on Friday night with the support of the Office of National Security Investigations of Immigration and Customs of the United States in several points of Lima against the criminal organization. He detailed that 23 delinquents linked to factions of the Aragua Train were apprehended and are being investigated for the alleged crime of human trafficking, in the modality of sexual and labor exploitation. He added that in the operation, 120 victims of exploitation were rescued, including three minors who were already placed in the care of the Special Protection Unit of the Ministry of Women. The Aragua Train has spread to Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, and Chile, where authorities accuse it of committing numerous crimes, including narcotics trafficking, extortion, kidnappings, and homicides. US President Donald Trump signed an executive order shortly after taking office to classify Mexican cartels, the Salvadoran gang MS13, and the Aragua Train as terrorist organizations. El Ejido Tuesday, February 11, 2025, 11:59 am The Andalusian Higher Court of Justice (TSJA) has confirmed a sentence of five years and six months in prison for a man accused of sexually abusing his 11-year-old niece for nearly four years, taking advantage of the fact that they were alone to touch her and even show her pornographic material. Specifically, the Andalusian high court imposes on the accused five years and one day in prison for a continued sexual abuse crime and six months more for showing pornography to a minor. It also agrees on 15 years of isolation and disconnection from the minor and 14 years more of supervised freedom. The sentence establishes that the accused, who was 37 years old at the time, took advantage of the visits that the minor made to his residence in El Ejido, where he was alone with her when she was 11 years old, to sexually abuse her. The minor did not tell her father, who is also the accused's brother, about the abuse out of fear of a family conflict, as they both lived with the accused's parents and siblings at their residence. The abuse, which occurred at least until 2022, took place in different circumstances and ways, to the point that the accused even offered money to his niece to touch her genitals or maintain intimate relationships, which she refused. Additionally, when the girl was 12 years old, the accused showed her a video on his mobile phone of adults engaging in sexual acts, followed by forcing the minor to touch his penis. This situation led to a depressive symptomatology in the minor, who also suffered physical discomfort and intrusive thoughts due to the distress she endured. In this sense, the Appellate Court supports the criteria followed by the Third Section of the Provincial Court of Almería in accepting without reservations the version provided by the minor, whose testimony practiced as preconstituted evidence was considered credible, verifiable, and persistent, inasmuch as it was supported by the expert report conducted on the minor.

LAS PALMAS DE GRAN CANARIA, 11 (EUROPA PRESS) The First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid player Raúl Asencio, who is one of the four young players from the Madrid team being investigated for their alleged involvement in the recording and dissemination of a sex video with a 16-year-old minor. This is stated in the ruling of the First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas, dated January 28, 2025, following the appeal filed by Asencio's defense, which argued that the investigation period had expired, as well as the lack of evidence of the crimes attributed to him due to the non-existence of the sex video that served as the basis for the investigation. However, the magistrate emphasizes in his legal reasoning that the case, initiated on September 18, 2023, began investigating a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets after the Civil Guard received a complaint about the dissemination of a video with explicit sexual content about sexual relations maintained by a 16-year-old girl on June 15, 2023, which apparently and, provisionally, would have been recorded by two boys with whom she had that sexual relationship. One of these young men would have sent the video to a WhatsApp group that the now appellant, Asencio, was part of, according to this auto, which he allegedly viewed and showed to a friend. It is stated that during the course of that pre-prosecutorial investigation, the Judicial Police seized four mobile terminals belonging to the four suspected individuals, including the defense of Real Madrid. The initial complaint was complemented by another complaint, dated September 19, 2023, agreeing to dump and extract the information contained in those four devices, and its subsequent analysis by specialists from the Organic Police Judicial Unit of Las Palmas. Although the initial complaint for preliminary proceedings was appealed by the Gran Canaria defense of Real Madrid, it was dismissed, validating the start of the investigation, considering that there were objective elements about a possible crime of revelation and discovery of secrets. That complaint of September 19, 2023, in substance regarding dumping, was confirmed by the Provincial Court of Las Palmas in the autos of January 17, 2024, and April 19, 2024, alluding to indications of a crime against intimacy or, in the alternative, a crime related to the sexual exploitation and corruption of minors. The judge also notes that the instruction should be considered finalized within a period of 12 months, unless by office or at the request of a party, it is extended. However, he adds that the appealed ruling is prior to the expiration of that ordinary 12-month period. The judge also rejects the argument that there cannot be a prospective investigation in the practice of a procedure that would allow identifying all the people who were part of the WhatsApp group in which the video circulated, in order to hear them as witnesses later on, in order to determine which video they received and from whom. The ruling concludes that, with the provisional nature of the process, Asencio allegedly received on his mobile phone in June 2023 a video with explicit sexual content starring a 16-year-old minor, who instead of deleting it, showed it to another person, thereby presumably committing not only the crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, but also child pornography, punishable by one to five years in prison for exhibiting that video to a third party, which, regardless of the outcome of the agreed investigations, already provides sufficient evidence at this time to reject the request for provisional dismissal instigated in his appeal.

The proposed agreement for the renewal of the State pact against gender violence, which the parties presented to the Congressional Equality Commission on Monday, in addition to considering measures against economic, digital, or vicarious violence for the first time, as El Periódico previously reported, contains proposals to strengthen prevention, detection, security, punishment of the aggressor, and comprehensive reparation in a total of 462 measures. The comprehensive report, in which the groups have worked for a year, emphasizes strengthening the actions, teams, coordination, and training of all operators working against all forms of machismo violence, including forced marriage or genital mutilation, although as there is no agreement among parties on prostitution, in this area it includes measures against human trafficking for sexual exploitation, pimping, or to discourage demand, but without delving into whether sex work should be prohibited or regulated. In any case, the commitment is such that the state budget allocated for the different administrations to implement the measures agreed upon by the parties goes from the 1,000 euros of the original pact (signed in 2017) to 1.5 billion euros, which will be invested over the next five years. The resolution will be approved, likely with the opposition of Vox, next week in the Committee on Equality of the Congress, and these are some of the main measures it contains Ámbito judicial. The agreement proposes eliminating the mitigating factor of confession and the one for damage repair, from which Dani Alves benefited, who saw his sentence reduced for rape by indemnifying the victim with 150,000 euros. The sentence sparked a storm of criticism because the mitigating factor facilitates justice for the rich and another for the poor. The agreement also provides that all processes related to the same victim will be tried in a single organ, which the family courts will consult compulsorily if there are criminal processes for gender violence in all processes that affect childhood or there are indications of violence, that all procedures that can complete the victim's statement be carried out, which can retract due to fear of the aggressor, that more resources be provided to the psychosocial and forensic teams so that they issue their reports without delay, or that the false Parental Alienation Syndrome (SAP) be eradicated. Other violences The agreement proposes incorporating economic, digital, and vicarious violence into the legal framework, which is exercised against children to harm the mother. These sections encompass dozens of new proposals, including the reinforcement of measures aimed at preventing cohabitation or visitation regimes with the aggressor and the need to conduct a paternofilia evaluation prior to the judicial resolution of visits when requested by the victim of gender violence. In addition, the parties propose creating a new crime that encompasses conduct that limits women's autonomy and economic independence and strengthen penalties for digital aggression. Education In the educational sphere, the pact foresees the promotion of affective-sexual education already covered by various laws and the school councils designate a responsible teacher for coeducation in equality, among other measures. Healthcare To increase the detection of victims who do not want to report, as most visit the doctor frequently, the pact requests that a universal screening be established in case it is suspected that a patient's symptoms may be associated with abuse, that the training of healthcare personnel be increased, and that the Plan for comprehensive care for children of mortal victims include psychological attention for their descendants. Additionally, it is foreseen that psychological therapy be offered to perpetrators who voluntarily request this service.Sexual Violence In addition to requesting the full implementation of the "yes means yes" law, the parties ask that mechanisms for verifying age and parental controls be established to prevent minors from accessing pornography, as also foreseen by the law on digital environment protection, which has yet to be approved. In addition, they demand measures, but without specifying how to do it to prevent platforms such as Sugar Daddy or OnlyFans from becoming means of capture for the sexual exploitation of young people. They also propose training for screenwriters so that audiovisual content is free of stereotypes and create the figure of an intimacy coordinator in audiovisual productions, to respect consent. Denialism Without specifying exactly how to do it, the new pact proposes strengthening the institutional response to face denialism in gender violence. And it proposes strengthening the training of workers in the tourism, hospitality, and leisure sectors so that they can detect and act on aggressions, as well as for company protocols against sexual harassment to record complaint data. . Specific measures are also contemplated to protect vulnerable victims such as immigrants, people with disabilities, or to reinforce actions in the rural area. Subscribe to continue reading.

Football Justice maintains charges against Real Madrid player Raúl Asencio for child pornography The Court of Las Palmas holds that there are rational indications of sufficient criminality against the white team's footballer Cristina GallardoURLFermín de la Calle The Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid player Raúl Asencio. The player is one of the four footballers investigated in a case of distributing sexual content with a 16-year-old minor. In the auto, issued on January 28, the three magistrates ensure that there are rational indications of sufficient criminality that the Canary Islands' youth footballer may have committed both a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, as well as another of child pornography. The defense of Asencio requested the dismissal of the case, arguing that the investigations agreed upon by the investigating judge were being conducted without solid indications of a crime due to the absence of the video in the investigation, and also argued that the instruction period had expired, in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law. They argued that since the video could not be recovered by the Judicial Police, its existence and content could not be proven, and there were no evidence linking the footballer to the crime. An unrecovered video The defense claimed that since the video was not recovered, there were no evidence of the crime. However, the ruling confirms that the absence of the video file does not mean it never existed and establishes that the crime would have been committed when the video was shared, even if it was later deleted. Additionally, an investigated individual stated that Asencio showed them the video, to which WhatsApp records on his phone indicate that he received it. The judges of the Audiencia have rejected these arguments and have ordered the investigated party to assume the procedural costs. In addition, they emphasize that the proceedings were ordered before the deadline expired, so they are valid, and they add that nothing prevents the opening of a separate case if new lines of investigation appear, which would allow extending the deadline if necessary.The investigation began on September 18, 2023, as a result of the complaint filed by the young woman's mother at a Guardia Civil barracks in Gran Canaria, accusing the possible dissemination of an explicit sexual content video starring the minor. The same had been recorded on June 15, and, according to the complainant, the relationships that took place in the reserved area of a leisure establishment in the town of Amadores, in the Canary Island municipality of Mogán, had been consensual. What was not consensual was the recording of the same. As a result of the complaint, the investigating judge charged four soccer players, Raúl Asencio, currently a member of Real Madrid's first team, Ferran Ruiz (who plays for Girona), Galician Juan Rodríguez (from Tarazona), and Balearic Andrés García (from Alcorcón).

The Justice confirmed the eight-year prison sentence for a police officer who sexually abused a young woman with hearing loss and speech difficulties in the bathroom of the Regional Hospital Río Grande, Tierra del Fuego, where the accused was on duty. The case, titled as Recurso de hecho deducido por la defensa en la causa Carabajal, Cesar Daniel y otro sURLabuso sexual simple en concurso real, arrived at the Supreme Court after a long process of appeals. Fernando Carabajal was sentenced in 2022 for simple sexual abuse in real concurrence with double aggravated sexual abuse with carnal access. During the trial, the accused did not deny the facts, but argued that there was consent from the victim and requested his acquittal. However, the young woman denounced the abuse and her account was consistent in all instances of the judicial process. Judge Edith Cristiano, in her vote at the Superior Court of Justice of Tierra del Fuego, highlighted that the sentence imposed by the Criminal Court of the Northern District Judicial Court was based on solid evidence that overcame all reasonable doubt. The magistrate also noted that the controversy centered on the alleged consent of the victim, but emphasized that the experts did not find elements that questioned the credibility of her account. In addition, she highlighted that the victim maintained her version of the facts from the complaint to the oral debate, and that her account even coincided with the version of the accused. Taking into account the victim's bilateral neurosensorial profound hearing loss, Judge Cristina argued that her statement should be analyzed with special attention, from a gender and disability perspective. Finally, the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation dismissed the defense's argument, which claimed arbitrariness in the sentence, and confirmed the eight-year prison sentence for Fernando Carabajal.

Mothers report that school director abuses children, says MEP in Vara BlancaA group of mothers of students from Julia Fernández Rodríguez School in Vara Blanca report that the current school director allegedly has committed acts of aggression against minors. According to their account, the school administrator apparently yells at the children, and in one of the incidents, she allegedly took a lira by force from a second-grade student and told her to leave because she didn't know a song. The director told her, "Please, give me that lira and you do me a favor and leave here." I feel that she, as a teacher and director, should not take that attitude, especially since they are young children, one of the complainants stated. They also mention that she verbally abused a sixth-grade student and that this type of event is frequent. She has yelled at my children, she doesn't have the gift of a teacher. And the treatment with the fathers is not good, they tell us we are farmers, one of the affected said. How did it all start The problem with the official began approximately 2 years ago due to school civic celebrations, according to the mothers' version. The initial trigger was when the director denied the children the right to celebrate September 14th with lanterns and the national anthem, a Costa Rican tradition. The school remained closed that day. On September 15th, the hierarchy carried out a civic act with the presence of the supervisor. Several mothers expressed their annoyance, but the director claimed to have a close relationship with the supervisor. Subsequently, a meeting was requested with the director to address the issue, but nothing was resolved. On her part, the supervisor would have supported the official, indicating, according to the complainants, that each director can do as they please in their institution. From that moment on, the director began to take other negative attitudes, including threats of defamation, as one of the affected parties recounts. Humiliations are exaggerated, both for teaching staff, students, and parents, it's unbelievable, she emphasized. Fear in children Some children are afraid to go to school due to the treatment they receive, and even some mothers decided to transfer their children to another educational center. In a specific case, one of the women recounts how her 4-year-old son came home telling her that the official had told them that there is a punishment chair. He arrived and asked me very scared that day, he said, Mom, the principal says there's a punishment chair. And I stayed like, yes, there's a punishment chair, and over it a belt for those who don't listen, so they sit there and they hit them with the belt, he commented.According to the complainant, this happened at the beginning of the 2024 school year, and immediately she sent a letter to the principal to clarify the situation, however, the headmaster said it was a lie and in one of the exchanged letters, she told her that she was going to sue her. On other occasions, it is mentioned that, apparently, she discriminated against a minor for being of another nationality. Complaints and lack of responseAs time passed, other cases emerged, and as a result of the 4-year-old boy's experience, other mothers joined to denounce the principal through letters. The complaints escalated to instances such as the Ministry of Public Education (MEP), and despite the complaints presented since December 2024, the mothers indicate that they have not received clear information on the progress of the case, as only 2 of them received a call and were asked to present the complaint at the regional offices of the MEP in San José, where they allegedly were told that the director would be suspended, but to date continues teaching. On the other hand, they indicate that there could be a friendship between the person receiving the complaints and the director, which causes them insecurity. This woman cannot be teaching where the children are, we were the ones who filed the complaints and she is teaching here. No, that cannot be. We were shocked to see that this woman began the school year as if nothing had happened, one of them mentioned. I am a person who wants the best for my child, and he is my only child, and I don't want him to be in an environment, or in a place where he is with a person like that woman, he added. Among other things, they also point out that several teachers have left the institution due to alleged workplace harassment.This medium consulted the MEP to know their position on the matter, and the response was from the Regional Directorate as follows:With superior instructions from the Regional Director and in response to your query, it is informed that this Regional Directorate has not received complaints of that nature against the director of the Vara Blanca School, nor is there a friendship relationship with her.However, since these proceedings correspond, by due process, to the supervisor, the supervisor of circuit 01 was consulted, who confirmed that some complaints were received and were sent to the Disciplinary Regime, the competent instance for analysis and resolution. Currently, the case is under review. As it is being investigated, the authorities stated that they cannot provide further details. Grupo Extra attempted to contact the educational center, however, by the end of this note, there was no response. An investigation was opened against Deputy Jorge Durán (RN), who was accused of sexual abuse. The incident allegedly occurred in the early morning of last Saturday, February 8, at the home he shared with his former partner. Around 2 am, Carabineros arrived at the congressman's residence in Colina, following a complaint from his former partner. The Prosecution classified the case as reserved due to the gravity of the accusations, while the victim was taken to the Medical-Legal Service around 3:30 am to undergo the necessary medical examinations. The results of these examinations are expected to determine the parliamentary's judicial situation. The Public Ministry instructed the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI to conduct the initial proceedings of this case.

(TdF OPI) The justice of Tierra del Fuego sentenced a man to serve a 16-year prison sentence for finding him guilty in two cases of sexual abuse in the city of Ushuaia. This was determined by the members of the Criminal Trial Court of the Southern District Judicial Court, who ruled against a 38-year-old man to serve a 16-year prison sentence in a verdict that was known on Friday. The decision is based on the evidence and testimonies for two incidents of abuse, one of repeated carnal access aggravated by the relationship, and the other for simple abuse. The man was sentenced for a carnal access abuse aggravated by the relationship when the accused was 17 years old, and it was decided to detain him immediately. The grounds of the ruling will be known on Friday 14, and the court was made up of judges Alejandro Pagano Zavalía, Maximiliano García Arpón, and Felicitas Maiztegui Marcó. (OPI Tierra del Fuego Agency)

An elderly man was detained by authorities after being accused of raping his own granddaughter. The citizen slept with his granddaughter and in the early hours of the morning, he would sexually abuse the minor, said Edison Dueñas, head of the Search Unit of the Police. She was 11 years old at the time of the assaults. The alert was given by the minor, who, tired of the constant abuse, decided to inform her parents. The incidents occurred in 2020 and since then, the man had been hiding in various sectors of the capital. Eight people detained for sexual abuse in 2025. The Police confirmed that so far this year, they have detained eight people for sexual abuse. The elderly man is awaiting trial and, if found guilty, could face a sentence of up to 19 years.

After a year of investigations, the State Attorney General's Office of Oaxaca secured a exemplary sentence against Antonio L, responsible for the sexual abuse of a young woman with psychomotor disability in San Pedro Pochutla. The facts The attack occurred on February 7, 2023, when the victim, a 19-year-old adolescent with language and memory problems, was at her home in the Fourth Section of San Pedro Pochutla. Antonio L entered the residence and sexually assaulted her. Investigation and capture Following the complaint, the Oaxaca Attorney General's Office initiated an investigation through the specialized areas for sexual crimes of the Regional Vice Attorney General's Office of the Coast. With the obtained evidence, a warrant for arrest was obtained, allowing for the detention and presentation of the aggressor to the judicial authority. Sentence and Penalties The Court of Trial imposed a 17-year prison sentence on Antonio L, in addition to imposing an economic fine and ordering him to pay for reparations for the damage. Commitment to Justice The authorities of Oaxaca reaffirmed their commitment to fighting against gender-based violence, assuring that they will continue with firm actions to protect the victims and punish the aggressors.

The Governor, Carlos Eduardo del Castillo, said that the operational order is ready to apprehend Evo Morales and announced that they are waiting for the precise moment and place. In contact with the press, Del Castillo stated that the objective is to fulfill the arrest order while avoiding unnecessary confrontations and that there be no police or civilian casualties, dead or wounded. Morales is sought to once again convulse our country, seeking grief, confrontation, that a Bolivian police officer lose their life or one of his followers. "We won't fall for those types of provocations, as we already have our operational orders prepared, we're waiting for the precise moment and place to carry out what justice has determined to avoid human life losses and to avoid unnecessary injuries in a confrontation, he asserted. In this sense, the Minister even stated that Morales is expected to leave the Trópico de Cochabamba to achieve his capture. And it's because Morales has been barricaded in the Trópico since last year, when the case against him for human trafficking and people smuggling was activated. In that region, considered his stronghold, his followers organized a syndical security to prevent his capture." In January, a judge declared Morales in contempt for failing to appear in court twice to resolve the aggravated charge of human trafficking against him, for having maintained a relationship with a minor with whom he later had a child, while he was president of Bolivia in 2016. Nevertheless, days ago Morales announced that he will lead a march to La Paz with the aim of registering his candidacy for the presidency, despite being disqualified by a ruling from the Plurinational Constitutional Court that limited continuous and discontinuous re-election in the country.

A woman who was a victim of sexual exploitation was rescued and her attacker was arrested in the Buenos Aires town of Pergamino. The case was initiated in November 2024 following various investigations conducted by police officers, as a result of a complaint received by the Functional Instruction and Trial Unit number 3 of the Pergamino Judicial Department, led by Nelson Mastorchio, for the crime of Economic Exploitation of the Exercise of Prostitution of Adults. In this way, and after various field tasks, sufficient evidence was collected. As a consequence, the Guarantee Court number 2 of the Pergamino Judicial Department, led by Julio Caturla, issued a judicial letter ordering the search of two properties, one of which is located on Joaquín V. González Street and the other on Pueyrredón Street. During the operations, the victim was successfully rescued, along with her minor daughter, who received psychological support and were placed at the disposal of the acting judiciary. Additionally, the aggressor was apprehended. In one of the raided homes, a marijuana plant was seized, with a total weight of 803 grams, three cellular phones, 35 condoms, sex toys, and other evidence of value for the investigation. The rescued woman, as well as the accused and the seized items, were placed at the disposal of the intervening magistrate to proceed with the judicial actions required. Source: NA.

The Dominican, Fermín Montilla, was sentenced on Monday to nine years in prison for his participation in a human trafficking attempt that resulted in the death of 11 immigrants. The accused attempted to illegally traffic 48 migrants to the United States, leading to the tragic deaths of 11 people. Human traffickers threaten national security and exploit vulnerable individuals for profit, disregarding their safety. The Criminal Division is committed to eliminating these transnational human trafficking criminal organizations and protecting the public and those who may fall victim to them, said Antoinette Bacon, supervisor of the Criminal Division of the Department of Justice in written statements. . PUBLICIDAD According to court documents, on the night of May 12, 2022, Fermín Montilla, 45 years old, was driving a vessel carrying 48 people from the Dominican Republic to Puerto Rico with the intention of smuggling them into the United States illegally. At some point during the journey, the vessel took on water and capsized, resulting in the drowning deaths of 11 people. Human trafficking operations not only violate U.S. law and threaten our national security, but also put the lives of trafficked migrants at risk and result in deaths, as in this case. The U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Attorney's Office will continue working with our federal, state, and local partners to bring to justice those who traffic in illegal immigrants and dismantle their criminal organizations, said U.S. Attorney W. Stephen Muldrow. It is essential to send a strong message to those who exploit the vulnerable, putting lives at risk and undermining the safety of our communities. In this single incident, we lost 11 lives. We must protect people from this heinous crime. We will continue to utilize all available resources to pursue and bring to justice transnational criminal organizations that put others at risk by exploiting immigration laws. To those seeking to be trafficked into the United States, remember that it is extremely dangerous and not worth risking your life, these individuals do not care, said Special Agent Rebecca Gonzalez-Ramos of National Security Investigations (HSI) in San Juan. On September 13, 2024, Montilla pleaded guilty to a charge of transporting immigrants to the United States in a location other than a designated port of entry, resulting in deaths.

In a joint operation between the Peruvian National Police (PNP), the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Crimes of Human Trafficking, and the Department of Criminal Investigation (DEPINCRI), a suspected prostitution ring operating in the establishment known as Villa Cariño, located in the Huallayco street, block 23, in Huánuco was dismantled. The operation was carried out in compliance with a judicial resolution issued on September 10, 2024, by the Second Civil Court of Huánuco, presided over by Judge J.C.F. The resolution rejected the establishment's continued operation due to the lack of a functioning license, the absence of a Civil Defense certificate, and the non-compliance with municipal ordinances. Detentions and SeizuresDuring the police intervention, four individuals identified by the initials A.S.R.R. (18), E.M.R.E. (35), C.E.L.Q. (50), and H.J.H.N. Sixty people, allegedly involved in the commission of the crime against personal liberty in the form of pimping. In addition, 16 women who allegedly offered sexual services within the establishment and 8 men who were found inside the premises at the time of the operation were intervened. As part of the investigation, authorities seized 17 mobile phones, three video recorders, cash in hand, and accounting documents related to the activities carried out in the establishment. Possible municipal cover-up In parallel, the Provincial Municipality of Huánuco, under the management of Mayor A.J.G., faces allegations of presumed omission of duties and possible cover-up of illicit activities. Despite the municipality having resolutions and municipal ordinances that ordered the closure of the establishment, these would not have been executed in a timely manner, which could lead to legal responsibilities for the mayor and their officials. Close sources to the investigation indicate that there could be an internal protection network in the municipality, which has raised suspicions about the presence of small mafias that facilitate the continuation of these businesses in the city. Investigations continue to determine the existence of alleged acts of corruption or negligence in the compliance with current regulations.

In representation of the Municipal President, the Honorary President of the Integral Development System for the Family (DIF) of Solidaridad, Eduardo Asencio, highlighted the urgency of addressing this issue with the collaboration of the three branches of government and the tourism sector. Child exploitation is a problem that requires an immediate and effective response. Deputy Jorge Durán after sexual abuse complaint Accuses woman of extortion and credit card theft Following the initiation of an investigation against him due to the sexual abuse and rape complaint filed by his ex-partner, Deputy Jorge Durán (RN) categorically denied all allegations and presented a completely different version. The complainant, who filed the accusation on Monday, stated that everything occurred at their shared residence in Chicureo, Colina, where after a discussion, the right-wing parliamentarian entered a room and allegedly committed the crimes on Friday. Jorge Durán accuses extortion In a press statement, Deputy Jorge Durán of Renovación Nacional defended himself, launching accusations against his ex-partner and announcing a pending lawsuit. In relation to the recent events involving my ex-partner and me, as seen on TVN, I would like to clarify the following:After the end of our relationship, and considering that my ex-partner was unemployed and without a place to reside, I offered them housing in a dependency within my property for humanitarian reasons.Last Friday, during a celebration at my home, my ex-partner voluntarily attended the gathering along with other guests. That night, we shared a consensual intimate moment together. The following day, in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch, maintaining a cordial coexistence.Furthermore, Senator Durán (RN) reported that after clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began demanding a sum of money, claiming that if I did not comply with their demands, I would be the one who would be harmed. In response to this extortion situation, and after discovering that my ex-partner had used one of my credit cards without my authorization, I proceeded to file a complaint on Monday night for extortion and theft with the Carabineros. The authorities arrived at my residence, where relevant background information was gathered. To my surprise, after my complaint, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, which has created a completely distorted situation and has significantly affected my public image, he explained. To conclude, Durán said that I have provided all necessary evidence and the corresponding expert assessments have been conducted in the presence of my family, including my children. I am confident that justice will shed light on the facts and the truth will be revealed. I put myself at the complete disposal of the MP with the purpose that the complaint made against me is investigated with the utmost diligence and the complaint I made in the first instance, which will be transformed into a lawsuit as soon as possible.

Jury Trial Judge to Decide Fate of Stroeder Man Accused of Abusing His Young DaughterA jury trial will take place from February 12 to 14 to examine the conduct of a man accused of abusing his young daughter in the Stroeder area. According to the case, investigated by UFIJ No. 14 led by prosecutor Marcelo Romero Garden, the incidents occurred between April and August 2021, when the victim was visiting her father's home and under his care. The complaint was filed by the victim's mother, who took her to the hospital for treatment after detecting injuries that raised suspicions of possible sexual abuse. The accused will face trial, charged with aggravated sexual abuse committed by an ascendant. The debate will be led by technical judge Dr. Christian Yesari, member of the Criminal Court N1, will be held at the fifth floor of the Palace of Tribunals, located at Estomba 34, Bahía Blanca.

The First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid player Raúl Asencio. This is one of the four young players from the Madrid-based team being investigated for their alleged involvement in the recording and dissemination of a video with sexual content featuring a 16-year-old minor. This is stated in the ruling by the First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas, dated January 28, 2025, following the appeal filed by Asencio's defense team, arguing that the investigation period had expired, and there were no indications of the perpetration of the crimes attributed to him, given the non-existence of the video that formed the basis of the investigation. However, the judge emphasizes in his legal reasoning that the cause, initiated on September 18, 2023, began investigating a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets after the Civil Guard received a complaint about the dissemination of a video with sexual content about explicit sexual relationships maintained by a 16-year-old girl on June 15, 2023, which, apparently and provisionally, had been recorded by two boys with whom she had that sexual relationship. One of these young men had apparently sent the video to a WhatsApp group in which the now appellant, Asencio, was a member, who, according to this auto, viewed it and showed it to a friend of his. It is stated that during the course of that pre-prosecutorial investigation, the Judicial Police seized four mobile terminals belonging to the four suspected parties, including the defender of Real Madrid. The indictment motion, it indicates, was then complemented with another motion, dated September 19, 2023, agreeing to the dumping and extraction of the information contained in those four devices, and its subsequent analysis by specialists from the Organic Police Judicial Unit of Las Palmas. Although the initial indictment motion for preliminary proceedings was appealed by the Gran Canaria defense of Real Madrid, it was dismissed, validating the start of the investigation, considering that objective elements concurred on a possible crime of revelation and discovery of secrets. That motion of September 19, 2023, in substantial terms regarding the dumping, was confirmed by the Provincial Court of Las Palmas in the motions of January 17, 2024, and April 19, 2024, alluding to indications of a crime against intimacy or in its case, a crime related to the sexual exploitation and corruption of minors. In addition, the judge notes that the instruction should be considered finalized within a period of 12 months, unless extended by the court at the request of a party. However, he adds that the appealed ruling was issued before the expiration of the ordinary 12-month deadline. The judge also rejects the argument that there cannot be a prospective investigation in the practice of a procedure that would allow identifying all individuals who were part of the WhatsApp group in which the video circulated, in order to hear them as witnesses later to determine which video they received and from whom. The auto concludes that, with the provisionality inherent to the procedural stage, Asencio allegedly received on his mobile phone in June 2023 a video with explicit sexual content featuring a 16-year-old minor, rather than deleting it, he displayed it to at least one other person. Therefore, he would be committing not only the crime of disclosure and revelation of secrets, but also that of child pornography, punishable by imprisonment of one to five years if he exhibited that video to a third party, which, regardless of the outcome of the agreed-upon investigations, already provides sufficient evidence at the moment to reject the request for provisional dismissal instigated in their appeal.

The Galicia Superior Court of Justice (TSXG) has confirmed the eight-year prison sentence imposed by the Corunna Provincial Court on a man who sexually abused his underage niece. The Galician High Court dismisses the appeal filed by the defendant's defense against a sentence that also obliges him to compensate the victim with 10,000 euros. The victim will not be able to approach him within 500 meters for 13 years. In its resolution, facilitated to the media this Tuesday by the TSXG, the panel reiterates that the victim's account is sufficient to support the charges against the defendant, as considered by the Corunna court. It emphasizes that the testimony of the minor has high credibility in narrating clearly what happened and perfectly orienting himself in the moment he suffered the episodes of blockage that the accused took advantage of to commit the abuses. And it is that the minor, who had moved in with her aunts due to the conflictive environment that was experienced in her parents' houses, suffered from syncope that left her still and unable to react in moments of tension. The accused took advantage of these moments to commit, at least on two occasions, sexual abuse against the minor, which the court also corroborates with the forensic reports presented during the trial. However, the sentence is not final as there is the possibility that the parties may present an appeal for cassation before the Second Chamber of the Supreme Court.

Spanish President Pedro Sánchez The equality training would be beneficial to some operators of the law The Prime Minister defends the Spanish model of fighting gender violence as the best in the world during the act of the 20th anniversary of the integral law If there is a silence that needs to be broken today, it is that of men. With this phrase, pronounced during the multitudinous act to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the integral law against gender violence, the Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has highlighted what he considers one of the most urgent and necessary issues for society, and the ultimate goal for which the norm was approved during the presidency of the also socialist José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, to end violence against women. Sánchez, who was in charge of closing an event attended by dozens of women and men who worked to advance that norm, recalled how the law was processed with three axes that seemed unattainable at the time. One, understanding that that violence is a structural violence anchored in machismo, two, taking it out of the private sphere, so shame would switch sides, and three, involving everyone on the same front against violence. By everyone, the president referred to everyone who works in that field at some point, from the police, medical staff, social services, or the justice system. Formation in equality would be good for some operators of the law, he also said, alluding to the last few weeks. In the last few weeks, the interrogation of judge Carretero to Elisa Mouilaá became public, and now the decision of a judge to deny, just a week ago, protection measures to Catalina. Measures she requested and that the Police requested. Catalina was murdered in the early hours of this Sunday in her home in Benalmádena by her ex-partner, by that man against whom she had requested protection from Justice and Justice did not protect her. Nor her four children who are now orphans, three of them minors. They, and she, have become this Monday the symbol of the 1,295 women who have been murdered by their partners or ex-partners since records exist, in 2003, and of the 474 minors whose fathers or stepfathers murdered their mothers, 474 only since official data has been collected, in 2013. Because before there were many others, and many others, and not just minors. Perhaps one of the most well-known, who never formed part of the statistics, is Raquel Orantes, the daughter of Ana Orantes, the woman that journalist Sandra Sabatés, host of the event at the Reina Sofía Museum, has named to tell how she put the body, put the voice so that that dark, invisible, hidden matter that was macho violence at that time, in 1997, became a social, and political matter. Raquel, her daughter, present today at the event, has said to be aware of the gratitude of thousands of women from all over the world towards her mother for that act of courage that was to speak in front of a television camera at that time. Women who are brave when they should be free. And she remembered how, institutionally, she and her siblings were alone, how the great forgotten are the children and daughters of the women murdered within the fight against violence. We were not victims, we became so afterwards, with the creation of that integral law. Some ministers I remember saying that it was an isolated incident. Now there are almost 1,300 isolated incidents. That which Raquel Orantes recalled, that lack of understanding of violence by a political representative, and her denial of it as structural violence, could have been, almost 25 years ago, understandable in a Spain where we still talked about passionate crimes and said they were family matters. Now, she added, there are still those who want to return that violence to the domestic sphere. Sánchez also made allusion to it. The unanimity with the law was a strong message to all of Spain, that we were together and together for this, and it was heard in Spain and all over the world. The first integral law against gender-based violence made history, for the good, and a month later, when it came into force, we began writing it. Unfortunately, such a broad consensus is no longer possible today, as the far-right's denialism has powerful platforms of influence and continues to inflict more pain on the victims, particularly when they speak of false accusations. Vicious rumors that spread across the internet and reach our children's mobile phones, voices that feed their professional and personal success with a fragile and toxic idea of masculinity, voices that lead many men to rely on the outdated notion of women's subjugation. However, we feminists are many more. Now, it's especially the men who, after the women's break of silence in Spain and in dozens of countries, must do the same. This silence must come to an end because it remains a deafening silence. And the law has thanked the former president, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, who sat in the front row of an auditorium filled with personalities and professionals in domestic violence. Zapatero, who had just spoken on the scene, said that the law was a political law in the deepest and noblest sense of the word, a fruit of listening, of the clamor of society. In Congress, that norm was approved on October 7, 2004, just after 12 noon. This was reported by journalist Charo Nogueira in this newspaper. The applause erupts before the result is announced. In the luminous display, 320 yes votes and 320 votes cast are read. The boxes for no and abstention are blank. A wave of jubilation and another of relief sweep through the PSOE benches, with their deputies standing up. The organic law project on integral measures to protect against gender-based violence is approved unanimously, as announced by the President of the Congress, Manuel Marín, just moments later. The former President recalled that he had promised that this would be the first law of his legislature. That commitment was the fruit of a very intense sentiment. What was changing the most in the democracy, without a doubt, was the empowerment of women to walk freely in all areas. And what could dignify us the most in the world would be to be the country that leads in equality. The greatest attack on equality is violence, stated the former president, referring to the current global political context. Machismo is one of the most historical manifestations of authoritarianism, the authoritarian reflex focuses its attention against equality because undoubtedly, there is nothing more democratizing and civilizing than equality. Feminism is not of one or another political ideology, but an advanced stage of civilization. Both the former president and the president and the Minister of Equality have pointed to the present through the Pact of State against Gender Violence, in the renewal of which they are now immersed. This same afternoon, the subcommittee in charge of that text, which could be ready today, is meeting in Congress. Sánchez has spoken of 400 new measures aimed at protecting minors, combating economic, digital violence, the trafficking of women and girls, and forced marriages. We will work to ensure that this renewal of the Pact goes ahead, because it is just and indispensable, and a priority. 20 years ago, Spain took a giant step to eradicate this violence. For those who survived and for those who suffer it today, let's fight for this cause until our last breath, Sánchez said. And Redondo, the Minister of Equality, has assured that she trusts that the vast majority of society will be able to overcome negationism. The Anniversary EventThe two-hour event, attended by several ministers and a minister, including Minister of Equality Ana Redondo, Third Vice President and Minister for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge Sara Aagesen, Minister of Inclusion, Social Security and Migrations Elma Saiz, Minister of Housing and Urban Agenda Isabel Rodríguez, and Minister of Economy, Trade and Enterprise Carlos Cuerpo, as well as former socialist ministers and ministers, but no representatives from the current government coalition, except for the former coalition's Feminismos of Podemos representative. The notable absence of representatives from the previous Equality Ministry, in whose term the Sexual Freedom Law was approved, has been the significant expansion of the 016 service and the antimaltrato wristbands, as well as the activation of the follow-up committees for macho violence murders, was notable. Two tables were set up to discuss the norm. The first, under the title It's Not Just a Law, It's a Social Demand, has been moderated by Violeta Molina, EFE's specialist journalist in equality, and on it, the Congress rapporteur deputy Mariví Monteserín María Durán de Themis has sat alongside social movements and Raquel Orantes, representing victims. The second, moderated by the event presenter Sandra Sabatés, have spoken Ana Redondo and José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero. A tribute has been paid to the women victims of macho violence through the screen on which the names of the 1,295 women murdered, officially counted so far, have succeeded, and through the voice, with the performances of Valeria Castro and Lourdes Pastor, and the poet Elsa Moreno. And 94 medals have been awarded to people who in one way or another contributed to the legislative approval of the law, from Ana Orantes, whose medal has been collected by Raquel, her daughter, to Soledad Murillo, former Secretary of Equality, Miguel Lorente, the first Government Delegate against machismo violence, or Ana María Pérez del Campo, a historical figure of the feminist movement in Spain, President of the Federation of Separated and Divorced Women since 1987. Just like the exclusive report published in this newspaper on its Saturday edition of February 8, Investigating Attorney No. 8 Juan Manuel Sánchez Ruiz is currently investigating a serious case that could be classified as human trafficking with suspected sexual exploitation of two minor sisters. The 12- and 14-year-old girls, along with their 7- and 9-year-old brothers, have already been institutionalized by the System for the Protection of Girls, Boys, and Adolescents. Although there are no arrests at this time, the Justice Department is scrutinizing two individuals closely related to the victims and a 63-year-old neighbor. In the search conducted at the latter's home on Friday, February 7, which was reported by this newspaper, multiple items were seized that could be related to the crime being investigated, such as computers, cell phones, hard drives containing child pornography, etc. At the end of January, an anonymous complaint to a state agency triggered an alert for the Police and Justice about a possible human trafficking case with the aim of sexual exploitation of two sisters in a neighborhood in the northern area of the city. Personnel from the Human Trafficking Division, under the direction of Prosecutor Sánchez Ruiz, took on the investigation in which they established the high level of vulnerability to which the four brothers were exposed, who lived with their mother and her boyfriend. At the same time, they gathered different pieces of evidence that made it plausible that the adolescents were victims of sexual exploitation in a neighboring residence. It was thus that on Friday, around 2 pm, the investigators raided the residence of a 60-year-old man who will not be identified to protect the victims. This residence had been identified in the anonymous complaint as the place where the minor victims were allegedly taken and subjected to sexual practices. On this site, a large number of items were seized and are being examined at the Valle Viejo Satellite Laboratory, including the mobile phones of the resident, the mother, and her partner, which will be reviewed shortly. On the other hand, judicial spokespeople reported that prosecutor Sánchez Ruiz is awaiting the results of the sexual abuse protocols that he ordered to be performed on the 12- and 14-year-old girls over the weekend. Additionally, he awaits the Gesell Chamber's ruling on the four siblings. Once the Public Prosecutor's representative has this information, along with the results of other testifying and expert measures, it will only be then that the case will be framed as human trafficking, and the file will be transferred to the federal Justice sphere.

During his visit to Colombia, Elvy Monzant, executive secretary of the Latin American and Caribbean Ecumenical Network for Migration, Displacement, Refuge, and Human Trafficking (CLAMOR), visited the headquarters of the Latin American and Caribbean Episcopal Council (CELAM) to participate in the Encounter of the Center for Programs and Pastoral Action Networks (CEPRAP), a space that brought together leaders from Pastoral Action Platforms, Networks, and Programs in the region. This Venezuelan layperson, committed to building bridges of solidarity that allow for the inclusion and protection of migrants, dialogued with ADN CELAM about several topics, including his participation in this encounter, the restrictive migratory consequences imposed by the government of current US President Donald Trump, and the aid work being provided by the Church in the face of this humanitarian drama. Fear and uncertainty mark the lives of migrants. Monzant referred to the deportation migration policies of US President Donald Trump and the consequences they bring to migrants who are deported. He described the chilling reality that migrants have to endure with three words: fear, uncertainty, and desperation. He showed how these new judicial deportation orders, particularly in the US, are generating fear among migrants, even those with their papers in order, who live with the fear of being caught and deported to a country that is not prepared to receive them. He agreed. Monzant observed that when regular migration routes are closed, people driven by desperation opt for more perilous routes, where they are exposed to human trafficking and exploitation groups, narco-trafficking, violence, and all types of abuse. What is going to happen is that they will migrate in even more vulnerable conditions, and they will be an easy target for the macabre trade of death that surrounds migration, he emphasized. CNN Photo.In response to the commitment to continue working, the Church said that the Clamor Network, made up of ecclesiastical organizations, continues with its commitment to continue applying the four verbs promoted by Pope Francis: to welcome, to protect, to promote, and to integrate. However, it warned that unfortunately, many of the attention works managed by the Church have been closing their doors due to lack of support from international financial entities. It hurts to see pastoral teams with closed houses while migrants outside are cold and hungry. In addition, he added that, despite economic difficulties, the 672 ecclesial communities affiliated with the Clamor Network in Latin America will continue their work by developing activities to raise funds and maintain their services. The Church will continue to be that Samaritan church that goes out to meet the wounded on the road to heal their wounds, to attend to them and accompany them in rebuilding the life that this system denied them, he emphasized. Latin American governments' responsibilityThe executive secretary underscored that, while migrating is a right that every person has, it is also a right to stay in one's own country where dignified conditions are offered. Our governments in Latin America must promote the common good and guarantee citizens' education, health, employment, and other rights, he indicated, adding that if the countries of origin continue to expel migrants, deportees will have to face an even greater drama. The role of society and the fight against xenophobia On the other hand, Monzant referred to the social rejection that migrants have to face from society. He recalled that Jesus identified himself with the migrant in the parable of the final judgment: "I was a stranger and you welcomed me, come, blessed by my father," he said. In the face of this plague, he indicated that xenophobia is a sign that breaks fraternity, justice, and peace. He observed that when a human being is discriminated against, it is as if Christ himself is being discriminated against. Therefore, we see contradictions in people who call themselves Catholic, who can go to mass every Sunday, who take communion, but then are racist, that is a total divorce between faith and life, he warned.The uncertainty about the future of migrants in the US Regarding the cancellation of the extension of the Temporary Protection Status (TPS) for Venezuelans and others, Monzant pointed out that this measure generates great uncertainty I think it's impossible for the United States to stay without the workforce that represents migrants, that's not going to happen, he said. He also noted that the US economy largely depends on migrant workers, as they are the main workforce. He added that they are waiting to know what substitute measure the Trump government will implement. Monzant urged to see migration as a phenomenon that enriches societies. Borders are a human invention. In diversity is richness, and in fraternity is the true dream of God for humanity, he noted. A meeting that united in diversity Before concluding the dialogue, the director shared his experience on his participation in the recent meeting of the Center for Studies and Projects for Pastoral Action (CEPRAP), on this he expressed his joy of having been able to share this space for dialogue among the various networks present. He emphasized the need to strengthen cooperation among ecclesiastical organizations to respond more effectively to the challenges of human mobility. It is essential that we have the possibility of establishing real networks, alliances that allow each one from our specificities to walk and contribute together to provide better service, he pointed out. Finally, he underscored the importance of pastoral training in a synodal key, promoting a Church in mission that accompanies and defends the rights of vulnerable people. The fight against organized crime in Peru has dealt a new blow with the capture of 23 members of the Tren de Aragua, in a joint operation between the Peruvian National Police (PNP) and the Office of National Security Investigations of Immigration and Customs of the United States (HSI, for its English acronym). During the intervention, carried out in the districts of San Martín de Porres and Puente Piedra, 120 people were rescued who were victims of sexual and labor exploitation, including three minors. The authorities have indicated that the victims will receive assistance from the State, while the minors were transferred to the Special Protection Unit of the Ministry of Women. According to Redacción EC for El Comercio, General Aldo Ávila Novoa, head of the PNP's Directorate Against Human Trafficking and Illicit Migrant Trafficking, stated that the Tren de Aragua is completely dismantled in Peru. All leaders have fallen. The organization, as such, has been dismantled, and its main leaders are serving prison sentences in Challapalca, Ávila stated. Operations against the Tren de Aragua and its remnants Despite the capture of its leaders, the Peruvian National Police acknowledges that remnants of the Tren de Aragua continue operating in the country, adapting and reorganizing under new criminal structures. Right now, we are attacking the remaining members of this organization. We have them mapped out and are developing joint operations for their capture, the general Ávila specified. Groups such as Los Hijos de Dios and El Antitren have emerged as factions of the mother organization, maintaining illicit activities in different regions of Peru. The support of HSI has been fundamental in the fight against the Aragua Train, providing access to advanced technology and strategic intelligence that have allowed for the coordination of operations with other countries where the criminal network remains active, including Ecuador, Colombia, Chile, Panama, Spain, and the United States. In addition to HSI support, the PNP also works hand-in-hand with Interpol and Europol to locate the leaders who still operate abroad. Among the main leaders of the organization, identified and sought internationally, are Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, alias Niño Guerrero. Yohan José Romero, alias Johan Petrica. Larry Álvarez Núñez, alias Larry Changa. The Aragua Train in Peru: A history of a criminal network Since its arrival in Peru in 2018, the Aragua Train has diversified its criminal operations, adapting to the reality of each country in which it has operated. In the Peruvian territory, the organization focused on human trafficking, extortion, and sicariato, taking advantage of the increase in Venezuelan migration in recent years. The modus operandi of the Aragua Train in Peru has been replicated in other countries in the region, consolidating a transnational criminal structure. In the country, the criminal group established a sex trafficking network in Lima, Trujillo, Arequipa, and other cities, kidnapping women under threats and forcing them to work in clandestine brothels. Additionally, their link to drug trafficking mafias, sicariato, and protection money from merchants and transporters has been documented, generating an atmosphere of insecurity in various areas of the country. Impact of the capture of the leaders of organized crime The arrest of the main leaders of the Aragua Train in Peru represents a hard blow to the organization, but authorities have warned that the fight against their remnants has not yet ended. The criminals who are still operating have changed their strategy, hiding their presence within other gangs or fragmenting into small groups that continue to commit crimes. We know that there are still criminal cells operating in different regions of the country. We continue working constantly to eradicate them completely, police sources said. The mega-operation in San Martín de Porres and Puente Piedra has allowed the PNP to identify new routes of human trafficking and establish a plan to dismantle the remaining groups that continue to be active in the country. International cooperation a key factor in the fight against the Aragua Train International support from agencies such as HSI, Interpol, and Europol has been crucial in coordinating actions against the Aragua Train. Thanks to international cooperation, key leaders have been captured in other countries, weakening the organization's structure in the region. The Peruvian National Police has requested that mechanisms for information exchange and extradition of criminals be reinforced with neighboring countries to prevent criminals from continuing to operate from abroad. What's next in the fight against organized crime in Peru While authorities have achieved significant advances in the fight against the Aragua Train, experts warn that the battle against organized crime is a constant process that requires more stringent security measures, strengthening of the judicial system, and effective border control. The capture of the leaders of the organization in Peru is an important step, but the PNP and security agencies must continue with operations to dismantle the remaining remnants and prevent other gangs from taking their place. The fight against organized crime in the country continues, and cooperation between national and international security forces will be key to ensuring the safety of the population.
