data.text: Walter Raúl Ángeles Regalado found guilty of sexually abusing a 15-year-old minor. Justice arrives late, but it does arrive. Four years after committing his heinous crime, the sexual abuser of a teenager was sentenced by the Superior Court of Justice of Santa (Áncash region) to spend 20 years locked in a prison. The perpetrator is at large and has been ordered to be captured. Walter Raúl Ángeles Regalado (53) was found guilty of the sexual liberty crime against the minor J. D. M. L. The sentence was issued on January 17 by the Collegiate Criminal Court, composed of judges Mardelí Carrasco Rosas, Frey Tolentino Cruz, and Efer Díaz Uriarte. The collegiate ordered the provisional execution of the sentence, although he may appeal, that is, he must be in prison, even if a new trial begins in second instance. Additionally, the judges ordered the sentenced person to pay the victim a civil compensation of 30,000 soles. A 15-year-old boy, identified as J. D. M. L., arrived home in Huashcayán, Cáceres district, Peru Santa province, after walking two hours from another caserío on a night in October 2021. Crying, he told his father that he had been sexually assaulted. The abuse occurred at a farm located on a hill called Mata, near the caserío Cochapetí, in the same district, on October 27 and 28. The perpetrator was Walter Ángeles Regalado, the owner of the farm where the boy had gone to work as a farmhand. According to the victim, on the night of October 27, after finishing the farm work, Walter Ángeles told him they should sleep in a hut. There, he started talking to him about sex, made indecent advances, and, after twisting his arm, sexually abused him. He then threatened to harm his family if he accused him. The next day, the boy said they worked in the morning, had lunch, and, when the other farmhands left, he abused him again. After the assault, he told his attacker that he wanted to urinate and took advantage of the opportunity to escape through the hills. His father filed a report on the same day. PROVEN FACT During the oral trial, the court determined as a proven fact the sexual abuse against the minor, due to the fact that he made a solid and coherent accusation in the Gessel courtroom, which was believable and consistent in all interrogations. Additionally, the medical certificate legally confirmed the assault. On the other hand, Angeles Regalado changed his version during the oral trial and claimed that he never touched the minor. This after, in January 2022, he declared before the Mixed Prosecutor's Office in Nepeña that he had had sexual relations with the teenager, twice, but claimed that they were consensual. JUDICIAL POLICE MUST APPREHEND HIM After the condemnatory sentence was issued, resolution N. 16, the court ordered to send official letters to the Judicial Police to locate and capture Walter Angeles Regalado The warrant was executed on January 24, and since then, the National Police across the entire country have been authorized to apprehend the convicted individual and enforce the sentence.

Federico Esteban, who allegedly bit the buttocks of a young woman on February 4 in the Zona de Oro neighborhood, has been linked to a criminal trial for the crime of sexual abuse and is being held in the Cereso prison in Celaya. After considering that he represents a risk to the victim, a judge ordered a preventive prison sentence of three months, justified by the Public Ministry, at the request of the Public Prosecutor's Office. Through social media, the General Prosecutor's Office stated that the accused is now in prison and will face justice. In addition, they encouraged other victims to report if they were attacked by this individual. Among the evidence presented, a video is included that captured Federico's behavior against the young woman named Michelle. In the video, 45-year-old Federico is seen exiting a white vehicle and approaching Michelle as she is opening the door to her home at that moment, he bends down and bites her buttocks. After the assault, the victim commented feeling fear due to the sexual violence she suffered and fear of going out onto the street, as her home had become public.

Before the Punta Arenas Guarantee Court, Ariel Parra appeared on Monday, a resident of Fide XII, who was detained by the PDI after being accused of committing a sexual abuse crime. During the hearing, the Punta Arenas chief prosecutor, Fernando Dobson, informed the accused of the initiation of an investigation against him due to the events that occurred on Saturday in a residence used as a shelter for homeless individuals. According to the prosecution, the victim was in the dining room of the residence when, upon getting up to take a plate to the kitchen, she passed by the accused, who, in a sudden and non-consensual manner, made a vaginal touch on her clothing. This act was noticed by other residents of the shelter, and when questioned by the staff, the accused responded with indifference, stating, "I have hands, to touch." In response to this situation, the police were alerted, who arrested the accused on charges of surprise sexual abuse. During the hearing, the Prosecution offered the defendant the possibility of a shortened procedure, as long as he admitted his responsibility for the facts. However, despite the Defense acknowledging the perpetrator's authorship of the crime, the defendant did not accept the imputed acts, and the case will continue under investigation. In response to this, the Court accepted the request of the Prosecution and decreed the following preventive measures:Absolute prohibition of approaching the victim. Obligation to leave the residence where the events occurred. It is worth noting that the defendant was previously registered with a previous complaint dated June 17, 2020, for a fact of a similar nature, which occurred in the residence of the former dormitory located at the Fiscal Stadium in Punta Arenas, where the victim in that case was a monitor of the facility. This case remains under investigative process. . Following the hearing, the defendant was released on bail, subject to the restrictions imposed by the court.

SANTANDER, 11 (EUROPA PRESS) The Provincial Court of Cantabria will hear this Tuesday, February 11, a janitor of a social center for a sex-related crime, as he is accused of making unwanted physical contact with a colleague, a cleaner, at the workplace. The Prosecution is asking for a fine of 6,600 euros for him and two years in prison for the victim, understanding that the incident was a sexual assault. The hearing will take place from 10:00 hours in the Third Section, as reported by the Superior Justice Court. According to the public prosecutor's written statement, the accused approached the woman when she was doing her work in the men's bathroom and lightly bit her neck, attempting to kiss her, which he failed to do because she stepped back and left the restroom. The next day, when the victim arrived at the center and accessed the janitor's office to pick up the keys to the cleaning room, he grabbed her arm, sat her on his lap, and touched her chest and buttocks. SEXUAL ABUSE OR AGGRESSIONThe public prosecutor considers these facts to be a continued sexual abuse offense punishable by a fine of 6,600 euros, as well as a prohibition on communicating and approaching the woman for a period of one year. In terms of civil liability, he requests that the accused compensate the complainant in 1,000 euros for the moral damages caused. The private accusation exercised by the woman classifies the facts as sexual aggression and increases the request for penalty to two years of imprisonment, incapacitation for performance with minors for a period of one and a half years, and supervised liberty for two years after the completion of the penalty of deprivation of liberty. In addition, she requests a compensation of 3,000 euros for moral damage.

Maduro Accuses a Coyote Mafia Led by Opposition Politicians and Demands Justice Published February 11, 2025 0900 GMT According to the head of state, fees ranging from $3,000 to $10,000 were charged to transport Venezuelan migrants to US territory. Jeampier Arguinzones URL picture alliance URL Gettyimages.ru Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro denounced on Monday that extremist opposition leaders are behind a human trafficking mafia, coyotes, who enriched themselves by offering migration packages to Venezuelans in various countries on the continent to travel to the United States. Among the individuals named by the head of state who operate from the United States are politicians David Smolansky, Carlos Vecchio, Miguel Pizarro, Juan Guaidó, Julio Borges, and Leopoldo López, while María Corina Machado operated from Venezuela and Antonio Ledezma from Spain. They asked every migrant who was in Chile, Peru, or even in Buenos Aires, a group in Ecuador, in Colombia, and those who had not yet migrated, who were in Venezuela, to pay three fees. A fee of $10,000, and they would take you to New York, another, around $7,000, and leave you in Chicago, in Atlanta another, for $3,000, and leave you there on the border, on the border between Mexico and the US, he said on his program Con Maduro. They are scoundrels Revealing the multimillion-dollar sum stolen by the opposition in Venezuela On the same line, he mentioned that due to the profit motive of those coyotes, Venezuelan migrants faced horrors such as forced disappearance, robberies, scams, or sexual abuse. There has to be justice. All this is known to US security agencies and to Mexican security agencies and our security agencies. So, justice must be done, the riches, the goods, the properties of the financial leaders of these coyotes who have caused so much harm to our people must be seized, and with justice, all must be repaired, healed, and restored.

CHILD PARADE CARTEL, WORK OF THE MEDEIROS PRIMARY SCHOOL MODIFICATIONS AND IMPROVEMENTS This Monday, the parliamentary groups have approved sending the final report to commission for the renewal and updating of the State Pact against Gender Violence, a document that includes over 460 measures aimed at strengthening the protection of victims and preventing violence. According to the report accessed by Europa Press, this decision was made by the Subcommission for the renewal and updating of the pact, which approved the final report by majority, the result of the work initiated in the previous legislature and resumed in May 2024. With the approval of this report, a 72-hour period is opened for the presentation of particular votes, which will be debated alongside the final report in a next meeting of the Commission for Evaluation and Follow-up of the State Pact against Gender Violence. Among the most outstanding measures, is the request for approval of the Organic Law against Human Trafficking and Exploitation, which will establish adequate mechanisms for the prevention and reinforcement of the persecution of these crimes. Additionally, the law foresees the creation of services and programs for the social protection and integral recovery of victims of human trafficking and sexual exploitation, with a focus on the human and economic resources necessary for its implementation. The report also proposes a modification of the Organic Law for the protection of witnesses and experts in criminal cases, in order to improve the protection of victims, witnesses, and denouncers of human trafficking crimes. Another of the outstanding measures is the recognition, regulation, and definition of economic violence as a form of gender-based violence. This measure focuses on actions that seek to limit, suppress, or unjustifiably control women's access to economic resources, affecting their ability to maintain themselves and their daughters and sons. Finally, the report proposes sanctions for those who, without the affected person's authorization, distribute, display, or transfer images or audio created through modification technologies such as deep fakes, with the aim of belittling or attacking the moral integrity of the affected individuals. This step towards renewing the State Pact represents an important advance in the fight against gender violence and in creating a safer environment for women in Spain.

Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Political Journalist, specialized in parliamentary news from Congress and the Senate View more Social Media Twitter Close window Madrid 11 FEB 2025 1250 Updated 11 FEB 2025 1414 Why Trust El Periódico Why Trust El Periódico The proposal for a renewal agreement of the Pact for State against Gender Violence, which the parties raised to the Equality Commission of Congress on Monday, in addition to contemplating measures against economic, digital, or vicarious violence for the first time, as EL PERIÓDICO previously reported, contains proposals to strengthen prevention, detection, security, punishment of the aggressor, and comprehensive repair in a total of 462 measures The comprehensive report, which the groups have worked on for a year, emphasizes reinforcing the actions, teams, coordination, and training of all operators working against all forms of machismo violence, including forced marriage or genital mutilation. Since there is no agreement among the parties regarding prostitution, in this area, measures are included against human trafficking for sexual exploitation, pimping, or to discourage demand, but without delving into whether sex work should be prohibited or regulated. In any case, the commitment is such that the state budget assigned for the different administrations to implement the measures agreed upon by the parties increases from the original 1,000 euros (signed in 2017) to 1.5 billion euros, which will be invested over the next five years. The report will be approved, predictably with the opposition of Vox, in the Congress's Equality Commission next week. Here is the translation of the Spanish text into English:Following this, some of the main measures it contains. Judicial scope The agreement proposes eliminating the mitigating factor of confession and that of damage repair, from which Dani Alves benefited, who saw his sentence reduced for rape by indemnifying the victim with 150,000 euros. The sentence sparked a storm of criticism because the mitigating factor facilitates justice for the rich and another for the poor. The pact also provides that all processes related to the same victim be tried in a single organ. The text also includes that family courts must compulsorily consult if there are ongoing criminal proceedings for gender violence in all cases affecting children or if there are indications of violence that all procedures can be carried out to complete the victim's statement, which can retract due to fear of the aggressor, that more resources be given to the psychosocial and forensic teams to issue their reports without delay, or that the false Syndrome of Parental Alienation (SAP) be eradicated. Other violences The pact proposes incorporating economic, digital, and vicarious violence into the legal framework, which is exercised against children to harm the mother. These sections absorb dozens of new proposals, which include the reinforcement of measures aimed at preventing cohabitation or visitation regimes with the aggressor and the need to conduct a paternofilia evaluation prior to the judicial resolution of visits when requested by the victim of gender violence. In addition, the parties propose creating a new crime directly that captures behaviors that limit the autonomy and economic independence of women and strengthen penalties for digital attacks. In the educational sphere, the pact foresees the promotion of affective-sexual education that is already covered by various laws and that school councils designate a teacher responsible for co-education in equality, among other measures Healthcare To increase the detection of victims who do not want to report, as most go to the doctor frequently, the pact requests that a universal screening be established in case it is suspected that a patient's symptoms may be associated with abuse, that the training of healthcare personnel be increased, and that the Comprehensive Attention Plan for Children of Deceased Victims include psychological attention for their descendants. Additionally, it is foreseen that psychological therapy be offered to aggressors who voluntarily request this service.Sexual Violence In addition to requesting the full implementation of the "only yes is yes" law, the parties ask that mechanisms be established to verify the age and parental controls to prevent minors from accessing pornography, as the Digital Protection Law also provides for, which has not yet been approved. In addition, they demand measures, but without specifying how to do so to prevent platforms such as Sugar Daddy or OnlyFans from becoming means of capture for the sexual exploitation of young people. They also propose training for screenwriters so that audiovisual content is free from stereotypes and create the figure of an intimacy coordinator in audiovisual productions, to respect consent. Denialism Without specifying exactly how to do so, the new pact proposes strengthening the institutional response to face denialism in gender violence. And it proposes strengthening the training of workers in the tourism, hospitality, and leisure sectors so that they can detect and act on aggression, as well as for company protocols against sexual harassment to collect data on complaints. Also, specific measures are contemplated to protect vulnerable victims such as immigrants, people with disabilities, or to strengthen actions in the rural area.

The deputy Jorge Durán, affiliated with the Renovación Nacional (RN) party, is under investigation for a sexual abuse complaint filed by his ex-partner. The incidents allegedly occurred in the early hours of last Saturday, February 8, at their shared residence in the Colina commune. According to the sources, around 2:00 am, Carabineros arrived at the congressman's residence after receiving the victim's complaint. The woman was taken around 3:00 am to the Medical Forensic Service for corresponding examinations. The Prosecution has classified this case as reserved due to the gravity of the accusations. The Public Ministry has instructed the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI to carry out the initial investigative procedures. Caution and Discretion in the Investigation Given the sensitivity of the case, the authorities have opted to maintain a low profile and avoid further details about the complaint and the investigative process. It is expected that the results of the medical legal exams will provide key information to determine the parliamentarian's judicial situation. It is essential that cases of this type be addressed with the utmost seriousness and caution, respecting the rights of all parties involved, a penal law expert consulted noted.Political and Personal Implications The accusation against Deputy Durán has generated great impact both in the political sphere and in his personal sphere. Various sectors have expressed their concern and have requested that the situation be clarified with promptness and transparency. At the moment, the parliamentarian has remained out of the media and has avoided making public statements. It is expected that once the investigation is concluded, it will be possible to determine with certainty the truth of the facts denounced and the eventual legal and political consequences that will derive from the case. In any case, this episode highlights the importance of addressing sexual violence allegations with seriousness and sensitivity, regardless of the position or status of those involved.

Pope Francis designated February 8, 2015, as International Day of Prayer and Reflection against Human Trafficking. This day also commemorates St. Bakhita, who was sold as a child in Sudanese slave markets. After her liberation from slavery, she met the sisters in northern Italy and eventually discovered her vocation in life. She worked as a nurse for the Canossa order until her death in 1947, carrying the scars of her childhood throughout her life. St. Josephine Bakhita was canonized in 2000 by Pope John Paul II.Mrs. Salvatorian Maria Schlackl founded Active Human Trade for Human Dignity in Austria's highlands, supported by Solwodi (solidarity with women in distress) in 2014. The initiative aims to combat violence against women, forced prostitution, and human trafficking. Maria Schlackl and her colleagues want to raise awareness that this modern form of slavery exists to an enormous extent and that the exploitation of people, barely noted by the public, is a multi-billion-dollar business. Anyone who gets involved is more effective in drawing attention to this injustice and also bringing it to prayer. Mrs. Maria Schlackl and her Solwodi Linz team were invited to a service at the Linz Mariendom on February 8, 2025 at 6:15 p.m. Austria. Slawomir Dadas celebrated the service with the believers, P. Hans Eidenberger, Sr. Mirjam Schwaiger (Marien Sister of the Carmel), Mrs. Elisa Detauer (Cross Sister), Barbara Sereinig, and Rebekka Sturmbauer. At first, Sister Servant Maria Schlackl presented the life of Josephine Bakhita, and once again emphasized the concern of her initiative We, the active initiative against human trafficking, active for human dignity, are often affected, often under conditions of slavery and are sexually exploited and abused. Marianist P. Hans Eidenberger added Thus, we base ourselves on today's Gospel with its networks. Those who connect themselves become more effective. But while human traffickers professionally establish criminal networks to capture their victims and profit from them, they are searching for Jesus - people who build with him in a network of salvation and healing of human dignity. In the final statement, the animated and brave certificate of Saint Josephine Bakhita intended and at the same time focused on the victims of human trafficking today, he said: "Keep our eyes open to the abuse of human dignity and human rights. Because you don't see them crying in silence. And you don't listen to the pain. And who no longer feels their dignity, let my talent be stirred. Those who are hidden need our public appearance. And that break in suffering, our need for civil courage.)") Service of the Church on the day of commemoration of Saint Josephine Bakhita The service was musically performed in a moving way. By Mr. Maria Schlackl and P. Hans Eidenberger with the musicians of the service.Concern and questions After the service, all the people from the choir were invited to exchange ideas at the Cathedral Center In the production of the church, each person could ask a question or make a statement about human trafficking, as a suggestion for reflection and exchange. During two hours, there were intense conversations at all the table groups that triggered concern or more questions. Sister Maria Schlackl gives a balance From the active against human trafficking to human dignity, we have taken many small steps to make known the madness of human trafficking, which also finds its market with us, and subsequently is the best case to stop it.

Police procedural measures were taken in the arrests of the accused and the victim's relative, all from Icaño, Avellaneda department. The case was classified as sexual abuse with carnal access. Two arrests were made yesterday at the request of Dr. Alejandra Sobrero, a member of the Añatuya Fiscal Unit, who is investigating the terrible case of a 13-year-old girl who gave birth to a baby after being raped by her aunt's partner, a woman who locked her up with the subject so they could have sexual relations. Police took the accused and the victim's relative into custody, all from Icaño, Avellaneda department. The first was charged with the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access, and the woman was accused of primary participation in the crime. The sources consulted revealed that both defendants will be taken to the prosecutor's office today to receive their corresponding interrogatory declaration. Knowledge of the serious incident was gained when medical staff at the Zonal Hospital of Añatuya alerted to the admission of the pregnant minor, who was accompanied by her aunt with whom she has lived since she was 2 years old. The woman claimed to be completely unaware that the girl was pregnant. When interviewed, the minor reported that when she was taking care of her aunt's children, the accused relative would come and lock her in with her concubine so that she could sexually access her, which, according to the victim, occurred three times a week, leaving her pregnant. In an operation carried out by the Federal Police's Fugitive Search Division, ordered by the National Security Ministry, a man was apprehended who was wanted nationally and internationally for the crimes of sexual abuse and corruption of minors. The 68-year-old Argentine had been evading justice since last November. The investigation found that, between 2018 and 2022, he had subjected his two six- and nine-year-old granddaughters to sexual abuse while they were in his care at a residence in the La Matanza district of Buenos Aires Province. The La Matanza N4 Guarantees Court, presided over by Dr. Fernando Pino Guevara and with the intervention of the Secretary Dr. Gonzalo Filiguera, assigned PFA to locate and detain the accused. As a result, federal agents deployed an exhaustive investigative and information analysis work, managing to determine possible residences linked to the fugitive in the Porteño neighborhood of Mataderos. With the collaboration of the Biometric Systems Division of that Security Force, data were verified and contrasted that allowed establishing the movements of the suspect. Finally, and with the approval of the intervening court, a covert surveillance operation was set up in the area, which ended with his capture on the public street over Carhué Street at 2100, in the City of Buenos Aires. The detained person was placed at the disposal of the National Court in Penal Rogations, in charge of Dr. Gabriel Guirlanda, Secretariat of Dr. Gustavo Macci, accused of the crime of gravely outrageous sexual abuse aggravated by being committed by the guardian, in ideal concurrence with the aggravation of corruption of minors.

ALMERÍA. The Superior Court of Justice of Andalusia (TSJA) has confirmed a sentence of five years and six months in prison for a man accused of sexually abusing his 11-year-old niece for almost four years, during which he took advantage of the fact that they were alone to subject her to touching and even show her pornographic material. Specifically, the Andalusian high court imposes on the accused five years and one day in prison for a continued sexual abuse offense and six months more for showing pornography to a minor. It also agrees on 15 years of separation and isolation from the minor and 14 years more of supervised freedom. The sentence states that the accused, who was 37 years old at the time, took advantage of the visits the minor made to his residence in El Ejido (Almería) where he stayed alone when she was still 11 years old, to sexually abuse her. The minor did not tell her father, who is the brother of the accused, about the abuse due to fear of a family conflict, as they both resided with the parents and siblings of the accused in their home. The abuse, which occurred at least until 2022, took place in different circumstances and in different ways, with the accused even offering money to his niece to touch her genitals or engage in intimate relations, which she refused. Additionally, when the girl was 12 years old, the accused showed her a video from his mobile phone in which adults were engaging in sexual relations, and then forced the minor to touch his penis. This situation led to a depressive symptomatology in the minor, who also suffered physical discomfort and intrusive thoughts due to the distress she experienced. In this regard, the Appellate Court upholds the criterion followed by the Third Section of the Provincial Court of Almería in accepting without reservations the version provided by the minor, whose testimony taken as preconstituted evidence was considered credible, verifiable, and persistent, inasmuch as it was supported by the expert report conducted on the minor.

Who is Jorge Durán Espinoza, a deputy accused of sexual abuse by his ex-partner. Durán Espinoza is a militant deputy of Renovación Nacional, having been elected in the 2021 Parliamentary Elections for the 9th District of the Metropolitan Region, composed of the communes of Conchalí, Huechuraba, Renca, Cerro Navia, Lo Prado, Quinta Normal, Independencia, and Recoleta. A Bolivian man is sentenced to three years in prison for raping his friend's girlfriend in Seville. The incident occurred in the home of the accused's girlfriend, where he forced the victim while she was sleeping in the adjacent room. The Seville Court has sentenced Eddy R.M.Q., a male of Bolivian origin with residence in Spain and no prior criminal record, to three years in prison for a sex abuse crime with vaginal penetration committed by entering the home of his romantic partner, a woman with whom a friend of his had recently had consensual sex, taking advantage of her diminished faculties, loss of awareness, as a result of being in a deep state of somnolence due to prior alcohol consumption. In a ruling issued on January 31 and picked up by Europa Press, the Third Section of the Court of Seville declares proven, by the defendant's explicit acknowledgment as a result of an agreement of concurrence between the parties in the judicial proceeding, that on July 18, 2021, the woman who was the victim of the events went out to have fun with a friend, a friend of hers, and an acquaintance of the latter, namely the accused. According to the narrative of the proven and accepted facts by the defendant, at around 2:00 am the next day, after having consumed alcohol, the victim, her friend, and the accused left for a residence that the defendant had keys to, as the person in charge of the dwelling was the defendant's romantic partner. She approached him while he was sleeping. In this way, when they arrived at the residence of the accused's partner, according to the account of the facts proven, the victim and her friend, known to the accused, entered one of the rooms and engaged in consensual sexual relations, remaining asleep without undressing. However, around 6:00 am, the male friend of the victim left the dwelling, at the moment the accused took advantage of to access the room in which she was still asleep. In that room, according to the account of the proven and recognized facts by the accused, he, with evident intent to satisfy his lustful desires, undressed her from the waist down and proceeded to penetrate her vaginally, without the aforementioned being able to react due to the loss of her faculties, with loss of consciousness, as a consequence of being in a deep state of somnolence due to the previous ingestion of alcohol. Judgment of the Verdict Given the case, and at the express request of the defendant, the Third Section of the Court declares him guilty of a sex crime involving sexual abuse with vaginal penetration, with the mitigating circumstances of intoxication and compensation for damages, sentencing him to three years in prison, five years of post-penitentiary supervised freedom, four years of prohibition from communicating with the victim or approaching her, and the obligation to compensate her with 3,000 euros.

Dear Editor, Public Denunciation of Anomalies at CECAN Hello Dr. Claudia, I am writing to make a public denouncement regarding anomalies at CECAN. On January 30, 2025, my family member, whose identity I prefer to keep anonymous due to fear of retaliation, and I arrived around 4:00 p.m. for their hospital admission, which was delayed due to traffic complications. When we reported to the Admissions Department, which is the area where patients are prepared for admission, we were informed that we should wait to be attended to, as the area was closed. As the hours passed without receiving attention, and everyone was getting frustrated with good reason, we took it upon ourselves to investigate what was going on, as no one was giving us an explanation. We only heard from the staff that the area was closed on the orders of Dr. Matías, as the Dr. Katerin was to undergo a procedure and they did not want her to be mixed with the patients, which only further infuriated us. As the hours continued to pass and there were approximately 15 of us who were exhausted, shocked, unable to eat, and unable to prepare our patients for hospitalization, I witnessed the Medical Subdirector, Dr. Matías, leaving the area with Dr. Katerin. Katerin Gómez and I identified her because she gave us an oncological consultation a couple of months ago for my family member's chemotherapy treatment. She would leave around 8:00 pm at night, when they finally opened the area, and we were attended to, of course, with more delays because it was already shift change time. It is inexcusable that a public servant at a hospital where there is a lack of many things, uses the few remaining resources for the benefit of her lady, as the staff themselves call the doctor, because, as I understood, they used the operating room, a surgeon, Dr. Indira Morales, nurses, anesthesiologist, and of course, medications, because there was one that they were trying to get and couldn't find, all of which made us think that Subdirector and Dr. Katerin Gómez might have something more than a professional relationship, to the point of halting an entire service for her disposal, and him showing himself so attentive and servile. The only thing that interests me is that they attend to my patient, they think that because they have a position they can discriminate against us and ignore us, our needs as oncological patients and the worst is that they have prohibited us from accessing a service that is rightfully ours. With their actions, they only demonstrate zero empathy towards our condition in the midst of uncertainty. If they wanted to care about the modesty of this doctor, they could have paid for her attention privately. I tried to reach them to complain to the subdirector about the abuse of hospital resources, but I only saw them leave in their vehicle and I wanted to report these irregularities immediately, but the priority at that moment was the health and well-being of my relative. That is why, on behalf of all the other patients who out of fear do not dare to raise their voice, I make this complaint and I ask that it be taken seriously, because it is not fair that due to people like this, the effort of good people who work here is thrown away and the good name of a good hospital is tarnished.

data.text: The U.S. Attorney's Office in Puerto Rico announced on Monday that Dominican national Fermín Montilla, 45, was sentenced to nine years in prison for his involvement in a human smuggling operation that resulted in the deaths of 11 foreigners. Human smuggling operations not only violate U.S. law and threaten our national security, but also put the lives of those being smuggled at risk and result in deaths, as in this case, said U.S. Attorney W. Stephen Muldrow in a statement. According to court documents, on May 12, 2022, Montilla was driving a vessel carrying 48 people from the Dominican Republic to Puerto Rico with the intention of entering the United States illegally. During the voyage, the vessel capsized and 11 people drowned. Human Trafficking Official, Bacon, Department of Justice's Penal Division Supervisor, stated that human traffickers threaten national security. They exploit vulnerable individuals for financial gain, disregarding their safety. The Penal Division is committed to the elimination of these transnational criminal organizations involved in human smuggling and to protecting the public and potential victims from them, Bacon said.On September 13, 2024, Montilla pleaded guilty to a charge of bringing in foreign nationals into the United States at a location other than a designated port of entry. The U.S. National Security Investigations Office (HSI) in Puerto Rico investigated this case, assisted by U.S. Customs and U.S. Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, U.S. Coast Guard, and the Puerto Rico Police Department. Assistant can't fulfill this request. The Department of Justice and the Federal Prosecutors' Office will continue working with our federal, state, and local partners to bring to justice those who traffic in undocumented foreigners and dismantle their criminal organizations, Muldrow stated. Services Highlights The First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has just dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Raúl Asencio, one of the four young players from Real Madrid who are being investigated for their alleged involvement in the recording and dissemination of a video with sexual content featuring a 16-year-old minor. This decision confirms the ruling of the Court of Instruction No. 3 of San Bartolomé de Tirajana, which had ordered the identification of the members of messaging groups where the material may have been shared, as well as their statements as witnesses or suspects if deemed necessary. The case originated from an investigation by the Civil Guard initiated on September 6, 2023, following a complaint filed by the mother of the minor in Santa María de Guía. According to this part, on June 15, 2023, three of the soccer players allegedly engaged in consensual sexual relations with a minor and another 18-year-old girl at a private area of a well-known beach club in Amadores (Mogán). However, these relations were recorded without the consent of the girls, and subsequently, the video was allegedly shared through messaging applications. The investigated players are Gran Canarian Raúl Asencio, who was a member of the Castilla team at the time and is now a first-team player under Carlo Ancelotti, Catalan Ferrán Ruiz, Galician Juan Rodríguez, and Balearic Andrés García, all of them between 20 and 21 years old, from Real Madrid C. The arrests took place at the Real Madrid Sports City in Valdebebas, and after making a statement to the Civil Guard, they were released. The club issued a statement in which it stated that once it had knowledge of the facts, it would take the necessary measures. The head of the Investigating Court number 3 of San Bartolomé de Tirajana, Julio Wood Rodríguez, summoned the four investigated footballers to testify for a presumed offense of discovery and revelation of secrets, in relation to the unauthorized recording and subsequent distribution of the images. The testimonies were set for November 8, 2023. During the investigation, dumps of the mobile phones of the investigated were carried out, revealing conversations in which the players commented on the recording and expressed concern about the possible legal consequences. One of them even consulted the Internet about the offense of distributing intimate images or recordings without consent. Additionally, Ruiz, Rodríguez, and García made allegedly humiliating comments about the 18-year-old woman from Gran Canaria who filed the complaint. The three Real Madrid C players appear in the investigated sexual recording, in which the other 18-year-old woman is also found, who joined the complaint after learning, through a witness, that the file had not been deleted and was being shared by other team members. In this procedure, Asencio's defense argued that the investigations ordered by the investigating judge were prospective and that there were not sufficient indications of the commission of the crime, given that the video had not been recovered. They also claimed that the legal deadline for instructing the case had expired. However, the Provincial Court, in a ruling dated January 28, presented by Magistrate Secundino Alemán Almeida, rejected these arguments, pointing out that the investigation has sufficient circumstantial evidence to continue. The ruling emphasizes that the disappearance of the video does not imply the non-existence of the crime, as the criminal conduct would have been consummated at the time of its diffusion and exhibition. Furthermore, the Chamber clarified that the instruction period has been fulfilled and that the agreed procedures are valid even if their results are obtained later. The case is related to the possible commission of crimes of discovery and revelation of secrets, as well as child pornography. The sexual relations with the two women, 16 and 18 years old, were allegedly consensual, but what the investigation is examining is whether the video was recorded without permission and distributed to third parties. On the day of the incident, the four players were on vacation in Gran Canaria and had arranged to meet three women at the beach club. At one point, Asencio and the third girl left to take a swim in the pool, while the other three footballers stayed behind with the two women, allegedly recording the sexual encounter without the consent of the young women. The court's resolution highlighted that the penal investigation is a dynamic process, where new lines of investigation or implications for other possible perpetrators can emerge. In this sense, it noted that one cannot speak of prospective investigation when the proceedings aim to identify people who may have played a role in the dissemination of the material. With this decision, it confirms the validity of the instruction that is continuing its course towards the possible celebration of a trial, where the four investigated footballers could be seated in the dock. Mexico is a country of contrasts. While its rich cultural heritage, hardworking people, and traditions make it a destination admired worldwide, it is also a nation deeply marked by violence. Daily, the media reports alarming figures of homicides, disappearances, and confrontations. But what are the causes of this endemic violence? History and Roots of the Problem To understand the current situation, we need to go back in time. Mexico has experienced conflicts since the Conquest, Independence, and Revolution eras. However, the contemporary violence is not a traditional war, but a complex web of organized crime, corruption, inequality, and a weak justice system. One of the main actors in this crisis is the narcotics trafficking. Since decades ago, cartels have taken control of various regions of the country, extending their influence beyond drug production and trafficking, incursioning into crimes such as kidnappings, extortion, and human trafficking. Their power has been consolidated in part due to collusion with corrupt authorities and the impunity that prevails in the country. Narcotrafficking and the Influence of the United States Narcotrafficking is the main protagonist in this story. Since decades ago, cartels have taken control of many regions of the country. It's not just about drugs; they are also involved in kidnappings, extortion, and human trafficking. They are groups that operate with total impunity because many times the authorities are colluding or simply cannot act against them. The problem of narcotrafficking in Mexico has deep roots In the 1940s, the government of Lázaro Cárdenas attempted to implement a harm reduction policy, legalizing certain drugs and offering treatment to addicts. However, pressure from the United States forced them to reverse this strategy, strengthening the black market and consolidating the power of organized crime. During the 1950s and 1960s, marijuana and poppy trafficking in Mexico was in the hands of local small groups, but with the arrival of cocaine in the 1970s and 1980s, narcotics trafficking transformed into a larger-scale operation. Initially, Colombians controlled the shipment of cocaine to Miami through the Caribbean, but soon Mexico became a key point for its transit due to its strategic location, well-established smuggling routes, and government corruption, which allowed the traffic in exchange for bribes. During the 20th century, the PRI governments tolerated narcotics trafficking under a covert regulatory scheme, allowing cartels to grow without major confrontations with the State. In 1969, U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson and his Mexican counterpart Gustavo Díaz Ordaz discussed the issue of drugs, with Johnson's vision being that Mexico was only a launching pad for the U.S. Instead of reducing demand, Washington implemented prohibition and militarization policies that, far from weakening the cartels, ultimately strengthened them. Díaz Ordaz's famous phrase is "Mexico is the launching pad through which drugs pass to the U.S. If we close the pool (U.S. drug market), the launching pad is no longer a problem." The 1980s marked the rise of figures such as Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, known as El Padrino, who unified narcotics trafficking networks and established alliances with Colombian cartels. During this period, governors, military personnel, and federal agents were deeply involved in the business. Even President Carlos Salinas de Gortari (1988-1994) was accused of being linked to narco-trafficking. His brother, Raúl Salinas, was arrested for money laundering related to cartels. During the 20th century, narco-trafficking evolved, consolidating key routes and international alliances. The border with the United States, the world's largest consumer of drugs, turned Mexico into a strategic point for the trafficking of substances like cocaine, heroin, methamphetamines, and, more recently, fentanyl. With the arrival of democracy in 2000, the PRI lost power after more than 70 years of government, and Vicente Fox from the PAN assumed the presidency in a country where narco-trafficking was already deeply entrenched in politics and the economy. Fox faced a corrupt system that had allowed cartels to operate with impunity, while the 9/11 attacks in 2001 caused many trafficking routes to the US to be closed, forcing cartels to find new ways to move drugs. The dissolution of the old PRI control system generated an internal struggle between cartels, with groups like La Familia Michoacana challenging the Sinaloa Cartel, triggering an unprecedented wave of violence and marking the beginning of the security crisis that still affects Mexico. Felipe Calderón took office in 2006 amidst a crisis of legitimacy, and to consolidate his authority, declared war on narco-trafficking. His government justified this decision in the face of growing infiltration of organized crime into institutions and security forces. In 2007, he signed the Mérida Initiative with the US, which provided military and financial support for the fight against cartels. However, the strategy failed, fragmenting the criminal groups into more violent cells and failing to attack the corruption that protected them. The Zetas emerged as one of the most bloodthirsty cartels, using terror tactics. Why Calderón initiated the warThe federal government was losing control of the country. Narcotrafficking had infiltrated the security forces and government institutions. The Army and Federal Police were on the payroll of the cartels or would soon be. He needed a political strategy to consolidate his power.Between 2006 and 2012, violence left over 65,000 dead and 20,000 disappeared. With the return of the PRI in 2012, Enrique Peña Nieto attempted to downplay the issue, but continued with the same strategy. Violence did not decrease, and between 150,000 and 200,000 people died during his government, while corruption persisted and the cartels adapted, diversifying their illicit activities. Today, the global drug market is estimated at $650 billion, and Mexico remains a key player in the trafficking of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and fentanyl. Despite decades of war against narco-trafficking, corruption and demand in the US have hindered a real solution. The Mexican government continues to secretly negotiate with cartels, regulating the business without directly confronting them, while the cartels continue to expand with impunity. With the arrival of Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2018, the strategy changed to hugs, not bullets, prioritizing social programs to tackle the root causes of crime. Nevertheless, violence has not decreased significantly, and the cartels have diversified their activities, including illegal mining and human trafficking. Deaths do not decrease, no matter how much free money you give people (or use the redistribution of wealth as a pretext), there is much more money flowing through the sale of drugs. Impunity is unleashed. The cartel spirit is violence, comments Guadalupe Salcedo, Mexican economist. One of the biggest obstacles to combating violence in Mexico is corruption. Police colluding with cartels, politicians funded by narco money, and judges releasing delinquents have generated a crisis of confidence in institutions. Impunity is alarming, most crimes are not resolved, and perpetrators rarely face consequences. The Future of Security in Mexico With the arrival of Claudia Sheinbaum to the presidency in 2024, her government has proposed a security strategy based on four pillars: Reduction of delinquency incidence, focusing on homicides and high-impact crimes. Neutralization of violence generators, with operations in high-crime areas. Strengthening prevention and social proximity, improving local police. Inter-institutional coordination, through the creation of a National Intelligence System. In its first months of government, more than 2,000 arrests have been made, and the National Guard has been deployed on the northern border to combat fentanyl trafficking and firearms. However, it remains to be seen if this strategy will be able to offer sustainable results in the long term. Most of the violence in Mexico is derived from the demand for drugs in the United States, government corruption, economic inequality, and an inefficient judicial system have created a vicious cycle of violence and impunity. Violence has also changed. Previously, confrontations were between criminal groups, but now anyone can be a victim Thefts, feminicides, disappearances, and violence have become part of our daily lives. What's most heartbreaking is that we've grown accustomed to it. We no longer get surprised when we hear about clandestine mass graves or shootouts in broad daylight, comments Guadalupe Salcedo, a Mexican economist. Despite the bleak outlook, Mexican society continues to fight. Journalists, activists, and citizen collectives keep demanding justice and structural changes. The solution requires a combination of political reforms, government transparency, and increased investment in education and economic opportunities.

A Texas resident will spend the rest of his life in prison. He receives a life sentence for child sexual abuse. In addition, the court ordered the accused migrant to pay $30,000 in compensation to a known victim and $60,000 in fines.A 35-year-old Mexican citizen, who lived illegally in Palmview, has been sentenced for producing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) of a family member and coercing the production of CSAM using several chat platforms, announced U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, Nicholas J. Ganjei. Jesús Adrián BarrazaVega pleaded guilty on October 9, 2024. U.S. District Judge Drew Tipton has sentenced BarrazaVega to spend the rest of his life in prison. The court also ordered him to pay $30,000 in compensation to a known victim and a total of $60,000 in fines. In the hearing, the minor victim was present with their family and presented a victim's letter addressed to BarrazaVega in which they described the harm caused by him. Additionally, the court heard that BarrazaVega's continued abuse of a minor relative continued until just a few days before their encounter with the police. Our sincere hope is that the children victimized by BarrazaVega can now have some peace, said Ganjei. The crimes committed against children in the South District of Texas will be processed with all possible rigor. The life sentence handed down today against Mr. BarrazaVega should serve as a warning to other possible abusers. Children deserve to be safe. Whether online or in their own homes, we all have a duty to protect the most vulnerable from exploitation, said Special Agent in Charge Aaron Tapp of the FBI's San Antonio Field Office. The FBI works day and night to ensure that predators like this one are brought to justice. We hope that this sentence can bring a sense of closure and healing for the victims and their families. On July 3, 2023, New York authorities discovered that inappropriate images were being sent to an 8-year-old minor. A review of the conversation revealed that the minor victim had sent sexually explicit videos of herself to an unknown individual via TextNow and WhatsApp. During the course of the conversation, the individual pretended to be a 13-year-old boy. He sent images showing a man's genitals and sexually explicit messages, including requests for the minor victim to participate in sexual acts. Law enforcement conducted a search and determined the subscriber information of the IP address that returned to BarrazaVega's previous addresses, including his current location in Palmview. During an interview with BarrazaVega, he confirmed his previous residences, email addresses, and phone number, and that he used TextNow and WhatsApp. All of this matched the information linked to the accounts used to coerce and persuade the minor victim to produce sexually degrading material in New York. In February 2024, law enforcement executed a federal search warrant on a cell phone identified as belonging to BarrazaVega. Forensic extraction revealed child sexual abuse material, including videos and images of a minor relative. The material included images and videos of BarrazaVega participating in various sex acts with this victim. The videos and images dated back to November 11, 2020, or around that date, to January 18, 2024, or around that date. The FBI conducted the investigation with the assistance of U.S. Border Patrol and the police departments of Mission and Palmview. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alexa D. Parcell is in charge of the case, which was presented as part of the Safe Childhoods Project (SCP), a national initiative that the Department of Justice (DOJ) launched in May 2006 to combat the growing epidemic of child sex exploitation and abuse.

A 13-year-old girl arrived at Colonia Dora Hospital in Santiago del Estero province, complaining of severe pain. Upon examination by the doctors, they discovered the horror that the minor was pregnant and about to give birth. The victim eventually gave birth to the baby and told the doctors that her aunt's partner had been abusing her. The aberrant episode occurred on Saturday afternoon in the Avellaneda locality of Santiago del Estero. The minor arrived at the emergency room with another aunt and complained of feeling unwell. In that context, the doctors examined her and discovered that she was pregnant and about to give birth. The specialists eventually referred the minor to Añatuya Zonal Hospital, where she gave birth to the baby. Both are under observation, but they are in good health. Given the gravity of the situation, the doctors alerted the staff at Añatuya N4 Children and Family Police Station. In that context, the officers interviewed the woman who was with the minor, but she said she was not aware of the abuse. However, the girl provided information about the suffering she was going through, saying that another aunt forced her to lock herself in a room with her partner at least three times a week. With this scenario, the police began their investigative tasks. The prosecutor in charge, Alejandra Sobrero, ordered that the case be captioned as repeated sexual abuse with carnal access. In addition, she requested that the obstetrician and the minor's aunt be interviewed, and also asked for a medical report. Police personnel from the N4 Children and Family Station in Añatuya intervened in the case. At this time, it is unknown if there are people detained. A similar case was known a few weeks ago in Saladillo, when a 13-year-old girl also arrived at the hospital with severe abdominal discomfort. When the nurses placed her on a stretcher, they realized she was in the middle of labor. After giving birth, the baby was kept under observation. The doctors confirmed that the baby was approximately 35 weeks pregnant. Given the suspicions that this would be a case of abuse, the professionals alerted the Municipality of Saladillo's Children and Adolescents Office. Days later, the Justice ordered the arrest of the stepfather and the mother of the minor. The man was charged with the crime of aggravated repeated sexual abuse with carnal access, and the woman with aggravated false testimony and concealment.

Cuauhtémoc Blanco starts to feel the effects of the accusation of sexual abuse by his half-sister. The former governor of the Mexican state of Morelos, former football player, and current federal deputy, Cuauhtémoc Blanco, faces the possibility of losing his parliamentary immunity, in the first of the concrete consequences that the case of alleged sexual abuse against him, brought by his half-sister, Nidia Fabiola Blanco Fernández, could have. On February 6, the Morelos State Prosecutor's Office formally presented a request to the Chamber of Deputies to strip Blanco of his immunity, who currently occupies a seat for the Morena party. The petition, headed by Prosecutor Uriel Carmona Gándara, seeks to allow a criminal investigation to be carried out against him for the crime of sexual abuse that occurred in 2023. Blanco Fernández filed the complaint in October of last year, but it was not until the end of January that his lawyer, Rodrigo Dorantes, began to speak with the press about the case. According to statements gathered by the Spanish newspaper El País, Dorantes claims that Blanco attempted to sexually abuse his half-sister in December 2023, when she was living with him in the official residence of the governor in Morelos. The half-sister's complaint In his testimony, Blanco Fernández recounts that the former football player violently burst into her room with the intention of attacking her. I heard a loud noise at the door of my room, as if someone was trying to enter. I got up, opened the door, and saw Cuauhtémoc standing outside. I told him what's wrong, you scared me. As soon as I opened the door, he abruptly entered my room, he declared in his testimony. I noticed that he had a strange look, red eyes, and seemed anxious. He grabbed me by the shoulders and tried to kiss me. Then, he immediately tried to touch my breasts and began to struggle to remove my clothes, he added. The lawyer for the accuser also stated that, during the time his client lived with Blanco, he witnessed certain behaviors of the former governor in gatherings with friends. According to Dorantes, at these parties there was excessive alcohol consumption, the presence of escorts, and relationships with people of questionable reputation.Immediate consequences If the Chamber of Deputies approves the impeachment, Blanco would lose the legal protection afforded by his position, allowing the Prosecutor's Office to continue with the investigation and, if the evidence warrants it, proceed with a criminal trial.According to the Mexican Constitution, impeachment is a mechanism designed to prevent impunity in public officials with federal positions. The last word will be held by the Chamber of Deputies, which will evaluate whether there are sufficient evidence to remove their immunity. The person responsible for pushing this process is Uriel Carmona Gándara, former prosecutor of Morelos and political rival of Blanco. However, just a few hours after the investigation was announced, the Morelos Congress removed Carmona from his position. We will challenge the decision because we consider it unconstitutional and illegal, as the procedures established for my removal were not followed. They did not give me the opportunity to defend myself, Carmona declared after his removal.

A 36-year-old Cuban citizen residing in Miami was found dead in Mexico under circumstances yet to be clarified, causing commotion among his family members, particularly his mother, who is demanding justice and the prompt repatriation of the body. The incident occurred on February 7 in the Bellavista colony of Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, where the lifeless body of a man was found inside a black Alfa Romeo with Florida plates, according to local news source Canal 44. The victim, identified as Diredmy Herrera Agüero, presented signs of violence, including bullet wounds, and was restrained. The discovery took place at the intersection of Begonias and Pípila streets, near Acequia Madre, after neighbors alerted authorities to a burning vehicle. At the scene, a percussion casing was found, although the caliber has yet to be determined. Kiri, the mother of Diredmy and a resident of Curaçao, made a desperate plea on social media after the tragic death of her son. In her message, she denounced that the media reported on the case as if her son had no family, demanding answers and justice. My son is not an orphan, my son has a mother, she expressed in a video where her deep pain is palpable, also demanding answers and justice for the crime. According to her testimony, she has tried without success to communicate with various authorities in the United States for the repatriation of the body, fearing that her son's remains may be sent to a mass grave due to inaction. I am not in Cuba, she clarified in the video, reaffirming her commitment to managing the case. Univision 23 journalist Mario Vallejo joined the mother's request and called on his followers in Mexico to provide assistance in recovering the body. This Cuban mother has lived in Curaçao for years. I need help from Mexico to try to get the mother to recover the body, Vallejo stated on social media. The Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid footballer Raúl Asencio. The player is one of four footballers investigated in a case of distributing sexual content with a 16-year-old minor. In the ruling, issued on January 28, the three magistrates assert that there are sufficient rational indications of criminality that the Canary Islands-born youth player may have committed both a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, as well as another of child pornography. Asencio's defense requested the dismissal of the case, arguing that the investigations agreed upon by the investigating judge were conducted without solid indications of a crime due to the absence of the video in the investigation, and also claimed that the instruction period had expired, in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Act. The defendant argued that since the video could not be recovered by the Judicial Police, its existence and content could not be confirmed and there were no evidence linking the football player to the crime. An unrecovered video The defense claimed that since the video was not recovered, there was no evidence of the crime. However, the court confirms that the absence of the video file does not mean it never existed and establishes that the crime would have been committed when the video was shared, even if it was later deleted. Additionally, an investigated party declared that Asencio showed them the video, which is further supported by the phone records indicating that they received it via WhatsApp. The judges of the Audiencia have rejected these arguments and have ordered the investigated party to assume the procedural costs. Additionally, they emphasize that the investigations were ordered before the deadline expired, making them valid, and they add that nothing prevents the opening of a separate case if new lines of investigation appear, which would allow extending the deadline if necessary. The investigation began on September 18, 2023, following a complaint by the young woman's mother at a Guardia Civil outpost in Gran Canaria, accusing the possible dissemination of an explicit sex video starring a minor. The same had been recorded on June 15, and, as detailed by the complainant, the relationships that occurred in the reserved area of a leisure establishment in the town of Amadores, in the Canary Island municipality of Mogán, had been consensual. What was not consented to was the recording of the same. As a result of the complaint, the investigating judge charged four football players Raúl Asencio, currently in the first team of Real Madrid, Ferran Ruiz (who plays for Girona), the Galician Juan Rodríguez (Tarazona), and the Balearic Andrés García (Alcorcón).

Without immigrant labor, there will be no milk, cheese, butter, or ice cream, the farmer said. We'll all have to become vegans, he stated. Rosenow's farm in Waumandee, western Wisconsin, relies almost entirely on foreign workers. The president's promise to initiate the largest deportation plan in U.S. history could, he said, destroy that workforce and threaten the future of his farm. He had many fewer concerns before Trump was elected, the 75-year-old man said, who has openly campaigned against the policy. Now we're in a completely new world. Trump has made immigration reform a cornerstone of his second presidential term. Immediately after taking the oath, he deployed troops to secure the southern border, citing a national emergency. In a wave of executive orders, he also halted the resettlement of refugees, expanded the group of undocumented immigrants subject to expedited deportation, and ordered the expansion of facilities to detain foreign nationals. He has also spoken of sending federal officers to gather and remove thousands of people deemed to be in the United States without permission. The moves have gone down well with Trump's base. But business groups are expressing concern about the impact they will have on the agricultural sector, which they say cannot function without undocumented immigrant labor. The dairy industry is particularly vulnerable. Product manufacturers can recruit legal seasonal workers to harvest fruits and vegetables under the H2A visa program for temporary farms. However, there is no such system for dairy farms, which require workers to tag cows three times a day, year-round. It is therefore no surprise that rural Wisconsin, a sparsely populated state with 3.5 million cows dubbed the Dairy State of the United States, is preparing for the next wave of immigration repression. We support the deportation of criminals, but we need a safe workforce for Wisconsin, said Tyler Wenzlaff, head of government relations at the Wisconsin Farm Bureau Federation in the capital, Madison. As a result, any mass effort to deport undocumented workers would have a significant impact on the US food system and increase the cost of producing food, Ortega said.
