We have been denouncing this not only publicly, but we have also accompanied many presentations, both collective and individual, of various women who dare to denounce the police's actions. These are procedures, raids and operations where there is no prosecutor who intervenes and gives them a seal of approval. It's a free-for-all, they start stopping all the people who have the stigma of being considered subjects of danger. For example, we have found raids where sex workers are forced against a wall, stripped naked in public spaces, or taken to temporary hotels, where they are searched and made to do push-ups to see if they can find any illicit act they are committing. If they don't find anything, just condoms, some money and a cell phone, they take the money as evidence. They steal it, in very few cases, where the women have managed to denounce it, there were prosecutors who returned it. Last year, they took 17,000 pesos from her and returned it to her in September, but now it's not worth the same. That's what's happening. APU And it's getting worse GO Yes, when they detain the companion in an arbitrary manner, against the wall and strip her naked in public, they take her money and if they don't find anything suspicious, they tell her to leave, but all that procedure, that public humiliation, that inhumane treatment, the insults they provoke, especially towards migrant women, and the beatings, have become normalized in that person's daily life. For us, that's dangerous because it's a step backward in the violation of the human rights of the companions. APU We had managed to set certain limits on the security force's actions. GO Until 2023, it was somewhat under control GO They were very careful in their actions. There were arbitrary detentions. I was also arrested in 2023 and 2022. I was arrested more times as a trade unionist than as a sex worker. That's the risk you take when you join the movement, it's not romanticizing it, where you become aware of class consciousness and organize, there are tensions and situations where you won't feel comfortable and you'll go through this type of humiliation. We understand the police's actions. Taking me in custody, taking our delegates, has an intention to break the unionization of sex workers, that is, no one else should dare to speak out for this collective. That's what they repeat to our fellow activists, that's the way they've found to intimidate them. APU Because the police also collect money from prostitution GO Of course, they extort it always. There's a saying, that there's a small police box, and we say it's not that small because it not only collects from sex workers, but also from street vendors and vendors, from informal workers and all those subjects who don't have a recognized job. On top of that, there are regulations that give the police power, it's a discussion we've always had, especially with colleagues and colleagues from the human rights field. There still exist contraventional codes that come from the military dictatorship. For example, in San Juan, a code still in force has figures that penalize scandalous prostitution in public spaces. What defines scandal? That's the problem. The code is made to sanitize neighborhoods, to make a cleanup, and there always those who enter the statistics in the penal system, who cross judicial processes and detentions, the component that unites us is skin color, social class, and informal work. APU It's about who we see, the street vendors, the women with carts selling coffee, the Senegalese men with a blanket who have to leave because if they don't, they lose their little merchandise, or the ones selling food. We have seen that in black bags they throw away all the food, take away the cart and the coolers, and cut off their legs because after coming back to start again, they don't have income for weeks. APU Progress was made during the Kirchnerism in terms of rights and persecution. The government of Alberto Fernández was very lukewarm to be able to give deep, complex, urgent, and necessary debates, which did not take place. We have tried to approach state institutions, the Ministry of Women, to tell them what we need, after calling and sending messages, attending some meetings, and even feminist assemblies. We made criticisms because we saw what was happening on the streets, for example institutional violence, and they on the other side told us they were preparing a report. You're not playing at being a CONICET research grantee, you're the State. First, study the field and then act, until it occurs that the lives of our companions pass away, who continue to be in a situation of homelessness and precariousness, and it deepens. We couldn't make any criticism, that was the major problem we have had. In politics, you have to debate and there are some things you agree on and some you don't. That's how we perceive politics. I'm not going to thank Alberto for giving us a ministry and ending patriarchy, but what's still missing. The Accompany Program cannot be six months, it has to be compatible with Potenciar Trabajo. APU And what did GO say? That we were making the game of the right-wing. In fact, at a public assembly on the eve of 8M or 3J, when we made this criticism, some responded that we should take care of the female officials. I got angry, I won't take care of anyone's salary. It's the opposite. You don't fight to get a job and then have us applaud you, obey you, not criticize you, and wait for you to come and enlighten us with your reports and bring us magical solutions. It's a different way, it's disputed in another sense in the political debate. There was no room for that, and that's how we are. APU There are comrades or comrades who have been precarious workers who voted for Javier Milei. GO Yes. First, for me, the workers who voted for the government can never be accused or pointed out. They are not fascists. We are standing from that place. After that, we are made to take responsibility for the fact that they used to vote for Peronism and now for Milei because they felt deceived and had their hopes played with. That promise of becoming better did not translate into increased purchasing power, registered work, and discussions with those who work informally, which remains a pending debt to have legislation that protects, recognizes, and grants rights, as social work and retirement contributions, and not just the social monotributo as the only alternative left for us. There are discussions that we have not yet found the possibility of having in political leadership. They have to do with the anger, frustration, and distance that those compañeras and compañeros have, first, with the State. I think the current government has been very clever in being able to pick up on that anger and put the State's role at the center of the discussion. I am a defender of the State, but I am also very critical of how it functioned with Alberto, and I cannot defend it. It didn't work out well, and we saw it every time we went to a government office, where they didn't resolve the problem but instead put up a lot of bureaucratic obstacles to give us a Work Enhancement or a housing subsidy. APU How much is a Work Enhancement? GO I think it's now 76,000 pesos, due to inflation and because there was a cut in that social program. It started being charged at 16,000 pesos during the pandemic. A room in a hotel in Constitución cost between 15,000 and 18,000 pesos. They would charge them, and quickly, on the 5th of every month, the money that was deposited would be translated into paying and maintaining their room. A precarious situation, in the conditions of the hotels and the pensions that we can access who don't have a pay stub. Today, a room in the Constitución neighborhood costs between 200,000 and 270,000 pesos per month, so a lot of people are living on the streets, including sex workers, trans women, and migrant collectives. They live from day to day. If I go out and earn 20,000 or 30,000 pesos, I pay for the room by the day to spend the night. You enter at 10 pm but have to leave by 8 am the next day or pay again. When they have that money, they can sleep in a bed, bathe, and clean themselves. The government, along with the Agency for Government Control and municipal operators, took away the few things they had with them on the streets, including blankets, documents, or clothing. Many people say that the person living on the streets does so because they want to, because they can go to a shelter. Let's talk about the shelters, the offer that the City Government has in this case, which are not a place where a person can stay all the time. It's like staying in a hotel, with a check-in time between 6 pm and 8 pm, and a check-out time at 8 am. During that time, those people are wandering on the streets, and if you work at night, you can't. Then, the dynamics of the shelters. If you have a family, a father, a mother, children, they can't stay together because there are shelters for men and for women with children. A homeless family is not going to want to separate. Additionally, the conditions of the shelter. For example, we have a case of a colleague that we are accompanying who suffered sexual abuse. They have also stolen their belongings inside, and there is no containment. Imagine a colleague who on top of that has a problematic substance abuse due to abstinence, there is no accompaniment. There are people who arrive without an ID and it is supposed to be the State inside, which should have an integral view. A bed, a meal, a shower, a plug to charge your phone, if you have one, and that's it. That's why many of our colleagues prefer to continue walking on the street rather than going to a shelter and going through all these situations. APU On the other hand, I remember a call for applications at the Faculty of Journalism of the University of La Plata that brought many students, beyond the controversy with other colleagues. GO Yes, I think it's the possibility of listening to someone in person, which doesn't often happen in academia. They speak for the cartoneros, people living on the street, and sex workers. APU Many times, in the militancy, sex workers are seen in a very critical way Our reading is that we entered a disputed field, that of feminisms, but then it is transferred to the State, academia, society, and the labor union, in all spaces where we have a voice. When AMMAR enters the labor union, as part of the CTA, it gives a discussion that had to do with being able to publicly tell, we always had to make it public, what we were doing there. Next year AMMAR will be thirty years old, the place they gave us to hold the first meetings was the basement, very representative. How sex workers arrive No, I won't arrive with a mameluco and the construction hard hat, but with my tacos. We leave work, go to the Central Workers' and discuss problems related to the police and permanent conflict situations that we have in public space. The male colleagues had told the female founders of the organization that they had to write on the back page of the monthly newspaper, which was distributed to members and affiliates, a public letter and explain briefly. Those opposing the sex workers' integration into the central were the women. The kids would tell you that if you said it was work, they had it a bit more figured out. APU Hugo Yasky. GO Yes, it's like my husband is publicly saying. He always gets into trouble because, just like how you were made to make that kind of academic denouncement, he always has to explain why he defends sex workers. Now not as much, but they've made him face public shaming. Yasky says he can in no way expel the organized sex workers, and less so when they always tell us what the police are doing. After that, for many years, even in the Secretariat of Gender, we had to give talks on why we wanted labor rights and explain to each of our colleagues our demands, our life trajectories, so that they understand that our fight is legitimate. I don't want another job, don't try to convince me. I didn't fall into sex work, there was a process and then a lot of things we had to undo, even ourselves. You claim sex work, like any other, has good and bad things GO No, I don't romanticize any job, I allow myself to acknowledge that all jobs are crap. There's no such thing as a dignified job. A lot come and tell us to ask the State, which job is dignified? Which worker and worker goes to their job every day happy, with their salary, with their working hours, and loves their boss? There's no such thing. We live in a capitalist system that oppresses us all, in which everyone is exploited. What really gets to me, and to sex workers, is that we always have to explain that our exploitation is legitimate, just like that of a worker or a domestic worker. If you don't like that, then you should have the right to paid vacation, Christmas bonus, pension, and social security, just like everyone else. So why are you questioning sex workers and not yourself? There are many colleagues, even teachers, who tell us about their working conditions and labor schedules. I wouldn't dare sit through that, but there's a stigma, and many people put it here, not all of them, that it's the devices of moral control and sexual control, which is sex. Many think that it shouldn't be transacted with money, but rather respond to patterns, like gratitude and love. I think it's much more honest that many acknowledge that what bothers them is that we get paid. If you come with the theory that if we lived in a just, free, and equal society, there wouldn't be a need to fight for a decent job, because we would have to struggle for a dignified job, where is that? I got out of the bubble. I agree to fight for that, the first thing that would be abolished is wage labor, then there would be no need to work at all. Now, reality tells me that I have to pay rent and raise a kid. For now, I have to work at something and what gave me the possibility of maintaining my life somewhat economically organized is sex work. I won't regret having earned money because that gave me dignity, a roof, educating my son, and working fewer hours. I'm not going to work 12 hours in a factory, I prefer to work on the corner for two or four hours and then do things that I enjoy, like militancy. APU You collaborated on Alanís, Sofia Gala's movie. GO We collaborated from AMMAR on Anahí Berneri's movie, who plays Sofia Gala. They brought us the script, it was the first time someone had thought about writing about sex work. They gave us the opportunity to modify it. It's very good, we liked that the main character was a mother and it's very representative of the sex workers' collective. Very brave and strong of Sofia, I think that when someone is convinced, they won't run away from a complaint or a public denouncement. We felt that Sofia had put on the t-shirt because she was convinced that it was right to problematize the reality of sex workers. APU Is the scene where they mistreat her while she's cleaning the bathrooms. GO Yes, that's something we've gone through. Social imagination thinks that our work history is the only thing that defines us as sex workers. No, we were many other things. I was a factory worker in a metal factory for a month, then I left. The hours weren't compatible with my son's daycare. The agreement was that I would arrive at 9 in the morning and leave at 4 in the afternoon, and after that, certain limits started to be enforced. That's when I began to value sex work because I lived it with a lot of guilt and a lot of shame. If a client hires me for an hour, I would do everything possible to make it last less, and if suddenly they want to stay longer, there's no way. It's about having the conditions clear from the beginning, and then the hotel itself tells you that you have to leave. That was a value for me. I couldn't tell my boss at the time that I was asked to load papers into an Excel spreadsheet that I would be leaving at 4 because if I did, they would fire me. When I said that that was no longer for me, they had asked me to do something that wasn't within what an administrative employee was supposed to do, which was making coffee. Again, they made me clean the bathroom. It was the same combo and the same salary. If I earned more, there was no problem, I would stay. They made me make coffee, they tasted it, and it was horrible. I don't like doing anything in the kitchen, I knew it was ugly, I put in the effort. My boss took it in front of everyone and said to put it back, so everyone returned the plate while looking at me like a subordinate. If a client tells me something doesn't suit them, it's their problem. I'm not going to return the money and it's paid in advance. APU Unlike the formal market. GO Yes, it was impossible to organize myself. I lived day to day and had found a way to organize that much money per day. Waiting thirty days was slavery, and besides, having to organize the next thirty. I was stuck with it all and then had to live with 29. When I said that job wasn't for me, they tried to convince me to stay with the guilt. What are you going to go back to the street? At least here you'll have social benefits and pension contributions, I have a month. It might be an advantage, I won't tell you it's not, being a registered job. The street gave me the value of, if I don't like something, the possibility of leaving. Here is the translation:Here we have certain limits, afterwards the issue of schedule and money. When we say it, some feminists get scared, but who doesn't like money. You'll stay if they pay you well, if not you'll look for another job to leave. If you like living well, why do you want us to live badly and go back to a precarious job where I suffered and they paid me poorly. I don't want a mansion, I'm aware of my class. I don't want to go hungry, nor for my child to go hungry, and sex work gave me the possibility of living as well as possible within the system of inequality we're in. Imagine that the libertarian government legalizes sex work as part of the market. For now, let's not give them ideas. The fear we have, and it's the discussion within the organization, is the issue of virtual platforms. There are some more well-known and others that aren't, where our comrades and comrades exercise virtual sex work. Yes, but many do not recognize themselves as sex workers, instead saying they are content creators or webcam models. We see that this has social acceptance, no one is shocked. It seems cool, there is that disconnection. It's not sex work because it doesn't involve contact with the client or being on the street and exposed to exploitation situations. You sell a photo, upload content, and earn dollars on top of it. It has to do with a class issue because the people who do it are mostly white and have a hegemony of beauty that is a totally validated stereotype by this system. They are middle class, bourgeois chicks, who what they need now is not to be poor, and they are virtual workers, many of them, to maintain a status. There is a differentiation. We clearly see that there is a class cut. What bothers us is the sex work of women, lesbians, transvestites, and trans people from the popular sectors. It's disturbing that there are women in the Constitución neighborhoods who are questioning the way they work. APU Those digital systems are an attack on unionization. Of course. It's a matter of, first, the erasure of the idea of work, and then there's entrepreneurship. Next, erasing everything collective, that is, you don't need the State. I've heard many say it, that what they need is a computer, a tire with lights and internet connection, but then problems appear. Some have come because they need the State, in the sense that you're exercising a job, even if you don't recognize yourself as a sex worker, which is not recognized, and what it implies is monetizing in dollars has to do with Argentina's foreign trade policy, and that's linked to the IMF agreement. They come with dollars and aren't going to give it to you like that, they're going to devalue it Young women came to say that they couldn't withdraw their money from virtual wallets because the bank's foreign trade had been consumed. They go and ask them to bring a receipt to see where it comes from and what service it provides. If you need the State, you might be a monotributista as a sex worker, and you'd have to invoice a certain amount of money for personal services you performed directly. APU We're falling way behind to ask to be a monotributista. GO Of course. I'm not saying it's better to be a prostitute to not be poor. I am poor, I'm not rich or middle class. I rent a small apartment in Constitución and my son goes to public school. I don't feel ashamed of being poor. What I want is to have a pension, just like all my colleagues who are over 60 years old and continue to work in sex in super precarious conditions. We want a social security plan. We want a government office to report police brutality cases. We don't want to go to the police station or go through judicial processes anymore. We don't want to face the difficulties we experience for doing a job that is clandestine and criminalized. We need an honest debate, that's what we ask from politics. Stop being hypocritical, because there's a lot of hypocrisy when talking about sex work. More than one has had what they call a pimp and has been paid, it's not hidden. What do you demand from those below? I'm not asking you to pay me a vacation in Marbella, but I want to vacation in Chapadmalal with social tourism in the Evita complexes, and that should be a state policy, not just for us but for informal workers. That's why we need you to be honest, to leave the hypocrisy and the fantasy of making us believe that you are the good ones. APU You are not. There is no good or bad, there are people who exercise a job that is not recognized. First, we need to be heard, second, we need an honest debate with our voices, not even those of dissidents. The dissident voices, who are the abolitionists, were part of the State and were in the Ministry of Women. If you crashed everything, don't come to give us lessons on dignity, if being part of the State you had the possibility of transforming the lives of sex workers and, however, you left and there are a lot who are sleeping on the street. Your abolitionist gaze failed because there are more and more prostitutes, more poor, older, more broken, more precarious, and on the streets. I won't defend a ministry or a State that didn't work. We need a present State, that works, but to discuss how we want it to intervene and how we no longer want to live our lives.

data.text: Misogynistic Violence The new agreement against gender violence contains 462 measures and for the first time addresses vicarious, digital, and economic violence. The PERIÓDICO has accessed the report submitted to the Equality Commission, with more than 450 measures aimed at updating the agreement, such as a perpetrator not being able to see their child or the non-payment of alimony being considered economic violence. After more than a year of work, Congress has taken the first step to update the State Pact against gender violence. On Monday, parliamentary groups submitted a report to the Equality Commission that includes more than 450 measures, aimed at strengthening and updating the agreement, incorporating actions aimed at improving the protection of minors and recognizing and combating economic, digital, sexual violence, human trafficking for sexual exploitation, or forced marriages. The groups' forecast is that the Equality Commission will approve the report, by majority and with the opposition of Vox, next week, and that, subsequently, the Congress plenary will give the definitive thumbs-up. Nevertheless, the parties will present particular votes and some warn that in the Commission they will try to further improve the text, so that it may still suffer some modification. But the bulk is already agreed upon. EL PERIÓDICO has had access to the report and these are the main measures it contains. Vicarious Violence One of the most extensive chapters of the Pact proposal is the one related to the protection of minors and vicarious violence, which is that exercised against children to harm the mother. At least 39 measures are contemplated, including a proposal to reform the law against gender violence to include as victims minors who are victims of vicarious violence following the breakdown of family cohabitation, on occasion of the visitation regime. With regard to this, the pact demands that agreement or maintenance of cohabitation or visits with the aggressor be avoided and obliges a paternofilial evaluation to be carried out prior to the judicial resolution on visits, when the woman victim of gender violence requests it and there is contradiction between the parties. Furthermore, it demands that a sufficient allocation be guaranteed in family intervention teams, that meeting points do not apply the parental alienation syndrome, or that healthcare professionals have a protocol to recognize and act when they detect violence against minors, among other measures aimed at improving training or repair. Economic Violence The report commits to incorporating economic violence into the Spanish legal system, understanding it as the action of limiting women's access to family resources or reducing their economic capacity with the aim of making them economically dependent on the aggressor. In this sense, the creation of a new penal offense is proposed to capture the behaviors that seek to limit women's autonomy and economic independence. In the same vein, the figure of workplace sabotage will be analyzed, when an aggressor takes actions that prevent the victim from having a job. On the other hand, the commitment is to reinforce Article 227 of the Penal Code, which punishes the non-payment of pensions, to include those agreed upon in a public deed before a notary and not only by agreement or judicial resolution. Additionally, an aggravated modality of this crime is proposed to be included when the non-payment of the pension implies for the victim the loss of housing, limits or prevents access to basic resources for life. Digital Violence The State Pact also contemplates the recognition of digital violence of gender, understood as any act of violence against women committed with the assistance, in part or in its entirety, of the use of information and communication technologies, or aggravated by this. In the report, measures are highlighted aimed at informing young people, as well as equipping them with tools to report any situation of gender-based violence in the digital environment. Furthermore, it is proposed to create a crime for the cases of digital violence or cybercrime of gender, including identity theft, among others. Additionally, those who, without consent, publish or disseminate photos modified with artificial intelligence simulating situations of a sexual or gravely humiliating nature, shall be penalized. Regarding AI, the document also includes the periodic request for reports from those responsible for monitoring digital systems to prevent gender biases and any situation of gender-based discrimination. Media and audiovisual content Another of the most interesting chapters refers to media and audiovisual content, in which training is recommended for professionals and agreements are proposed with associations and unions of screenwriters to promote the treatment of women free from stereotypes and prejudices. Likewise, in the courses of training in film and television scripts, the pact demands the incorporation of content that allows for a critical view of sexist stereotypes. Additionally, the report advocates for creating the position of intimacy coordinator or coordinators in audiovisual productions, ensuring respect for agreed-upon boundaries with interpreters and respect for consent. Furthermore, it generally calls for promoting mechanisms to prevent gender biases in social media, applications, video games, etc.Financing As occurred with the unanimous pact signed in 2017, the agreement contains proposals whose implementation corresponds to different agents, such as the Government, communities, municipalities, or justice, each within the scope of their competencies. Moreover, according to Júlia Boada, one of the presenters of the Sumar group's report, the pact foresees an increase in financing, which is very positive because we have confirmed that there are not enough resources.

69-year-old man allegedly abused a 9-year-old girl in Santa Rosa de Lima, north of Bolívar. A 69-year-old adult male was judicialized in recent hours for the crimes of sexual acts with a minor under 14 years old aggravated and commercial sexual exploitation of a person under 18 years old. According to the investigation by the Prosecutor's Office, between August and September 2021, the man allegedly sexually assaulted his neighbor, a 9-year-old girl, on multiple occasions, taking advantage of the moments when she was alone. The incidents occurred in the Montebello neighborhood of the municipality of Santa Rosa de Lima, in the north of the department. According to the Prosecutor's Office, the man allegedly touched the intimate parts of the minor and, apparently, offered her money in exchange for her silence. Following a judicial order, the National Police captured the alleged abuser in public in the municipality. During the preliminary hearings, the man did not accept the charges brought against him, and a judge of control of guarantees ordered him to be held in a correctional center as a measure of guarantee. At this time, the Prosecutor's Office continues with the investigations to clarify all the details of this case. Read also Governor of Bolívar makes a fourth call to the national government after clashes in the region Other facts in Bolívar In a macabre finding, the lifeless body of Néider Paúl Atencia Sierra, 26 years old, was found in the rural area of the municipality of Zambrano, Bolívar. The victim, with a national ID card issued in Cartagena, showed visible signs of torture and three bullet impacts in the head, according to the report delivered by the authorities at the time of the body's lifting. The body was discovered tied up by hands and feet in a farm known as Juncales, located on the road that leads to the municipality of Córdoba. According to preliminary reports, Atencia Sierra was one of the most wanted men by the National Police in the departments of Córdoba and Sucre, due to his extensive criminal record that includes nearly 22 entries and 8 of these, related to homicides. The victim had several tattoos that could have helped authorities in their identification because, apparently, at the time of discovery, they did not find any probative elements or physical evidence. The investigation has been assigned to the Technical Investigation Body (CTI) to determine the circumstances surrounding their death. Read also Police in Cartagena seize marijuana stash and capture suspected member of the Gulf Clan Néider Paúl Atencia Sierra, according to the National Police, would be linked to the Gulf Clan and was pointed out for being involved in several homicides in the Sucre department. His criminal record includes entries for eight homicides, nine for narcotics trafficking, and other crimes such as conspiracy to commit a crime and the use of minors to commit crimes. The last entry in his record was made on January 7, 2025, for a homicide committed in Sucre.
Investigations are underway against Deputy Jorge Durán (RN) for a complaint of sexual abuse against his ex-partner.

The Supreme Court confirms the one-year prison sentence for a hospital patient who sexually assaulted his nurse. No woman bears the burden or servitude of tolerating a man's desire to perform acts of sexual touching, no matter how minor, on the victim's sexual parts, the High Court reminds. Partial disability granted to a laundry official because he needs superior physical effort. The Supreme Court has confirmed the one-year prison sentence for the hospital patient who sexually assaulted the nurse attending to him. The proven facts highlight that the convicted man, while admitted as a patient in the Madrid hospital room and being attended to by the nurse of said hospital, with the intention of satisfying his sexual desires, performed touching on the left side of her buttocks. In addition to the deprivation of liberty sentence, a measure of supervised liberty has been imposed with the obligation to attend sexual education programs for a period of one year and a prohibition on approaching and communicating with the victim for a period of two years. The Supreme Court emphasizes that the defendant has carried out acts of sexual touching on a nurse in a hospital setting, which constitutes the commission of a crime of old sexual abuse and currently of sexual aggression as per article 178.1 of the penal code. And as additional points to be considered for sentencing, the following are added in relation to the crime committed against a nurse, attacking her sexual freedom while performing her duties as such. The facts that have been declared proven constitute, in the present and at the time of the facts, a crime against the sexual freedom of a woman. A sexual act is performed involving the touching of sexual content and sexual parts of the victim, violating the woman's right to be respected and preventing anyone from performing any act of touching without her consent. The woman has the perfect right that she will not be objectified through sexual touching acts if she does not consent to them. If the woman has not given her explicit or implicit consent to the sexual act, there is sexual aggression. It is not the man who performs the touching of the woman who decides how and when to carry out sexual acts. Bilateral agreement is required in a pact to perform touchings on sexual content parts and the area established in the proven facts is. The woman's consent to the sexual act is not the author's subjective interpretation property. It is not valid to believe that there is consent, but rather, there must be certainty that the woman consents, and that this is derived from the circumstances of the case, which is what the art. 178 CP cites. The woman's consent to the sexual act is not presumed by the perpetrator, but is explicit or tacit. The belief in consent does not validate the performance of sexual acts. The woman's will to engage in sexual activity must be clearly expressed. The art. 178.1 CP requires that consent be freely expressed through acts that, in light of the circumstances of the case, clearly express the person's will. Subjective interpretation of consent without clear evidence from the woman fills the typicity of art. 178.1 CP as it stood at the time of the facts and art. 181.1. Unilateral action from one party cannot be spoken of, but rather, bilateral action from both parties. The proven facts demonstrate a clear act of sexual content, in which a person admitted to a hospital center takes advantage of the medical treatment being given by a nurse and, in the approach of the same to help him, he takes advantage to carry out an act that constitutes a clear attack on the sexual self-determination of a nurse who does not have the servitude of having to endure that a patient takes advantage of her medical attention to sexually assault her, which is what the defendant did when he committed the acts proven, namely, with the intention of satisfying his sexual desires, he carried out touchings on the left side of the buttocks. This is an authentic act of sexual aggression against the woman. No woman has the burden or servitude of enduring the desire of a man to perform acts of sexual touching, no matter how minor, on the victim's sexual parts. Hello, it does not integrate, as it has been understood in other times, a mere coercion or mild harassment, but it constitutes a genuine act of sexual aggression against the woman. And even more in this case in which it supposes an attack on a healthcare professional who, when approaching to carry out her medical assistance actions on a patient in a hospital center, takes advantage of the repeated approach to carry out acts of sexual content, which not only represents a physical excess, but also a penal offense typified in the Penal Code as sexual aggression in the present and at the time as sexual abuse. In this sense, women, and in this case healthcare professionals in healthcare centers, do not have the obligation to endure any type of excess by patients who are admitted to a hospital center, and when they integrate an attack on parts of sexual content of the victims, it constitutes a crime of sexual aggression. On the other hand, in response to the request to reduce the sentence imposed by the Supreme Court, it is dismissed and it is recalled that the Supreme Court understood that there was already a relevant gravity in the causation of the facts in consideration of the sexual attack on the nurse, who, in her medical care of the patient, was surprised by a sexual attack, as it is stated in the proven facts, which cannot be considered in any way as a fact of lesser gravity, and that it entails the application of the sentence that was imposed by the court at the time. On the other hand, the Supreme Court recalls that in cases of sexual crimes, the penal mediation path, as indicated by the recently approved Organic Law 1/2023 of January 2, is not applicable, just like in cases of gender violence, but notes that in the rest of the cases, this path of restorative justice or penal mediation is very effective in speeding up the resolution of cases and the satisfaction of the victim, remembering that there are penal typologies that include attenuated subtypes, such as in this case, or prison alternatives, in which the Organic Law 1/2023 of January 2 has included the restorative justice path in the Additional Provision 9th of the LECRIM, by which it develops the general principles of restorative justice, within the framework of which the regulatory framework for the application of penal mediation is established, to be developed by the protocols implemented by the mediation service of the CGPJ, in a decided bet on this path with origin in the Anglo-Saxon law, in order to launch the intrajudicial mediation derived by the judge, or at the request of the parties. And for this, to achieve a better position for the victim in the penal process, she feels more comforted with situations such as the accused's request for pardon, the accused's remorse, commitment not to repeat the reprehensible social and penal behavior, consignment for payment of civil responsibility, and the acceptance and express acknowledgment of the penal illegality committed by the same (Art. 15 of the Law 4/2023 of the Statute of the Victim of the Crime). All of this leads to a mediation agreement with the intervention of expert penal mediators formed in mediation by the mediation institutes and coordination of the CGPJ in its implementation. And from this, the penal conformity is reached where the agreement between the defense and the most severe of the accusations is in place regarding the reduction of the penalty, in their case, if mitigating circumstances of penal responsibility are appreciated, and the application of attenuated subtypes, as in this case is proposed, or of alternative penalties to imprisonment collected in the penal type that is the object of the accusation, although this does not form part of the mediation or restorative justice agreement, but of the penal conformity agreement between the accusations and the defense, which contributes to the acceleration of the penal justice and of a greater attention to the victim, who remains more comforted with the application of restorative justice in the penal process.

data.text: The National Police of Peru (PNP) assured this Monday that the transnational criminal gang Tren de Aragua is completely dismantled in the country and highlighted that its main leaders are detained in Challapalca's maximum security prison. At this moment, we have the Tren de Aragua dismantled. As a criminal organization, the Tren de Aragua is completely dismantled in Peru. All leaders have fallen (are serving their sentence) in Challapalca, stated to RPP radio the General of the National Police of Peru (PNP), Aldo Ávila Novoa. The official pointed out that the Tren de Aragua has a very special behavior and an undefined structure and that they are studying together with the Government of the United States how it is organized. In this regard, he stated that its structure is neither pyramidal nor collegiate and the hypothesis is that it is a differentiated organization with upper and intermediate levels distributed across countries such as Peru, Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Spain, Brazil, Panama, the United States, and Costa Rica. The Aragua Train has two main characteristics, adaptability and negotiation capacity. In Peru, we mapped them in 2017, and when the migration wave arrived in 2018, they began to occupy territories for human trafficking, Ávila said. He stated that they fight against separate groups from the gang like Hijos de Dios and Los Gallegos, but he cannot provide the exact number of different remnants located in various points of the country. Collaboration with the United States Ávila referred to the mega-police operation carried out on Friday night with the support of the Office of National Security Investigations and Customs of Immigration and Customs Enforcement of the United States in various points of Lima against the criminal organization. He detailed that 23 delinquents linked to factions of the Aragua Train were captured, who are being investigated for the alleged crime of human trafficking, in the modality of sexual and labor exploitation. He added that in the operation, 120 victims of exploitation were rescued, including three minors who have already been placed in the care of the Special Protection Unit of the Ministry of Women. The Aragua Train, born in the Tocorón prison in Aragua, extends to Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, and Chile, where authorities accuse it of committing numerous crimes, including narcotics trafficking, extortion, kidnappings, and homicides. A court clerk from a social center will be judged at the Cantabria Provincial Court on Tuesday, February 11, for a sexual liberty crime, as he is accused of touching a colleague, a cleaner, at the workplace. The Prosecution is asking for a fine of 6,600 euros for him and two years in prison for the victim, understanding that the incident was a sexual assault. The hearing will take place from 10:00 am in the Third Section, reported the Superior Justice Court. According to the public prosecutor's written statement, the defendant approached the woman while she was working in the men's bathroom and lightly bit her neck, attempting to kiss her, which he failed to do as she stepped back and left the restroom. The next day, when the victim arrived at the center and accessed the reception to pick up the keys to the janitor's room, he grabbed her arm, sat her on his lap, and touched her breasts and buttocks. SEXUAL ABUSE OR ASSAULTThe public prosecutor considers these events a continued crime of sexual abuse deserving of a fine of 6,600 euros, as well as a prohibition on communicating with and approaching the woman for a year. In terms of civil liability, he requests that the accused compensate the complainant with 1,000 euros for the moral damages caused. The private accusation exercised by the woman classifies the events as sexual assault and raises the request for punishment to two years in prison, incapacitation for performing with minors for one and a half years, and supervised freedom for two years after the end of the deprivation of liberty sentence. Additionally, she requests a compensation of 3,000 euros for moral damage.

The Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid footballer Raúl Asencio, one of the four footballers investigated in a case of distributing sexual content with a 16-year-old minor. The resolution confirms the decision of an investigating court in southern Gran Canaria, which ordered the identification of participants in messaging groups where the material may have been shared, as well as their summons to testify as witnesses or suspects. In its auto, issued on January 28, the three magistrates assert that there are sufficient rational indications of criminality that the Canary Island youth may have committed both a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets and another of child pornography. The investigation began on September 18, 2023, following a complaint by the young woman's mother at a Civil Guard barracks in northern Gran Canaria, accusing the possible dissemination of an explicit sex video featuring the minor. This had been recorded on June 15. According to the woman, those relationships, which took place in the private area of a renowned leisure establishment in Amadores, in the municipality of Mogán, had been consensual, but the recording, which was carried out without the knowledge of the young women, was not. In September of the same year, the investigating judge charged the four footballers. Since then, the Gran Canaria footballer who will turn 22 on September 13 has settled as a regular in the team led by Carlo Ancelotti. The remaining investigated individuals are Catalan Ferran Ruiz (Girona), Galician Juan Rodríguez (CD Tarazona), and Balearic Andrés García (Alcorcón). The defense of Asencio presented several arguments to request the dismissal of the case. They argued that the agreed-upon investigations by the investigating judge were merely prospective, that is, they were being carried out without solid indications of a crime and with the aim of searching for evidence in an indiscriminate manner. They argued that the investigation period had expired, in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law. They also pointed out the absence of the video in the investigation and argued that, if the video had not been recovered by the Judicial Police, its existence or content could not be proven, and finally, there were not enough evidence to link the footballer. The judges of the Audiencia reject these arguments point by point and impose on the investigated party to bear the procedural costs, emphasizing that the agreed-upon investigations were ordered before the expiration of the period, and therefore are valid. Even if the data analysis is carried out after the deadline, the Supreme Court jurisprudence establishes that this does not invalidate the investigation, in addition to the fact that they hold that nothing prevents the opening of a separate case if new lines of investigation appear, which would allow extending the deadline if necessary. The defense argued that, since the video has not been recovered, there were no evidence of the crime. The order makes it clear that the absence of the video archive does not mean it never existed, establishing that the crime would have been consummated at the moment the video was shared, regardless of whether it was later deleted. Additionally, they recall that there is a statement from one of the investigated individuals, who claimed that Asencio showed him the video, along with the phone records that indicate he received it via WhatsApp. The magistrates, finally, recall that the content of the video can be reconstructed from the testimonies and digital evidence obtained. The analysis of the mobile phones seized from the investigated during the instruction revealed compromising conversations that reinforced the evidence against them. In the data dumps, messages were found in which the investigated commented on the recording and expressed concern about the possible legal consequences. One of the implicated even searched the internet for information on the crime of distributing intimate images without consent, suggesting that they were aware of the gravity of the facts and the possible penal implications. Furthermore, in the intercepted conversations, three of the investigated made derogatory and humiliating comments about the minor who filed the complaint, which adds an aggravating element to the case. The judge maintains Raúl Asencio under investigation for suspected child pornography. According to an exclusive revelation by El Confidencial, the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has rejected the player's request to close his case. Raúl Asencio remains an imputed party in the case of the recording and distribution of a sexual video of a minor. The Real Madrid player had access to the video from two of his colleagues from the club's academy, which is headed by Florentino Pérez, who had sex with two girls in the Canary Islands. Images obtained without the consent of the young women, one of whom was a minor, were shown to Asencio, who then showed the video to a third party, as exclusively revealed by El Confidencial. Now, the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has rejected the filing of the case affecting the player. According to this, Asencio could have committed a suspected crime of child pornography, punishable by up to five years in prison. According to El Confidencial's explanation in a resolution issued on January 28, the Provincial Court asserts that it is rational to conclude, obviously with the provisionality inherent to this procedural stage, that the appellant indeed received on his mobile phone in June 2023 a video with explicit sexual content starring a 16-year-old minor, who instead of deleting it, shows it to at least one other person. In fact, the person to whom Raúl Asencio allegedly showed the video was the partner of one of the girls who had maintained sexual relationships with their classmates. It was at that moment that the girls became aware of the existence of that video and went to report it to the Civil Guard. Although Asencio did not participate in that sexual activity, as he was elsewhere with a third girl, the judges claim that the Madrid player committed not only the crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, which could be a minor crime, but also the crime of child pornography punishable by one to five years in prison upon displaying that video to a third party, and they add that regardless of the outcome of the investigations agreed in the now questioned auto, they already provide sufficient evidence at this time to reject the request for provisional dismissal instigated in his appeal.

The discussions on citizen security, the application of the law, and the guarantee of the revolving door policy for detained delinquents crossed the thick walls of the building at Comodoro Py 2002 in defiance of a recent resolution that declared unconstitutional the norms that prohibited conditional liberty for detained narcotics traffickers, another chamber of the Federal Chamber of Cassation Penal that had signed that decision resolved the opposite on Monday. With the signature of judges Mariano Borinsky and Javier Carbajo, the Chamber IV of the country's highest penal tribunal validated the rejection of conditional liberty for a person sentenced to 6 years in prison for narcotics trafficking. The case concerns Javier Alejandro Romero, a member of a 14-person criminal organization that was convicted of transporting, storing, distributing, and commercializing narcotics on a wide geographical scale in various jurisdictions across the national territory. With partial dissent from Gustavo Hornos, who did not vote in favor of narco Romero but rather to convene a hearing to address the case, the Supreme Court declared the defense's appeal against the decision of the Federal Criminal Oral Court 1 of Rosario inadmissible. The appeal had been made because, according to his lawyers, Romero met the temporal requirement and the remaining conditions established by Article 13 of the Penal Code. However, Borinsky and Carbajo upheld the rejection of the aforementioned appeal, highlighting among other issues that Romero not only has an absolutely unfavorable report from the detention unit where he is housed, but he is also being processed in another ongoing case in which he is being held in preventive detention. In addition, in that second case, Romero is accused of selling drugs inside the prison where he was serving a sentence that he now wanted to end through conditional release. Beyond the personal luck of the narco-trafficker, the Chamber IV's resolution reveals a deep internal juridical conflict within the Federal Casation Court, where all appeals of the federal oral courts' sentences are processed, which judge crimes of narco-trafficking, human trafficking, and corruption of national public officials. Days ago, with the votes of judges Juan Carlos Gemignani and Angela Ledesma, the Federal Casation Court had ordered Carlos Hernán Beati, who was condemned to six years in prison in 2020 for illegal trafficking of psychotropic substances, to receive the benefit of conditional release that the TOF 3 of San Martín had denied him. The ruling was appealed by the Casation Prosecutor Raúl Pleé, who seeks that the Supreme Court revoke it. The Plea argued that the differentiation in the treatment of convicts for serious crimes is reasonable and justified by the magnitude of the damage that these illicit acts generate in society, and requested that the Chamber of Cassation issue a plenary ruling, that is, that the four chambers of the court convene and unify the criterion that will then be adopted by the Oral Tribunals.

The flow of reports of disappearances of girls and adolescents is becoming increasingly frequent, impacting communities and families. Some appear in distant locations from their home and reveal that they were contacted through social media by unknown individuals who made them attractive offers. The descriptions of how girls and adolescents are captured from the Cyber Space are similar to those of women, girls, and adolescents who are victims of human trafficking for sexual exploitation, child pornography, labor exploitation, and other modalities. The operation of these networks tends to become invisible due to the confused relationship established between the supposed consent or voluntariness of the girls and adolescents, which hides the strategies of manipulation, blackmail, and extortion used to persuade and capture them. In the comments and titles, morbidity towards girls and adolescents is used with complete denial that they are girls and adolescents who do not have tools or guidance to make decisions and are therefore psychologically manipulated by adult aggressive men with psychological violence strategies, such as occurs in sexual abuse and incest. The human trafficking networks operate and have a seemingly invisible fabric with different forms of capturing victims from family relationships, neighborhood relationships, among peers, and social media. In recent years, social media has acquired a predominant role in capturing childhood, adolescence, and adult individuals with apparently attractive monetary offers in exchange for their participation in podcasts, videos, photo sessions, and equally in supposedly artistic activities. One of the main prevention actions that must be developed is education and guidance for the child population, adolescents, and adult caregivers. Deception is one of the main strategies used by these networks, taking advantage of the limited information and guidance that girls and adolescents have about the implicit scheme and its risks. The operation of sex trafficking networks in the country has been analyzed in various studies (Gallardo 2005) (OBMICA 2012) Sorensen (2019) (VargasURL2019) (Vargas and Maldonado 2018) (Vargas, Núñez, and Beltrán 2022). In these, the significant weight of childhood and adolescence exposed daily to the risks of sex trafficking, child pornography, domestic servitude, forced marriage (sold by families to foreign or Dominican adult men), forced begging, and labor exploitation is demonstrated. In the study Luchando contra la marea (Tejeda, Vargas y Martine 2022), the emphasis given by community organizations, NGOs, and government institutions on the relationship between the increased vulnerability of childhood and adolescence to sexual exploitation and the presence of tourist activity in certain municipalities such as Boca Chica, Higüey, Puerto Plata, and Sosúa is presented, where they are captured by adults of Dominican and foreign nationality. The tourist activity in these municipalities invisibilizes the practices of foreign adult men (mainly from the United States and various European countries) who move easily accompanied by adolescents and girls. There is a tendency to blame them or their families for the practices of sexual exploitation and child pornography in which the aggressors and perpetrators incur. In addition to this, there is a lack of awareness about the rights of childhood and adolescence, and a need for mechanisms and protection strategies to be activated for this population. Similarly, prevention, detection, and prosecution of sexual exploitation and trafficking practices that threaten their integrity are necessary. One of the main prevention actions that must be developed is education and guidance for the child, adolescent, and adult caregivers about the capture pathways for sexual exploitation and trafficking and the operation of these networks in their new modalities from the Cyber space. Both the child, adolescent, and adult populations from families, communities, and institutions need tools for this. In the same way, it is essential to highlight that promoting tourism must be accompanied by a more critical perspective that dismantles the sale of the country as a sex tourism destination abroad, and what this implies for our children, girls, and adolescents, as well as a justice system that pursues aggressors regardless of their nationality and economic status with sanctions against corruption and impunity. In the Primer Plano program, an audio recording was played in which Campos defended himself against the claims of his sons, who have supported their sister in her complaint. In his statement, I remember that those women were very young, not adults, I noticed by their facial features. He had many photos of different young girls naked. On the other hand, Pedro Campos remembered warning his father about the safety of his sister, saying I only said that if something happened to Raffaella or something was done to her, I wouldn't forgive him. According to Pedro, his father's reaction was dismissive, referring to Raffaela as a crazy person and a nymphomaniac, and also discrediting his mother, suggesting that the situation was a vendetta motivated by personal hatred. Response from Cristián Campos In response to the statements of his children, Cristián Campos sent an audio to the CHV program, where he refuted the accusations and spoke of a communication strategy against him. In his statement, he said: Regarding the statements of Antonio and Pedro Campos di Girolamo, leaked from the judicial process file against me, released by Canal 13, I feel the need to clarify the following. I have never had any tendency or affinity with a repugnant habit like the one maliciously described by Antonio Campos in his statement. Additionally, Campos criticized the leak of the testimonies, considering it a defamatory strategy and expressed his indignation at what he considers a grotesque fabrication of so much lies and so much desire for discredit. Defense of his character and relationships The actor continued his defense, stating that the material mentioned by Antonio Campos was not what had been suggested. According to him, the material to which Antonio Campos de Girólamo referred in his statement are videos, intimate and personal photographs perfectly normal of habitual and consensual situations between adults. Campos argued that confusing these memories with pornographic material is a distortion of reality. Finally, Cristián Campos described himself as a responsible father, stating My affective and sexual relationships have always been perfectly normal. And I can say, without false modesty, that I have been a very good dad. He also mentioned that he had been present in the upbringing of his children and that he felt hurt by the current situation, where his children have been manipulated against him. The actor concluded his statement reaffirming his position and denying the accusations against him.

data.text: Gender Violence The State Pact asks to eliminate the mitigating factor of confession and damage repair, which Dani Alves benefited from. The agreement increases funding from 1,000 to 1,500 euros for victims of human trafficking, including those who have been subjected to sexual exploitation, forced labor, or other forms of modern slavery. 500 million, proposes psychological assistance for perpetrators of abuse, a universal screening for medical detection, and a responsible for co-education in schools. The new pact against gender violence includes 462 measures and addresses for the first time vicarious, digital, and economic violence. Manifestation on February 1 in Langreo for the murder of Karilena, a 40-year-old woman, allegedly at the hands of her partner. Paco Paredes The proposal for the agreement to renew the state pact against gender violence, which the parties submitted to the Commission on Equality of Congress on Monday, in addition to contemplating for the first time measures against economic, digital, or vicarious violence, as reported by EL PERIÓDICO, contains proposals to strengthen prevention, detection, security, punishment of the aggressor, and integral reparation in a total of 462 measures. The comprehensive report, in which the groups have worked for a year, emphasizes strengthening the actions, teams, coordination, and training of all operators working against all forms of machismo violence, including forced marriage or genital mutilation, although, as there is no agreement among the parties on prostitution, in this area it includes measures against human trafficking for sexual exploitation, pimping, or to discourage demand, but without delving into whether sex work should be prohibited or regulated. In any case, the commitment is such that the state budget allocated for the different administrations to implement the measures agreed upon by the parties goes from the 1,000 euros of the original pact (signed in 2017) to 1.5 billion euros, which will be invested over the next five years. The resolution will be approved, likely with the opposition of Vox, next week in the Congress Equality Commission, and these are some of the main measures it contains. The agreement proposes eliminating the mitigating circumstances of confession and damage repair, which benefited Dani Alves, who saw his conviction reduced for rape after paying 150,000 euros in compensation to the victim. The sentence sparked a storm of criticism because the mitigating circumstance facilitates justice for the wealthy and another for the poor. The agreement also foresees that all processes related to the same victim be tried in a single body, which family courts must consult compulsorily if there are penal processes for gender violence in all processes affecting children or if there are indications of violence, that all the procedures that can complete the victim's statement be carried out, which can retract due to fear of the aggressor, that more resources be given to psycho-social and forensic teams so that they issue their reports without delay, or that the False Syndrome of Parental Alienation (SAP) be eradicated. The agreement proposes incorporating economic, digital, and vicarious violence into the legal framework, that is, the violence exercised against children to harm the mother. These sections take up dozens of new proposals, including the reinforcement of measures aimed at preventing cohabitation or visitation with the aggressor and the need to conduct a paternofilia evaluation prior to the judicial resolution of visits when requested by the victim of gender violence. In addition, the parties propose creating a new crime directly that captures the behaviors that limit the autonomy and economic independence of women and strengthen the penalties for attacks committed through digital means. In the educational field, the pact foresees the promotion of affective-sexual education that is already covered by several laws and that the School Councils designate a teacher responsible for co-education in equality, among other measures. To increase the detection of victims who do not want to report, as most visit the doctor frequently, the agreement requests that a universal screening be established in case it is suspected that a patient's symptoms may be associated with abuse, that the training of healthcare personnel be increased, and that the Comprehensive Care Plan for children of mortal victims include psychological attention for their descendants. Furthermore, it is foreseen that psychological therapy be offered to aggressors who voluntarily request this service. In addition to requesting the full implementation of the yes is yes law, the parties ask that mechanisms be articulated for verifying the age and parental controls to prevent minors from accessing pornography, as also foreseen by the digital protection environment law, which has not yet been approved. In addition, they demand measures, but without specifying how to do so, to prevent platforms like Sugar Daddy or OnlyFans from becoming tools for the sexual exploitation of young people. They also propose training for screenwriters to make audiovisual content free of stereotypes and create the position of intimacy coordinator in audiovisual productions, to respect consent. Without specifying how to implement it, the new pact proposes strengthening the institutional response to address denialism in gender-based violence. And it proposes strengthening the training of workers in the tourism, hospitality, and leisure sectors so that they can detect and act on aggression, as well as for company protocols against sexual harassment to collect data on complaints. Specific measures are also contemplated to protect vulnerable victims such as immigrants, people with disabilities, or to reinforce actions in rural areas.

In Cantabria, a janitor is accused of sexual assault for making unwanted contact with a cleaner while working. The Public Ministry considers these incidents a continuous sex abuse crime, while the private accusation asks that the facts be judged as sexual assault. A janitor at a social center faces an accusation of sexual assault for making unwanted contact with a cleaner at the same center while working. The Provincial Court of Cantabria will judge this Tuesday, February 11, a janitor at a social center for a sex-related crime, accused of making unwanted contact with a cleaner at the workplace. The Prosecution asks for a fine of 6,600 euros for him and two years in prison for the victim, understanding that the incident was a sexual assault. The trial will take place from 10:00 hours in the Third Section, according to information from the High Court of Justice. The defendant allegedly approached the woman while she was working in the men's restroom and lightly bit her neck, attempting to kiss her, which he failed to do as she stepped back and left the bathroom. The next day, when the victim arrived at the center and accessed the reception area to collect the keys to the cleaning room, he grabbed her arm, sat her on his lap, and touched her breasts and buttocks. The judge will decide whether these incidents constitute abuse or sexual aggression. The Prosecution considers these events to be a continued crime of sexual abuse, deserving a fine of 6,600 euros, as well as a one-year ban on communicating and approaching the woman. In terms of civil liability, the prosecution requests that the accused compensate the complainant 1,000 euros for the moral damages caused. On its part, the private prosecution exercised by the woman asks that the facts be judged as sexual aggression and raises the request for sentence to two years of imprisonment, disqualification for performing with minors for a year and a half, and supervised liberty for two years after the completion of the deprivation of liberty. In addition, she requests a compensation of 3,000 euros for moral damage.

A U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agent was arrested on Saturday, February 8, accused of participating in drug and human trafficking on the El Paso border for years, authorities reported. The arrested individual, identified as 32-year-old Manuel Pérez Jr. from El Paso, was caught while still wearing his uniform by agents from the FBI's Border Corruption Task Force in El Paso as part of an investigation involving multiple federal agencies. According to judicial documents, between December 21, 2023, and February 5, 2025, Pérez allegedly facilitated the crossing of vehicles driven by undocumented individuals through the Paso del Norte bridge in downtown El Paso. He is accused of repeatedly allowing the entry of these vehicles as part of a human trafficking network operating for profit. The federal government asserts that Pérez not only allowed these irregular crossings, but also charged for them, turning his position into an illicit business that guaranteed him personal profits. Years of cocaine trafficking In addition to human trafficking, Pérez also faces charges for conspiring to possess and distribute cocaine. According to the indictment, from November 1, 2019, to February 5, 2025, the agent conspired with other individuals to traffic more than five kilograms of cocaine. It is believed that the drug was destined for different distribution points in Texas, Louisiana, North Carolina, and other areas. Corruption and betrayal of the uniform The arrest of Pérez Jr It is the result of an extensive investigation led by the FBI's Task Force on Border Corruption in El Paso, in which several federal agencies participated, including the U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Office of Professional Responsibility, the Department of Homeland Security's Office of the Inspector General, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the Texas Department of Public Safety, and the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. The special agent in charge of the FBI in El Paso, John S. Morales, condemned Perez's actions, stating that the accused violated his oath to protect and serve. Instead of fulfilling his duty, he facilitated human and drug trafficking in our community. His actions not only benefited criminal organizations, but also eroded the public's trust in law enforcement. He soiled the uniform worn with honor by so many others, Morales declared. As the judicial process advances, Pérez remains detained without the right to bail in the El Paso County Jail. To date, no defense attorney's name has been recorded in the court documents. According to the county's public access portal, Pérez is described as a 1.55-meter (5 feet 1 inch) tall individual weighing 127.5 kilograms (281 pounds), also known as Manuel Minjarez. Photos of the agent's arrest in uniform circulated on FitFam El Paso's Instagram page, as he was apprehended at the Paso del Norte bridge in front of dozens of witnesses crossing the border.

This event highlights the grave situation of human trafficking in the country, as well as the relevance of intensifying protection and prevention measures to safeguard the population.

By Ciudad Cero In a span of less than two months, the Secretariat of Public Security (SSP) of Puebla has rescued four minor victims of human trafficking, all from other states. This type of crime, according to authorities, has a particular incidence in the region of Puebla and Tlaxcala, areas that have been identified as critical points in human trafficking. Francisco Sánchez González, head of the SSP, highlighted that these minors are now with their families, representing progress in rescue operations. However, he acknowledged that the phenomenon does not only involve minors, as adults have also been rescued in similar conditions. A relevant case occurred on January 3, 2025, at Bar Barra Bear, where a woman from Veracruz was freed after being a victim of deception related to job offers Vice Admiral Sánchez emphasized the complexity of some cases, especially when victims are adults. Often, individuals involved in exploitation situations are reluctant to leave the places where they are controlled due to emotional manipulation and threats from their aggressors. This challenge requires authorities to intervene with the families, who become essential allies in convincing victims to leave their situation of abuse behind. Human trafficking in Puebla and CJNG control in Puebla and Tlaxcala continue to be focal points regarding human trafficking. Therefore, the SSP has worked in coordination with various sex workers' collectives, seeking both the prevention of the crime and the recognition of the rights of individuals who engage in sex work. The collaboration with these groups has allowed for progress in the identification of victims and the promotion of public policies aimed at their protection. In this context, authorities have also conducted operations in various nightclubs, resulting in the closure of several establishments. However, those responsible for these businesses are addressing the observations made by the Secretariat, and the reactivation of their activities depends on the resolution of these issues.

According to the denunciation, which invokes the Belém do Pará Treaty, Sturzenegger, along with Carlos Ivaldi, Claudio Saffirio, and Gustavo Mastracchio, are accused of repeated carnal access, structural corruption, and institutional violence. The denunciation reports that Camila Lomonaco, Sturzenegger's former secretary and right-hand woman, allegedly discovered irregularities in the approval of millions of dollars in unsecured credits, involving companies such as Mirgor SA and the Palermo Horse Racing Track Society. In response to her repeated internal complaints about these irregularities, the young woman was subjected to a systematic plan of intimidation that culminated in sexual aggressions intended to silence her. The account describes a meeting at the Banco Ciudad headquarters where the complainant was sexually abused by Ivaldi, Mastracchio, and Saffirio, while Sturzenegger, fully aware of the situation, remained impassive and would have encouraged these practices to cover up the irregularities. The minister's behavior is especially scandalous, as in his capacity as head of a major ministry, he is expected to act with transparency and ethics; however, the complaint accuses him of using his position to perpetuate a climate of corruption and abuse, demonstrating an absolute lack of commitment to protecting human rights. Fernando Míguez demands that a criminal investigation be initiated immediately to clarify the responsibility of each of the accused and to take firm measures to put an end to these abuses. The complaint requires the summoning of Sturzenegger and the others involved to testify, as well as the collection of all necessary reports and documentation to dismantle a network of corruption that, apparently, operates with total impunity. The case has generated strong indignation in various sectors, which demand that the principles of ethics, transparency, and justice be restored in public service. The minister's actions, in charge of Desregulation and Transformation of the State, not only call into question his suitability for the position, but also reveal a disturbing institutional corruption that, far from protecting society, seems to design mechanisms to silence and victimize those who dare to report irregularities. Society demands a firm and immediate response to this scenario, in which impunity and institutional violence cannot continue to be the norm.
