Lawyers and specialists in law gathered at the Institute of Comparative Studies in Penal and Social Sciences (INECIP) to comment on the repeated prison breakouts from Buenos Aires police stations. On Sunday, February 9, six prisoners escaped from a police station in the Caballito neighborhood. The National Security Minister, Patricia Bullrich, and her Buenos Aires counterpart, Waldo Wolff, publicly discussed the responsibility for the repeated breakouts that have occurred in recent months. However, neither of them referred to these five key data points to understand the problem of prisoners in police stations in the city:1) The number of prisoners in police facilities in Buenos Aires increased by 136% over the past two years. According to reports from the National Prosecution Office, between October 2022 and October 2024, the number of people detained in police facilities increased by 136%. The police stations are spaces that are not designed for long-term detentions. In the police stations, patios, sheds, offices, and even armory storage rooms are used, with improvised or non-existent security measures. On the other hand, the detention centers, in many cases, were named as such administratively, but in terms of infrastructure, they are the same internal guards of the local police stations with holding cells.2) Ninety percent of the prisoners in police stations and detention centers in the city are at the disposal of the National Justice. According to the National Penitentiary Prosecutor's Office, 90% of the prisoners are at the disposal of the National Justice, 6% are at the disposal of the local justice of the City of Buenos Aires, and 2.4% are at the disposal of the Federal Justice. The City of Buenos Aires is the only one where three different judicial systems intervene. Federal crimes, for example, human trafficking, narcotics trafficking, or corruption linked to the National Public Administration. The Federal Justice, headquartered in Comodoro Py, intervenes in common crimes. For example, thefts, thefts, injuries, threats, and sexual abuse. In all provinces of the country, these crimes are prosecuted and judged by provincial justice. However, in the CABA (Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires), this function is divided between the City Justice. It only intervenes in a few crimes that were transferred to it, such as simple threats or injuries in a brawl. The National Justice intervenes in all crimes that have not been transferred to the City. Judges of the Judicial Power of the Nation, prosecutors of the National Public Prosecutor's Office, and defenders of the National Public Defense Office intervene in all crimes. Although the 1994 constitutional reform established that the City Justice should have its own justice, the transfer of criminal justice was never finalized. For the past 10 years, the Supreme Court has been urging the completion of that process, as it did in the recent Levinas ruling. This exceptionalism of the CABA generates, among other problems, a difficulty in coordination that allows for the establishment of a criminal policy in line with prison capacities and that prevents the use of police stations as detention centers. 3) National Judges were criminally denounced for the degrading situation of detainees in police stations. In December of last year, the INECIP criminally denounced the National Judges of Execution and all those judges responsible for having allowed, through action or omission, for police stations to become centers of cruel, inhuman, and degrading punishments. The denunciation was based on official reports that indicate that thousands of people spend weeks, months, and even years detained in precarious cells, sheds, courtyards, offices, storage rooms, underground areas, and internal police stations or prison administrations, in degrading and inhumane conditions. For example, extreme overcrowding situations were detected, with up to 5 people being held in a cell of 11.5m², or using armories as cells, where detainees spend 24 hours a day locked up without any possibilities for resocialization activities. The National Constitution establishes, in its Article 18, an exceptional measure for compliance with its mandates, the judicial responsibility of judges who order any measure for detained persons, under the pretext of precaution, that leads to their mortification. Behind every detained person is a judicial resolution that validates that detention. If the situation of confinement is degrading, the judge who authorized that detention has penal responsibility. 4) Detentions at police stations increase the risk of escape and reduce police personnel on the streets, affecting citizen security. The one in Caballito was not the first escape from police stations in Buenos Aires, nor will it be the last. The police stations and jailhouses lack security measures, as they were not designed for the current function of incarceration. Many inmates are housed in offices or courtyards without any protective measures. Everything depends on police surveillance, which, with the slightest mistake, facilitates escapes. In recent months, there have been escapes of 6 detainees in Caballito in February, 17 detainees in Liniers in December, and 11 detainees in Barracas in November. 5) The National Congress is on the verge of passing a Reiterance Law that could exacerbate this problem. Last week, the Chamber of Deputies gave a first approval to a law that seeks to introduce a new causal of preventive detention into the Federal and National Penal Codes, distinct from the risk of flight and obstruction of the investigation, which are the only valid risks for our National Constitution and international treaties with constitutional rank. If the project is approved, a person can be detained preventively for merely being investigated in more than one penal cause, regardless of whether they have sufficient evidence or proof. It does not even require formal charges. This law, being national, will only apply to the Federal Justice and the National Justice (until it is transferred to the City). Therefore, the new prisoners this law will generate will worsen the situation in the Buenos Aires police stations. In the Chamber of Deputies, it was not clarified where the new prisoners generated by this law will be housed. Therefore, its approval would only worsen the problem of prisoners in police stations. It would also not provide more security, as it would promote a criminal policy focused on less relevant actors in the criminal markets, instead of prioritizing strong links.

Every minute, four Latin American girls become mothers, warns the UNFPA This happens mostly in Afro-descendant and indigenous communities, where girls lose control of their bodies, evidenced by the UNFPA Regional Director for Latin America and the Caribbean, Susana Sottoli, to EFE. In Latin America and the Caribbean, 36,000 minors under 15 become mothers every year, which means that four girls give birth every minute in the region, warns the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). This happens mostly in Afro-descendant and indigenous communities, where girls lose control of their bodies, evidenced by the UNFPA Regional Director for Latin America and the Caribbean, Susana Sottoli, to EFE. Almost a million young people in Honduras neither work nor study, and 72% of them are women. At the Fifth Regional Conference on Population and Development of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC), Sottoli was in charge of inaugurating and closing the meeting, which dealt with topics such as adolescent pregnancy or maternal mortality. The UNFPA director showed concern for the youngest sector of communities that have less access to medical resources or contraceptive means. For girls between 15 and 19 years old, it is an obstacle to their life projects to have to leave school to take care of their premature children prematurely, the regional director said. However, Sottoli drew attention to the alarming rise in pregnancies among girls under 14 years old, a phenomenon that is directly linked to the violation and sexual abuse, which urgently require a penal approach from the Justice system. Social Inequality According to the 2024 State of the World Population Report by UNFPA, teenage pregnancy is up to twice as common among the poorest adolescents, belonging to rural, indigenous, and Afro-descendant communities in the region. In response to this, the directive stated that Latin America and the Caribbean is a deeply unequal region, not necessarily a poor region in general, but with wealth that is poorly distributed. A woman from these communities is, in turn, three times more likely to die from complications during pregnancy or childbirth than any other woman in the region, something that the jurist finds unacceptable, because science knows how to prevent these deaths, it is a matter of public policy and discrimination. To the situation of women discriminated against racially, another difficulty is added, especially if she is not heteronormative, as they usually suffer greater social exclusion by their own community. State Economy The economy of an entire country loses economically if more women continue to die in childbirth and without more girls continue to become pregnant prematurely, Sottoli said. That's why she mentioned the data from a study by the Population Fund on the opportunity cost of not reducing teenage pregnancy in 14 countries. The figure of what a country loses if this situation remains is 0.28% of the GDP. To illustrate the figure, he added that in Panama, that opportunity cost is equivalent to having the income of the Panama Canal detained for approximately 3 months, knowing that this is the country's economic backbone. The Government of Solidarity joins forces with the hotel sector to prevent and eradicate the sexual and labor exploitation of girls, boys, and adolescents. Through the Executive Secretary of Sipinna, they offer awareness and sensitivity talks directed at the tourism and travel sector in PLAYA DEL CARMEN. The Government of Solidarity, headed by Municipal President Estefanía Mercado, launched, through the Executive Secretary of the System for the Integral Protection of Girls, Boys, and Adolescents (SIPINNA), awareness and sensitivity talks directed at more than 150 hotel staff members of the Grand Riviera Princess, with the objective of preventing the sexual and labor exploitation of girls, boys, and adolescents in the tourism sector. In representation of the Mayor, the honorary president of the Integral Development System for the Family (DIF) of Solidarity, Eduardo Asencio, emphasized the urgency of addressing this issue with the collaboration of the three branches of government and the tourism sector. Child exploitation is a problem that requires an immediate and effective response. It is fundamental that each one of you, as collaborators, join this effort, as your work is crucial in preventing these crimes, he emphasized.POPULATION AT RISK We work for the integrity of the population at risk, conducting constant patrols with the support of various instances at strategic points, he stated. Furthermore, he urged to report any case of child exploitation to the DIF line 984 309 39 48, available 24 hours, to 911 or to make an anonymous denunciation to 089. During the event, Eduardo Asencio thanked Juan Carlos Arte, subdirector of the Grand Riviera Princess hotel, for his commitment to fighting child labor and his zero-tolerance stance on the exploitation of girls, boys, and adolescents. In her intervention, Yamile Domínguez, head of the Executive Secretariat of SIPINNA, highlighted the fundamental role of the tourism sector in preventing and combating child exploitation before the conference. Tourism is a great ally in this cause. It is crucial to incorporate strategies that help detect and eradicate these crimes, as well as prevent their normalization, she expressed. The conference "Tourism Protects Childhood," directed at hotel employees, aimed to raise awareness and train them on preventing child exploitation in the travel and tourism sector, providing them with tools to act appropriately in case of identifying a high-risk situation.

Cristina GallardoFermín de la CalleMadrid11 FEB 2025 1313The Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by Raúl Asencio's defense team. The Real Madrid player is one of four soccer players being investigated for distributing sexual content with a 16-year-old minor. In the ruling, issued on January 28, the three judges assert that there are sufficient rational indications of criminal activity suggesting that the Canarian youth player may have committed both the crimes of disclosure of secrets and child pornography. Asencio's defense team requested the dismissal of the case, arguing that the investigations agreed upon by the investigating judge were being conducted without solid indications of a crime, given the absence of the video in the investigation, and also claimed that the instruction period had expired, according to the Criminal Procedure Law. He argued that since the video could not be recovered by the Judicial Police, its existence and content could not be proven, and there were no evidence linking the footballer to the crime. An unrecovered video The defense argued that since the video was not recovered, there was no evidence of the crime. However, the ruling confirms that the absence of the video file does not mean it never existed and establishes that the crime would have been consummated when the video was shared, even if it was later deleted. Furthermore, an investigated party declared that Asencio showed him the video, which is corroborated by the phone records indicating that he received it via WhatsApp. The judges of the Court of Appeal have rejected these arguments and have imposed the investigated party to assume the procedural costs. Additionally, they emphasize that the investigations were ordered before the deadline expired, making them valid, and add that nothing prevents the opening of a separate file if new lines of investigation appear, which would allow extending the deadline if necessary. The investigation began on September 18, 2023, following a complaint filed by the girl's mother at a Civil Guard outpost in Gran Canaria, accusing the possible dissemination of an explicit sex video starring the minor. The same had been recorded on June 15, and according to the complainant, the relations that occurred in the private area of a leisure venue in the town of Amadores, in the Canary Island municipality of Mogán, had been consensual. What was not consented was the recording of the same. As a result of the complaint, the investigating judge charged four soccer players Raúl Asencio, currently on the first team of Real Madrid, Ferran Ruiz (who plays for Girona), the Galician Juan Rodríguez (Tarazona), and the Balearic Andrés García (Alcorcón).

Human trafficking is constantly reinvented and today it is thriving in the virtual sphere, said Yanina Boschmann. Yanina Boschmann, Coordinator of Prevention, Protection, and Assistance to Victims and Witnesses of Human Trafficking and Trafficking of Persons in the Province, pointed out that this year the main line of action that the team she leads will have is prevention. The goal is to sensitize the population in Misiones about the problem of human trafficking and the exploitation of people, which passes very close to us but which we often do not see. We are in a moment where this scourge is reinvented from the fact that it has greater auge in the virtual sphere, that's why we consider it fundamental to address the issue by talking about methods of care, especially in children, girls and adolescents, she stated to Noticias and Canal 2. In the meantime, the head of the organization under the Vice Governor's office in Misiones added that today, the main method of capturing the most vulnerable population is through digital means such as social media, devices, and gaming sites. For adults, they offer deceptive job offers, and for girls, boys, and adolescents, it is through video game platforms that enable chat or audio videos. This is precisely where the networks that aim to capture victims operate, explained Boschmann. At the same time, she commented that currently, sex trafficking has been almost entirely virtualized since the client is virtual, as is the content being exploited and the currency used for payment. In these cases, assets such as cryptocurrencies or bitcoins are used, which are very difficult to control. Due to these reasons, the fight is now within virtuality, and even though finding a human trafficking network has always been challenging, it is even more difficult now because they have gone virtual, she explained. In this line, she added that in the face of this situation, from the Vice-Governor's office of Misiones, what we are trying to do is focus all prevention efforts on tools for the care of child and adolescent victims of trafficking. They are given talks about the existence of grooming, virtual trafficking, about the existence of malicious individuals, and that these networks operate in this realm, she emphasized.

The Departmental Prosecutor of Tarija, Sandra Gutiérrez, reported that a 28-year-old man, identified as the stepfather of a 12-year-old girl, has been sentenced for the crimes of rape and aggravated sexual abuse. The incident came to light on the past Friday, February 7, 2025, when the victim's mother took her to a hospital due to severe stomach pains the girl was experiencing. Following a medical examination, it was discovered that the minor was pregnant, approximately five months along. In response to this finding, both the mother and the gynecologist who treated the minor began investigating the circumstances of the pregnancy, considering it a serious crime. According to the victim's statement, affected and tearful, she reported that since April 2024, her stepfather had been repeatedly sexually assaulting her, resulting in the pregnancy. Immediately, a formal complaint was filed with the Public Prosecutor's Office, and the corresponding investigations were initiated. The authorities acted with haste, and in less than 48 hours, the stepfather was detained and brought to a hearing on precautionary measures. During the judicial process, the defendant opted for a streamlined procedure, accepting the maximum penalty established by the legal order of 30 years in prison without the right to pardon. The Public Prosecutor rejected any possibility of reducing the sentence, ensuring that the maximum rigor of the law would be applied. Finally, the judge issued an executable conviction sentence, imposing a 30-year prison sentence that the convicted person will serve at Morros Blancos prison. The case has been handled with extreme discretion to protect the identity and rights of the minor, thus avoiding revictimization. The authorities have emphasized the importance of acting quickly and firmly in cases of sexual violence, especially when victims are minors. Gutiérrez stated that this judicial ruling sets a significant precedent in the fight against impunity in cases of child sexual abuse, demonstrating that the justice system can act effectively to ensure that those responsible face the consequences of their actions. Between December 21, 2023, and February 5, 2025, Manuel Pérez Jr. allegedly attempted to smuggle undocumented non-citizens into the United States for commercial advantage and private financial gain. The indictment alleges that, in multiple cases, Pérez Jr. admitted a vehicle driven by an undocumented non-citizen at the Paso Del Norte port of entry as part of human smuggling operations. Additionally, Pérez Jr. allegedly accepted payment from the undocumented non-citizens for his role in facilitating their entry into the United States. Pérez Jr. allegedly conspired to possess a substance containing at least five kilograms of cocaine from November 1, 2019, to February 5, 2025, to distribute it throughout Texas, Louisiana, North Carolina, and other areas. Pérez Jr. is charged with one count of conspiracy to bring aliens to the United States for financial gain, three counts of bringing aliens to the United States for financial gain, and one count of conspiracy to possess a controlled substance with the intent to distribute. If convicted, Pérez Jr. faces up to five years in a federal prison for the human trafficking conspiracy charge, three to 10 years in prison for each of the three additional human trafficking charges, and 10 years to life in prison for the drug trafficking charge. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the United States Sentencing Guidelines and other legal factors. In Migrations of Puerto Chalanas in Aguas Blancas, the Modular Office of the Safe Spaces program for the protection of victims of human trafficking and smuggling of migrants is already operational. The inauguration was headed by Governor Gustavo Sáenz and Minister of Security Patricia Bullrich, who agreed that the crime is one of the worst forms of crime. The new office is part of the Plan Güemes, which was launched two months ago in this same location. This is another step, Sáenz said, and stated that the Plan Güemes is more than a national security plan, it is a joint working strategy for relentless combat against organized crime, narcotics trafficking, contraband, human trafficking, and related crimes. The Governor highlighted the Government's commitment to the northern border and especially to Bullrich. It's the first time in our history that a National Security Minister has been here so many times in this hot border, she assured. In addition, he emphasized that the implementation of the Plan Güemes is involving a significant increase in the number of investigative procedures. Regarding this, the Minister specified that in this time 55 cases, 87 procedures, of which 46 are related to sexual exploitation, especially of minors under 16, and labor exploitation, and the rest are still to be determined. There are criminals capable of kidnapping children and inventing stories or at gunpoint, she indicated. Therefore, it is a sensitive task in the border area of one of the most terrible forms of slavery, considered Bullrich. Therefore, Sáenz stated that our border should be an absolutely secure area, there is no room for criminals, but also, we are here to protect the most vulnerable. And he added Today that there is a national government that listens to us, I ask all the political leaders to put aside their party affiliations and not use issues of narcotics trafficking, human trafficking, and organized crime to make politics. We must be more united than ever. In the same vein, Bullrich stated We are proud of what we are doing here. We want to improve the lives of the citizens of Aguas Blancas and Orán. We work to save the victims of this modern exploitation. The Deputy Director of the National Directorate of Migrations, Mariano Goyenechea expressed that this safe space is for the protection of the victims of crimes linked to organized crime that requires joint efforts to detect them, identify the victims, and prosecute the perpetrators. The northern border areas of our country in general, and in this case in Aguas Blancas and Puerto Chalanas in particular, constitute critical areas for recruitment, transportation, and exploitation, which obliges us to strengthen alert and response mechanisms for these problems. I am pleased that we have a place where victims can be protected until the national system for the protection of victims and trafficking can truly reassign them, give them the security and tranquility that it will not happen again, and that they can truly feel safe. Here in Aguas Blancas there is an extensive border that is being patrolled because we work to care for those who are victims, said the Minister of Security. The head of the Mission in Argentina of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), Alejandro Guidi, highlighted this comprehensive approach by national, territorial, public security, and civil society authorities, which is the most opportune, with the idea of easy identification of victims to act accordingly. During the inauguration ceremony, the delegate of Aguas Blancas, Adrián Zigarán, the mayor of Orán, Baltasar Lara Gros, the secretary of the Fight against Narcotrafficking and Organized Crime, Martín Berrier, the Minister of Security and Justice of the Province, Gaspar Solá Usandivaras, were present. Additionally, the operational director of the Executive Committee to Combat Human Trafficking and Exploitation and to Protect and Assist its Victims, Verónica Toller, the National Deputy, Pamela Calletti, provincial and federal justice authorities, Gendarmerie chiefs, and others were present.

Gustavo Batallán and Luis Monjes, the accusers The Catamarca priest Eduardo López Márquez will be the first priest in all of Argentina to be put on trial by a jury and could set a judicial precedent in the province and in the country. Against him, serious accusations are weighing for sex crimes against two seminarian children, now adults. In 2018, this priest was sentenced to 25 years in prison for having outraged 25 seminarian children. The priest is serving his sentence at home, with an electronic ankle bracelet, and Pope Francis withdrew his clerical status. This was reported yesterday through a press conference convened by the Network of Survivors of Ecclesiastical Abuse. Press conference with Hernán Rausch, of the Network of Survivors of Ecclesiastical Abuse After several instances, the case finally entered the Office of Court Management (OGA) of the Judicial Power at the end of last December to process the trial by jury. This will take place in La Paz and according to the OGA's agenda, it could be confirmed by mid-year. In this case, prosecutor Virginia Duarte Acosta charged López Márquez with three different incidents, as the abuse was continuous over time. For a second incident, he was charged with sexual abuse with carnal access, qualified by the situation of guardianship and committed by a cult minister, as an author, and aggravated corruption of minors due to the victim's age, as an author. The third fact attributed to him is sexual abuse with carnal access, qualified by the situation of guardianship and committed by a cult minister, as an author, and corruption of minors as an author, in ideal concurrence. The prosecutor also emphasized that these are three facts in real concurrence. During his statement, the priest kept silent. These incidents allegedly occurred between 2002 and 2003, when the victim was 12 years old. The priest has other open cases that have not reached trial. The second complaint was filed in March 2023 for outrages that would have occurred between 1997 and 2001 in Capayán. In this case, the priest has not yet been questioned. In both cases, López Márquez had raised prescription, so the judicial process had to go through several instances. It is essential that you join the support we need. We appreciate that (Hernán) is with us. It is essential. His case is similar to ours. His support is essential for our cases to move forward. I have the support of my family at every stage. It is difficult and we know that the trial is coming, expressed Luis. In turn, Gustavo commented on the expectations for the realization of a trial by jury. It will be difficult for me because it will be the first time I will be in a trial and I really have a bit of fear, but I will be able to overcome it, it will cost me a lot, he stated. Despite the nerves, he also assured feeling positive, waiting for justice to be served and trusting in the Justice. The jury trial will take place in La Paz. In relation to the second case, the prescription was rejected. They must be investigated and charged. We must separate. The Church institution does an important social work. The pedophile clergy are a negative factor. Many people have distanced themselves from the Church due to the damage they cause to the institution. One of the great factors of the Church's loss are the sex offenders against children that the Catholic Church has, commented the plaintiff's lawyer Sebastián Ibáñez. The starting point for the victims is to look in the mirror and say to myself they did it to me. From there, we advance because we cannot go back. It depends on us. It is very difficult to prove it. An abuser will not do it in public, commented Hernán during the press conference. data.text: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) expressed its shock and concern on Monday, February 10, over the discovery of more than 40 bodies of migrants in two mass graves found in Libya. Although the causes of death are still unknown, some bodies showed bullet impacts, according to the IOM. Following the discovery of two mass graves in the Libyan desert, the IOM, a United Nations agency for migration, issued a statement expressing its shock over the discovery, as well as revealing that local authorities found bullet wounds on some of the exhumed bodies. The IOM has expressed its shock and concern over the discovery of two mass graves in Libya containing the bodies of dozens of migrants, some with bullet wounds, as stated in the organization's statement, detailing that the graves were discovered by authorities during a crackdown on the site of operations of a human trafficking gang in the country. On February 6, local authorities reported the discovery of the first clandestine grave in the town of Jakharrah, in southeastern Libya, where 19 bodies were found. The second grave was discovered on February 9 in the surroundings of the Kufra desert, also in southeastern Libya, where authorities recovered at least 30 corpses. The Agency for Combating Irregular Immigration in Eastern Libya warned that the number of bodies in the second grave could exceed 70. The causes of death are still unknown, but Libyan authorities stated that they could have been victims of a human trafficking network. The National Police reported the detention of three people allegedly linked to the criminal network. In late January, Libyan Justice confirmed the release of 263 migrant individuals from Eritrea and Somalia who were being held in extremely deficient human and health conditions by a group of traffickers within Alwahat province in the northeast of the country. On the other hand, the IOM called on Libyan authorities to ensure a dignified recovery, identification, and transfer to their countries of origin, so their families can give them a dignified burial. Read alsoLibya finds 28 bodies of migrants near an illegal detention centerThe migrants' fear of the Libyan nightmareLibya has become a hotspot for African migration flows, composed of people fleeing instability in neighboring countries such as Chad or Sudan, and seeking to reach Libyan coasts to embark on a journey across the Mediterranean to Europe. According to IOM data, Libya hosts around 720,000 migrant individuals from 44 countries, mostly Africans and especially Sudanese, who are fleeing a conflict rooted years ago. Migrants and asylum seekers, including children, detained arbitrarily in facilities controlled by armed groups affiliated with both governments or smugglers and traffickers, have suffered inhumane conditions, torture, forced labor, and sexual aggression, Human Rights Watch mentioned in a recent report addressing the situation of migrants in Libya. In March 2024, Libyan authorities reported the discovery of 65 lifeless bodies of migrant individuals in another mass grave in the southern region of the territory. Among the 965 reported deaths and disappearances of migrants in Libyan territory, 22% of them occurred on land routes, as revealed by the IOM. With EFE, Reuters, and local media.

Current News  Deputy Jorge Durán responds to sexual abuse accusation, accused by his ex-partner Constanza Vásquez of extortion  AGENCY UNO  Deputy Jorge Durán defended himself against the accusation of sexual abuse by his ex-partner, arguing that the intimate encounter was consensual during a celebration at his home. Durán stated that after refusing to rekindle the relationship, the accuser demanded money from him and accused him of extortion and theft, and he first filed a complaint for those crimes. The parliamentarian claimed to have handed over evidence to the authorities and put himself at the disposal of the Public Ministry to clarify the facts.  Developed by Bío Bío Comunicaciones  Deputy Jorge Durán defended himself after it was made public in the last hours that his ex-partner had accused him of a crime of sexual abuse.  Let's recall that, according to the background, the criminal act would have occurred in the early hours of Saturday, February 8th, at the parliamentarian's home, located in the Colina commune. In response to this, Durán issued a public statement in which he confirms that there was indeed an intimate encounter with his ex-partner, which he claims was consensual. Last Friday, during a celebration at my home, my ex-partner voluntarily participated in the gathering alongside other guests. That night, we shared an intimate moment in a consensual manner. The following day, in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch, maintaining a cordial coexistence, he stated. In the written statement, the parliamentarian recounts that after this encounter, he clarified to the complainant that the sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, at which point she would have demanded money from him. My ex-partner began demanding a sum of money from me, claiming that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the one to suffer the consequences, he reported. In response to this extortion situation and after discovering that my former partner had used one of my credit cards without my authorization, I proceeded to file a complaint for extortion and theft with the Carabineros on Monday evening. The authorities arrived at my residence, where relevant information was gathered, he added. Durán mentions that he filed a complaint against his former partner for extortion before she filed a complaint for sexual abuse. To my surprise, after my complaint, my former partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, which has created a completely distorted situation and has significantly affected my public image, he expressed. Finally, the parliamentarian stated that he has provided all necessary evidence and is at the disposal of the Public Ministry with the goal of having the facts investigated. I trust that justice will clarify the facts and that the truth will be revealed, he concluded.

On Monday, the Attorney General of Salta, Pedro García Castiella, participated in the inauguration of the Safe Site for Victims of Trafficking at the Migration Office in the port of Chalanas. Accompanied by the National Minister of Security, Patricia Bullrich, and the Governor of the province, Gustavo Sáenz, the event brought together national, provincial, municipal authorities and representatives of the security forces. The act took place at 10:59 a.m., with the presence of prominent figures in the justice and security field, who toured the facilities of the 28 de Julio Post of the National Gendarmerie, where equipment was also handed over for the protection of victims of trafficking. The Safe Site aims to provide an adequate space to assist people affected by this crime, improving the conditions of security and attention for victims. The initiative responds to a joint commitment of the different levels of government to strengthen the fight against human trafficking and ensure the comprehensive protection of victims.

Former Deputy Germán Kiczka and his brother Sebastián have been detained since August 2024 after remaining fugitives for several days. The charges against Germán and Sebastián Kiczka, accused of the crime of possession and distribution of child sexual abuse material, were elevated to trial after the announcement by Judge of Instruction N4 Miguel Ángel Faría. The brothers have been detained since August 2024 after remaining fugitives from justice for several days. Germán was found in Corrientes, while Sebastián, who is also to be judged for a case of abuse, was captured in Misiones. Since August, both have been housed in the penitentiary unit of the locality of Cerro Azul, accused of possession and distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and of sexual abuse, in the case of Sebastián. According to the details, neither of the parties objected, so it has already been confirmed that the investigation was elevated to trial. The only thing left to know is when the debate will take place. Both were arrested after an extensive international investigation, called Digital Guardians of Childhood, in which it was exposed that there was a human trafficking network in several countries, one of them being Argentina. After several months of research, it was confirmed that the former deputy from Misiones and his brother were involved in the possession and distribution of child abuse material. It was confirmed that on Germán's computer, 603 files of a sexual nature were found, although in other raids it was announced that 913 files were found on additional devices. At the beginning of September 2024, the provincial Legislature met and formalized Germán's expulsion from the Activar party as a deputy due to the aberrant facts that involve his criminal actions.

PDI Investigates Sexual Abuse Allegations Against Deputy Jorge Durán (RN)During the early hours of this Tuesday, the PDI arrived at the residence of Deputy Jorge Durán (RN) in the Colina commune, to conduct investigative proceedings following a sexual abuse complaint filed against him. According to preliminary information, the alleged incidents occurred on the previous Friday and the victim reportedly filed the complaint during the first hours of this Tuesday. The Prosecution Office instructed the Sexual Crimes Brigade to oversee the investigation to clarify the events. It is essential to note that the authorities must verify the accusations against the parliamentarian. At this point, it has been reported that the deputy has not been detained and remains at his residence in the Chicureo sector, where the PDI is conducting relevant inquiries.

In Guayas, on Monday, February 10, a suspect was sentenced to 17 years in prison for allegedly committing the crime of sexual abuse of a child. The Guayas Penal Court heard this case through the anticipated testimony of the victim and her mother, as well as other crucial and documentary evidence. Authorities handed down a sentence to Danny Orlando Z. Ch., to 17 years and four months in prison for sexually abusing a minor who was 5 years old at the time. On June 2, 2023, the victim's mother filed a complaint with the Prosecution Office, according to the woman, the perpetrator was a family acquaintance who took advantage of the victim's grandmother having a medical appointment to be alone and commit the crime. Afterward, the infant managed to escape and locked herself in her room to avoid the accused from causing her harm. Once she told her mother what had happened, she indicated that this was not the first time the abuse had occurred at the hands of Danny Z. It is in this way that the victim's mother immediately notified the authorities and alerted the Police to apprehend them in flagrante. During the trial hearing, the prosecutor presented the investigative reports, the recognition report of the crime scene, medical, psychological, and social environment reports, the victim's mother's complaint, twelve witnesses, and other evidence. After evaluating the evidence, the Court issued a condemnatory sentence against the perpetrator and ordered the payment of 80 Unified Basic Salaries, that is, USD 36,800 as a fine. In addition, the defendant must pay USD 4,000 as integral compensation for the victim. Furthermore, it was ordered that the minor undergo psychological and educational rehabilitation through the Ecuadorian Center for the Promotion and Action of Women (CEPAM). The case was processed based on the provisions of Article 170, third paragraph of the Integral Organic Penal Code (COIP), which sanctions sexual abuse with ten to thirteen years in prison. In addition, aggravating circumstances from Article 48, number 9 were applied, increasing the imposed sentence.

In an operation conducted in the vicinity of the Simón Bolívar International Airport, in the Carlos Soublette parish, Vargas municipality, La Guaira state, a commission of the Scientific, Penal, and Criminal Investigations Body (Cicpc) arrested Saifrenys Neimar de La Caridad Cedeño Sánchez, 19 years old, on charges of human trafficking. According to Cicpc Director Douglas Rico, thanks to an exhaustive investigation that included phone and computer expertises, it was possible to establish a direct connection of the woman with a network of criminals operating from Spain. These individuals, under the promise of a better life and economic stability, would lure their victims before sending them to that European country. Once in the European country, the victims were provided with air tickets and passports to exploit them sexually, profiting at the expense of their physical and mental integrity, added Rico. As part of the collected evidence, the Municipal Police's K-9 unit seized three mobile units and two passports from the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. All these items, along with the detained individual, were turned over to the Fourth Prosecutor's Office of the Public Ministry of the Penal Judicial Circumscription of the state of La Guaira, to continue with the investigations and corresponding legal proceedings. State and Attorney General's Office (FGE) Rescue 11 Kidnapped Persons FGE Reports Other Actions By Juan José García Amaro. Authorities Seize Narcotics Worth Over $1.5 Million Detain BOI Cells in Guachochi, Six Violence Generators Arrested in Ciudad Juárez Detain Three with Firearms in Ciudad Juárez Notified Arrest Order for Criminal Objective Sentenced for Murder and Injuries in a Fight Sentenced Aggressor of a Minor in Jiménez Charged with Family Violence, Injuries, and Liberty Deprivation Elements of the State Security Public Secretariat (SSPE) and the State Attorney General's Office (FGE), dismantled a kidnapping gang and managed the rescue of 11 people who were being held hostage in a safe house in Ciudad Juárez. In the first case, on February 1, members of the criminal gang demanded 6 million pesos from a family in exchange for not killing one of the victims, who were being held by 6 subjects detained in two operations. In a second incident registered on February 4, the group of attackers entered a residence while posing as security agents, kidnapping a victim to demand a ransom of the same amount, it was highlighted. The situations mentioned earlier led analysts from the Centinela Platform and police detectives from the SSPE, in coordination with analysts from the State Attorney General's Office, to generate the necessary intelligence and exact tracing to identify two of the suspected perpetrators, who, upon being intercepted by the police, were identified as Yair Omar T. V. and Aldo Alexis C. V. They also detained 81 people, 73 for common law crimes and 8 for federal crimes. Elements from the Interinstitutional Operational Bases participated in these actions. Elements from the Army, National Guard (GN), and the State Secretary of Public Security (SSPE) participated in these deployments.Luis Ángel Aguirre Rodríguez, undersecretary of State Major of the SSPE, reported that on February 4, three people were detained, and four rifles, 16 magazines, 709 cartridges, and three tactical vests were seized. The individuals were taken to the FGR facilities in Parral, as one of them is the leader of a criminal cell.On February 5, two people from a criminal group were detained, and four long arms, 18 magazines, 580 usable cartridges, and two tactical vests were seized. Through the Centinela Platform, it was confirmed that the vehicles are involved in an illegal deprivation of liberty that occurred in December 2024. Two packages of cocaine, two firearms, 14 usable cartridges, a 2021 red Silverado model, and a 2017 blue-marine Versa model vehicle were secured, he said. Agents from the State Investigative Agency of the North District Attorney's Office served a warrant to a known criminal target at the Tlalnepantla Penitentiary and Reintegration Center in the State of Mexico, to notify Salvador M. S., alias El Lápiz, of an arrest warrant for the attempted murder charge. On December 27, 2018, Salvador M. S. arrived with several individuals at the intersection of Lucero and Claudio de Lorena streets in the Parajes del Sol neighborhood of Ciudad Juárez, where they exited their vehicle and fired a firearm at the unidentified victim, it was reported. Following the notification of the arrest warrant issued by a Control Judge of the Bravos Judicial District, he will be presented at the initial hearing, where the public prosecutor of the Specialized Unit for Investigating Crimes Against Life will formulate an accusation against him for the aforementioned incidents. In a special abbreviated procedure, the District Attorney's Office of Zona Sur obtained a condemnatory sentence of three years and six months in prison, issued against the defendant Rommel Michael J. G., for the aggravated crime of sexual abuse. Derived from the evidence presented against him, the accused accepted responsibility for the events that occurred on November 4, 2024, in which he sexually assaulted a minor in a residence in the Centro neighborhood, in the city of Jiménez. He is being prosecuted for family violence, injuries, and deprivation of liberty. The Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Attention to Women Victims of Crime due to Gender and Family Reasons, established the probable responsibility of Ángel de Jesús D. The Attorney General's Office of the Nation brought charges against a man in Santa Rosa de Lima (Bolívar), who allegedly committed the crimes of sexual acts with a minor under 14 years old aggravated and soliciting commercial sexual exploitation of a person under 18 years of age. According to the investigation, the defendant, a 69-year-old man, between August and September 2021, allegedly committed sexual touching of a 9-year-old neighbor on at least three occasions. The incidents were reported in the Montebello neighborhood. Pursuant to a judicial order, the now implicated man was apprehended by the National Police in a public street of the municipality. A woman identified as Mariangel Victoria González Rodríguez (18), who pretended to be a victim of sexual abuse, was detained by officials from the Scientific, Penal, and Criminal Investigations Body (Cicpc), assigned to the Municipal Delegation of Maturín. The Cicpc reported that investigations into the case and technical-scientific expertises were initiated after the victim, accompanied by her representatives, moved to the police station where she reported being a victim of a bus driver and a bus collector. According to the young woman, she boarded the unit after leaving Rómulo Gallegos University, located in Las Cocuizas, with the intention of traveling to her home during the journey, noticed that the other passengers got off and began to cough, losing consciousness, and woke up on the banks of the main avenue of La Pica, without a shirt. In addition, she stated that upon arriving at her residence and after showering, she noticed that she had bleeding and pain in her intimate area, informing her parents and aunts, who reside with her, that she had been a victim of sexual abuse by the bus driver and collector, which is why they are heading to the Cicpc to file a complaint. The officials conducted thorough and exhaustive investigations after González failed to attend the respective forensic medical examination, where a gynecological exam was requested to confirm the truth of what had occurred, which raised the suspicions of the detectives, determining that González had fabricated the crime due to fear of her family. Detectives were able to verify that on that day, the young woman had stayed with her sentimental partner with whom she had engaged in sexual relations, returning home late at night. It was also known that throughout the year, this woman had not presented herself to the university. The case was handed over to the First Prosecution Office of the Public Ministry of the Monagas state.

data.text: The city of Santiago de los Caballeros has been marked in recent years by loud cases of transnational structures linked to illicit trafficking and human trafficking, which exploit their victims laborally and sexually, regardless of their age. From the Public Ministry, dozens of organizations have been impacted that are dedicated to that scourge with national children, girls, adolescents, and adults, as well as migrants from countries such as Haiti, Venezuela, Colombia, and other nations. One of those dismantled networks is that of a Dominican who supposedly trafficked in children, sons of Haitian citizens, whom he forced to beg on the streets like beggars. According to the investigative body, the accused Franklin Agustín brought minors from Haiti under the promise of a better life. However, he forced the victims to ask for money to profit from the collected funds. Immigrants were required to pay a daily fee to the leader of the dismantled structure in 2023 for housing, food, and their stay in the national territory. Another case related to minors involves Juan Carlos Sosa Bencosme, accused of sexually exploiting several Dominican adolescents. The accusatory file indicates that Sosa Bencosme induced the minors, aged between 14 and 15 years, to engage in sexual relations with clients he previously selected in exchange for cash that he managed and decided how much to give to the victims. The testimonies of the young women used by Juan Carlos reveal that the accused recruited them and, after convincing them to join the business, threatened them to continue and remain silent. Operation Lotus Flower The illicit trafficking and human trafficking networks that have been uncovered in Santiago also include women who travel to the country, deceived, as well as voluntarily, in search of a better future, to engage in prostitution. In the year 2024, the Public Ministry launched Operation Lotus Flower, where 45 women were rescued, 43 of whom were Colombian and two were Venezuelan, who were allegedly being sexually exploited and held captive in various apartments in residential complexes in the Gurabo community, in the northern part of Santiago. According to the MP, Junior David Matos Monegro, known as Junior, and Estarly Almanzar Perez were leading that organization dedicated to recruiting women. Both men, who are being processed in the courts, had control over the identifications of some of the victims. The factual document reports that the defendants were the ones receiving the payment from the clients of the trafficked individuals, whom they presented with a catalog of sexual services and prices to be paid through the WhatsApp messaging platform. The defendants traveled to Colombia to select and recruit their victims, covering migration and housing costs, thereby indebting the victims, who were forced to engage in sex work under conditions set by them to settle these economic commitments.Human Trafficking of Haitians For decades, Santiago has also been one of the main destinations for Haitian migrants in the country. Citizens of the neighboring nation arrive in that Cibaeña demarcation by paying high sums of money to organized structures dedicated to human trafficking, violating human dignity. The traffickers, allegedly act on multiple occasions with the complicity of authorities, transport up to 20 people inside vehicles that have a capacity for only five passengers. Moreover, on motorcycles they manage to cross remote towns that connect the towns of the Northwest line with the heart city. Fares A source with knowledge of the trafficking, informed Panorama that currently Haitians are paying RD$10,000, RD$12,000, and RD$15,000 to be transported from the North border strip of the Dominican-Haitian border to Santiago and other localities in the region. In 2024, one of those structures that traffics undocumented Haitians was dismantled in the municipality of Navarrete. That organization, made up of 10 people, is defined by the Santiago Prosecutor's Office as a mafia structure (currently with coercive measures), which was used for human trafficking, where they would smuggle undocumented individuals across the border in an irregular manner, hiding them in shacks, cabins, farms, and other places they had set up for these purposes, and then redistribute them, according to the interest of the person being trafficked and how much they could pay in exchange. They are attributed with the deaths of 13 Haitians, which occurred in August 2023, when the truck they were being smuggled in caught fire and fell into an irrigation canal along the Peñuela-Navarrete highway. Authorities SpeakFor the prosecutor of Santiago, Osvaldo Bonilla, one of the most heinous crimes committed is human trafficking and the exploitation of people, as it severely and directly violates the rights of individuals who are the victims of these crimes, but also negatively impacts the security and identity of the nation. He states that those who are typically targeted are women, who are converted by these structures into objects for sexual and commercial purposes. Traffickers take advantage of a need, a vulnerable state of individuals, and they commit the crime to generate a commerce around this practice, he indicates.The judicial official explains that usually the trafficker contacts the person being trafficked, and this person in turn agrees to pay exorbitant sums for it. Bonilla states that, in most of the dismantled structures, they are led by Dominican citizens who do not think about how they are affecting the identity of their country, by earning illicit money. The official understands that it is necessary to continue raising awareness among all actors (judges, prosecutors, military, and police) so that they apply the drastic sanctions contemplated by the regulations. Additionally, he expresses the need to guide the population, especially the transportation sector, so that they can identify when they are facing a possible trafficked person, or when the routes are being used for trafficking. The prosecutor highlights that for the current year 2025, they project strengthening the investigation and prosecution teams, in order to continue impacting these mafia groups of traffickers and those who associate with them. To that end, she said they are coordinating with the General Directorate of Migration (DGM), the Dominican Republic Army (ERD), and the National Police, the policy of interception and judicialization of cases in flagrante delito presented by the security agencies of the State, and working structures alongside the Special Prosecutor's Office against Human Trafficking and Smuggling of Persons functioning at the national level.Human Rights The crime of human trafficking and smuggling constitutes one of the great concerns of the organization Hispanos Unidos por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos. Rebeca Henríquez, representative of that entity in the country, explained that from the institution they work permanently on denouncing that crime. She says that most of the cases they attend are related to women and girls linked to the sex industry. In conversations with victims, Colombian, Venezuelan, and Haitian women, Henríquez says that a large percentage of them tell her that they were deceived into coming to the country with offers to work in the formal job market (bars and restaurants). When they are here, they often withhold their documents, according to what they have told us, so that their handlers can have control, the activist explains. Henríquez highlights that the organization Hispanos Unidos por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos accompanies the victims in the psychological and legal aspects when they decide to file a complaint with the competent authorities. A historical scourge The sociologist Víctor Burgos stated that the illicit crime of human trafficking and trafficking is a problem that has existed since ancient times, evolving through the different stages of history and adapting to the social, economic, and cultural contexts of each era. The expert reports that the main historical causes of human trafficking include the demand for cheap labor in agriculture, mining, and construction. He also notes that as a professor at the Autonomous University of Santo Domingo (UASD), the current form of trafficking takes various forms, with sexual exploitation standing out. He asserts that women, girls, and children are forced into the sex industry. The phenomenon also occurs in child labor exploitation. He understands that despite legal progress, human trafficking remains a lucrative activity for criminal networks, generating billions of dollars annually and leaving millions of victims worldwide. He argues that socio-economic factors, inequality, violence, and corruption have created a conducive environment for the expansion of this crime in the region, particularly in the Dominican Republic. SuggestionsThe sociologist considers that the effective implementation of policies and comprehensive attention to the problem are still the greatest challenges to face this scourge. He understands that authorities must attack the root of the situation, strengthening judicial and security institutions. Similarly, he suggests establishing prevention campaigns focused on vulnerable communities, as well as expanding protection and comprehensive assistance programs for victims. He also expresses the need for international organizations to offer greater cooperation to dismantle transnational structures.Judicial PrecedentsOne of the first cases of Human Trafficking and Smuggling of Persons that transcended in Santiago was the one known as Bahamas by the Public Ministry, which involves 18 people in a transnational criminal network dismantled in 2019, and whose final trial has not yet concluded. The prosecuting organ indicates that the group constitutes a large extortion organization, linked to the falsification of travel documents of various countries and diplomatic missions established in Santiago, Dominican Republic, as well as the possession and carrying of firearms without authorization. Among those linked to that network, still in the process of judicialization, are seven inspectors from the General Directorate of Migration (DGM). Lawyer José Gregorio Vásquez, legal representative of one of the defendants in that process, questions the slowness with which the Bahamas case and other cases linked to illicit trafficking and human trafficking are progressing. He reports that in 2022, he received a dismissal in favor of his represented party in the case in question, a decision that was appealed by the Public Ministry, without that appeal being known to this day. Attributes the delay to the lack of interest from judicial authorities after the cases stop being front-page news in the media. In the Santiago judicial district, there are other precedents of the illicit in question, in which the Public Ministry has achieved convictions. Among them stands out the 15-year prison sentence imposed on Amaury Amado Tejada de la Cruz for illicit trafficking of migrants and falsification of public and private documents, including identification, property titles, passports, and visas from various countries, including the United States, Spain, Panama, Venezuela, Chile, Costa Rica, among others. Another sentence achieved 20, 15, 10, and 7 years in prison for aggravated trafficking of persons, money laundering, and other illicit activities, was the judicial process known as Casa Blanca Night Club. The women, Colombian and Venezuelan citizens, were sexually exploited to profit, affecting the dignity of the victims. Penalties The Law 13,703 on Illicit Trafficking of Migrants and Human Trafficking is a tool that allows judicial actors to employ better tools in the pursuit and judicialization of the criminal structures dedicated to this illegal practice. The law contemplates severe penalties against human trafficking and migrant trafficking, with penalties ranging from 10 to 20 years. The Puebla State Public Safety Secretariat (SSP) reported that in less than two months, they rescued four minors who were victims of human trafficking. These actions are part of the SSP's efforts to combat this crime in the entity. According to the Secretary of Public Safety for the entity, Francisco Sánchez González, the minors are now with their families and came from other entities, which is not unusual in the crime of human trafficking between Puebla and Tlaxcala. We have rescued, in our time, four minors and have handed them over to their families. Yes, they are from other states. You know that there are some indicators that both Tlaxcala and Puebla have us focused on as a trafficking zone, so yes, we are seeking to establish a connection (between authorities), Sánchez González indicated. In addition to the minors, the SSP also rescued some adult victims of human trafficking. One of those cases was that of the Bar Barra Bear bar, where they rescued a woman who had arrived from Veracruz looking for work. The SSP highlighted that there are cases in which the victims refuse to leave the place where they are being sexually exploited due to emotional manipulation, therefore, the authority resorts to the families to rescue them, providing them with all the necessary legal support. As an authority, when the person is an adult, we have certain limitations. What we are looking for is for the family to approach them and try to convince them, we provide them with all the necessary legal support, to be close to them, but in many of the cases, the will of those people (the victims) has a lot to do with it, Sánchez González declared. In this sense, Sánchez González stated that he had already met with a collective of sex workers who seek to avoid manipulation in the exercise of their profession, and they have already been channeled to the State Attorney General's Office (FGE) to address this issue.

Armie Hammer has repeated his denial of allegations that he is a cannibal and that he sexually abused several women. The actor was speaking on Louis Theroux's podcast on Spotify and responded to Theroux's direct question, "Are you a cannibal, Hammer?" Hammer replied, "You know what you have to do to really be a cannibal? You have to eat human flesh. So, no." Hammer was accused of rape and physically abusive behavior in 2021 by a woman known as Effie, who claimed that he raped her in 2017, and shared screenshots of graphic text messages that she alleged were sent by Hammer, including one in which the actor appeared to declare himself a cannibal. Subsequently, at least two other women presented allegations of sexual coercion and emotional abuse by Hammer between 2017 and 2020, including his former girlfriend Paige Lorenze. Hammer told Theroux that he wouldn't discuss the messages, but that they formed one side of a conversation, and that it was funny to joke about whether he was high or drunk or laughing while writing these messages. Hammer also denied having eaten the entire heart of an animal, saying "take a bite of the heart and you've got all your friends around you, inciting you, it's like a man almost too loaded with a rite of passage when you go hunting for the first time." Everyone I know who went hunting for the first time had to do something similar. The actor denied that his behavior was criminal. I left many people in that wake very angry with me because of my behavior, idiot behavior. There's no way to avoid that, it makes me a complete idiot. As for me, I don't have a problem admitting that. I was an idiot. That's not illegal. Hammer said that after the scandal broke and much of his acting work was canceled, he entered a trauma treatment center, which he described as one of the most useful things I've done for myself. He said he was getting closer to acting work, having completed a film in the United States and with offers coming in every week. He also said he loved his short-term work selling shared times in the Cayman Islands and that he also held jobs such as school janitor and apartment block manager. He was at a point in his life where, as, things were so dark that having something to do felt incredible. However, the Cayman Islands denied him a work visa and he cannot live there permanently. Theroux also asked Hammer if, if offered a role, he would work with Woody Allen. The actor responded, "If I say no, I would never work with Woody Allen, then everything I'm doing is saying I believe in this system that cancels people. I honestly think I would say I would like to sit down with him first, and I would like to talk to him."Information and support for any person affected by issues of rape or sexual abuse are available through the following organizations. At that time, the child was lying on their stomach when, according to police, Dandridge grabbed the child's left arm and aggressively flipped them over onto their back before throwing them back onto their stomach. The action caused the child to hit their eye against the side of the crib, which was covered in a mesh material that, according to police, left an imprint on the child's face. Dandridge then placed a toy under the child's face and pushed their head into it, mouth-first, according to police, who said that a surveillance video captured the incident. In the sworn statement, it was noted that the child had no reported marks before attending the daycare. The Clearwater Police Department arrested Dandridge and charged her with child abuse. (The Montonero). Various approaches indicate that illegal economies in Peru mobilize more than $9,000 million USD, amidst growing informality in all sectors of the economy. In other words, narco-trafficking, illegal mining, illegal deforestation, and human trafficking, among others, have become social and political actors that no one can ignore if we don't want Peru to become a failed state. The private sector must lead the proposal for formalization. From the total of illegal economies, some estimates indicate that illegal mining mobilizes more than $5,000 million USD, and the trend is towards a constant increase, considering the price of an ounce of gold (over $2,000 USD) and that of a pound of copper (around $4 per pound). The destructive role of illegal mining is highlighted above all because it needs to destroy the established system of property rights established in the Constitution, national laws, contracts, and international treaties signed by Peru. In other words, it needs to destroy the current rule of law. That is why illegal mining supports all anti-system movements. As illegal mining advances, destroying the property rights system in Peru, it needs to ally itself with various forms of organized crime to intimidate formal mining concessions. Illegal mining, therefore, combines money and firepower to neutralize the institutions of the law. In Pataz province in Libertad, for example, the state of emergency decreed by the state has not halted the advance of this scourge, revealing a devastating lack of political decision-making by the Executive. In other words, the presence of the armed forces, the national police, the central government, the regional government, and the entities of the justice system have not been able to prevent the murder of 18 workers from formal companies, the destruction of over 15 high-voltage towers, and the approximately 12,000 trucks that, last year, transported the stolen mineral from formal companies that pay taxes and preserve the environment. Something similar is starting to happen on the southern highway corridor, on the border between Peru and Ecuador, the Madre de Dios region, and over 22 rivers of the Amazon. What will happen if the Executive continues to renounce restoring the state of law threatened by illegal mining in mining areas? Perhaps it is worth noting that illegal mining is defined as the activity that violates the rights of formal mining concessions and in areas of natural parks and reserved zones. As it has been sustained, it is a central attack on the property rights system established in the 1993 Constitution. If things are as they are, which sector knows most about the activities of illegal mining? It is evident that the sectors of modern mining that daily denounce the invasions of exploration and exploitation concessions. Up to today, the private sector has only proposed interdiction. In this sense, in the midst of the general failure of the formalization implemented by the Mining Formalization Registration System (Reinfo) of the Energy and Mines sector, which has only served to exempt illegal miners in an indefinite process of formalization from penal responsibilities, it should be noted that the private sector has not led an integral proposal for the formalization of small-scale mining. While it is true that the responsibility for formalization is exclusive to the State, the gravity of the situation obliges the private sector to develop a proposal for formalization, especially considering that the sector is the one that knows the problem best. Up to this day, the private sector has only proposed interdiction, a central and fundamental element in the war against illegal mining. However, a proposal is needed to formalize the informal sector, to create a powerful alliance between large, medium, and small-scale mining, and in this way, to strike with the full weight of the rule of law at illegal mining.

The Armed Forces of Ecuador announced the capture of the most dangerous terrorist of the criminal gang Los Lobos, in an operation that was executed this Monday morning in a shrimp farm (shrimp hatchery) on Puná Island, located in the Gulf of Guayaquil. Infobae URL: EFE The naval operations command announced through a statement that the detained person is Cristian Javier Barreiro (Negro Barreí), the alleged leader of Los Lobos, one of the largest criminal gangs operating in Ecuador, considered a terrorist group by the Government since the declaration of internal armed conflict last year. The operation, commanded by the Security Block composed of officers from the Armed Forces and the National Police, was carried out on Monday morning thanks to citizen collaboration through the Reward Plan 131, a state anonymous service that provides information on the most wanted delinquents by the authorities. Regarding Barreiro, there was an outstanding arrest warrant for organized crime, and he was one of the most wanted individuals in Ecuador. The Lobos, Los Pipos, Los Chone Killers (900 members), and Los Tiguerones (1,200 members), grouped together under the name Nueva Generación. The Ecuadorian Ministry of National Defense also celebrated this decisive blow against organized crime on social media. In addition, during the intervention, a total of five firearms were seized, including a submachine gun, an ammunition clip, and a 9mm pistol, as well as ammunition for the armament and various accessories, such as two bulletproof vests. Since the beginning of 2024, Noboa has elevated the fight against organized crime to the level of an internal armed conflict, thereby classifying organized crime gangs as terrorist groups and issuing a series of states of exception with actions such as the militarization of prisons controlled by criminal structures. Organized crime gangs are considered the cause of the escalation of violence and insecurity that the country is experiencing, which in 2023 ranked as the first in the homicide rate in Latin America with around 47 per 100,000 inhabitants, a rate that in 2024 decreased slightly to 38. The Wolves have strengthened their presence in Ecuador's organized crime, diversifying their operations beyond narcotics trafficking. The criminal group has expanded its range of illicit activities to include illegal mining, the commercialization of counterfeit vaccines, and human trafficking. Regarding this transformation, former Vice Minister of Interior and security analyst, Max Campos, commented that they have been changing and mutating, evidencing the adaptation of the gang to different forms of delinquency. The Wolves dominate key areas of the criminal chain, manipulating strategic points within Ecuadorian territory to facilitate their criminal activities. According to the Police, this criminal group was born in the Azuay province, whose capital is Cuenca, in 2019, under the leadership of Wilmer Chavarría alias Pipo or Tuerto, who would have been a member of Los Choneros, the country's largest megaband. After obtaining his preliberty in 2019, alias Pipo settled in Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas. There, he would have joined the Franco Cedeño family clan with whom he coordinated his illicit activities. We have made progress in the protection of children, girls, and adolescents. Published on 10/13/2022 (Press Office, Directorate of Communication). For legislator Dalia Estigarribia (PLRA, Central), chair of the Committee on Childhood and Adolescence of the Chamber of Deputies, the recent times have been positive in terms of legislative work related to childhood and adolescence, taking into account achievements and advances that, although still not sufficient, mark the path and open up hopes, as she pointed out. I feel proud. I believe we have made significant progress in the topic of protecting our children, girls, and adolescents. We have achieved accomplishments that we must highlight, as well as acknowledge that there is still much work to be done, she said. She highlighted the recent promulgation of a law that modifies and increases penalties for child sexual abuse, whose official document was the One that modifies articles 128 and 135 of Law 1,160, Penal Code, modified by Law 3 What modifies and increases the penalties for child sexual abuse. He recalled the work done to modify the original project, where special emphasis was placed on increasing the penal framework for the most serious situations. In particular, it was established that sexual abuse through intercourse in children under 10 years old will be punished with a minimum sentence of 15 to 20 years in prison, which can extend to 30 years depending on the severity. Many times we think that only adults suffer from depression, but unfortunately, it is not the case. Following an investigation, it was reported that approximately 200 children were detected with depression, and even there were attempts at suicide, he reported. He described the situation as alarming and announced that they will focus on this in the present year of work.

Peruvian police authorities captured 23 suspected delinquents allegedly linked to the Aragua Train. Among those apprehended were 12 Venezuelan citizens and 11 Peruvians. The men were detained during an operation carried out in the San Martín de Porres and Puente Piedra districts, as reported by the RPP medium. During the operation, authorities rescued 84 victims of sexual and labor exploitation, all of whom were Peruvian and Venezuelan nationals. Among the affected individuals were three minors, who were placed under the care of the Special Protection Unit of the Ministry of Women. The head of the PNP's Directorate Against Human Trafficking and Smuggling of Migrants, General Aldo Ávila Novoa, stated that the Aragua Train had been dismantled in that country. They are no longer acting directly, but are instead using collaborators, who are nationals, to try to act and, above all, in the crime of human trafficking. The leaders of the criminal gang are serving their sentences at Challapalca prison. However, he warned that there are still factions of the organization in existence. The official reported that the detainees were transferred to the headquarters of the Dirincri on Avenida España, in the Cercado de Lima, where their legal due process will begin. A 24-year-old Latin American immigrant faces severe charges for the crime of child sexual abuse against an 11-year-old girl in Georgia, United States. Authorities are evaluating his deportation. The accused is identified as Rolando Osbaldo Funes, whose arrest was made in Powder Springs, according to local news outlet Mundo Now. The Cobb County Police Department's arrest warrant stated that Funes allegedly raped an 11-year-old girl on January 28. The incident occurred at 8:00 p.m. in a residence in that locality. Two days later, the accused was detained and held in custody at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center. Prison records confirmed that the suspect remains under arrest and is not eligible for bail. Due to the severity of the crime, authorities denied the possibility of the suspect being released on bail while the judicial process unfolds. The Department of Homeland Security has not issued a detention order against the immigrant, which could mean that, after his criminal trial, he will be handed over to immigration authorities. According to judicial records, Funes is in the United States illegally. His situation could worsen his legal status, as, in addition to facing a possible sentence for child abuse, he could be deported from the country. The victims of child abuse and their families in Powder Springs can seek support from local organizations that offer legal and psychological assistance.
