The head of the Directorate Against Human Trafficking and Illicit Migrant Smuggling of the Peruvian National Police (PNP), Aldo Ávila Novoa, reported on Monday 09Feb that the criminal organization Tren de Aragua was completely dismantled in the country. We have the Tren de Aragua dismantled. As a criminal organization, in Peru, we have it completely dismantled. All the leaders have fallen and are serving their sentence in Challapalca, he said in an interview with RPP radio station. Ávila indicated that the main leaders of the gang are currently detained in the maximum security prison of Challapalca. Additionally, he emphasized that the authorities are working in collaboration with the Government of the United States and Europol to better understand the structure of the organization. Furthermore, he noted that the structure of the Tren does not define itself as pyramidal or collegiate. The PNP is working with the hypothesis that this gang operates as a differentiated organization, with higher levels and other intermediate levels scattered in several countries in America and Europe, including Peru, Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Spain, Brazil, Panama, the United States, and Costa Rica. They also specified that Peruvian and foreign authorities are fighting the so-called cells of the organization, such as Antitren or Los Hijos de Dios. Ávila pointed out the adaptability and negotiation capacity of the Venezuelan gang, highlighting that it was mapped for the first time in Peru in 2017, however, since the 2018 migration, they began to expand their influence in territories related to human trafficking. Finally, he mentioned that the PNP maintains operations against associated groups. Nevertheless, he was unable to provide precise figures on the remnants of the gang scattered throughout the national territory. We are currently attacking the remaining members of this organization. I still cannot provide an exact number of how many are left because they are located in different points across the country. We have them mapped out and are already developing joint operations, he said.

The bodies of at least 28 migrants have been recovered from a mass grave in a desert in southeastern Libya, said the country's prosecutor general. The grave was discovered north of Kufra, just days after another mass grave with 19 bodies was found in a farm in the same city. Authorities found the latest grave after a raid on a human trafficking site, where authorities freed 76 migrants who had been detained and tortured, the Office of the Prosecutor General posted on Facebook. One Libyan and two foreigners were also arrested, it added. There was a gang whose members deliberately deprived the illegal migrants of their freedom, tortured them, and subjected them to cruel, humiliating, and inhumane treatment, the statement said. Images shared online, which the BBC has not independently verified, show police and volunteers digging in the sand before placing bodies in black bags The search in Kufra, more than 1,700 kilometers (1,056 miles) from the capital of Libya, Tripoli, continues. The Attorney General states that the recovered bodies have been taken for autopsy, and investigators suspect links to smuggling networks. Authorities are documenting the testimonies of the survivors. Last year, a mass grave containing the bodies of at least 65 migrants was found in southwest Libya. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) described it as deeply impactful at the time. Since the overthrow of Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, the country has become a key transit route for migrants risking perilous sea and desert crossings to reach Europe. UNICEF has said that in 2024, the number of people who died or went missing in the Mediterranean while trying to reach Europe exceeded 2,200. Migrant bodies recovered in Libya, say authorities.

The Provincial Court of Tarragona has confirmed the decision of the investigating judge from Valls to archive the proceedings against a retired teacher from the Collegi Baltasar Segú due to allegations of sexual abuse. The judges have determined that the facts, which date back more than 25 years, have expired. The case was opened at the end of November 2022 due to six complaints filed by former students, now adults, of this educational center who had the investigated individual as a tutor and a private tutor. The alleged incidents would have occurred between the years 80 and 90 of the last century, according to Diari de Tarragona. Appeal ProcedureThe Valls court ordered a dismissal and archiving of the proceedings in July 2023, but the complainants filed an appeal with the support of the Prosecution. They argued that in some cases, it was a continuous crime, which could delay prescription, and pointed out a lack of motivation in the judge's ruling. The Provincial Court has now ruled in favor of the judge.Changes in the Penal CodeOne of the complainants allegedly suffered the abuse during the 1987-1988 school year when he was 14 years old. According to his testimony, the teacher would often take him to the school bathrooms, where he would perform unwanted touching. According to the current legislation at the time, notes the Provincial Court, these acts would have been classified under the chapter of the Penal Code that describes dishonest abuse, punishable with a lesser prison sentence and prescribing to five years. La Romana, Dominican Republic. With the goal of strengthening ethical and responsible journalism, the Association of Hotels La Romana Bayahibe (AHRB) and the La Romana Bayahibe Tourism Cluster (CTRB), in collaboration with MAISECPAT Dominican Republic, conducted a workshop for 23 journalists in the region on the proper treatment of topics related to the sexual exploitation of children, adolescents, and minors in the context of travel and tourism (ESNNAVT). During the session, participants acquired tools to report on this issue without contributing to re-victimization or compromising investigations, always promoting the protection of victims' rights. Only through education can awareness be generated about the harm caused by child sexual exploitation in tourism. That's why more and more companies are adopting this code of conduct, promoting a collective rejection of this practice, highlighted Leidy M. Rivera, representative of MAISECPAT in the Dominican Republic. The training is part of a global initiative to eradicate this crime, where collaboration between media outlets, tourism sector companies, and civil organizations is key. Journalists play a fundamental role in the fight against child sexual exploitation. Their work not only informs but also contributes to prevention and denunciation, said a representative of The Code. The AHRB aims for this workshop to mark the beginning of a strategic alliance with La Romana's media outlets, promoting a joint commitment to address this issue responsibly. La Romana is a reference in promoting good practices in tourism, and the formation of all tourism sector actors is crucial to continue advancing, said Ana García Sotoca, executive director of the Association of Hotels and the La Romana Bayahibe Tourism Cluster. Human trafficking is one of the most severe violations of human rights, with multiple forms affecting millions of people worldwide. From sexual exploitation to labor exploitation, through forced begging or organ trafficking, these realities are complex and often invisible. Behind cold statistics of over 50,000 victims in Spain and millions worldwide, there are life stories broken by deception and the exploitation of these people, stripping them of their dignity and rights. But also stories of hope and transformation of those who manage to become survivors. On February 8th, liturgical memory of Saint Josephine Bakhita, the XI World Day of Prayer and Reflection against Human Trafficking was held, this time with the slogan Ambassadors of Hope Together Against Human Trafficking. To commemorate this occasion, Madrid will observe a Prayer Vigil, organized by the Diocesan Commission Against Human Trafficking, which will take place this Wednesday, February 12th, at 8:00 PM, at Our Lady of Anguish Parish (Rafael de Riego, 16). The celebration will be led by the Auxiliary Bishop of Madrid, Vicente Martín. The Archdiocese of Madrid (@archimadrid) and the Coordinator of the Madrid Anti-Trafficking Commission (@binapam) call on us to join forces with hope and action to eradicate this plague together. Let's unite on Thursday to begin this pilgrimage towards our commitment to eradicate human trafficking from our society.Elba, from victim to survivor. Elba's (fictitious name) testimony, which has transformed her from a victim to a survivor, helps us understand human trafficking from the inside. The young woman, born in Esmeraldas, Ecuador, explains that she did not feel loved in her family, and at 14 years old, I fell in love with a boy. My mother didn't want me to go out with him, but he treated me very well, he was very in love, he would give me gifts, etc. One day the boy proposed that we travel to Quito. Elba didn't tell anyone, not even her mother, because she knew she wouldn't let me. In this sense, she explains that life with him was easier, so in the end she ran away to Quito, a place where no one knew me. When we arrived in the city, her boyfriend took me to an apartment where there were more women. He convinced me to have a relationship with him, although I didn't want to, but he told me I was selfish and that he had done everything for me. Since Elba wanted to, I agreed. As the days passed, her boyfriend told me that he had a commitment with a friend and that I had to have a relationship with him. I refused and he hit me, telling me that I had to comply with his desires because that was the only way to show him my love. Over time, it was no longer just a friend, but several men would force me to do things I didn't want to do. If I didn't please him, my boyfriend would hit me. I felt like trash. The dream of a happy life turned into a nightmare, but Elba still loved me and believed that what I was going through would eventually end. It wasn't that way because the situation worsened. One day, another man arrived at the house and told me that he had bought me and that we were going to Cuenca (Ecuador). Upon arriving in the city, he took her to an apartment where three women lived. The boss was a very violent man who forced us to prostitute ourselves and beat us whenever we disobeyed. There, Elba received more beatings. Nobody loved me and I felt like trash. In the situation I was living, the young woman didn't know what to do and gradually began to understand that her boyfriend didn't love her and had betrayed her. I couldn't call anyone, not even my mother, nor leave the apartment. My ordeal continued for a year and a half. One day, a client seeing the bruises and marks on my body asked who had done that to me. Elba opened up to him. It seemed like a good person and I no longer had anything to lose. Additionally, she asked if she did that job because she wanted to, and she answered no. A few days later, the police appeared and helped the women escape from there. We worked taking care of the land. The young woman recounts that the caregivers attended to us with kindness, taught us to care for the plants, and told us that one day we would become strong women despite the difficulties and the terrible situations we had lived through years ago. In this sense, Elba explains that the caregivers formed them with care and attention to work. The plants, the land, and the women of the house taught me a lot, little by little my confidence in myself was growing, and also in trusting the people around me. The young woman dreamed about her future. She started a small business to cultivate vegetables and fruits, reconciled with her mother Elba says that, although she didn't trust men, she couldn't forget that one had saved her life. One day she met a simple and good man who, although he didn't make her gifts or promises, was happy with her, explains Elba. We got married and have two daughters. Now I am happy. Additionally, she collaborates with the organization that saved her and restored her confidence in herself. She also helps the women in the neighborhood when she senses they're being mistreated. In this sense, Elba affirms that what she has lived has served to help other women who are going through the terrible situation she lived through a few years ago. For me, small victories are important.

The Court of Appeals in Las Palmas has rejected the appeal presented by the defense of Real Madrid player Raúl Asencio against the ruling of the Investigating Court Number 3 of San Bartolomé de Tirajana (Gran Canaria), which agreed to continue the investigation against him for allegedly disseminating a sexually explicit video of a 16-year-old minor. According to the ruling released this Tuesday by the Press Office of the High Court of Justice of the Canary Islands, the First Section of the Court confirms the decision to continue the investigation and dismisses the provisional dismissal requested by the defense of the Real Madrid youth player, who is a defendant in the case, along with three other players from the white team's affiliates. According to the ongoing investigation, in June 2023, two of the players allegedly recorded a sexual relationship they had with two girls, one of whom was a minor, in the tourist municipality of Mogán, where a third party was present, and whose images allegedly were shared by Asencio with a contact once they arrived on his mobile phone. In their appeal, the Real Madrid player's defense questioned the judge's ruling, arguing that the proceedings were prospective, the instruction period had expired, and there was no sexually explicit video allegedly shared by Asencio. Two of the Madrid's young players accused of sharing a sexually explicit video decide not to testify The ruling, among other considerations, considers the request for provisional dismissal to be premature and qualifies the defense's thesis of non-existence of the crime as singular and unsustainable, as there is no sexually explicit video at the center of the investigation. Regarding this last issue, he states that one thing is that the video itself never existed, in which case the thesis could be considered, and another very different thing is that during the investigation conducted by the Judicial Police, and more specifically by the Cybercrime Unit, a copy of the video that did exist could not be recovered. He adds that the existence of the video and its content, combined with the criminal conduct attributed to the player, consisting of receiving and exhibiting it, has been proven circumstantially by the results of other proceedings conducted in due time and form, and considered valid for these purposes. Therefore, it is claimed that there is testimony from the friend to whom Asencio showed the video, which explains its content in detail, without any reasons to doubt its veracity, as well as the examination by the Guardia Civil's Cybercrime Brigade of the phone of Real Madrid player Raul Asencio. The Court notes that it is rational to conclude, with the procedural provisionality of this moment, that the aforementioned player indeed received a unique viewing video in June 2023 on his mobile phone, which, instead of deleting, exhibits at least one other person, thereby not only committing the crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, which could be light, but also one of child pornography, punishable by one to five years in prison, for exhibiting the video to a third party. Furthermore, the ruling states that from the Guardia Civil report, it can be inferred that Asencio himself, through a voice message sent to this friend, admitted later in September that he indeed had shown that video. Therefore, it adds that regardless of the outcome of the agreed-upon proceedings in the now-questioned ruling, there is currently sufficient evidence to reject the dismissal. Other quarry workers implicated The procedure, in which quarry workers Andrés García, Ferrán Ruiz, and Juan Rodríguez, none of whom are now at Real Madrid, are also implicated, was initiated following a complaint filed in Gran Canaria by a woman after discovering that a video of her 16-year-old daughter was circulating on WhatsApp, engaging in sexual relations. This first complaint states that the sexual relations were consensual, but that the young women were recorded without their consent, and later found out that those images were circulating on social networks and mobile apps. Shortly after, the second woman, an adult, also filed a complaint about the dissemination of a sex video that, allegedly, was recorded by one of the investigated individuals while they were engaged in consensual sexual relations, but not the recording and subsequent dissemination of the images were not consensual.

The Prosecution Office opened an investigation against Deputy Jorge Durán (RN) following a complaint of sexual abuse presented by his ex-partner. The PDI carried out procedures at his residence, while the complainant was subjected to medical examinations at the Forensic Medical Service. Durán denies the allegations, stating that the relationship was consensual and that his ex-partner extorted him after he refused to rekindle the relationship. He also accused her of theft and extortion. The Prosecution Office maintains the case under reserve and, for now, has not ordered his detention.The Prosecution Office opened an investigation against Deputy Jorge Durán of National Renewal (RN), following a woman's complaint of sexual abuse. The accusation was presented in the early hours of the morning, which led to Police Investigation Department (PDI) personnel arriving at the parliamentarian's house in Colina, where the complainant resided. According to preliminary information, the woman initially went to the Carabineros, after which she was taken to the Forensic Medical Service to perform forensic examinations. In response, the Public Ministry instructed the PDI's Sexual Crimes Brigade to carry out the necessary procedures and clarify the facts. At the moment, Durán has not been detained, and the Prosecution requested that the investigation be kept entirely confidential. Durán defends himself It was consensual and my ex-partner extorted me Hours after the complaint was known, the deputy categorically denied the accusations and assured that the meeting with his ex-partner was consensual. I trust that justice will clarify the facts and we will reach the truth This complaint is completely detached from reality, he stated in a public statement. Durán explained that, after the end of his relationship, he allowed his ex-partner to continue living in a dependency within his property for humanitarian reasons, as she was unemployed and had nowhere to live. During a celebration at my home last Friday, my ex-partner voluntarily participated in the gathering along with other guests. That night, we shared an intimate moment in a consensual manner. The next day, in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch, maintaining a cordial coexistence, the deputy recounted. However, according to his version, when he made it clear to the complainant that the sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, she demanded money from him. My ex-partner began demanding a sum of money, claiming that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the one to suffer the consequences. Facing this extortion situation and after discovering that my ex-partner had used one of my credit cards without authorization, I proceeded to file a complaint on Monday evening for extortion and theft with Carabineros. The authorities arrived at my home, where the relevant background information was gathered, he explained. The congressman stated that it was after he filed this complaint that his ex-partner accused him of sexual abuse. To my surprise, after my complaint, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, which has generated a completely distorted situation and has significantly affected my public image, he declared.

Politics The Government Announced Changes to the Gender Identity Law Prohibit Hormone Treatment in Minors They will also render ineffective gender adaptation treatments for those under 18 years old. This was announced by presidential spokesperson Manuel Adorni. The Government of Argentina has taken a significant measure by modifying the Gender Identity Law and prohibiting hormone treatment and adaptation in minors under 18 years old. This decision was communicated by presidential spokesperson Manuel Adorni, who explained that the measure seeks to establish new regulations around gender identity in the country. This change in legislation has generated various reactions in society, especially among organizations that defend the rights of transgender people and the health of minors. OFFICIAL STATEMENT Buenos Aires City, February 5, 2025 The President's Office reports that President Javier Milei has made the decision to prohibit treatments and surgeries for gender transition in minors. Ideology taken to the extreme and applied to children through force or psychological coercion constitutes outright child abuse. Children do not possess the necessary cognitive maturity to make decisions on irreversible processes that, in many cases, involve the mutilation of healthy organs, and are capable of causing infertility, cardiovascular problems, and catastrophic consequences for mental health. This is why pioneering countries in child gender transition such as the United Kingdom, Sweden, Finland, and, most recently, the United States, are taking a step back, prohibiting minors from undergoing these procedures. On the other hand, in line with the frontal fight against gender extremism, the President of the Nation will also decree that the accommodation of detainees will be determined based on the sex registered at the time of the criminal act, to prevent anyone from using the excuse of gender change to request a transfer from the prison they are in. Additionally, no man who has requested the correction of his gender before committing a crime will be housed in women's prisons if he was convicted of sexual offenses, human trafficking, or violent crimes against women, nor in the event that the penitentiary evaluation determines it. This Government was elected to end privileges and promote equality before the law. Ending child abuse manipulated on a gender agenda and ending the pampering of delinquents are fundamental steps in this direction. Office of the President of the Argentine Republic

On February 6, the 54th session of the Permanent Peoples' Tribunal (PPT) came to a close, addressing the genocidal crimes committed by the Turkish State against the Kurdish people and other peoples inhabiting the Rojava region in northern and eastern Syria. On February 5 and 6, 2025, at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) in Brussels, the 54th version of the PPT, titled Rojava VS Turkey, convened. There, the accusations of severe human rights violations and war crimes committed by Turkey and its allied forces in northern and eastern Syria were examined, where the Rojava Revolution has been unfolding since 2012, becoming the first revolution of the 21st century and the first anticapitalist revolution led by women. Currently, Rojava represents approximately 30 percent of Syria's territory. This session of the TPP was requested and supported by the Committee for Justice, Law, and the Foreign Relations Department of the Autonomous Democratic Administration of North and East Syria (AADNES), the Women's Rights Research and Protection Center, the AlJazira and Afrin Human Rights Organizations, as well as MAFDAD e.V (Association for Democracy and International Law), ELDH (European Association of Lawyers for Democracy and World Human Rights), IADL (International Association of Democratic Lawyers), the KNK (National Congress of Kurdistan), the Kurdish Institute of Brussels, and the Free University of Brussels. The lawyers and prosecutors representing the people of Rojava presented evidence of the permanent genocidal practices implemented by the Turkish state against the Kurdish people and on the Rojava revolution from 2018 to 2024. The evidence denounced the terrorist actions initiated since 2018 with the occupation of the Afrin region, up to the events of December 2024 with the new interventions of the Turkish military forces and self-proclaimed jihadist paramilitaries, the so-called Syrian National Army (SNA), which seek to enter the Kobane region by attacking the Tishreen Dam, from which more than a million people depend for water and electricity supplies, and which has been permanently bombed, putting the population at risk of an unprecedented catastrophe.What is the Permanent Peoples' Tribunal? This is an international opinion tribunal competent to rule on any serious crime committed against the peoples and minorities. The initiative was born in Bologna in 1979 in the context of the Universal Declaration of the Rights of Peoples (1976) and, following the jurist and politician Lelio Basso, transformed the experiences of the Russell Tribunals on Vietnam (1966-1967) and on the dictatorships in Latin America (1973-1976) into a permanent listening institution for peoples forced to face the absence of law and impunity. The Tribunal is composed of a network of international experts and recognized personalities, convened periodically to form the jury of each session. To date, 54 sessions have been held worldwide, ensuring the participation of peoples and social movements, creating a work agenda for human rights and the rights of peoples at a global level. Through its sessions, numerous cases of serious human rights violations, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and genocide have been brought to light. The Rojava VS Turkey case jurors were Czarina Golda S. Musni (Philippines), human rights lawyer and member of the Union of People's Lawyers in Mindanao (UPLM), Gabrielle Lefèvre (Belgium), journalist since 1972, Rashida Manjoo (South Africa), emeritus professor of public law at the University of Cape Town, Frances Webber (United Kingdom), former immigration, refugees, and human rights lawyer, Giacinto Bisogni (Italy), judge since 1981 and at the Court of Cassation since 2002, Domenico Gallo (Italy), former President of the Section of the Court of Cassation, José Elías Esteve Molto (Spain), full professor of Public International Law and International Relations.Occupation of Afrin in 2018 The court proceedings began with information on the forced displacement of the population of Afrin in 2018, where approximately 167,000 people were displaced, but the current number has risen to 300,000 displaced people. This occupation brought about a change in the demographic composition of the region, meaning that after the population was forced to leave their historic lands, the Turkish state installed a new population to control the territories. Hand in hand with this situation, a process of erasure of Kurdish identity began through methods such as changing the names of streets and Kurdish symbols to Arabic and Turkish names and symbols. In Afrin before 2018, the Kurdish population made up 90% of the population, but today it only represents 20% of the population. It is essential to highlight that historically, Afrin has been a place of resistance for the Kurdish people, and in the contemporary Kurdish liberation struggle initiated in 1978, this region has always accompanied the resistance with great determination, sacrificing martyrs and entire families in the revolutionary struggle, which is why Afrin played a symbolic role in the Rojava resistance. In the same manner, Afrin is one of the most fertile territories in the region, where food was produced ensuring food self-sufficiency for its population. It was one of the most prosperous territories in Syria. The occupation of Afrin by Turkey was strategic to break a symbol of Kurdish resistance. In the trials presented before the TPP, it was denounced that after the forced displacement of 2018, on December 2, 2019, the victims were attacked again, leaving a toll of 10 assassinated children and girls and more than 15 injured in the midst of the so-called Operation Spring of Peace developed by Turkey. All these genocidal practices are legitimized before international organizations under the discourse of combating terrorism. Both in Afrin and in the rest of the Rojava region, the Turkish state's attacks are not only against communities, but directly target the industrial and humanitarian infrastructure of the region. These are grave political strategies of the Turkish state that pose a risk to the entire region, as Turkey refuses to sign agreements to prevent interventionist policies in other countries, and at the same time, fails to ratify the Geneva agreements that include specific norms to protect armed combatants and civilians in war scenarios, thus becoming a threat to any country and people in the region. Turkey is an affront to humanity These occupation tactics and strategies of the Turkish state are not new. In the courtroom, it was evident how the same logic was implemented on the people of Cyprus in 1974, when the Turks displaced thousands of Greek Cypriots and altered the island's historical population. It was mentioned that a third of the population was displaced throughout the process. It is worth noting that these strategies are also imposed through economic pressures that lead to displacement due to the high cost of living. The gravity of the situation faced by the people of Rojava is that, although the occupation and genocide are being witnessed by the world, international organizations such as the United Nations are absent in attending to the displaced and humanitarian crises. It must not be hidden that the situation of occupation experienced in Rojava has similarities with the situation of the Palestinian people. Despite this, silence is imposed. In the court, it was evidenced that there is a de facto occupation in Rojava that seeks ethnic cleansing and the imposition of Islam as the official religion. The representatives of Rojava also denounced that among the war strategies used by the Turkish State, the use of prohibited weapons such as chemical weapons (white phosphorus) and the use of drones against the civilian population are presented. Strategies of war using water-impact methods are also employed in the region. Complaints mentioned the political attacks on the leadership of the Autonomous Democratic Administration of North and East Syria by Turkey. Selective assassinations materialize through the strategic use of drones to eliminate patriotic individuals (defenders of the land welatparez) who today are defending their self-governance system organized under the paradigm of Democratic Confederalism and its three pillars of women's liberation, communal democracy, and social ecology. The attacks against society target especially the women who lead women's organization tasks, which evidences a practice of political feminicides. At the same time, bombings in schools were reported, and evidence was presented of massacres such as the one that occurred in Heseke, where five girls were killed on July 18, 2022. These attacks against women are not only carried out through murders, but also through sexual assaults and tortures that are committed in secret prisons of the Turkish State, where no legislation or human rights apply. At the TPP, testimonies from women such as Nadia Nassam Soleimani were presented, who reported being imprisoned for two years without any judicial charges in Turkish courts of justice. Nadia Nassam reported the permanent tortures to which she was subjected, where she was sexually abused along with other women, the witness repeatedly stated that the abusers were directly members of the Turkish secret services (MIT). From the AADNES, it was reported that there were proofs of more than 3,000 women who were imprisoned in these secret prisons, subjected to sexual abuse and torture, and forced to witness the torture of other women, a situation that was described as "psychological annihilation" by the victims. .000 documented cases of abuse against women were reported, and it was stated that these Turkish state strategies aim to instill fear in women so they do not join the women's liberation movement and the society that is developing under the Democratic Confederation system. Similarly, the cultural genocide practice implemented by the Turkish state was denounced, starting from the destruction of the Kurdish people's memory, represented in humanity's cultural heritage. Videos were shown where Turkish-backed paramilitary forces attack cemeteries and sacred shrines for the Kurds. In these tests, attacks on Eyn Dara, an archaeological site that guards the memory of over 3,500 years of Kurdish history, were shown. There, the ENS jihadist forces destroy and sell the archaeological material on the black market. On the other hand, evidence was presented of the attacks against journalists who disseminate the truth about what is happening in the Rojava revolution and against the infrastructure of the Simov printing press in the city of Qamishlo, where learning materials for society (books and all types of reading materials to build the cultural foundations of a revolution that confronts the logics of capitalism) were being produced. Finally, the war crimes that have been taking place in the Thisreen Dam were mentioned. There, the Turkish State uses drones to permanently bomb the civilian population, leaving dozens of people assassinated since December 2024 in the complete silence of the international community. Videos replayed in the same court confirm the illicit practices of Turkish forces, such as double-tap or double bombing of the same point. In its preliminary statement before the verdict, the Permanent Peoples' Tribunal asserted that the Turkish State was systematically committing war crimes and crimes against humanity with the aim of genocide. It happened in Detroit. The perpetrator approached an ICE office and asked to be detained before committing crimes. An undocumented Venezuelan immigrant from the United States was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after voluntarily entering an office in Detroit and demanding to be arrested, warning that otherwise he would go out to commit crimes. The 23-year-old man will remain in custody while facing immigration proceedings. We appreciate that this individual surrendered before putting public safety at risk, said Robert Lynch, director of the ICE office in Detroit. Recent ICE arrests ICE also announced the capture of other undocumented immigrants with criminal backgrounds in Colorado and New York Adan Desederio PavonAndino, a 30-year-old man from Honduras, was detained in Colorado He been convicted of marijuana possession and faces charges for fentanyl trafficking, illegal re-entry, and firearms possession. Kail Sebastian Cardenas Aguirre, a 27-year-old Ecuadorian citizen, was arrested in New York after being convicted of sexual abuse. In collaboration with the Peruvian National Police, ICE helped dismantle the Aragua Train crime group in Lima, resulting in the arrest of 23 suspects and the rescue of over 80 victims of human trafficking, including three minors.

Convict Man for Raping Friend of a Close Friend in His Girlfriend's Home While She Was Intoxicated. In a news story that has generated outrage and condemnation in society, the Seville Court has sentenced a man to three years in prison for a horrific sex abuse crime with vaginal penetration. This individual took advantage of his girlfriend's home, where he exploited the vulnerability of a woman with whom his friend had previously had consensual relationships. According to the proven facts, the accused used the victim's state of deep somnolence due to alcohol consumption to his advantage. The sentence issued on January 31 reveals that the accused, a Bolivian national with no prior convictions, entered the woman's home with the intention of satisfying his lust, completely ignoring her consent. It is macabre and chilling to know that the aggressor undressed the woman and penetrated her vaginally without her being able to react, given her inability to do so due to her state of somnolence. It is also mentioned that the accused had consumed alcohol beforehand, which affected his cognitive and volitional capacities. It is worth noting that, as part of the judicial process, the aggressor agreed to deposit 995 euros into the court's account as compensation for the victim. Despite this gesture, the Seville Court of Auditors found him guilty of a sex crime, sentencing him to three years in prison, five years of post-penitentiary supervised freedom, and other restrictive measures such as the prohibition of communicating with the victim and the obligation to compensate her with 3,000 euros. This unfortunate event highlights the vulnerability of women in the face of macho violence, as well as the importance of continuing to fight against the culture of impunity that allows cases like this to happen. The sentence imposed by the Seville Court of Audiences represents a small step forward in the search for justice for victims of sexual abuse, but it also reminds us of the urgent need to continue working towards eradicating this social scourge.

The start of the trial by jury against two young men from Florencio Varela, accused of sexually abusing a former classmate, was postponed once again, the first postponement having been due to the absence of citizens summoned the previous day. Yesterday, prosecutor Marcelo Selier recused the technical judge in charge of directing the process, Dr. Natalia González Aguirre of the Oral Court N 2 of Varela, as a result the debate was suspended. The prosecutor filed the recusal based on decisions made by the magistrate that would have broken the impartiality of the judge. It is worth remembering that the process was supposed to begin last week but it was not possible to form the jury because many of the neighbors summoned did not show up. The defendants are T LL and J C, who are accused of an act that occurred in October 2020 in an apartment on Lavalle Street, in Villa Vatteone. The partiesThe Prosecution, the private party affected and the defense had begun days earlier to conduct the selection interviews of jurors at the La Esmeralda judicial building. However, due to the parties' motions and absences, the body of jurors was not completed. Everything was heading towards the start yesterday but the prosecutor filed a recusal of the judge and now the jury process has been suspended. The victim's family is represented by attorney Guillermo Granillo Fernández, while the accused are represented by the defense of Dr. Daniel González Stier. The facts The sexual abuse reported occurred on November 8, 2020, when the victim, 22 years old at the time, met her former high school classmates at an apartment located on Lavalle Street, between Corrientes and Eva Perón Avenue. According to the complaint, after accepting the invitation to have a drink, she was sexually abused Now, we will have to wait and see how the process proceeds in Florencio Varela. From now on, another judge from the same tribunal may or may not accept the doctor's González Aguirre's excuse. If it is accepted, a new selection of jurors will have to be made. If the peers reject the excuse, the case will go to the Chamber of Guarantees and Appeals, and one of the two halls will have to draw the tribunal in which the process will be held.

In the year 2000, the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime was signed in Palermo, Italy, the same city where, eight years earlier, on May 23, 1992, Judge Giovanni Falcone was assassinated. Along with Paolo Borsellino, who was killed two months later, Falcone became a maximum symbol of the fight against the mafia. The Palermo Convention, ratified by more than 180 countries, establishes a comprehensive framework for combating organized crime. However, many governments ignore its guidelines, and with each new administration, new strategies emerge marked by improvisation. The fundamental pillars include, among others, international cooperation, typification of crimes, seizure of assets, protection of witnesses, reciprocal legal assistance, joint investigations, sanctions for obstruction of justice, assistance and protection of victims, fight against corruption, as well as specific protocols on human trafficking, illicit trafficking of migrants, and firearms trafficking. Despite its relevance, this instrument is, at the very least, underutilized, resulting in disconnected national efforts from the global framework. In the United States, for example, erratic policies against narco-trafficking and money laundering persist. With Donald Trump back in the presidency, what could have been a new impetus in the fight against organized crime was, by decree, transformed into a fight against terrorism. The strategy prioritizes external threats without addressing the criminal networks that have been entrenched in the power structures of North America for decades. In Europe, responses to human trafficking and financial crime remain inconsistent. In Latin America, the emphasis is on the use of the Armed Forces for public security and combating organized crime, rather than strengthening civilian institutions, improving justice systems, and consolidating a solid Judiciary. Ignoring the Palermo Convention has visible consequences, including a lack of effective cooperation, repetition of failed strategies, and waste of resources in plans without continuity, rebranded with new names to appear innovative. However, the ultimate consequence is the expansion of criminal networks, which exploit the lack of global coordination. Breaking this cycle requires mechanisms for evaluating compliance with the Convention and abandoning isolated approaches. At the same time, it is urgent to strengthen the Judiciary and professionalize police forces with technical capabilities for investigation and intelligence, conceived with a long-term vision, and not as reactive responses with each change of government. As long as the response remains local and improvised, transnational organized crime groups will continue to accumulate power. The blood spilled by Falcone and Borsellino, as well as that of thousands of people around the world, will continue to flow while the path that their sacrifice helped to build, embodied in the Palermo Convention, is not resumed. BY MANELICH CASTILLA PAL

Child grooming in Cádiz: prosecutor asks for 26 years in prison for accused of sexual cyberstalking of minors The prosecution also charges the defendant with the crimes of sexual abuse, exhibitionism, and the creation of pornographic material The accused lured the children through his Instagram profile, according to the indictment Confirmation of the sentence of a piano teacher from Cádiz for sexually assaulting minors Child grooming or sexual cyberstalking of minors, creation of pornographic material using also minors, exhibitionism, and sexual abuse. These are the crimes that the Cádiz prosecutor's office imputes to an accused who will sit in the dock on the 17th to be judged as responsible for them. The public prosecutor considers him the author of 10 crimes, five victims are counted, and asks for a total prison sentence of 26 and a half years. According to the fiscal's written assessment, between May 29th and 30th, 2021, the defendant, from his Instagram profile, contacted a 12-year-old minor and, driven by the desire to satisfy his lustful desires, asked him to send naked photos. The child initially refused, but eventually sent him a photo in which he appeared naked through the social network. Subsequently, the prosecution continues, the defendant again demanded from the minor the sending of more photos. The victim refused, and the adult, to overcome this refusal, offered him an exchange of images, sending him photos and videos in which the defendant's genitals appeared. He also sent him a photo of a naked woman of a sexual nature with whom, supposedly, the accused had maintained sexual relations. Months earlier, in March 2021, the defendant used the same social media platform to contact a second 14-year-old boy, the prosecutor states in his provisional conclusions. Again, and knowing that he was dealing with a minor, the man began sending him sexually explicit photographs featuring naked women that the minor later viewed, he invited him to participate in sexual acts using expressions such as "one day you'll come and see." The public prosecution states, after gaining the minor's trust, the accused began asking him intimate questions and asked the minor to tell him how long his penis was, what type of sexual practices he performed with his girlfriend, and if he had ever taken sexually explicit photos. The version of the facts maintained by the Public Ministry speaks of a third 14-year-old victim, whom the defendant contacted in September 2021 also through Instagram. Just like with the other victims, the defendant asked the minor intimate questions to satisfy his lustful desires and even sent him photographs of a sexual nature featuring naked women with whom he allegedly had sexual relationships, the prosecutor reveals, adding that once the defendant had already gained the trust of the minor, and in this intimate relationship atmosphere, he began to ask the boy to send him photographs in which he appeared naked. The victim sent a photo in which he appeared without a shirt, in a suggestive pose, showing only his bare back. There are two previous cases of cyberstalking mentioned in the prosecutor's provisional accusation. Before 2016, the defendant contacted a minor under 16 and, driven by the intention of arranging a sexual encounter to satisfy his lust, began to gain the minor's trust by asking intimate questions, including some of a sexual nature, sending photos, and proposing to meet in person, according to the Public Prosecutor's Office. At an unspecified date between 2016 and 2017, the accused traveled to a location to arrange a meeting with the victim, picked him up at his home, and took him to a hotel. Once in the room, the defendant asked the minor if it bothered him if he masturbated, and the minor replied that he should not do it in his presence. Subsequently, the accused took the minor to a football stadium and, on the way, made sexual innuendos and asked if they could do something more, to which the minor refused, pretending to have an appointment with his father due to the discomfort caused by the situation. Finally, the prosecutor concludes that between 2018 and 2019, the accused again contacted a 16-year-old minor, repeating the same modus operandi. He posed intimate questions to the young man about his sexual practices with his partner and told him episodes about his own sexual life, later proposing to him to arrange a meeting to have a threesome. With the same intention of satisfying his lustful desires, the accused required the minor to send him nude photos of his body and to have sex with his partner, although the minor never sent such documents, according to the public prosecution. Furthermore, and according to the prosecutor, the accused sent the minor sexual photographs and videos. In one of those videos, he even appeared himself alongside a naked woman. In addition to the sentence of imprisonment, the Prosecution is requesting that the accused be disqualified from exercising any profession or trade, whether remunerated or not, that involves regular and direct contact with minors, as well as a prohibition on approaching and communicating with the victims. It also seeks the imposition of a five-year period of supervised liberty after serving the sentence, in the event of a conviction.

The United States and Peru successfully carried out an operation against the Tren de Aragua, a dangerous criminal organization. With over 300 agents involved, they dismantled the network in several locations, ensuring regional protection.In a joint operation unprecedented in its scope, the United States and Peru have delivered a crushing blow to the Tren de Aragua, one of the most dangerous and widespread criminal organizations in Latin America. More than 300 agents from the Directorate Against Human Trafficking and Smuggling of Migrants participated in the operation, carried out in Santa Anita, San Martín de Porres, and Puente Piedra. Authorities identified at least eight locations where this criminal network operated, involving around 50 minors. The U.S. Ambassador In Peru, Stephanie SyptakRamnath highlighted the importance of bilateral cooperation in the fight against organized crime. Transnational criminal organizations have no place in the strong and secure region we are building. This operation demonstrates the positive impact of collaborative work. On the other hand, Paul Salamon, HSI Lima attaché, reaffirmed the United States' commitment to regional security. Peru is a key partner in the fight against transnational crime. Together, we protect our nations and guarantee the security of our citizens. The U.S. Embassy reiterated its commitment to combating organizations like the Aragua Train, assuring continued support for Peruvian law enforcement forces. Additionally, it called on citizens to report any suspicious activity related to human trafficking. Operations in the U.S. While in Peru this network was being dismantled, in the United States, operations were also being carried out against the criminal organization. In Aurora, Colorado, ICE managed to apprehend at least 100 members of the gang. Tom Homan, U.S. Border Czar, reported that one of the raids was leaked, putting the agents involved at risk. When operations are leaked, our officers are put in danger. We will not tolerate this and it will be investigated thoroughly, Homan stated. The collaboration between the United States and Peru in the fight against the Aragua Train is an example of the commitment of both countries to regional security. The disarticulation of this criminal network is an important step to protect victims of human trafficking and ensure the safety of citizens.

Actions Against Crimes. Minister Juan José Santiváñez reports that 279 delinquent gangs and 5 criminal organizations have been dismantled. A total of 7,371 people were detained in flagrante delicto for various crimes in the course of the last week, according to Minister of the Interior, Juan José Santiváñez. The head of the sector stated that of the total number of detainees, 6,964 are Peruvian nationals and 407 are foreigners, mainly Venezuelans and Colombians, as confirmed by sources from the Peruvian National Police (PNP) consulted later. Details He specified that, in addition to the captures of people in flagrante delicto, the disarticulation of 279 delinquent gangs and 5 criminal organizations is added, as a result of a series of operations carried out as part of the Territorial Control Plan. Additionally, the Peruvian National Police apprehended a total of 1,810 people with outstanding warrants nationwide, some of whom were included in the Rewards Program. Santiváñez added that 128 firearms used to commit various crimes such as extortion, sicariato, and aggravated robbery against defenseless citizens were also seized. He later highlighted the joint operation carried out with agents from the National Security Agency of Immigration and Customs of the U.S. Embassy, which allowed the capture of over two dozen people (two foreigners and 11 Peruvians) who would be members of the group Los Hijos de Dios, a remnant of the criminal organization Tren de Aragua. During the intervention, 120 victims of human trafficking were rescued, including three minors. data.text: February 11, 2025 8:48 PM A 45-year-old Dominican man was sentenced to nine years in prison on Monday for the death of 11 people he was attempting to smuggle to Puerto Rico illegally. According to a press release issued by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Puerto Rico, on the night of May 12, 2022, Fermín Montilla piloted a vessel with 48 people from the Dominican Republic. At some point during the journey, the boat began taking on water and sinking, resulting in the deaths of 11 people, as stated in the press release. On September 13, 2024, Montilla pleaded guilty to a charge of bringing immigrants into the United States through means of human trafficking, which resulted in death. Human traffickers threaten our national security and exploit vulnerable individuals for financial gain, disregarding their safety, stated Antoinette T. Bacon, Supervisory Special Agent of the U.S. Department of Justice's Criminal Division. Human trafficking operations not only violate the rights of the United States and threaten our national security, but also put the lives of trafficked immigrants at risk and result in death, as the U.S. Attorney General in Puerto Rico, Stephen Muldrow, reported. The case was investigated by the Homeland Security Investigations Division (HSI, in English) along with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP, in English), the Coast Guard, and the Puerto Rico Police. The U.S. Department of Justice's Criminal Division also provides support through a program called the Extraterritorial Criminal Travel Strike Force (ECT), which focuses on dismantling human trafficking networks that pose a risk to public and national security.

data.text: La Paz, January 2, 2025 (ANF). Cecilia Urquieta and Vladimir Ochoa, lawyers for Evo Morales, requested that the Attorney General of the State, Roger Mariaca, initiate investigations into human trafficking against Minister Eduardo Del Castillo and the departmental prosecutor of Tarija, Sandra Gutiérrez, as well as close the case against the former president. After Cindy, the young mother who had a child with former President Evo Morales, accused Eduardo Del Castillo, now Minister of Government, and Sandra Gutiérrez, current prosecutor of Tarija, of the crime of human trafficking and trafficking of persons. We request that an investigation be conducted against these individuals (Eduardo Del Castillo and Sandra Gutiérrez) because the victim is revealing who the true human traffickers are. We ask the Attorney General of the State to fulfill his constitutional role and grant justice to this victim's petition, Urquieta stated at a press conference. Cindy said that on August 26, 2019, Del Castillo came to her house to tell her that the lives of her and her daughter were in danger and that's why they had to leave the country immediately. At first, we didn't want to leave the country because we would have to leave everything we had worked for. But he told us that my life was in danger, and then we had to leave the country. It was then that the (now) departmental prosecutor of Tarija, Sandra Gutiérrez, appeared, because she was representing the Magistrature at the time and she was the one who obtained the travel permits from the judge in Yacuiba for the three minors, who were my daughter and my two younger brothers who traveled with us to Buenos Aires. We were taken by these two people who committed the crime of human trafficking and people smuggling with us, the mother of Morales' daughter reported. The young woman declared herself a victim of those who are now supposedly trying to do justice, and she emphasized that they committed the crime of human trafficking with aggravation because at that time Del Castillo and Gutiérrez were public officials. The complaint I presented to the General Prosecutor's Office is very clear. They have been accomplices of the previous Government, they took my family out of the country in 2019 to hide us, to silence the truth. We, being threatened and harassed, had to leave mainly to safeguard the life of my daughter, the young woman reiterated. According to Urquieta, the young woman in her complaint and memorial presented to the General Prosecutor's Office of the State has requested that Prosecutor Gutiérrez be removed from the investigation because she is part of the case, inasmuch as she supposedly processed a petition before a judge to authorize the trip to Buenos Aires of three minors. The lawyers argue that there are no elements to support the process against the former president, because the crimes fall on other authors. This process against Evo Morales should be extinguished, affirmed Ochoa, because in his opinion there is no object of the crime. If Luis Arce knew about these facts why did he not denounce in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, why did he start the denunciation in 2024 during a protest mobilization, questioned the lawyer Vladimir Ochoa. The president told an international medium that the link between Morales and adolescents was a secret to everyone. Asked if they should also investigate Cindy's confession that Evo Morales is the father of her daughter and that she was forced to change her daughter's surname. The lawyers pointed out that the crime of statutory rape has already been investigated and closed in 2019 or 2020, therefore, it no longer has reason to be reopened. Urquieta said that it's about talking about the crime of human trafficking and trafficking of people, what you mention does not fall within the crime of human trafficking and trafficking of people (regarding) all of this, she has not denounced Evo Morales, he said. What we say is that the crime for which Evo Morales is being persecuted is no longer valid, no longer has legal force. The process against Evo Morales should be left without effect, he reiterated.48 hours after the young mother's statements, neither Gutiérrez nor Del Castillo made a statement on the accusations. The State Attorney General's Office has also not provided any information.

Argentina's Security Minister, Patricia Bullrich, signed a contract on Monday to build a fence in Aguas Blancas, Salta Province. This measure aims to control migratory flow and combat narcotics trafficking, as well as human trafficking. Bolivia's Foreign Ministry has expressed concern over this initiative, urging that border issues be addressed through dialogue mechanisms. Bullrich was present in Aguas Blancas, where municipal authorities signed the contract with local company Construcciones y Servicios. Construction is expected to begin in the coming days, with the fence expected to be 200 meters long and 2.5 meters high. According to the contract, the company has a 60-day deadline to complete the work. Opening of office for victims The contract signing ceremony coincided with the inauguration of the modular office of the Safe Site for Victims of Trafficking in Aguas Blancas. This office was built in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and in partnership with the Eurofront program, funded by the European Union. Argentine authorities explained that the goal of the fence is to slow down and control the migratory flow coming from Bermejo, with the construction of the fence included in a plan to combat narcotics trafficking, contraband, and human trafficking. Focus on human trafficking Bullrich emphasized human trafficking, describing it as one of the most terrible forms of slavery. The minister celebrated the inauguration of the new office in the border zone and stated that it is a place where victims can be protected until the National System for the Protection of Victims of Human Trafficking can truly rehouse them. Attendance of Authorities The ceremony was also attended by the Governor of Salta, Gustavo Sáenz, the Head of Mission of the IOM in Argentina, Alejandro Guidi, and the Deputy Director of the National Directorate of Migration, Mariano Goyenechea. Bullrich had already traveled to Salta in December to present the Güemes Plan, which aims to strengthen borders with neighboring countries such as Brazil and Paraguay. Concern of Bolivia The Bolivian Foreign Ministry reiterated its concern over this measure and stated that border issues should be addressed through established bilateral dialogue mechanisms between states to find coordinated solutions to common issues. In parallel, the Argentine Defense Minister, Luis Petri, met with his Paraguayan counterpart, Óscar Luís González Cañete. Both agreed that the armed forces would strengthen cooperation in vigilance actions on the border to combat the common enemy of organized crime. Deployment of forces at the border Petri stated that Argentina has deployed 10,000 personnel in the northern region of the country and is in the process of purchasing drones for border surveillance. Bullrich has recently expressed her intention to reinforce different border points shared with Brazil.

Public letters to the editor about a public complaint about anomalies in the CECAN. Hello good day Dr. Claudia, the reason for my complaint is that I want to make it public and report the following. I am a family member of an oncology patient at CECAN and we have been receiving attention at the hospital for some years now, which is why I know part of the staff that works there and I speak from experience with what I am about to manifest. On January 30, 2025, my family member, whose identity I prefer to keep anonymous out of fear of reprisals, and I arrived around 4:00 p.m. so that they could be admitted, we arrived late due to road traffic disruptions. When we reported to the Admissions Department, which is the area where patients are prepared for admission, we were informed that we should wait to be attended to, as the area was closed. As hours passed without receiving attention and everyone began to get restless with good reason, we decided to investigate what was happening, as no one would give us an explanation. We only heard the staff saying that it was due to instructions from Dr. Matías that the area remained closed, as Dr. Katerin was going to undergo a procedure and they didn't want her to mix with the patients, which only made us even angrier. As the hours continued to pass and we were nearing 15 people who were exhausted, shocked, unable to consume food, and unable to prepare our patients for hospitalization, I witnessed the Medical Subdirector, Dr. Matías, leaving the area with Dr. Katerin. Katerin Gómez and I identified her because a couple of months ago she gave us an oncological consultation for my family member's chemotherapy treatment to leave around 8:00 pm at night, the time when they graciously opened the area and we were finally attended to, obviously with more delay because it was already the shift change. It is unforgivable that a public servant at a hospital where there is a shortage of many things, uses the few remaining resources for the benefit of her lady, as the staff themselves call the doctor, because as I understood, they took advantage of the operating room, a surgeon, Dr. Indira Morales, nurses, anesthesiologist, and of course, medications, because there was one that they were looking for and couldn't find, all of this made us think that Subdirector and Dr. Katerin Gómez may have something more than a professional relationship, to the point of stopping an entire service for her disposal and him showing himself so attentive and servile. The only thing that interests me is that they attend to my patient, they think that because they have a position, they can discriminate and not care about us, our needs as oncological patients, and the worst is that they have prohibited us from accessing a service that rightfully belongs to us. With their actions, they only demonstrate zero empathy towards our condition in the midst of uncertainty. If they wanted to care about the modesty of this doctor so much, they should have paid for her attention privately. I tried to reach them to complain to the subdirector about their abuse of hospital resources, but I only saw them when they both got into their vehicle and I wanted to report these irregularities immediately, but the priority at that moment was the health and well-being of my family member. It is for this reason, in the name of all the other patients who, out of fear, do not dare to raise their voices, that I make this complaint and take action, because it is not fair that the effort of good people who work here is thrown away and the good name of a good hospital is tarnished, all because of people like this. More from Castro: How Honduras became an uncomfortable US ally (and what might change with a left-wing presidency)Honduras se ha convertido en un aliado incómodo para Estados Unidos, un país que ha sido un bastión de la democracia y la estabilidad en América Central durante décadas.En la década de 1980, Honduras se convirtió en un escenario clave para la lucha contra el comunismo en América Central, después de que Nicaragua se convirtió en una república socialista bajo el liderazgo del Frente Sandinista de Liberación Nacional (FSLN). El gobierno de Washington, encabezado por el presidente Ronald Reagan, vio en Honduras un aliado clave para apoyar a la oposición nicaragüense y contener el avance del comunismo en la región.En la década de 1990, Honduras se convirtió en un destino popular para los turistas estadounidenses, atraídos por sus playas de ensueño y su rica cultura. Sin embargo, en la década de 2000, la situación en Honduras comenzó a cambiar. La corrupción y la impunidad se extendieron por todo el país, y la violencia se convirtió en un problema cada vez más grave.En 2009, un golpe de Estado depuso al presidente Manuel Zelaya, lo que desencadenó una crisis política y social en el país. La situación empeoró en 2010, cuando se eligió a Porfirio Lobo Sosa como presidente, un político conservador y cercano a los intereses estadounidenses.En la década de 2010, Honduras se convirtió en un punto de partida para las migraciones masivas hacia Estados Unidos, especialmente después de la crisis migratoria de 2014. Muchos de los migrantes eran hondureños que habían sido víctimas de la violencia y la corrupción en su país.En 2020, Honduras eligió a Xiomara Castro como presidenta, una política de izquierda que prometió combatir la corrupción y la violencia en el país. Su victoria fue una sorpresa para muchos, especialmente para los intereses estadounidenses que habían apoyado a la oposición conservadora en el país.La elección de Castro ha generado una gran expectación en Honduras y en la región. Muchos esperan que su gobierno sea un cambio positivo para el país, especialmente en lo que respecta a la lucha contra la corrupción y la violencia. Sin embargo, otros temen que su gobierno pueda ser un desafío para los intereses estadounidenses en la región.La relación entre Honduras y Estados Unidos es compleja y multifacética. Aunque Honduras ha sido un aliado clave para la seguridad y la estabilidad en América Central, también ha sido un punto de partida para las migraciones masivas hacia Estados Unidos. La elección de Castro ha generado una gran incertidumbre sobre el futuro de la relación entre ambos países.La política exterior de Estados Unidos hacia Honduras ha sido un tema de debate en los últimos años. Algunos argumentan que el país ha sido demasiado permisivo con la corrupción y la violencia en Honduras, mientras que otros argumentan que ha sido demasiado agresivo en su enfoque hacia el país.La elección de Castro es un momento crítico para la política exterior de Estados Unidos hacia Honduras. La administración de Biden debe decidir si seguirá apoyando a la oposición conservadora en el país o si se alineará con el nuevo gobierno de izquierda. La respuesta a esta pregunta tendrá un impacto significativo en la relación entre ambos países y en la estabilidad en la región.

Last minute in elEconomista.es15 The First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas has dismissed the appeal filed by the defense of Real Madrid player, Gran Canarian Raúl Asencio, who is one of the four young players being investigated for their alleged involvement in the recording and dissemination of a video with sexual content featuring a 16-year-old minor. This is stated in the ruling of the First Section of the Provincial Court of Las Palmas, dated January 28, 2025, following the appeal filed by Asencio's defense, who argued that the instruction period had expired, as well as the lack of evidence of the crimes attributed to him due to the non-existence of the sexual video that underpins the investigation. However, the magistrate emphasizes in his legal reasoning that the cause, initiated on September 18, 2023, began investigating a crime of discovery and revelation of secrets after the Civil Guard received a complaint about the dissemination of a video with explicit sexual content on sexual relationships maintained by a 16-year-old girl on June 15, 2023, which, allegedly and provisionally, two boys with whom she had that sexual relationship would have recorded. One of these young men is said to have sent the video to a WhatsApp group that Asencio, the now appellant, was part of, according to this auto, which he allegedly watched and showed to a friend. It is stated that during the pre-prosecution investigation, the Judicial Police seized four mobile terminals belonging to the four suspects, including the defender of Real Madrid. The indictment, indicated, was then complemented by another indictment, dated September 19, 2023, agreeing to dump and extract the information contained in those four devices, and its subsequent analysis by specialists from the Organic Police Judicial Unit of Las Palmas. Although the initial indictment for preliminary proceedings was appealed by Asencio's defense, it was dismissed, validating the start of the investigation, considering that objective elements converged on a possible crime of revelation and discovery of secrets. That indictment of September 19, 2023, in substance regarding dumping, was confirmed by the Provincial Court of Las Palmas in the autos of January 17, 2024, and April 19, 2024, alluding to indications of a crime against intimacy or, in the alternative, a crime related to the sexual exploitation and corruption of minors. In addition, the magistrate notes that the instruction should be considered finalized within a period of 12 months, unless extended by court order at the request of a party. Nevertheless, he adds that the appealed ruling is prior to the expiration of that ordinary 12-month period. The magistrate also rejects the idea that there cannot be a prospective investigation in the practice of a procedure that would allow identifying all individuals who were part of the WhatsApp group in which the video circulated, in order to subsequently hear them as witnesses to determine which video they received and from whom. The judgment concludes that, with the provisional nature of the procedural moment, Asencio presumably received on his mobile phone, in June 2023, a video with explicit sexual content starring a 16-year-old minor, who instead of deleting it, shows it to another person at the very least, thus presumably committing not only the crime of discovery and revelation of secrets, but also the crime of child pornography, punishable by one to five years in prison upon exhibiting that video to a third party, which, regardless of the outcome of the agreed investigations, already provides sufficient evidence at this time to reject the request for provisional dismissal instated in his appeal.

Nine years in prison for a man in Salamanca for paying a minor to have sexual relations The court has increased the sentence of one of the four accused to nine years in prison and acquitted the eldest of them, 76 years old, considering that he could not know the real age of the minor. The Superior Justice Court of Castile and León increased the sentence of a man convicted of a continuous sexual abuse crime against a 15-year-old minor, whom he paid up to 12 times to maintain sexual relations. This is a procedure in which four men were sentenced in total, and through an appeal, the TSJCyL acquitted one of them, the eldest, due to an invincible error. The Provincial Court had reduced the requested penalties for all of them, imposing the minimum legal penalty for the crime, that is, two years in prison. In addition, it included, in addition, five more years in a regime of supervised freedom for each of them. The total amount of the compensation was around €24,000. Additionally, he was forced to prohibit the four men from approaching within 500 meters of the victim and from communicating with him through any means, as well as being disqualified from any office or profession related to minors. According to the sentence detailed by Ical, the events date back between December 2020 and March 2021, when the men contacted the young man through a social network, on which none of them introduced their personal data, with the young man presenting a physical appearance and psychological development consistent with his chronological age. In all instances, the young man received amounts of money ranging from €20 to €55 after engaging in sexual relations with the accused. However, the appeal filed by the prosecution before the TSJCyL, exercised by the minor's parents, resulted in the multiplication of the sentence of one of them, who at the time was 35 years old, as he maintained up to 12 encounters with the minor, even going so far as to declare that he thought there was a sentimental relationship between them, despite being paid. In turn, the convicted individual filed his own appeal requesting his own acquittal, but it was dismissed. In the case of the older man, who was 76 years old at the time of the events, the high court estimates the appeal and grants him a free acquittal, arguing an irreparable error, in other words, considering him the author of the facts, he considers that he could not know, in this case, the minor's real age and appreciates the brevity of their only encounter, which lasted just ten minutes.

The facts, which occurred in El Ejido, were not commented on by the minor out of fear of family conflict ALMERÍA TODAY URL 11022025 The Superior Court of Justice of Andalusia (TSJA) has confirmed a sentence of five years and six months in prison for a man accused of sexually abusing his 11-year-old niece for almost four years in which he took advantage of them being alone to subject her to touching and even show her pornographic material. In particular, the Andalusian high court imposes on the accused five years and one day in prison for a continued sexual abuse crime and six months more for the exhibition of pornography to a minor. It also agrees on 15 years of separation and disconnection from the minor and 14 years more of supervised freedom The sentence establishes as proven that the accused, at the age of 37, took advantage of the visits made by the minor to his residence in El Ejido, in which she stayed alone when she was still 11 years old, to sexually abuse her. The girl did not tell her father, her brother, or the accused, due to fear of a family conflict, as they all lived with the accused's parents and siblings in their home. The abuses, which occurred at least until 2022, took place in different circumstances and in different ways, to the point that the accused even offered money to his niece to touch her genitals or maintain intimate relationships, which she refused. Additionally, when the girl was 12 years old, the accused showed her a video on his mobile phone of adults engaging in sexual relations, and then forced the minor to touch his penis. The situation gave rise to a picture of depressive symptomatology in the minor, who also suffered physical discomfort and intrusive thoughts due to the distress suffered. In this sense, the Appellate Court supports the criterion followed by the Third Section of the Provincial Court of Almería in accepting without reservations the version provided by the minor, whose testimony practiced as preconstituted evidence was considered credible, verifiable, and persistent, inasmuch as it was supported by the expert report conducted on the minor.

data.text: In the year 2024, 1465 reports of sexual abuse were registered in Junín, with the majority of victims being women, children, girls, and adolescents, according to the national program Aurora. The Promoter of the Women Emergency Center (CEM) of the Huancayo Police Station, Jorge Rojas Smith, stated that in the province of Huancayo, the CEM attended 192 cases of sexual violence (107 cases of children, girls, and adolescents) and 76 cases of adult women. Meanwhile, the CEM in Huancayo attended 87 cases of sexual violence in children, girls, and adolescents, 48 adult women, and 1 case of an elderly adult. On the other hand, in January 2025 alone, the CEM of the Huancayo Police Station already attended eight cases of sexual violence, of which seven are victims of children, girls, and adolescents, and one case of an adult woman. Close aggressor. The psychologist mentioned that most cases of sexual abuse occur within the victim's home, and in 70% of cases, the aggressor is someone known to the victim, who can be the father, grandfather, cousin, uncle, godfather, or neighbor. In that situation, he pointed out that it is necessary to teach children, girls, and adolescents to communicate if they are victims of touching or abuse, since aggressors usually gain the trust of the victims, give them bribes, and ask them to keep the abuse a secret, under the threat of harming the life of their parents. Parents should have good communication with their children and daughters and should talk to them about sex in an appropriate manner to prevent early sexual relationships and unwanted pregnancies, the specialist demanded. They do not report. Another problem is that many women who were victims of sexual abuse remain silent due to shame and do not report the sexual abuse. Sexual abuse marks the lives of victims for life, as there is an impact on their sexual, intimate, and loving life, as it leaves a trauma that must be treated, said Rojas Smith. The Ministry of Women launched the "Prevenir para proteger" (Prevent to Protect) campaign with the goal of sensitizing the population about taking care of women, children, and girls, as they are the most vulnerable groups. As part of the campaign, they aim to eradicate the macho culture, as for years, the idea has been spread that if the man does not control his impulses, it is because the women provoke him, which attempts to justify any manifestation of sexual aggression that harms and generates guilt in them.
