In the town of Aguas Blancas, Governor Gustavo Sáenz and Minister of Security of the Nation, Patricia Bullrich, led the inauguration of the Safe Site for Victims of Human Trafficking. The new facility, located within the Puerto Chalanas Migration Office, aims to strengthen assistance and protection for vulnerable individuals in the northern border, one of the most sensitive areas in the country in terms of organized crime. Voces Críticas was present at the event, covering it and highlighting the importance of this initiative for regional security. During her speech, Patricia Bullrich warned of the gravity of the human trafficking crime and its impact on the region. We are in a hot border, with blind spots where criminal networks operate, trafficking people, often with children, she expressed. The Minister emphasized that the fight against human trafficking is a top priority and assured that concrete measures are being taken to strengthen controls at border crossings. Bullrich highlighted that the new Safe Site will allow for immediate assistance to be provided to victims, but also to improve case detection. This space is a fundamental step to protect those who are caught by these mafias and ensure that they receive the containment they need, she stated. Furthermore, she explained that a specific protocol for action will be implemented to optimize the response of security forces and competent agencies. Along these lines, Patricia Bullrich announced that the presence of Gendarmerie at the border will be reinforced and that new equipment will be provided to the force to improve its operational capacity. We cannot allow criminal organizations to continue operating unpunished on our borders. We will intensify controls and pursue those who profit from human exploitation, he emphasized. After the inauguration, the minister and governor visited the works at Puesto 28 de Julio, a strategic point for surveillance in Aguas Blancas. With these actions, the national and provincial governments aim to strengthen the fight against human trafficking, a crime that continues to hit border areas and requires a resolute response from the State. Voces Críticas.

The National Security Minister, Patricia Bullrich, traveled to Salta to kick off the work that will be carried out to reinforce the border between the locality of Aguas Blancas with Bermejo, in Bolivia. The Salta government in cooperation with the Nation aim to build a 200-meter fence at the Aguas Blancas border crossing to prevent smuggling, the transit of drugs, and human trafficking between Argentina and Bolivia. In January, the Salta governor, Gustavo Sáenz, announced the new measures that he would implement together with the National Ministry of Security within the called Plan Güemes, a program to reinforce security in the border zone with Bolivia. On Monday, the minister traveled to the northern province and moved to the place where the fence would be built, symbolically placing the first post that will support the structure alongside the provincial governor. FENCED BORDERS, NARCOS CORNERED Before they jumped as if nothing, now they are cornered In Aguas Blancas, Salta, with this fence and cutting-edge technology, the lack of control is over, there are no more shortcuts, no more impunity. Fortified borders, maximum security. pic.twitter.com/URLPatricia Bullrich (PatoBullrich) February 10, 2025 Additionally, Bullrich and Sáenz visited the Aguas Blancas Gendarmerie base to deliver biometric recognition equipment to the security forces. The equipment came from a deal signed between the Ministry of Security and Homeland Security, the US security department. Their last activity in the area was visiting the Safe Site for Victims of Trafficking, which will begin working at the Puerto Chalanas Migration Office. Adrián Zigarán, the intervenor who signed the bid with the head of the company Construcciones y Servicios, Pablo Esteban Osadcia Sánchez, was present along with the officials. The work will go from the local bus terminal to the Migration Office. Patricia Bullrich We must achieve that this is a safe and clean zone. After Bullrich and Sáenz's interventions in Aguas Blancas, both led a press conference about the security problems the area faces. During the conference, the minister said Human trafficking is one of the most terrible forms of slavery. There are criminals capable of kidnapping girls, inventing a story about a better life or simply putting them in a car at gunpoint and taking them. After this, Patricia Bullrich reaffirmed her commitment to increasing security measures in Aguas Blancas, in Orán. We have to make this a truly clean zone, improve the quality of life of the citizens here and of visitors, as well as workers, she emphasized.

It is deplorable, but in Mexico, safe social and family environments for childhood and adolescence are scarce. This is due to multiple factors, such as the lack of resources to meet basic needs such as food and housing, which in turn triggers a series of abuses, including sexual violence and human trafficking. To put these challenges into perspective, we will address the most recent statistics: malnutrition and obesity affect an average of one million children, primarily in southern states such as Chiapas, Quintana Roo, Tabasco, Yucatán, Guerrero, Morelos, Oaxaca, and Puebla (Ensanut 2022). The Network for Children's Rights in Mexico reports that, on average, 27 girls, boys, and adolescents are victims of human trafficking each month, with a greater impact on women than men. Regarding Child Sexual Abuse (ASI), there are no exact figures, however, the Senate estimates that around 4.5 million minors are victims of this crime each year in the country. According to the film The Sound of Freedom, child trafficking is one of the fastest-growing illicit businesses worldwide, and a striking statistic is that a child can be sold 5 to 10 times a day. It's likely that you've already heard these numbers, but the question is what we're doing to protect childhood from this reality. We all have a role to play in this, although these problems may seem bigger than us and impossible to tackle, one way to make a difference is to take an interest in the initiatives and organizations that work every day to make a change. In February, the Ama con Causa event will be held, organized by the AMA Food Bank, which for 10 years has been combating food waste by rescuing products removed from supermarkets and businesses at the Central Market due to damaged packaging or being close to their expiration dates, but still suitable for human consumption, which are distributed free of charge in communities with greater social marginalization in Mexico City and other states. The Ama con Causa event aims to combine efforts to address hunger, child sexual abuse, and human trafficking. It will take place from February 18 to 20 at Av. Constituyentes 968, Lomas Altas, CDMX. During this space, information on these issues will be shared through lectures by expert individuals. Some of the presentations are Saskia Niño de Rivera's The Reconstruction of the Social Fabric, a social activist and defender of the rights of childhood and adolescence in Mexico, Paula Aguilar's Introduction to Abuse, who has dedicated a great part of her life to combating ASI, and Tim Ballard's The Hidden War Against Our Children, a special agent of the National Security Department of the United States, whose rescue story of hundreds of children from human trafficking served as the basis for the movie The Sound of Freedom, among other figures. All the funds raised will be donated to non-profit organizations that guarantee the rights of childhood such as Ama con Causa, which fights hunger, Freedom Foundation, which fights child trafficking for sexual exploitation, and Casa Paloma, a home for children who suffered violence or abandonment and are waiting to be incorporated into a family. Learn more at amaconcusa FOUNDATION GROUP ANDRADE FOUNDATION GROUP ANDRADE

data.text: The Third Section of the Jaén Court of Audiences has sentenced a 64-year-old man to 30 years and a half in prison for raping his two minor granddaughters over four years, since they were 6 and 10 years old. The sentence, accessed by Europa Press, condemns this man to 30 years in prison as the author of two continued sex crimes with intimidation and family relationship abuse. In addition, he is sentenced to three more months in prison for a crime of physical abuse and another three months for a crime of child pornography possession. On the other hand, he is acquitted of two continued threats crimes, two crimes of psychological injuries, and a minor crime of physical injuries for which he was also being accused in this cause. As an accessory, the sentence imposes a prohibition on communicating or approaching the girls for ten years, in addition to a prison sentence once served, as well as ten years of supervised freedom and one year of deprivation of the right to possess and carry firearms. In terms of civil liability, he must indemnify each of the minors 50,000 euros for the moral damages and harm caused to the two girls. The facts date back to May 2018 and extended until January 2023. To achieve the girls' silence, the grandfather told them that if they told anything, he would kill the two of them, their mother, and his wife, which caused an absolute state of fear in the minors, who did not dare to tell until February 1, 2023. In addition to the sexual aggressions, the sentence condemns him for an episode of physical abuse against one of the girls, whom he grabbed strongly by the shoulders and pushed against a wall in the middle of the street. During the trial, it was discovered that the defendant's mobile phone had been seized, and after analysis, explicit images of a child under the age of 18 and a video of his four-year-old grandson naked were found, in which the accused asked him to dance. THE TRIAL Although the accused pleaded not guilty during the January trial, the verdict confirms that the accused repeatedly violated and subjected his two granddaughters to various forms of sexual abuse, taking advantage of their familial relationship and the numerous occasions when he was alone with them, as their parents left them in his care while they worked. The verdict also states that the accused used intimidation and threats to overcome the resistance the girls may have shown to the execution of the sexual acts, to the point of threatening to kill their mother and grandmother if they revealed anything. The defendant defended himself in the trial, saying that everything was a lie, but the court establishes that the testimony of the two minors, with all the details about the practices they were subjected to by their grandfather, allows such a high degree of certainty that it constitutes sufficient evidence to issue a condemnatory sentence. The minors' statement was made in the trial with the reproduction of the statement they made under preconstituted testimony. The minors detailed, with their own words, numerous alleged violations and physical aggressions perpetrated by their own grandfather, the person who, after violating them, would sometimes give them money. He gave us five euros or bought us clothes, the girls pointed out. He did it a thousand times, said the older sister, who noted that she and her younger sister made a pact not to tell until their grandfather died because he threatened to kill their parents and their grandmother if they told anything about what was happening. It was the older sister, who was 12 years old, who told her friends from school what her grandfather was doing to her, and they in turn told a teacher who was the one who raised the alarm and brought the case to the attention of the family, which the girls had never told before. The mother of the younger girls, who testified behind a screen that separated her from the accused, said that the girls would often stay with the accused. Who would have thought, she said, emphasizing that she loved her father madly and that it never crossed her mind that her daughters were going through, as she put it. As a mother and as a daughter, this situation was horrible, it was a disappointment, it was a person I loved because it was my father, and as a mother, I felt terrible because they were my daughters, the accused testified in court, while rejecting the existence of family conflicts as argued by the accused. The prosecutor's attorney, Francisco Navea, maintained that the evidence against the accused was conclusive and gave full credibility to the girls. That is why the family has sought justice to be done, for the facts that these girls have suffered at the hands of their grandfather, whom the attorney defined as a monster.

This advance reflects the commitment of the different levels of the National and Provincial State in the fight against organized crime and in the protection of victims of Trafficking, ensuring presence and concrete action in one of the most sensitive areas of the country. The Provincial Attorney General of Salta, Pedro García Castiella, accompanied the Minister of Security of the Argentine Nation, Patricia Bullrich, the Governor of Salta Gustavo Sáenz, and other authorities at the inauguration of the Safe Site for Trafficking Victims, which will operate at the Migrations Office in Puerto Chalanas, in Aguas Blancas. Three years ago, we installed in the public agenda the urgent problem of narco-trafficking and organized crime in the north of the province. Since then, we have taken this claim to every debate space, even to the Federal Public Prosecutors' Council, demanding a coordinated strategy that involves Nation, Province, and federal and provincial forces, the Attorney General stated. The fight against narcotics trafficking and organized crime is a global challenge that requires concrete and articulated responses. After two decades, for the first time in the province, the national and provincial governments, along with their respective security forces and provincial and federal jurisdictions, work together in a coordinated manner. Seeing this effort become a reality is a huge satisfaction and a fundamental step in building an effective response to this scourge, García Castiella highlighted. As part of the visit, authorities participated in the inauguration of the Safe Site for Victims of Human Trafficking or related crimes on the Aguas Blancas Migrations grounds Additionally, they delivered donated equipment from a US company, which included BITMAP devices for the biometric identification of individuals with a history of transnational crimes. They later visited the National Gendarmerie Post 28, where they supervised the operation of the new scanners and equipment received. Source: Penal Fiscal Authorities

A shocking incident in the city of Tarija has ended with a exemplary sentence. A 28-year-old man has been sentenced to 28 years in prison for the aggravated crime of rape against a 12-year-old girl. The victim is also pregnant as a result of the constant sexual abuse she suffered. Source: La Voz de Tarija The complaint was filed by the girl's mother, who noticed her daughter's severe abdominal pains and decided to take her to a medical center. There, the pregnancy was confirmed, leading to an investigation that resulted in the accused being apprehended. The First Sentencing Court of Tarija, after evaluating the presented evidence, imposed the maximum penalty for this serious crime. This case has highlighted the importance of reporting cases of sexual violence against minors and has sparked a call to society to redouble efforts in preventing and fighting this type of crime. The competent authorities must ensure that the necessary support services are provided to the victim and their family, as well as ensure that the convicted person serves their sentence in its entirety. It is essential to implement public policies and prevention programs that address the causes of sexual violence and empower children, girls, and adolescents to identify high-risk situations and seek help. Furthermore, it is necessary to strengthen the justice system to ensure that sexual aggressors are punished with the full weight of the law.

A judge handed down a 90-year and 6-day prison sentence to Ricardo Adrián N, 31 years old, for the femicide and disappearance of his wife, as well as a series of sex crimes and human trafficking in child pornography mode committed between 2015 and 2021. The ruling also includes the payment of 6,000 installments of fine and a compensation for death and funeral expenses. According to the investigation by the Nuevo León Attorney General's Office, on October 8, 2021, in a residence in the Benavides neighborhood, in Cerralvo, the defendant attacked his wife Y.L., 26 years old, with a blunt object, causing her death from deep skull contusion. Subsequently, he concealed the body in a clandestine burial site in the El Balastro ranch, located in Congregación Uña de Gato, kilometer 79 of the Miguel Alemán Highway. The corpse was found on May 25, 2022, following a search warrant. The investigations revealed that Ricardo Adrián N had a history of gender violence, subjecting his wife to blows and psychological pressure, elements that strengthened the accusation of feminicide. During the interrogation, it was discovered that the accused was also a generator of sexual violence against minors, as he produced, stored, and distributed child exploitation material. It was found on his phone content in which adults appear in real or simulated sexual acts with children between 3 and 12 years old. This led to the opening of multiple investigation folders, adding to his sentence crimes such as rape, corruption of minors, and human trafficking in the mode of child pornography. The judge ordered his reclusion in a State Rehabilitation Social Center, thus fulfilling one of the severest sentences in the history of Nuevo León for crimes of this nature.

Although he has been suspended, he has not faced a legal process that ensures he will be held accountable for his actions. Child Sexual Abuse Allegations Made Against Multiple Children at Merida Nursery School Suspension of Teacher Insufficient for ParentsThe parents are outraged, as they consider the suspension of the teacher insufficient, and the school is operating as if nothing has happened, ignoring the severity of the situation. They also point out that this is not the first time a case of child sexual abuse has occurred at this nursery school, which even changed its name after a similar incident in the past.Rosy Santana, mother of one of the girls allegedly affected, recounted to the media the difficult process her daughter is going through, who is experiencing psychological trauma and a fear of being touched by others.How to Act in a Case of Child Sexual Abuse Survivor Recounts the SufferingAccording to Rosy, the students at the nursery school had been exhibiting strange behaviors in the weeks leading up to the allegations. The children cried and resisted going to school, especially on Mondays, the day they had physical education. The snake game, a game allegedly used by the teacher to touch minors. The mother reported that her daughter told her about a game called the snake, in which the teacher would ask them to sit, close their eyes, and lick them when supposedly they were going to capture them. Upon hearing this, Rosy felt devastated and decided to investigate if other children had suffered the same situation. Healing to grow and transcend How to approach topics like child sexual abuse with children When talking to other mothers, they discovered that their daughters had also been victims of the same game and that the teacher had threatened to beat them and their parents if they reported it. Families have filed complaints for alleged child sexual abuse. To date, six families have formally filed complaints with the Prosecution Office, although they have not yet received the final verdict on the case. The parents feel frustrated and outraged, not only by the alleged abuse, but also by the initial response of the kindergarten director, who appeared incredulous to their complaints and did not immediately activate the corresponding protocol. Although the director ultimately activated the protocol and the authorities initiated an investigation, the parents demand justice and for the teacher Guillermo N to be detained and face the legal consequences of their actions. The parents of the Ovidio Crowley kindergarten demand a firm response from the authorities and commit to continuing the fight until justice is done for their children.

data.text: The Güemes Plan is not just a set of measures, it's a demonstration that in Salta we will not allow crime to intimidate our people, that narco-trafficking will not poison our young people, that human trafficking will not destroy their lives, I affirm the governor after the inauguration at Migrations in Puerto Chalanas in Aguas Blancas, the Modular Office of the Espacios Seguros program is functioning for the protection of victims of human trafficking and illegal human trafficking migrants. The inauguration was headed by Governor Gustavo Sáenz and the National Security Minister, Patricia Bullrich, who agreed to classify the mentioned crime as one of the worst forms of crime. The new office is part of the Güemes Plan, which was launched two months ago in this same place. This is another step, said Sáenz and affirmed that Plan Güemes is much more than a national security plan, it is a joint strategy to fight tirelessly against organized crime, narcotics trafficking, contraband, human trafficking, and related crimes. At the same time, Sáenz highlighted that the implementation of Plan Güemes is involving a significant increase in investigative procedures. The numbers recorded, The Minister specified that in this time 55 cases were registered, 87 procedures, of which 46 are related to sexual exploitation, especially of minors under 16, 16 of labor exploitation and the rest to be determined. 9-year-old boy survives week alone in Mexican jungle Photos October 17, 2024 The search for Ana Carolina Saucedo, a 22-year-old UVM student, who disappeared in Monterrey since last Friday, ended tragically. Her body was found by the search operation, and the circumstances of her death are being investigated. Ana Carolina Saucedo Bahena, a 22-year-old young woman and UVM student, was found dead after several days of search in the Cerro de las Mitras, Monterrey. The young woman had been reported missing on February 7 when she was heading to her university in the Cima de las Cumbres colony. Ana Carolina was last seen on Friday, February 7. According to reports, she was heading to the Cumbres campus of UVM, but never entered the facilities, and her name does not appear on the attendance list for that day. The young woman's mother reported that she had left her at the university in the morning, but upon returning to pick her up at 2:00 PM, she was no longer found at the location. On the same day of her disappearance, the family reported the case to the authorities, which led to the issuance of a missing person's file by the Special Investigations Agency. The file detailed that Ana Carolina was wearing a light blue denim pant, a short-sleeved gray t-shirt, and rose-colored shoes with gray from the Hoka brand. Her physical characteristics were also mentioned, including light brown wavy hair, light brown eyes, a height of 1.70 meters, and a scar on her left wrist. Coahuila Magistrate Luis Efrén Ríos Vega, Ana Carolina's uncle, used his social media to disseminate the missing person's file, requesting support to locate his niece. On her part, the young woman's mother also asked for help through social media, asking friends and family to share the information. The search operation began the weekend with the participation of 74 rescuers who used advanced technologies such as drones, aerial surveillance with helicopters, and specialized canine units for odor detection. The authorities focused on Cerro de las Mitras, a mountainous area west of Monterrey, known for its rugged terrain and dense vegetation, which made the search efforts difficult. On Monday morning, the operation was reinforced with additional personnel and specialized equipment. Elements from Nuevo León's Civil Protection, Civil Force, the Commission for the Search for Missing Persons, and various local corporations joined the search. The perimeter was cordoned off to ensure a safe and thorough search. The authorities also requested the public's collaboration, asking residents near Cerro de las Mitras to review their security cameras and provide any relevant information. Ana Carolina's family and friends launched campaigns on social media to gather clues about her whereabouts. Ana Carolina's body was found on Monday morning during the search operation on Cerro de las Mitras. The location was confirmed by municipal police officers who participated in the ground and air operation. The clothes, sneakers, and accessories found matched the description provided in the missing person's file, leading the authorities to consider it highly likely that it was the young student. Unofficial information indicated that the body was found with signs of possible violence, and for that reason, the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Feminicides took over the investigation of the case. The authorities are waiting for official identification by a family member to confirm the identity of the victim. The lifeless body of the young woman was found on a path leading to an area known as Cama de Piedra, a difficult-to-access area due to the rocky and steep roads. The terrain conditions complicated the rescue efforts, and the search had to be temporarily suspended on Sunday night due to low visibility, resuming early on Monday. Preliminary investigations include reviewing security recordings and witness testimonies indicating that Ana Carolina entered the Cerro de las Mitras area alone. Authorities continue with forensic analysis to determine the exact cause of death and whether there were signs of a criminal act or an accident. The deputy prosecutor of the Nuevo León Public Ministry, Luis Enrique Orozco, reported that they were tracing Ana Carolina's cell phone signals and the vehicle application record used. However, the last registered location of his phone is not the Cerro de las Mitras but a different one, which has opened up new lines of investigation. Cases of disappearance always shake the foundations of the populations in which they occur. Local authorities have assured that everything is being done to clarify the circumstances in which the death occurred. The Prosecutor's Office will continue with the investigations, and it is expected that in the coming days, more details will be provided about the case. The General Güemes prosecutor, Gustavo Vilar Rey, charged a 60-year-old man with the crimes of bestiality and home invasion in a real concurrence. The complaint was filed by the pet owner, who accused him of attacking her dog in her absence. Neighbors from the locality marched in repudiation of the incident and demanded harsher penalties for animal abusers. The owner of the canine, named Rabito, reported her neighbor for an aberrant case of sexual abuse that occurred on January 27 in the Santa Rosa de Campo Santo neighborhood. According to her testimony, upon returning to her home in the afternoon, she found the man in the backyard of her house, allegedly abusing the dog. Upon noticing her presence, the suspect fled the scene. The case went viral on social media, where the owner and various users identified the man as the alleged perpetrator of the attack. Following the complaint, a veterinarian examined the animal and found injuries in the anal region, although she could not confirm their origin with certainty. Nevertheless, the medical report certified the animal's poor health, reinforcing the suspicions of sexual abuse. Prosecutor Vilar Rey stated in the indictment that the accused would have committed an act of sexual abuse against the animal, causing unnecessary suffering and mistreatment out of sheer perversity. In addition, he is accused of breaking and entering, as he allegedly entered the residence without permission by crossing a fence. During the indictment hearing, the accused presented his version of events, although details of his testimony have not been made public yet. March in demand for justice The outrage over the case mobilized the community of General Güemes On January 31, around 150 neighbors marched through the streets of the city demanding justice for Rabito and harsher penalties for animal abusers. The mobilization passed through streets adjacent to the central square and ended in front of the Salcedo family's veterinary clinic, where the dog was treated. In an emotional moment, Rabito was taken to the sidewalk to receive the affection of the protesters. We want justice, we want the abuser to pay for what they did, and we want this not to happen again. We need tougher laws against animal cruelty because today's penalties are laughable. We want the council members to work on an ordinance with exemplary punishments, said the animal protectors who organized the march.

A store employee in Viedma kissed a girl and was charged with simple sexual abuse. The prosecutor's office in this city filed charges against a man of Chinese nationality, for the crime of simple sexual abuse that he allegedly committed inside the supermarket where he works. A translator participated in the hearing, who translated the content of the hearing into Mandarin Chinese, so that the accused could understand the accusation and the evidence that supports it. He was accused of being the one who, on September 17 of last year, at 12:30 pm, took advantage of a 9-year-old girl who was alone for a moment and away from her mother, and kissed her on the mouth against her will, affecting her sexual integrity. This happened in a supermarket located on Boulevard Sussini N 532 in Viedma, where the man works. The accusation classified the events as simple sexual abuse for which the man is responsible as the author, in accordance with Articles 45 and 119 of the Penal Code. As evidence, the Prosecution mentioned having a filed penal complaint from the victim's mother and the statement given by the girl and her brother in a closed-door hearing. Additionally, they added the testimony of the person who heard the girl recount what happened as soon as she left the store, and the images obtained from the security cameras' footage recording inside the establishment, where the entirety of the described event is visible. The defendant's defense opposed the filing of charges, recounting the events in a different manner than how they were accused. Nonetheless, after hearing from the parties, the intervening Judge of Guarantees considered the charges to be filed. In addition, at the request of the prosecution, the judge extended the precautionary measures that had already been imposed on the man, including a ban on approaching and contacting the victim and their family members as well as the witnesses who testified in the case.

Police Breakthroughs Key Revelations The new autopsy in the double murder of Florencio Varela ruled out sexual abuse BY REPORTING STAFF The investigation into the double murder of 16-year-old Paloma Gallardo and 14-year-old Josué Salvatierra, which occurred in Florencio Varela, took a turn with the results of the supplementary autopsy report. This analysis revealed that there were no indications of sexual abuse, contradicting the initial hypothesis of the victims' parents, who claimed that the crime was motivated by an attempt at rape. The report indicated that the young people were beaten on the head with a blunt object for at least 30 minutes before losing their lives. This chilling data was one of the most impactful revelations of the forensic analysis, which also confirmed that the cause of death was a double skull fracture. Despite these new findings, Paloma's family continues to claim that there was an uncommitted sexual abuse. The complaint will continue to pursue this line of investigation, despite the autopsy results contradicting this claim. On the part of the Salvatierra family, through their lawyer, they stated that the boys would have been killed because they saw something related to the narcomenudeo operations that take place in the abandoned land where the bodies were found. The situation in the case became even more complicated when prosecutor Hernán Bustos Rivas requested to be removed from the case after receiving threats and harassment from the lawyers of the complaint. The prosecutor argued that the moral violence he was exposed to prevented him from continuing the investigation with the necessary balance. In response to this resignation, Judge Adrián Villagra of the 8th Guarantees Court of Quilmes accepted his request and determined that a new prosecutor's office would take over the case. The clarification of the double crime continues without significant progress. Despite the efforts of the Prosecution, they have not yet been able to identify suspects or carry out successful raids in the area where the crime occurred. The hypotheses continue to face each other while the police version points to a robbery followed by murder, the victims' family questions this interpretation and suggests that the young people were murdered because they witnessed something related to illicit activities at the crime scene. The investigation continues open, with more questions than answers, while the Florencio Varela community awaits justice for the victims.

A Better Life in Europe The shipwreck occurred in Marsa Dela, in the city of Zawiya, where approximately 65 people were traveling to Europe, according to a report by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan. Among the 37 survivors, 33 are in custody of Libyan police and one is receiving medical attention at a hospital. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed his condolences for the tragedy and ordered the identification of the victims and assistance to their families. Furthermore, he promised to take action against the human traffickers responsible for the incident. Many migrants, particularly from Kurram in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, risk their lives on perilous routes due to a lack of job opportunities in their country. Human trafficking networks exploit their desperation, exposing them to extreme conditions and scams. According to R3cp, Libya has become a key point for migrant trafficking since the fall of Gaddafi in 2011. In 2024, at least 674 people have died and more than 1,000 remain missing in their attempt to cross the Mediterranean. According to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Despite the risks, thousands of people continue to embark on the perilous journey to Europe. International authorities demand stricter measures against traffickers and greater protection for migrants seeking a better future.

The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) of Elon Musk has ravaged the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). From a workforce of 10,000 employees, only 300 remain, putting hundreds of organizations that provide vital security services at risk. Numerous child safety groups, including those fighting against child sexual exploitation and abuse online, claim that their efforts have been severely hindered. The task of helping without resources has become a major challenge.According to various organizations that spoke to WIRED, groups that identify victims and assist those who have been exploited or trafficked online face difficulties in helping vulnerable children. These child safety projects typically take place in the poorest countries, which may have fewer resources to support victims or investigate crimes. The sources claim that the funding for safe houses has been interrupted, exposing those affected to further harm, and efforts to identify the perpetrators behind these crimes have also been suspended. "It will be very difficult for us to identify the victims," says Chantal Yelu Mulop, of the Coordination for Youth and the Fight against Sexual Violence and Human Trafficking (CJVFFT), in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The country, already devastated by war, is facing new humanitarian crises and battles over child trafficking to work in cobalt mines linked to the production of smartphone and electric vehicle batteries. When USAID funding was withdrawn last week, Mulop reports that her organization was just starting to help around 25 newly identified victims of human trafficking, all of them under 17 years old. The group was transferred to a shelter managed by another organization. When we took them there, USAID was willing to help. Hours later, they cancelled. There's no food, nothing we can provide for them. Although USAID's cuts have been immediate, global child protection projects have also faced a halt in funding from the Department of State. This external aid pause, issued by the Trump administration, will last at least 90 days. USAID did not respond to WIRED's request for comment, nor did the Department of State (DOS). Both government agencies have provided funds to help countries and people worldwide. This includes the vast range of USAID health care and education programs, whose withdrawal puts millions of lives at risk and limits the fight against the climate crisis. In Southeast Asia, several patients from a migrant camp died after medical aid was withdrawn. The immediate repercussions of the funding cuts for the fight against human trafficking typically include funds for projects that help take decisive action against child exploitation and online sexual abuse. The funding may be allocated to international organizations that coordinate efforts and work with field partners, such as the CJVFFT in Mulop. The funding may help victims directly, as well as provide specialized knowledge to national officials, and prevent more children from becoming targets. Many of these victims are connected to their traffickers through electronic means. It's an exploitation that advances through digital technology, explains Jessica Ryckman, executive director of the non-profit organization Lawyers Without Borders (LWOB), specializing in child trafficking and exploitation programs, and also affected by funding changes. Over the years, the programs have been effective. For example, a four-year partnership between the US and the Philippines, which began under the first Trump administration and ended in 2021, helped protect over 350 children, and nearly 100 potential criminals were arrested. The new cuts come as record levels of online child sexual abuse images are being uncovered. Both victims and perpetrators come from various regions and countries, highlighting the need for continued international commitment and coordinated efforts to address these crimes comprehensively. An employee of a South American child protection group works to combat human trafficking and online sexual abuse. The institution, like others featured in this report, was granted anonymity due to the sensitive nature of their work and uncertainty over future funding. Disruptions to these funds inevitably limit the scope and reach of these critical services. A person working for an organization that carries out multiple child protection projects reports that operations in a Southeast European country have been widely disrupted. The source highlights that within the country, the organization's projects have 147 victims of human trafficking under their care. The current pause and potential cessation of funding would have a significant and negative impact on our capacity and ability to provide essential services to these vulnerable victims who are at fragile stages of their recovery, some of whom are currently enrolled in ongoing programs for psycho-social counseling related to their trauma. Who will watch over the children? Several members of LWOB claim that the children are at greater risk in the projects they oversee in Eastern Africa. It may not be possible to identify these children and support practices to reduce their trauma at this time, Ryckman asserts. Even if they are identified, they may be put in a situation where they will have to face repeated interviews about their trauma or face their traffickers again. Lulu Makwale, coordinator of services for victims at Abogados sin Fronteras, highlights that LWOB has identified, along with associated organizations, around 200 victims of human trafficking in Tanzania, and most have been referred to reception centers. The majority of funding for the reception centers has been interrupted, meaning that services and the needs of the victims have also ceased. She adds that the organization has maintained contact with refugees with investigators. It is possible that the victims are no longer well-connected with law enforcement. In addition to directly supporting the victims, many initiatives also provide training or technical assistance to the police, enabling them to investigate crimes better. One of the programs included in the DES funding list claims to be providing training to combat child sexual exploitation on the internet for 10,000 police officers, prosecutors, and judges from 100 countries. A person linked to the organization's work in a European country denies that their organization has 74 ongoing investigations into traffickers, as well as 66 ongoing prosecutions. They emphasize that the changes in funding will have a significant and negative impact on these criminal proceedings and the safety of individuals who may be called to testify in cases. Recently, Lawyers Without Borders completed the creation of an online database to identify and track child exploitation victims in Kenya. Ryckman argues that although the database is functional, the training of personnel has been paused, and there will be a slower adoption of the system, which will be very useful. But these victims are here now. They shouldn't wait. Originally published in WIRED. Adapted by Alondra Flores.

Although the overall picture is complex, data from the National Public Security System (SESNSP) up to April 2024 points to 2,529 cases of human trafficking among people aged 0 to 17, with a significant majority of females (1,890 women vs. 639 men). The entities with the highest incidence are the City of Mexico (24 cases), Quintana Roo (24 cases), and the State of Mexico (22 cases). These figures, although partial, paint a worrisome picture of the situation. Deputy Luis Chávez from Morena has presented an initiative with the goal of modifying Article 1 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States. His proposal aims to consider human trafficking as a form of slavery, reinforcing the gravity of the crime and its classification as a crime against humanity. In Mexico, there are no clear data on the economic gains from human trafficking with various purposes, including sexual exploitation. Due to possible activities related to sex trafficking for exploitation, 1,410 bank accounts were blocked for 116 individuals, totaling 144 million 197 thousand 710 pesos, Chávez states, citing a 2021 forum of the Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF). This initiative is based on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, specifically Article 19, which promotes comprehensive protection of childhood against any form of abuse, including exploitation. Additionally, it aligns with the Palermo Protocol, ratified by Mexico in 2003, which defines trafficking as the capture, transportation, transfer, reception, or accommodation of people. Chávez's proposal aims to amend the fourth paragraph of Article 1 of the Constitution, explicitly including the prohibition of trafficking as an extension of the prohibition of slavery. This initiative is currently under analysis in the Joint Committees on Constitutional Matters and Citizen Initiatives and Human Rights.

A German mercenary identified as Ben R. has been arrested in Ukraine on suspicion of multiple sex crimes in his home country. This former German Armed Forces soldier, who joined the forces of Kiev, had been considered a hero by several German media outlets before allegations against him surfaced. According to the German weekly Der Spiegel, Ben R. faces charges of rape and sexual assault, as well as possession and distribution of child pornography in Germany. He is also being investigated for the rape of a minor in Ukraine. German authorities have requested his extradition, as per the public prosecutor's office of Bavaria. Ben R.'s troubled past saw him join the German Armed Forces in 2013, signing a 12-year contract that is set to expire in 2025. In 2021, the military authorities initiated an investigation after receiving complaints from at least four women who accused him of sexual harassment and rape. However, two of these complainants withdrew their complaints, and the investigations were ultimately dismissed for various reasons. The case of Ben R. resurfaced in 2022, when the U.S. National Center for Missing and Exploited Children alerted German police about the distribution of child pornography linked to him on the Discord platform. In March of that year, German police conducted a search at his residence in Bavaria, where they seized electronic devices containing thousands of images and videos of sexual violence against minors. Following these incidents, Ben R. moved to Ukraine, where he joined a group providing medical aid to soldiers on the front lines. In June 2022, the German tabloid Bild portrayed him as a German hero saving the lives of Ukrainian soldiers. However, in September 2022, the Bavarian prosecutor's office issued a European arrest warrant against him. Despite the arrest warrant, Ben R. continued to communicate with German media and, in the summer of 2023, claimed to be officially integrated into the Ukrainian army, receiving between €2,000 and €2,500 for his services. The German authorities requested his extradition to Ukraine in 2023, but did not receive a response. In November 2023, new pornographic materials linked to Ben R. were discovered on the internet, leading investigators to suspect at least six new cases of rape. The Santiago del Estero Peasant Movement (Mocase) issued a statement informing the arrest of a man suspected of being involved in an armed attack on an indigenous community in the interior of Mitre Department. In the statement, the peasant organization asserts that the subject, Kemel, is implicated in numerous criminal activities, including ties to the Rosario-based narco gang Los Monos. The organizer of armed gangs in the Pinto area, Aguirre Department, Diego Kemel, business partner of Cordoba businessman Andrés Camaduro and Spanish businessman Fuentes Barrau, was arrested in Añatuya, General Taboada Department, after months of being a fugitive from justice. Diego Kemel had a national arrest warrant and preventive imprisonment, as he was involved in the armed attack on the indigenous community Sentimiento de mi tierra of the Sanavirón people in the Las Abras area, Mitre department, in October 2024. Kemel is being investigated for his involvement in crimes, organized robbery, narcotics trafficking, and human trafficking. He is suspected of links to the Rosario cartel Los Monos, as well as being involved in the embezzlement of public funds during Emilio Rached's tenure as mayor of Pinto in the 2000s.

data.text: Suspected members of the Venezuelan gang Aragua Train were among the eight people charged with federal human trafficking charges in Tennessee, the US Department of Justice said. Acting Attorney General Robert E. McGuire said on Tuesday that two of the accused used their affiliation with Aragua Train to intimidate the victims and force them to continue engaging in sex trade. All eight accused are Venezuelan citizens, and five of them are women, according to the federal indictment. The human trafficking conspiracy members conspired to identify and recruit young, poor, and vulnerable women from Venezuela and other countries in South and Central America with the intention of transporting them to the US and profiting from their sex acts, the indictment alleges. The US Attorney's Office The Middle District of Tennessee announced the charges at a press conference shortly after the indictment became public. While the arrests focused on dismantling a prostitution ring, at least one of the accused human traffickers was also charged with illegal possession of a firearm, McGuire said. After the victims arrived in the United States, an inflated debt was imposed on them and they were required to engage in sex trade acts for the benefit of the accused until, and sometimes even after, the debt was paid, the indictment alleges. Due to the imposed debt, the victims continued to engage in sex trade acts out of fear of the severe harm they or their families could suffer if they attempted to leave before paying their debts, the indictment alleges. CNN was unable to locate a defense attorney for the accused and no attorney was listed in court records. The investigation by multiple agencies began as a local inquiry by the Metropolitan Police Department of Nashville and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), according to federal officials. The Tren de Aragua crime gang was born in a Venezuelan prison and has gradually spread to both the north and south of the Caribbean country in recent years. Recently, it brought terror not only to Venezuela but also to Bolivia, Colombia, Chile, and Peru. While the gang has primarily focused on human trafficking and other crimes affecting migrants, it has also been linked to extortion, kidnapping, money laundering, and drug smuggling, according to the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury. A U.S. government decree Signed on January 20, it specifically named the Aragua Train and the Salvadoran gang MS13 as threats to the stability of international order in the Western Hemisphere, based on their campaigns of violence and terror in the United States and internationally. As CNN previously reported, federal officials dismantled in April 2024 another human trafficking network linked to the Aragua Train that was based in Louisiana and operated storage houses used for human trafficking in Texas, Virginia, New Jersey, and Florida. Prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro requested today the dismissal of Matanza district chief Fernando Espinoza in the case of alleged sexual abuse against his former private secretary Melody Rakauskas. According to the prosecution's argument in an 80-page document, Cuñarro's request is based on the fact that there is no evidence in the case files to support the charges beyond the statements of the accuser. Following this presentation, the judge presiding over the case must decide whether to grant the prosecution's request. The judge in charge of the case was Luis Schelgel, but he was replaced by Fernando Caunedo. The plaintiff had requested the case be sent to trial and, at that stage, the judge requested Cuñarro's opinion, who recommended the dismissal of Espinoza. Meanwhile, despite the prosecution's request, Rakauskas's defense team may still insist on sending the case to trial against the community chief. The former secretary of the Intendant of La Matanza was presented in 2021, when she accused him of having abused her in a meeting that took place outside of working hours. The Chamber of Crimes had ratified, in July 2024, the prosecution of the Intendant for the crimes of sexual abuse and disobedience to a judicial order. This left the case ready for trial. The accusation of disobedience is based on the fact that, despite having a restriction that prevented him from approaching, Espinoza would have contacted Rakauskas to ask him to cancel the complaint. The community chief has publicly expressed criticism of his former secretary under the argument that she refused to hand over her cell phone and computer to be analyzed. Espinoza also argued that the complaint is part of a case of espionage against him. Local news was never so important SUBSCRIBE to this special promotion

Yamila Cuello's trial will begin on February 20. The case has two defendants accused of murder. The young woman was abducted in October 2009. Yamila Cuello has been missing since October 25, 2009. A young woman from Coronel Olmedo's neighborhood got into a fight with one of the defendants on that day, left her house to eat with some friends, and never arrived at her destination. After years of struggle by her family and relatives, a trial will take place in which there are two men accused. It will begin on February 20 at the Federal Oral Court No. 2. Thirteen years without Yamila Cuello: a new march demanded justice in Córdoba. Néstor Simone, her former partner, is accused of murder, and his brother, Horacio Palacios, is accused of human trafficking for sexual exploitation and murder. Juan Pablo Cuello, a friend of Yamila's family, spoke with Canal 10 about the start of this long-awaited trial and expressed: We hope for an exemplary sentence and to get a little bit of justice for this family. Cuello also explained that Simone cannot be judged for human trafficking because he was acquitted less than a year after Yamila's disappearance, which is very striking and we want to make visible in this trial. 13 years after her disappearance, they confirmed the charges in the Yamila Cuello case. It took 13 years for charges to be confirmed and three more years for the trial to begin. Her family fought and made the fact visible throughout this time. It's essential that they know what happened to her.

The prosecutor requested the dismissal of Fernando Espinoza in the case of alleged sexual abuse. The request was made by prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro in the case of alleged sexual abuse against Melody Rakauskas, former private secretary of the mayor of La Matanza. Prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro requested today the dismissal of the mayor of La Matanza Fernando Espinoza in the case of alleged sexual abuse against his former private secretary Melody Rakauskas. According to the arguments presented by the prosecution in an 80-page document to which the Argentine News Agency had access, Cuñarro's request is based on the fact that there are no elements of evidence in the case files that support the accusation, beyond the statements of the complainant. After this presentation, the judge intervening in the case must decide whether to grant the prosecutor's request. The responsible magistrate was Luis Schelgel, but he was replaced by Fernando Caunedo. The indictment had requested the case to be elevated to oral trial, and in that instance, the magistrate asked for the opinion of Cuñarro, who recommended the dismissal of Espinoza. Meanwhile, despite the request of the prosecution, Rakauskas's defense can insist on the elevation of the case to trial against the community leader. The former secretary of the Intendant of La Matanza was presented in 2021, when she accused him of having abused her in a meeting that took place outside of work hours. The Chamber of Crimes had ratified, in July 2024, the processing of the Intendant for the crimes of sexual abuse and disobedience to a judicial order. Therefore, the case was left ready for trial. The accusation of disobedience is based on the fact that, despite having a restriction that prevented him from approaching, Espinoza would have contacted Rakauskas to ask him to annul the complaint. The community leader has publicly expressed criticism towards his former secretary on the grounds that she refused to hand over her cell phone and computer for analysis. Espinoza also argued that the complaint is part of a case of espionage against him.

(Pictures) Two Young Men Arrested for Car Theft Ring in Cristo Rey and Heredia Two 20- and 22-year-old males were detained for allegedly being part of a criminal gang responsible for vehicle thefts in San José, Heredia, Cartago, and Alajuela. The individuals are a 20-year-old man with the last name Castro and a 22-year-old man with the last name Pérez. Castro was apprehended by authorities in a public area in the Cristo Rey neighborhood, San José. Meanwhile, the 22-year-old Pérez turned himself in voluntarily at the Heredia Courts. This was confirmed by the Judicial Investigation Organization (OIJ). Detained by the OIJ in Cristo Rey, San José. Photo courtesy. The Case The Judicial Police carried out a total of 34 operations in the morning of Monday to dismantle the criminal structure in various points of the Greater Metropolitan Area (GAM). At dawn on Monday, 19 people were detained who were suspected of involvement, and at least 40 more alleged perpetrators were expected to be apprehended. It appears that this gang, linked to high-end vehicle theft, is also being investigated for extortion, drug trafficking, fraud, and other apparent crimes. It is presumed that the gang is led by a man named Gatjens from prison, who would be the ringleader of the criminal group. The Morena deputy, Luis Chávez, proposed an initiative to reform Article 1 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States with the aim of equating human trafficking with slavery, since it is an international crime against humanity that violates the rights of people, including children. According to the crime incidence statistics of the common jurisdiction of the National Public Security System (SESNSP), as of April 2024, 2,529 people aged 0 to 17 (1,890 women and 639 men) have been victims of human trafficking in Mexico. The entities in which the most victims of human trafficking among people aged 0 to 17 have been registered from January to April 2024 have been Mexico City (24), Quintana Roo (24), and the State of Mexico (22). In Mexico, there are no clear data on the economic gains from human trafficking for various purposes, including sexual exploitation. At a 2021 forum, the head of the Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) noted that 1,410 bank accounts were blocked for 116 people suspected of human trafficking for sexual exploitation, totaling 144 million 197 thousand 710 pesos. Luis Chávez Human trafficking is a crime that seriously endangers girls, boys, and adolescents. Therefore, it is indispensable to provide the legal protection that the Convention on the Rights of the Child recommends in Article 19, which includes all legislative, administrative, social, and educational measures to protect the child from any form of harm or abuse, physical or mental, neglect, or mistreatment, including sexual abuse. In addition, it incorporates the Palermo Protocol, ratified by our country on December 25, 2003, which has among its goals, the prevention and combat of human trafficking, paying special attention to women and children. The protocol defines human trafficking as the capture, transportation, transfer, reception, or accommodation of people, resorting to threats or the use of force, or other forms of coercion, kidnapping, fraud, deception, abuse of power, or a situation of vulnerability, or the provision or receipt of payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person who has authority over another, with a view to exploitation. That exploitation will include, at a minimum, the exploitation of another's prostitution or other forms of sexual exploitation, forced labor or services, slavery, or practices analogous to slavery, servitude, or the removal of organs. Due to this reason, the convention calls for establishing broad policies, programs, and other measures to prevent and combat human trafficking, as well as to protect human trafficking victims, especially women and children, against a new risk of victimization. On the other hand, the General Law to Prevent, Punish, and Eradicate Crimes Related to Human Trafficking, and to Protect and Assist Victims of these Crimes expands the concept of human trafficking to include any intentional action or omission to recruit, entice, transport, transfer, retain, deliver, receive, or harbor one or more persons for the purpose of exploitation. In the same law, exploitation is understood as slavery, the condition of a serf, alien prostitution or other forms of sexual exploitation, labor exploitation, forced labor or services, forced begging, the use of people under 18 years old in criminal activities, illegal adoption, forced or servile marriage, the trafficking of human organs, tissues and cells of living humans, and illicit biomedical experimentation on humans. The initiative of legislator Luis Alberto Chávez García proposes to reform the fourth paragraph of Article 1 of the Constitution, which prohibits slavery and trafficking in the United Mexican States. Foreign slaves who enter the national territory will, by this fact alone, achieve their freedom and the protection of the laws. The initiative was turned over to the Joint Committees on Constitutional Matters and Citizen Initiatives and that of Human Rights for analysis and discussion.

data.text: WASHINGTON The Trump administration requested help from National Tax Service agents (IRS in English) in their fight against irregular immigration, especially in regards to human trafficking and identifying businesses that employ undocumented immigrants. The request was made in a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem. Instead of having (under President Joe Biden's administration) 87,000 IRS agents taking more money from Americans, I requested that they help taxpayers save money by assisting ICE in gathering undocumented immigrants for deportation, Noem stated on her X account. According to FOX News, a high-ranking DHS official consulted by that channel stated that the expectation is that the request will be approved. The DHS requested in the letter to the Treasury Department to authorize agents from the IRS's Criminal Investigation Division to participate in the enforcement of immigration policies. Since 2022, the IRS's Criminal Investigation Division has experienced a specialized expansion, specializing in financial crimes with armed agents and the authority to make arrests. The officers already collaborate with other federal agencies in cases of drug trafficking and corruption. According to FOX, Noem, who signed the letter, said that President Trump ordered her agency to take all necessary measures to complement the available personnel to secure the southern border and enforce US immigration laws, including the use of the agency's authority to delegate federal employees to perform immigration functions.

On Tuesday, a 57-year-old man was arrested and accused of abusing his nieces when they were minors. He is currently being held at Batán prison, charged with sexual abuse with carnal access and sexual abuse. According to the police report, the first reported incident does not specify a date, but it is detailed that from 2012 to 2016, the accused, who was in charge of his nieces, repeatedly sexually abused them at their home in the Los Acantilados neighborhood, by touching their intimate areas under their clothing in exchange for money. In a second instance, the second incident referred to in the investigation, for which no exact date could be provided, but occurred during 2016 and up to February 2024, and in relation to one of the then minors, the incidents evolved into carnal sexual abuses accessing her vaginally and anally, according to the cause. After various investigations and investigative tasks carried out following the presentation of a complaint, personnel from the Sexual Integrity Crimes Bureau of the DDI obtained a search warrant and arrest order that could not be materialized, leaving the defendant as a fugitive. Crimes occurred between 2020 and 2022 when the victim was between 12 and 14 years old. A man identified as J.F.L.C. was sentenced to 18 years and 3 days in prison for the crimes of rape and repeated sexual abuse against his own goddaughter in Curicó, in the Maule Region. The court determined that the defendant took advantage of his relationship of trust with the minor to commit the attacks between 2020 and 2022, when the girl was between 12 and 14 years old. A home turned into a scene of abuse According to the details provided by the Prosecution, the convicted man was a live-in partner of the victim's mother and the godfather of the minor, thus having direct access to the girl in the family home. On repeated occasions, he abused her while she was under his care, leading the minor to live years of terror and silence. Finally, the affected party gathered the courage to tell her mother and school authorities what had happened, allowing the opening of an investigation. Investigation and Conviction After the complaint, the Sexual Crimes Investigator Brigade (Brisex) of the PDI carried out various procedures, collecting key evidence for the trial. Prosecutor Tatiana Díaz highlighted the strength of the evidence presented. The Prosecution had a series of evidence, including documentary, testimonial, and expert evidence, including the victim's statement, who attended the oral trial and declared under judicial protective mediation, noted the prosecutor. Thanks to these precedents, J.F.L.C. was sentenced to serve the sentence in its entirety, with no possibility of prison benefits. Zacatecas, Zac. Senator Geovanna Bañuelos has requested that the Secretariat of Public Security and Citizen Protection, the National Guard, and the security authorities in the 32 federal entities provide protection to migrant girls, boys, and adolescents who are being deported as a result of the policies implemented by the United States. This is because, as minors, they are a double-vulnerable group and are at risk of suffering crimes such as human trafficking, extortion, or being recruited by criminal groups and organized crime. In addition, the vice-coordinator of the Parliamentary Group of the Workers' Party, requests that the Secretariat of Governance coordinate with the state governments, especially with the entities of the northern border, to establish temporary shelters for migrant girls, boys, and adolescents of Mexican origin who return to national territory with the goal of protecting their physical integrity, dignity, and human rights. Through a point of agreement presented to the Senate Plenary, Geovanna Bañuelos calls on the National Migration Institute, to strengthen, in coordination with the National System for the Integral Development of the Family and with the Executive Secretary of the National System for the Protection of Girls, Boys, and Adolescents, the measures of attention, assistance, and follow-up for migrant girls, boys, and adolescents, guaranteeing their human rights at all times. In the document published in the Gazette, the legislator from Zacatecas highlights that migrant girls, boys, and adolescents represent one of the most vulnerable groups within migrant flows. In Latin America and the Caribbean, for example, a significant increase has been observed in the number of migrant girls, boys, and adolescents, many of whom are under the age of 11, posing additional challenges for migration policies and humanitarian responses in the region. Since minors face specific risks such as family separation, recruitment by criminal groups, and limited access to education and healthcare, Geovanna Bañuelos warns that the migration of girls, boys, and adolescents is a growing phenomenon. With the anti-immigrant policies implemented by the government of Donald Trump in the United States, they face multiple humanitarian and legal challenges. The problem itself is already severe and could worsen further. In 2024, the United States deported 28,270 Mexican girls, boys, and adolescents, either alone or accompanied by their families. This is the highest number since 2008, when there were 34,083 cases, according to data from the Office of Immigration Policy of the Ministry of the Interior. Among the 28,270 Mexican children and adolescents returned, 16,303 are between 12 and 17 years old, and 1,967 are between 0 and 11 years old. Of the latter group, 11,813 traveled accompanied and 154 alone. As a result, it is crucial that during their repatriation, their human rights be safeguarded, as well as their integrity and dignity. The problem of migrant girls, boys, and adolescents that the government of the United States seeks to deport is multifaceted and requires urgent attention, asserts Geovanna Bañuelos. In this sense, she asserts that it is essential for immigration policies to prioritize the well-being and rights of minors, ensuring their protection and access to fair and just legal procedures. Additionally, it is necessary to guarantee the attention to the psychological and social effects that these policies have on children and their families, promoting solutions that ensure their integrity and dignity. In the Workers' Party, we have emphasized the need to establish support mechanisms for migrants, especially the most vulnerable, avoiding that they suffer risks such as human trafficking, child exploitation, recruitment into organized crime, among others, concluded Geovanna Bañuelos.

Government officials from the Ministry of the Family conducted nighttime patrols in border areas, recreation and leisure zones in Corinto, Cárdenas, Moyogalpa, and Granada, with the goal of sensitizing business owners and entrepreneurs about the consequences of human trafficking and sex exploitation. It was reported that from February 7 to 9, direct presence visitation days were held in neighborhoods, rural communities, indigenous villages, production zones, and border checkpoints, where 1,867 people were spoken to, reaffirming family unity, practicing values, fraternal and peaceful coexistence to prevent manifestations of domestic violence. A planning session was participated in by the inter-institutional commission Amor para los Más Chiquitos de León, to develop preventive actions, update vaccination schedules, and weigh and measure children aged 6. With MINSA, the weight and height of 38 children from Ocotal, Nueva Segovia were registered. Additionally, shared and complementary responsibility was strengthened among 203 families nationwide, promoting their active, protagonistic, and continuous participation in their children's school life, preventing early school dropout. Similarly, 108 children and adolescents from San Francisco Libre, Cárdenas, Santa Teresa, and La Paz were integrated into preventive, formative, sports, and cultural programs to overcome social risk. Furthermore, the capacity to identify and prevent sexual violence was strengthened with 84 families from Pueblo Nuevo, La Paz, and Bocana de Paiwas. 26 family counseling sessions were provided to 36 mothers and fathers, strengthening the attentive, fraternal, and respectful dialogue that must prevail in couple relationships to prevent misunderstandings and manifestations of violence. A new cycle of Values Schools began with 91 mothers, fathers, and guardians from Belén, Managua, and Granada. Additionally, we continue developing these training cycles with 14 adolescents and young people from Muelle de los Bueyes and 5 firefighters from Nindirí. From the Psychosocial Attention, we strengthened peaceful coexistence for the construction of safe, protective, and violence-free environments in 40 homes in Managua, Granada, Carazo, Estelí, Nueva Segovia, Siuna, and Bonanza. Likewise, specialized psychological attention was provided to 2 children and adolescents, contributing to their emotional recovery. The rights of 7 children in a vulnerable situation were reinstated, guaranteeing their integral safety and protection. We also accompanied 6 children before the Civil Registry of the People of Managua and León, ensuring their right to a name, nationality, and family. We attended 15 administrative conciliations in favor of 20 children, with a total of 27,818.07, and paid 1,535 alimony pensions totaling 3,950,548. 0.05 córdobas was provided with information and guidance to families regarding international food collection in benefit of 5 children. 567 people were attended to through the 133 Line, and we also provided counseling and information to 77 protagonists through WhatsApp messaging, detecting 8 high-risk situations in the delegations of Carazo, Managua, and Rivas. MIFAMILIA continued providing accompaniment and permanent emotional support to 573 children and adolescents who use the Digital Application ARI (remote emotional assistant), where 1 situation of loss of love for life was detected, leading to valuation and accompaniment by the municipal delegation of Mateare.
