The Barahona Court of Justice sentences a man to 15 years in prison for sexually abusing a 12-year-old. The defendant must also pay RD$200,000.00 to the Dominican State and RD$500,000.00 to the plaintiff for moral damages. The College Chamber of the Penal Chamber of the First Instance Court of the Judicial District of Barahona sentenced a man found guilty of sexually violating a 12-year-old student in the municipality of Enriquillo, a coastal area of the province. The incident occurred in 2020. The court, composed of judges Celina Novas Jiménez, acting president, Santa Kenia Pérez Feliz, and Elidermia Ortiz Vargas, found the defendant T.F.G. guilty of the charges. In addition to sentencing the defendant to 15 years in prison, which he must serve in the public prison in Barahona, the defendant must pay a fine of RD$200,000.00. In favor of the Dominican State, the sum of RD$500,000.00 was ordered in favor of the plaintiff for moral damages caused and the costs of the penal process. Attorneys Hugo Francisco Gómez Pérez and Melvin Manolin Reyes Batista represented the victim D.O.F.C. and her parent L.M.C.F., whose identities, as well as that of the perpetrator, are omitted to protect the identity of the minor, as established in Law 13603 or the Code of Protection for Children, Adolescents, and Youth. The judges found sufficient elements to condemn the defendant for violating the provisions contained in Articles 330 and 331 of the Dominican Penal Code, Article 396, letter C, of Law 13603, which typify and sanction the crime of sexual abuse of a minor. Aura Deyanira Fernández Cury, prosecutor of the Unit for Attention to Victims of Gender Violence, Family Violence, and Sexual Crimes, who requested the imposition of the imposed prison sentence, for violating Articles 330 and 331 of the Dominican Penal Code and Article 396, letter C, of Law 13603. On February 10, 2020, around 8:30 am, in a house located near the José Antonio Álvarez educational center, located in the Las Merceditas community, Enriquillo municipality, the accused T.F.G., a native of La Ciénaga, sexually assaulted the minor D.O.F.C., who was 12 years old at the time. On that day, the minor was on her way to school but stopped at a convenience store to buy sweets. The perpetrator took advantage of the situation to invite the child to his house and, upon entering the residence, he lowered his pants and underwear and committed the sexual assault. When the minor arrived at school, her teacher M.S.F. and the principal B.P.M. noticed that she was visibly distressed and asked her what was wrong. Upon noting the child's tardiness in arriving at the educational center, they observed that he looked very nervous and appeared to have been traumatized, so, upon questioning him, he confessed that he had been raped by the convicted perpetrator. Additionally, the forensic psychological report, applied by Dania Romero, forensic psychologist, confirms what the minor stated about the sexual assault by the accused.

However, in 2023, he appeared in Ukraine, fighting near the city of Artiómovsk (also known as Bakhmut), filming battles, and was wounded. Afterwards, he reported his experience in a Bild podcast. In addition to the three cases mentioned, there would be others related to attacks on women. It is detailed that in Ukraine, he also committed sex crimes and then published videos of his crimes on the internet. According to Der Spiegel, Ben R. possessed thousands of photos and recordings of child abuse, which were found after a search of his apartment in Germany. Now he is being investigated in Kiev, among other things, for the rape of a minor.

Published 12 Feb 2025 0610 MADRID, 12 Amnesty International has warned on Wednesday that the relentless violence in Haiti has put more than a million children and young people in the hands of criminal gangs, victims of all sorts of atrocities, from forced recruitment, murders, kidnappings, and rapes. Too many children in Haiti are seeing their lives destroyed, Amnesty International Secretary-General Agnes Callamard lamented in a latest report presented on Wednesday, titled I am a child, why has this happened to me? Aggressions by criminal gangs against childhood in Haiti. Since the assassination of President Jovenel Moise in July 2021, violence has significantly increased in Haiti, whose capital, Port-au-Prince, is largely under the control of criminal gangs, responsible for at least 5,600 deaths in the past year. Criminal gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti. They threaten, beat, rape, and kill children and girls. They have committed multiple abuses against the rights of the child, including the right to life, education, and freedom of movement, Callamard has reported. More than a million minors live in areas controlled by criminal gangs. Children and girls suffer daily violations of their bodies, minds, and hearts. Haiti urgently needs assistance to protect children and prevent new cycles of violence, Callamard has demanded. In this sense, Amnesty has pointed out that the conclusions of this report were presented in advance to Haitian authorities, who have not yet commented on this matter, and has reproached both the Government and the international community for their lack of action. They are stealing childhood.  Hollow expressions of concern are not enough, Amnesty International's Secretary General has protested. SEXUAL VIOLENCE Amnesty International has documented a dozen cases of girls who have suffered sexual violence at the hands of members of these criminal gangs in recent times, who have made rape a common practice during attacks on neighborhoods and territories controlled by rival gangs. In turn, many of these young women have been raped on their way to school, collectively, or in their own homes, have become pregnant or have been victims of sexual exploitation. I think about it and I say to myself I am a girl, why did this happen to me, a girl who spoke with Amnesty International asks. Amnesty International has explained that the situation of these young people is further exacerbated by the precariousness of the health and security systems, and there is no police presence. One of the victims, who has been raped multiple times, has recounted that the restrictive laws also pose a problem, as abortion is still penalized in Haitian legislation.FORCED RECRUITMENT On the other hand, the young people who have been forced to join these criminal organizations agree with the NGO that it is impossible to refuse without putting their lives at risk. "If I hadn't done it, they would have killed me," a 12-year-old boy, who was recruited as an informant, recounts. Not only children are victims of this forced recruitment, mainly to work as spies, distributors, or to perform small tasks for gang members, but also girls, who are usually employed in domestic tasks. This has led to dozens of these minors being killed by gangs that considered them full-fledged members of rival groups. Added to this are minors who die or are injured in attacks by gangs on rival territories. Children and girls are exposed to indiscriminate and direct fire, as explained by the NGO, which warns of the mental health problems that arise from this extreme situation. Calamard has called on the international community to demand a joint action plan to effectively curb the serious problems that Haiti has been facing for years, even though the crisis is much deeper and dates back decades. In this sense, she has urged that the action plan include an integrated plan to protect childhood, including programs for demobilization and social integration, comprehensive medical and legal assistance. Additionally, the Government must speed up judicial processes to bring perpetrators to justice. Amnesty has also called for controlling the massive influx of arms into Haiti, as well as halting the deportation of Haitians while the campaign of terror by criminal gangs and the broader human rights crisis continues. Author: Judicial CommunicationThe Supreme Court has confirmed the one-year prison sentence for the sex crime imposed in the appeal court against the sentence of the Penal Court by the Madrid Provincial Court against a patient who sexually assaulted a nurse who was providing him with assistance. The Supreme Court was composed of Magistrates Andrés Martínez Arrieta (President), Vicente Magro (acting as rapporteur), Susana Polo, Leopoldo Puente, and Ángel Luis Hurtado. The proven facts highlight that the defendant, while admitted as a patient in the Madrid hospital room and being attended by the nurse of said hospital, with the intention of satisfying his sexual desires, carried out touchings on the left side of the buttocks. In addition to the deprivation of liberty penalty, the security measure of supervised liberty with the obligation to attend sexual education programs for a period of one year and prohibition of approaching and communicating with the victim for a period of two years has been imposed. The Supreme Court emphasizes that the defendant has carried out acts of sexual touching of a nurse in a hospital center, which constitutes the commission of a crime of old sexual abuse and currently of sexual aggression of article 178.1 of the penal code. And as additional points to consider for sentencing, the following are taken into account for the crime committed against a nurse who assaulted her sexual freedom while she was exercising her profession:1. The declared facts constitute, at the time of the events and currently, a sex crime against a woman's sexual freedom.2. An act of touching of sexual content and parts of the victim was carried out, violating the woman's right to be respected and preventing anyone from performing any act of touching if it is not with her consent.3. The woman has the perfect right that she is not objectified through acts of sexual touching if she does not consent to it.4. If the woman has not given her consent to the sexual act explicitly or tacitly, there is a sexual aggression.5. It is not the man who performs the touching on the woman who decides how and when to carry out acts of sexual content. . The bilateral nature is required in a pact to perform touching in parts of sexual content and the area that consists of the proven facts is. 6. The woman's consent to the sexual act is not the author's subjective interpretation. It is not valid to believe that there is consent, but rather it must be ensured that the woman consents, and that this is derived from the circumstances of the case, which is what the art. 178 CP cites. 7. The woman's consent to the sexual act is not presumed by the author, but is explicit or tacit. The belief in consent does not validate the performance of sexual acts. 8. The woman's will to the sexual act must be clearly manifested. The art. 178.1 CP requires that the consent has been expressed freely through acts that, in consideration of the circumstances of the case, express the person's will in a clear manner. 9 The subjective interpretation of consent without its clear existence by the woman fills the typicality of art. 178.1 CP current and 181.1 at the time of the facts. 10. There cannot be talk of unilateralism from one part, but bilateralism from both. The proven facts demonstrate a clear sexual act, in which a person admitted to a hospital takes advantage of the medical treatment given by a nurse and takes advantage of the nurse's approach to help them when they carry out an act that constitutes a clear attack on a nurse's sexual self-determination, who does not have the obligation to endure a patient taking advantage of their medical attention to sexually assault them, which is what the defendant did when they carried out the acts proven in the facts, with the intention of satisfying their sexual desires, by making contact with the left side of the nurse's buttocks. No woman bears the burden or servitude of tolerating a man's desire to perform acts of sexual touching, no matter how minor, on the victim's sexual parts. And this, far from being a mere coercion or mild harassment, as it has been understood in other times, constitutes a genuine act of sexual aggression against the woman. And even more so in this case, in which it represents an attack on a healthcare professional who, as she approaches to carry out her medical assistance to a patient in a hospital center, takes advantage of the recurring proximity to perform acts of a sexual nature, which not only constitutes a physical excess, but also a penal offense typified in the Penal Code as sexual aggression in the present and at the time as sexual abuse. In this regard, women, and in this case, healthcare professionals, are not required to tolerate any type of excess by patients admitted to a hospital, and when they integrate an attack on parts of sexual content of the victims, it constitutes a sex crime. On the other hand, in response to the request for a reduction in the imposed penalty, the Supreme Court dismissed it and reminded that the Court understood that there was already a relevant gravity in the causation of the facts in attention to the sexual attack on the nurse, who, in her medical care to the patient, was surprised by a sexual attack, as stated in the proven facts, which cannot be considered in any way a less serious fact, and that it entails the application of the penalty imposed by the court at the time. On the other hand, the Supreme Court recalls that in cases of sexual crimes, the penal mediation path, as indicated by the recently approved Organic Law 1/2022 of January 2, is not applicable, just like it is not in cases of gender violence, but points out that in the rest of the cases, this path of restorative justice or penal mediation is very effective in accelerating the resolution of cases and the satisfaction of the victim, recalling that there are penal types that include attenuated subtypes, such as in this case, or alternative penalties to imprisonment, in which the Organic Law 1/2022 of January has included the restorative justice path in the Additional Disposition 9th of the LECRIM, by which, in 9 points, it develops the general principles of restorative justice, in virtue of which the regulatory framework of the application of penal mediation is established to be developed by the protocols implemented by the mediation service of the CGPJ, in a decided bet on this path with origin in the Anglo-Saxon law, in order to put in motion the intrajudicial mediation derived by the judge, or at the request of the parties. And all of this, in order to achieve a better position for the victim in the penal process, who feels more comforted with situations such as the accused's request for pardon, the accused's remorse, commitment to not repeating their reprehensible social and penal behavior, the consignment for payment of civil liability, and the acceptance and express recognition of the penal illegality committed by the same (Article 15 of the Law 4/2021 of the Statute of the Victim of the Crime). All of this leads to a mediation agreement with the intervention of expert penal mediators trained in mediation by mediation institutes and the coordination of the General Council of the Judiciary in its implementation. And from this, the penal agreement is reached where the defense and the most severe of the accusations agree on a reduction of the penalty, in this case, if mitigating circumstances of penal responsibility are appreciated, and the application of attenuated subtypes, such as in this case, or alternative penalties to imprisonment collected in the penal type that is the object of the accusation, even though this does not form part of the mediation or restorative justice agreement, but of the penal agreement between the accusations and the defense, which contributes to the acceleration of penal justice and greater attention to the victim, who is more comforted with the application of restorative justice in the penal process.

data.text: Ex-partner accuses Deputy Jorge Durán of abuse amidst crossed versions. DENUNCIATION. Parliamentarian assured it was a consensual relationship. Yesterday morning, it was made known that Deputy Jorge Durán's ex-partner filed a complaint against him for the alleged crime of sexual abuse. The parliamentarian defended himself and assured that he had previously denounced the woman. On the other hand, his party announced that it would take the case to the Supreme Court of the collective. The Public Ministry initiated an investigation following a complaint made yesterday by the woman, who accused the parliamentarian of a presumed sexual abuse that occurred on February 8. As a result, the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI arrived at the deputy's residence to conduct some procedures while the accuser was taken to the Medical Legal Service to undergo medical examinations. Hours later, Durán issued a statement in which he stated that on Friday he had a meeting at his house in Colina, where he claimed to have had a consensual intimate encounter with her in the early hours of Saturday. The parliamentarian said that after the end of our relationship, and considering that my ex-partner was unemployed and had nowhere to live, I offered her accommodation in a dependency within my property, where we would have had relationships. Afterward, he claimed that in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch (...) Subsequently, after clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began to demand a sum of money, alleging that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the most harmed. In the face of this extortion situation and after discovering that she had used my credit cards, I filed a complaint for extortion and theft with the Carabineros on Monday evening. To my surprise, after I filed my complaint, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, he claimed. On the other hand, the woman said I was only asking him to pay pending tickets because I managed his social media (...) I did not file a complaint before because I was afraid, because he had me threatened and before this happened. He always told me that I was the girlfriend of a deputy and that I had to behave like that (...) I was locked up in the cabin over the weekend. Upon learning of the investigation, the leadership of Renovación Nacional sent the background to the Supreme Court of the party to initiate an investigation. Courts Judge a Geriatric Aid for Sexual Abuse of an 81-Year-Old Resident Prosecutor Seeks Three Years in Prison for the Accused Trial at the Provincial Court of Toledo against a Geriatric Aid Accused of Sexual Abuse of a Particularly Vulnerable Victim, 81 Years Old. The prosecutor is seeking three years in prison. In addition, he requests a six-year and eight-year disqualification from any profession involving regular and direct contact with the elderly or people with disabilities, as well as compensation of €6,000 for moral damages to the victim. The facts being judged date back to October 7, 2021, when the accused was working as a geriatric aid for 18 years. Between the hours of midnight and 3:30 am, the defendant was delivering medication to residents on the ground floor of the center and entered the victim's room, who had been diagnosed with moderate cognitive decline in the context of a delirious senile dementia due to Alzheimer's disease. Once inside the room, according to the prosecutor, he took advantage of the victim's companion being asleep and undressed the resident, taking her to the private bathroom of the room, where he committed the sexual abuse. At that moment, the other auxiliary who was working that night at the residence entered the room and surprised the accused in this situation, prompting him to run out and beg her not to say anything about what had happened, that it would never happen again, and that he would ruin her life, although the auxiliary reported the incident to the center's director.

The charges against Real Madrid's Raúl Asencio for child pornography are maintained. With the decision of the Las Palmas Court to maintain Asencio's charges, the case remains open and could lead to a judicial process with severe consequences for those involved. Gabriel Izcovich Wednesday, February 12, 2025, 11:46 am. Justice has decided to keep the investigation open against Raúl Asencio, defender of Real Madrid, who is charged with a child pornography crime. The Las Palmas Court has dismissed the appeal presented by Asencio's defense and has rejected the provisional dismissal of the case, meaning the judicial procedure will continue. The case dates back to 2023 and took place in Mogán, on the island of Gran Canaria. According to the investigation, two Real Madrid reserve team players were filmed while engaging in sexual relations with two girls. One of the key aspects of the case is that one of them was under 16 years old, which makes the recording and its dissemination a penal offense. In addition, a third player was present during the scene. Although Raúl Asencio was not at the scene of the crime, the judicial investigation points to the fact that the defender would have received and retransmitted the video in question, linking him to the case. For this reason, he is charged with the offense of disseminating sexual content with a minor. Ferran Ruiz, a player of Girona's reserve team, who has had minutes with the first team, is also implicated in the case. Although no further details have been revealed about his participation, his name has been linked to the ongoing investigation. With the decision of the Las Palmas Court to maintain Asencio's indictment, the case remains open and could lead to a judicial process with severe consequences for those involved. Meanwhile, the Real Madrid player will continue to be subject to the action of the justice system while all the details of this delicate matter are clarified.

data.text: Surprise raid by ICE at a Kansas restaurant sought a man and detained 12 workers A ICE operation in Kansas City ended with the detention of 12 employees of a restaurant, raising questions about the legality of the procedure. Lawyers and activists are demanding clarity on the use of fingerprints and the lack of a judicial order. The presence of federal agents from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Service in a commercial establishment usually generates alarm, especially when detentions affect workers who are unaware of the reasons for the intervention. In a recent operation carried out in Kansas City, authorities detained several employees, sparking questions about the legality of the action. The incident occurred at a local restaurant and left families and civil rights organizations on alert. While some question the procedure, others demand greater clarity on the actions of ICE and the lack of communication with local agencies. YOU CAN SEE A father of four was murdered in New York following a confrontation over a parking space Why ICE intervened at a Kansas City restaurant According to official reports, the National Security Investigations agency (HSI) entered the El Potro restaurant in Kansas City to locate a person wanted for sex crimes against minors. However, during the operation, they decided to check the identities of several employees, resulting in the detention of 12 workers. Clay County Sheriff Will Akin stated that his office was not previously informed about the operation. I have no way of accessing or, you know, enforcing immigration laws, Akin expressed, highlighting the lack of coordination between local and federal agencies. One of the most contentious points of the case is the absence of a court order from ICE for entry into the establishment and detaining immigrants. Photo Telemundo GOOD NEWS for immigrants in the USA receives your American citizenship if you meet these requirements in the US. ICE had a search warrant One of the most contentious points of the case is the absence of a judicial order for entry into the establishment. According to the organization Advocates for Immigrant Rights and Reconciliation (AIRR), ICE agents did not show documentation to justify the raid. Attorney Michael SharmaCrawford stated that the suspected sex abuser who motivated the operation was not found, but that the agents detained the workers after verifying their fingerprints. Additionally, he mentioned that the officers claimed to have received consent from a property owner, although it is unknown if this person had the legal authority to grant it. What rights do employees have during ICE operations? Detentions have raised concern among immigrants and labor rights organizations. The Kansas Missouri Dream Alliance recommended to business owners and employees that they inform themselves about their rights in the face of migrant operations. SharmaCrawford explained that ICE can enter any business that is open to the public, but employees have the right to ask them to leave if they do not present a court order signed by a judge. She also emphasized the importance of knowing the legal procedures to avoid arbitrary detentions. The community is closely following the development of this case, while lawyers and activists are pressing for clarification on whether the federal agency acted in accordance with the law or if there were violations of the rights of the detained workers.

The trial of Néstor Pinta began at the Criminal Court N 3 in Bahía Blanca. The well-known footballer is accused of covering up the sexual abuses committed by his father, Aldo Pinta, between 2015 and 2016 against at least two young people. You may be interested in the Pinta Case It has reached the trial stage, which is very important for the victims The accusation is driven by one of the victims, Victoria Carrión, along with her lawyer, María Fernanda Petersen. The particularity and novelty is that the judicial process, initiated this Monday 10, was carried out without the accusation of a prosecutor. It is the first time that in Bahía Blanca a trial of this type has developed without the intervention of the Public Ministry. Initially, it is an atypical process, generally accompanied. It was difficult for the victims, especially the way they found out about the decision from the Prosecution Office. One of the victims found out from us The lack of proximity and the possibility of communicating properly with the victims was very difficult for them, Petersen commented on the novelty of the case. It is a decision we made and we are here with the evidence that we consider will give us the possibility of accrediting what we are trying to accrediting, that's why we continue with each of the mobilizations we were organizing, added the lawyer. The trial will develop until Wednesday, 12. It is expected that key witnesses will testify, including other young people who attended the kayaking school at the time. We believe there are a million proofs and that's why we have attended each of the appeals and the pleas we have made. It is not a whim of the victims to want to reach trial, emphasized the lawyer. The case In 2020, Victoria Carrión filed a complaint against Aldo, the coach's father. Shortly after, the person pointed out as the perpetrator of the abuse, took his own life. In response to this, the criminal indictment against him lapsed. However, the investigation continued against Néstor as an indispensable accomplice. In 2021, the Bahía Blanca Prosecutor's Office charged him, but later requested his dismissal. However, the plaintiff appealed and the Penal Chamber, with a divided vote, ruled in his favor. Pinta's defense took the case to the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation, which still has to rule.

The Constitutional Court of Colombia has prohibited child marriage in the country, declaring this practice unconstitutional. In a recent ruling, the Court noted that early marital unions constitute a grave violation of the rights of children, exposing them to irreparable risks. In this way, the Tribunal declared that Articles 117 and 124 of the Civil Code are unenforceable, while establishing that the minimum age for marriage must be 18 years. The ruling, backed by Magistrate Cristina Pardo Schlesinger, highlights that child marriage goes against constitutional principles and the constitutional block. In the statement issued by the Court, it is emphasized that early unions are based on gender stereotypes and cultural paradigms that must be eradicated. Although the practice was prohibited, the Court instructed the Congress of the Republic to develop public policies to prevent and eradicate child marriage, promoting education and pedagogical alternatives that enable girls and adolescents to make informed and autonomous decisions. Furthermore, it was emphasized that it is necessary to strengthen the rights and participation of minors in various areas of society, such as the economy and sports. As part of the implementation of the ruling, the Court ordered the Ombudsman's Office to identify areas with the highest incidence of child marriages and launch pedagogical campaigns to inform the population, especially in rural and ethnic communities. This measure must also involve the educational community, including students, teachers, and parents. It is worth noting that before this sentence, Colombian legislation allowed marriage from the age of 14, which is now excluded following the judicial decision. Furthermore, the Attorney General's Office had previously requested a declaration of unconstitutionality of child marriage, appealing to international treaties on women's rights and the elimination of discrimination.

The government has officially banned transferring prisoners who change gender. The decision took effect through Decree 61, published in the Official Gazette. The measure was previously announced by Javier Milei in November and reaffirmed this Wednesday by the presidential spokesperson, Manuel Adorni. The Government officially approved this Thursday the measure that establishes that the accommodation of detained persons will be determined according to the sex registered at the time of the crime for which their arrest was ordered, without the possibility of transfer in case of subsequent gender changes. The provision was published in the Official Gazette through Decree 61 of the Executive Power, signed by President Javier Milei. The place of accommodation, reassignment, or transfer of the person deprived of liberty will be assigned by the penitentiary administration within its own jurisdiction, according to the sex registered by the person, in accordance with Law No. 743, at the time of the fact for which their detention was ordered, article 1 of the decree establishes. In the following article, it is specified that the competent authority for the direction of penal institutions will deny any request for reassignment or transfer within the same jurisdiction to the person who, after the fact for which their detention was ordered, initiates the rectification registry procedure of sex, first name, and image provided for in Law N 26.743, when they invoke the aforementioned rectification for the approval of their request. The decree establishes that penal institutions must take the necessary measures to ensure the safety of individuals who are in the process of or have already completed a rectification registry procedure of sex, in the terms of Law N 26.743. .743 and in no case measures can be taken that may represent a risk to the safety, physical, psychological, or moral integrity, or the life of other inmates in the penal establishment. In line with the above, it was established that it will not be possible to house a person in a women's penal establishment, who has processed the rectification of their sex registry, when the deprivation of liberty is imposed for the commission of a crime foreseen in Titles I, III, or V of Book Two of the PENAL CODE, or for any other crime that was committed with violence against a woman. In the same way, these people will also not be relocated if the technical evaluation carried out by the penitentiary administrative authority determines that their accommodation in a penitentiary establishment would pose a risk to the safety, physical, psychological, or moral integrity, or the life of the other inmates in the penitentiary establishment. The ban had been anticipated by Milei. President Javier Milei had previously announced this measure in November last year, during a ceremony to hand over sabers and dispatches to the Armed Forces at the Casa Rosada. On that occasion, he criticized the guarantee policies implemented during the Kirchnerism and anticipated that he would prohibit the possibility of detainees requesting a change of gender while serving their sentence. The criminals will not be able to request a change in sentence under the umbrella of gender identity, and we will be pushing an initiative so that the provincial prison systems can adhere, he expressed in his speech at the Salon Blanco of the Casa Rosada. During the same event, the governor mentioned the case of Guille Cantero, leader of the narco gang Los Monos, who declared himself bisexual and polyamorous to expand the list of close contacts. Only in a country whose values have been profoundly turned upside down can such barbarity be allowed. This stupidity is over. We are going to prohibit it, he stated. On the other hand, this Wednesday the presidential spokesperson, Manuel Adorni, in addition to announcing that treatments for gender change will be prohibited for minors under 18, referred to the new regulation on transfers in prisons. The current system allows convicted people to commit crimes against victims who are also women, he sustained. The case that occurred in Córdoba mentioned in the decree In the considerations of the decree, the Government referred to a recent case that occurred in Córdoba Province in which a person, convicted of a crime involving violence against a woman, underwent the rectification of their sex registry and, as a result, was relocated, which led to the commission of various abuses against the inmates housed in the establishment. The official text states that it is unreasonable that the recognition of a right, within the framework of the execution of a prison sentence, can be used to put the lives, safety, and sexual integrity of women who are serving their sentences in penitentiary establishments at risk. On Wednesday, the Second Turn Sexual Integrity Crimes Prosecution Office in Córdoba re-filed charges against the same person after two new complaints of sexual abuse against other inmates. The accused, Gabriel Fernández, entered Bouwer prison in Córdoba in 2016 as a man. Two years later, he underwent the procedure to change his sex, changed his name to Gabriela, and was transferred to a different wing. He subsequently sexually abused and impregnated a detainee.

A man was arrested on Tuesday while attending La Bombonera to watch the match between Boca Juniors and Independiente Rivadavia, but was detained due to an outstanding arrest order for aggravated outrageous sexual abuse. The subject was captured by agents of the City Police within the framework of the security operation being carried out for the encounter between Boca and La Lepra in the fifth round of the Professional Football League, through the Tribuna Segura program. The man was being sought by order of the Penal Guarantees Court No. 6 of the Judicial Department of San Martín and was identified by City Police officers and detained immediately. In the meantime, the Secretary of Public Affairs of the City, Waldo Wolff, confirmed in a post on the social network X the situation of the detainee and added It's with families in the stadiums, without delinquents. It's with order.

More than 13 years in prison for a music teacher who abused his underage student in Ourense The TSXG confirms the sentence against the accused, who contacted the victim through social media and committed the crimes in the school and other places The Civil and Penal Chamber of the Superior Justice Court of Galicia (TSXG) has confirmed the sentence imposed on a music teacher for continued sexual abuse and rape of a minor who was his student at a school in Ourense. The sentence ratifies the resolution issued on the day by the Provincial Court of Ourense, which sentenced the teacher to a total of 13 years and 6 months in prison, as well as various measures of isolation and supervised liberty. According to the proven facts recorded in the sentence, the accused established contact with the minor through social media when she was only 11 years old, hiding his identity Later, when the victim was 12 years old, the accused began to ask her for sexual images and videos. From the age of 14, the abuses materialized into in-person encounters at the school and other locations, where the convicted perpetrator exercised physical violence and coercion over the victim. The sentence details that the accused, taking advantage of his position as a teacher and the emotional vulnerability of the minor, manipulated her to establish an emotional dependence relationship, thereby facilitating the encounters and the abuses. The minor reported the incidents in September 2021, after suffering the last assault months earlier. Appeal rejected The TSXG has rejected the accused's appeal, which claimed error in the evaluation of the evidence and violation of the right to the presumption of innocence. The tribunal, however, considers the victim's statement to be coherent, persistent, and supported by forensic and testimonial evidence. Additionally, the resolution highlights that the testimonial evidence and psychological reports reinforce the credibility of the minor and demonstrate the defendant's guilt. The imposed sentence includes, in addition to imprisonment, absolute incapacitation for the duration of the sentence, a 16-year ban on communicating or approaching the victim, and a 30,000-euro obligation to compensate her. Furthermore, the defendant is also incapacitated from working with minors for 17 years and is subject to a subsequent period of supervised liberty after serving the prison sentence. The sentence is not final and an appeal for cassation can be lodged before the Second Chamber of the Supreme Court.

The First Penal Court of Ceuta has sentenced a resident of Miramar Bajo for corruption of minors. The defendant V.M.C.C. was arrested in May 2023 as part of a National Police operation following an investigation conducted by the Technological Crimes Unit of the UDEF. Upon entry and registration, a large amount of child pornography was found that he shared with users, using the eMule and uTorrent programs. It was police-tracked that he had downloaded up to 48 files, sharing their entirety and all of them being of a pedophilic nature. The intervention of agents from this unit brought an end to an investigation that was crucial, as it was tracked that months prior, specifically in January, he had practiced those downloads. The judicial resolution is firm and based on the same, the confessed author of this crime accepts a sentence of 2 years in prison, disqualification for the exercise of a profession in which they have contact with minors for 7 years, in addition to the imposition of a measure of supervised liberty for another 5 years. Condemnation and another trial for the same reason pending. The sentence is suspended for a period of 2 years, but always conditioned to the fact that they do not commit a crime and that they complete a sex education course. When they committed these acts, they were a primary offender, that is, they did not have a prior record, and therefore the suspension was applied. It happens that the same convicted person is now in pre-trial detention awaiting another trial, since they were detained again in November 2024 for child pornography while they were out on bail. Now they already have a prior record because there is this firm resolution, which will weigh when the oral hearing takes place for those other facts. Use of the NetworksThe commission of this child corruption crime was carried out through the use of internet file-sharing networks. The Police tracks these networks to identify pedophiles using police tracking software. This is how they can locate users who share these contents. In the case of the suspects, investigators were able to locate the IP address used by the already convicted person for these downloads. With prior judicial authorization, they were able to access the suspect's home, where they found multiple child pornography contents.

The right-wing government of Argentina prohibits gender-affirming care for minors under 18. Argentine President Javier Milei has announced a ban on medical care for trans individuals under the age of 18. The right-wing populist president implemented a decree on Thursday, February 6, following similar moves in the United Kingdom, Sweden, and Finland. Forced or psychologically coercive imposition of extreme gender ideology on children constitutes clear child abuse, a spokesperson for the president's office stated. There is no evidence that minors are being forced to begin gender-affirming medical care in Argentina. The decree also requires trans inmates to be housed in prisons according to their birth sex. Milei's action marks a significant rollback of queer rights in a country once considered among the best in the world for equality. In 2012, Argentina became the first country to enact an auto-identification law as part of several pro-LGBTQ policies. A spokesperson for the non-profit organization ILGA World condemned the new policy, stating that it promotes stigmatization and criminalization of diversity. Argentina was a beacon in the region by recognizing the right to gender identity without pathologization or judicialization. This setback, imposed by decree without parliamentary debate or participation from affected sectors, constitutes an abuse of executive power and an attack on democratic institutions, the spokesperson added. They called on the country's supreme court to annul the decree. The advertisement comes just days after thousands of people took to the streets in the capital, Buenos Aires, in support of LGBTQ rights, following Milei's comments, in which he has branded progressive policies, including trans rights, feminism, and climate activism as a cancer that must be excised.

data.text: Community Fights to Prevent Teacher's Deportation MILWAUKEE (TELEMUNDO WI) The community has come together in an urgent call to prevent the deportation of teacher Yessenia Ruano, who could be expelled from the country this Friday, February 14, if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) does not grant her more time to complete her immigration process. Local leaders, elected officials, clergy members, and Voices of the Border activists gathered this afternoon to express their support and request an extension from ICE in Ruano's case, who has dedicated her life to education and service to her community. We know that many people at risk of deportation are not criminals. They are hardworking people, parents, and individuals making positive contributions to their community, said Christine Neumann-Ortiz, representative of Voices of the Border. For Yessenia Ruano, returning to El Salvador represents a mortal risk My brother was murdered in 2017, and some friends were murdered, and I witnessed many things. It's not a safe environment, she said with concern. Mother of two young daughters, both U.S. citizens, Ruano has applied for a T visa, a migratory benefit designed for victims of human trafficking. Despite having the process ongoing and her strong ties to the community, she recently received the news that she could be deported. I applied for the T visa in May and at that time they didn't give me a deadline, but in December things changed. They told my lawyer that I have to be deported, although I don't have a criminal record and I've attended all my appointments, Ruano explained. Activists and community leaders insist that this is a crucial moment for solidarity. At this moment, the community needs to be around Yessenia and other families in similar situations, concluded NeumannOrtiz As time passes, the future of teacher Ruano hangs in the balance. Her case is not just a reflection of the tough immigration policies, but also of the struggle of many families seeking security and stability in the United States.

data.text: In an operation in Arequipa, the PNP and Customs seized tons of minerals, chemical inputs, and more than 3 million illicit cigarettes that were allegedly destined for Lima and the northern part of the country. The seized cigarettes represent a loss of over 1 million soles in selective consumption tax. In an operation against illegal mining in Chala, Arequipa, the National Police and Customs intervened 11 concentrator plants where minerals are processed, as well as dozens of trucks and trailers carrying other products in an irregular manner. As a result of the actions, in addition to the seizures of minerals and chemical inputs, over 3 million contraband cigarettes were seized that entered the country illegally through the border with Bolivia and are valued at least 4.5 million soles, resulting in a loss of over 1 million soles in selective consumption tax. The discovery of over 3 million illicit cigarettes in an operation against illegal mining confirms what we have been warning: the illicit trade of goods is not an isolated fact, but rather part of a much larger criminal scheme. These organizations use the same routes, logistics, and even the same means of transportation as illegal mining, arms trafficking, explosives, and even human trafficking, explained Rubén Vargas, expert in organized crime. Additionally, the former Minister of the Interior, commented that blows like this demonstrate that a comprehensive approach is key to combating organized crime. Continuing to attack these networks in a coordinated manner will not only stop illicit trade, but also weaken the criminal structures that generate violence and insecurity in the country, he said. Products had Lima as their destination. Initial investigations indicate that the over 3 million Paraguayan origin cigarettes of the Golden Beach, Hamilton, Euro, and Campeao brands had Lima and northern country markets as their destination. It is worth highlighting that all the products, in addition to not paying the corresponding taxes, did not have any of the health warnings established by law. The intervention took place with the presence of Assistant Prosecutor Jesús Vilca Romero, and it was reported that the truck driver, identified as Wilfredo Atamari Ccopacondori (44), was detained as a suspect in the customs crime of smuggling and could face an effective prison sentence of between 4 and 8 years, while the illegal merchandise was transferred to the warehouses of Customs in the city of Mollendo, Islay province, for subsequent destruction. It is worth noting that in the past few weeks, authorities have delivered significant blows against organized crime, seizing more than 3 million contraband cigarettes in operations carried out in Lima, Pucallpa, and Puno, this amount, added to the more than 3 million cigarettes seized in Arequipa, totals more than 6 million contraband cigarettes seized. The interventions took place in large warehouses that supplied markets in Lima and northern Peru.

Seoul, 12 Feb (EFE). The South Korean Prosecutor's Office charged Kim Nokwan, 33, with a sex trafficking and abuse crime on 234 people, including minors, on Wednesday, for leading a network that committed all types of sexual crimes and recorded and distributed them via Telegram. The defendant, Kim Nokwan, has been in preventive detention for some time for allegedly leading a network known as "The Vigilantes" that, for almost five years, blackmailed hundreds of victims and committed sexual abuse and rapes against them to produce videos that were later sold online through the mentioned messaging platform, according to the Seoul Central District Prosecutor's Office. The number of victims, including children and adolescents, is higher compared to two similar cases that surfaced in 2020, in which a total of over 170 people, including dozens of minors, were exploited. The individuals responsible for these two networks, Moon Hyungwook and Cho Joobin, were sentenced to 34 and 45 years in prison, respectively. The instant messaging system Telegram has been under scrutiny by South Korean authorities in recent years for hosting content from networks of this type as well as groups that produced and distributed ultra-false pornographic content (deepfakes) on the platform. Last September, Telegram, which has its servers abroad, began cooperating with South Korea's telecommunications regulator to remove this type of content and collaborate on investigations. EFE

Dr. Rosario Sasieta, former Minister of Women and Vulnerable Populations, reported Trujillo prosecutor, Shano Efraín Cuizano Valencia, for allegedly shelving the case of Luis Alberto Aguirre Bazán, a University of Trujillo professor, who is being investigated for the alleged crime of sexual assault of a postgraduate student from that higher education institution. It is essential to note that this professor has been reported to the Trujillo Prosecutor's Office for the alleged crimes of sexual harassment, sexual extortion, and rape of a postgraduate student. It is painful to point out that, despite having all the evidence, on January 30, prosecutor Shano Efraín Cuizano scandalously shelved this complaint without considering the multiple indications that demonstrated the professor's guilt, assured Dr. Rosario Sasieta. Additionally, he stated that a prosecutor who is supposed to protect the victim and prosecute the perpetrator should not be the one to declare the case closed and allow the aggressor to go unpunished. NO ONE IS WATCHING On the other hand, attorney Alexis Ochoa, who accompanied Sasieta, stated that the crime of sexual abuse usually does not have witnesses and the investigation should be conducted following certain patterns that the Judicial Power has established. If any prosecutor does not follow these patterns, the case will obviously be archived because we have to take into account that these are crimes without witnesses or cameras that record the incident, therefore they are special crimes and the investigation should also be special, Ochoa asserted. The attorney indicated that in this type of infringement, the victim's statement is relevant, therefore, prosecutors must assess whether the victim is being consistent or fanciful, if they contradict or not. The Dr. Rosario Sasieta stated that in the psychological examination applied to the victim, it is demonstrated that she has post-traumatic stress disorder. The prosecutor, by not conducting a thorough investigation, has cut short the victim's life project, who is in a state of shock and is not working or doing anything because she is still affected. This has to be paid for; we cannot allow there to be sexual predators in this region, emphasized the doctor in law. Subsequently, she indicated that this case will be brought to the attention of the Minister of Education and the National Superintendent of Higher University Education (Sunedu) because, in her opinion, the teacher should be investigated. She added that the alleged aggressor was summoned to testify, but did not appear and the prosecutor did not request that he be apprehended with a degree of force. . FINALLY, Sasieta demanded that the Unified Registry of Victims and Aggressors (RUVA) be made public so that everyone knows the violent individuals and those who have a habit of mistreating their peers. This registry is not public and nobody knows which person has a habit of harming others, so I demand that the RUVA be made public knowledge, concluded the lawyer.

data.text: The Justice sentenced Fernando Sosa to 15 years in prison, accused of sexual abuse and kidnapping, and three other cases of completed and attempted kidnapping, committed in Rosario and Arroyo Seco between 2020 and 2022. For the Prosecution, the four attacks on vulnerable women had the same intention of sexually subjugating them. Before the verdict, in the closing argument, prosecutor Luciana Vallerella pointed out that it was proven that the accused is a serial abuser, who even had cases in the previous penal process system for similar acts that did not reach trial. She also stated that there was premeditation and planning of the facts. The first case tried involved a 14-year-old victim, committed on September 28, 2020, at night, when the accused followed her on his motorcycle while she was walking towards the South Park in Rosario. She offered to take her and in the Las Palmeras area at 1400, where she attempted to flee, she restrained her and committed the abuse. After that, he fled. He was also charged with the incident of February 5, 2022, at dawn, in Moreno between Irigoyen and Mitre of Arroyo Seco, when Sosa, 55 years old, approached a 21-year-old victim under threats, and made her get into a gray Volkswagen Gol. According to the Prosecution, the accused intercepted her with the intention of attacking her sexual integrity. When he realized the young woman had a cell phone, he took it, threw it in the back seat, and threatened her again. After that, he turned the car around, the victim removed the safety catch, and struggling with the accused, she jumped out of the car and managed to call for help. That phone had real-time location tracking activated, which allowed for a trace to be made. Before being detained, on February 10, 2022, at dawn, he approached a 19-year-old girl in Rivadavia between Colón and Gaboto of Arroyo Seco, when she was walking. She approached running, grabbed her with her arm around her neck and held her tightly while with the other hand she tried to cover her mouth with the intention of committing a crime against her sexual integrity. The victim managed to break free and escape, the accuser says. Finally, on February 12, 2022, at dawn, in Libertad and Don Orione of Arroyo Seco, he intercepted a 45-year-old victim who was walking through a plaza. He approached the woman, extracted a white knife, and intimidated her with the intention of committing a crime against her sexual integrity, causing the victim to start screaming, and he ran away from the scene. The court that sentenced the defendant is composed of Ismael Manfrín, Gonzalo Fernández Bussy, and Gonzalo López Quintana. The prosecution requested 22 years in prison and in the initial pleading requested that the traumatic nature of the situation that the victims lived be taken into account. Now, the grounds of the ruling are expected to be known in order to analyze whether an appeal will be filed or not, as the sentence is for a lower penalty than the one requested. The prosecution pointed to a modus operandi, as the accused chose victims who were in a situation of vulnerability due to various reasons, such as walking alone in the street, being young, and being unknown to the accused. Additionally, the location where he approached them was similar in the southern zone or Arroyo Seco, which is located south of Rosario. The crimes were committed at a similar time, during the night or early morning, with the aim of ensuring their success and impunity. Furthermore, in relation to the nine cases in the conclusive system, another common point is that Sosa used threats to control and retain the victims, even with a knife and locks in some cases. He also used physical force. In addition to the fact that all victims described their attacker with similar characteristics, which coincide with those of the accused, the prosecution believes that the defendant's motivation was clearly sexual submission. It was even indicated in the debate that the victims offered the accused money, their belongings, and that in no case did he take any valuable object. For the prosecutor, there is consistency in Sosa's criminal behavior, a pattern that repeats itself, which in some cases is interrupted before by the resistance of his victim, but all belong to the same series.

data.text: Hundreds of people have been displaced by violence generated by criminal gangs. In the photo, a woman stands outside her home in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on September 21, 2024 (Amnesty International). Numerous criminal gangs are responsible for human rights abuses against children in Haiti. Extreme violence and intimidation prevail in Port-au-Prince and surrounding areas. Too many children in Haiti are seeing their lives destroyed. Agnès Callamard The relentless violence of criminal gangs in Port-au-Prince and its surroundings has resulted in a brutal attack on childhood in Haiti, as stated by Amnesty International in a new report. I am a child, why did this happen to me? Documenting the aggressions of criminal gangs against children in Haiti, it reveals how children are subjected to numerous human rights abuses, including recruitment into criminal gangs, rape, and other forms of sexual violence, kidnappings, homicides, and injuries. It also documents the disproportionate impact on children with disabilities. Since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021, the violence of armed criminal gangs has significantly increased in Haiti, with an estimated 5,600 lives lost in the past year. Criminal gangs control most of the capital, Port-au-Prince, while over 5.5 million people urgently require humanitarian assistance. Criminal gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti. They threaten, beat, rape, and kill children and girls. Multiple abuses of children's rights, including the right to life, education, and freedom of movement, have been committed, said Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International. Too many children in Haiti are having their lives destroyed, and they have nowhere to turn for protection or justice. They are being persecuted and, in some cases, killed by self-defense groups, while authorities arbitrarily detain them. They are being robbed of their childhood. It is time for Haitian authorities and the international community, including donors, to redouble their efforts. Empty expressions of concern are not enough. Children suffer daily violations of their bodies, minds, and hearts. Haiti urgently needs assistance to protect children and prevent new cycles of violence. According to estimates, more than one million children live in areas controlled by criminal gangs or under their influence. The research team interviewed 112 people and visited Port-au-Prince in September 2024. Among those interviewed were children and adolescents, government officials, humanitarian aid workers both from Haiti and internationally, and UN personnel. The investigation covered abuses and human rights violations committed in eight communes of the West Department. In December 2024, Amnesty International wrote to the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier FilsAimé to present a summary of their conclusions. At the time of publishing this statement, no response had been received. Sexual violence and rapeCriminal gang members have kidnapped, raped, and sexually assaulted girls during attacks on neighborhoods or after taking control of areas. Attacks on girls who venture out onto the streets are common, and they are also deliberately targeted in their homes. The members of the criminal gangs have also sexually exploited girls in relationships and for commercial sex. Amnesty International has documented the cases of 18 girls who were raped and subjected to other forms of sexual violence by members of criminal gangs. Some of them were attacked more than once. In 10 cases, the girls were subjected to gang rape, and in 9 cases, kidnapped. International law requires states to protect minors from sexual exploitation and abuse, including prostitution. Members of a criminal gang kidnapped two teenage sisters on their way home from school and subjected one to gang rape, with five men raping one sister and six men raping the other. One of them told Amnesty International, "I think about it and I tell myself, I'm a girl, why did this happen to me." Several girls told Amnesty International that they had become pregnant as a result of a rape. Due to abortion still being a crime in Haiti, some resorted to unsafe methods to attempt to interrupt their unwanted pregnancies. In December 2023, members of a criminal gang intercepted a 17-year-old girl who lived in CarrefourFeuilles while she went out to buy food at night. The attackers, dressed in black and wearing their faces covered, took her to a house where five of them raped her by turns. The girl told Amnesty International "They told me, 'You won't tell this. If you do, we'll kill you.' Then they told me to leave. Later, she discovered she was pregnant. 'It destroyed me. I have no one to help me with the baby.'"Those involved in commercial sex acts as minors are victims of sexual exploitation. A 16-year-old girl who lived in an area controlled by the 5 Segon gang said she had started in commercial sex with members of the gangs after she and her child had gone several times without food.Translated text preserves the original meaning, tone, and terminology, especially when describing traffickers, victims, and survivor narratives. He said I have no choice They see you and say Let's go If you refuse, they hit you with a weapon Any day they could shoot me dead They grab you and kick you. Some pay, others don't. Girls who are victims of sexual violence at the hands of members of criminal gangs require highly specialized medical care to support their physical and psychological recovery. Despite this, Haiti's limited healthcare services have been affected by the gang attacks. Survivors face different obstacles in accessing justice, amidst the widespread impunity that plagues Haiti. Many of those interviewed did not intend to report the attacks to the authorities due to the absence of police forces in areas controlled by criminal gangs. A child who was kidnapped and raped by several members of a criminal gang in 2023 and was again sexually assaulted by a member of a criminal gang in 2024 said, "There is no police. The only authority in the area are the gang members. You can't tell them no." Child Recruitment by Criminal Gangs. Amnesty International interviewed 11 boys and 3 girls recruited and used by criminal gangs. The minors described being exploited in various ways, including spying on rival gangs and police, making deliveries and domestic tasks, construction work, and repairing vehicles. The 14 children and girls said they had no choice and acted predominantly out of fear or hunger. A 12-year-old boy said that members of the Grand Ravine criminal gang had forced him to be an informant. "If I hadn't done it, they would have killed me." Another preadolescent reported that a criminal gang had forced him to carry a weapon to commit criminal acts. He told Amnesty International what I did, I didn't do it with my heart. I didn't understand what I was doing. I used a weapon, not to harm, but to take care of myself. Some children and adolescents received beatings and threats for refusing to follow orders. A 17-year-old girl reported that members of the criminal gang Ti Bwa would send her to buy gifts for their girlfriends and clean houses for minimal amounts of money, such as $2 US dollars. She added Sometimes I respond I don't want to. Then they yell at me and tell me If the boss asks you to do something, you have to do it. You can't say no. The UN and civil society groups have documented the murder of minors and adults that the self-defense groups known as the Bwa Kale movement believed were associated with criminal gangs. Several minors said they were trying to hide their association with gangs out of fear of reprisals from community members. A child said: "If someone points at me, they might kill me." The government is detaining dozens of minors, including many who are allegedly recruited and used by criminal gangs, along with adults in a overcrowded center originally designed to rehabilitate children. At the time of the investigation, none of the children had been declared guilty because the Juvenile Court in Port-au-Prince stopped functioning in 2019. The recruitment and use of children and girls by criminal gangs in Haiti are prohibited by international and national law, as it turns minors into victims of human trafficking, among many other abuses. Deaths and Injuries Criminal gangs frequently kill and injure minors during their incursions into neighborhoods. In areas under the control of gangs, children and adolescents are exposed to random and direct gunfire. Amnesty International has documented cases of 10 minors who were injured and two who died as a result of violence perpetrated by criminal gangs and associated incidents. Their ages ranged from five to 17 years. In at least two cases, there was crossfire between the gangs and the police. A 14-year-old girl described how a stray bullet, fired by a member of a criminal gang near her home in September 2024, pierced her face. She said, "It's not a quiet area. There are problems all the time. Many shots are fired. I hate the shots. Her brother had died three months earlier, also from a stray bullet fired in her neighborhood. Childhood mental health suffers significant damage. A 13-year-old girl suffers from constant flashbacks of the day when members of a criminal gang threatened her family at gunpoint and burned her house down. She said, "I see corpses, I have nightmares, I can't sleep. Images of what I saw come to me. Before, I could study without problems. Now it's difficult."Children and adolescents with disabilities Children and adolescents with disabilities face a higher risk of being caught up in violence, among other things due to their limited mobility and having to leave behind their assistive devices. Amnesty International interviewed 11 children and adolescents with disabilities, including those with physical and psychosocial disabilities. The research team documented inaccessible conditions in displacement centers, as well as attacks on a school and a clinic for children and adolescents with disabilities. Many survivors continue to believe that their lives will improve. A child who lost a leg from a sniper's bullet said: "This story is not the end of my life. I hope my life will change." Recommendations Children and girls associated with criminal gangs are above all victims. Amnesty International calls on the international community, including donors, to work with Haitian authorities and civil society to design a roadmap aimed at introducing lasting changes based on human rights, and to prevent future cycles of violence. The Haitian government and international donors must collaborate to develop a comprehensive and inclusive child protection plan, Agnès Callamard has stated. Effective programs to demobilize and reintegrate children and girls associated with criminal gangs, and to provide complete medical and legal assistance to those who survive sexual violence, are a priority. The government must also address impunity by accelerating the creation of specialized courts to prosecute abuses and severe human rights violations. We must control the massive flow of firearms into Haiti that enables the widespread abuses by criminal gangs. Countries must also stop forcibly deporting Haitians while the gangs' terror campaign and the broader human rights crisis continues.

Lizzet Pérez In the government led by Alejandro Armenta Mier, 4 minors who were victims of human trafficking have been rescued, said Vice Admiral Francisco Sánchez González, Secretary of Public Security (SSP), who highlighted that through this rescue, the minors were returned to their families. In an interview with the media, he specified that despite the fact that these victims were from other states, Puebla and Tlaxcala are classified as one of the points with human trafficking. However, through various operations, in coordination with the three branches of government, they work to eradicate this type of crime. In fact, he mentioned that last week he met with a group of sex workers, who asked for his support. Therefore, he made contact with the State Attorney General's Office (FGE) to be able to link them, since what they seek is to avoid being pressured by certain groups or manipulated.

The Public Prosecutor's Office has charged a 19-year-old young woman, identified as Saifrenys Neimar de La Caridad Cedeño Sánchez, with the crime of human trafficking. This charge comes after complaints from relatives of one of the victims, who alerted authorities to the situation their loved one was facing. According to information released by the Prosecution Office through their official Instagram account, Cedeño Sánchez was apprehended near the Simón Bolívar International Airport of Maiquetía, in the Carlos Soublette parish, La Guaira state. The director of the Scientific, Penal, and Criminal Investigations Corps (CICPC), General Commissioner Douglas Rico, reported that the young woman was involved in a network dedicated to recruiting women to send them to Spain with the aim of forcing them into prostitution. Rico explained that, thanks to an exhaustive research work and analysis of telephone and computer communications, it was possible to establish a connection between Cedeño and other delinquents in Spanish territory. These criminals deceive their victims by promising them a better life and economic stability, paying for their air tickets and passports, only to exploit them sexually later. As part of the investigative process, crucial evidence has been collected, including three mobile phones and two Venezuelan passports. These elements have been handed over to the Fourth Prosecution Office of the Public Ministry of the La Guaira Judicial Circuit, where the corresponding process will continue. This case highlights the importance of joint work between authorities to combat human trafficking and protect the rights of victims involved in this alarming problem. data.text: Ex-colleague accuses MP Jorge Durán of abuse amidst conflicting versions DENUNCIATION. Parliamentarian claimed it was a consensual relationship. Accuser responded that he had her threatened. RN referred the case to the TS. Yesterday morning, it became known that the MP's ex-partner filed a complaint against him for the alleged crime of sexual abuse. The parliamentarian defended himself and claimed that he had previously denounced the woman. On the other hand, his party announced that it would take the case to the Supreme Court of the community. The Public Ministry initiated an investigation following a complaint filed yesterday by the woman, who accused the parliamentarian of a presumed sexual abuse that occurred on February 8. As a result, the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI arrived at the MP's residence to conduct some proceedings, while the complainant was taken to the Medical Legal Service to undergo examinations. Hours later Durán issued a statement in which he stated that on Friday he held a meeting at his home in Colina, where he claimed to have had a consensual intimate encounter with her on the early hours of Saturday. The parliamentarian said that after the end of our relationship, and considering that my ex-partner was unemployed and without a place to reside, I offered her accommodation in a dependency within my property, where we would have had relations. Afterward, he claimed that in the presence of witnesses we shared breakfast and lunch (...) Subsequently, after clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began to demand a sum of money, alleging that if I did not comply with her demands I would be the most harmed. Faced with this extortion situation and after discovering that she had used my credit cards, on Monday night I filed a report for extortion and theft with the Carabineros. .) To my surprise, after my complaint, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, he claimed. On his part, the woman said I was only asking him to pay pending tickets because I managed his social media (...) I didn't file a complaint before because I was afraid, because he had me threatened and before this happened. He always told me that I was the girlfriend of a deputy and that I had to behave as such (...) I was locked up in the cabin over the weekend. Supreme Court Upon learning of the investigation, the RN party's director sent the case files to the party's Supreme Court to initiate an investigation. This is a serious complaint that must be investigated within our penal system, RN said. On the other hand, the Minister of the Interior, Carolina Tohá, said that an accusation of rape is serious because there is a person, in this case a woman, who has been vulnerable (...) We take it very seriously indeed.

The Attorney General of the Republic, Tarek William Saab, announced late on Monday night that the Public Ministry (MP) had charged a 19-year-old woman identified as Saifrenys Neimar de La Caridad Cedeño Sánchez with human trafficking. She was recruiting other women and sending them to Spain for sexual exploitation. Through the social media platform Instagram, the Public Ministry stated that this case came to light after a complaint was filed at one of the institution's offices in La Guaira state. The mother of one of the victims made the accusation. In this regard, the agency detailed that after Cedeño Sánchez's capture by officials from the Scientific, Penal, and Criminal Investigations Corps (Cicpc) near the Simón Bolívar International Airport of Maiquetía, the 4th Prosecution Office was assigned, which charged the victimizer with the crime of human trafficking of women and requested the preventive measure of detention. Saifrenys Neimar Cedeño Sánchez was charged, as she was allegedly capturing women traveling to Spain to work as prostitutes, until these young women paid off the costs of their trip, the MP publication states.
