data.text: The captured individuals are Guatemalan brothers, and they would have had similar confrontations with authorities in the past for managing brothels. A desperate 911 call allowed the rescue of two women who were victims of human trafficking in Lake Worth Beach, Florida, and the detention of two Guatemalan brothers, migrant Yudvin and Glin Zúñiga Latin, who are accused of operating a brothel where the victims were sexually exploited under threats of violence. The operation was led by the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office (PBSO), according to authorities at a press conference. The case began on Sunday, February 9, around 7:45 a.m., when a young woman managed to contact 911 to report that she was being held against her will. The victim was not sure exactly where she was, but mentioned that she had been confined to a house for several days by two men, reported the PBSO Due to the limited information and general location provided by the phone, the agents initiated an urgent investigation in a densely populated area. The tracking led them to an apartment located at 1400 Lake Avenue, near Lake Worth Community High School, where they observed two men with suspicious behavior. The discovery of isolated and frightened women As they approached the individuals, the agents noticed their nervousness and decided to investigate further. Through a window, they were able to visualize a woman inside the apartment, which led them to enter immediately due to the gravity of the situation. Inside the residence, they found two women in separate rooms, visibly terrorized and without the possibility of communicating with each other, authorities reported. According to Sergeant Carlos Lisboa of the PBSO's Special Investigations Division, the victims were deceived with false promises of employment and transported to Palm Beach, where they were forced into prostitution. The women also reported the presence of firearms in the apartment, which were used by the suspects to keep them subdued. This case is not an isolated incident. Authorities acknowledge that it is a recurring problem in Palm Beach County, where clandestine brothels operate in residential neighborhoods. This is just one of many cases, noted Sergeant Lisboa, who explained that broader investigations are underway to dismantle organized human trafficking networks. Suspect backgrounds and charges The detained individuals were identified as Yudvin Zúñiga Latin and his brother Glin Zúñiga Latin, both Guatemalan nationals and undocumented immigrants in the United States. According to the authorities of the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, both are subject to ICE detention orders. Glin Zúñiga Latin, who was previously arrested in 2023 with his mother for operating a brothel near the location of the recent operation, faces more severe charges this time, including:Two counts of human traffickingSexual assault by an adultAggravated assault with a deadly weaponResisting an officer without violenceBenefiting from prostitutionUsing a property for prostitution activitiesYudvin Zuniga Latin faces similar charges, although without the accusation of sexual assault or aggravated assault. Both are being held without bail, according to official reports. The authorities' response focuses on dangerous criminals. During the press conference, Sheriff Ric Bradshaw defended the work of the PBSO and clarified that the focus is on detaining criminals, not on conducting mass raids on immigrants. This is not a mass operation, we are after dangerous people, Bradshaw stated. The sheriff also announced that the county is evaluating the possibility of confiscating properties used for human trafficking activities. If the people living in these houses represent a danger to the community, we will consider taking away their homes, Bradshaw emphasized. Meanwhile, the Zúñiga Latin brothers will remain under custody while the investigation advances, facing charges that could result in long sentences if they are found guilty. Additionally, due to their irregular migratory status, they could be deported after the judicial process. The authorities urge the community to collaborate in reporting any suspicious activity related to human trafficking, by contacting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office directly. Every call can save a life, concluded Bradshaw.

Double Homicide in Florencio Varela Confirmed: Paloma Was Not Abused The supplementary autopsy confirms that Paloma Gallardo was not abused, while the prosecutor leaves the case without significant progress. This Tuesday, the supplementary autopsy of Paloma Gallardo (16) and Josué Salvatierra confirmed that the young girl was not a victim of sexual violence, thus contradicting the theory that her parents had been supporting since the discovery of the bodies in a vacant lot in Florencio Varela. Sources close to the case reported that, in addition to this fact, the forensic examination revealed that the adolescents received blows to the head for approximately half an hour, a fact that highlights the brutality of the attack. I want it to be clear what happened. My daughter was raped and Josué defended her. That's why they were killed, Omar Gallardo had declared during his daughter's funeral. Despite the preliminary forensic examination having already ruled out indications of sexual abuse, the father continued to insist in several interviews that he had seen bruises and bite marks on Paloma's erogenous and genital areas. However, these details were refuted by the expanded autopsy report. Nevertheless, from the prosecution team, the idea of an unconsummated sexual abuse against Paloma is still being maintained. Investigation without Progress and Change in Prosecutor The autopsy confirmed the double skull fracture as the cause of death for both young people and added a chilling detail: the blows with a blunt object extended for more than 30 minutes, indicating the cruelty of the act. Without significant progress in the investigation, the prosecutor in charge of the case decided to step down, and it is expected that their replacement will be appointed this Wednesday. This change occurs in a context where solving the crime seems still far off, and the tensions between justice and the families of the victims continue.

Measures Against Teenage Pregnancies in Coahuila are WorkingPublic health policies implemented by the different government agencies have managed to reduce the number of cases of pregnancies in women under the age of 20 over the years. For example, in Coahuila, of the 38,000 cases registered in the last year, 16% correspond to this population. Regarding this, Marco Antonio Ruiz Prado, in charge of the Preventive Medicine Department at the Coahuila Health Secretary, stated that the implemented strategies have had a positive impact. According to national health and nutrition surveys, 78% of adolescents know and use contraceptive methods, such as condoms, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the dissemination of information on sexual health. Additionally, in Coahuila, most teenage pregnancies occur in girls over 15 years old, although the goal for 2030 is to completely eliminate pregnancies in those under that age. Dr. Marco Antonio Ruiz Pradis emphasized that the prohibition of child marriage and the promotion of contraceptive methods have been key policies in reducing unplanned pregnancies. He also highlighted the role of the Autonomous University of Coahuila in disseminating this information, as students become replicators within their communities. Women using implants have the right to a healthy sexuality. The application of devices against unplanned pregnancies remains a contentious issue, nonetheless, it was reported that this public prevention policy is legally derived from the right of women to decide on a healthy sexuality. Marco Antonio Ruiz Pradis, head of the preventive medicine department at the Coahuila Health Secretariat, explained that adolescents have access to modern contraceptive methods, such as the subdermal implant, which is an effective and discreet option to prevent unplanned pregnancies. In addition, she pointed out that her application is free in health units and mobile clinics, ensuring that young people can exercise their rights without economic limitations. Ruiz Pradis detailed that these implants can be placed from 15 or 16 years old, depending on the onset of each person's active sex life. Also, she emphasized that, before its application, counseling is provided so that adolescents can choose the contraceptive method that best suits their needs, thus guaranteeing respect for their sexual and reproductive rights. With these measures, the Secretary of Health seeks to strengthen sexual health education and promote informed decision-making among young people in Coahuila.

The Ecuadorian National Police, through the National Interpol Unit and the National Unit for Investigation Against Human Trafficking and Illicit Migration Trafficking, successfully apprehended and extradited Stalin Z., an Ecuadorian citizen, who was requested by the Los Ríos Quevedo Judicial Unit for the crime of human trafficking. The hard work of the National Police units made it possible to identify those responsible for this criminal network and manage the Interpol Red Notice, which facilitated the location and capture of Stalin Z. His extradition represents a significant step forward in the fight against human trafficking and impunity, reaffirming the institution's commitment to protecting the rights of victims and strengthening citizen security. The Ecuadorian National Police reaffirms its commitment to fighting organized crime and protecting society through coordinated actions with national and international organizations. We will continue working tirelessly to ensure justice and security for all citizens.

data.text: Federal prosecutors in Tennessee, United States, charged eight individuals on Tuesday, February 11, with allegedly being linked to the trafficking of women from Venezuela. Authorities reported that two of the accused allegedly used their connections with the Venezuelan criminal gang known as the Tren de Aragua to intimidate them, according to The Tennessean. Although the prosecutors' accusation did not specify if the individuals were members of this criminal organization, the American media outlet identified one of them as a member of the Tren de Aragua.The charges against the accused According to the authorities, the accused allegedly convinced dozens of victims to travel to the United States with the promise of a better life, paying for their trips. The subjects then loaded the women with debts exceeding the cost of their travel. Women were forced to engage in sexual relations with strangers to pay off debts, according to Tennessee District Attorney Rob McGuire. The illicit sex trafficking operation, run by these individuals, was in operation from at least July 2022 to March 2024. District Attorney Rob McGuire clarified that they cannot release information about the victims, who are undocumented in the US and may face deportation proceedings. We will do whatever it takes to try to save the lives of the victims we are serving, McGuire assured The Tennessean. The possible fate of the suspected members of the Cartel of the Suns in the US On February 5, US Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announced that the suspected members of the Cartel of the Suns detained in the US would be transferred to the Guantanamo prison in Cuba. In Guantánamo Bay, as President Donald Trump has said, we will receive the worst of the worst. We are after those bad guys, Noem said in a video shared on her X account. Public Prosecutor's Office Charges Young Person with Human Trafficking and Prostitution in SpainThe head of the Scientific Penal and Criminal Investigations Body (Cicpc), General Commissioner Douglas Rico, reported that the young person was involved in a network dedicated to capturing women to send them to Spain with the aim of forcing them into prostitution. Rico explained that, thanks to an exhaustive research and analysis of telephone and computer communications, it was possible to establish a connection between Cedeño and other criminals in Spanish territory. These criminals deceive their victims by promising them a better life and economic stability, paying for their air tickets and passports, only to exploit them sexually. As part of the investigative process, crucial evidence has been collected, including three mobile phones and two Venezuelan passports. These elements have been handed over to the Fourth Prosecution of the Public Ministry of the Penal Judicial Circuit of the La Guaira State, where the corresponding process will continue. This case highlights the importance of joint work between the authorities to combat human trafficking and protect the rights of the victims involved in this alarming problem.

Mateo Santiago's Killer Had Photos of Minors on His Phone The case of Mateo Santiago continues to shock after the discovery of photos of minors on the suspect's phone. The case of Mateo Santiago, a 12-year-old boy reported missing on February 4 in León, Guanajuato, has shocked Mexico. After an intense search, the lifeless body of Mateo was found on February 7 in a field between León and Lagos de Moreno, Jalisco. Christian Augusto N, a doctor who worked at a clinic where the minor supposedly performed cleaning tasks, was arrested as the main suspect. According to the Attorney General's Office of the State of Guanajuato, the detained man confessed to having abandoned Mateo's corpse in a vacant lot. After being discovered, he attempted to take his own life to avoid facing the authorities, although the self-inflicted injury was not fatal. He was taken to a hospital, where he made his statement However, what seemed to be an isolated case of murder has taken a darker turn. On February 11, authorities revealed that on Christian Augusto N's mobile phone, they found photographs of minors in suspicious situations. Investigation advances in Mateo Santiago case after discovery of photos This discovery has opened a new line of investigation related to a possible child abuse ring. Investigators are working to identify other possible individuals involved in this crime. Mateo's family lawyer has dismissed the possibility that the minor had any connection to the doctor or worked at the clinic in question, contradicting the initial versions of the case. Authorities continue to advance in the investigation, and the community demands justice, with family and friends calling for a complete clarification of this heinous crime. The authorities continue to analyze the evidence found on the detained person's cell phone, and it is expected that more details will emerge in the coming days.

In a landmark ruling that sets an important precedent in the fight against child sexual abuse, a court in Punta Arenas sentenced a man to prison for sexually abusing a minor over several years. The incidents, which took place between 2012 and 2021, occurred in the Puerto Natales commune. Prosecuting Attorney Romina Moscoso explained that the accused, the partner of the victim's grandmother, took advantage of his position of trust to commit the abuse on multiple occasions. The Public Prosecutor's Office requested a prison sentence of seven years in effect for these extremely serious acts, noted the prosecutor. The investigation, carried out by the Punta Arenas Prosecution Office, gathered solid evidence that allowed the facts to be proven. Among the presented evidence are the victim's and other witnesses' testimonies, as well as psychological expert opinions that corroborated the damage caused to the minor. The reading of the verdict, where the definitive sentence that the convicted person will have to serve will be announced, will take place next week.

data.text: Complaint filed against alleged child abuse of an 8-year-old girl at a primary school in Tlaquepaque A suspected case of child abuse was reported at a primary school in Tlaquepaque, where a minor was allegedly sexually abused. Authorities are investigating the incident. The incident occurred on Monday morning inside the school, located in the Lomas de Tlaquepaque colony. The child said "If you do something or say something, it's going to get worse for you," and the girl didn't say anything, María Guadalupe Ramos, the victim's grandmother. Angry and concerned parents of the family arrived at the school. The State Prosecutor's Office reported, through its social communication link, that an investigation file was opened to clarify what happened inside the primary school and identify the alleged responsible individuals.

Letters from Readers Not to Overexpose Minors on Social Media María Paz Álvarez Lorente Recently, it was announced that Minister Yolanda Díaz has a draft law to prevent the lucrative work of children in social media. Any law regulating this matter is welcome, but I fear it is too late. Family channels expose the children 24 hours a day (even while sleeping) to the children and girls. On YouTube, there are authentic aberrations: children in bathtubs, children in hospitals, children in vulnerable situations. These videos are recorded and edited by the parents. We're not talking about a photo you can share on a social network; we're talking about children who have their entire childhood exposed, children who make advertisements, often hidden, for which their parents, who have no scruples, get rich. This business is so lucrative that parents leave their jobs. Sometimes these children are the breadwinners for their families, a responsibility that doesn't belong to them falls on them, besides they are famous for exposing their private lives, not for having any skill. Which rights are being violated The right to honor, intimacy, and one's own image, as collected in Title I, Chapter Two, Section One of the Spanish Constitution. The children do not have the age to give their consent nor are they aware of the thousands of people who know everything about them. What consequences follow Recently psychologists are talking about Trauma by Betrayal, this occurs when they reach adulthood and realize the degree of exposure that besides creates an unerasable digital footprint for the rest of their lives, which can have repercussions when looking for a job, for example. Besides, it creates a digital identity forever that is very difficult to erase. And if you download the videos. A good option, but you will never be able to delete videos that have been downloaded and shared, which people save on their computers, so what you upload to the internet you cannot control and remains there forever. But who is behind the computer or phone screen Many times there are pedophiles and pedophiles, the material provided is used by them and puts the children of others in danger. The networks are dangerous and are not for children, parents have the duty to protect their children and provide them with everything they need. What working conditions do they have These children have no type of contract or social security and their money goes entirely to their parents, who can keep it for their future or not. In this sense, it is very different from child actors or singers on television, who already have a regulation. In short, put yourselves in the place of these children and avoid consuming these channels.

In a coordinated operation led by the Division of Investigations of Crimes Against Women, Child, Girl, and Adolescent, officials managed to apprehend Jorge Luis Mendoza Blanco, (38), accused of forcing children and young people to perform forced labor under threats. By Miriam Kuepper Published 2114 EST, February 11, 2025 Updated 2114 EST, February 11, 2025 An assistant principal caught with over 11,500 images of child abuse has been fired after being let off with jail time for his heinous sex crimes. Gareth Mellor, 45, pleaded guilty to two charges of making indecent images of children and one count of possessing them, and was handed a two-year suspended prison sentence at Leeds Crown Court in December 2023. He was arrested at his home in Staffordshire in May 2021 after paying for indecent images of minors through an encrypted cloud storage service. Mellor had worked as a teacher at Kettlethorpe High School in Wakefield, none of his offenses, which occurred between January 2014 and May 2021, were related to his students, according to the National Crime Agency. He was the designated school safety officer as well as the pastoral leader for 320 students. The 45-year-old teacher has now been banned from teaching indefinitely after a panel from the Teaching Regulation Agency (TRA) discovered that a ban was proportionate due to the gravity, duration and volume of his crimes. Thousands of photos, not taken by Mellor, were found on his devices, the majority of which were of adolescents. Approximately 520 images and videos were Category A material, 619 Category B and 10,450 Category C according to the panel's decision. Gareth Mellor (en la foto), de 45 años, admitió dos cargos de creación de imágenes indecentes de niños y una acusación de posesión de dichas imágenes y recibió una sentencia de prisión suspendida de dos años en la Corona de Leeds en diciembre de 2023. Mellor había trabajado como maestro en Kettlethorpe High School en Wakefield, pero según la Agencia Nacional de Crimen, ninguno de sus delitos, que ocurrieron entre enero de 2014 y mayo de 2021, estaba relacionado con sus alumnos. Cuando Mellor pagó a un proveedor conocido por proporcionar material indecente, la Agencia Nacional de Crimen rastreó la dirección de correo electrónico utilizada para la transacción al maestro y lo arrestó. Mellor admitió que había intentado eliminar el contenido de su teléfono móvil, sin embargo, la policía aún podía recuperar una cantidad significativa de material indecente, según la decisión del panel de TRA. He been sentenced to two years in prison, suspended for two years, as well as 200 hours of unpaid community service, a program activity and a rehabilitation activity. He was also made subject to a 10-year sexual harm prevention order and his name was added to the sex offender register. Although Mr. Mellor's conduct took place outside the school environment, the panel noted that the behavior involved in committing the offence could have had an impact on the safety of pupils and members of the public given the nature and gravity of the offences, the TRA decision said. The panel also noted that within the sentencing hearing there was reference to Mr. Mellor searching for pupils at the school on social media platforms, although the offences did not involve pupils. The panel did not receive a testimony or reflection from Mellor that confirmed he had completed the requirements for rehabilitation of his sentence. Mellor is indefinitely banned from teaching and cannot teach in any school, sixth form college, relevant youth hostel or children's home in England, said decision-maker Sarah Buxcey on behalf of the Secretary of State. Furthermore, given the gravity of the allegations found against him, I have decided that Mr. Mellor will not have the right to request the restoration of his eligibility to teach. Evo has been confined to the tropics for 4 months and the Police are still analyzing how to apprehend him. Four months have passed since the capture order was issued against Evo Morales and almost a month since the Police received it, in the context of an investigation into human trafficking, the permanent guarding and vigilance by his bases intensify at different points in Chapare and particularly in the locality of Lauca Ñ, where the former president resides. The executive secretary of the Yungas Federation of the Cochabamba tropics, David Veizaga, told Los Tiempos that Evo Morales' integrity is strictly safeguarded by the population. The State does not guarantee the rule of law and citizens' security. Therefore, there is no other mechanism than for the people to organize themselves, provide their own guarantees, and take care of their representatives and leaders, and in this case, our brother Evo. Wielding handmade clubs and shields, delegations from the tropics and various points in the country have expressed on several occasions that they will not allow Morales to be apprehended. Veizaga added that as a strategy, other mechanisms of vigilance and protection are not being revealed, but that there is constant coordination and vigilance. According to lawyer and constitutionalist William Herrera Añez, one of the Executive's attributions is to comply with the resolution issued by the justice. Asked if Evo's assistance to register his candidacy before the Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE) would be the opportunity to apprehend him, Herrera warned that it is not necessary for Morales to be physically present. He can do it through a proxy or legal representative, it is not a personal act, he emphasized. On the other hand, the penal lawyer, Marco Quiroga, asserts that the arrest warrant must be executed anywhere in the country, so that he can be transported and presented before the investigating judge of the case. Order of OperationsThe Minister of Government, Eduardo Del Castillo, assured that the order of operations to execute the arrest of Evo Morales is already ready, however, they are waiting for the precise moment and place to execute it. We are waiting for him to leave the tropical region. Again, we assert that this man is looking to convulse the country, he is looking for confrontations, said Del Castillo. They will prevent others from getting hurtSince last month, the government of Luis Arce has been criticized for not executing the capture of Evo Morales. From the official side, it was responded that this action would be planned, in order to prevent their personnel from being attacked or to generate a confrontation with groups from different social sectors and from different departments, which take turns setting up vigilance blockades. The groups, some carrying sticks, clubs, or whips, are arriving and rotating in the municipality of Villa Tunari.

It was her mother who facilitated the arrest, thanks to her alerting the agents of the Scientific, Penal, and Criminal Investigations Corps. After that, she was accused of a human trafficking crime. According to the Prosecutor's Office, the court issued a measure of deprivation of liberty against the detained woman, who will remain at the CICPC headquarters in La Guaira. Diddy Sued for Sexual Assault AGENCY REFORMA Mexico City Diddy Combs, former music mogul, has been sued for sexual assault by a street musician who claims to have been a victim of rape by the ex-music industry executive. The complaint, filed in the New York State Supreme Court, alleges that Combs used a Bad Boy Records employee to lure the alleged victim with false promises of a record contract. According to documents obtained by Us Weekly, the plaintiff, identified under the pseudonym John Doe, reported that in November 2022, he was performing music on the streets of Los Angeles when a supposed talent scout invited him to a private party organized by Combs. During the party, Combs enthusiastically greeted the street musician and offered him a drink, which, according to the complaint, contained GHB, a substance associated with sexual assaults. PROMISE OF A RECORDING CONTRACTThe plaintiff alleged that the interpreter, Ill be missing you, promised to help him obtain a record contract and led him to a private room under the pretext of showing him his collection of jewelry. However, once in the room, he noticed that there was no jewelry and felt strange, with an unusual sense of euphoria and disorientation, considering he had only consumed one drink.Combs made numerous promises to help Doe obtain a significant record contract, according to the legal text. The alleged victim stated that Combs asked him if he had ever practiced oral sex and, after his denial, insisted that he should try it. Upon resisting, he claimed that Combs sexually assaulted him, exerting pressure to comply, assuring him that he would only sign a contract if he did so. Combs refused to let Doe leave and insisted that Doe would not receive any contract unless he complied. Despite Doe's refusal to accept Combs' advances, Combs continued to exert increasing pressure and made promises about launching Doe's music career, it was alleged. The legal document detailed that Combs orally and anally raped the street musician before leaving the room. The next day, an unknown person administered an intravenous injection and returned him to the nightclub where he had been picked up the night before. Since the alleged attack, the plaintiff has had no contact with Combs and has experienced severe emotional trauma, according to his lawyers, who claim that the musician did not report the incident earlier due to fear of Combs' power and influence. This lawsuit adds to recent allegations against Sean Combs, who is facing charges of sex trafficking and extortion, and is currently being held at the Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center, awaiting a scheduled trial on May 5.

After presenting evidence in court and reviewing the case files submitted by the Castro District Attorney's Office, the court determined the 61-year-old defendant's sentence. Andreas Kusch, assistant prosecutor of the Castro District Attorney's Office, stated that the victims reported suffering sexual aggressions, sexual abuse from childhood and adolescence, as well as rapes by the accused, who was the father of both victims. Along with the victims' testimonies, evidence of context and corroboration presented in the trial was carried out by the Investigating Police, particularly the Sexual Crimes Investigating Brigade, which conducted a series of proceedings aimed at reviewing witness statements, such as work at the crime scene. The court considered the police evidence presented in court, the testimonies of forensic experts from the Medical Legal Service (SML), as well as other evidence, and ultimately imposed a 20-year prison sentence in its maximum degree for the repeated crimes of sexual abuse and rape, in addition to a four-year prison sentence in its maximum degree for the crime of serious injuries in the context of domestic violence, detailed the lawyer. The representative of the prosecuting agency added that the total penalty to be imposed on the defendant is 24 years in prison, which the defendant will have to serve in its entirety in private confinement, a situation that has been maintained since he was formalized in preventive prison to already serve this sentence. As a Prosecutor's Office, the professional added that we express our agreement, inasmuch as the facts were accredited and the court adopted this sentencing decision, imposing the highest sanctions contemplated by our penal legal framework. data.text: Amnesty International Report I am a child, why did this happen to me? Child abuse by criminal gangs in Haiti The relentless violence of armed criminal gangs in Port-au-Prince and its surroundings has led to a brutal attack on childhood in Haiti, as documented by Amnesty International in a new report. I am a child, why did this happen to me? Documenting child abuse by criminal gangs in Haiti, reveals how children are subjected to countless human rights abuses, including recruitment into criminal gangs, rape and other forms of sexual violence, kidnappings, murders, and injuries. It also documents the disproportionate impact on children with disabilities. Since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021, armed criminal gang violence has significantly increased in Haiti, with an estimated 5,600 lives lost in the past year. Criminal gangs control most of the capital, Port-au-Prince, while over 5.5 million people require urgent humanitarian assistance. Criminal gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti. They threaten, beat, rape, and kill children and girls. They have committed multiple abuses of children's rights, including the right to life, education, and freedom of movement, Agnès Callamard, Amnesty International Secretary General, has stated. Too many children in Haiti are seeing their lives destroyed, and they have nowhere to turn for protection or justice. They suffer persecution and, in some cases, homicide at the hands of self-defense groups, while authorities arbitrarily detain them. They are being robbed of their childhood. It is time for Haitian authorities and the international community, including donors, to redouble their efforts. Empty expressions of concern are not enough. Children and girls suffer daily violations of their body, mind, and heart. Haiti urgently needs assistance to protect childhood and prevent new cycles of violence. According to calculations, more than a million children and girls live in areas controlled by criminal gangs or under their influence. The research team interviewed 112 people and visited Port-au-Prince in September 2024. Among those interviewed, there were children and girls, government authorities, humanitarian aid staff from Haiti and internationally, and UN personnel. The investigation covered abuses and human rights violations committed in eight communes of the West department. In December 2024, Amnesty International wrote to the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier FilsAimé to present their conclusions. At the time of publishing this statement, no response had been received. Sexual Violence and AbuseMembers of criminal gangs have kidnapped, raped, and sexually assaulted girls during attacks on neighborhoods or after taking control of areas. Girls who go out onto the streets are frequently attacked, and they are also deliberately targeted in their own homes. Members of criminal gangs have also sexually exploited girls in relationships and for commercial sex. Amnesty International has documented cases of 18 girls who were raped and subjected to other forms of sexual violence by members of criminal gangs. Some of them were attacked more than once. In 10 cases, the girls were subjected to gang rape, and in 9 cases, they were kidnapped. International law requires states to protect children from sexual exploitation and abuse, including prostitution. Some members of a criminal gang abducted two teenage sisters who were returning from school and subjected one of them to a gang rape, with five men raping her, and six men raping the other. One of them told Amnesty International "I think about it and I say to myself I'm a girl, why did this happen to me?" Several girls told Amnesty International that they became pregnant as a result of a rape. Since abortion remains a crime in Haiti, some resorted to unsafe methods to try to terminate their unwanted pregnancies. In December 2023, some members of a criminal gang intercepted a 17-year-old girl who lived in Carrefour-Feuilles when she went out to buy food at night. The attackers, dressed in black and with their faces covered, took her to a house where five of them raped her in turns. The girl told Amnesty International "They told me Don't tell anyone about this. If you tell anyone, we'll kill you. Then they told me to leave." Later, she discovered she was pregnant It destroyed me I have no one to help me with the baby. Minors involved in commercial sexual acts are victims of sexual exploitation. A 16-year-old girl living in an area controlled by 5 Segon said she had been initiated into commercial sex with members of criminal gangs after she and her child had gone several times without food. She said I have no choice They see you and say Let's go. If you refuse, they beat you with a gun Any day, they could shoot me. They grab you and kick you. Some pay, others don't. Girls victims of sexual violence at the hands of members of criminal gangs require highly specialized medical care to support their physical and psychological recovery. Despite this, Haiti's limited healthcare services have been affected by the attacks of criminal gangs. The survivors face different obstacles to access justice, amidst the widespread impunity that plagues Haiti. Many of the interviewees did not intend to report the attacks they suffered to the authorities due to the absence of police forces in areas controlled by criminal gangs. A girl who was kidnapped and raped by several members of a criminal gang in 2023 and was again sexually assaulted by a member of a criminal gang in 2024 said: "There's no police. The only authority in the area are the gang members. You can't tell them no."Recruitment of children and girls by criminal gangs. Amnesty International interviewed 11 children and 3 girls who were recruited and used by criminal gangs. The minors described being exploited in various ways, including spying on rival gangs and the police, making deliveries and domestic tasks, working on construction projects, and repairing vehicles. . The 14 boys and girls said they had no choice and were acting predominantly out of fear or hunger. A 12-year-old boy said that members of the Grand Ravine criminal gang had forced him to be an informant, saying If I hadn't done it, they would have killed me. Another preteen recounted that a criminal gang had forced him to carry a gun to commit crimes. He told Amnesty International I did it, but not with my heart. I didn't understand what I was doing. I used a gun, not to harm, but to protect myself. Some boys and girls received beatings and threats for refusing to follow orders. A 17-year-old girl reported that members of the Ti Bwa gang sent her to buy gifts for their girlfriends and clean houses in exchange for minimal sums of $2 USD. She added Sometimes I respond I don't want to. Then they yell at me and tell me If the boss asks you to do something, you have to do it. You can't say no. The UN and civil society groups have documented the killings of minors and adults whom self-defense groups known as the Bwa Kale movement believed were associated with criminal gangs. Several minors said they tried to hide their association with gangs out of fear of reprisals from community members. A child said, "If someone points a finger at me, they could kill me." The government has detained dozens of minors, including many who are allegedly recruited and used by criminal gangs, along with adults in an overcrowded facility originally designed to rehabilitate children. At the time of the investigation, none of the children had been declared guilty because the Juvenile Court in Port-au-Prince had stopped functioning in 2019. The recruitment and use of children by criminal gangs in Haiti are prohibited by international and national law, as it turns minors into victims of human trafficking, among many other abuses. Deaths and InjuriesCriminal gangs frequently kill and injure minors during their incursions into neighborhoods. In areas under the control of gangs, children and girls are exposed to both indiscriminate and direct fire. Amnesty International has documented cases of 10 minors who were injured and two who died as a result of violence caused by criminal gangs and associated incidents. Their ages ranged from five to 17 years old. In at least two cases, there was crossfire between the criminal gangs and the police. A 14-year-old girl described how a stray bullet, fired by a member of a criminal gang near her home in September 2024, pierced her face. He said It's not a quiet area. There are problems all the time. Many shots fired. I don't stand the shots. Her brother had died three months earlier, also due to a stray bullet fired in their area. The mental health of childhood suffers significant damage. A 13-year-old girl suffers constant retrospective visions of the day when members of a criminal gang threatened her family at gunpoint and set fire to her house. She said I saw corpses I have nightmares, I can't sleep. Images of what I saw come to me Before I could study without problems. Now it's difficult. Children and girls with disabilities Children and girls with disabilities face a greater risk when fleeing violence, among other things due to their limited mobility and having to abandon their assistance devices. Amnesty International interviewed 11 children and girls with disabilities, including those with physical and psychosocial disabilities. The research team documented the inaccessible conditions in displacement centers, as well as attacks on a school and a clinic for children and girls with disabilities. Many survivors continue to believe that their life will improve. A child who lost a leg from a sniper's bullet said: "This story is not the end of my life. I hope my life will change." Recommendations Children and girls associated with criminal gangs are above all victims. Amnesty International urges the international community, including donors, to work with Haitian authorities and civil society to design a roadmap to introduce lasting changes based on human rights and prevent future cycles of violence. The Haitian government and international donors must collaborate to develop an integrated and inclusive child protection plan, Agnès Callamard has stated. The programs to effectively demobilize and reintegrate children and adolescents associated with criminal gangs, and to provide comprehensive medical and legal assistance to those who survive sexual violence, are a top priority. The government must also address impunity by accelerating the creation of specialized courts to prosecute serious abuses and grave violations of human rights. The massive influx of firearms into Haiti must be controlled, which enables the widespread abuses of criminal gangs. Countries must also stop forcibly deporting Haitians while the gangs' terror campaign and the broader human rights crisis continue.

data.text: RN Representative Durán is accused of abuse amidst a parliamentary cross-examination. The parliamentarian claimed it was a consensual relationship. The accuser responded that he had her threatened. RN sent the case to the Supreme Court. Matías Gatica Lindsay Yesterday morning, it was reported that the former partner of RN Representative Jorge Durán filed a complaint against him for the alleged crime of sexual abuse. The parliamentarian defended himself and claimed that he had previously denounced the woman. On the other hand, his party announced that they would take the case to the Supreme Court of the collective. The Public Ministry initiated an investigation as a result of a complaint made yesterday by the woman, who accused the parliamentarian of a presumed sexual abuse that occurred on February 8. As a result, the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI arrived at the parliamentarian's residence to conduct some proceedings while the accuser was taken to the Medical Legal Service to undergo medical examinations. Hours later, Durán issued a statement in which he stated that on Friday he had a meeting at his home in Colina, where he claimed to have had a consensual intimate encounter with her in the early hours of Saturday. The parliamentarian said that after the end of our relationship, and considering that my ex-partner was unemployed and without a place to live, I offered her accommodation in a dependency within my property, where we would have had relationships. Afterward, he claimed that in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch (...) Subsequently, after clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began to demand a sum of money, alleging that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the most harmed. Faced with this extortion situation and after discovering that she had used my credit cards, on Monday night I filed a report with Carabineros for extortion and theft. To my surprise, after I made the complaint, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, he claimed. On his part, the woman said I was only asking him to pay pending tickets because I managed his social media (...) I didn't file a complaint before because I was afraid, because he had me intimidated and before this happened. He always told me that I was the girlfriend of a deputy and that I had to behave like that (...) I was locked up in the cabin over the weekend. Upon learning of the investigation, the RN leadership sent the background to the Supreme Court of the party so that an investigation can be initiated. This is a serious complaint that must be investigated within our penal system, RN stated. On the other hand, the Minister of the Interior, Carolina Tohá, said that an accusation of rape is serious, because there is a person, in this case a woman, who has been vulnerable (...) Certainly, we took it with the utmost gravity.

Prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro requested the dismissal of La Matanza's Intendant, Fernando Espinoza, in the case in which he is being prosecuted for sexual abuse against Melody Rakauskas. Cuñarro argued that there are not enough evidence to support the accusation and pointed out that the accuser would have maintained a pattern of behavior in which she would relate to married men, record them, and then ask for money. However, the case could still be elevated to oral trial, since Rakauskas, in her role as the plaintiff, requested that the investigation be closed and the process be advanced. Espinoza remains prosecuted for simple sexual abuse and disobedience, after the Chamber of Crimes confirmed the accusation. According to the complaint, the Intendant allegedly forced and molested Rakauskas in May 2021 during a work meeting at his apartment. He is also accused of disobeying a restraining order by contacting her through an ex-partner to dissuade her from filing the complaint. Prosecutor Cuñarro stated that the complainant's account is not believable and that her refusal to undergo psychiatric evaluations or provide her electronic devices prevents corroborating her version. Additionally, she stated that there are no material evidence to support the complaint, such as medical attention, 911 calls, witnesses, or security camera records. The evidence collected does not allow verifying that there was a simple sexual abuse by her part against the plaintiff, she stated in her opinion. An episode that occurred in March 2023 in New Delhi was also considered by the prosecutor. According to diplomatic reports, Rakauskas was hospitalized after having ingested psychiatric medications in an attempt to commit suicide, while she claimed that Indian agents tried to kill her with a suspicious substance, relating the incident to the case against Espinoza. The doctors recommended her psychiatric hospitalization and subsequent repatriation.

Mariano Valdivia, the lawyer for Mateo Santiago Ramírez Martínez's family, assured that the minor had no work-related relationship with Dr. Christian Augusto Jafet, who was presented before a judge on Tuesday, accused of the crime of disappearance committed by private individuals, and, for the time being, not by homicide or infanticide. The State Attorney General's Office (FGE) reported that they have managed to apprehend Christian Augusto Jafet N for his participation in the crime that has shaken the community, and added that thanks to an exhaustive investigation, they were able to attribute responsibility to Christian in the events. Without providing further details, they only stated on FGE account X that Christian Augusto Jafet is at the judge's disposal to determine his legal situation. Justice is following its course, and we work towards a humane prosecution of justice. Dr. Christian was discharged from León General Hospital on Tuesday, February 11, after being admitted due to a gunshot injury before being detained by León Police. At 12:40 pm, elements from the Criminal Investigation Agency (AIC) executed the arrest order issued against Christian for the crime of disappearance by private individuals, a crime that will be aggravated by homicide. On February 4, Mateo Santiago went missing after leaving school, and his body was found on February 7 in the Lagunillas community, on the border of Lagos de Moreno and León. When Dr. Christian was detained, he confessed where he left Mateo's body. It was known that Mateo left the Technical High School number 39, located in the Las Mandarinas colony, on the afternoon of Tuesday, February 4, where he was in his first grade, and it had been mentioned that he headed towards a medical clinic located at the corner of Manuel de Austria Boulevard and Jalisco Street, in the Chapalita colony, to perform cleaning tasks. At this location, Dr. Christian Augusto worked, who was arrested on Friday, February 7, when the Guanajuato State Attorney General's Office confirmed the discovery of the minor's body. On February 8, a Third Pre-Candidates Forum of the Centro Democrático was held in Valledupar on illicit economies. There, it became evident how narcotics trafficking, contraband, illegal mining, and human trafficking, as well as migrant trafficking, became the backbone of criminal structures, and a structural challenge that affects public order and national security, weakens the formal economy, reduces investment, limits opportunities, and increases inequality, devastates forests, contaminates water and soil, and erodes trust in institutions and among people. Narcotics trafficking is the greatest threat to national stability. Our country is the world's main cocaine producer with 253,000 hectares of coca registered in 2023, and a potential alkaloid production that grew 53% between 2022 and 2023, reaching 2,664 metric tons. The plantations are located in 19 of the 32 departments, concentrated in 15 productive enclaves in Norte de Santander, Sur de Bolívar, Antioquia, Cauca, Nariño, and Putumayo. 48% of the crops are in special management zones and 89.5% are in the same territories as a decade ago. The key is to attack the concentration zones (agro-industrial model), which represent 80% of the cocaine and 52% of the cultivated territory, demanding 82% of the chemicals, 98% are under the control of an illegal structure, and 42% report social leader homicides. This growth is due to the abandonment of glyphosate fumigation since 2015, and because this Government practically ended manual eradication (9,403 hectares were eradicated in 2024, while the average of the previous four-year period was 91,300 hectares), and weakened substitution programs. According to Professor Daniel Mejía, narco-trafficking exceeded 4% of the GDP in 2024. Illegal mining is a parallel business to narco-trafficking that causes ecocide and is controlled by the ELN, the Gaitán Clan, and the FARC. In 34% of municipalities with coca, there is illegal exploitation of alluvial gold. The dynamics of illegal mining are centered on gold, which has grown due to the high price on international markets (it went from US$1,769.6 per ounce in 2020 to US$2,739.2 in January 2025). Of the 100,000 hectares of illegal open-pit mining, 51% are in forest reserves or natural parks, and 73% of alluvial gold are illicit exploitation. Unfortunately, the government's attack on legal mining and inaction against illegal mining made the investment in the sector drop from US$3,290 million in 2023 to US$1,269 million in 2024, and royalties and taxes of $9.1 billion in 2023 to $4.16 billion. Smuggling that weakens competitiveness and fosters informality mainly comes from China (28%), the United States, and Bolivia (8%), followed by Panama and Brazil. Between 2018 and 2022, 10% of the value of merchandise entering the country was contraband (exceeding $8.8 million in 2022), 90% was technically smuggling through under-invoicing. Colombia is a country of origin, transit, and destination for human trafficking for sexual and labor purposes. In 2023, this increased by more than 50%. The Aragua Train and the ELN operate sex trafficking networks on the border with Venezuela, and the Darién bottleneck, controlled especially by the Gulf Clan, has become an important migration route over the past four years, with 106,840 people in 2021, 539,959 in 2023, and 400,614 in 2024. To overcome this situation, we require a state policy that encompasses an integrated strategy, allowing for territorial control, institutional strengthening, and capital flow surveillance.

In a petition submitted today, prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro requested the dismissal of La Matanza Intendant Fernando Espinoza from the investigation into alleged sexual abuse against his former private secretary, Melody Rakauskas. According to an 80-page report to which the Agencia Noticias Argentinas had access, Cuñarro argues that there are not enough evidence to support the accusation, beyond the statements of the accuser. In response to this request, the judge in charge of the case must determine whether to accept or reject it. It is worth noting that the original judge, Luis Schelgel, was replaced by Fernando Caunedo. In another instance, the prosecution had requested that the case be taken to trial, so the judge asked for Cuñarro's opinion, who recommended the dismissal of Espinoza. However, although the prosecution has requested this, Rakauskas's defense team can still insist on the case being taken to trial against the municipal leader. The former secretary of the Intendant of La Matanza filed a complaint in 2012, accusing him of having abused her outside of working hours. In July 2024, the Criminal Chamber confirmed the prosecution of the Intendant on charges of sexual abuse and disobedience to a court order, leaving the case ready for trial. The charge of disobedience is based on the fact that, despite having a restriction that prevented him from communicating with Rakauskas, he allegedly made contact with her to ask her to withdraw the complaint. The local chief has publicly criticized his former secretary, claiming that she refused to hand over her cell phone and computer to be investigated. Espinoza has also stated that the complaint is part of an attempt to spy on him.

data.text: Here you will find a readable version of the report. Numerous criminal gangs are responsible for human rights abuses against children in Haiti. Extreme violence and intimidation prevail in Port-au-Prince and surrounding areas Too many children in Haiti are seeing their lives destroyed Agnès Callamard The relentless violence of criminal gangs in Port-au-Prince and its surroundings has resulted in a brutal attack on childhood in Haiti. This is what Amnesty International has stated in a new report. I am a child, why has this happened? Documenting the aggressions of criminal gangs against children in Haiti, it shows how children and girls are subject to countless human rights abuses, including recruitment into criminal gangs, rape and other forms of sexual violence, kidnappings, murders, and injuries. It also documents the disproportionate impact on children with disabilities. Since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021, armed gang violence has significantly increased in Haiti, with an estimated 5,600 lives lost in the past year. Armed gangs control much of the capital, Port-au-Prince, while more than 5.5 million people require urgent humanitarian assistance. Armed gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti. Haiti urgently needs assistance to protect children and prevent new cycles of violence. Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International, stated that armed gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti. They threaten, beat, rape, and kill children and girls. They have committed multiple abuses against the rights of the child, including the right to life, education, and freedom of movement, Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International, has stated. Too many children and girls in Haiti are seeing their lives destroyed, and they have nowhere to turn for protection or justice. They are being persecuted and, in some cases, murdered by self-defense groups, while authorities are detaining them arbitrarily. They are being robbed of their childhood. It is time for Haitian authorities and the international community, including donors, to redouble their efforts. Empty expressions of concern are not enough. Children are suffering daily violations of their body, mind, and heart. Haiti needs urgent assistance to protect children and prevent new cycles of violence. According to estimates, more than one million children live in areas controlled by criminal gangs or under their influence. The research team interviewed 112 people and visited Port-au-Prince in September 2024 Among the people interviewed were children and adolescents, government authorities, humanitarian aid personnel from Haiti and internationally, and UN personnel. The investigation covered human rights abuses and violations committed in eight communes of the West department. In December 2024, Amnesty International wrote to the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier FilsAimé to present a summary of their conclusions. At the time of publishing this statement, no response had been received. Sexual violence and rapeMembers of the criminal gangs have kidnapped, raped, and sexually assaulted girls during attacks on neighborhoods or after taking control of areas. It is common for girls who go out on the street to be attacked, and they are also deliberately targeted in their homes. Members of the criminal gangs have also sexually exploited girls in relationships and for commercial sex. Amnesty International has documented the cases of 18 girls who were raped and subjected to other forms of sexual violence by members of criminal gangs. Some of them were attacked more than once. In 10 cases, the girls were subjected to gang rape, and in 9 cases, they were kidnapped. International law requires states to protect minors from exploitation and sexual abuse, including prostitution. Members of a criminal gang kidnapped two adolescent sisters who were returning from school and subjected them to gang rape; five men raped one of them and six men raped the other. One of them told Amnesty International, "I think about it and I tell myself, 'I'm a girl, why did this happen to me?'". Several girls told Amnesty International that they became pregnant as a result of a rape. Because abortion remains a crime in Haiti, some resorted to unsafe methods to attempt to interrupt their unwanted pregnancies. If you refuse, they hit you with a weapon. Any day, they could shoot me. 16-year-old girl threatened by members of a criminal gang. 5 Seconds Ago In December 2023, members of a criminal gang intercepted a 17-year-old girl living in CarrefourFeuilles when she went out to buy food at night. The attackers, dressed in black and with their faces covered, took her to a house where five of them raped her in turns. The girl told Amnesty International "They said This you're not going to tell. If you tell, we'll kill you. Then they told me to leave. Later, she discovered she was pregnant Me destroyed I have no one to help me with the baby. Children involved in commercial sexual acts are victims of sexual exploitation. A 16-year-old girl living in an area controlled by 5 Segon gang members said she was initiated into sex trafficking by members of these criminal gangs after she and her child had gone through several periods without food. She said, "I have no choice. They see you and say, 'Let's go.' If you refuse, they hit you with a gun. They can shoot me dead any day. They grab and kick you. Some pay, others don't." Girls who are victims of sexual violence at the hands of gang members require highly specialized medical care to support their physical and psychological recovery. Despite this, Haiti's limited healthcare services have been affected by gang attacks. Survivors face various obstacles in accessing justice amidst the widespread impunity that plagues Haiti. Many of those interviewed did not intend to report the aggressions they suffered to the authorities due to the absence of police forces in areas controlled by criminal gangs. A girl kidnapped and raped by several members of a criminal gang in 2023 and who was again sexually assaulted by a member of a criminal gang in 2024 said, "There is no police. The only authority in the area are the members of the gangs. You can't tell them no." Recruitment of children and girls by criminal gangs. Amnesty International interviewed 11 boys and 3 girls recruited and used by criminal gangs. The minors described being exploited in various ways, including spying on rival gangs and the police, making deliveries and domestic chores, construction work, and repairing vehicles. The 14 children and girls said they had no choice and were acting predominantly out of fear or hunger. A 12-year-old boy said that members of the Grand Ravine gang had forced him to be an informant. If I hadn't done it, they would have killed me. Another pre-teen told Amnesty International that a gang had forced him to carry a gun to commit crimes. He said, "What I did, I didn't do it out of the heart. I didn't understand what I was doing. I used a gun, not to harm, but to take care of myself." Some children and adolescents received beatings and threats for refusing to follow orders. A 17-year-old girl reported that members of the Ti Bwa gang sent her to buy gifts for their girlfriends and clean houses for minimal amounts, such as $2. She added, "Sometimes I respond, 'No, I don't want to.' Then they yell at me and tell me, 'If the boss asks you to do something, you have to do it. You can't say no. If I hadn't done it, they would have killed me.'" 12-year-old boy forced to be an informant The UN and civil society groups have documented the killings of minors and adults whom self-defense groups known as the Bwa Kale movement believed to be associated with criminal gangs. Several minors said they tried to hide their association with gangs out of fear of reprisals from community members. One boy said: "If someone points at me, they could kill me." The government has detained dozens of minors, including many who are allegedly recruited and used by criminal gangs, along with adults in an overcrowded facility originally designed to rehabilitate children. At the time of the investigation, none of the children had been declared guilty because the Juvenile Court in Port-au-Prince had stopped functioning in 2019. The recruitment and use of children by criminal gangs in Haiti are prohibited by international and national law, as it turns minors into victims of human trafficking, among many other abuses. Deaths and injuriesCriminal gangs frequently kill and injure minors during their incursions in neighborhoods. In areas under gang control, children are exposed to both indiscriminate and direct fire. Amnesty International has documented cases of 10 minors who were injured and two who died as a result of violence caused by criminal gangs and associated incidents. Their ages ranged from five to 17 years old. In at least two cases, there was crossfire between the gangs and the police. I have nightmares, I can't sleep. I keep seeing the images of what I saw. 13-year-old girl threatened with a gun at gunpoint. A 14-year-old girl described how a stray bullet, fired by a member of a criminal gang near her home in September 2024, pierced her face. She said, "It's not a quiet area. There are problems all the time. Many shots. I hate the shots." Her brother had died three months earlier, also from a stray bullet fired in her neighborhood. Childhood mental health suffers significant damage. A 13-year-old girl suffers from constant retrograde visions of the day when members of a criminal gang threatened her family at gunpoint and burned down her house. She said, "I saw corpses. I have nightmares, I can't sleep. Images of what I saw come to me. Before, I could study without problems. Now it's difficult." Children and adolescents with disabilities Face a higher risk of danger when fleeing violence, among other things due to their limited mobility and having to abandon their assistive devices. Amnesty International interviewed 11 children and adolescents with disabilities, including those with physical and psychosocial disabilities. The research team documented inaccessible conditions in displacement centers, as well as attacks on a school and a clinic for children and adolescents with disabilities. Many survivors continue to believe that their lives will improve. A child who lost a leg due to a sniper's bullet said: "This story is not the end of my life. I hope my life will change." Recommendations Children and adolescents associated with criminal gangs are primarily victims. Amnesty International urges the international community, including donors, to work with Haitian authorities and civil society to design a roadmap aimed at introducing changes that bring lasting solutions based on human rights, and to prevent future cycles of violence. The Haitian government and international donors must collaborate to develop a comprehensive and inclusive child protection plan, Agnès Callamard has stated. Effective programs to demobilize and reintegrate children associated with criminal gangs, and to provide complete medical and legal assistance to those who survive sexual violence, are a priority. The government must also address impunity by accelerating the creation of specialized courts to prosecute serious abuses and violations of human rights. It is essential to control the massive influx of firearms into Haiti that enables the widespread abuses by criminal gangs. Countries must also cease forcibly deporting Haitians while the campaign of terror by criminal gangs and the broader human rights crisis continues.

data.text: Since July 9, 2024, N.R.T.V. went missing from her hometown of Desaguadero, in neighboring Bolivia, leaving no trace behind. Nine months later, she managed to escape the hell she was subjected to thanks to social media. WhatsApp AssistanceThe woman took advantage of her captor's momentary lapse to access her WhatsApp and ask for help from her family members. She indicated that she was being held captive in a residence in the Jequetepeque district, in the Pacasmayo province, in the north of Peru, under the extreme violence of Percy Junnior Angulo Soto. The Desaguadero Police reported the communication to the agents of the Jequetepeque police station, who set up an operation that began with the arrest of Percy Angulo, a 19-year-old motorcycle taxi driver who did not hesitate to confess his crime. He detailed that the victim was being held captive in his residence located at Manco Cápac Street, N 500. Months of TerrorAfter the taxi driver's confession, the police arrived at his residence and rescued the woman, who in her statement detailed that her captor subjected her to physical, psychological, and sexual violence. Additionally, she stated that she was kept locked up and isolated in her bedroom, and that on some occasions, she was tied to a chair or bed under the threat of killing her parents if she wanted to leave for another place. The PNP stated that due to fear of the threats, the victim was afraid to ask for help or return to her country. The case is now in the hands of the Mixed Provincial Attorney's Office of San Pedro de Lloc. Prosecutor Taly Chaiguaque ordered the detained individual to be charged with crimes against personal liberty (kidnapping) and against sexual liberty (rape). Police sources informed BuenaPepa that the investigation into the woman's kidnapping is ongoing to determine if she was under the influence of an international mafia dedicated to human trafficking in the form of sexual exploitation. Percy Angulo, the confessed kidnapper, is being held in the cells of the Pacasmayo Depincri.Disappearances: a chronic problem in PeruThe case of the Bolivian citizen is a reminder of one of the social problems that go unnoticed in Peru and Latin America: the disappearance of people. According to the Police Complaints Information System, between January and December 2024, 17,317 complaints were filed for missing persons in Peru. The majority of victims range in age from 12 to 17 years old, especially girls. 10,728 complaints were filed for missing women. The regions most affected are Lima (6,615), Cusco (651), Arequipa (514), Junín (494), Lambayeque (489), Piura (373), La Libertad (336), Puno (322), Ica (255), Ayacucho (146), and Loreto (134). The report "Qué pasó con ellas" (What Happened to Them) from the Defensoría del Pueblo warns that in 2024, 7,097 alerts were reported for missing women, a figure that increased by nearly 37% compared to 2023. Moreover, in 2024, as in previous years, the majority of disappearances corresponded to girls and adolescents, with 65% of the cases, it details. It also specifies that the region with the highest rates of complaints for the disappearance of women in 2024 continues to be Lima (3,574 cases), due to its larger population. Cusco (651) follows, then Lambayeque (540), Arequipa (536), Junín (535), Piura (468), Huánuco (428), La Libertad (427), Callao (389), and Puno (376). Furthermore, of the 170 femicides registered in the last year, 15% of the cases had been previously reported as disappearances. In December 2024, 877 girls and adolescents were reported missing. Of this total, 671 were female girls and adolescents, which is 77%. This confirms the relationship between gender and age as vulnerability factors. The disappearance of women by private individuals is a form of violence often linked to crimes such as femicide, human trafficking, sexual violence, etc. The gender factor and intersectionality with other forms of discrimination are key to understanding the greater exposure to living this type of violence, explains the DP. Regarding this, the Legislative Decree N 1428, which regulates measures for attention in cases of disappearance of people in a situation of vulnerability, establishes that a person is considered missing if they are absent from their habitual domicile and their whereabouts are unknown. Within this group, women who have suffered violence are considered to be in a situation of vulnerability. Reporting Channels In the event of information or the location of a person reported as missing, the person or authority must immediately inform the police or report it through the 114 Line. Presenting a report at the national level in any police station, Depincri, or in the Division of Investigation and Search for Missing Persons, without the need to present a DNI or other identification document, and without the 24 hours having passed since the disappearance was known, and without having a direct relationship with the victim, was detailed by the DP.

Federal prosecutors in Tennessee, United States, charged eight individuals on Tuesday, February 11, with participating in a sex trafficking ring of Venezuelan and other foreign women into the North American country. According to The Tennessean, the accused were identified for luring numerous victims to the US under the false promise of a better life. Once the women arrived, they were imposed with exorbitant debts that far exceeded the costs of their travel, leaving them in a situation of vulnerability and extortion. The victims were forced to engage in sexual acts with strangers for the economic benefit of the accused, as stated by Rob McGuire, interim federal prosecutor for the Middle District of Tennessee. The criminal operation was in operation from July 2022 to March 2024. All the accused are currently in federal custody, and two of them are allegedly linked to the Aragua Train. The individuals allegedly used their influence in the major criminal organization to intimidate Venezuelan women, although the charge does not specify if they were official members of the organization. McGuire stated that his office will do everything possible to save the lives of the victims we assist, adding that it is crucial for his office that any survivors of sex trafficking can bring their perpetrators to justice. Although there was no comment regarding the possible deportation of victims who may be in the country without proper documentation, the prosecutor stated that the intention is to ensure that survivors have a path to justice. The medium reported that the accused are Yilibeth Del Carmen Rivero de Caldera, Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero, Yuribetzi Del Valle Gómez Machuca, Wilmarys Del Valle Manzano Soloranzo, Endrik Alexander Morales Rivero, Ariannys Beatriz Gutiérrez Carrillo, Frankyanna Del Valle Romero Rivero, and Jesús Enrique Castillo Rodríguez. It was established that the criminal activity had family characteristics, as Del Carmen Rivero de Caldera and Mota Rivero are mother and son. The remaining accused are relatives or spouses of Mota Rivero. All face charges of conspiracy to transport individuals across state lines for prostitution, as well as other related charges involving organized crime. Meanwhile, Gómez Machuca, Mota Rivero, and Del Carmen Rivero face an additional charge of conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking, which carries severe penalties, including the possibility of life imprisonment.
