Armenia Spokespeople from Redpapaz warned that in the last year in Colombia, they have received 40,000 reports of child sexual exploitation material involving children and adolescents between the ages of 4 and 13 through social media and the internet. Alejandro Castañeda, head of the Safe Internet Center of Vigías of the Colombian Mothers and Fathers Network Redpapaz, explained that recent studies indicate that one in six children and adolescents in Colombia and Latin America are suffering from a situation that unfortunately is becoming increasingly widespread: intimate images, videos, and content of them are being shared on the internet. Imagine all those private photos taken at home, in family, even in intimate and very personal situations that show the naked body. Seriously, it's a problem that's becoming increasingly prevalent, especially because it's a situation that's happening mostly to girls and women between 4 and 13 years old, which is almost 8 out of 10 cases we see here at the report line. And I want to detail that last year alone, to give you an idea, we received approximately 40,000 reports of those cases, which corresponded to the dissemination of more than 180,000 images of victims, as I was saying, young girls and adolescents who are being disseminated and who see those contents that were not necessarily meant to be shared on the internet, that they did not want to be shared, unfortunately they are being shared on the internet without their consent. How those who use these images operate and what we must do to protect children, adolescents, and minors from having their information used is crucial. The evidence is that almost always, this is a result of strong manipulation that children and minors are suffering due to their contact with people on the internet. I want to emphasize this because the problem is not that the child takes the photo, that is not the problem, and let's not make the victim of this situation the perpetrator. In this situation, they are another victim who responds to very difficult situations where girls are being extorted, manipulated, and receiving messages from strangers, even friends and family members. Because that is also a problem that is seen among families that share, there is a lot of personal information, content, name, address, location, and from there onwards, a strong entanglement mechanism is built, a very powerful mechanism of manipulation that often leads to the girl and the boy sharing or divulging and sharing that intimate image. Recommendations First recommendation to mothers, fathers, and caregivers is to be very attentive to what girls and boys do on the internet. Do not let them be alone when using the cell phone. Many times what we see is that those images, those videos are when girls and boys have contact with their parents' cellphones or are attentive to being connected in a very personal space. The idea is to be very attentive to them, be very aware of what girls, girls and boys, our children and our children, are doing, and to take care of how to be attentive when there is a warning signal, such as comments from an unknown person, for example, when we start to see that our daughters and our children are talking to other people or that they are withdrawing from social life and becoming very private, and do not want to talk to anyone. These are warning signs that we should be aware of as an alarm. Smartphones are not digital babysitters Alejandro Castañeda, the head of the Secure Internet Center Vigías de Red Papás explained that what's important is to see that electronic devices and social media, in reality, any cell phone and device, are not digital babysitters. They are not there to take care of girls and boys. And that's very important because many times we're focused, as you say, on how a cell phone can emotionally contain or regulate a child's emotions at a specific moment, or help them not be so bored, but what we need to see is that the device and the way children use it will never be regulated. The device will never tell them when a content is not suitable for them. And it added: At no point will the device tell them, for example, not to put their personal information on the internet. The device, and especially if it belongs to an adult who is very open, does not have privacy settings, is not configured, let's say, to allow children to use it in a slightly safer way, as it will have many risks. For example, the fact that we are increasingly leaving our banking information available, which can be used, can also be used to share photos. Therefore, we must be aware that it is not a babysitter, it will not answer many things, and it will be regulating those moments when girls and boys are using that device. Children learn by repetition. That is why children and children learn a lot through repetition. And here we are making a call as Redpapaz, to be very vigilant about what we as mothers and fathers are doing when we are with our children with our cellphones. What the research and evidence tell us is that many times, almost always, girls and boys learn and very early, from babies, from 6 months old, from one year old, when we see them using the platform, the Tablet or the cellphone, and they know perfectly how to click. It's not that they're learned, it's not that they're born with it, they're born knowing precisely everything from one, because they repeat and repeat what we do. So, we're seeing that girls and boys with a high dependence on device use relate very closely, very closely, to mothers and fathers who are also very addicted and always attached to their cellphones, we use it when we eat with them, we use it when we're caring for them, and that becomes a situation that generates a lot of difficulty. Mobile or electronic devices are not babysitters.

In every strengthened community, there lies the opportunity to interrupt the cycle of violence. In the case of schools, it is especially true to prevent recruiters of girls, boys, and adolescents from criminal groups with promises of rapid advancement in the social hierarchy and to impose the consumption of drugs. The recruitment of minors is a global problem and concern. It violates the fundamental rights of the victims and perpetuates conditions of violence and delinquency. According to estimates from the International Red Cross, around 300,000 girls and boys are forced to participate in armed conflicts or criminal situations, physical abuse, and sexual abuse. In Mexico, civil organizations estimate that it could be around 35,000. The data expose the need for public policies to prevent this problem, highlighted by the head of government of Mexico City, Claudia Sheinbaum, as the urgency to prevent minors from dropping out of school and becoming cannon fodder for criminal groups. Or consumers of toxic, illegal, and deadly addictive substances such as the dark varieties of fentanyl. Opportunities for the development of this population sector are strengthened with scholarships for different age groups initiated in the national capital by the current president, Claudia Sheinbaum, as well as a school security model aimed at confronting the sale of drugs and hooliganism in the vicinity of public and private schools. And this always requires the community without which there is no security and least of all school security. Girls, boys, and adolescents can dangerously normalize criminal behaviors and become more susceptible to recruitment, with profound repercussions for them and their families. Participation in criminal acts generates traumas and mental disorders, such as post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and anxiety. Minors involved in organized crime are stigmatized and it is complex their social reintegration. Their incorporation into organized crime is criminally sought for the continuation of these criminal structures and fuels cycles of violence with community damage. On January 12, World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers, in addition to remembering those who have been employed by armed groups, it is necessary to accompany strategies to prevent recruitment, keep them away from criminal environments from an early age, and build spaces of peace and security around schools. The Auxiliary School Program, presented by Brugada this week, promotes community participation to build paths to peace at school entrances and exits, with the presence of public servants and the strengthening of video surveillance from the C5. Only through joint and sustained efforts will we be able to create suitable environments for girls and boys.

In a joint operation between the Peruvian National Police and the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Crimes of Money Laundering, a clandestine location known as El Castillo and other properties linked to an investigation into alleged money laundering, human trafficking, and promoting prostitution were seized. According to preliminary information, the owners of the establishment, Juan Carlos Choque Sullasi and his wife Rosa Cayra, have been under investigation since 2024 for allegedly enriching themselves illicitly through delinquent activities linked to human trafficking and promoting prostitution. The operation, which included the support of specialized units such as DIRILA, USE, and the Grupo Terna, involved breaking into and ransacking several properties, where goods that could be related to the illicit activities of the couple were seized. The authorities continue with the investigations to gather evidence that will clarify the facts and determine the responsibility of those being investigated. RSM Editing

Near 9:00 am, the judges of the Penal Chamber No. 1, Drs. Mauricio Navarro Foressi, Fernando Esteban, and Daniela Barrionuevo, opened the hearing by summoning the defendant to recount the events, who was accompanied by his lawyer, Attorney Pedro Vélez. Thereafter, the defendant, whose identity is not disclosed to protect the victim with whom he had a romantic relationship at the time of the incidents between April and August 2023, sat before the witness stand and made a statement. As the trial takes place behind closed doors, the press does not have access to the courtroom. However, judicial sources reported that in his statement, the accused essentially denied all of the accusations. Then, the victim entered the courtroom to testify. In general, the woman recanted and, in front of the Chamber's prosecutor, Alejandro Dalla Lasta, said that the events did not occur as she had denounced them earlier. After the testimony of the complainant, the court decided to adjourn until 9:00 am today to continue with the statements of five other witnesses summoned for the plenary session. Regarding the accusations, judicial spokespeople reported that the events allegedly occurred between the months of April and August of 2023, in a residence in the capital. Following the denunciation, the prosecutor in charge ordered the arrest of the now-accused, who is currently serving preventive detention at Miraflores prison.

San Luis Potosí, Tuesday, February 11, 2025. Prosecutors obtained a guilty sentence of four years in ordinary prison against Lázaro N for the qualified sexual abuse crime in the municipality of Tierra Nueva. The facts occurred between June and August 2023, when the victim visited a residence in the El Original neighborhood for religious reasons. However, the accused took advantage of those visits to commit indecent acts against her. The General Prosecutor's Office of the State of San Luis Potosí (FGESLP) integrated the case into an investigation file, which allowed the detention of the accused and his presentation before the judicial authority. During the process, Lázaro N accepted his responsibility, and his defense requested an expedited procedure. The Judge of Control issued a sentence of four years in prison, which he must serve in a penitentiary center, in addition to imposing on him the payment of reparatory damages and a pecuniary fine in favor of the State.

data.text: Deputy Durán is accused of abuse amidst crossed parliamentary statements. The parliamentarian claimed it was a consensual relationship. On the other hand, the accuser responded that he had her threatened. RN referred the case to the Supreme Court of the party. Matías Gatica Lindsay Yesterday morning, it was made known that Deputy RN Jorge Durán's former partner filed a complaint against him for the alleged crime of sexual abuse. The parliamentarian defended himself and claimed that he had previously denounced the woman. On the other hand, his party announced that it would take the case to the Supreme Court of the collective. The Public Ministry initiated an investigation following a complaint made yesterday by the woman, who accused the parliamentarian of a presumed sexual abuse that occurred on February 8. As a result, the Sexual Crimes Brigade of the PDI arrived at the deputy's residence to conduct some proceedings while the accuser was taken to the Medical Service for medical examinations. Hours later, Durán issued a statement in which he stated that on Friday, he had a meeting at his house in Colina, where he claimed to have had an intimate, consensual encounter with her in the early hours of Saturday. The parliamentarian said that after the end of our relationship, and considering that my ex-partner was unemployed and had nowhere to live, I offered her accommodation in a dependency within my property, where we would have had relations. Afterward, he assured that in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch (...) Subsequently, after clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began to demand a sum of money, claiming that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the most harmed. Faced with this extortion situation, and after discovering that she had used my credit cards, on Monday night, I filed a complaint for extortion and theft with Carabineros. To my surprise, after I made the report, my ex-partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, he claimed. On the other hand, the woman said I was only asking him to pay pending bills because I managed his social media (...). I didn't report it before because I was afraid, because he had me threatened and had been threatening me even before this happened. He always told me that I was the girlfriend of a deputy and that I had to behave like one (...). I was locked in the cabin over the weekend. Upon learning of the investigation, the Renovación Nacional leadership sent the background to the Supreme Court of the party for an investigation to be initiated. This is a serious accusation that must be investigated within our penal system, RN said. On the other hand, the Minister of the Interior, Carolina Tohá, said that an accusation of rape is serious because there is a person, in this case a woman, who has been vulnerable (...) Certainly, we took it with the utmost gravity. The government avoids referring to the disqualification of Deputy Pérez We should avoid referring to cases that are being investigated, Etcheverry said. A day after the Court of Appeals in Antofagasta accepted the request for disqualification of Deputy Catalina Pérez (ex-FA), who is being investigated for suspected tax fraud for signing three agreements worth $426 million between the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning (Minvu) and the Democracy Viva Foundation, the Government largely avoided referring to this situation. On this case, the Government's spokesperson, Aisén Etcheverry (FA), told radio Pauta that as Government and spokesperson, I have to reiterate something we have always said: these are judicial processes, autonomous powers, and it is our interest that they advance in a good way. To that, she added that in order for them to advance in a good way, we have to avoid referring to cases that are being investigated, that are in progress, and limit ourselves to providing all the information so that the processes advance in a good way. In the Monday hearing, the Public Prosecutor's Office revealed chats between Catalina Pérez and her ex-partner Daniel Andrade in which they talked about the agreements. In fact, prosecutor Cristian Aguilar pointed out that she directed the organization, which he claimed created a scheme to benefit from fiscal contracts with political purposes. The sentencing hearing will be on February 20. However, Pérez's defense announced that they will appeal to the Supreme Court. Chile Falls Back in Corruption Index Despite dropping three places, it is the second-best evaluated in South America after Uruguay. Transparency International released the latest Corruption Perception Index yesterday, which revealed that Chile dropped three spots in the ranking led by Denmark and ranked 32, its worst record since joining this measurement. Previously, in 2023, Chile had occupied the 29th position on the list. Despite the low score this year, where it obtained 63 out of 100 points, it continues to rank as the second-best evaluated country in Latin America, after Uruguay, which ranked 13th. Further back in the region are Costa Rica (42) and Cuba (82). On the other hand, Mexico recorded the third-largest decline worldwide, dropping 14 places and ranking 140th, while Paraguay suffered a significant decline of 13 positions and ranked 149th. Meanwhile, Colombia ranked 92nd, Argentina 99th, the Dominican Republic 104th, Brazil 107th, and Panama 114th. In the region, the worst result was obtained by Venezuela, which ranked 178th, as the third-worst evaluated country worldwide. On the other hand, the ranking is led by Denmark, Finland, Singapore, New Zealand, Luxembourg, Norway, and Switzerland, in that order. Preventive imprisonment was ordered for 14 accused members of Los Piratas de Aragua. Yesterday, the 11th Guarantee Court in Santiago ordered the preventive arrest of 14 presumed members of the criminal gang Los Piratas de Aragua, who were formalized for the crimes of criminal association, extortion, homicide, kidnapping, and kidnapping with homicide. Among these cases is the murder of Venezuelan former police officer Roland Ojeda. In that particular case, prosecutor Héctor Barros stated that seven of the formalized individuals would be linked to this crime. In total, there are three other people formalized in this case who were already serving sentences, in addition to four detainees abroad, making a total of 21 accused.

Federal agents dismantle prostitution ring; eight accused are allegedly linked to the Aragua Train. The district attorney of Tennessee says the accused were arrested in Tennessee and other states. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Tennessee announced the formal indictment of eight Venezuelan citizens allegedly linked to a human trafficking operation. The formal indictment alleges that the eight worked together to recruit and bring women from Central and South America to the United States, specifically to Tennessee and other states, to operate a commercial sex business. Prosecutors claim that the accused targeted young, poor, and vulnerable women from Venezuela and other countries. The formal indictment states that the defendants convinced the women that they would have a better life, but once in the United States, they forced them to pay the exorbitant cost of their trip by engaging in sex with strangers. I want to reiterate that human trafficking is a real problem here in our community, said federal prosecutor Robert Maguire. Ignoring it won't make it disappear. We can't live in the shadows, we have to bring it to light and make those who commit crimes in the darkness accountable. Authorities said this was the result of a years-long investigation into this operation with the help of multiple local, state, and federal agencies. The leaders say that the investigation began with the Nashville Metropolitan Police Department (MNPD) and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. The following people were formally charged: Yilibeth del Carmen RiveroDe Caldera (also known as Yibi) charged with conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution, conspiracy to transport individuals within and outside the country or in support of organized crime enterprises, conspiracy to commit human trafficking Kléiver Daniel Mota Rivero, also known as Kléiber, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution, conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to transport individuals in aid of organized crime enterprises, conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, and possession of a firearm by an undocumented foreign national.Yuribetzi del Valle Gómez Machuca, also known as La Gorda, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution, conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to transport individuals in aid of organized crime enterprises, and conspiracy to commit sex trafficking.Wilmarys del Valle Manzano Solórzano, also known as La China, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to transport individuals in aid of organized crime enterprises. Éndrik Alexánder Morales Rivero, also known as Endri, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or transportation for the benefit of organized crime enterprises.Ariannys Beatriz Gutiérrez Carrillo, also known as Nani or Nany, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or transportation for the benefit of organized crime enterprises.Frankyanna del Valle Romero Rivero, also known as Franya, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate travel within and outside the country or transportation for the benefit of organized crime enterprises. Jesus Enrique Castillo Rodriguez, also known as Chu Chu, is accused of conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate travel within or outside the country or transportation in aid of organized crime enterprises. The indictment alleges that those involved used hotels in the Nashville area to lure clients to locations where they would force victims into sex work in exchange for favors. According to court documents, they used online advertising and messaging services like WhatsApp to determine prices based on certain sexual favors. Prosecutors claim that Yibi and Kléiber used their connections with the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua to intimidate victims into continuing to participate in commercial sex acts. We rely on the community to make a difference in the lives of the most vulnerable women and girls who have been separated from their families under false pretenses and forced into the worst imaginable hell, Maguire said. Several law enforcement agency representatives spoke at a press conference on Tuesday, condemning human trafficking and urging community members to remain vigilant. Human trafficking is abhorrent to all of us, said MNPD Chief John Drake. It's a modern form of slavery. I want to be clear that our police department will always make human trafficking investigations a priority, regardless of where a suspect may be located. Maguire said they were focused on prosecuting defendants here in Nashville before deportation is mentioned. Specifically, the message authorities are sending with this indictment is that human trafficking is an abomination, added Maguire. We will find it wherever and whenever it exists. We will recover the survivors and put an end to it once and for all. Maguire says that the dozens of victims in this case will receive victim support services, likely through local and state organizations. The eight defendants are in federal custody awaiting prosecution. They were arrested in multiple states, including Tennessee and Texas. R. Kelly's Sex Trafficking Conviction Confirmed A federal appeals court confirmed on Wednesday the sex trafficking conviction and 30-year prison sentence imposed on music star R. Kelly. The ruling The US Second Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan rejected Kelly's claims that the evidence did not support the charges and that some jurors were biased. Circuit Judge Denny Chin stated that the prosecutors presented extensive evidence demonstrating how Kelly lured young girls and women into his orbit, endeavored to control their lives, and ensured compliance with his personal and sexual demands through verbal and physical abuse, extortion threats, and humiliation. Chin also noted that the jurors might conclude that Kelly, 58, intended to convince the victims that they would suffer harm if they failed to comply with his sexual demands. Possible Appeal Kelly's attorney, Jennifer Bonjean, stated that her client may appeal to the United States Supreme Court because the decision unreasonably expands the scope of the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO). Bonjean argued that the decision gives the government unlimited discretion to apply the RICO statute to absurdly remote situations from the statute's original intent. The statute aimed to punish organized crime, not individual behavior. Previous Case Kelly serves a 30-year prison sentence after a Brooklyn, New York, jury found him guilty in September 2021 of extortion and eight counts of violating the Mann Act, which prohibits transporting people across state lines for prostitution. His case became one of the most high-profile prosecutions of the #MeToo era. Previously, Kelly was more known for his 1996 Grammy-winning hit song I Believe I Can Fly. Upcoming trial The Wednesday decision came as the imprisoned rapper and music mogul awaits his May 5 trial in a Manhattan federal court on sex trafficking charges. Dozens of women and men have filed civil lawsuits accusing him of sexual misconduct. Past accusations and convictions Kelly's trial followed two decades of misconduct allegations, which he repeatedly denied. The jurors heard testimony from 45 government witnesses, including several victims, who described in often graphic detail the alleged abuse imposed by Kelly and his entourage. This included requirements that victims refer to Kelly as "dad," obtain permission to eat or use the bathroom, and write apology letters that purported to absolve him of guilt. The case is independent of Kelly's conviction in September 2022 by a Chicago jury for child sex crimes. There, he was sentenced to 20 years in prison, but the judge added only one year to Kelly's prison term, and the other 19 years were stacked on top of his 30-year sentence. Kelly is currently incarcerated at the medium-security prison in Butner, North Carolina, which once housed the late Ponzi schemer Bernard Madoff. He is eligible for release in December 2045, at the age of 78.

data.text: Laferrere Police Arrested a Man and His Son Accused of Sexually Abusing a Young Girl When She Was 5 Years Old Following an investigation overseen by the National Security Ministry, Federal Police officers arrested a man and his son for sexually abusing a young girl between the ages of 5 and 6. According to police sources revealed to TN, the victim reported the incidents when she came of age and claimed that between 2010 and 2012, she was attacked by her then-stepfather in a house located in the Buenos Aires suburb of Gregorio de Laferrere. The young girl stated that the abuses occurred when she was under the care of her mother's ex-partner and that he later threatened her with death to prevent any accusations against him. With this modus operandi, the accused remained unpunished for years, subjecting the minor to various sexual practices. Later, between 2016 and 2017, the family moved to another house located in the neighborhood of La Tablada, in the La Matanza district. It was in this context that the victim was abused again, this time by her half-brother, that is, the son of her first aggressor. After reaching the age of majority, the young woman filed a complaint at the end of January of this year. In the case, the Functional Unit of Instruction and Judgment specialized in Family Violence and Gender Violence and Sexual Integrity Crimes N1 of the La Matanza Judicial Department intervened, led by prosecutor Pamela Piatelli, who requested the participation of the Division of Public Health Crimes of the Federal Police to locate the suspects. Finally, after an investigation to find the whereabouts of the accused, federal agents were able to apprehend them with the approval of the La Matanza Guarantees Court, presided over by Dr. Rubén Norberto Ochipinti. Both were intercepted in public places, one of them in the locality of Laferrere and the other in González Catán. The accused men were placed at the disposal of the Justice and were charged with the crime of severely traumatic sexual abuse for having been committed against a minor under 18 years old, taking advantage of the situation of cohabitation and having been committed by the person in charge of the guard, in ideal concurrence with aggravated corruption of a minor.

Three defense lawyers in the case being pursued against the suspected sex trafficking ring uncovered through Operation Cattleya, recused the judges of the Third Collegiate Tribunal of the National District on Wednesday, alleging a lack of impartiality. The recusal was filed against Judges Arlín Ventura, Leticia Martínez, and Evelyn Rodríguez, who had rejected a motion of opposition from the litigating lawyers against the admission of expert evidence presented by the Public Ministry. The lawyers who filed the recusal, alleging that the accusatory body was being favored by the judges, are Brayan Humberto Santana Martínez, Domingo Aquino, and Bomar Quezada, legal representatives of the accused María Paula Morillo, Oscar Wilson, José Alberto, and the corporate defendant Hotel Oscar Inn. (DIARIO LIBRE URLMATEO) These lawyers argued that the opposition sought that the Public Ministry not present some five hard drives, considering that these were not validated and could not be presented in the hearing process.

The Judicial Investigation Organization (OIJ) Detains One of the Most Wanted for Homicide and Illicit Trafficking in Public in Heredia Agents of the Judicial Investigation Organization (OIJ) detained this Wednesday a man who is among the most wanted, since August 2024, for the crimes of presumed homicide and drug trafficking. It is about a man who was on the run, named Patterson. The police action was carried out by OIJ agents from Batán de Limón, this afternoon, in public roads in La Valencia, Heredia. After an investigation, the Judicial Police determined that the man was in Heredia and proceeded with his detention. The detained person was placed at the orders of the Public Ministry to determine his judicial status. On digital platforms such as Facebook and TikTok, El Diario found yesterday various publications from December and January in which coyotes, polleros, coyoteros, or enganchadores offer irregular entry into the United States through the bridge. Active with crossing from CD.JUARES to PASO. We already have crossing over the BRIDGE. UPDATES. DESTINATIONS, it reads in one of the publications with a date of December 20, 2024. New route, crossing at Cd. Juárez safe and guaranteed, whether walking 45 minutes, over the bridge or through the tunnel, at order (sic), another trafficker offers to migrants from countries such as Guatemala and Ecuador since January 15, 2025. Crossing to USA without walking, all by car over the bridge, is read in another publication made on December 13, 2024. We cross over the bridge. Another one over the bridge, my people, says another publication in which a migrant asserts to already be in the United States on December 23 of last year. Safe crossings. Good routes without walking so much, over the bridge, over the tunnel, another people trafficker offers since January 11, 2025. Most cases involved the misuse of legitimate documents, but the U.S. government did not break down the statistics by the manner in which they occurred. Human trafficking attempts continued through international border crossings during the fiscal year 2025. On the night of December 2, a woman was caught by CBP officers attempting to smuggle a couple hidden in a vehicle's trunk. On February 8, a U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agent was arrested and charged with participating in drug trafficking since 2019 and human trafficking since 2023 through the Paso del Norte border crossing. The officer, identified as 32-year-old Manuel Pérez Jr. from El Paso, was detained by Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Task Force on Border Corruption agents in El Paso while still wearing his uniform as part of a multi-agency federal investigation. According to court documents, between December 21, 2023, and February 5, 2025, Pérez Jr. allegedly smuggled and attempted to smuggle undocumented foreign nationals into the United States for commercial advantages and private financial gains, reported the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas. The formal indictment alleges that, in multiple instances, Pérez Jr. Pérez Jr. admitted a vehicle driven by an undocumented foreign national at the Paso del Norte entry port in El Paso as part of human trafficking operations. Additionally, Pérez Jr. allegedly conspired to possess a substance containing at least 5 kilograms of cocaine from November 1, 2019, to February 5, 2025, inclusive, to distribute it in Texas, Louisiana, North Carolina, and other locations, according to official information. Pérez Jr. is charged with one count of conspiracy to bring foreign nationals to the United States for financial gain, three counts of bringing foreign nationals to the United States for financial gain, and one count of conspiracy to possess a controlled substance with the intent to distribute it. If found guilty, he faces a federal prison sentence of up to five years for the charge of conspiracy to smuggle people, three to ten years in prison for each of the three additional charges of human trafficking, and ten years to life in prison for the charge of drug trafficking. A federal district court judge will determine the sentence after considering the United States Sentencing Guidelines and other legal factors.

Everything is ready in Bolivia to arrest Evo Morales. The Bolivian police are waiting for the former president Evo Morales to leave his stronghold and political bunker in Cochabamba in order to execute the arrest order issued against him for the alleged crimes of sexual violence against minors and human trafficking. This was stated by the Minister of the Interior, Eduardo Del Castillo, who emphasized that the police have already received the operational order to proceed with the capture of the former head of state (2006-2019) but we are waiting for him to leave that region. Since the beginning of the investigation against him in October, Morales has been almost exclusively in the Cochabamba region, the political and trade union stronghold of the leader of the coca growers, where, according to the authorities, he lives protected by a tight network of security formed by members of the local rural community. The request for Morales' detention was issued by the preliminary hearing judge of the Tarija court after the former president ignored a second summons in January to appear before the magistrate to respond to charges against him. Morales is under investigation for an alleged intimate relationship with a 15-year-old activist from a youth movement with whom he had a daughter in 2016. The former president denounces the process against him as part of a conspiracy allegedly orchestrated by the current head of state and his former right-hand man, Luis Arce, to prevent him from running for a new presidential term.

Federal Agents Dismantle Human Trafficking Ring Eight Accused Tied to the Aragua Train The U.S. Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee announced the formal indictment of eight Venezuelan nationals allegedly linked to a human trafficking operation. The indictment alleges that the eight defendants worked together to recruit and transport women from Central and South America to the United States, specifically to Tennessee and other states, to operate a commercial sex business. Prosecutors claim that the defendants targeted young, poor, and vulnerable women from Venezuela and other countries. The indictment alleges that the defendants convinced the women that they would have a better life, but once in the United States, they forced the women to pay exorbitant travel costs by engaging in sex with strangers. I want to reiterate that human trafficking is a real issue here in our community, said U.S. Attorney Robert Maguire. Ignoring it won't make it disappear. We can't live in the shadows, we have to bring it to light and hold accountable those who commit crimes in the dark. Officials said this was the result of a years-long investigation into this operation with the help of multiple local, state and federal agencies. Leaders say the investigation began with the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department (MNPD) and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. The following people were formally charged: Yilibeth del Carmen RiveroDe Caldera (also known as Yibi) charged with conspiracy to transport across international borders for prostitution, conspiracy to travel in or out of the country or transportation in aid of racketeering enterprises, human trafficking conspiracy Kléiver Daniel Mota Rivero, also known as Kléiber, charged with conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution, conspiracy to facilitate or aid in travel within or outside the country in support of organized crime enterprises, conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, and possession of a firearm by an undocumented alien. Yuribetzi del Valle Gómez Machuca, also known as La Gorda, charged with conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution, conspiracy to facilitate or aid in travel within or outside the country in support of organized crime enterprises, and conspiracy to commit sex trafficking.Wilmarys del Valle Manzano Solórzano, also known as La China, charged with conspiracy to transport individuals across international borders for purposes of prostitution and conspiracy to facilitate or aid in travel within or outside the country in support of organized crime enterprises. Andrik Alexander Morales Rivero (also known as Endri), accused of conspiring to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiring to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to assist organized crime enterprises. Ariannys Beatriz GutierrezCarrillo (also known as Nani, Nany), accused of conspiring to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiring to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to assist organized crime enterprises. Frankyanna del Valle RomeroRivero (also known as Franya), accused of conspiring to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiring to facilitate travel within and outside the country or to assist organized crime enterprises. Jesus Enrique Castillo Rodriguez, also known as Chu Chu, is accused of conspiring to transport individuals across international borders for the purpose of prostitution and conspiring to travel within and outside the country or transport in aid of organized crime businesses. The indictment alleges that those involved used hotels in the Nashville area to lure clients to locations where they would coerce victims into engaging in sexual favors. According to judicial documents, they used online advertising and messaging services such as WhatsApp to determine prices based on certain sexual favors. Prosecutors claim that Yibi and Kléiber used their connections with the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua to intimidate victims into continuing to participate in commercial sex acts. We rely on the community to make a difference in the lives of the most vulnerable women and girls who have been separated from their families under false pretenses and forced into the worst imaginable hell, Maguire said. Several law enforcement representatives from various agencies spoke at a press conference on Tuesday, condemning human trafficking and urging community members to remain vigilant. Human trafficking is abhorrent to all of us, said MNPD Chief John Drake. It is a modern form of slavery. I want to be clear that our police department will always prioritize human trafficking investigations, regardless of where a suspect is located. Maguire said they were focused on prosecuting defendants here in Nashville before deportation was discussed. Specifically, the message that authorities are sending with this indictment is that human trafficking is an abomination, Maguire added. We will find it wherever and whenever it exists. We will recover the survivors and put an end to it once and for all. Maguire says that the dozens of victims in this case will receive victim support services, likely through local and state organizations. The eight defendants are in federal custody awaiting prosecution. They were arrested in various states, including Tennessee and Texas. data.text: (Fotos) Massage Rooms What the OIJ Seized Victims Were Forced to Pay Fines if They Refused Demands The Judicial Investigation Body (OIJ) detailed what was seized during the raids on massage rooms, resulting in a total of 6 people being detained. According to the authorities, 12 mobile phones, 1 hard drive, 4 vehicles, 3 computers, 5 recorders, 2 tablets, and various documents related to the investigation were seized. Approximately $1 million in cash was also found. In addition, during the operations, 15 women who were victims were identified. According to the OIJ director, Randall Zúñiga, these women were hired to offer massage services, and if they refused, they were forced to pay a fine. Authorities detained 6 individuals: Morales, 32 years old (apparent leader of the gang), Godínez, 29 years old (female), Ureña, 29 years old (female), Vargas, 19 years old (female), Barboza, 28 years old (female), and Picado, 39 years old (female). The incidents allegedly took place from September 2021 in various locations across the country, including Pavas, Curridabat, Barrio Escalante, Rohrmoser, and Los Yoses. New York, United States. The American rapper Sean Combs, known as Diddy, filed a defamation lawsuit yesterday against NBC Universal and the production company Ample for a documentary that links him to the death of his ex-partner Kim Porter, certified as natural death, and portrays him as a serial killer. The lawsuit, which claims $100 million in compensation, argues that the documentary Diddy The Making of a Bad Boy (Diddy the Creation of a Bad Boy) insinuates that the artist committed a series of murders, among other heinous crimes, as reported by Page Six on Wednesday. (The documentary) maliciously and unfoundedly concludes that Mr. Combs is a monster and the embodiment of Lucifer with many similarities to Jeffrey Epstein, say Combs' lawyers, who consider his reputation, finances, and right to a fair trial to be damaged. Sean "Diddy", 55 years old, and who remains incarcerated in a New York prison, will face trial on May 5 for federal charges of organized crime, sex trafficking, and transporting prostitutes, of which he has pleaded not guilty, and has been the subject of dozens of abuse complaints in recent months. The documentary, which aired on NBC in January and is available on the Peacock streaming platform, analyzes the charges against Diddy and includes an interview in which he is linked to the death of Kim Porter, his ex-partner and mother of several of his children, who died of pneumonia in 2018. The aforementioned interview was with Porter's ex-husband, Al B. Sure, who questions Porter's death certificate and presents a conspiracy theory in which Diddy was responsible for the deaths of rapper Notorious B.I.G., murdered, or record executive Andre Harrell and rapper Heavy D, who died of health problems. The audiovisual document also records complaints that Diddy sexually abused minors, based on a civil lawsuit from a person who allegedly saw him with two underage girls, and the artist's lawyers claim that the two women have been discredited, saying they were of legal age at the time.

The Bolivian justice system issued a new arrest order today against former President (2006-2019) Evo Morales for human trafficking and statutory rape charges, after his appeal was rejected by the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court (south). The order, signed by Judge Nelson Rocabado, instructs the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime to carry out the apprehension, given that on January 27, the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court declared the appeal as inadmissible, warning that the issued resolution does not admit subsequent appeal. The former head of state is investigated by the Tarija Prosecution for his relationship in 2016 with Cindy Saraí, who was a minor at the time, and from whom a daughter was born. In line with this, the Attorney General of the State, Roger Mariaca, reaffirmed that after the rejection of the appeal, the arrest order is reinstated and must be executed by the Police, and a prosecutor may intervene in case a search is required. On January 17, after Morales failed to appear for the second time to testify, he was declared in contempt of court, thus confirming the existing arrest order since October 2022, and his bank accounts and assets were frozen. The former president is barricaded in his stronghold in the Chapare, Cochabamba department (center), his political stronghold, where he is supported by hundreds of coca growers who have warned of a possible social convulsion in case of his detention. In response to this, the Minister of Government, Carlos Eduardo del Castillo, stated on Monday that the operation order is ready to apprehend them, but we are waiting for the precise moment and location to execute it without generating confrontations and avoiding the loss of human lives.

The former Undersecretary of the Interior, accused of sexual abuse and rape, requested this permit to recover his blocked Unique Key, and the judge in the case approved the request on January 27 last year. The National Association of Non-Commissioned Officers of the Gendarmerie (Ansog) expressed its rejection of the judicial authorization granted to Manuel Monsalve, to use a computer and receive a visit from a public notary while serving preventive detention in the Capitán Yáber Penitentiary Annex. The former Undersecretary of the Interior, accused of sexual abuse and rape, requested this permit to recover his blocked Unique Key, and the judge in the case approved the request on January 27 last year. Ansog argues that this authorization could establish a dangerous precedent, allowing other inmates to request similar permits and putting the prison regime at risk. Additionally, the organization questions the justification for computer access, recalling that the Gendarmerie coordinates with the Civil Registry to enable inmates to conduct administrative procedures without the need for electronic devices. The Ansog also calls on authorities to review the benefits granted to Monsalve and evaluate the measure taken, ensuring that the established procedures in the Penitentiary Establishments Regulation are met. Finally, it calls on authorities to verify and evaluate the criteria and responsibility in granting permits, highlighting concern over the possible implications of this authorization.

The National Court has sentenced the Sevillian Manuel Gerardo Blanco Vela to nine years in prison for sexual aggression crimes committed against three American young students as the responsible for the company Discover Excursions, when the same students studied at the universities of Salamanca and Valencia and participated in the trips promoted by the company to Morocco and Portugal in 2013 and 2017, according to the sentence issued by the court last Monday, January 10. In their sentence, the magistrates of the First Section of the Penal Chamber of the National Court impose on the accused, identified as Manuel Blanco Vela, a sentence of six years in prison for a crime of aggression with the mitigating circumstance of undue delays in relation to the initial complainant of the case, the Moroccan victim, and two sentences of one and a half years in prison for two sexual aggression crimes regarding the remaining two complainants, for the events that occurred in Lagos (Portugal). In addition, it imposes a prohibition on him from working as a tour guide for seven and a half years and condemns him to compensate the girl who suffered the sexual assault in Morocco with 40.00 euros and 1,500 euros to each of the other two victims, despite acknowledging that it is not possible to automatically translate moral damages into money and that the only thing we can do is to value the importance of the harm in consideration of the victims' circumstances and try to convert this estimate into a specific monetary amount. The sentence is thus confined to the main outlines of the Public Prosecutor's Office's request, which had demanded nine years in prison for the accused for a presumed sex crime, rape, and two alleged sex abuse crimes, currently three sex crimes of different typification as well as six years of prohibition from approaching the first victim or communicating with her, one year of the same prohibition with regard to each of the two subsequent victims and eight years of disqualification from the profession of tourist guide and that compensates with 40,000 euros to the first victim and with 1,500 euros to each of the two subsequent ones. The private accusation, on the other hand, requested a total of 23 years in prison, as well as a compensation of 600,000 euros for the first young woman and 150,000 euros each of the two following ones while the defense had requested his acquittal.

The trial scheduled to start today has been suspended due to a police abuse in Stroeder. Immediately The trial that was supposed to start today to examine the behavior of a man accused of abusing his 4-year-old daughter in a case that mobilized the town of Stroeder, has been suspended and will have to be rescheduled. It is that the Criminal Court N° 1 (under the control of Judge Christian Yesari) was unable to form the jury, which must be composed of 18 people (12 regular members and 6 substitutes, in equal parts in terms of men and women). As a result, the trial will have to be rescheduled and the date has not yet been defined because the parties have to coordinate their agendas.According to the case, investigated by UFIJ N° 14, currently under the charge of prosecutor Marcelo Romero Jardín, the incidents occurred between April and August 2021, when the victim was visiting her father's house and under his care. The complaint was filed by the minor's mother, who took her to the hospital for treatment after detecting injuries that raised suspicions of possible sexual abuse. The accused is charged with the aggravated crime of sexual abuse, given that it was committed by a family member. SOURCE La Nueva Te may be interested

Table of ContentsState Representative Héctor Suárez Basurto (Morena) presented an initiative to reform the Guerrero Penal Code with the goal of expanding and refining the definition of femicide, incorporating aggravating factors such as the perpetrator's previous violence, threats in various contexts, sexual exploitation, or the victim's disappearance. The proposal aims to strengthen protection measures for women and ensure an effective response to reports of gender-based violence. During his intervention in Congress, Suárez Basurto emphasized that femicide is the most extreme form of violence against women and a reflection of the brutality they face. He cited data from the National Census of State Justice Prosecution, which recorded 966 femicide victims in 2023, evidencing a concerning increase in this crime in Mexico. In Guerrero, the first days of 2025 have witnessed impactful cases, such as that of Leuteria Reyes Benito, a traffic official in Alcozauca, who was stabbed over 30 times by her ex-partner. Despite previously reporting the violence she suffered, she did not receive adequate protection from the authorities, who classified her case as domestic violence. The initiative proposes modifying Article 135 of the Guerrero Penal Code to include conditions and aggravating factors that allow for a more precise classification of femicide. Among these are: Prior violence by the aggressor. Threats in the public, digital, or political sphere. Sexual exploitation. Disappearance of the victim. Additionally, it is established that all violent deaths of women, girls, or adolescents must be investigated as possible femicides, in order to avoid impunity and guarantee justice. Suárez Basurto recalled that femicide is codified in the Federal Penal Code and in state legislations, and that Mexico has signed international treaties to protect women's rights. However, he pointed out that the lack of an effective regulatory framework and inconsistency in definitions between states hinders the application of laws. It is urgent to strengthen protection and support measures for women, and to ensure that reports of violence are effectively addressed by the Prosecutors' Offices, the legislator stated.

The Central Directorate of Investigation (DICRIM) of the National Police conducted a wide operation in the last 24 hours, resulting in the arrest of more than 50 people in different locations across the country for the commission of various crimes, including robbery, physical aggression, child abuse, attempted armed assault, threat of death, and other crimes. Among those arrested is Miguelito Bello, who was detained in the Duvergé region for physically assaulting his romantic partner, causing a contused trauma on the forehead, according to a medical diagnosis. Additionally, in the Polo community, Barahona province, Delys Féliz Jiménez (also known as Denis Negrito) was apprehended by court order, accused of stabbing another woman with a knife due to jealousy. In another incident, Saymor Pascal Heredia Medrano, 22 years old, was detained for causing fractures and severe injuries to a citizen during a brawl that occurred in October 2023. While in another case, 34-year-old William Bladimir Mena Hernández was arrested on a judicial order after being accused of stealing a phone from an 8-year-old child and attacking the complainant with a machete when he demanded it back. Additionally, Elidionio Asencio Amado was apprehended in flagrante delito while attempting to commit a robbery in a public area, carrying two machetes and a screwdriver. On the other hand, a 17-year-old teenager from the Jarro Sucio sector in Barahona was caught with an artisanal firearm (Chilean-made) on his belt. In San Cristóbal, Dauri Francisco Andújar (alias El Guachi) was detained after threatening a woman due to a labor-related debt. Meanwhile, in Azua, 31-year-old Ramón Feliz was arrested on a judicial order, accused of sexual abuse against an 8-year-old minor in the La Bombita sector. The authorities also reported the arrest of other citizens in San Juan de la Maguana, Pedernales, Haina, Santiago, the National District, and other locations, as part of the efforts of the National Police to strengthen citizen security and bring to justice those who break the law.

The Municipal Intendant Baltasar Lara Gros welcomed the speakers from the Ministry of Security of the Nation, at the Second Update Seminar on early detection of human trafficking and trade in border areas, within the framework of the EUROFRONT Program. This took place yesterday, Tuesday, February 11, at Casa del Bicentenario. The first session, Espacio SeguroPresentation Protocol, was held on Monday, February 10, in Aguas Blancas. One of the scourges weighing on girls, boys, adolescents, and women is human trafficking, a multi-million dollar business. It consists of the recruitment, transportation, and delivery for exploitation, whether labor, sexual slavery, sale of tissues and organs, and other forms of exploitation. A delicate and contentious issue that must call our attention to awaken awareness and reflection on this and other prevention topics. Among the authorities present were Juan Capella, General Director of Migratory Movements of the National Directorate of Migrations, Gabriel Fernández, head of operations of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and Marcelo Romero, Secretary of Criminal Investigation of the National Security Ministry.

The victim managed to ask for help after a week of captivity. By Silvana Cuéllar, Fuente Red Uno Bolivia. A 20-year-old man was apprehended in Peru, accused of kidnapping and abusing an 18-year-old Bolivian woman. The victim, who had met the perpetrator through social media, traveled to Trujillo, Peru, with the hope of establishing a romantic relationship. However, upon her arrival, the man forcibly detained her against her will in a property for a week, subjecting her to sexual abuse. The captor, who used a false profile to gain the trust of the young woman, convinced her to travel to Peru under false promises of love. After being held captive and subjected to harassment, the young woman managed to ask for help when the perpetrator neglected her phone. This allowed Peruvian authorities to locate and rescue the victim. Attorney Cristian Sánchez warned about the dangers of interacting with strangers on social media, emphasizing the importance of proper digital education. The man was detained by Peruvian police and faces charges of kidnapping, torture, and sexual abuse.

Renovación Nacional Suspends Membership of Congressman Jorge Durán Following Sexual Abuse Allegations What Happened The Supreme Court of Renovación Nacional (RN) decided on Wednesday to suspend the membership of Congressman Jorge Durán after he was accused of sexual abuse by his ex-partner, who filed a complaint with Carabineros for a suspected crime that allegedly occurred last Saturday. Given the gravity of the case, the RN tribunal decided to initiate a disciplinary proceeding against Durán, granting him a maximum of 10 days to respond. The ruling issued states that a provisional measure will be adopted, suspending the rights of the affiliated member during the processing of the case. No Voluntary Suspension of Membership Exists In parallel, Durán's request to suspend his membership was rejected, as there is no provision for voluntary suspension of membership in the internal regulations or applicable legislation. . THE LATEST The resolution instructs the General Secretary to notify the Political Commission, the RN Deputy Bench, and all instances where Durán participates as an affiliate. In the court's communication, it is reported that disciplinary proceedings will be initiated and measures will be determined based on the investigation's results. Complaint If you are a victim or witness of violence against women, the orientation hotline set up by the National Women's Service and Gender Equity (SernamEG) is 1455. The number can be dialed from a fixed or mobile phone, and from there, they provide guidance to help victims of abuse or guide you on how to file a complaint. This article reports on an ongoing judicial process, and the parties involved should not be considered guilty until the relevant authorities determine otherwise. Read more

The Attorney General's Office of the State (FGE) reported that with the presentation of the DNA evidence, the anticipated testimony of the victim, and other probative elements, the Public Ministry demonstrated Eduardo Nicanor T.'s authorship in the rape committed against a 65-year-old woman. The Penal Court of this jurisdiction declared the accused guilty and sentenced him to nineteen years of deprivation of liberty. On the morning of September 27, 2023, according to the Attorney General's Office, the victim left her residence and headed to the farm of her property in the General Proaño parish of the Morona canton. While performing agricultural work, she was surprised by Eduardo Nicanor T., 38 years old, who had his face covered with a t-shirt and was holding a machete. The aggressor threatened the woman with the white weapon, robbed her of a purse, and raped her sexually, according to the Public Ministry. That same day, the victim reported the incident to ECU 911. The agents took her to the Prosecutor's Office, where proceedings were initiated, including the medical-legal examination, which included taking samples from the victim's body and their clothing, through swabbing. The DNA test scientifically proved that Eduardo Nicanor T. is responsible for the sexual assault, as his genetic profile was found in the samples collected from the victim's underwear. The experts who prepared these reports testified at the trial hearing. In addition, the Prosecutor presented the woman's anticipated testimony and the testimonies of the expert who performed the psychological evaluation and the police officers who took the procedure and conducted investigative proceedings. According to the judicial resolution signed and issued on January 27, the First Penal Chamber of the Departmental Court of Justice of Tarija declares the incidental appeal filed by the private lawyer of Juan Evo Morales Ayma inadmissible. After the rejection of the appeal by the Tribunal, the judge Alberto Rocabado now ratified the capture order against the former Bolivian head of state. He is being investigated for aggravated human trafficking, in which he is accused of having maintained a relationship with a minor with whom he allegedly had a child in 2016 in Tarija, while he occupied the presidency of the Andean country. In turn, in the judicial resolution, Morales was declared in contempt of court for not appearing at two precautionary hearings before the judge. The impugned resolution, being a declaration of contempt, is not susceptible to further appeal. This is because contempt is considered a direct consequence of the defendant's procedural attitude, who does not appear at the judicial summons without a valid justification, the ruling states. Now, from the government of Luis Arce, they ask the former president to surrender to Justice, and even the Minister of the Interior, Eduardo del Castillo, stated that the Police already have an operational order and they expect the accused to come out of the Chapare locality, his political and union stronghold, where he has been since November 2024, protected by hundreds of coca growers and militant peasants. On his part, the former president declared himself a victim of the Executive, which would have as its goal, according to Morales himself, to prevent him from being enabled as a presidential candidate for the general elections on August 17. In turn, the leader of the Movement for Socialism (MAS) recently stated that if there is no victim, there is no crime, making reference to the woman with whom he supposedly had a relationship when she was a minor. In the locality of Tarija, there are also seven other complaints against the former president for alleged abuses against minors. In October, the Prosecutor's Office had already issued an arrest warrant against Morales, but his followers blocked roads for 24 days to prevent his apprehension. Additionally, the Justice prohibited him from leaving the country and ordered the preventive annotation of his assets and the freezing of his bank accounts. Meanwhile, followers of the former president warned that they are conducting permanent vigils in various localities of the Cochabamba tropics and that they will even dig wells to prevent the landing of planes or helicopters in the area. This judicial process is another chapter in the tense relationship between Morales and the current president of Bolivia, Luis Arce (also from MAS), due to differences in state administration and party control. Luis Arce Evo Morales.jpg Evo Morales and the current president of Bolivia, Luis Arce, have been distant since 2021 due to differences in state administration and party control. The case against Evo Morales Evo Morales, who was already prevented from participating in the next elections, was accused of committing the crimes of human trafficking and statutory rape with a minor, with whom he allegedly had a child, whose birth certificate in the locality of Yacuiba would represent the main proof. This would have happened in 2016 when the leader was President and the teenager was 15 years old. Additionally, in the process, it is stated that the victim's parents profited from her by handing her over to the former president in exchange for favors. The victim's father is currently in prison with preventive detention, and her mother was declared in rebellion after failing to attend the Tuesday hearing to which she was summoned. In this context, the former head of state targeted Luis Arce, the current president, and assured that this is a case of persecution and an attempt at political proscription in the face of the 2025 elections. It is a black plan to eliminate me politically and physically to take me out of the electoral race, he said. At the moment, he did not speak of the formal indictment nor of the arrest order for the case of alleged abuse of a minor who became pregnant.

Members of the Peace Construction Coordination Table expressed their support for the actions taken as part of Operation Atarraya, as part of the research work conducted by federal and state authorities in the areas of security and justice administration in the State of Mexico. The exchange of information within this mechanism, headed by Governor Delfina Gómez Álvarez, indicates that the seized properties, located in 20 municipalities, had prior investigation files prior to the operations conducted. From January 1, 2022, to February 6, 2025, the State of Mexico's Attorney General's Office and other federal and state institutions registered 1,337 criminal incidents at establishments like barbershops, related to crimes such as homicide, femicide, kidnapping, disappearance, human trafficking, and deprivation of liberty as well as sexual violence, abuse, harassment, and assault, and complaints for crimes against health. Regarding the allegations made on social media about the cultivation of drugs, on Friday, February 7, the Mexican state's Attorney General's Office initiated an investigation ex officio to determine the corresponding responsibilities. Additionally, as a precautionary measure, the Agent of the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Commander of the Investigation Police responsible for the diligence practiced at the Santiago Miltepec delegation in Toluca municipality were removed from their positions. Operation Atarraya began on December 13 with the objective of intervening establishments used by criminal groups for illicit activities such as extortion, human trafficking, or the consumption and trafficking of narcotics. It is carried out with the joint participation of authorities from the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection, the National Guard, the Secretariat of National Defense, as well as the state Security Secretariat and the Justice Prosecutor's Office of the State of Mexico.

In the framework of commemorative activities for a new anniversary of Marita Verón's disappearance, the vice governor, Miguel Acevedo, received Susana Trimarco, president of the foundation bearing her daughter's name. The meeting took place at the Provincial Legislature. There, details were defined on a series of talks that will be held on April 3rd. The objective is to raise awareness and sensitize about the fight against human trafficking. Following the meeting, Trimarco expressed: For me, it's always a pleasure to speak with the Vice Governor, since he's a person who has always collaborated with the foundation and supported our work. April 3rd is approaching, and 22 years have passed since Marita's kidnapping and disappearance. We all do different activities every year to remember her and to promote and disseminate the crime of human trafficking. We're going to organize a talk for different state agencies, right here at the Legislature, she informed. The URL emphasized the importance of continuing to talk about topics such as domestic violence, gender violence, and, particularly, human trafficking. They also considered these problems to be a daily reality that is faced every day at the foundation, where the suffering of the victims is confronted. Now, the government of this province has stepped up the pace and is doing an important, impeccable job on the topic of narco-trafficking that is closely tied to human trafficking, they highlighted.

Sean Combs, conocido como Diddy, demandó a NBCUniversal y a la productora Ample por difamación por un documental que lo vincula con la muerte de su expareja Kim Porter, cuya causa de muerte fue certificada como fallecimiento natural. La demanda, que reclama una compensación de 100 millones de dólares, argumenta que el documental "Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy" insinúa que el artista cometió asesinatos en serie y otros crímenes atroces. El documental llega a una conclusión maliciosa e infundada de que el Sr. Combs es un asesino en serie. Diddy is a monster and the embodiment of Lucifer with many similarities to Jeffrey Epstein, indicate the rapper's lawyers, who consider his reputation, finances, and right to a fair trial damaged. Diddy, 55 years old and currently imprisoned in a New York jail, will face a trial on May 5 for federal charges of organized crime, sex trafficking, and transporting individuals for prostitution, of which he has pleaded not guilty, and has been the subject of dozens of abuse allegations in recent months. The documentary, which aired on NBC in January and is available on the streaming platform Peacock, examines the charges against Diddy and includes an interview in which he is linked to the death of Kim Porter, his ex-partner and mother of several of his children, who died of pneumonia in 2018. The aforementioned interview was with Porter's ex-husband, Al B. Someone who questions the forensic certificate of the woman and presents a conspiratorial theory in which Diddy is responsible for the deaths of rapper Notorious B.I.G., murdered, or of music executive Andre Harrell and rapper Heavy D, who died from health problems. The audiovisual document also records accusations that Diddy sexually abused minors, based on a civil lawsuit from a person who supposedly saw him with two underage girls, and that Diddy's lawyers claim have been discredited by the two women, who said they were of legal age at the time.

data.text: The children of Haiti continue to be victims of the violence perpetrated by gangs that, since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse on July 7, 2021, are fighting for territorial control, according to a report presented by Amnesty International on Wednesday. It is estimated that more than one million children live in areas controlled or influenced by armed gangs in Haiti, the document says. Amnesty International found, among other things, that 18 girls were raped or suffered sexual violence at the hands of gang members. Two of the victims were kidnapped while returning from school to their homes and abused in groups. I think about it and I tell myself, I'm just a girl, why did this happen to me, a minor told Amnesty International. The girls are also victims of sexual exploitation, as reported by another of them, 16 years old, who lives in an area controlled by the 5 Segon gang. I have no choice, they see you and tell you to come. If you refuse, they hit you with a gun. One day you could receive a gunshot. They grab you and hit you. Some pay, others don't, he said. Another problem that Amnesty International highlighted is that gangs are recruiting minors to spy on rival gangs and the police, as well as to make illegal deliveries, perform construction work, repair vehicles, and do domestic chores. During their fieldwork in Puerto Príncipe, Amnesty International documented that 10 children were injured and two lost their lives in raids carried out in neighborhoods by gangs. The situation is even worse for minors with disabilities, as fleeing gangs have had to give up their assistive devices and arrive at shelters that are physically inaccessible to them.

A 100-Year Prison Sentence Handed Down to Edmund Davis, Identified as Boyfriend of Alicia Navarro of Glendale, ArizonaThe authorities have handed down a 100-year prison sentence to Edmund Davis, a man from Montana who admitted to being the boyfriend of 14-year-old Alicia Navarro from Glendale, who went missing for four years. This is the maximum sentence allowed for the charge of child sexual abuse. In addition to serving 100 years in prison, Edmund Davis is not eligible for parole for 25 years. Fifty years of his sentence were suspended in October 2024, after he pleaded guilty to a charge of child sexual abuse, according to the Montana Department of Justice. Police obtained a search warrant after Alicia presented herself at the police department in July 2023 to request that she be removed from the list of missing persons, as she had turned 18 and wished to start her life as an adult. Following a search in his apartment in the city of Havre, authorities found on Edmund Davis's cell phone diverse material of child sexual abuse. Disturbing details in the case of Edmund Davis, linked to the case of Alicia Navarro. The authorities' review of the content of the cell phone, which the subject attempted to delete, found that the people depicted were minors under 13 years old, with two images of children under 5 years old, including images of babies and young children, and other computer-generated or animated content that showed children being sexualized, as specified in a statement from the state Department of Justice. Edmund Davis has not yet been charged in connection with Navarro's disappearance. It is worth noting that Alicia Navarro, diagnosed with autism, disappeared on September 15, 2019, just before turning 15 years old, from her family home in Glendale. After her disappearance, Jessica Nuñez, Navarro's mother, found a note on her daughter's desk that said "I escaped. I'll be back. I promise. I'm sorry." Alicia had been living with Edmund Davis, who was identified as her boyfriend, for a time until July 2023, when he presented himself at the Police Department. There is no clarity on how long the two were together or where Navarro may have been during the time she was missing.

Mexico City. Rapper Sean Diddy Combs filed a $100 million lawsuit against the creators of a recent revealing documentary about him, produced by NBC. The music mogul and producer, currently incarcerated in New York awaiting a federal trial for sex trafficking and extortion charges, claims that Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy is filled with lies and defamations. According to Page Six, this Wednesday, Diddy's lawyer revealed that the lawsuit is directed at NBC television network, its streaming service Peacock, and production company Ample. Legal documents state that the documentary supposedly includes false statements about the rapper. The documentary's premise allegedly assumes that Combs has committed numerous heinous crimes, including serial murder, child molestation, and child sex trafficking, as read in the lawsuit. The program maliciously and without basis jumps to the conclusion that Combs is a monster, and includes statements that the creators knew were false or were published without regard to whether they were true or not. As compensation, Diddy demands $100 million in damages for the damage to his reputation and economy that the documentary is causing him at the moment. The documents claim that the program falsely, imprudently, and maliciously accuses Combs of murdering people in his entourage, including his ex-partner Kim Porter and rapper Christopher Wallace, known as Biggie Smalls and The Notorious BIG. Combs' lawyer, Erica Wolff, stated in a press release that NBC, Peacock, and Ample made a conscious decision to line their pockets at the expense of truth, decency, and basic standards of professional journalism, and that they maliciously and imprudently disseminated scandalous lies. Diddy Faces Lawsuit After String of Accusations. This lawsuit against Diddy comes after a series of allegations against the controversial singer, both from men and women, with currently more than 30 civil lawsuits pending against him. The actor, also, has been accused of kidnapping, drugging, and forcing men and women to engage in sexual relations, sometimes using firearms and threats of violence. He is also accused of assaulting and raping multiple people, including minors. Combs has consistently denied the allegations, calling them repugnant, while declaring himself innocent of all criminal charges.
