data.text: Maritime Contraband Interception off the Coast of FloridaFebruary 11, 2025, the Aerial and Maritime Operations (AMO), an operational unit of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office, successfully intercepted a maritime smuggling attempt off the coast of Florida. This operation resulted in the arrest of 13 individuals attempting to enter the country illegally.The intervention was part of ongoing efforts to combat illicit trafficking and ensure border security. Authorities reported that the operation was carried out successfully, thus preventing a significant violation of U.S. immigration laws.Against Illicit TraffickingAgents involved in this operation highlighted the importance of teamwork and coordination between different agencies to carry out these missions. Thank you to your prompt response, this human trafficking network was successfully dismantled before it could achieve its goal. Air and maritime operations continue to be a fundamental pillar in the fight against human trafficking and other illicit activities in waters near the United States. The AMO reaffirms its commitment to protecting borders and national security.

Until the Menzuly neighborhood, in a rural area of the municipality of Piedecuesta, agents from the CTI of the Prosecutor's Office and police officers arrived to effect the capture of an 18-year-old young man, who was required by the First Criminal Court of Mobile Guarantees of Bucaramanga. He is accused of committing a series of sexual abuses against three minors under the age of 13, who at the time of the incidents were between 13 and 14 years old. Apparently, he contacted them through social media. He sexually abused three girls by taking advantage of the fact that they had mutual friends and moved in the same social circle. He contacted them through social media, such as Instagram, and proceeded to harass them to meet in person, revealed the Prosecutor's Office after its investigation. When they agreed, the accused picked them up in his vehicle and took them to isolated locations. There, he allegedly subjected them to sexual relations. The parents of the victims, upon learning of the events, decided to file the corresponding criminal complaint with the prosecuting authority. In this way, evidence was gathered against the accused man, resulting in his arrest. The 18-year-old youth was placed at the disposal of the First Specialized Unit for Children, Girls, and Adolescents of Bucaramanga. He must respond to the charge of violent sexual intercourse and aggravated sexual intercourse with a minor under 14 years old. This way, you can report cases of sexual abuse in Bucaramanga. In Bucaramanga, there are several specialized services that can provide comprehensive support (medical, psychological, and legal) for victims of sexual abuse. The authorities have different lines of attention to report cases of sexual aggression or any type of violence based on gender. You can find the phone numbers 123 of the Police, 122 of the Prosecutor's Office, 141 of the ICBF, and the line 155. The Attorney General's Office also has the email address denunciaanonimafiscalia.gov.co for anonymous denunciations.

Raúl Asencio, a Real Madrid player, remains an accused in the case of child pornography distribution. The Spanish defender played in the Champions League yesterday against Manchester City and learned that the investigation against him is still ongoing. After giving one of his best performances wearing the Real Madrid jersey, Raúl Asencio found out that his appeal in the case of child pornography distribution, in which he has been an accused since 2023, was rejected, and the investigation is still ongoing in search of a resolution by a court. The Real Madrid youth player, along with other players who are part of the youth teams, were accused a couple of years ago of distributing sexual videos of two girls in Las Palmas, one of whom was a minor, which is classified as an aggravating factor in the crime. According to ESPN, a few weeks ago, Asencio and his legal team had filed an appeal before the High Court of Justice of the Canary Islands with the intention of dismissing the case, however, this was rejected and the defendant's indictment remains, at least for now. The sexual relations, according to the same source that recovered the complaint from one of the involved women, were consensual, however, the recording and subsequent dissemination of the video were not. If he is declared guilty, Asencio could be eligible for a sentence of between one and five years, according to Spanish law. The case has transcended in a media sense due to the important role that Raúl has taken on in Real Madrid's first team this season. Who is Raúl Asencio Fundamental for Carlo Ancelotti, with injuries throughout the season such as those of Éder Militao, Antonio Rüdiger or David Alaba, Asencio was born in Las Palmas on February 13, 2003, he is 21 years old (22 tomorrow) and began his football career precisely in the Las Palmas team. After a few years in the Canary Islands team, Raúl Asencio became a player for La Fábrica and his opportunity with the first team arrived this season 2024 He largely assumed the position of central defender, as he did yesterday in the Champions League against Manchester City. Kevin Spacey Faces New Sexual Abuse Allegations. The American actor, known for films such as American Beauty and The Usual Suspects, is facing charges in the UK, marking his third court appearance for these reasons. What is Known About the New Lawsuit Against Kevin Spacey A civil lawsuit was filed against Kevin Spacey by an actor identified as Ruari Cannon, who accuses the actor of sexually assaulting him. The complaint was submitted to the High Court of London on February 12, a year after the actor was acquitted of the same charges in a criminal trial. The allegations also target the London theater known as Old Vic, where the actor held a significant role as artistic director between 2004 and 2015. Private but not Secret. The Romantic Detail of Kenia Os with Which Peso Pluma Brags About Their Romance VIDEO The law firm Fieldfisher, which defends the victim, did not disclose details about their client's allegations, but apparently, the allegations were revealed in the documentary Spacey Unmasked, in which Ruairi accused the actor of inappropriately touching him in London in 2013, when he was 21 and the man was 53 years old. In the same documentary, nine other men joined the allegations against the actor. As in the previous trial, the 65-year-old American actor denied all the allegations against him. Up to this point, neither the theater nor the actor has made an official statement, and no additional data has been published on the matter. Past Allegations Against Kevin Spacey It is worth mentioning that Kevin Spacey has been involved in allegations of abuse for years. The first occurred in 2017 by actor Anthony Rapp, who accused him of inappropriate sexual conduct. This led to the actor losing important papers in his career, including his role in House of Cards, which was completely removed from the Netflix series. In 2023, the actor was tried at the Southwark Crown Court in London for charges of sexual assault, involving 4 men in the UK. Ultimately, the jury acquitted him of all charges on the same day he celebrated his 64th birthday, although this marked him professionally and he has not been able to recover his place in the entertainment industry.

Port-au-Prince, 12 Feb (EFE). Amnesty International (AI) denounced on Wednesday that criminal gangs in Haiti are recruiting, attacking, and raping minors, within the framework of a growing crisis. According to a report from this organization, more than a million children and girls live in areas controlled by criminal gangs or under their influence. Criminal gangs have caused widespread anguish in Haiti, as they threaten, beat, rape, and kill children and girls, stated Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of the organization. Sexual Exploitation of Girls Members of the criminal gangs have kidnapped, raped, and sexually assaulted girls during attacks on neighborhoods or after taking control of areas, according to AI. The organization noted in its report that attacks against girls who go out onto the street are common, and they also deliberately attack them in their homes. Similarly, members of criminal gangs have sexually exploited girls in relationships and for commercial sex, Amnesty International added, documenting the cases of 18 minors who were raped and subjected to other forms of sexual violence by outlaw groups. Ten of them were subjected to gang rape, the report added, indicating that some became pregnant and several resorted to unsafe methods to try to interrupt the pregnancy because abortion is illegal in Haiti. Survivors face different obstacles to accessing justice, amidst the general impunity that plagues Haiti, where 5,626 people died in 2024 as a result of the actions of criminal gangs (1,000 more than the previous year), 2,213 were injured, and 1,494 were kidnapped. Many of the minors interviewed, the report added, did not intend to report the aggressions they suffered to the authorities due to the absence of police forces in areas controlled by criminal gangs. A girl who was kidnapped and raped by several members of a criminal gang in 2023 and was again sexually assaulted by a member of a criminal gang in 2024 told AI "There is no police. The only authority in the area are the gang members. If someone points me out, they could kill me." Amnesty International also interviewed 11 boys and 3 girls who were recruited and used by the criminal gangs. The minors described being exploited in various ways, including spying on rival gangs and police, making deliveries and domestic chores, performing construction work and repairing vehicles. The 14 minors said they had no choice and acted predominantly out of fear or hunger. The UN and civil society groups have documented the murder of minors and adults whom self-defense groups known as the Bwa Kale movement believed were associated with criminal gangs. Several minors said they tried to hide their association with gangs out of fear of reprisals from community members. A child said "If someone points a finger at me, they could kill me." In light of this situation, Amnesty International asked the international community, including donors, to work with Haitian authorities and civil society to design a roadmap aimed at introducing changes that would bring lasting solutions based on human rights, and prevent future cycles of violence. The Haitian government and international donors must collaborate to develop an all-encompassing and inclusive child protection plan, Callamard stated, also noting that the massive influx of firearms into Haiti must be controlled, allowing for the widespread abuses by criminal gangs. Countries must also cease forcibly deporting Haitians while the campaign of terror by criminal gangs and the broader human rights crisis continues, she concluded.

Bolivia Justice issued new arrest order against Evo Morales The former president is accused of human trafficking and rape. URL 2055 Justice issued new arrest order against Evo Morales Bolivia's Justice Department issued a new arrest order today against former President (2006-2019) Evo Morales for crimes of human trafficking and rape, after his appeal was rejected by the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court (south). The order, signed by Judge Nelson Rocabado, instructs the Special Force to Combat Crime to carry out the arrest, since on January 27, the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court declared the appeal request inadmissible, warning that the issued resolution does not admit a subsequent appeal. The former head of state is being investigated by the Tarija Prosecutor's Office for his relationship in 2016 with Cindy Saraí, who was a minor at the time, and with whom he had a daughter. Also to be seenThe audit of Non-Contributory Pensions for Work-Related Disability has begunIn line with this, the Attorney General of the State, Roger Mariaca, reiterated that after the rejection of the appeal, the arrest order is reinstated and must be executed by the Police, and a prosecutor may intervene in case a search is required. On January 17, after not appearing for a second time to testify, Morales was declared in contempt by the justice system, thereby confirming the existing arrest order since October 2022, and an order was issued to freeze his accounts and assets.The former president is barricaded in his stronghold in the Chapare region of Cochabamba (center), his political stronghold, where he has the support of hundreds of coca farmers who have warned of a possible social convulsion in case of his detention. In response to this, the Minister of Government, Carlos Eduardo del Castillo, stated on Monday that the operational order to carry out the apprehension is already ready, but they are waiting for the precise moment and location to execute it without generating confrontations and avoiding the loss of human lives.

Twenty-four years after the sexual abuse and murder of Natalia Melmann in Miramar, the investigation that has already led to two oral trials with four former police officers sentenced to life imprisonment, prosecutor Ana María Caro requested the DNA analysis of a fifth suspect, in search of finding compatibility with the fifth and last sample of genetic material stored in the case. According to La Capital newspaper, weeks ago Caro asked the Appeals and Guarantees Chamber to authorize the blood extraction of the 110 people who worked in the different police departments of Miramar in February 2001, when the incident occurred. Of the total, the Chamber only allowed the procedure to be carried out on a particular suspect. It is a 60-year-old man who is currently retired from the force. After locating his whereabouts in a Trenque Lauquen field, Justice summoned him to Mar del Plata to carry out the procedure. The same took place at the Expert Advisory (the Scientific Police cannot intervene in the case due to officials from the same force being implicated) during the January judicial fair. Now, this man's DNA will have to be matched with the genetic sample that has been kept safe since the start of the case. Natalia Melmann's crime is committed by four convicted former police officers. The first three, Oscar Echenique (63), Ricardo Anselmini (55), and Ricardo Suárez (60), were tried and sentenced to life imprisonment in September 2002. During the oral debate, a new lead emerged about a fourth police officer implicated and an investigation was ordered first, followed by a second trial. The deadlines were extended, and it was not until 2023, more than 22 years after the crime, that the fourth former police officer, Ricardo Panadero, was sentenced by the Oral Court No. 4. To reach a clarification of the case, a key element emerged during the Penal Preparatory Instruction (IPP). Five genetic material samples belonging to the suspected perpetrators were collected. Four of them were matched and indicated a high probability of compatibility with the convicted individuals. The fifth, on the other hand, was never known to correspond to anyone, but was kept on hold, and it was after the Panadero trial that prosecutor Caro decided to go to the bottom of the matter and requested the Justice to match it with the totality of the police officers serving in Miramar in February 2001. The Court denied that measure, but authorized the blood extraction of one of them, who at that time lived or spent most of his time in a kind of unnumbered building and appeared abandoned, where parties were held to which, according to the investigation, police officers took young women. According to La Capital, now prosecutor Caro awaits the results of the forensic analysis to determine if the genetic sample stored is indeed compatible with the DNA of the fifth suspect. If not, she would insist on having 109 blood extractions carried out to eliminate any impunity in the case and dispel all doubts about the identity of the remaining perpetrator of the crime.The Natalia Melmann CrimeThe Natalia Melmann crime, recalls La Capital, occurred on February 4, 2001, and, as established in the 2002 trial, the victim was forced to get into a police truck and taken to a house on the southernmost part of Miramar, where she was sexually assaulted and then, with the unmistakable purpose of procuring the impunity of the sexual assault, was strangled with a cord from her sneakers. Her body was found buried in the Florentino Ameghino nursery four days later.

data.text: A federal court in Tennessee has charged eight Venezuelans with allegedly participating in a sex trafficking ring that transported women from Central and South America to the United States. According to the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee, the suspects deceived vulnerable women with promises of legitimate employment, but upon arrival in the country, they forced them to engage in sexual acts under threat. Among those charged are a father and his adult sons, as well as two married couples, reported WKRN, a Nashville, Tennessee television station. The indictment alleges that the suspects recruited their victims, paid for their travel, and once in the United States, inflated a supposed debt that they were forced to settle through sexual exploitation. Modus operandi and ties with the Aragua Train The judicial documents indicate, according to the medium, that the suspects sent money through Western Union and MoneyGram to cover the transportation of women. Upon arrival, they posted online ads and used WhatsApp to negotiate tariffs for sexual encounters. The victims were transported to hotels in Nashville, where they were forced to engage in prostitution. The accusation also states that some women continued to be exploited even after paying off their supposed debt. They received threats against their families, warnings of deportation, and retention of their identification documents to keep them under control. Two of the main suspects, Yilibeth del Carmen Rivero and Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero, allegedly maintained ties with the criminal organization known as the Aragua Train, notorious for its involvement in human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Eight Venezuelans accused of participating in a human sex trafficking ring face multiple charges for serious crimes. Nashville's Metropolitan Police Chief, John Drake, described human trafficking as a form of modern-day slavery and assured that investigations will remain a top priority. Regardless of where the suspects come from, we will dismantle this network and its perpetrators will face justice, he stated. On the other hand, Tennessee's Investigations Office Director, David Rausch, warned that they will not allow the expansion of the Aragua Train in the state. We won't stand idly by and let this criminal organization establish itself in Tennessee. We will use all available tools to make them accountable.

The victim was attacked when she was 5 and 6 years old. A father and his son were arrested today in the Buenos Aires province, accused of being the perpetrators of a sexual abuse against a minor. Police sources informed NA that the case began when the victim came of age and filed a complaint in which she stated that she was assaulted during her childhood by her then-stepfather. According to the police report, the incidents occurred in the family home located in the town of Gregorio de Laferrere, between 2010 and 2012, and when the victim was 5 and 6 years old. According to her testimony, the sexual attacks took place when the victim was left in the care of the accused, who threatened her with death on multiple occasions and avoided any accusation against him. However, during a move carried out between 2016 and 2017, the victim was sexually attacked again, but at that time the perpetrator of the crime was the son of the main suspect. In this context, at the end of January, the Specialized Unit for Instruction and Specialized Judgment in Family and Gender Violence and Sexual Integrity Crimes number one of the La Matanza Judicial Department convened the Division of Public Health Crimes of the Federal Police with the purpose of identifying and capturing the suspects. The officers apprehended those involved on García Merou Street (Gregorio de Laferrere) and Riglos Street (González Catán) respectively. Both detainees, one of them a Bolivian national, were placed at the disposal of the intervening judge for the crime of severely humiliating sexual abuse committed against a minor under 18, taking advantage of the situation of cohabitation and committed by the person in charge of the guard, in ideal concurrence with aggravated corruption of a minor.

Franco Fusetti, 26, Who Was Missing, Found Alive in Aguas Chiquitas Franco Fusetti, the 26-year-old young man who had been missing since Tuesday, was found alive on Wednesday in the Aguas Chiquitas area, near the El Cadillal Dam. Superintendent Florencia Rodríguez, from the Human Trafficking Division, confirmed the news to eltucumano after an intense search operation. The case had generated great concern since Fusetti left his house on Tuesday and didn't return. According to his father's account to Canal 10, the young man had accompanied his mother to a hypermarket on Avenida Néstor Kirchner. At one point, he went to the bathroom and, upon returning, his mother noticed that he seemed strange. Later, Fusetti returned home to look for his ID. He briefly spoke with his father and assured him that he would return to the supermarket to reunite with his mother. However, he never arrived. With his cell phone dead and out of reach, his family began the search, but were unable to gain access to the security cameras of the store. On Wednesday morning, the Police found the young man's car parked at the New Bus Terminal. Upon reviewing the security footage, they confirmed that Fusetti entered the building, opened the trunk of his vehicle without removing anything and left. The authorities intensified the search operation until they finally found him in Aguas Chiquitas. The young man was without a life jacket and covered with a blanket. At this time, no further details have been released about his state of health or the reasons for his disappearance.

Sean Diddy Combs, also known as Puff Daddy, faces a new controversy this time related to the premiere of a documentary that, according to him, portrays him as a monster and even compares him to the pedophile magnate Jeffrey Epstein. Known for being an icon in the hip-hop industry, the rapper is currently behind bars awaiting a trial in which he is accused of sex trafficking, illicit association, and transporting for prostitution. However, his focus is today on suing NBC and Peacock's streaming service to censor and withdraw from circulation a footage that, in his opinion, defames him and puts his legal defense at risk. Why Sean Diddy Combs is suing NBC In January, Peacock premiered Diddy The Making of a Bad Boy, a documentary that delves into the life and career of Sean Diddy Combs The rapper's reaction was forceful, filing a lawsuit demanding $100 million in damages for defamation, alleging that the production unfairly links him to a series of heinous crimes, including murders, rapes, and child trafficking networks. Among the complaints of Combs' lawyers, it highlights the way the documentary addresses the death of Kim Porter, Combs' ex-partner and mother of three of his children, who died in 2018 due to pneumonia. According to the lawsuit, the footage suggests that Porter's death was not natural and blames Combs for being responsible. Additionally, it mentions other unexplained tragedies, such as the murder of Notorious B.I.G. in 1997, in which it implies that it is not a coincidence and that the protagonist could have been involved. The documentary about Sean Diddy Combs, Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy, offers a chronological review of the career of Sean Diddy Combs, from his beginnings as a music producer to his transformation into one of the most influential (and controversial) figures in hip hop. The 90-minute footage does not only cover his artistic achievements but also addresses the numerous lawsuits and investigations against the rapper, including allegations of inappropriate sexual conduct and possible links to the deaths of people close to him. One of the most contentious moments is the appearance of Al B. Sure, the singer who had a child with Kim Porter, who on screen suggests that his ex-partner was murdered or, at the very least, that there were strange circumstances surrounding his death. The documentary, according to the lawsuit, goes so far as to characterize Combs as the embodiment of Lucifer and draws parallels with Jeffrey Epstein, the billionaire accused of leading a sex trafficking ring for minors. Who participates in Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy. Peacock's production not only gathers testimonies from personalities close to Combs' entourage in the music industry, but also includes statements from alleged victims and former employees. Among them are Al B. Sure, who claims that Kim Porter died just before becoming the next Cassie Ventura, alluding to another rapper ex-girlfriend who accused him in 2023 of numerous crimes of abuse and violence. Ashley (pseudonym) accuses Combs of raping her with a remote control in 2018. Her testimony, seen in the documentary, describes the trauma and distrust she has carried since then. Former bodyguards and childhood friends add details about the rapper's private life, which point to a dizzying and dark lifestyle behind the scenes. Lawyers and legal representatives who comment on the sexual trafficking allegations and their possible penal implications Why the Rapper Wants to Censor the Documentary For Sean "Diddy" Combs, the release of this material poses a legal and media risk. The artist argues that it distorts the facts, mixes conjectures and unverified testimonies to place him at the center of a criminal web. According to the filed complaint, the documentary spreads false information with the intention of portraying him as a serial killer, child molester, and monster. The rapper's main strategy is to demonstrate that NBC and Peacock attribute crimes for which there is no evidence or official investigation linking him directly. In the lawsuit, it is emphasized that competent authorities have ruled out the involvement of third parties in Kim Porter's death, and that no formal complaint places him at the scene of the mentioned murders. Ashley's testimony was also investigated and dismissed by the Contra Costa Police Department, Combs asserts, and he finds it implausible that she possesses sex tapes with minors. Peacock's response to the allegations Until now, NBC and Peacock have limited themselves to defending the journalism and freedom of expression involved in the documentary's production. They have not removed the transmission from the platform nor announced changes to the work. However, the controversy generated leaves the legal future of the production in the air. Combs demands its elimination and a multimillion-dollar indemnity. On the other hand, some of the interviewees have reaffirmed their statements and insist that there are loose threads regarding suspected deaths and accusations of violence within Combs' environment. Nevertheless, the singer and producer continues to proclaim his innocence and denounces a witch hunt against him. Where and when can the documentary "Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy" be seen? Despite Sean Combs' attempts to censor it, the documentary "Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy" is available for viewing on the streaming platform Peacock from January 14, 2025. To access the documentary, a subscription to Peacock is required, a streaming service owned by NBCUniversal. Although Combs' lawsuit may lead to future legal actions and controversies, for now, the documentary remains accessible to the public.What can we expect from the trial of Sean "Diddy" Combs? The rapper is currently in pretrial detention while awaiting the start of the federal trial on charges including human trafficking, extortion, and prostitution. The scheduled trial date is May 2025, but it may be delayed depending on the defense and prosecution strategies. Meanwhile, the lawsuit against NBC and the producers of Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy is added to the multiple legal fronts that Combs will face in the coming months. If the court grants Combs a restraining order, Peacock may be forced to withdraw or edit the documentary, thus fulfilling the rapper's wish to censor it. On the other hand, if the justice determines that there is no defamation, the platform will maintain the broadcast, which will reinforce the narrative that the artist is still being harassed by testimonies that he considers false and opportunistic.

The International Labor Organization (ILO) estimates that there are more than 150 million children in child labor situations, an alarming figure that we cannot ignore. Criminal Investigation Agency of Coahuila Locates Man for Controlled Deportation On the US-Mexico border in Coahuila, the Criminal Investigation Agency detained a man allegedly guilty of child abuse charges and deported him to his country. SALTILLO, Coahuila. The Criminal Investigation Agency of the State Attorney General's Office, in collaboration with the National Migration Institute (INM) and US authorities, carried out the location and controlled deportation of a US citizen, identified as James N, who was being sought in his country for child abuse charges. Binational coordination for deportation Following an investigation and intelligence work, the suspect was located in the city of Saltillo, from where he was secured and subsequently transferred to the International Bridge 2 in Piedras Negras municipality, Coahuila. Local authorities have identified a kidnapped person in an operation by the Investigation Agency. At this point, the National Migration Institute, in compliance with its powers, conducted the controlled deportation process, handing it over to U.S. Marshal Service agents to face pending charges in the United States. With this type of operation, the Coahuila State Attorney General's Office reaffirms its commitment to collaborating with national and international authorities to strengthen security and ensure the prosecution of justice in both countries.

Luis Medina A former counselor at a Christian academy in Riverside was sentenced today to 30 years in prison on federal charges for possessing child pornography and producing it by secretly recording students using the children's bathroom in front of his office at the private school. During a search of his home in Loma Linda in March 2020, police found that Matthew Daniel Johnson possessed a laptop containing numerous illegal video files of prepubescent children participating in sexually explicit conduct, according to his guilty plea agreement presented in the federal court in Los Angeles. At the time of the investigation, Johnson admitted to members of the task force on child Internet crimes in Fontana that he had hidden a recording device in the shape of a pen in a roll of toilet paper inside a school bathroom, on the other side of the hallway from his office at La Sierra Academy, according to the guilty plea agreement. Within the office, investigators found an external hard drive containing over 100 illicit video files showing more than 60 minors, created by Johnson with the camera he installed inside the bathroom, according to the document. Court documents show that the Fontana task force also recovered videos of the defendant adjusting the hidden recording device. Another video file found by investigators showed Johnson adjusting a recording device inside a different bathroom in a secondary school's Bible camp where he worked as a student mentor, the plea agreement states. Johnson, 34, pleaded guilty in October 2024 at the Los Angeles federal center to a federal charge of producing child pornography and possessing child pornography. In addition to prison time, Johnson was ordered to serve a lifetime of supervised release. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office, a restitution hearing is scheduled for May 28. The Sierra Academy is a Seventh-day Adventist Christian school accredited from kindergarten to 12th grade. Johnson was fired from the school following his arrest in March 2020. Federal agents first learned of Johnson in 2019 when detectives observed an IP address sharing files on an encrypted service. Those files were found to contain child pornography, authorities said. In a statement on the impact of the victim presented to the court, a father of one of Johnson's victims wrote that the case has had a profound impact on our lives. I feel a deep sense of violation and anxiety regarding my child's safety and trust in institutions, the father wrote. The emotional instability I have faced has strained my relationships with my child and other family members. The fear and anxiety surrounding their well-being have been overwhelming and it's a daily struggle to overcome these feelings. In January 2021, attorneys for three of Johnson's victims, aged 8 to 13, filed a civil lawsuit against him, La Sierra Academy, and the Southeastern California Conference of Seventh-day Adventists, seeking unspecified damages. In April 2021, the parents of a fourth child filed a similar lawsuit against the same defendants.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), reported that 3.5 million Venezuelans received humanitarian aid in 2024. The figure represents a 68.6% achievement of the target set for the previous year, which was 5.1 million people who were to receive humanitarian aid. However, reaching 3.5 million people assisted represents a 29.6% increase compared to 2023, when aid reached 2.7 million people, according to OCHA figures. Aid reached 303 of the country's 335 municipalities, thanks to the work of 158 organizations, 90 of which were national and a dozen belonging to the United Nations system. 3.5 million Venezuelans received humanitarian aid related to nutrition and quality of life. Of the total assisted in 2024, the ONU Office reports that 60% were women and girls, and the majority of the 3.5 million Venezuelans received aid in health, food security, and livelihoods. It was also noted that assistance was provided in areas such as nutrition, protection, water, sanitation and hygiene, education, housing, energy, and household items. However, this does not mean that the needs of these individuals were fully met. The main spaces where humanitarian aid arrived were communities, followed by health facilities and schools or other types of educational centers, according to OCHA. Furthermore, of the total, 186,000 people live in indigenous populations, 142,000 were pregnant and lactating, 24,000 had disabilities, and 3,000 belonged to the LGTBI collective. On the other hand, 253,000 people attended sessions on mental health care, assistance, and psychosocial support and socio-emotional learning, while 359,000 participated in activities to raise awareness about protection against exploitation and sexual abuse, the multilateral organization's office added. data.text: The Crimes of the Aragua Train Against Sex Workers in Lima An InSight Crime investigation gathers the testimonies of the women who live under the threat of the criminal gang that arrived in Peru in 2019. Their stories reconstruct how this organization took over the sex trade business on our streets. Since 2019, Carmen, Fernanda, Katherine, Lucía, Liliana, Marcela, Paulina, and Roxi have lived in fear of being extorted, violently attacked, murdered, or disappeared by the Aragua Train, the megaband from Venezuela that has expanded across South America. The fear of these women is fueled by the fact that they act as the criminal thermometer of the city, as they are the first to experience the effects of the predatory criminal economies that have driven the expansion of the Aragua Train in Lima. Written by Lara Loaiza InSight Crime Paulina has worked on the streets of Lima as a sex worker for 15 years She did it to support her family, as she had no other means of sustenance. When you have children, you have to look for anywhere to be so that they can eat, Paulina says. Throughout all these years working as a sex worker, she has lived through countless acts of violence firsthand and has witnessed the abuses suffered by other sex workers. Paulina thought she had seen it all, until in September 2022, some criminals murdered a fellow sex worker in one of the main streets in the center of Lima. They killed her for not paying and for denouncing that they were charging a quota, she recounts, referring to a type of extortion that the criminal groups charge to sex workers in exchange for allowing them to work on the streets. Paulina feared falling under the radar of the criminals and them starting to charge her a quota, so for the two months that followed the murder of her fellow sex worker, she did not return to work. However, their fear became a reality in November, when she began receiving different WhatsApp messages. The suspected authors were members of the Tren de Aragua, a Venezuelan megaband that has expanded throughout South America since 2019, and has become the main criminal threat to Lima. They clearly left a warning, stating they were the Tren de Aragua and if they did not pay protection money, they would kill them. REMEMBER: "Father rescues daughter from Los Hijos de Dios del Tren de Aragua in Moquegua was a victim of human trafficking" They were charging her 400 soles (around US$100) as an enrollment fee to continue working in the area where she had been working for years. In addition to the initial fee, she had to transfer 150 soles (US$40) per week to an account, and send a photo of the payment receipt with her name. Fearing for her life, and that of her children, Paulina began paying the protection money Regardless of whether you work or not, you have to collect their money, because if you don't pay them, they'll kill you, he added. However, he soon began to have difficulties in collecting the full amount of money. On the days when there weren't enough clients, it was impossible for him to gather the entire payment. In some cases, he had even had to stop eating in order to pay the quota. But when he couldn't gather the full amount, Paulina would send the little he managed to get to the criminals. Even so, they threatened her for not paying the full quota. If you don't like the rules, leave the area, so you don't get killed, one of the messages would sentence. Although Paulina was very afraid of suffering reprisals, denouncing the situation wasn't an option for her. In Peru, sex work isn't penalized, but there isn't a specific framework for its regulation, and sex workers like her have been left unprotected against all types of violence. Additionally, the security forces, which had been the main aggressors of sex workers in Lima, generally discriminate against them and do not usually help them in situations like this. You go to report and they tell you "No, no, I don't believe it, I don't believe they're going to kill you." And when they kill you, they say "Why didn't you report it? Why didn't you warn us?" And when you call them, they don't show up, explain. YOU CAN SEE Mayor of Ate attacks Dina Boluarte over disbandment of the Aragua Train If it were true, there wouldn't be extortions. Sex workers in Lima have systematically faced extortions, beatings, rapes, and even murders and disappearances at the hands of their families, clients, security forces, and local mafias. Despite the constant abuse and mistreatment in their lives, the different factions of the Aragua Train have taken the violence to unprecedented levels. The Street is Tough Before the arrival of the Aragua Train in 2019, among the main perpetrators of violence against sex workers were the local mafia led by "mamas" and "papis," known as pimps, who, on occasion, extorted small groups of sex workers. The mamas and papis also managed local networks of human trafficking for sexual exploitation. There have always been mafia groups, explains Ángela Villón, leader of Miluska Vida y Dignidad (MVD), a sex workers' association in Lima. They would cut your clothes and tell you, "If you don't pay the next time, we'll do the same thing, but on your skin." It's a terror, but they wouldn't kill you. However, in addition to the mamas and papis, for decades, the main aggressors of sex workers in Lima were members of the Peruvian National Police (PNP) and the Municipal Serenazgo, an institution in charge of urban security. Using loopholes in Peruvian law surrounding sex work, members of the Peruvian National Police (PNP) and local security forces conducted operations against sex workers, arbitrarily detaining them, according to a dozen sex workers who spoke with InSight Crime. They claim to have received beatings, abuse, extortion, and even sexual abuse during these operations. Another sex worker leader, Leida Portal, who heads the organization Rosa Mujeres de Lucha, dedicated to advocating for sex workers, was a victim of three police officers who burst into her workplace, beat her, stole her money, and took her to the police station, where they subjected her to further abuse and discrimination. However, things took a turn for the worse for sex workers with the arrival of Venezuelan criminal groups in 2019. About a decade ago, thousands of Venezuelans began fleeing their country to escape the economic and political crisis. One of the first destinations for migrants was Peru, where currently 1.6 million Venezuelans reside, according to numbers from the humanitarian coordination platform R4V. In 2018, when the Venezuelan migration flow reached unprecedented levels, the Aragua Train began expanding across South America, using migrant trafficking to establish itself outside of Venezuela. Sex workers have mobilized against the crimes committed by the Aragua Train. Photo: Lara Loaiza URLInSight Crime To take root in Peru's capital, a notorious faction of the group known as Los Gallegos began displacing small Peruvian criminal groups. Among their main objectives were the networks that were extorting sex workers in Lima According to sex workers and members of the Peruvian National Police (PNP) who spoke with InSight Crime, the arrival and expansion of Los Gallegos in the area was announced on the night of Thursday, January 9, 2020, when three men assassinated Isaac Hilario Huamanyalli, known as Cholo Isaac. Cholo Isaac allegedly controlled the collection of quotas in the Lince district, a hotspot for sex work in central Lima. The assassination of Cholo Isaac was one of the key moves that highlighted the expansion of the Aragua gang faction in the city. However, it was not the only signal. According to sex workers who spoke with InSight Crime, one of the Peruvian madams also opened the door to Los Gallegos. A girl got together with a Venezuelan man. He taught her how to collect quotas and the Venezuelan mafia man took the girl away, and he kept everything for himself, says Roxi, a Venezuelan sex worker who has been working in Lima for three years. The Aragua Train's factions displaced other Peruvian mom and pop networks and usurped the throne in the commission business. With local competition out of the game, Venezuelan criminal groups extended their tentacles over sex workers. The Gallegos began extorting Venezuelan sex workers and then focused on Peruvian, Colombian, and Ecuadorian sex workers. What they did at that time was kidnap sex workers and kept them for two, three days () in a space where they didn't let them sleep () all the time they told them how they were going to kill them, precise Ángela. With the arrival of the COVID-19 pandemic, sex workers who couldn't go out to the streets of Lima migrated to messaging apps like WhatsApp to coordinate with each other and schedule appointments with their clients. The Gallegos took advantage of this, not only holding onto the cellphones of sex workers, but also collecting the numbers of others through group chats they were part of and thus catching new victims in their extortion web. Even when we were in the midst of the pandemic, they sent us the first message where they presented themselves, recalls Ángela. They were communicating that from that moment on, we had to pay them the fees to them. Pay or die. Today, six years after the arrival of the Tren de Aragua in Peru, all the women who dedicate themselves to sex work on the streets of Lima must pay a fee to this gang, or to one of its associated factions, such as Los Gallegos, Los Hijos de Dios, or the Dinastía Alayón. What interests them is their money. Either you pay or they'll kill you, says Liliana, a Venezuelan sex worker. Extortion is everywhere. Some, like Paulina and Liliana, receive threatening messages from criminal groups on their phones and in groups they use to communicate with other sex workers. Others are cornered on the streets and even in their homes. They are closing in on all fronts, and somehow you end up trapped in that circle of criminalization, where if you don't pay, you don't work, adds Lucía, a Peruvian sex worker who works through ads on websites. Criminal groups that target sex workers who advertise on websites like hers, track their contact information to collect "cupo" (a fee) from them. They send constant messages on WhatsApp, threatening them even before they see their ads, Lucía notes. The text messages lead them to specific bank account numbers where they must deposit a certain amount of money. First, they must pay the permit, or the registration, as the extortionists call it, to be able to work in the areas under the group's control. The price depends on the faction and the area, which can be between 200 and 400 soles (US $50-100). Then, like Paulina, they must make a weekly payment that ranges from 150 to 250 soles (US $40-66), although it can sometimes reach 500 (US $130). The payments are not the same for everyone. The Venezuelans, who were the first to be extorted, must pay more simply because they are Venezuelans. And if they delay the payment, their debt accumulates. Despite the threatening messages usually coming from men, the women who are part of the Aragua Train, or in some cases, victims of human trafficking, are the ones who collect the fees on the streets. According to the testimonies of sex workers and leaders, these women pass through the areas where sex work is concentrated every day to collect the fees. Some of them, despite being associated with the criminal group, are also targets. One of them was killed by the group after becoming known in the area, according to sex workers who spoke with InSight Crime. They charged her and the same criminals killed her, says Katherine, another woman who spoke with InSight Crime. She charged all Peruvian women, but as she became ambitious, she joined with other stronger people. But with the mafia, no one plays, because the mafia gets bored and kills you. If any woman refuses to pay or does not have permission from the group to work in the area, they threaten her, beat her, and even kill her. The violence is not random. It is a written warning with blood for other sex workers who refuse to pay and will face the same fate. Members of criminal groups kidnapped Lucía in 2023. She had agreed to meet a client at a house, but upon arrival, she realized the situation was not what she had expected. Inside the dwelling, she found a man armed, who told her that she was not on his list of authorized women to work and abused her while threatening her with the gun. Although she managed to escape, Lucía fears being attacked again. The families of sex workers are also in the crosshairs. In August 2023, Katherine's husband was having lunch with his family in the capital. Unaware that armed men were following him, he stepped out to hail a taxi, but moments later the men shot and killed him. Because he didn't pay the quota, Katherine says. The murders of sex workers year by year According to the records of sex workers' organizations and InSight Crime's media monitoring, between 2018 and 2019, at least 7 women were murdered. Between 2020 and 2021, there were 8 reported murders. In 2022, 35 women were killed, according to the monitoring by Miluska Vida y Dignidad. Another 36 went missing, and it is believed that several are dead. We have not found their bodies, but no one is listening to us, comments Ángela Villón. In 2023, 36 women were murdered, and 39 went missing, and in 2024, at least 39 were killed or went missing. It was not until February 2022 that the violence drew national attention. That month, two sex workers, one from Venezuela and one from Ecuador, were murdered in the heart of Lima.

Bangkok, February 13 (EFE). Thai Police are verifying the cases of 260 people from 20 nationalities, including two Brazilians, who were released in Myanmar (Burma), where they were allegedly being held as slaves in online scam centers. In a statement, the Thai military explained that they are confirming whether the citizens released on Wednesday in Myawaddy by the Democratic Buddhist Army of Karen, one of the guerrilla groups vying for territorial control in Myanmar, are indeed victims of human trafficking and not perpetrators who are part of these criminal networks. The released individuals are mostly from Ethiopia (138), followed by 23 citizens of Kenya, 16 from the Philippines, 15 from Malaysia, 12 from Pakistan, 10 from China, 8 from Indonesia, 7 from Nepal, and 7 from Taiwan, 6 from Uganda, and 6 from Laos, 2 from Brazil, 2 from Burundi, and 2 from Bangladesh, as well as one from Cambodia, one from Sri Lanka, one from Ghana, one from India, one from Nigeria, and one from Tanzania. The Defense Minister, Phumtham Wechayachai, told the public Thai PBS that Thailand will not establish a refugee center to house those rescued from the scam centers and, on the contrary, the Government has been in contact with embassies of Latin America, Asia, and Africa to coordinate immediate repatriations. The Police are interviewing the released individuals in the Tak province, bordering Myanmar, and expect to receive more people from the scam centers, where criminal groups enslave thousands of people who were caught under deception with false job offers, forcing them to find new victims. Thailand is seeking to resolve this problem, which especially affects Southeast Asia and China, with strengthened measures in recent weeks such as cutting off the electricity and fuel supply to the Myanmar side of the border, implemented last week. At the same time, the Thai police have set up a committee to investigate alleged ties between high-ranking officials of the security forces and Burmese criminal gangs, after five officers, including a police chief, were removed from their posts this week for allegedly collaborating with these gangs. The Burmese military junta, which seized power after the February 2021 coup, claimed in January that since October 2023, it had captured and deported more than 57,700 foreigners involved in scams, including over 53,000 Chinese. Among other nationalities, they highlighted then that there were over 1,100 Vietnamese, around 600 Thais, as well as Filipinos, Indians, Cambodians, and a Spanish national, without providing further details.

data.text: Over 50 arrested The El Faku sextortion scheme targeted victims from all over Spain, including the Comunitat Valenciana region The number of arrests exceeds 50 and the National Police has reached the final recipients of the money Investigators, who have also pursued money laundering, have blocked high-value assets and numerous bank accounts Teresa DomínguezURLIgnacio Cabanes As in all previous occasions when the National Police has struck the El Faku gang, along with Salva and Erik, all pseudonyms of the main leaders, in this latest police operation, announced exclusively by LevanteEMV on Wednesday, the victims of their sexual extortion with a background count by dozens and are spread across half of Spain At the moment, more than half a century of detainees have been arrested in this large-scale operation, according to various sources, which began at dawn on Tuesday in numerous homes in València, where most of the arrests in Pobla de Vallbona and, above all, Benissa took place. It was there, in a chalet in one of the multiple urbanizations of that municipality in the Marina Alta, that the supposed gang supposedly led by sextortion on the scale by Facundo B. S. H., 24 years old, who goes by the nickname El Faku, Ismael B. O., alias Salva, and Massinissa F. M., Erik, had set up their headquarters this time in the form of a call center from where they made the dozens of calls to cybersex workers until one of them fell into the provocation and ended up paying the revolutionary tax in exchange for not spreading their perversions or not physically attacking them. Faku and Salva, whose mediation led to the arrest of former Levante UD footballer Toño during the dismantling of the same network in 2019 (the player was completely exonerated), were detained in Benissa, as they personally supervised the work of those attending to the call center. However, in this case, the specialists from the Kidnappings and Extortions Unit of the UDEV central office in Madrid, who have been leading the investigation, and those from Cybercrime of the Superior Police Headquarters in València, have taken a step further and have reached, according to sources of utmost reliability, the highest echelon of the plot, the one who manages and launders the hundreds of thousands of euros that they have obtained from their victims over the past years. According to these sources, dozens of bank accounts would have been frozen, not only those opened by the mules so that the pimps who accessed to pay deposits could deposit the various amounts they were demanding under very serious threats, but above all, those of the genuine perpetrators of the scheme, which has been operating for more than six years. In that sense, the investigators would have managed to freeze an important assets with the goods acquired in the process of capital laundering and with money stored in those accounts, as well as in cryptocurrency credentials. In principle, the arrested individuals will be handed over to the judge in charge of the case next Friday morning, the presiding judge of the Instruction Court number 20 of Valencia. The most media of the arrested is, without a doubt, the Uruguayan Facundo B. S. Facundo B. S. H., alias El Faku, was arrested for the first time at 21 years old and, three years later, rose to become one of the leaders of the organization's part dedicated to setting up fake prostitution contacts and subsequent threats to sex workers who fell for calls from pages that promoted sexual exploitation. As reported by the National Police in a statement following the arrest of Facundo B. S. H. in the spring of 2021 in a town in Jaén where he was hiding, as part of Operation Girasol, exclusively advanced by LevanteEMV, the alleged offender referred to himself as the "Messi of the work" (they called "work" his business and the method they used in sex trafficking, the same as any other similar scheme) on his Instagram account, where he defined himself with the term "I'm a criminal." With over 20 police and judicial complaints against him and an undeniable criminal record, this confessed criminal is currently back behind bars for now.

A 14 years in prison and stripped of custody for man convicted of sexual abuse of neighbor's daughter in Seville. SEVILLE, February 13. The Provincial Court of Seville has issued a sentence that condemns a man to 14 years in prison for a chilling case of sexual assault against his neighbor's daughter, who at the time of the events was only seven years old. In addition, the court has determined a special seven-year incapacitation of the rights of custody and guardianship of his own children. The ruling, issued on January 21 and disseminated by Europa Press, states that Fernando R.R., the convicted man, had no prior criminal records that affected his situation. He resided alongside his partner and their two children in a home in a Seville municipality, right next to the house of the father of the minor, who was visiting the place due to the visitation schedule established after the separation of his parents. According to the case details, the minor, with her father's authorization, entered the accused's home to play with his children, with whom she maintained a friendly relationship. This type of visit was not unusual, and the girl had returned to her home in the afternoon for a snack before returning to Fernando's house. The testimony of the girl's father reveals that he was concerned when he saw his daughter return home without the short pants she was wearing when she left to play. The accused's older brother, who accompanied the girl, explained that they were playing and the father saw no reason to be alarmed. At this time, the accused communicated with the girl's father, sending him photos of the children to reassure him. Later that same night, Fernando R.R. requested permission from the girl's father for her to spend the night at his home, claiming that the children wanted to have a pajama party. With the father's consent, the minor stayed for dinner and subsequently spent the night at the defendant's house, according to the communication maintained between the two through WhatsApp. However, the situation took a devastating turn. On the night of September 16 and the early morning of September 17, Fernando R.R., taking advantage of the girl's vulnerability, took her to his bedroom, where, driven by an evident lustful desire, he proceeded to strip her of her clothes and initiate inappropriate and abusive sexual practices. Once the accused had carried out his intentions, the minor, showing fear, decided to return home in the middle of the night. Upon arrival, her father noticed that she was scared and crying, and after inquiring about what had happened, the girl spontaneously confessed the acts she had suffered. The alarming situation led the father to inform the mother of the girl about what had happened, and both decided to take her to a medical center where, after being examined, the medical findings confirmed the aggressions, including signs of sexual abuse. The clarity and coherence of the minor's testimony were crucial to the conviction. According to the court, the girl presented a clear and coherent account of the events, which was corroborated by medical evidence and other testimonies that strengthened her version of events. Despite the accused's defense, who denied the charges, the evidence obtained and the firmness of the victim's declaration led the Court of Auditors to conclude that there was no doubt about their guilt and the nature of the crimes committed. As a result of this trial, Fernando R.R He been sentenced to 14 years in prison not only for the sexual assault, but also to 17 years of prohibition from approaching the minor, as well as seven years of disqualification from exercising any right over his own children. Additionally, he has been ordered to serve five years of supervised freedom upon his release from prison and to compensate the victim with 6,000 euros as compensation for the damage suffered.

Horrific Scandal in Morrillo: Two Men Allegedly Abused a 15-Year-Old Boy The aberrant incident shocked the community SALTA (Voces Críticas News Desk) The Justice system of Salta is advancing in the investigation of a new case of child abuse in the province. The public prosecutor for Family and Gender Violence in Tartagal, Lorena Martínez, charged two men, aged 42 and 58, with the crime of sexual abuse with aggravated carnal access due to the number of perpetrators. The incident occurred in the locality of Morillo, where the victim, a 15-year-old minor, was allegedly attacked. According to the abuse complaint filed by the minor's mother, her son was intercepted by the accused while returning from a meeting with friends. The men, who were traveling in a car with two other people, allegedly told the victim to get into the vehicle. Hours later, the young boy woke up in a residence with pain in his intimate areas and unable to remember what had happened. The victim reported that the incident allegedly occurred between January 24 and 31 in a house near the railroad tracks in the Villa Las Rosas neighborhood. There, the two defendants allegedly committed the heinous act, according to the testimony collected by the Prosecution. The intervention of the Justice system occurred after the mother filed a complaint at the local police station. During the hearing for abuse charges, the accused opted not to testify and were assisted by an official public defender. The prosecutor requested that the Court of Guarantees in turn maintain the detention of both while the investigation advances. The case caused commotion in the Morillo community and reignited the demand for stricter measures to prevent child abuse. The authorities urged citizens to report any suspected incidents and reinforce the protection of minors in vulnerable situations. Voces Críticas reports.

The Aragua Train is known as one of the most pursued Venezuelan organized crime groups in South America, expanding across the continent with extreme violence through extortion, murders, kidnappings, human trafficking, arms, and narcotics. The gang has expanded easily through Venezuela, its country of origin, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, and has even reached the United States, taking advantage of the route of migrants entering the countries, mostly through border crossings. Its leaders dominated the criminal structure for years, from the Tocorón prison, a penitentiary center in Aragua, Venezuela, from where they supervised and benefited from cells established in at least three other South American countries. In September 2023, 11,000 Venezuelan police and military officers stormed Tocorón to take control of the alleged operations center of the Aragua Train. Despite the blow dealt by the loss of their operational base, the gang's leadership escaped and its transnational cells continue to operate. This is their story. The National Police (PNC) investigates possible link of the Tren de Aragua in armed attack on highway to El Salvador HISTORYThe criminal gang was born in Tocorón prison, in the state of Aragua. Its name comes from a union of a railway construction project that never concluded. One of its first leaders, identified as Héctor Rustherford Guerrero Flores, alias the Niño Guerrero, during his imprisonment in Tocorón, turned the Tren de Aragua into what it is today, a massive criminal structure. During his stay and leadership, the Niño Guerrero turned Tocorón into one of Venezuela's most notorious prisons, due to an unofficial government policy that gave them freedom to engage in illicit income and the construction of a zoo, pools, children's park, restaurants, and even a nightclub. It is still unclear where the new nucleus of the group will be located after the invasion of Tocorón in September 2023. However, there are no indications that the gang has stopped operating in Venezuela. Casa Blanca claims that migrants sent to Guantánamo were members of the Tren de Aragua EXPANSION The Tren de Aragua began to expand into the San Vicente neighborhood, from where it established control and received resources from the Government through the Somos El Barrio JK foundation. As the years passed, the gang expanded its network to different states in Venezuela, becoming transnational in 2018, when it attempted to establish itself between the Venezuela-Colombia border. After being near the Colombia border, the Tren Aragua faced significant Colombian criminal groups, which fought for control of the border crossings that house various illicit economies, such as the trafficking of drugs, contraband of goods and migrants. In Chile, there are at least 100 active members of the criminal organization. Photo La Hora La Tercera of Chile. In this process, the Aragua Train had already expanded its file of crimes, including extortion, kidnappings, human trafficking for sexual exploitation, migrant trafficking, contraband, illegal mining, retail drug trafficking, cybercrime, and robbery. However, it took advantage of the opportunity to seize Colombian lands through Venezuelan migrants, who fled the country in search of better opportunities, taking them clandestinely to Colombia and controlling several nodes of the human trafficking market for sexual exploitation, while their competitors focused on narcotics trafficking. Outside of Venezuela, the Aragua Train has established permanent cells in Colombia, Peru, and Chile, with reports of their activities in Brazil, Ecuador, Bolivia, and the United States. MODUS OPERANDIBetween 2018 and 2023, the organization built a transnational criminal network, establishing groups in Colombia, Peru, and Chile, and sporadic presence in Ecuador, Bolivia, and Brazil. The group continues to maintain its radar through Venezuelan migratory flows, as its presence increased in border crossings and urban areas where these migrants congregate. In addition to extortion and migrant trafficking, foreign factions of the Tren de Aragua control an illegal lending system, also known as gota a gota, micro-trafficking, kidnapping, small-scale international drug trafficking, human trafficking, and robbery. Each cell specializes in different activities, depending on local conditions. This is not an article about human trafficking. However, I can translate the article into English for you.Guerrero's Gang: This is how the loan shark network operated in GuatemalaThe Boy Warrior and His ClanThe group's leader is Guerrero Flores, alias Niño Guerrero, who led the Tren de Aragua from Tocorón prison until September 2023. Niño Guerrero escaped before the operation to retake the prison, after being warned in advance, according to reports from Venezuelan civil society. To this day, his whereabouts remain unknown.According to the records of the Supreme Court of Justice of Venezuela, Guerrero began his criminal career in 2005, when he murdered a police officer in Aragua. Since then, he was imprisoned for the first time in Tocorón in 2010, but escaped two years later.Guerrero Flores, alias Niño Guerrero. Photo La Hora Ministerio del Poder Popular para las Relaciones Interiores, Justicia y Paz de Venezuela He was recaptured in 2013 and returned to the same prison, where he began to consolidate the criminal structure known as Tren Aragua alongside other delinquents who gained his trust and became co-founders of the organization, including Larry Amaury Álvarez, alias Larry Changa, and Yohan José Guerrero, alias Johan Petrica. Alias Larry Changa escaped from Tocorón in 2015 and arrived in Chile in 2018 to lead the expansion of the group. In 2022, when authorities began investigating him, he fled to Colombia, from where he continued to lead operations and plan the expansion of the structure to Colombia. Larry Changa, co-founder of Tren de Aragua, was captured in Colombia. Photo La Hora Policía Nacional de Venezuela. Alias Johan Petrica has dedicated himself to directing a powerful illegal gold extraction in La Claritas, in the south of Bolívar state, which is known as the Las Claritas Syndicate. According to reports, the Niño Guerrero and Petrica could be hiding in Las Claritas, following the invasion of Tocorón. Yohan Jose, Johan Petrica, Photo La Hora US Department of State Various lieutenants of the Tren de Aragua have been sent to cells across the region, some of which even appear to rotate between several countries, maintaining a hierarchical structure, with Niño Guerrero at the helm. With information from OCCRP.

data.text: While the Federal Chamber advances with the review of Judge Pozzer Penzo's investigation, questions are growing about the actions in the first stage and the lack of data during the arrests. By Leo GarcíaFor several weeks, the Federal Chamber of Corrientes has been analyzing the investigation into the disappearance of Loan Danilo Peña on June 13, 2023, and it is expected that in the coming days, specific situations of the case will be defined, especially the prosecution and preventive detention of the seven accused. In this review, questions have resurfaced that are related to the initial hypotheses, as the latest statements have completely undermined the possibility that it was a case of human trafficking for sale, and the hypothesis that sexual exploitation is the central point of the case has grown again. With this profile, the plot of the appearance or false appearance resounds again the night after the disappearance and the movements, communications, and even some medical examinations on the detained. Just a few hours after Loan's disappearance, Antonio Benítez, Loan's uncle, and Daniel Ramírez and Mónica Millapi, the couple who are friends with Loan's father, were detained. They were initially accused of abandoning a person and it was surprising that a police officer participating in the search called Millapi, who was at the police station, to ask how Loan was dressed. Later, the three of them ended up in the jail cell. Beyond that disorganization, a series of examinations were conducted, including one on Benítez's genitals. At that time, the investigators, with the support of Commissioner Walter Maciel, suspected a sexual assault, but that type of examination was only done on Benítez and not on the other detained men. Now, part of the investigators and the prosecution are questioning if that wasn't another distraction and cover-up process. Juan Pablo Gallego, the prosecution attorney, assured El Destape that Maciel suspected sexual abuse and reviewed Benítez, but it's unclear what evidence he had and why he didn't examine the others. The representative of José Peña and María Noguera questioned why that hypothesis of sexual abuse was the main one at the time, and why it was put aside to cover up for someone. In the same vein, he stated that from the prosecution, we have the case resolved in 98% and that the judge has a coinciding view with that situation. That view once again puts the focus on whether there was a distraction operation that allowed other accused to gain time, and those other accused are the ones who were left in the area, Laudelina Peña, Carlos Pérez, and Victoria Caillava, with the help of Walter Maciel. With that gaze, the investigation into the calls and movements in the afternoon of Loan's disappearance is being revisited. It is necessary to analyze the calls between Laudelina and Caillava during the supposed search, Gallego assured, and he wondered if those calls had to do with the search or with the possibility of the child's return. Along those lines, he insisted on the hypothesis of kidnapping that he presented in the last weeks, where part of the chain was that Laudelina handed the child over to Pérez and Caillava, and the movements of Comisario Maciel were to cover up those actions. There, it is questioned whether during the night the child was taken to a field and then taken again to an unknown location. For this, those messages in which they found Loan from the already detained Benítez, Millapi, and Ramírez are being analyzed, although it was later denied and they were kept behind bars. There it is reconsidered the fundamental role of Carlos Pérez as the leader of a gang that perhaps planned a type of attack and then formed another situation. For some reason, among which is fundamentally fear, the pact of silence that seems to reign in the cause since the first day did not break. Pérez was or is still the boss of 9 de Julio, considered the lawyer Juan Pablo Gallego and emphasized that he tends to think that there is a reverential fear of Pérez and detailed that in fact when Laudelina, still in a doubtful version, mentioned that they took Loan away Pérez and Caillava there was a huge operation and deployment that included putting her in jail. That deployment, explained the plaintiff, has to do with the appearance of those who referred to belonging to the Lucio Dupuy Foundation and the hypotheses presented by Gustavo Vera. These movements include help from their own daughter, Macarena, and even changing her lawyer to one chosen by those who claimed to belong to the Dupuy Foundation, Gallego said. Within those lines, the representative of Loan's parents also assured that Macarena and Laudelina are the masterminds of the tragedy and place them with essential participation on the day of the disappearance. Now, the prosecution's expectation is mainly focused on whether the Federal Chamber finally ratifies the charges against Antonio Benítez, Laudelina Peña, Mónica Millapi, Daniel Ramírez, Carlos Pérez, Victoria Caillava, and Walter Maciel, and it can advance with firmness towards an oral trial where one of the implicated individuals may break the silence to avoid spending several years in prison. Additionally, they expect the situation to be resolved in the connected case of obstruction of justice and hindering the investigation, since the arrest in another case of Alan Cañete, one of the individuals involved who claimed to belong to the Dupuy Foundation, explains that despite the restrictions ordered by the Justice, they continue to commit crimes.

Unknown individuals forced a 15-year-old boy into a vehicle and he endured a grave ordeal, a complaint states. Two suspects allegedly committed the worst against a minor of age, when he was returning home. The penal prosecutor for Family and Gender Violence of Tartagal, Lorena Martínez, provisionally charged two men, aged 42 and 58, for the alleged commission of the crime of sexual abuse with aggravated carnal access due to the number of perpetrators. The prosecutor's intervention occurred after a complaint from the mother of a 15-year-old boy, filed at the Morillo police station (Coronel Juan Solá). The woman reported that the incident allegedly occurred between January 24 and 31, when her son returned on foot from a meeting with friends and encountered the accused. The two individuals, traveling in a vehicle with two other people, allegedly told the minor to get in. After that, the teenager stated that he did not remember what happened. Subsequently, according to the testimony of his mother, the victim was found in a nearby dwelling near the railroad tracks, in the Villa Las Rosas neighborhood, at which time the two accused allegedly took advantage of him. The minor reported waking up with pain in his intimate areas. During the arraignment hearing, the accused, assisted by the official defense attorney, chose not to testify. On the other hand, Prosecutor Martínez requested the Juzgado de Garantías to maintain the detention of both accused individuals.

The Investigating Prosecutor of Río Tercero, Paula Bruera, ordered the indictment, capture, and detention of a 36-year-old male suspect for allegedly committing the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access qualified by the pre-existing cohabitation situation and aggravated corruption of minors due to guardianship. The investigation began at the Specialized Fiscal Unit for Sexual Integrity Crimes in Rosario, Santa Fe. From there, on January 15, 2025, it was forwarded to the jurisdiction of Río Tercero, Córdoba province, as some incidents allegedly occurred in a locality belonging to the Calamuchita department. The accused was detained in the city of Santa Fe and later transferred to Córdoba, where he remains in Bouwer prison. The investigation determined that under extreme vulnerability, the defendant allegedly manipulated and sexually abused his 11-year-old stepdaughter, who, at 13 years old, gave birth to a girl who would be a product of that relationship. These events allegedly occurred in the city of Río Tercero. After the birth of the baby, when they had already moved to the province of Santa Fe, the defendant allegedly manipulated the minor victim to the point that on multiple occasions, the minor left the home she shared with her mother to live secretly in the rural area of the Santa Fe province. This motivated the mother of the victim and former partner of the defendant to file complaints in the province of Santa Fe in search of locating her daughter, now 14 years old. The case continues its investigation. To date, the defendant has been interrogated and is detained and housed in the Bouwer Penitentiary Service facilities.
