data.text: The Judicial Investigation Agency confirmed that they have located 15 victims in the raids carried out on Wednesday in a case of sexual exploitation. The women were forced to engage in sexual services under the guise of massage rooms by the dismantled organization. The victims were found by judicial agents in the various points raided. Authorities also confirmed the arrest of the organization's leader, a 35-year-old man named Morales, as well as his romantic partner, a 31-year-old woman. In addition to the leader and his partner, four other women involved in these human trafficking crimes were also apprehended. During the investigations, the OIJ seized multiple pieces of evidence of importance to the investigation: 12 cellular phones, 1 hard drive, 4 vehicles, 3 computers, 5 recorders, 2 tablets, and varied documentation related to the investigation. Approximately one million colons in cash was also seized. According to Randall Zúñiga, OIJ director, the operation included six raids in sectors such as Barrio Escalante, Curridabat, Pavas, Rohrmoser, and Ciudadela 25 de Julio. The criminal organization, according to the investigations, was dedicated to recruiting women under the pretext of offering therapeutic massages, but once the victims arrived at the locations, they were forced to offer explicit sexual services to clients. The leader and his partner allegedly established an entire criminal organization, which recruits women to appear to offer some type of therapeutic massage. However, once the people arrive, it's obviously no longer just a therapeutic massage, but also an explicit sexual service that is offered to clients as such, explained Zúñiga. In addition, the OIJ director stated that the women involved in this crime were forced to perform these acts under threat of fines or sanctions if they refused.

The Internal Revenue Service is at the center of a controversy after the Department of Homeland Security requested its participation in immigration operations in the United States. The proposal could mark a before and after in the relationship between the tax system and immigration policies. What role does the IRS play for undocumented immigrants? The DHS, led by Secretary Kristi Noem, proposed that IRS Criminal Investigation Division agents work together with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to identify human trafficking networks and businesses that employ undocumented immigrants. The IRS Criminal Investigation Division is the only division of the IRS with the authority to make arrests and conduct penal investigations. Its agents are trained in the analysis of illicit money flows and have been crucial in cases of tax fraud and organized crime. In 2024, the agency reported the discovery of over $9 billion in irregular financial activities. This request is part of a broader strategy by former President Donald Trump to tighten immigration policies, involving various federal agencies in identifying and deporting undocumented immigrants. Undocumented immigrants: How the IRS will use tax data One of the main points of contention is whether the IRS can share taxpayer information with ICE. U.S. tax law protects the confidentiality of data under Section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code, allowing access only in specific criminal investigations. Despite this, if Congress modifies this regulation, tax information could be used to reinforce migrant operations. Civil rights groups expressed concern over this possibility. They argued that access to tax data could be used in a discriminatory manner and create a climate of fear among immigrant taxpayers. IRS impact on taxpayers and employers If the IRS expands its role in immigration operations, both workers and employers could face increased scrutiny. In recent years, ICE has intensified audits of businesses to detect the employment of undocumented workers, resulting in economic penalties and arrests. With the IRS's participation, these controls could be even more exhaustive, given the agency's access to financial records and tax returns. Immigration experts advise taxpayers to keep their tax returns in order, as a solid tax history can be a positive factor in immigration processes. Additionally, employers must ensure compliance with labor regulations to avoid penalties.

More than 260 foreign nationals have been rescued from online scam operations in Myanmar and handed over to authorities in Thailand. The rescue is part of a growing crackdown on human trafficking and cyber fraud along the border of the two countries. A Myanmar insurgent group, the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army, which recently raided scam centers in the region, handed over the victims to Thai authorities on February 12. The head of staff of DKBA, seen by San Aung, the Burmese service of VOA, in a phone interview, said that the group's forces raided casinos in Myawaddy district, Karen State, in search of trafficked foreign workers. On February 11, we identified 261 victims and transferred them to Thai authorities on February 12, he said. We are handing over all those we found today, but the process is difficult. The Immigration Department of the Board (Myanmar) is making demands, and the terrain is a challenge. We have to rescue the victims before transferring them to the nearest Thai authorities, said Major San Aung. Thai soldiers photograph and film the 261 foreign nationals rescued from online scam operations in Myawaddy, Myanmar, as part of an intense crackdown on human trafficking and cybercrime along the border. (DKBA courtesy) A rescue worker and eyewitness who requested anonymity for security reasons told VOA in a phone interview on Wednesday that online gangs force human trafficking victims to meet monthly profit targets of up to $50,000. If they failed, they were tortured. They were only allowed to sleep for two or three hours a day and worked non-stop. Thai officials confirmed that the rescued individuals were taken by boat to Phop Phra, Thailand, before being transferred to a secure facility. China pressed for strong action against scammers China's tensions with Myanmar escalated after Chinese actor Wang Xing was kidnapped and held captive in Myanmar in January, before being rescued from the scam centers in Myawaddy. In response to this incident, China pressed Thailand to take strong action against the scam networks operating in the region. It is widely believed that this pressure is a key factor behind Thailand's decision to cut off electricity and fuel supplies to Myanmar, significantly affecting areas controlled by ethnic armed groups Karen. The delivery on Wednesday follows another transfer on February 6 when Myanmar's ruling council and another armed group, the Karen Border Guard Force, handed over 61 trafficked individuals, including 39 Chinese nationals, to Thai custody. Among the rescued and returned on Thursday, many were from Africa, including 46 Ethiopians and 33 Kenyans, according to the DKBA. In recent days, Myanmar's military leadership has also highlighted its efforts to represent illegal online gaming and fraud operations in cooperation with the international community. In the audio message shared with the media last Friday, the junta's spokesperson, General Zaw Min Tun, said that many trafficking victims were lured with promises of well-paying jobs in computer-related translation fields. They were deceived by the prospect of high salaries and good working conditions. Most of them arrived in Mae Sot from Bangkok before being smuggled across the border illegally by online money laundering gangs, said General Zaw Min Tun. Myawaddy's Myawaddy syndicate refugee camp, located in Karen State along the Thai border, is controlled by armed Karen groups, including the DKBA and the Karen BGF, the latter of which was previously aligned with Myanmar's army. The BGF-controlled town of Shwe Kokko has become notorious for being a center for online scams. As of May 2022, reports indicated that 1,225 Chinese citizens, along with individuals from Hong Kong, Taiwan, India, and the Philippines, were trafficked in Shwe Kokko to work on online scam operations. These victims were lured by false job offers and then coerced into online scam schemes. Since the Karen BGF cut ties with the Myanmar army and rebranded itself as the Karen National Army last year, online scams have faced greater scrutiny. The United States Institute of Peace warned that online scams originating from Southeast Asia, particularly Myanmar, are a major security threat and cause significant financial losses in the United States. In 2023, USIP estimated that Americans lost $3.5 billion to scams from the region. These scams, including forced labor, romantic relationship scams, and other financial crimes, target US residents through fraudulent job solicitations and fake high-tech job postings. Aye Aye Mar, a Burmese service from VOA, contributed to this report.

In a joint operation conducted in Florencio Varela, Quilmes, and Almirante Brown, the Cybercrime Investigation Division carried out five raids as part of an investigation into illicit activities, following the detection of social media posts inciting land seizures in the Bosques locality. The investigation began on February 4, when a message on Facebook was detected calling for the occupation of the land where two teenagers, Paloma and Josué, had been found dead a few days earlier, a case that has shocked the community in recent days. The post was replicated in various WhatsApp groups, prompting the authorities in Florencio Varela to file a complaint with the justice system. According to the inquiries, at least five people were organizing the land seizure, dividing the property into plots and recruiting families for the occupation. Based on the analysis of social media profiles and phone records, three main suspects were identified and notified of the charges against them. During the raids, 11 mobile phones, a notebook, and handwritten notes detailing a land parceling plan, as well as a list with 217 names, were seized. One of the investigated individuals, whose voice matched audios calling for 500 families to join the takeover, was found to be in possession of eight mobile phones. Another suspect was in charge of the logistics of the plan, while the third detainee managed the WhatsApp groups used for coordination. The post inviting people to take over the land and the audio with the organization's plan were seized by the authorities. Two other suspects could not be located at their homes, as they frequently left due to substance abuse issues. The authorities consider that, with this operation, they managed to dismantle the organization before it could gather the necessary number of people to carry out the takeover. The investigation is ongoing. In recent days, Judge Adrián Villagra of the Guarantee Court N8 of Quilmes, granted the request of separation of the prosecutor Hernán Bustos Rivas, head of the UFI N5, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the case. The former prosecutor of the case argued that he had been a victim of threats by the lawyer of Josué's family. However, the lawyer denied the accusations, assuring that his only goal is to clarify the crime. This double homicide continues to reveal shocking details. Kelly's convictions for extortion and sex trafficking, along with a 30-year prison sentence, were confirmed by a federal appeals court on Wednesday, which concluded that the singer exploited his fame for over a quarter of a century to sexually abuse young girls and women. The Second Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan ruled Wednesday after hearing arguments in March. The multiple Grammy-winning composer was convicted in 2021 in Brooklyn Federal Court on multiple charges, including extortion and sex trafficking. Jennifer Bonjean, R. Kelly's attorney, stated in a statement that she believed the Supreme Court would agree to hear an appeal. She called the Second Circuit's ruling unprecedented, saying it grants prosecutors unlimited discretion to apply extortion law to absurdly remote situations from the statute's intent. Last year, the Appellate Court declined to hear an appeal of Kelly's 20-year sentence after he was convicted in 2022 of child sex charges, including charges of producing child sexual abuse images in Chicago. The Second Circuit rejected Kelly's arguments that the trial evidence was period inadquate, the constitutionality of some state laws used against him was period inscordible, four jurors were biased, the trial judge made some inappropriate decisions, and a charge more commonly used in organized crime cases was inapropiate.  Enabled by a constellation of managers, assistants, and other private individuals for over twenty-five years, Kelly exploited his fame to lure young girls and women into his reach, the appeals court said, noting that members of his entourage helped him present underage girls. The evidence presented at the trial showed that they would isolate them from friends and family, control almost all aspects of their lives, and verbally, physically, and sexually abuse them, the three-judge panel said. The appeals court said it was not arbitrary or irrational to allow several accusers to testify at the trial that Kelly gave them herpes without revealing that he had an STD, and it was not excessively prejudicial or cumulative to allow seven witnesses who were not yet adults when Kelly began to abuse them to testify. None of the testimonies were more inflammatory than the charged acts, the appeals court said. The Second Circuit also said it was not unfairly prejudicial for the trial judge to allow the jurors to see graphic videos. The videos, the appellate court said, were properly admitted to show the means and methods of the company, including the level of management and the control Kelly had over his victims. Bonjean, on behalf of R. Kelly, also cited a partial dissent in which Circuit Judge Richard J. Sullivan agreed with what he described as the majority's excellent opinion, but dissented in part from an award of restitution granted to a victim for a lifetime supply of a suppressive herpes regimen medication. The award was based on the cost of the brand-name medication when a generic medication is available. This was not restitution, Bonjean said. Sean Combs files a lawsuit against the NBC network for defamation in a documentary and claims $100 million. The rapper's lawyers, who are in jail awaiting trial for sex trafficking, claim that the footage accuses him of being a monster and compares him to Jeffrey Epstein. In jail awaiting trial, accused of sex trafficking, racketeering, and transporting for prostitution, with over a hundred lawsuits pending, Sean Combs, known as Puff Daddy or Diddy, is now taking action on his own. The musician and entrepreneur has filed a lawsuit against the American television network NBC and its streaming service Peacock over a documentary centered on his life that has been airing on the platform for weeks. Sean Combs demands $100 million for defamation. Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy. (Diddy, the Making of a Bad Boy) premiered on January 9, and it tells the life of Combs, including one of his most well-known episodes, the death of Kim Porter, who was his on-again, off-again partner from 1994 to 2007 and with whom he had three children. Porter died at her home in Toluca Lake, north of Los Angeles, California, in November 2018, at the age of 47. According to Combs' lawyers, in the documentary, he is accused of murdering the love of his life and the mother of his children, despite authorities assuring that her death occurred naturally. In the footage, an image of Porter's autopsy report appears, stating that she died due to pneumonia, and that the police have no suspicions of any other type of death. However, in the documentary, one can also see an interview with a singer named Al B Albert Joseph Brown III, who also had a child with Porter, speaks of a meeting with her using the following words: It was two, three weeks before her supposed murder... I must say supposed. Brown also claims that Porter died because she was going to be the next Cassie Ventura, in reference to Combs' also ex-partner who reported him for multiple crimes of abuse and violence, in the first lawsuit against him, in November 2023. From there, Combs has decided to sue the network, as well as the production company. His lawyers claim that the footage is based on the premise that their client has committed numerous heinous crimes, such as serial killings, child rape, and child sex trafficking, and attempts to psychologize him bluntly The document maliciously and without foundation leaps to the conclusion that Combs is a monster and an embodiment of Lucifer with many similarities to Jeffrey Epstein, they claim, in reference to the pedophilic magnate accused of a child trafficking ring that took his own life in prison in August 2019. Additionally, the documentary's hour and a half also discusses the death of rapper Notorious B.I.G. in a shootout in Los Angeles in March 1997, in a murder that has never been cleared, and one that some people, such as an ex-bodyguard, have accused Combs of. The documentary advances a false narrative that it cannot be a coincidence that Porter and others in Combs' orbit have died, in a malicious attempt to insinuate that Combs murdered them, it reads in the court document. NBC has not commented on the matter. The lawsuit is against the chain, although not against Brown, but who is being sued is a man named Courtney Burgess, who claims to have recordings of Combs engaging in sexual relations with celebrities as well as minors. Burgess's lawyer, Ariel MitchellKidd, is one of the voices in the documentary and appears frequently in it, expressing her doubts about Porter's natural death. That is why Combs also sued her. In September 2024, the three children Combs and Porter have in common sent a statement speaking about their mother's death, following a series of speculations and offensive and false memoirs that revived Porter in the wake of supposed memoirs Our lives were shattered when we lost our mother. She was our world. And nothing has been the same since her passing. Although it has been incredibly difficult to accept that they took her away from us so soon, the cause of her death was clarified a long time ago. They also asked for respect while they continued to face their loss every day. January 12, 2025 We began our Circle of Silence remembering that last Saturday, February 8, the church celebrated the 11th World Day of Prayer and Reflection against Human Trafficking, with the theme Ambassadors of Hope Together Against Human Trafficking. According to the RAE, an ambassador is the person of highest rank to represent a state, and for us, the state is Hope. A hope that is united with our mission to work together against human trafficking. This day invites us to join forces, all together, to take on the challenge of ending human trafficking, so that no one else is subjected to the yoke of slavery and exploitation, and in favor of a humanity of free and equal people. Human trafficking is one of the most serious violations of human rights that affects millions of people around the world. Consists of the exploitation of individuals through coercion, fraud, or abuse of power, with the aim of subjecting them to forced labor, sexual exploitation, or other forms of servitude. In 2023, law enforcement agencies formally identified 497 victims of human trafficking, 294 of whom were victims of sexual trafficking and 203 of labor trafficking, among whom, two were victims of forced begging and six of exploitation for engaging in criminal activities. This represented a significant increase compared to the 227 victims of human trafficking in 2022 and 187 in 2021. Of the victims formally identified by law enforcement, six were minors, 17 were of Spanish nationality, 348 were women, and 143 were men. In contrast, NGOs reported having detected 1 .084 potential victims of human trafficking in 2023 were not all formally identified by the police, of which 822 were victims of sexual trafficking, 110 were victims of labor trafficking, and 152 were victims of unspecified forms of trafficking. Of the 1.084 victims, 37 were minors (20 boys and 17 girls), 23 were of Spanish nationality, 891 were women, 58 were men, and 9 were LGBTQI. As we can see from the data provided, the most vulnerable groups, and those most affected by this problem, are women, children, and migrants. Human trafficking often feeds on conditions of poverty, inequality, and lack of opportunities, leading many people to take risks in search of a better life, unaware that they may fall into exploitation networks. The story of Saint Josephine Bakhita, a victim of human trafficking, who was enslaved and for many years suffered from a lack of freedom and abuse, reminds us of the importance of fighting against this injustice. Her legacy inspires concrete actions to prevent human trafficking and protect those who have suffered its effects. Moreover, combating this crime is not only the responsibility of governments and organizations, but also of each one of us. The importance of our individual action lies in the fact that, by joining forces, we can generate a significant impact in the fight against human trafficking. Firstly, education plays a fundamental role. Informing ourselves about the causes and consequences of human trafficking allows us to recognize high-risk situations and act accordingly. Sharing this information in our social circles helps to create awareness and sensitize more people to the problem. Denunciation is another critical aspect. If we witness suspicious situations, reporting to the authorities can be a vital step in rescuing victims and bringing perpetrators to justice. Every alert counts in this fight. Furthermore, choosing responsible consumption also plays a crucial role in the fight against human trafficking and sexual exploitation. By selecting brands that not only commit to ethical practices, but also promote equality and social justice, we contribute to dismantling the networks that perpetuate trafficking. Education and awareness about the origin of products are fundamental to addressing these problems. By supporting initiatives that tackle these issues, we help create an environment where the respect and dignity of all people are the norm. Choosing ethical brands fosters fair and sustainable business practices. In conclusion, every individual action, no matter how small it may seem, can have a ripple effect. By joining forces, as the slogan of this year's World Day of Prayer and Reflection Against Human Trafficking reminds us, we not only help those suffering from this injustice, but also build a more conscious, solidarity-driven, and just society. We cannot close our eyes or look the other way. Certainly, we must create social awareness, because the abuse of power and authority also occurs among us with immigrants living in our cities and towns. It's not as far from us as we think. Friends, our TIME OF SILENCE has begun. CADIZ AND CEUTA DIOCESAN TABLE FOR MIGRANT AND REFUGEE ATTENTION AND WELCOMING. Collaboration of Juan García de Paredes.

data.text: The United States Department of Justice issued a public statement confirming the formal and public indictment of four charges in Nashville, Tennessee, against eight Venezuelans allegedly linked to the Aragua Train who participated in a transnational commercial sex business. According to judicial documents, the defendants, all Venezuelans, are Yilibeth del Carmen Rivero de Caldera, 51, Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero, 35, Yuribetzi Del Valle Gómez Machuca, 39, Wilmarys Del Valle Manzano Solórzano, 22, Frankyanna Del Valle Romero Rivero, 30, Endrik Alexander Morales Rivero, 25, Jesús Enrique Castillo Rodríguez, 24, and Ariannys Beatriz Gutiérrez-Carrillo, 24, who operated an illegal sex trade and sex trafficking business in Nashville motels from July 2022 to March 2024. Members of Tren de Aragua were found living in the suburbs of Middle Tennessee and have been arrested for running a sex slavery operation for Tren de Aragua, according to authorities. Watch FOX 17 News full update on today's arrests. #FoxNashville (FOXNashville) February 12, 2025 According to the indictment, once the accused facilitated the arrival of the victims in the United States, they used online commercial sex websites to post ads for the victims and then used the internet and their cell phones to direct sex buyers to participate in commercial sex with the victims at motels. This formal indictment demonstrates our commitment to stopping human trafficking wherever we find it, and to making those involved accountable, said Acting U.S. Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee Robert E. McGuire. He added that we are pursuing transnational criminal organizations, but this case shows that we will do what is necessary to stop those who traffic women and girls, regardless of who is behind their suffering. The success of this operation to disrupt the operation of the Aragua Train in our communities is a significant step forward in our ongoing fight against human trafficking and transnational organized crime, said Agent Rana Saoud of the Nashville National Security Investigations Office (HSI). This investigation exemplifies the importance of collaboration between local, state, and federal agencies to put an end to these crimes in our communities and leave a trail of suffering in their wake. Photo courtesy of FBI Houston We will not let the Aragua Train, or any criminal organization, take root in Tennessee, said Tennessee Investigations Office Director David Rausch We are grateful to our local, state, and federal partners who joined us in investigating this case, and we are ready to continue aggressively investigating human trafficking in our state, holding traffickers and buyers accountable and helping victims take their first steps to becoming survivors. Human trafficking is one of the most heinous crimes faced by the FBI, said Special Agent Joseph E. Carrico of the FBI's Nashville Field Office. This devastating crime explodes on vulnerable members of communities across the country, including those in Tennessee. The FBI and our partners are committed to rescuing victims, investigating and prosecuting traffickers, and supporting survivors. Fighting Against the Aragua Train While this investigation focuses on human trafficking, the Aragua Train is involved in all types of criminal activities, including the sale of narcotics and dangerous drugs, said Special Agent Jim Scott of the Louisville Division of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). DEA men and women will continue working hand in hand with our federal, state, and local partners to liberate our communities from transnational criminal gangs like the Aragua Train. Human trafficking is abhorrent to all of us; it's a modern form of slavery. I want to be very clear: our police department will always make human trafficking a priority of investigation, regardless of where the suspects are, and will work with our partners to provide an intentional and coordinated law enforcement response, said Police Chief John Drake of the Nashville Metropolitan Police Department. A grand jury from Middle Tennessee previously presented formal charges against eight defendants for their respective roles in facilitating the recruitment of young women from impoverished areas of Venezuela and other countries in South and Central America, and then facilitating their transportation across the US southern border and state borders to participate in commercial sex in the Nashville area. Three of the defendants, Yilibeth del Carmen Rivero De Caldera, Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero, and Yuribetzi Del Valle Gómez Machuca, are also charged with sex trafficking conspiracy for conspiring to use force, fraud, and coercion to compel the women to engage in commercial sex acts for the benefit of the defendants, including invoking alleged ties to the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua and its reputation for violence. The formal accusation also charges the defendant Kleiver Daniel MotaRivero with possession of a firearm by an illegal alien. The accused, mother and son, RiveroDe Caldera and MotaRivero, are charged with conspiring to impose a coercive debt plan on the victims to force them to continue participating in commercial sex acts until the accused deemed their debts had been settled. Accused RiveroDe Caldera and MotaRivero were previously arrested and detained on state charges related to their conduct. If convicted of conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, the accused face a maximum life sentence. A conspiracy to transport individuals across state lines for purposes of prostitution carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison, and a conspiracy to transport individuals across state and international lines or to aid organized crime businesses carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison. If found guilty of possession of a firearm by an illegal alien, MotaRivero also faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison. More on this story: In Denver raid, suspected members of the Aragua Train are captured. The case was investigated by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) office, the FBI, and other federal, state, and local partners of the Organized Crime and Drug Enforcement Task Force, who coordinated law enforcement operations across multiple jurisdictions. Natalia Melmann was murdered in Miramar in 2001 after being kidnapped, tortured, and asphyxiated with a shoelace cord. Almost 23 years after Natalia Melmann's crime, which occurred in Miramar in February 2001, prosecutor Ana María Caro requested DNA analysis of a fifth suspect, a 60-year-old former policeman from Trenque Lauquen. The measure aims to determine if the genetic profile of the suspect matches the evidence collected from the victim's body. The analysis was conducted at the Trenque Lauquen Forensic Advisory due to the Scientific Police being disabled from intervening in this case, since some of the convicted perpetrators belonged to the Bonaerense force. The sample will be compared with the genetic traces found on the victim, which revealed the participation of at least five aggressors. Natalia, 15 years old, was found murdered in the Florentino Ameghino nursery after being kidnapped, raped, and asphyxiated with the cord of her shoes. The autopsy revealed signs of multiple physical aggressions, including bruises, burns, fractures, and a blow to the skull. Throughout the investigation, forensic expertise confirmed that Melmann's body contained genetic traces from at least five individuals, indicating the involvement of more people in the crime. As proven in the trial, the teenager was intercepted by a group of police officers from Buenos Aires, who forced her to get into an official vehicle where she was sexually assaulted. She was then taken to a residence in the southernmost part of the city, where she was tortured and sexually abused. The young woman died from asphyxiation, strangled with a lace made from the cord of one of her sneakers. The Scientific Police were removed from the Melmann case due to some convicted individuals belonging to that force. The recent request by prosecutor Caro seeks to determine if the 60-year-old former policeman, whose identity has not yet been disclosed, is one of the as-yet uncondemned perpetrators. His link to the case has not yet been publicly clarified, but his inclusion in the forensic analysis suggests that there are indications linking him to the crime scene. In an interview granted a few months ago to Infobae, Natalia's father, Gustavo Melmann, expressed: I have a thought that torments my mind every day, and it happens when I think about what Naty suffered in the hours leading up to her death at the hands of her murderers, who not only raped her but also tortured her, I cannot bear it. In September 2024, Gustavo reported a robbery with a mafia message in his home. It was the second time he had suffered this type of incident in his apartment in the Tribunals area. During the course of hearings in which the release of the former police officers was being processed, both incidents occurred. In that month, they had granted Ricardo Anselmini, one of the convicts sentenced to life imprisonment for the crime, temporary releases, but the following month, they took back the benefit because he was caught violating the conditions they had imposed on him. A judicial process with convictions and reviews The police officers Anselmini, Suárez, and Echenique have been serving a life sentence since 2002 for the collectively committed crime (Télam) In September 2002, the former police officers Ricardo Anselmini, Ricardo Suárez, and Oscar Echenique were sentenced to life imprisonment for the crime of Melmann, found guilty of kidnapping, aggravated sexual abuse with carnal access by multiple people, and homicide crimine causae In turn, Gustavo Gallo Fernández, a former convict with a criminal record, was sentenced to 25 years for his participation in the kidnapping, although the sentence was later reduced to 10 years. Another of the accused, Ricardo Panadero, was acquitted twice due to lack of evidence. However, in 2019, the Penal Cassation Court of Buenos Aires Province annulled the acquittal and ordered him to be retried. Finally, in 2023, Panadero was sentenced to life imprisonment for aggravated deprivation of liberty, aggravated sexual abuse, and double aggravated homicide committed by the premeditated concurrence of two or more people and committed to ensure impunity.

Pope Francis sent a letter to the Catholic bishops of the United States focused on the situation of undocumented immigrants in that country, containing a severe critique of Donald Trump's political decision aimed at expelling those people from North American territory. In his epistle, disseminated by the press office of the Holy See, the Pope acknowledges a nation's right to defend itself and keep its communities safe from those who have committed violent or serious crimes while in the country or before arriving, but warns that the act of deporting people who in many cases left their own land due to extreme poverty, insecurity, exploitation, persecution, or the severe deterioration of the environment, hurts the dignity of many men and women, entire families, and leaves them in a state of special vulnerability and defenselessness. Do not yield to narratives that discriminate In the same note, Jorge Bergoglio urges all faithful of the Catholic Church, and all men and women of good will, not to yield to narratives that discriminate and unnecessarily cause suffering to our migrant and refugee brothers. A few days before Trump's inauguration, the Pope appointed Cardinal Robert McElroy as Archbishop of Washington, a cleric aligned with his orientations, who had previously spoken out against the mass deportation of illegal immigrants and climate change. In his inaugural address on January 20, Donald Trump said he would expel millions and millions of illegal immigrants to fulfill a campaign promise. Immediately following, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, president of the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), described some of the executive orders issued by Trump in the early stages of his term as deeply troubling. Broglio, who is also the apostolic vicar of the US Armed Forces, stated that the provisions centered on the treatment of immigrants and refugees, foreign aid, the expansion of the death penalty, and the environment are deeply troubling and will have negative consequences, many of which will harm the most vulnerable among us. Other US bishops also expressed similar views, as did the Clamor Network (Latin American and Caribbean Ecclesiastical Network for Migration, Displacement, Refuge, and Human Trafficking). The harsh message of Francis Now the Pope began his letter warning that these words with which I start are not artificially articulated and recalled that the Son of God, by making himself human, also chose to live the drama of immigration. Francis then says that the itinerary of slavery to freedom that the People of Israel traversed, as narrated in the book of Exodus, invites us to look at the reality of our time, so clearly marked by the phenomenon of migration, as a decisive moment in History to reaffirm not only our faith in a God always close, incarnate, migrant, and refugee, but the infinite and transcendent dignity of every human person. Remembering Bergoglio, referring to the social doctrine of the Church and the teachings of Jesus Christ, all Christian faithful and people of good will are called to examine the legitimacy of laws and public policies in the light of the dignity of the person and their fundamental rights, not the other way around. And he points out that a true rule of law is verified precisely in the dignified treatment that all people deserve, especially the poorest and most marginalized. Because the true common good is promoted when society and government, with creativity and strict respect for the rights of all, welcome, protect, promote, and integrate the most fragile, unprotected, and vulnerable. She points out that this does not prevent promoting the maturation of a policy that regulates orderly and legal migration, but warns that the mentioned maturation cannot be built through the privilege of some and the sacrifice of others because what is built based on force, and not on the truth about the equal dignity of all human beings, starts badly and will end badly. Francisco stated that Christians know very well that, only affirming the infinite dignity of all, our own identity as persons and as communities reaches maturity because the human person is a subject with dignity that, through the constitutive relationship with all, especially with the poorest, can gradually mature in their identity and vocation. And he emphasized that worrying about personal, community, or national identity, regardless of these considerations, easily introduces an ideological criterion that distorts social life and imposes the will of the strongest as a criterion of truth. In recognition of all this, the Pope acknowledged the valuable effort of yours, dear bishops of the United States, when working closely with migrants and refugees, announcing Jesus Christ and promoting fundamental human rights.

data.text: Federal police officers arrested a father and his son in different locations in La Matanza, who are accused of sexually abusing a minor. The case originated when the victim, upon reaching adulthood, filed a criminal complaint stating that she was outraged during her childhood by her then-stepfather. The incidents occurred in their family home located in the Bonaerense locality of Gregorio de Laferrere, La Matanza party, between 2010 and 2012, and at the time the victim was 5 and 6 years old. According to her testimony, the abuse occurred while she was under the custody of the suspect, who, using repeated threats of death, managed to remain unpunished and avoid any accusations against him, forcing her to remain silent and perform various sexual practices. Notwithstanding, in the years 2016 and 2017, and within the framework of a family move to another residence located in the neighboring town of La Tablada, the minor was abused again, this time by the aggressor's son. At the end of January of the current year, and once the respective complaint was filed, the Specialized Unit for Instruction and Judgment of Family and Gender Violence and Crimes Against Sexual Integrity N1 of the La Matanza Judicial Department, led by Dr. Pamela Piatelli, summoned the aforementioned PFA Division with the objective of locating and subsequently apprehending the individuals. It was thus that through various field tasks and intelligence, the federal agents identified the whereabouts of the sought-after individuals. Therefore, and with the approval of the La Matanza Guarantees Court, N3, led by Dr. Rubén Norberto Ochipinti, the uniformed officers were able to make their arrests, both in a public setting, on García Merou Street (Gregorio de Laferrere) and Riglos Street (González Catán) respectively. The detainees, adults, were placed at the disposal of the intervening judge for the crime of Grave Sexual Abuse, as it was committed against a minor under 18 years old, taking advantage of the cohabitation situation and committed by the guard in charge, in ideal concurrence with Aggravated Corruption of a Minor.

Judicial Sentence Reduced to a Summary Trial Condemned a Man for Sexually Abusing the Daughters of His Partner BY EDITOR This Wednesday, February 12, a man was condemned for sexually abusing the daughters of his partner. The accused, identified only by the initial V, received a sentence of three years of conditional imprisonment, meaning he will not go to prison, but must comply with a series of behavioral norms. The complaint was filed by the father of the minors, aged 13 and 11, on November 19. According to the report, the victims lived with the abuser from 2021 to 2024, as he was in a relationship with their mother. When left alone with the minors, the accused would take advantage of the situation to touch their intimate parts on repeated occasions. Following the information gathered, the San Juan Justice system condemned the accused for simple sexual abuse through a summary trial, imposing a sentence of three years of conditional sentence. Additionally, he was imposed with conduct guidelines and was prohibited from approaching or maintaining any type of contact with the victims and their families.

The Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) opened a disciplinary incident against former Colonel Jorge Enrique Galarcio Medina for alleged pimping with a minor under 14, which could result in the loss of benefits within transitional justice. The Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) decided to open a disciplinary incident for verification of compliance with the conditional regime against the former Colonel of the Army, identified as Jorge Enrique Galarcio Medina, for acts related to the alleged sexual exploitation of a minor under 14. The process is part of Case 03, Subcase Meta, which investigates the presentation of illegitimate deaths as combat casualties and other conduct attributed to members of the public force. The opening of this disciplinary incident is based on information obtained by the JEP following the referral of a file from the ordinary justice. According to Auto ARA035 of 2025, the Chamber of Recognition of Truth and Responsibility, led by Magistrate Alejandro Ramelli Arteaga, indicates that it was established that, in accordance with the written accusation, the events occurred between April and June 2019, although no exact date is specified. The former military officer, retired from the Army, had previously appeared before the JEP on two occasions for his alleged participation in extrajudicial executions in the Meta region, but did not acknowledge responsibility. It was later known that he had been captured in November 2020 under the alias JorgeMega for allegedly leading a child exploitation network. The documentation sent to the JEP indicates that the former officer faces a criminal process for pandering a minor under 14 years old, in conjunction with the crime of using or facilitating means of communication to offer sexual activities with individuals under 14 years old. The oral trial is advancing in the Twenty-Ninth Penal Circuit Court with Jurisdiction to Know in Bogotá, following several preliminary and preparatory hearings held since 2021. According to the case information, a preventive detention measure was imposed on Galarcio Medina in 2020, but he is currently at liberty due to the expiration of terms from November 22, 2022. In Auto ARA035, the JEP explains that the verification process of compliance with the conditional regime aims to determine whether the defendant would have violated their obligations by committing delinquent acts after December 1, 2016. If such non-compliance is confirmed, the former soldier could lose benefits or even be excluded from the Special Jurisdiction for Peace. The JEP ordered to open the incident of non-compliance and gave a five-day deadline for the defense of Galarcio Medina, the victims, and the Public Ministry to present or request additional evidence. After this stage, the judge Ramelli's office will decide if the defendant committed the conditions of not repeating criminal behavior, which could result in sanctions ranging from suspension of benefits to eventual exclusion from the JEP.

15 massage parlor victims were paying fines if they refused to comply with 5 women arrested in operation 5 women detained in an operation by the Judicial Investigation Organization (OIJ) in different points of San José to detain suspects of committing crimes in massage parlors, were left in total 6 detainees. In the words of Randall Zúñiga, OIJ director, he stated that the women were hired to offer massage services. If they refused, they had to pay a fine. Judicial authorities detained 6 people Morales 32 years (apparent leader of the gang) Godínez 29 years (woman) Ureña 29 years (woman) Vargas 19 years (woman) Barboza 28 years (woman) Picado 39 years (woman) The incidents allegedly occurred since September 2021, in different points of the country such as Pavas, Curridabat, Barrio Escalante, Rohrmoser and Los Yoses. This organization apparently carried out the criminal acts in businesses with a partition that offered massage services. The OIJ indicated that a total of 15 people were offended. The case is under investigation, within case 230000451321PE. The National Court has sentenced the Sevillian Manuel Gerardo Blanco Vela to nine years in prison for sexual aggression crimes committed against three young American students as the responsible party of the company Discover Excursions, when the same students were studying at the universities of Salamanca and Valencia and participating in the trips promoted by said company to Morocco and Portugal in 2013 and 2017, according to the sentence issued by the court last Monday, January 10. In its sentence, the magistrates of the First Section of the Penal Chamber of the National Court impose on the accused, identified as Manuel Blanco Vela, a six-year prison sentence for a crime of aggression with the attenuating circumstance of undue delays in relation to the initial complainant of the case, the Moroccan victim, and two prison sentences of one and a half years each for two sexual aggression crimes in relation to the other two complainants, for the events that occurred in Lagos (Portugal). Additionally, it imposes on him the prohibition of exercising as a tourist guide for seven and a half years and condemns him to indemnify the girl who suffered the sexual aggression in Morocco with €40.00 and €1,500.00 to each of the other two victims, despite acknowledging that it is not possible to automatically translate moral harm into money and that the only thing we can do is value the importance of the harm in attention to the circumstances of the victims and try to convert that estimate into a specific monetary sum. The sentence is thus confined to broad outlines to the prosecution's request, which had requested the accused nine years in prison for a presumed sex crime, rape, and two alleged sex abuses, currently three sex crimes of different typification as well as six years of prohibition from approaching the first victim or communicating with her, one year of the same prohibition with regard to each of the two subsequent victims and eight years of disqualification for the profession of tourist guide and that compensates with 40,000 euros to the first victim and with 1,500 euros to each of the two remaining ones. The private prosecution, on the other hand, requested a total of 23 years in prison, as well as a compensation of 600,000 euros for the first young woman and 150,000 euros each of the two following ones, while the defense had asked for his acquittal.

data.text: A suspected sex abuser was hiding behind the facade of a taxi driver to attack women in Cúcuta, Norte de Santander. Authorities arrested him in the last hours. It is Elkin Jesús Barbosa García, who was arrested near the Modelo Prison, after attacking his last victim. This man, according to the investigation carried out by the authorities, had a pattern of attack established. Caught in the act It was 9:35 p.m. when a woman was thrown from a moving taxi, the violent scene was observed by a police patrol that was making rounds of vigilance in the El Salado neighborhood. Immediately, they made the signal to stop the taxi driver, but he ignored it. In this situation, a pursuit was initiated, which extended over several blocks until they were able to intercept and prevent him from escaping. While this was happening, the woman, who suffered several injuries due to the strong blow, was assisted and taken to the Basic Community Unit, where she recounted the nightmare she lived after getting into that taxi. According to the woman's statement to the authorities, she took a taxi service to get to her residence and, in the middle of the trip, the driver began to threaten her, demanding that she undress. When she refused, the man not only committed indecent touching in her intimate areas, but also hit her repeatedly. When the victim resisted, he opted to violently throw her out of the moving vehicle. The taxi driver, according to the complaint, was Elkin Jesús Barbosa García, who was caught in flagrante delito for the crime of sexual abuse. A Serial Abuser. After being made aware of this case, the authorities determined that the modus operandi of Barbosa García matched other complaints filed in previous months by women who were victims of sexual violence after getting into the taxi driven by this man. In December 2024, for example, the Police reported that a woman had filed a complaint stating that the same taxi driver had assaulted her, but in that instance, in addition to threatening and attacking her, he had also sexually assaulted her. According to the authorities, the pattern of attack by Elkin Jesús Barbosa García consisted of cruising the streets of Cúcuta at night and picking up solo women along the way, intimidating them to subject them to his sexual desires. If the victims resisted, he would resort to violence to subdue them. These findings reinforce the hypothesis that this is not an isolated case, but rather a serial sex predator who used his job as a cover to attack vulnerable women. Barbosa García was turned over to the Prosecutor's Office and presented before a judge of guarantees, who ordered a measure of assurance in a prison center while the judicial process against him continues. The authorities are calling on the women who have been victims of this man to come forward to the Prosecutor's Office and file a complaint.

The National Court has sentenced the Seville tourist guide Manuel Gerardo B.V. to nine years in prison for sexual aggression crimes committed against three American young students as the responsible of the Discover Excursions company, when the students were studying at the universities of Salamanca and Valencia and participating in the trips promoted by that company to Morocco and Portugal in 2013 and 2017, according to the sentence issued by the court last Monday, January 10. In its sentence, distributed by the National Court itself, the judges of the First Section of the Criminal Chamber impose on Manuel Gerardo B.V. a six-year prison sentence for a crime of aggression with the attenuating circumstance of undue delays in relation to the initial denouncer of the case, the victim from Morocco, and two prison sentences of one and a half years for two sexual aggression crimes regarding the two remaining denouncers, for the incidents that occurred in Lagos (Portugal). Additionally, the court imposes a ban on him working as a tour guide for seven and a half years and sentences him to compensate 40,000 euros to the first Moroccan victim and 1,500 euros to each of the other two victims, despite acknowledging that it is not possible to automatically translate moral damage into money and that the only thing we can do is assess the importance of the damage according to the circumstances of the victims. He is also sentenced to seven and a half years of post-penitentiary supervised liberty, six years of prohibition from approaching the first victim or communicating with her, and one year of the same measure of distancing himself from each of the remaining two victims. The sentence thus almost entirely coincides with the Public Prosecutor's Office's request, which had requested nine years in prison for the accused for a presumed sex crime, rape, and two alleged sex abuse crimes, currently three sex crimes of different typification as well as six years of prohibition from approaching the first victim or communicating with her, one year of the same prohibition with regard to each of the two subsequent victims and eight years of disqualification for the profession of tour guide and that he compensate with 40,000 euros to the first victim and with 1,500 euros to each of the two remaining ones. The private accusation, on the other hand, requested a total of 23 years in prison, as well as a compensation of 600,000 euros for the first young woman and 150,000 euros each of the two following ones while the defense had requested his acquittal, since he has always denied any crime. Proven Facts The convicting sentence, subject to appeal, declares proven that in the framework of the trip promoted by the company Discover Excursions in November 2013 to Morocco, the last night before returning to Spain, on November 2, at a hotel in Tangier, the accused approached the initial complainant of the case, an American student then affiliated with the University of Salamanca, and her roommates, when they were on the hotel's patio bar. The defendant, according to the sentence, proposed that they drink champagne in their room, to which they agreed, and once in the room they shared, the accused, while they were drinking the champagne, proposed a game of truth or dare and challenged them to remove their t-shirts, which they refused, but he removed his clothes except for his underwear. According to the verdict, the victim started feeling very tired and fell asleep, and upon waking up, she found herself alone in the room, and went to the bathroom, where she saw her friends in the shower in their tank tops with the defendant in his underwear. Once the three of them left the bathroom, she entered and sat on the toilet, according to the account of proven facts, which adds that then the accused entered the bathroom in a surprising manner, introducing his penis into the girl's mouth, who then fell to the ground, becoming unconscious, something that the accused denied. In Portugal, the verdict addresses the events related to the other two victims, American students from the Florida State University of Valencia, on the night of May 28, 2017, the last day of the trip to Lagos promoted by the company of the accused at that time. According to the account of proven facts, the accused gave these young women drink tickets at a bar, inviting them afterwards to attend a party in his hotel room, which they accepted under the belief that more people would be attending, even though upon arriving at the room in the dead of night, they realized that there were no other guests. In the room, according to the account of proven facts, the accused asked if they could make themselves more comfortable, removing his pants and remaining in his underwear. After that, according to the condemnatory sentence, he asked them about their sexual experiences, proposed playing truth or dare, and at a certain moment, after they refused his proposals of a sexual nature, he told them to remove their pants, to which the two women refused, asking him, as if it were a challenge, if they kissed their tour guide. Both of them kissed her on the cheek and, despite her insistence, they gave her a superficial kiss on the lips, the verdict states that the young women refused the more sexual dance he asked for, after which the defendant, with the intention of satisfying his sexual desires, grabbed one of her right hands and the other of her left, immobilizing them in a corner of the room. They wanted to leaveWhen one of the victims tried to free herself, saying she wanted to leave, he responded, according to the account of proven facts, that she should not do so because they had been "turned on," with one of the girls kissing him and placing the hand of the other young woman on his genitals, after which both were finally able to leave the room.For the conviction, the court takes the testimony as true and credible from the first complainant, persistent in the fundamental, without appreciating that with it she obtains a benefit or lends it out of enmity or resentment. It is true that the complaint was filed a long time after the fact, practically five years. The fact that it took years to report the incidents does not diminish credibility, as not all women react in the same way to an attack on their sexual freedom, and in this case, the victim recounts in an absolutely coherent manner why she reported the incidents years later, stating concretely that she did so upon learning of other women who have been victims of the same perpetrator. Her statement is also corroborated by peripheral testimonies, such as the testimony of the victims of the incidents that occurred in Portugal and that of the police officers investigating the incidents. The court thus highlights the identical pattern reported by the victims in this procedure and those with whom the police officers have contacted. It involves, explains, foreign female students, Americans, who embark on a trip where the accused serves as their guide, gaining their trust by displaying kindness, being well-mannered, appearing confident in what he does, and having knowledge of the cities. Following this, the assault on the victims occurs at the last moment, on the last day of the trip, so that they have fewer possibilities of reacting.In the execution of the facts, the judgment continues, the author follows the same pattern. He approaches the young women, all very young, in a friendly manner, invites them to have a drink and play the same game, finally intending to attack their sexual freedom, concludes.

Edixon Jesús Sánchez, 56 years old, was arrested by officers from the Bolivarian Police Corps of the Zulia State (Cpbez) after being denounced for continued sexual abuse against his step-daughter, a 13-year-old adolescent. The unfortunate incident occurred in the Servio Tulio Peña sector, Libertad parish, Machiques de Perijá municipality. The complaint arose from the educational institution where the minor studies, where the young woman revealed to her teacher that she was forced by her stepfather to maintain sexual relations with him. According to the testimony of the young woman, Sánchez forced her to perform orogenital sex acts and supplied her with birth control pills. After being informed of the complaint, the police officials went to the location where Sánchez was found and proceeded with his detention. The detained individual was taken to the Machiques Police Coordination Center and placed under the jurisdiction of the 20th Prosecution Office of the Public Ministry. . Meanwhile, the teenager was transferred to Our Lady of Carmen Hospital to receive medical and psychological attention.

Prosecutor Mónica Cuñarro requested a dismissal due to lack of evidence against Matanza's mayor, Fernando Espinoza, who is charged in the case for alleged sexual abuse of his former private secretary, Melody Rakauskas. Cuñarro acted in response to a request from the judge in the case, Fernando Caunedo, following a complaint to elevate the process to oral trial. According to Cuñarro's arguments, there are no elements of proof in the case files that support the charges, beyond the statements of the complainant. The simple sexual abuse case was opened in 2021 after Rakauskas reported that Espinoza attempted to abuse her during a meeting outside of work hours. In July 2024, the Court of Crime had ratified the prosecution of the mayor for the crimes of sexual abuse and disobedience to a judicial order.

The District South Prosecution Office is investigating a complaint from the parent of a minor regarding alleged sexual abuse. A 24-year-old man was detained in connection with the case, who nearly suffered a lynching by the family and neighbors of the young girl when they discovered the alleged sexual abuse. Police and judicial sources consulted by this newspaper reported that on Tuesday around 10:00 p.m., personnel from the Rapid Intervention Group (GIR South) arrived at a residence in the Santa Marta neighborhood, where there was a disturbance. Upon arrival, the officers saw a subject lying on the ground while being kicked by a group of people surrounding him. In the face of the situation, the uniformed officers approached and rescued the subject being beaten, then dialogued with one of the people attacking him. This person claimed to be the father of a minor and stated that the person they had rescued had sexually abused their daughter. After hearing the neighbor's account, the police arrested the accused subject and took him to the Ninth Police Station, where he was examined by SAME personnel. Meanwhile, the child's parent and alleged victim went to Judicial Unit N 9 and filed a complaint against the 24-year-old for allegedly sexually abusing his daughter. Notified of the complaint from the Southern District Attorney's Office, it was ordered that the child undergo a sexual abuse protocol and receive necessary containment. In the Santa Marta neighborhood, a young man accused of abuse was lynched by the family of a girl. The prosecutor ordered the child to undergo a sexual abuse protocol and receive containment. There is a new arrest order. Evo's defense tries to take the human trafficking case to Cochabamba. The resolution dismissing the appeal also warns that the defense cannot file another appeal to reverse its declaration of rebellion, as a result of its refusal to appear before the Justice. This Wednesday it was confirmed that the First Penal Chamber of the Departmental Court of Justice (TDJ) declared the incidental appeal inadmissible, with which the defense of Evo Morales Ayma sought to paralyze the process for alleged human trafficking, that is, it confirms the declaration of rebellion and there is a new arrest order. The resolution signed by the Chamber President, Luis Esteban Ortiz Flores, and the vocal Claudia Gamarra Hoyos, does not admit a subsequent appeal, that is, it is unappealable. Following the indictment, on January 14, the first precautionary hearing that was to be held before the Penal Instruction Court, Anticorruption, Against Violence to Women Fifth of the Capital was suspended because Morales supposedly was ill. He was supposed to appear on the 17th, but he did not. The judge Nelson Rocabado considered that there was no valid justification, so he issued a declaration of rebellion, a warrant for apprehension, the freezing of his accounts, the annotation of his assets, and his arrest. The defense presented an incidental appeal, but the Penal Chamber did not admit the appeal and validated the judge Rocabado's decision. Declares the incidental appeal inadmissible. It is warned to the parties that the present resolution does not admit any subsequent appeal, as stated in its conclusion. Additionally, it is pointed out in a previous paragraph that defiance is considered a direct consequence of the defendant's procedural attitude, who does not appear for a judicial summons without a valid justification. Defense attorney Cecilia Urquieta assured that the process aims to incapacitate Evo Morales in the general elections and pointed out that she will continue her strategy to extinguish the case or transfer it to Cochabamba. Although, there are already rulings that confirm that the process will proceed in Tarija. After the resolution of the Penal Chamber, Judge Rocabado issued a new warrant of apprehension for the police to bring the former president to the courtroom. Minister of Government Eduardo Del Castillo had previously stated that there is already an order of operations, but he awaits the indicated moment.

A member of the Aragua Train, who was being sought for murder in Dallas, was captured in early February in Houston, Texas, during a federal deportation operation. The detained individual, whose identity is not being disclosed for legal reasons, had been hiding in an apartment in a neighborhood known for its high crime rate and large immigrant population. ICE officers received information about the gang member's presence after he was seen walking his dog. For hours, agents, along with other federal agencies, conducted surveillance at the location, waiting for the target to emerge again. When he finally appeared, he was surprised by several agents who surrounded him as he crossed the residential complex courtyard. He surrendered immediately, visibly surprised by the situation. The agents had a warrant for his arrest issued by the Dallas authorities, and their plan was to apprehend him at a time when he would not have the possibility of defending himself. This arrest is part of a series of detention operations that have resulted in more than 11,000 arrests of undocumented immigrants in just the first 18 days of the Trump administration, which seeks to intensify these actions. On the same day, the FBI arrested three suspected members of the Aragua Train in another Houston complex, linked to a sex trafficking network operating in several states. Images of this event, shared on social media, showed FBI and Department of Homeland Security agents detaining the individuals involved. The director of the ICE office in Houston, Bret Bradford, described the arrest of the gang member as a great victory, arguing that a suspected killer is being taken off the streets. He denied that indiscriminate arrests would take place and assured that the operations are carefully directed, with a focus on the most dangerous offenders. The Aragua Train has been mentioned in multiple incidents of violence in the United States, which has generated concern and a call to authorities regarding the growing criminality linked to this organization.

data.text: A 19-year-old man from El Churqui, Jiménez department, who had sexual relations with a 14-year-old relative, and under deceit, encouraged her to commit suicide, has been detained in a cell. The decision was made by Dr. Diego Martín Vittar, judge of Control and Guarantees for the Río Hondo and Jiménez Circumscription, who ordered preventive detention. The magistrate accepted the request of Dr. Rafael Zanni, a member of the Fiscal Unit of that jurisdiction, who accuses the defendant of simple sexual abuse, the old crime of statutory rape, and instigation to commit suicide. The teenager attempted to commit suicide three times using a diving suit given to her by the accused, but was unable to do so. Some details The 5th of January of the current year, the minor had attended the celebration for a 15-year-old classmate's birthday, which took place in the Cachico area, where the accused arrived on his motorcycle and asked the victim to go with him to his house. However, while they were traveling on a nearby road in a mountainous area of the Suri Pozo locality, the accused stopped the vehicle and incited the minor to commit suicide, making her hang from a tree with a rope tied around her neck, but the element came loose since it had been poorly tied. After two more attempts, the teenager gave up and the individual left the scene, leaving her abandoned. It was then that the minor called her relatives to come and pick her up. The girl revealed that she had been having sex with the accused for some time, indicating that he was afraid that the parents would find out and something bad would happen, so he didn't know what else to do but tell the minor to commit suicide and that he would do the same, but that didn't happen only by a miracle.Prosecutor's Request After the complaint was filed, the individual was detained and charged with the crimes of sexual abuse with access due to the exploitation of the victim's sexual immaturity, and instigation to commit suicide. Zanni warned about the risks of procedural hazards, and asked to issue a coercive measure against the accused.

The harassment and abuse suffered by Nicaraguan women and adolescents on a daily basis on public transportation has once again come to light. Citizen Griselda Blandón, through her social media, denounced that her niece was a victim of harassment and touching by three individuals, who took advantage of the fact that the unit in which the young woman was traveling was overcrowded. The young woman boarded a bus on the Matagalpa-Jinotega route, operated by Transportes Rodríguez of the Cooperativa Transporte InterUrbano Norte, and, according to Blandón, the unit was so crowded that it couldn't even hold a pin. Three men harassed her from head to toe. She told them to leave her alone and hit them with the water bottle she had. She told the bus attendant (ticket collector) and he ignored her, denounced the citizen Blandón reported that the staff in charge of the service provided in the unit were omitted, and he even confronted them at the Cotran Norte, but they denied that the young woman had asked for help. The driver and assistant denying that my niece had asked for help. No one did anything, no one helped, Blandón pointed out.Cooperative defends version of its workersThe Cooperativa Transporte InterUrbano Norte, through its social media, released a statement in which it affirms that its personnel were never notified by the young woman of the situation of harassment and abuse that she faced during the trip, which began in Matagalpa and ended in Jinotega. They also assured that they are not indifferent to the young woman's uncomfortable and fearful moment, as she deserves to be respected as a woman. Blandón questioned that the Cooperative and its personnel, with their statements, implied that the young woman had lied. They think a young girl is going to lie about that, it's ridiculous, why nobody came forward, you think by giving a statement the girl will calm down or is it that you only care about the integrity of the cooperative, she wrote on her Facebook account in response to the Cooperative. It may interest you: What every Nicaraguan should know about street harassment. The buses are running that there's no room for even a pin because they're stingy. You, as directors of the Cooperative, should have summoned me and my niece, not just sticking to your illustrious versions, she added. The feminists and women's rights defenders of Las Venancias, through social media, denounced the street harassment and sexual abuse of which the young girl was a victim and pointed out that as a result of that complaint, other testimonies from women emerged who confirmed that they had experienced the same in that unit and in other buses in the northern zone of Nicaragua, and despite requesting it, they did not receive any help. Urgent action is needed from authorities. The defenders urged not only public transportation workers and owners, but also passengers, who daily board buses in the country, to do something to stop the aggression against women, and not to normalize the violence. The impact of this type of harassment generates stress and trauma for women who are forced to use public transportation and, even when they raise their voices to defend themselves, they are ignored, and are revictimized again, the defenders emphasized. Read also: A woman was threatened with a knife, another was injured with a nail, and another was touched inappropriately; women recount the violence and abuse they suffer in Managua. A human rights defender, in an interview with LA PRENSA, denounced that the harassment against women is part of the macho violence that manifests itself daily in all public spaces. She pointed out that in Nicaragua, women daily suffer from touching, lewd stares, and genital rubbing, the latter especially in collective transportation units, which are the favorite scenario for aggressors who perpetrate such actions due to being always overcrowded. She noted that unfortunately in Nicaragua, there are no measures from the State or any other space, cooperatives, bus owners, or the general population to reduce the harassment, let alone to penalize and sanction the harassers. The Venancias, in consonance with what was expressed to the press by the defender, demanded that the authorities of Nicaragua respond officially to this denunciation and ensure an exemplary punishment not only for the direct aggressors, but also for the transportation unit workers, who denied help while a crime was being committed.

data.text: It's not that there is a lack of tools. The Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, approved by the United Nations General Assembly, has been in effect for 23 years, and Colombia is a signatory. It obliges signatory states to prevent the recruitment and use of children and adolescents by armed groups, as well as to attend to those who have been their victims. February 12 was also chosen to commemorate International Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers, a symbolization aimed at rejecting these crimes. However, Colombia cannot just limit itself to commemorative and visibility activities for programs because it is failing to comply with this Protocol. The State has failed and we have failed as a society. We must take immediate action to stop exposing our minors to harm, because the armed conflict and its actors continue to be a threat, and there are no guarantees to protect them, not even from the Colombian Institute of Family Welfare, which is responsible for this population. UN figures confirm this. 44,102 children and adolescents displaced by the armed conflict and violence in Colombia throughout 2024 and 433 severe violations against this population in 2023. Additionally, the Ombudsman's Office presents a dark picture of the recruitment of minors in the country last year, 409 of whom, 61% boys and 39% girls, fell into the hands of guerrillas, dissidents, and other armed groups, (300 in the Cauca department). This represents a significant increase compared to the 342 cases in 2023. In the 44 days of 2025, we worsened if we consider the violent incursions in Catatumbo, Arauca, Cauca, and Chocó, but there are also records of recruitment and use of minors in other departments, so everyone knows that these are war crimes, even for the guerrilla fighters themselves. No minor can be there to watch roads and points of sale for illicit activities, carry messages, transport drugs and supplies, learn to handle weapons and war tactics, collect extortion money, be an informant for the Public Force, do hard work in camps, be subjected to sexual abuse, among many other crimes pointed out by the Ombudsman. Neither children nor adolescents should be separated from their families, their environments, and their age-appropriate activities to favor armed groups and swell their ranks. This cannot be allowed by governments, but it is well known that many are recruited voluntarily through deceit, under threats, or by force. It's not just a matter of asking for a specific date to stop the recruitment and use of minors, but to demand through legal mechanisms that it not be done because there is a current protocol, otherwise, issue arrest warrants for those committing crimes. Children and adolescents must be protected subjects, they cannot continue to be exploited and abused for war.
