data.text: A 36-year-old man, Felipe A. M., a 36-year-old turner by profession, was detained for allegedly molesting a 10-year-old girl whom he picked up from school. Accused of sexual abuse against a 10-year-old girl, Felipe A. M. was arrested today. Agents and investigators from the Secretariat of Public Security (SSP) and the State Attorney General's Office (FGE) presented evidence to a judge, based on which he issued an arrest warrant. The girl's father filed a complaint in which it is stated that Felipe A. M. allegedly committed lewd acts against the victim on January 30 in a vehicle parked in the streets of the Ciudad Caucel subdivision, threatening to harm her and her family if she reported the incident. The individual, from Mérida, Yucatán, was placed at the judge's disposal.

The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Service, commonly known as ICE, released a report on its operations from February 1 to 7 across the entire American territory. It stated that during this period, it carried out a series of strengthened immigration control operations in Baltimore, Maryland; Charleston, South Carolina; Hillsboro, Texas; Denver, Colorado; Washington, D.C.; and New York City. ICE reported on the most notable operations in which several immigrants were captured who were being sought by the justice system for various crimes. The immigration service's balance reports a Guatemalan immigrant from Baltimore, accused of breaking and entering and possession of a firearm, a Mexican undocumented immigrant captured in Texas, who was being sought in Hidalgo, Mexico for aggravated homicide, and a Mexican undocumented immigrant detained in Philadelphia due to a history of arrests for driving under the influence and for having re-entered the United States on multiple occasions in an illegal manner. In ICE's report, mention is also made of several arrests of suspected members of the MS13 criminal gang, the arrest in Texas of a Venezuelan citizen, suspected member of the so-called Tren de Aragua, a suspected member of the Gulf Cartel, and a man from Hudson County who had a sentence for possession of child pornography. Regarding the New York territory, ICE stated that they detained an undocumented immigrant of Ecuadorian origin, convicted of third-degree sexual abuse. Kail Sebastian Cardenas Aguirre, 27 years old, was arrested in New York City on February 3, according to the Immigration Service report. ICE emphasized that their efforts are initially focused on undocumented immigrants who have committed crimes. ICE gives high priority to identifying, arresting, and deporting foreign criminals who pose a threat to public safety and national security, said the Acting Field Office Director for Enforcement and Removal Operations in New York City, William P. Joyce. According to the ICE report, Cardenas was admitted to the United States as a non-immigrant on May 15, 2021, in New York and violated the terms of his admission. The New York City Police Department arrested Cárdenas on March 9, 2023, and charged him with sexual abuse and carnal abuse. He was found guilty of third-degree sexual abuse for subjecting another person to unwanted sexual contact on January 13, and sentenced to probation, according to the ICE report. Cárdenas will remain in ICE custody pending his deportation. ICE stated that daily routine operations continue, operating in conjunction with enhanced enforcement operations that involve federal law enforcement partnerships with the FBI, DEA, ATF, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Marshals Service for a government-wide approach.

The Departmental Prosecutor of Beni, Gerardo Balderas Arteaga, reported that, in an oral trial hearing, the Public Prosecutor's Office presented conclusive evidence that Pablo P.Q., 77 years old, is the perpetrator of the aggravated sexual abuse of an 11-year-old girl, a crime that occurred in 2023 in the municipality of Trinidad. In response, the Penal, Anti-Corruption, and Violence Against Women Court No. 1 sentenced the defendant to 15 years in prison at the Mocoví Penitentiary. The case prosecutor, Aldryn Roca, stated that the incident occurred in a residence in Trinidad and was discovered on December 5, 2023. The 11-year-old victim lived in the home of her aunt, where the 77-year-old man worked as a caregiver. The perpetrator took advantage of the victim's isolation at night to make indecent advances, a behavior that repeated itself on multiple occasions.

Judge Marcela Vargas had ruled a week ago that Gustavo Penadés, former senator of the Republic, and Sebastián Mauvezín, history professor, would serve home detention under electronic monitoring. The 4th Criminal Appeals Court overturned this Wednesday the judge's decision after the Prosecution appealed her ruling that ordered home detention for Penadés and Mauvezín, who are charged with sex-related crimes linked to minors. The prosecutor for Sexual Crimes, Alicia Ghione, was the one who requested the extension of the preventive detention measure until June 10, 2025, while the investigation continues. Penadés and Mauvezín were charged on October 10, 2023. Penadés is charged with 22 sex-related crimes against minors, and Mauvezín is charged with seven crimes of contributing to the sexual exploitation of minors.

A basketball coach in Granada accused of a suspected sex attack on three minors in Granada Following the man's statement, the head of Instruction agreed to his provisional release without adopting any type of precautionary measures The Investigating Court number 5 of Granada, on duty, has taken a statement from a basketball coach of a sports club in Granada, who is being investigated for a sex-related crime, following the complaint presented by at least three of the players. According to judicial sources, the man was placed at the disposal of the judiciary on February 4th and has been released on provisional liberty while the investigation is ongoing, without the adoption of precautionary measures. According to judicial sources, the instruction phase has just begun and the National Police has taken charge of this case. Now the case is pending the Public Prosecutor's Office informing in favor or against the dump of the mobile phone data of the investigated person. The same judicial sources have specified that, for the moment, it is still to be determined what type of crime will be investigated and it will be the instruction of the case that will determine whether the accusations represent a crime of sexual aggression or sexual abuse, or, on the contrary, the case will be dismissed. For now, the complainants have not made a judicial statement and the court will summon three alleged victims in the coming days to do so. The coach has been fired. The sports club where the investigated person worked has sent a statement to the families indicating that, after being informed of the alleged abuses, it activated the protocol provided for such cases and, among other actions, fired the coach. The entity has stated that it is facing its first case of this type and that the coach, who has already been removed, was not a newcomer, but had been linked to the entity for several years. For the time being, the age of the minors who allegedly were victims of sexual aggression by this sports monitor is unknown. The Granadian club where the investigated coach was a coach has members of different ages, from children to adolescents.

Hospitalillo de San José in Getafe will host a Diocesan Vigil of prayer and reflection against human trafficking on Friday, February 14, at 7:30 PM, as part of the XI global celebration of the Day of Action. In the course of the Vigil prepared by the Human Trafficking Department of the diocese, the theme of the Day of Action "Ambassadors of Hope together against human trafficking" will be remembered, which aims to report, raise awareness, and raise consciousness about a reality suffered by millions of people worldwide, and this year, it is framed within the Jubilee of Hope. All the faithful of the diocese who want to pray for the end of this scourge are invited to the call. Isi Curieses, member of the human trafficking team of the diocese, explains that the Vigil will consist of a prayer with testimonies of people who have been victims of human trafficking. Some will share it in person, and others, the team will read it on their behalf. We want to thank you for your strength, your resilience, and for having been able to escape that time of slavery. Thank you to the people who have accompanied you on those tortuous paths. It's a thank you to God and it's to put before God this reality of suffering and also of liberation and survival of these people who in this case are women, she relates.Curieses emphasizes that it's essential to explain what human trafficking consists of. First, we talk about a crime that is specifically defined as such and all the situations where the person is caught, threatened, often through deception or other means with the aim of being exploited at different levels. Sexual exploitation is one of the goals, but there's also labor exploitation, for committing crimes, the whole issue of organ trafficking... In short, there's a very, very broad typification of the people being trafficked. Now in Spain, especially, it is rising with the aim of labor exploitation and with the aim of committing crimes, it is assured. The great challenge that the Church, in general, and the Diocesan Department of Trafficking, in particular, faces is to make this reality visible, which is near us, in our neighborhoods, where we live, to unmask the underlying causes of trafficking, such as, for example, the entire business behind it, all the profits made by many people with a lot of money, and it is a continuous work that must be done slowly. SEXUAL ABUSE The court requested 15 years in prison for rower Néstor Piri Pinta for covering up the abuse The multiple winner of the Río Negro Regatta is accused of covering up the abuse committed by his father. The trial against Néstor Piri Pinta, a renowned rower and former Sports Director of Patagones, reached a decisive moment. The victims' lawyer requested a 15-year prison sentence for covering up the sexual abuse that his father allegedly committed against two students of the rowing school that he himself directed. The multiple winner of the Río Negro Regatta was the rowing school's coach and would take his students to have a snack at his father's house after training, where his father would give the girls massages. Aldo Pinta committed suicide on the same day he learned of the girls' denunciation in the Justice of Buenos Aires. According to the accusations, the man, under the pretext of loosening his muscles, would take advantage of the situation to sexually abuse the young women, locking them in a room The victims stated that during this period, Pinta would have had knowledge of the facts and would not have acted to stop his father's maneuvers. The trial took place in Bahía Blanca and set a precedent in the region as it was the first case in which the debate was conducted without the direct intervention of the prosecution. In her argument, lawyer María Fernanda Petersen emphasized that the presented evidence, including the statements of the victims and the psychological reports, reinforces the accusation against Pinta. All the accredited evidence reinforces the accused's responsibility, the lawyer stated. Pinta was charged in 2021, but at the time the prosecution failed to prove the accused's involvement in the facts, which led to the request for his acquittal. However, the complaint appealed the decision, and the Penal Chamber determined the continuation of the trial with a divided verdict. The defense of Pinta, represented by attorney Maximiliano De Mira, requested the nullification of the trial, arguing the lack of conclusive evidence directly incriminating him. In addition, De Mira requested the prosecution of one of the witnesses for false testimony and the acquittal of his client. Judge Daniela Castaño, presiding over Criminal Court 3, has the responsibility of deciding Pinta's fate. The verdict will be announced on the following Thursday, February 20th at noon, and the community of Patagones, as well as the sports realm, remain attentive to the outcome of this case that has caused great commotion in the region. The accusation against Néstor Pinta Piri was a recognized and a source of pride for his people. With a record of rowing competitions on the Negro River won, he had enough merit to lead the canoeing school. Trainings ended at his father's house, where students would have a snack With the excuse of giving them massages, Aldo Pinta would take the students to the bedroom, close the door, and begin to apply cream and with his hands try to relax their muscles. However, things went further with the girls. In the complaints, the victims clearly state that he inserted his fingers into their vagina. The accusers assure that Piri's father's attitudes were not unknown to Piri, who nonetheless continued with the snacks as the end of the training. Aldo Pinta took his own life on June 30, 2020, when he found out that the victims had ratified the complaint against him at the Bahía Blanca prosecutor's office. The criminal action against him lapsed due to his death, however the trial continued against his son, considering him an accomplice for covering up the abuses.

Thieves stole a truck and drove it away at gunpoint with a car. Two individuals with strong criminal backgrounds were detained last night after the crime that occurred in the Vista Alegre area. Two men with strong delinquent backgrounds and convictions were detained because they allegedly stole a truck and drove it away at gunpoint with a car in the Vista Alegre area. The crime originated in the middle of the day yesterday and, by nightfall, led to the apprehensions of Maximiliano Héctor Toto, 37 years old, and Walter Tello, 41. It happened when two people arrived at Pacífico 2471 and took possession of a Ford F100 truck, with license plate CSL 344, that was present at the scene, belonging to a 60-year-old neighbor. Personnel from the investigative office of the Quinta police station intervened in the incident and, thanks to the support of the CEUM cameras, it was established that the vehicle had been stolen at gunpoint with a Renault Megane, with registration number DKI 095. The sweep allowed the authors to be intercepted, around 20:30, in the Charlone 2450 area. In this way, they were also able to recover the Ford and seize the Renault used for the crime. Both accused were placed at the disposal of UFIJ N° 7. At the time of his arrest, Tello presented an active arrest order from the 3rd Guarantees Court, for possession and carrying of a firearm without the necessary authorization. He also has a record for other property-related crimes. Toto, on the other hand, has convictions in the context of a case involving human trafficking and was also linked to the supposed gang led by the Vidal Ríos brothers.

La Paz, 12 Feb (Xinhua) The Bolivian justice system issued a new arrest warrant today, Wednesday, against former President (2006-2019) Evo Morales for crimes of human trafficking and statutory rape, after his appeal was rejected by the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court (south). The order, signed by Judge Nelson Rocabado, instructs the Special Force Against Crime to apprehend him, given that on January 27, the First Penal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court declared the appeal inadmissible, warning that the resolution issued does not admit further appeal. The former head of state is being investigated by the Tarija Prosecutor's Office for his relationship in 2016 with Cindy Saraí, when she was a minor and he was the President of Bolivia, and from which a daughter was born. In this regard, the State Attorney General, Roger Mariaca, reaffirmed that following the rejection of the appeal, the arrest warrant is reinstated and must be executed by the Police, and in which a prosecutor may intervene in case of a search. Last January 17, after not presenting himself to testify for the second time, Morales was declared in contempt by the justice system, thus confirming the existing arrest warrant since October 2022, and an order was issued to freeze his accounts and assets. The former president is holed up in his stronghold in Chapare, Cochabamba department (center), his political stronghold, where he has the support of hundreds of coca growers who have warned of a possible social convulsion in case of his detention. In response to this, the Minister of Government, Carlos Eduardo del Castillo, stated on Monday that the operational order to apprehend them is ready, but we are waiting for the precise moment and location to execute it without generating confrontations and avoiding the loss of human lives.

Courts Admit Elder Abuse in a Nursing Home J.Moreno Thursday, February 13, 2025 The Prosecution Agrees to Impose a Fine on Honorio, a Geriatric Auxiliary for at Least 18 Years, for Rubbing His Genitals Against an Alzheimer's Patient in a Nursing Home in the Torrijos District (Toledo) Court Admits Elder Abuse and Spares Prison Honorio Waited Outside the Provincial Court Yesterday with a Backpack, a Padded Jacket, and Jeans. He Departed with His Lawyer Waiting for the Trial. In the End, He Decided to Admit the Facts with Brief Yeses. This Man Worked for 18 Years as a Geriatric Auxiliary in a Nursing Home in the Torrijos District and Admitted Yesterday in the First Section of the Provincial Court to Committing a Crime of Sexual Abuse on a Resident Diagnosed with Alzheimer's, Considered a Particularly Vulnerable Victim. The agreement with the Prosecution Office implies evading a prison sentence if it includes the imposition of a fine of 22 months at a rate of six euros per day. In this way, the accused admitted to undressing the 80-year-old and entering her in the private bathroom of the room. It was October 7, 2021, after midnight. The worker, now 65 years old and who delivered medication to residents at that hour, placed the victim leaning on the sink, positioned himself behind her, lowered his pants and underwear, and began at that moment to rub his genitals against the buttocks and the back of the body of the 80-year-old elderly woman. The other auxiliary who was on duty that night at the Torrijos comarca residence surprised the accused in this act. The woman ran out of the resident's room and was followed by the accused, who repeatedly asked his companion to keep quiet about what had happened, according to the prosecution's indictment, which initially sought three years in prison for the incident.The agreement with the prosecution followed the legislation in effect in 2021, which was more beneficial for the defendant than the subsequent reform of the Penal Code. In addition to the economic fine, the pact prohibits Honorio from approaching the elderly woman within 500 meters for five years and includes a 3,500 euro compensation to the woman for moral damages.The forensic expert who examined the resident concluded that the 80-year-old woman presented moderate cognitive decline in the context of a delusional dementia of Alzheimer's disease, a chronic and irreversible progressive disorder. The court in Torrijos that was handling the case issued a ruling on October 9, 2021, that prohibited the defendant from approaching within 150 meters of the elderly residence, the octogenarian's home, as well as any of the residents. Honorio, with the bag slung over his body during the hearing, left the first section courtroom of the Provincial Court without even speaking with his lawyer.

A Bolivian man was detained by Carabineros after verbally assaulting a couple of officials from the institution who were carrying out traffic duties in the center of Iquique, Tarapacá Region. The apprehended individual, in addition, touched the body of a female police officer, which led to his formalization for the crime of surprise sexual abuse. After the apprehension, the system also revealed that the captured individual had an outstanding arrest warrant for other crimes. Colonel Adrían Andrades, prefect of Carabineros in Iquique, reported that the incident occurred in the afternoon of Monday. A Carabinero and a Carabinero were carrying out traffic duties when an unknown individual initially began insulting the officials, despite the Carabinera's recommendation for the individual to leave the area. This, without any provocation, and in response to an irrational and dishonest act, struck the police officer with his hand on the buttocks, and as a result, he was detained. The officer added that once detained, the foreign citizen threatened to kill and verbally uttered a large number of incoherent statements, requiring the assistance of a patrol to be transported to the police station. The Estrella de Iquique reported that from the institution, it was explained that currently the police officer is supported by his peers, in addition to the legal support that the institution will provide, which is being done through the legal advisor of the Prefecture of Iquique. Additionally, the commissioner of the First Comisaría and the prefect met in the last hours with the regional minister of Women and Gender Equity to participate in the actions. The Prosecutor's Office of Iquique, together with the prosecutor of Carabineros, formalized an investigation against the accused for the crime of surprise sexual abuse. The court decreed the precautionary measures of prohibition of approaching the victim, national preventive detention, and monthly signature. By order of the prosecution agency, specialized personnel from the PDI took charge of the proceedings of the case.

data.text: Santo Domingo, RD. In the framework of the visit that the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, is making to the Dominican Republic, the Zile Foundation has issued a statement this Wednesday night where it takes a position on the deportations being made of Haitians and Dominicans from the northern country. Full statement: The Zile Foundation expresses its deep concern about the impact of the recent mass deportations from the United States to Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Since last October, Haiti has been receiving more than 10,000 repatriated individuals weekly from the Dominican Republic. The recent measures adopted by the US government to intensify these deportations put at risk the social and economic stability of both countries that share the island. The situation in Haiti is critical, with a humanitarian crisis exacerbated by the chaotic violence of armed gangs that control some sectors of the territory. This has led various United Nations agencies to request the main recipients of Haitian migrants to suspend forced repatriations. However, despite these calls, deportations and repatriations continue, generating severe consequences in the region. Main impacts of deportations:1. Exacerbation of the humanitarian crisis in Haiti The massive arrival of deportees in a country without the capacity to receive them multiplies food insecurity and lack of access to basic services, exacerbating the situation of extreme vulnerability.2. Reduction of remittance flow Haitian and Dominican migration in the United States generates more than $15 billion in annual remittances, including informal transfers. With the forced return of thousands of migrants, this important economic support is reduced, affecting the island's economy.3. Increase in instability on the island Haiti's inability to reintegrate deportees strengthens the vicious cycle of insecurity and poverty, increasing the risk of further migratory pressure on the Dominican Republic.4. Tension in bilateral relations The constant arrival of deportees from the United States and the Dominican Republic generates friction between the two countries, making it difficult to restart bilateral dialogue for necessary cooperation.5. Lack of viable alternatives for repatriated individuals Without integration mechanisms, repatriated individuals are left in a situation of extreme vulnerability, which fosters irregular migration, exploitation by human trafficking networks, and the possibility of recruitment by Haitian armed gangs. Proposals for Solutions through a Tripartite DialogueConsidering the specific case of this island shared by two countries with a delicate relationship, the Zile Foundation urges the U.S. administration to reconsider repatriation policies and promote a trilateral approach through dialogue between the United States, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic. Among the possible actions we suggest:1. Pilot Program for Repatriated Persons' ReintegrationImplementation of a two-year plan with urgent U.S. funding to create free trade zones on the border, with the aim of providing employment for deportees and ensuring their economic stability.2. Regularization of Migration Programs in the United States and the Dominican Republic for Haitians with family and labor roots or those with at least three years of residence. Also for undocumented Dominicans in Puerto Rico and other U.S. states.3 1. Strengthening international cooperation to support stability in Haiti and prevent deportations from exacerbating the crisis.2. Creation of humanitarian corridors that allow deportees to access basic services and employment opportunities in Haiti or third countries.3. Inter-governmental dialogue involving international organizations such as the OAS and the UN to design development strategies in Haiti and reduce migratory pressure, particularly on the Dominican Republic.4. Monitoring of human rights to ensure that deportations and repatriations are implemented in strict adherence to international norms and respect for human dignity.Call for effective international actionIt is noteworthy that, during his visit to the region, Secretary of State Marco Rubio did not consider it opportune to visit Haiti. This is especially relevant at a time when the US government has frozen funds for the international security mission led by Kenya, has closed USAID aid programs, and, coincidentally, with the arrival of Salvadoran soldiers in the country. The current situation in Haiti requires, in addition to the efforts and commitment of local leaders, immediate and coordinated action, not only from neighboring countries but also from the international community, as the Dominican Republic has repeatedly requested. We urge the United States, a country that maintains historical relations with Haiti and the Dominican Republic, to use its leadership to promote sustainable solutions that reduce island migration flows to its territory, while adopting robust measures to combat the trafficking of arms and ammunition that affects island stability from its coastlines. Regarding the Zile Foundation Created in Santo Domingo in May 2005, the Zile Foundation is a non-profit organization dedicated to promoting cooperation and understanding between Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Comprised of Haitians and Dominicans, the organization works tirelessly to build bridges of dialogue and collaboration between the two peoples with the goal of strengthening peace and social cohesion on the island. Its Board of Directors is co-chaired by Anglican Bishop Oge Beauvoir (Haiti) and Catholic Priest Julín Acosta (DR)

The Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals overturned the home detention of Gustavo Penadés and Sebastián Mauvezín, reported journalist Diego Martini and confirmed Javier Benech, spokesperson for the Prosecutor's Office. For both, preventive detention was ordered until June 10, as initially planned. In recent days, Judge Marcela Vargas had ordered home detention with an electronic ankle monitor for Penadés and Mauvezín. That magistrate believed they did not pose a risk and could await the judicial process in their homes. However, prosecutor Alicia Ghione and the lawyers of victims presented an appeal. This Wednesday, the court accepted it and left without effect the resolution of Vargas. Penadés was charged on October 10, 2023, with preventive detention, for the alleged commission of 22 crimes, eleven of which for retaliation for the sexual exploitation of minors.

The coca leader, through his legal defense, sought to render ineffective the arrest warrant issued against him. The Justice in Tarija declared the appeal inadmissible. The Investigating Magistrate in Penal, Anti-Corruption, and Against Women's Violence 5th of Tarija, Nelson Rocabado, ratified releasing the arrest warrant against former President Evo Morales, with a preventive notation of his assets, according to EL DEBER. The mandate was signed on Tuesday, February 11, and bears the label of Mandate for Arrest and Conduction No. 01 of the Special Force to Fight Crime and Authority Not Impeded by Law of the Department of Tarija and the Plurinational State of Bolivia, to apprehend and conduct Mr. Juan Evo Morales Ayma, as stated in the document. This decision comes after the First Criminal Chamber of the Departmental Court of Justice of Tarija, determined to reject the appeal presented by the legal defense of the coca leader against the arrest order that is being pursued against him for the crime of human trafficking. This Wednesday and from Sucre, the Attorney General of the State, Róger Mariaca, stated that they await the Police to comply with the arrest order, and even offered the collaboration of the Public Ministry, in case it is necessary to carry out searches or other acts within their jurisdiction. Since October 16, 2024, there has been an arrest warrant against the former president issued by the Departmental Prosecutor's Office of Tarija, and since January 17, 2025, the judge declared the former official in rebellion for not declaring before him in the case of human trafficking. Last week, the Minister of Government, Eduardo Del Castillo, announced that the Police have received orders to apprehend the leader of the six Federations of the Cochabamba Jungle. They will not arrest him at his stronghold, but will wait for him to leave the area to carry out the arrest order. We are waiting for (Evo Morales) to leave the region of the Cochabamba Jungle again, and we demonstrate, What is this man looking for, this man is looking to convulse our country once again, he is looking for mourning, or he is looking for confrontations, argued the head of that office. On that occasion, Del Castillo pointed out that they have well-planned operations, and they are only waiting for the precise moment and location to carry out what justice has determined, in order to avoid human losses and thus also avoid severe, extremely serious injuries in an unnecessary confrontation. The evaders are in permanent readiness with delegations from all over the country that take turns for vigilance in Lauca Ñ, a place that Morales chose so as not to leave and roam through the towns of the Cochabamba tropics.

Salvador Guerrero Chiprés In every strengthened community, there lies the opportunity to interrupt the cycle of violence. In the case of schools, it is especially true to prevent recruiters of girls, boys, and adolescents by criminal groups with promises of rapid advancement in the social hierarchy and to impose the consumption of drugs. The recruitment of minors is a global problem and concern. It violates the fundamental rights of victims and perpetuates conditions of violence and delinquency. According to estimates from the International Red Cross, around 300,000 girls and boys are forced to participate in armed conflicts or criminal situations, physical abuse, and sexual abuse. In Mexico, civil organizations estimate that there could be around 35,000. The data expose the need for public policies to prevent this problem, highlighted by the Head of Government of Mexico City, Claudia Sheinbaum, as the urgency to prevent minors from dropping out of school and becoming cannon fodder for criminal groups. Or consumers of toxic, illegal, and deadly addictive substances like the dark varieties of fentanyl. Opportunities for the development of this population sector are strengthened with scholarships for different age groups initiated in the national capital by the current President Claudia Sheinbaum, as well as a school security model aimed at addressing the sale of drugs and hooliganism near public and private educational institutions. And this always requires the community, without which there is no security, and even less school security. Girls, boys, and adolescents can dangerously normalize criminal behaviors and become more susceptible to recruitment, with profound repercussions for them and their families. Participation in criminal acts generates traumas and mental disorders, such as post-traumatic stress, depression, and anxiety. Minors involved in organized crime are stigmatized and their social reintegration is complex. Their incorporation into organized crime is deliberately sought for the continuation of these criminal structures and fuels cycles of violence with community damage. On January 12, World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers, in addition to remembering those who have been employed by armed groups, it is necessary to accompany strategies to prevent recruitment, keep them away from criminal environments from an early age, and build spaces of peace and security around schools. The Auxiliar School Program, presented by Brugada this week, promotes community participation to build paths of peace at the entrance and exit of the schools, with the presence of public servants and the strengthening of video surveillance from the C5. Only through joint and sustained efforts can we create appropriate environments for girls and boys.

Rapper and music producer Sean Diddy Combs, currently incarcerated and awaiting trial for sex trafficking in May, has filed a multimillion-dollar lawsuit against NBC Universal and producer Ample. The artist accuses the network of defamation over the documentary Diddy The Making of a Bad Boy, which links him to the death of his ex-partner Kim Porter and points to him for alleged heinous crimes. A defamation and reputation damage lawsuit According to Page Six, which had access to the legal document, the lawsuit alleges that the documentary makes malicious and unfounded claims against Combs, suggesting that he is responsible for multiple crimes, including serial murder, child sex trafficking, and child rape. Combs's lawyers argue that NBC's production not only distorts reality but also severely impacts his right to a fair trial by portraying him as comparable to Jeffrey Epstein. They claim that the artist's public image, finances, and career have been irreparably damaged by the content of the documentary. The documentary, released in January through NBC and available on the Peacock platform, deepens the charges against Combs and exposes testimonies that link him to the death of Kim Porter, the mother of several of his children, who died in 2018 due to pneumonia, according to the official forensic report. Additionally, the production captures statements from Porter's ex-husband, Al B. Sure, who questions the cause of her death and presents a conspiracy theory that involves Diddy in the death of rapper Notorious B.I.G., music executive Andre Harrell, and rapper Heavy D, who died under different circumstances. The Legal Process of Combs Possibilities of Defense Sean Combs remains at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, New York, following his arrest as part of a federal investigation into human trafficking, extortion, and transporting individuals for prostitution purposes. Although the founder of Bad Boy Records has denied any wrongdoing and pleaded not guilty, he faces a possible sentence of between 15 years and life in prison. His trial is scheduled for May 5, while his legal team continues to seek to reverse the media damage, which they claim has been caused by the case coverage and documentaries such as the one by NBC. Will this lawsuit be a strategy to clean his image or an attempt to change the narrative before his trial? The Diddy case continues to generate controversy and anticipation in the entertainment industry.

The National Police captured the most wanted man in the province of Cañar, Luis N., in Ohio, United States, on Wednesday, February 12, 2025. According to further news, the citizen had a red alert from the International Police (Interpol) for the alleged crime of femicide, which occurred in Azogues in 2019. The man remained a fugitive from justice for nearly six years. He was listed on the Most Wanted Program of the Police, in the category of gender violence. During these years, the defendant grew a beard and mustache to try to hide his appearance. Luis N. is accused of the alleged murder of his romantic partner Brenda G., who died while pregnant. After being detained, he was put under the orders of the authorities in the United States, awaiting his formal process for deportation to Ecuador. Femicide is punishable by a prison sentence of 22 to 26 years in the country. This crime is penalized according to Article 141 of the Integral Organic Penal Code (COIP). An Ecuadorean citizen was deported for alleged human trafficking. In another Interpol procedure executed in the United States, a citizen was deported to Ecuador this Wednesday, February 12. Stalin Z. was required by national justice for the alleged crime of human trafficking. The man also maintained an international red notice, in addition to a valid arrest warrant. Upon arriving in Ecuador, the individual was transferred to the competent authorities. The Cuauhtémoc municipality has positioned itself as one of the red points in the CDMX due to the high incidence of street-level drug dealing. (Photo Cuartoscuro) Personnel from the Ciudad de México's Secretariat of Citizen Security (SSC) detained a Venezuelan in possession of over 30 doses of drugs in the streets of the Tabacalera neighborhood, Cuauhtémoc municipality. In a statement from the capital's department, it was reported that their officers were conducting patrols for crime prevention when they identified a person on Avenues Paseo de la Reforma and Hidalgo while manipulating several plastic bags similar to those used by street-level drug dealers. When the officers approached for an inspection, the subject in question fled, but they intercepted them and upon searching their belongings, they found 37 bags with dry and green herb, characteristics typical of marijuana, so they presented them to the public prosecutor's agent to define their legal situation. During the interrogation, the detained individual stated to be 40 years old and from Venezuela, which led to an investigation into possible ties with the Aragua Train Cartel, a criminal organization with presence in Mexico City. It is worth noting that on February 11, two Venezuelans were arrested for stealing 520,000 pesos worth of merchandise from a store located inside the Parque Lindavista plaza in the Gustavo A. Madero municipality. Venezuelans arrested for robbery in GAM These three arrests add to the detention of Nuvia N, a Venezuelan woman accused of human trafficking for forcing a woman to engage in sex work in exchange for help reaching the United States. Nuvia N is also linked to the femicide of two women (also Venezuelan) committed in July 2024 in the Tlalpan municipality. Nuvia N is linked to Euclides Manuel Arias Suárez, alias el Morgán, Joy Maikel N, Yannier Abraham N, and Evelyn N, all allegedly members of the Aragua Train Cartel and involved in extortion, extortion, human trafficking, and homicides, crimes committed in the Cuauhtémoc, Tlalpan, and Gustavo A. Madero aldermanies. Although the arrests of Venezuelans linked to the Aragua Train Cartel have been presented since mid-2024, just last week the Head of Government, Clara Brugada, acknowledged the operations of the criminal group. However, not only in Mexico City have the arrests of alleged members of this criminal group been registered, since at the end of January last year a cell of the Aragua Train Cartel was dismantled that operated in the city of Chihuahua and charged for lodging and protection to migrants.

Draft Inés Arroyo The deputy Luis Alberto Chávez García has presented an initiative to modify Article 1 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States. His proposal aims to recognize human trafficking as a crime comparable to slavery, being a grave violation of human rights and a crime against humanity. According to data from the National Public Security System, as of April 2024, 2,529 people between 0 and 17 years old have been victims of human trafficking in Mexico, of which 1,890 are women and 639 are men. The entities with the highest incidence of these cases are the City of Mexico, Quintana Roo, and the State of Mexico. Chávez emphasized that there are no clear figures on the profits derived from human trafficking. However, at a forum held in 2021, it was mentioned that the Financial Intelligence Unit blocked 1,410 bank accounts linked to human trafficking activities, for an amount exceeding 144 million pesos. The legislator argues that, due to the magnitude of this crime, it is urgent to provide greater protection to victims, especially children and adolescents. In this sense, the initiative aligns with the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which urges the adoption of legal and social measures to prevent abuse and exploitation. The proposal also reinforces Mexico's commitment to the Palermo Protocol, which defines human trafficking as any form of coercion to exploit individuals in activities such as prostitution, forced labor, and organ extraction. With the reform, Article 1 of the Constitution would be modified to explicitly establish the prohibition of slavery and human trafficking, ensuring that any enslaved person entering the country would immediately obtain their freedom and the protection of Mexican laws. The proposal was sent to the Joint Committees on Constitutional Matters and Citizen Initiatives and Human Rights for analysis. If approved, it would represent an important step forward in the fight against human trafficking in Mexico, strengthening the protection of victims and punishing those responsible for this crime with greater severity.

A U.S. citizen wanted for various crimes in his country, including child abuse, was detained in Saltillo, Coahuila, by agents from the Criminal Investigation Agency and the National Migration Institute. The man was handed over to authorities from his country at the 2nd International Bridge in Piedras Negras. The State Attorney General's Office reported that the detainee's name is James and was the National Migration Institute that carried out the controlled deportation at the International Bridge. Based on a research work and coordination with other security dependencies, the Criminal Investigation Agency of the State Attorney General's Office located the detainee in the city of Saltillo. In January of last year, a U.S. citizen was also detained in Coahuila, accused of being responsible for a hit-and-run in Miami, Florida. The alleged perpetrator, identified as Zeniel Francisco N, 25 years old, was located and detained in the city of Piedras Negras, Coahuila, by elements of the State Secretary of Public Security, in coordination with the Police of Action and Reaction. Following his arrest, Zeniel was turned over to the National Migration Institute for subsequent transfer to the United States, where he faces charges of vehicular manslaughter and flight. JCS

A heart-wrenching denouncement has shaken the foundations of this community, revealing a suspected case of child abuse and human trafficking involving two minors and prominent local figures. The mothers and aunts of the victims have spoken out, demanding justice for their daughters and nieces, who allegedly suffered horrific acts of abuse at the hands of their own uncles and aunts. The names of the suspected perpetrators resound with force in Hidalgo's political and social scene: Arturo Williams Trejo Leal, former campaign coordinator for Governor Julio Menchaca. Bertha Eva Medina Hernández, Arturo's wife. Alhely Medina Hernández, local deputy for Hidalgo's district 1 and national counselor for Morena. Ixtshelle Trejo Leal, Arturo's sister, currently a fugitive from justice along with her husband. Eduardo Bibiano Badillo Mejía, Ixtshelle's husband, also a fugitive from justice. The severity of the accusations has been corroborated by seven expert reports, both from the Attorney General's Office and the FGR, confirming the crime of sexual abuse. The girls, in their statements to the Public Ministry, have recounted with horror how their uncles forced them to perform aberrant acts, including the introduction of objects into their intimate areas. As a consequence of what has been mentioned earlier, the girls have attempted to commit suicide and currently live in safe houses alongside their mother. In addition to the emotional sequelae they face, they suffer from physical illnesses, such as the human papillomavirus, which has led the 7-year-old girl to undergo a hysterectomy. Despite the contiguity of the evidence, justice appears to be hindered by the political influence of the alleged perpetrators. Judge Janett Montiel Mendoza released them from custody after their capture, allegedly following instructions from someone in the state government. However, they never did anything until Dr. Santiago Nieto took over as the head of the Attorney General's office in Hidalgo, and after his investigation, he issued arrest orders. The Secretary of Government, Guillermo Olivares Reina, is being pointed to as the protector of these individuals, who allegedly deceived the governor by downplaying the case as a political matter. The situation becomes even darker upon discovering that the suspected aggressors and other individuals involved belong to a Christian church called El Buen Samaritano, Zimapán branch. The girls have testified that during the abuse, people wearing masks sang religious music and recorded videos. It is suspected that this place could be a cult where victims were drugged to erase their memories. The consequences of these abuses have been devastating for the girls, who have attempted suicide and suffer from emotional and physical sequels, including human papillomavirus. The mother of the victims cries out for help, demanding that the FGR accelerates the investigations and that the Secretariat of Women and FEVINTRA takes action to bring the perpetrators to justice. This case demands a clear and swift response from the authorities. The protection of the rights of minors and the fight against impunity are imperative demands that cannot be ignored. Hidalgoan society and all of Mexico demand justice for these girls and the clarification of this disturbing case.

This concerns a 68-year-old man who had been evading justice since November last year. The investigation found that, between 2018 and 2022, he had subjected his two six-year-old and nine-year-old granddaughters to sexual abuse while they were in his care in a residence in the La Matanza partido in the province of Buenos Aires. The 4th Guarantees Court of La Matanza, presided over by Dr. Fernando Pino Guevara and with the intervention of the Secretariat of Dr. Gonzalo Filiguera, assigned the Federal Police (PFA) to locate and detain the accused. As a result, federal agents conducted an exhaustive investigation and analysis of information, determining possible addresses linked to the fugitive in the Mataderos neighborhood of Buenos Aires. With the collaboration of the Biometric Systems Division of that Security Force, data was verified and contrasted, allowing the establishment of the suspect's movements. Finally, and with the consent of the intervening court, a covert surveillance operation was implemented in the area, which culminated in his capture in a public place on Carhué street at 2100 in the Mataderos neighborhood of the City of Buenos Aires. The detainee was placed at the disposal of the National Court for Rogatory Matters, under the charge of Dr. Gabriel Guirlanda, Secretary of Dr. Gustavo Macci, who is being charged with the crime of severely outrageous sexual abuse, aggravated by being committed by a guardian, in ideal concurrence with aggravated corruption of minors.

As part of the efforts to eradicate child labor in Quintana Roo, the municipal president of Solidaridad, Estefanía Mercado, signed a collaboration agreement with the State Secretary of Labor and Social Security, with the aim of strengthening prevention and eradication strategies for this social problem. Child labor is not an option, it's an injustice. We must ensure that no girl or boy sacrifices their childhood for exploitation, Mercado stated after signing the agreement.A Commitment to ChildhoodThe legislator emphasized that this action is part of the New Agreement for the Well-being and Development of Quintana Roo, promoted by Governor Mara Lezama, whose focus prioritizes the protection of childhood, access to education, and the elimination of any form of child exploitation. The agreement seeks to implement concrete actions to identify and address cases of child labor in the state. Create prevention and awareness programs in vulnerable communities. Coordinate efforts between institutions to ensure compliance with children's rights. Inter-institutional coordination to combat child labor Estefanía Mercado emphasized that eradicating child labor requires a joint effort between authorities, the private sector, and civil society to create opportunities that allow childhood to develop in a safe environment with access to education. We continue working on strategies that strengthen the protection of childhood in Quintana Roo. We cannot allow child labor to be normalized or tolerated, she stressed. Towards a Quintana Roo Free from Child Exploitation With this agreement, Estefanía Mercado reaffirms her commitment to promoting public policies that guarantee the rights of childhood and contribute to the construction of a Quintana Roo where all girls and boys have access to a childhood free from exploitation and with opportunities for development.

The former president of Bolivia from 2006 to 2019, Evo Morales, is facing difficult times. The justice system of his country issued an arrest order against him in the framework of the case for allegedly sexual abuse, and the government of Luis Arce supported the measure. After the First Criminal Chamber of the Tarija Justice Court rejected Morales' appeal, Judge Nelson Rocabado ordered the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime to apprehend the former head of state and coca leader. In this context, Minister of Government Carlos Eduardo del Castillo stated on Monday that the operational order is already ready to carry out the apprehension, but they are waiting for the precise moment and place to execute it without generating confrontations and avoiding human life loss. The Tarija Prosecutor's Office, which is investigating the case, is targeting Morales for alleged statutory rape and human trafficking. Former MAS leader Morales is accused of having sexual relations with Cindy Saraí in 2016 when she was a minor, from which a daughter was born. In this scenario, Morales was supposed to appear for questioning on January 17, but as he failed to appear for the second time, the Justice system declared him in contempt and confirmed the arrest order that had been issued in October 2024. Additionally, the court ordered the freezing of his accounts and assets. Ten days later, on January 27, the Tarija Tribunal rejected the defense's appeal, thus worsening Morales' judicial situation. The State's Attorney General, Roger Mariaca, reaffirmed that the arrest order must be executed by the police. Mariaca also determined that a prosecutor may intervene in case a search is required. In response to the court orders, Morales is taking refuge in the Chapare, a department in Cochabamba (center), his political stronghold, where he has the backing of hundreds of coca growers who have warned of a possible social convulsion in case of his detention. Evo Morales denounces persecution by the Bolivian Justice and Government After the issuance of the arrest order, the minister of Government of President Luis Arce, Evo Morales denounced illegal and abusive persecution and a Plan Negro against him. The new media operation by the government to detain me within the framework of its Plan Negro (lawfare) aims to cover up the already unhidden scandal of corruption over the contracts to give away lithium to foreign companies, Morales expressed on his social networks. Moreover, he linked the decision of the Justice with the crisis in his country. The Arce regime does not seek justice. He translated the text with absolute accuracy to preserve the original meaning, tone, and terminology.He only wants to cover up his disastrous administration, the economy that's been sunk and the institutional destruction, his right-wingization and betrayal of the people and his submission to North American imperialism. That strategy consisted of inventing an accusation for a supposed crime just to detain me, destroy me politically and morally, and take me out of the electoral race, by manipulating a prosecutor and using a judge appointed by the illegal self-extended Council of the Magistrature, he added.Morales accuses the penal and electoral courts of his country of complicity with the management of his former political partner to pursue him. The Black Plan of Arce also included, with the complicity of the TCP and the TSE, the theft of the MAS acronym and the designation of leaders at will, without the vote of the militants, he affirmed. Two de facto magistrates of the Constitutional Court, Gonzalo Hurtado and Iván Espada, protected by the judiciary, issued unconstitutional sentences that aim to disqualify me as a presidential candidate, concluded Morales in his publication on X.

data.text: The Vietnamese Xuan and modern slavery on a cannabis plantation in England Xuan was drowning in cannabis. Day and night, locked up and alone, this Vietnamese migrant was exploited on a plantation in England under the threat of being killed by the traffickers if the harvest was not good. Vietnamese migrants are among the largest number of people crossing the English Channel irregularly, behind Afghans and Iranians. The British Home Office recorded 3,307 people from this Asian country between January and September 2024. They are also among the most exposed to forced labor. Almost 1,000 Vietnamese were allegedly victims of modern slavery in 2023, according to figures communicated to British authorities. For James Fookes of the NGO AntiSlavery International, they represent only the tip of the iceberg of a well-oiled people trafficking between Vietnam and the United Kingdom. Just like Xuan, many Vietnamese people end up in a cannabis plantation after getting into debt in their country. When I invested in the real estate market, I lost a lot of money, he explains to AFP, using a fake name for security reasons. Unable to pay off his debts with what he calls gangsters, in 2015 they offered him instead to sell his organs or go to work in the United Kingdom. Xuan flew to Russia, then to the Netherlands and took a train to France to subsequently cross the English Channel, hidden in a truck, along with around ten other people, mostly Vietnamese. Discovered by the police, he was interned in a refugee center and later managed to settle in his nephew's house in London. In 2016, when he was leaving a police station where he had to report regularly, two unknown individuals violently pushed him into a car and forced him to talk on a phone. A Vietnamese man told me on the phone to obey those two men, or they would kill me, explains Xuan. I was terrified. I was taken to the north of England. I was terrified, he recalls. For months, he worked in a warehouse, loading boxes with mysterious contents, unpaid, alongside other men, with whom he was not allowed to communicate. He was beaten often, he says, crying, Xuan, who is now 58 years old. He only wanted to stay alive so one day he could see his children again, he adds.Later, he was taken to a cannabis plantation, which was a three-story house but with cannabis plants everywhere except in the bathrooms and kitchen. At night, he got little rest, lying on a mattress. He was alone, periodically checked by those who had brought him to the house, which was locked, he explains.He had to water, fertilize, and ensure the cannabis grew well. In 2021, during the pandemic, he fell ill. He couldn't breathe or work. She feared they would kill her if she didn't do the job well, she says. And she decided to escape by breaking a window, as she had nothing to lose. She was going to die anyway, she says. She managed to get to London by train, where she collapsed on the street at one point. After being treated in the hospital, she contacted the police. The authorities handed her over to The Salvation Army, an organization contracted by the government to help victims of modern slavery, which has been helping 135 Vietnamese nationals since 2021. Although Xuan managed to escape, the forced labor of many others often ended when the police conducted a raid on a plantation. If I go back, they will kill me. In April 2024, the UK and Vietnam signed an agreement to combat human trafficking. The Vietnamese government has made significant progress in helping its citizens avoid modern slavery, says Mitsue Pembroke, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) representative in Hanoi. It is crucial to strengthen cooperation with transit and destination countries, she emphasizes. The agreement between the two countries also aimed to discourage irregular immigration to the UK. Xuan, who often struggles to sleep, lives on the outskirts of London in a protected house, whose address the Salvation Army keeps secret. His dream is to stay and have his two children join him. If I return to Vietnam, the gangsters will kill me, he says. His asylum request was rejected in 2024, and he now awaits a decision on an appeal he submitted.

Mexico City, February 12, 2025 With your permission. Honorable colleagues, I am here today to speak about the silent victims of human cruelty, those beings who have no voice, who every day feel fear, pain, and abandonment, and unfortunately, cannot ask for help. In our country, every day, thousands of animals are beaten, tortured, abandoned, and even sexually abused. We see horses and donkeys exploited to death, birds caged for life in tiny cages, and wild animals taken from their habitat to live in captivity. Mexico ranks third in the world in animal abuse and 86 percent of the perpetrators are men. This could be a prelude to social violence, the National Institute of Statistics and Geography reports that approximately 60,000 animals die each year due to abuse, 70 percent of stray dogs and cats suffer abandonment or abuse, and seven out of ten dogs end up on the street or on a rooftop. Therefore, today this Initiative was presented to fine with up to 7 percent of income those who share audiovisual content promoting violence against animals of any species without any purpose of denouncing it. Social media platforms play a central role in disseminating information, ideas, and content that connect millions of people worldwide today, but they have also opened the door to normalizing or promoting violent and inhumane behaviors. In the coming days, I will be presenting another Initiative to codify in the Federal Penal Code the sexual abuse of animals, with a penalty of up to six years in prison and economic fines for those found responsible. Studies have shown that those who sexually abuse animals have a higher probability of committing other violent crimes, including abuse against people, specifically against children and women. We cannot turn a blind eye to the suffering, we cannot justify indifference, every mistreated animal is a reflection of the society we are and the violence that surrounds us. Let us not normalize cruelty, let us report animal abuse, let us educate new generations in respect and love for animals. Animal abuse is an open wound in our humanity, a reflection of the indifference that invades us. Behind every frightened gaze, every injured body, there is a being that feels. The change begins, colleagues, with us, and the hope of many, many Mexicans is that we can build a more just, more compassionate, more conscious, but above all, more human Mexico. Respect and empathy should have no limits or species, and to conclude, I want to tell you that animal abuse only reflects the lack of empathy and respect for life, and I ask you, as lawmakers, what are we willing to do for them. That's all, Madam President. Text and Photo Grupo Parlamentario del PRI in the Chamber of Deputies

Boca Chica is a paradise where anything can happen. In this tourist municipality of the Santo Domingo province, nestled in the San Andrés bay, 30 kilometers east of the National District, prostitution has been ignored for decades to become a massive sex market for children and girls offering their services to tourists and nationals regardless of sex or age. For some, the intensity of the phenomenon has decreased. But on the ground, child pornography, trafficking, and exploitation are an open secret. The plague has spread to all four sides. But now it runs underground, with a new face. The predators have adapted to new technologies. They use web pages and social networks to locate and promote their prey. With the new modality, many minors are contacted in a hidden manner by pimps and tourists who, in many cases, make direct offers to family members who, for a few pesos, enter the game of providing their children and daughters to the highest bidder, as if it were a public auction. A stretch of Duarte Street, the main artery of this comarca of 167,000 inhabitants, 85,406 women, and 81,634 men (Census 2022), continues, however, as a propitious scene to contact victims directly. They close off from 7 pm to midnight from the Hamaca hotel to the corner of the park. And, from 11 pm onwards, women and men become key actors to offer their charm to strangers. Pregnant with needs, dollars, and euros, their eyes bulge, but the Dominican pesos. That piece of street becomes an ideal space for lust and vice. The consumption of drugs never misses, it's our daily bread. Scenes Unfolding Freely Life in this 147.7 square kilometer town unfolds as if nothing is happening. The residents of Bocachica go about their daily lives, resisting the bitter temptation of poverty. This occurs under the indifferent, in some cases complicit, gaze of authorities responsible for ensuring the safety and public order of both local and foreign citizens who frequent the area. This is confirmed by a conversation with members of the Tourist Police (Politur) and municipal police, who matter-of-factly recount how, from that hour on, Duarte Street becomes a no-man's land. With nonchalance and a hint of cheekiness, one of the agents (name withheld) explains how the scenes change depending on the hour. At 7 pm, the street is closed, tourists head out for dinner, but from 10 pm to 11 pm, things change and the cueritos (young female sex workers) take over the area. But what do you do with the cases of minors? Respond with resignation. Imagine, one of them is arrested, but a few days later, they're back. No one can stop it. It's that simple. Anyone can easily realize the situation. Some think that agents receive economic or material benefits from the trafficking of women and whites and the indiscriminate trafficking of drugs. Others, desperate, believe that this practice has been legalized due to the influence trafficking in high spheres. Everything can be possible in this den of perdition. Meanwhile, members of Politur, the Secret Service of the Police, and the National Directorate of Drug Control (DNCD), with their hands tied, watch as in these three blocks, the prostitution of minors grows and grows along with the indiscriminate consumption of drugs and other highly addictive substances. The offers are directed at tourists and Dominicans, including minors and adolescents. Nothing matters about their rights. Their testimonies are terrifying. They move everyone, except for pedophiles and the authorities who are called upon to face the evil. A simple stop near the central park in Boca Chica provides the conversation with a 13-year-old girl (M), who describes the early hardships in that world that resembles a public brothel. She is 13 years old, but bears 60 years of forced experience. She is sexually exploited. She reports that she was contacted by an Italian tourist, one of those who installs himself for months in rented homes. He offered her 50,000 pesos to find a girl who is a virgin. She fulfilled the assignment to earn the offered amount. She contacted (J) to satisfy the foreigner's turbulence. In the end, they only paid her 10,000 pesos, not the 50,000 agreed upon for the task. And she no longer knows what happened to M. The case does not appear to be new or to have occurred behind the family's back. The case gained attention due to the disputes between the families of the minors who were demanding the missing money. The authorities had no choice but to take notice. A hazardous routine ensued, with everything forgotten in a matter of hours, and life went back to normal for the authorities. No enforcement of the law. M received psychological accompaniment from a private entity. However, J continued down the treacherous path of the sex trade. As the study "Luchar contra la marea" (Fighting the Tide) conducted by anthropologist Tahira Vargas highlights, an important aspect in these areas is the presence of tourism, which is seen as a cause, a facilitator of human trafficking, and a generator of the concealment and invisibility of the same, in order to avoid scandals that affect this sector. In that tourist paradise called Boca Chica, the children are there, in the red zone, destroying their existence in front of the indifferent gaze of tourists, foreign investors, authorities, and everyone who, in one way or another, benefits from it. Boca Chica is a municipality in the province of Santo Domingo founded in October 2001. Its municipal district is La Caleta. Its identity seal is the beach of the same name, highly frequented by tranquil, low, and white sand. With a population of 167,040 inhabitants, according to the 2022 census. Of that number, nearly 105,000 lived in the urban area and about 63,000 in the rural area. Despite the involvement of minors in sexual exploitation, the preliminary data from the most recent census do not establish how many people that population amounts to. According to a Wikipedia article, the community was founded in 1779 during the government of Brigadier Juan Isidro Peralta Rojas, under the name of San José de los Llanos, and developed by the Dominican State through the Boca Chica sugar mill established in 1916 and later in 1920 by Juan Bautista Vicini Burgos, with sugar cane plantations. In 1926, the road connecting it to the Capital was built, and in 1932, it was separated from San José de los Llanos and San Pedro de Macorís and integrated into the National District. The municipality was founded in 2001. According to a 2006 study by the United Nations on violence against children worldwide, it was estimated that 150 million girls and 73 million children under 18 years old had been forced to engage in sexual relations or had been victims of other forms of sexual violence. According to an investigation by Tahira Vargas, Luchar contra la marea (2022), on human trafficking in eleven municipalities, Boca Chica shows many coincidences regarding human trafficking in its various forms. The most acute modality is the trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation in the municipalities of the tourist zones of Higüey, La Romana, Puerto Plata, and Boca Chica, the latter with a strong concentration in the capture of child and adolescent population as victims of commercial sexual exploitation. However, in the Dominican Republic, specifically in the Boca Chica community, there are no percentage figures of the commercial sexual exploitation of minors. What is evident is that children, abandoned to their fate, are sought out in this environment, where officials from institutions such as Politur, provincial government, among others, are necessarily first-line witnesses, since the buildings that house them are right in the center of the daily bacchanal of this tourist place. There also exists a Protocol for Comprehensive Attention of Children, Girls, and Adolescent Victims of Sexual Exploitation. The document, prepared by the Public Prosecutor's Office in coordination with international organizations such as UNICEF, is clear: The sexual exploitation of children, girls, and adolescents in any of its manifestations constitutes a crime against the dignity, integrity, and superior interest of that population in the Dominican Republic. Drugs, and sankypankismo, a separate chapter Despite the permanent vigilance by the authorities, not only in the closed section of Duarte Street, but in its surroundings, the consumption of prohibited and non-prohibited substances is the bread of every night. A 12-year-old boy roams near Duarte Street. He looks very skilled for his age. He speaks resolutely about the sankypankies that abound in the place. He defines those protagonists of the environment in his own way. They are the ones who go with the gringos to do things with them for money and drugs. El hombre, con una actitud teatral y una cierta dosis de ironía, afirma que los niños que se prostituyen en la playa de Boca Chica son personas que viven en la playa y que hay niños pequeños que fuman drogas. Él no considera que se encuentre en ese mundo. Establece una gran diferencia entre sus propias vestimentas y las de los niños que se prostituyen, argumentando que él asiste a la escuela y se viste de manera diferente. Describe las situaciones a las que son sometidos los niños en ese lugar, sin que las autoridades tomen medidas. Algunos de ellos se acuestan en camitas en la playa, mientras que otros se dirigen a lugares como La Coca, un callejón oscuro donde se consumen drogas. También hay personas que se llevan a los niños, los golpean y los llevan detenidos, diciendo que son sus hijos. Algunos testigos corroboran este testimonio, aunque afirman que no es cierto para todos. El alcalde Ramón Candelaria rechaza esta versión, asegurando de manera firme que la prostitución infantil en Boca Chica es un mito. The director and founder of the NGO Caminantes, which is specifically responsible for preventing the sexual and commercial exploitation of minors in the area, Denisse Pichardo, is not convinced by the mayor's statements, and her quick response was "He doesn't even believe it himself." Pichardo not only doubts the assertion made by the local government leader. She goes further and emphasizes the new modality of sexual predation that encompasses everything from beach incursions in search of older tourists, to contact with pimps who frequent the area, using minors as mules for micro-trafficking, and exposing girls through web pages. And that's not a secret, neither for the authorities nor for anyone. Without hesitation, she observes "The drug points are there. They operate in the same way as in La 42, in the capital, with the teteos, rooms, games of chance, and everything that catches the attention of minors, right on Duarte Street, and in full view of everyone." Pichardo reveals that the most commonly used for micro-trafficking are young boys, who are also initiated into the consumption of narcotics. In the new modality, those minors, known as "haqueadores," are placed in strategic locations on Duarte Street as vigilantes and informants for those who pass through that den of iniquity who are not recognized by those responsible for the micro-trafficking business. He emphasizes that in this way, an entire network operates, putting everyone on alert regarding the incursion of a new person, who may be police officers or members of the DNCD, or any other unrecognized person. Normally, those minors end up arrested, since the traffickers, who have their own means of defense, almost always manage to evade capture. They claim that there is effective surveillance on the Duarte Street stretch in Boca Chica, but the trafficking of women and men, as well as the indiscriminate consumption and trafficking of narcotics, is a common and everyday occurrence. Finding them, listening to them, is easy. Women and men want to speak, tell their stories, and above all, demand a healthy space where they can develop as human beings. They have received promises in bulk. From those who use them and from the authorities who rush to them whenever there is a report about the drama they suffer. That's all. Meanwhile, danger lurks. Children born out of time of misery and desperation are germinating in the greenhouses of the street. Later, they bloom as a living expression of degradation, crime, delinquency, or as a lower caste of social parasites. Stories are many, and all are heart-wrenching. These children, adults out of time, to whom innocence and naivety have been denied, have the right to exist as people. The Department of Protection for Children, Girls, and Adolescents has a fertile ground in these minors who yearn for a stable life, free from the ups and downs and dangers of the street and the irresponsibility of relatives who expose them. They are there, right in the middle of vice and immorality. It is necessary to rescue them.
