data.text: A father and his son were arrested today in the province of Buenos Aires for allegedly being the perpetrators of a sexual abuse against a minor. Police sources informed the Argentine News Agency that the case was initiated when the victim came of age and filed a complaint in which she stated that she was outraged during her childhood by her then-stepfather. According to the police report, the events allegedly occurred in the family home located in the town of Gregorio de Laferrere, between 2010 and 2012, and when the affected person was 5 and 6 years old. According to her testimony, the sexual attacks took place when the victim was left in the care of the accused, who threatened her with death on multiple occasions and avoided any accusations against him. However, during a move carried out between 2016 and 2017, the victim was sexually assaulted again, but at that time the perpetrator of the crime was the son of the main suspect. In this context, at the end of January, the Specialized Unit for Instruction and Specialized Trial in Family and Gender Violence and Sexual Integrity Crimes Number One of the La Matanza Judicial Department convened the Division of Public Health Crimes of the Federal Police with the purpose of identifying and capturing the suspects. The officers apprehended those involved on García Merou Street (Gregorio de Laferrere) and Riglos Street (González Catán) respectively. Both detainees, one of them a Bolivian national, were placed at the disposal of the intervening judge for the crime of Gravely Aggravated Sexual Abuse, committed against a minor under 18, taking advantage of the situation of cohabitation, and committed by the person in charge of the guard, in ideal concurrence with Aggravated Corruption of a Minor.

Santo Domingo. Lawyers for five defendants in the so-called Operation Cattleya, which investigates a suspected sex trafficking ring, recused the judges of the Third Collegiate Court of the National District, alleging that they lack impartiality to continue the process. The judge's recusal occurred after the admission of a forensic evidence presented by the Public Ministry, which, according to the defense, constitutes a procedural violation. Among the recusants of Operation Cattleya are the lawyers for María Paula Morillo, Oscar Wicene, José Alberto Soriano, Alejandro Arturo alias El Gato, and the business entity Hotel Oscar. Judges Arlín Ventura, Leticia Martínez, and Evelyn Rodríguez denied the allegations against them. While the Public Ministry characterized the recusal as a strategy to delay the trial. Prosecutor Eduardo Velásquez assured that the evidence contained in the hard drives will demonstrate the penal responsibility of the 17 accused. According to him, these individuals were sexually exploiting more than 80 women, mostly of Colombian and Venezuelan nationality. The lawyers of the other 13 defendants did not join the recusal. Now, the decision is in the hands of the Appellate Court, which will determine whether the case should be reassigned to another tribunal.

The United States has identified at least five members of the criminal organization involved in these activities. Members of the Gulf Cartel caught. The illicit activities of the Gulf Cartel do not only limit to drug and human trafficking, as its tentacles have also extended to illegal fishing, which generates millions in profits. According to information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, the cartel is involved in the illicit trade of red snapper species, also known as huachinango, and sharks. Although the Treasury does not specify which shark species they hunt, a recent publication by Milenio states that it is the bull shark, whose skin is used to create luxury accessories. Additionally, the liver oil of the animal is used for the manufacture of cosmetics, among other things. That US source details that the cartel's operations are carried out on fast and lightweight boats, the same ones used to transport illicit drugs and migrants. The activities are coordinated from Playa Bagdad, also known as Playa Costa Azul, located in the municipality of Matamoros, in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas, several kilometers south of the border with the US. Apparently, Mexican fishermen cross into US waters, where these species are abundant, and carry out fishing, to then transport their catch to the camps in Mexico. The product, according to the Treasury, has two destinations to be sold to Mexican seafood markets or fraudulently labeled to be exported to the US. However, in the recent publication by Milenio, it is mentioned that most of the catch is destined for the Gulf Cartel's partners in Asia. The remaining catch is sold to exclusive restaurateurs, who have menus that only their loyal customers know about. This activity generates millions of dollars a year for the speedboat camps. Additionally, it also causes the death of other marine species that are caught unintentionally, the Treasury Department says. The operators In November of last year, the US sanctioned five members of that criminal organization for these actions. They are the brothers Ismael and Omar Guerra Salinas, alias Mayelo and Samorano, respectively, Francisco Javier Sierra Angulo, known as El Borrado, Raúl Decuir García, La Burra, and Ildelfonso Carrillo Sapién, El Chivo. Photo of a caught shark. The Guerra brothers, 34 and 38 years old, would be the members of the Gulf Cartel in charge of Playa Bagdad, who, in addition to overseeing fishing, manage narcotics trafficking and human smuggling operations. Alias El Borrado, a 36 years old, was identified as the leader of the Gulf Cartel in Matamoros, while La Burra and El Chivo (53 and 48) are owners of boat camps that supervise and allow fishermen to cross into US waters on behalf of the Gulf Cartel. These men, according to information provided by the US, are from Tamaulipas, except for Carrillo, who is from Veracruz.

Recently, news has emerged about the dismissal of the case of the four-year-old girls from the Europa school by the Getxo Court. This brings us to ask: Are judicial and police institutions prepared to address the demands of childhood? Are we really protecting our minors when they are victims of such violence? Child sexual abuse is not a new phenomenon, but it is recently that we are appreciating its true dimension, thanks to increased awareness, investigations, and dynamics that encourage testimony. The report on sexual freedom crimes refers to the fact that, alone in 2023, there were 9,185 child victimizations in the Spanish State. And these occur in greater proportion if compared to those of adults (Ministry of the Interior of the Government of Spain, 2023). It is essential to remember that these data correspond only to reported cases. It is estimated that only 15% of child sexual abuse cases are reported, due to social stigma, economic difficulties, the fact that in most cases the perpetrator is a family member or acquaintance, or simply the arduous nature of the judicial process. Additionally, approximately 70% of cases of sexual violence against minors who enter the legal system never reach a trial. This is precisely the fate that has befallen the cases of the girls from Getxo and the minors recorded in the locker rooms of the municipal swimming pools in Ugao-Miraballes, among others. And it is essential to understand that child sexual abuse does not always imply physical contact. Recording a child or exposing them to sexual content also constitutes abuse. In the case of Ugao, Court Number 6 of Bilbao dismissed the case, considering that there were not enough evidence to support the accusations against a man who, allegedly, recorded girls aged 11 and 12 in the municipal locker rooms. This occurred despite the testimonies of dozens of people and the precedent that a school football coach had identified the same individual recording the young female players from the locality months earlier. Nevertheless, the court determined that there was not enough evidence to continue with the case. The families publicly expressed their discontent, stating that neither the suspect's residence nor their electronic devices were searched. Ironically, it was one of the mothers who was eventually charged by the alleged perpetrator, and in this case, an oral trial was held, although the woman was ultimately acquitted. In the case of the four-year-old girls from the Europa school in Getxo, the families have stated that the court did not accept key evidence, such as the statements from the pediatricians at the Hospital who treated the minors, nor the statements from the non-reporting parents of the same. Nor was the pre-constituted test conducted on a girl with autism, nor was her mother allowed to testify, which violates her fundamental right to express herself through other people. And despite the evidence, having medical reports and several girls pointing to the same man, in this case, the judge also decided to archive the case for the time being.Another more recent example is given in the comarca of LeaArtibai, where the child psychological service of the DFB alerted that there were indicators of possible abuse to a five-year-old girl Following a swift trial at the Gernika courts, it has been decided provisionally that the parent will continue with the visits typical of shared custody. The affected families agree that the judicial system is not adapted or prepared to address childhood, a diagnosis shared by various studies, including that conducted by Save the Children (2023). According to this organization, court proceedings are too lengthy, and minors must declare multiple times, in some cases up to three or four times before the trial. Only 24.9% of cases utilize the pre-constituted evidence, which allows for recording the testimony to prevent re-victimization. Moreover, the professionals involved are not always sensitized or trained to handle minors in situations of extreme vulnerability. Instead of adequate protocols and psychological support, they are faced with prolonged judicial processes, obstacles to the credibility of their testimonies, and a sense of vulnerability that can inhibit future denunciations. This further aggravates the impact of abuse on victims (Estrategia Vasca contra la Violencia hacia la Infancia y la Adolescencia, 2022). In light of all this, we consider it urgent to take into account the existing regional, national, and international regulations that establish fundamental principles for the protection of minors in the judicial sphere, such as avoiding revictimization, minimizing the number of interviews, ensuring that they are conducted by trained professionals, recording them for use as evidence, and guaranteeing that the victim does not have direct contact with the accused. In the end, those responsible for protecting minors often fail to provide them with the necessary protection and support, leaving their families in a state of vulnerability, uncertainty, and desperation. The voices of children and adolescents are not always heard, nor are their testimonies valued. It is essential to improve our institutions and adapt them to these realities. Reporting a crime not only serves a punitive function, but also allows us to identify the perpetrators and prevent new cases. However, the protection of childhood does not end in the judicial sphere. There is still much work to be done in other social spaces, such as the fight against the hyper-sexualization of children in the audiovisual industry, the media, and fashion, with examples like padded bras for girls or inappropriate costumes. Child sexual abuse is not an isolated or distant problem. Denying its existence only benefits the perpetrators. It is time to act with firmness in prevention, protection, and justice.

data.text: Nashville (Tennessee). El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos presentó una acusación formal en el Distrito Medio de Tennessee contra ocho ciudadanos venezolanos, acusándolos de su presunta participación en una red de tráfico sexual que operó en moteles de Nashville desde julio de 2022 hasta marzo de 2024. Los acusados enfrentan cargos por diversos delitos, incluido el tráfico de personas y la explotación sexual con fines comerciales. According to judicial documents, the accused were running a human trafficking network that facilitated the arrival of young women in the United States, who were subsequently forced to participate in sex exploitation activities.Yilibeth del Carmen Rivero De Caldera, 51 years old Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero, 35 years old Yuribetzi Del Valle Gómez Machuca, 39 years old Wilmarys Del Valle Manzano Solórzano, 22 years old Frankyanna Del Valle Romero Rivero, 30 years old Endrik Alexander Morales Rivero, 25 years old Jesús Enrique Castillo Rodríguez, 24 years old and Ariannys Beatriz Gutiérrez Carrillo, 24 years old.The indictment details that the accused used online advertising websites to coordinate sexual encounters and managed commercial activity through phone calls and mobile messages. The buyers of these services were directed to specific motels in Nashville, where the victims were sexually exploited under the control of the accused, who ensured that all profits obtained from the illegal activity were collected. Three of the accused, RiveroDe Caldera, MotaRivero, and Gómez Machuca, are also facing charges of sex trafficking conspiracy, allegedly employing coercion, fraud, and threats to subject the victims and force them to participate in these acts. Federal and state authorities stated that this operation is part of a larger effort to dismantle transnational criminal organizations, including the Aragua Train, a dangerous Venezuelan gang with presence in several countries in Latin America and the United States. Interim U.S. Attorney Robert E McGuire emphasized the Department of Justice's commitment to combating human trafficking and pursuing organized crime networks, stating that they will pursue any organization involved in the trafficking of women and girls, regardless of the scope of their operation. We are pursuing transnational organized crime groups like TdA, but this case demonstrates that we will do whatever it takes to stop those who traffic women and girls, regardless of who is behind their suffering, McGuire said.Investigations also revealed that RiveroDe Caldera and his son, MotaRivero, implemented a coercive debt system to subjugate the victims. This scheme involved forcing them to pay exorbitant sums they supposedly owed for their transportation and stay, trapping them in the exploitation network until the accused decided the debt was paid. This type of practice is common in human trafficking organizations and is designed to maintain control over the victims, who many times do not see an exit due to threats of violence or reprisals against their families in their countries of origin. Additionally, the formal charge indicates that MotaRivero faces an additional charge of possession of a firearm as an illegal alien, which reinforces the connection of the network with broader criminal activities. If found guilty, the accused could face severe prison sentences. The conspiracy to commit sex trafficking carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment, while the interstate transportation for prostitution and assistance to organized crime businesses have a maximum penalty of five years in prison. Additionally, MotaRivero could face up to 15 years in prison for the charge of illegal possession of a firearm. The Department of Justice noted that, although the accused have been formally charged, they are presumed innocent until proven otherwise in a court of law. The case was investigated by a coalition of federal, state, and local agencies, including the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). These entities work together within the Organized Crime and Drug Enforcement Task Force (OCDETF) to dismantle criminal networks that pose a threat to the security of the United States. The FBI has categorized human trafficking as one of the most heinous and pressing crimes of the present day. Authorities have urged anyone with information about human trafficking to report it by calling the National Human Trafficking Hotline at 1 (888) 373-7888, available 24 hours a day.

A member of the Aragua Train gang, wanted for murder in Dallas and hiding in an apartment in Houston, got the surprise of a lifetime early this month when federal agents surrounded him as part of President Trump's nationwide deportation raids. The Post was on the scene with Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials as they watched the suspected killer's hideout in a crime-ridden neighborhood with a large immigrant community. LATEST The New York Post Reveals images of the dramatic moment ICE captures a suspect in the Aragua Train murder case who was hiding in HoustonURLpic.twitter.com Albert Rod News (AlbertoRodNews) February 12, 2025 Federal agents had received a tip that the documented member of the Venezuelan prison gang was in the area after he was spotted walking his dog During hours, ICE officers and a series of other federal agencies waited for the target to reappear. When he finally came out, the gang member with a baby face, whom authorities asked the Post not to reveal his name because he was still being processed, seemed dazed when he was surrounded from behind by sturdy federal agents while crossing the complex courtyard. He surrendered quickly without resisting, his face turned pale when he realized what was happening. The agents had a warrant for arrest from the Dallas authorities and wanted to catch him when he was not in his element to ensure he could not take out a weapon and defend himself. The Trump administration's mass deportation effort had already resulted in 11,000 arrests of illegal immigrants in its first 18 days, and the White House is pushing for more. And on Tuesday, everything went back to normal as FBI agents arrested three suspected gang members of the Tren de Aragua in another Houston apartment complex after they were allegedly linked to a sex trafficking ring that threatened and abused victims in several states. Images shared on X showed FBI and HSI agents cuffing the suspected perpetrators in a local apartment complex. The Tren de Aragua gang member was just one of the few migrant offenders detained on the streets during The Post's ride-along. Agents from several federal agencies met with ICE at 5 a.m. that day to gear up and brief on their objectives: catching illegal immigrant criminals. ICE Houston Field Office Detention and Removal Operations Director Bret Bradford told The Post that the arrest is a huge victory. That is a suspected murderer we are removing from the community and off the streets here in Houston so he will not reoffend and victimize even more people in the community, said Bradford. The officers and ICE agents are identifying targets, conducting background investigations, and conducting surveillance to ensure they are taking the worst of the worst off the streets, said the ICE Director in Houston. When we leave this building, we know exactly who we are going to pursue on the streets, said Bradford. Bradford said the agency's operations are targeted, and added We don't do anything indiscriminately, we're not going into areas to control them or anything like that. The Caravan of Aragua has unleashed violent crime across the entire United States after massive waves of illegal immigrants entered the country during the Biden years. A well-known example of the terror of the Aragua Train in the United States is the brutal murder of Laken Riley, a Georgia nursing student. France is facing its largest-ever trial for child abuse with the case of Joël Le Scouarnec, a digestive surgeon accused of sexually assaulting hundreds of patients, many of whom were minors, while they were under anesthesia in hospitals in Brittany and western France. The trial will begin on February 24 in Vannes and will last four months, sparking outrage and concerns over child protection in France. It is estimated that Le Scouarnec, 73 years old, attacked 299 people between 1989 and 2014, of whom 256 were under 15 years old. The average age of the victims was 11 years old. Key evidence in the trial includes notebooks written by hand by Le Scouarnec, in which he recorded the initials of his patients and the crimes committed against them. The police compared these records with hospital files to identify the victims, some of whom were unconscious when they were assaulted. Despite the FBI having alerted French authorities in 2004 about his consumption of child abuse material online, the surgeon only received a suspended four-year sentence in 2005 and was able to continue working with children at prestigious hospitals. Prosecutor Stéphane Kellenberger noted that Le Scouarnec explained his modus operandi, his determination to act, and his strategies for concealment. The accused has partially admitted to some charges, while denying others.Penal background of Scouarnec Francesca Satta, lawyer for 10 victims, highlighted that this trial is unique in the world due to the number of those affected. Two of her clients took their own lives after learning of the events when they were children. Satta recalled that in 2020, Le Scouarnec was sentenced to 15 years in prison for assaulting four children, one of whom was hospitalized. In 2017, police raided Le Scouarnec's home after neighbors filed complaints in Jonzac, discovering images of child abuse, notebooks, and dolls hidden under the floor. Frédéric Benoist, lawyer for the organization La Voix de L'Enfant, reported a chain of institutional failures that allowed Le Scouarnec to continue committing crimes. The FBI warned in 2004 about his activity in the dark net, but police only summoned him to testify without raiding his home or office at the hospital. After his conviction in 2005, no psychiatric treatment was imposed, nor were any restrictions placed on him working with minors. Even in 2006, doctors alerted management about his strange behavior and conviction, but he continued to practice.

The man who was murdered on the streets of the Hipódromo Condesa colony last weekend has been identified as Miguel Ángel N, a Colombian national and member of the Aragua Train organized crime group, local Fiscalía sources told Excélsior. They added that the direct attack was allegedly carried out by members of an antagonistic group and that the body had not been claimed until last Monday. The homicide occurred on the night of February 8, at the intersection of Avenues Nuevo León and Michoacán, where the victim was in a public area when two individuals arrived on a motorcycle and opened fire on him. Through the video surveillance and private security cameras in the area, the authorities confirmed that the suspected perpetrators posed as fast food delivery personnel. According to sources consulted, the authorities mapped the escape route of the hitmen, and are now monitoring the area where they arrived to make their arrest. The Aragua Train is a criminal organization that originated in Venezuela, primarily dedicated to human trafficking in its sexual exploitation modality. Local authority reports indicate that this group has settled in the center of Mexico City. In recent months, three members of the Aragua Train were apprehended for their alleged involvement in the femicide of two young Venezuelan women, whose bodies were found charred in the Topilejo area.

In the eye of the hurricane is Deputy Jorge Durán (RN), who was accused this Tuesday of physical abuse, sexual abuse, and rape by his ex-partner, Macarena Villablanca, after receiving a complaint of robbery and extortion made by the parliamentarian himself, allegedly committed on the previous Saturday in the Santiago commune of Colina. That night, we shared an intimate moment in a consensual manner. The next day, in the presence of witnesses, we shared breakfast and lunch, maintaining a cordial coexistence. According to the legislator, after that and clarifying that our sentimental relationship would not be rekindled, my ex-partner began demanding a sum of money, claiming that if I did not comply with her demands, I would be the one harmed. In response to this extortion situation and after discovering that she had used one of my credit cards without my authorization, I proceeded to file a report on Monday evening with Carabineros for extortion and theft. The authorities came to my residence, where they gathered the relevant information, he assured. To my surprise, after my report, my former partner filed a complaint against me for abuse, which has created a completely distorted situation and has significantly affected my public image, the Renovación Nacional politician concluded. At a press conference, Macarena Villablanca gave her version of the events and categorically denied attempting to extort the legislator. I was asking her to pay the outstanding tickets because I managed her social media, she said in her defense. I'm getting tired of him inventing things, lying. He always told me that I was the girlfriend of a deputy, that I had to behave like one. Jorge threatened to destroy my life and that of my family, the accuser alleged. Villablanca also pointed out that on more than one occasion, the legislator was aggressive towards her. He had violent attitudes, but they were casual. In other words, he was also under psychiatric treatment, he was on medication, and was dealing with a declared depression, which was being treated, but at the same time he was drinking alcohol, which is counterproductive to his treatment. Regarding the complaint she filed for physical abuse, sexual abuse, and rape, the woman detailed that he mentioned it was consensual, but in the conversation, he said "I'm drunk, I'm here by the pool." If he was drunk, how is he going to know or be able to discern if I gave or didn't give him my consent, she argued. Regardless of whether the sexual examination comes out or not, at least this has come to light. This is not the first time he has committed abuse, she concluded.The reactions were immediate, and from the government, the Minister of the Interior, Carolina Tohá, stated that no one in Chile can question that an accusation of rape is something serious, in any case, because there is a person, in this case a woman, who has been vulnerable. The authority added that if the accused person, in addition to having a position of authority, this is even more serious. In parallel, Renovación Nacional reported that the case has already been forwarded to their Supreme Court and everything points to Durán's continuation in the party hanging by a thread. This was highlighted in a conversation with Mucho Gusto morning show by Deputy Ximena Ossandón, who stated that when we conduct investigative commissions, when we hold special sessions, he never signs things on behalf of the bench, a matter that has us quite annoyed.

Sean Combs, known professionally as Diddy, has filed a lawsuit against NBC Universal, alleging that a documentary by the network falsely accuses him of multiple crimes, including murder and child sex abuse. The lawsuit, filed in a New York state court on Wednesday, claims that the documentary titled Diddy Making of a Bad Boy includes statements that NBC Universal knew were false or were published with reckless disregard for the truth, in order to defame the founder of Bad Boy Records. Combs is seeking at least $100 million in damages, arguing that the documentary presents a series of baseless accusations that damage his reputation and his right to a fair trial. The documentary assumes that Mr. Combs has committed numerous heinous crimes, including serial murder, child rape, and child sex trafficking, according to the lawsuit. In addition, the text mentions that the documentary portrays him as a monster and compares him to Jeffrey Epstein. The documentary, which premiered last month on the Peacock TV streaming service, aims to explore Combs' life from his childhood to his rise as a music mogul. However, its description suggests that it focuses on the controversies and the darker side of his career. Combs is currently incarcerated in Brooklyn, following his arrest in September on charges of conspiracy to extort and sex trafficking. Federal prosecutors have alleged that he used his wealth and power to coerce victims into participating in prolonged sexual performances under the influence of drugs, known as Freak Offs. According to the indictment, Combs allegedly used blackmail and violence to intimidate his victims, in a pattern of abuse dating back to the early 2000s. Combs has pleaded not guilty and his trial is set to begin in May 2024. Combs' attorney Erica Wolff argues that NBC and other parties involved in the lawsuit transmitted scandalous lies to increase the documentary's audience. By creating and disseminating these falsehoods, the defendants only seek to capitalize on the public's appetite for scandal, without regard for the truth and at the expense of Mr. Combs' right to a fair trial, Wolff states in a statement. The lawsuit also addresses allegations that Combs was involved in the deaths of several close associates, including Kimberly Porter, Christopher Wallace, and Dwight Arrington Myers. Porter, Combs' former girlfriend and mother of some of his children, died in 2008 at 47 years old due to complications from pneumonia. Wallace, known as The Notorious B.I.G., was murdered in a shootout in 1997 that remains unsolved. Myers, known as Heavy D, died in 2011 due to a pulmonary embolism. In addition, the lawsuit criticizes the documentary's treatment of the claims about Combs' supposed relationship with minors, citing a civil complaint that has been entirely discredited. Combs' lawyers argue that the women mentioned in that complaint have confirmed they were adults at the time of the incidents.

Pinta's Defense Requests Acquittal (Pablo Leguizamon) In the closing of the trial against kayaking multi-champion Néstor Piri Pinta, the prosecution asked that the elite athlete be sentenced to 15 years in prison, allegedly having handed over former students to his father to abuse them. After the Criminal Court N° 3 of Bahía Blanca rejected a nullity request by the defense for the second time, the King of the River admitted that there were several similarities in the testimonies of the witnesses. The lawyer for the complainants against the sports reference from Carmen de Patagones, María Fernanda Petersen, argued that the accused should face a sentence of 15 years in prison, plus legal accessories and costs, considering him criminally responsible for the crime of gravely outrageous sexual abuse, as a necessary participant in two real concurrent facts. Mr. Néstor Pinta did not reach this stage merely because he is the abuser's son, but for his deliberate cooperation in the perpetration of the sexual abuses that occurred, the prosecutor argued, after highlighting that the incidents had been going on for a long period of time. During the prosecution's argument, the prosecution emphasized that his role as a coach of a canoe school implies an ethical and legal obligation to protect minors, referring to the fact that the complainants were minors at the time the abuses occurred. The judges will have a one-week deadline to announce their verdict (CIJur). In the document to which Infobae had access, Petersen pointed out that his inaction not only defrauded the trust deposited in him, but also allowed acts of abuse to be perpetrated that could have been avoided. And he pointed out that without this cooperation, not watching over the care of the victims, deliberate omissions, the crime would not have been committed, nor sustained over time. Another of the details highlighted by the complaint consisted of the invitations that the accused would have made to the complainants to join the kayaking team he trained at the Carmen de Patagones Municipal School. At the same time, he emphasized that his idol role was a key factor, since both claimed to have felt proud of being called by him. It was not just the sports director, who was in charge of the canoe school, but also the sports icon, the idol, with whom all, according to the statements of the victims, wanted to row, he emphasized by pointing out that the weight of his image would have been used as a tool to ensure trust. After reiterating that it was impossible for him not to know about the alleged abuses committed by his father in their marital bedroom, since he was in the adjacent room during lunch with the rest of the team, he claimed that Pinta, knowing what was happening, continued to invite young people to join this institution. The lawsuit highlighted that Pinta's status as a sports idol was crucial for the events to occur (Pablo Leguizamon). Even, the lawyer questioned the nature of the massage sessions that his father performed on the athletes, after pointing out that the parents of the underage girls were never informed. In addition, he stated that the room in which the events occurred was not prepared for that purpose, because there was not even a massage table inside. In addition to pointing out that Aldo Pinta did not have any type of authorization or hiring for offering that kind of service to athletes, the complaint highlighted that as an elite athlete, he should not have allowed young athletes to receive massages before going to the gym, as it is not recommended. The sentencing of Mr. Néstor Pinta should be seen as a step towards justice, not only for the victims, but also as a clear message about the importance of responsibility and the duty of protection that people in positions of trust have, Petersen sentenced. Before this, the canoeing reference made use of his right to declare before the court, where he again denied having any knowledge of the alleged abuses that his father would have committed against his former students. And he assured that he would have found out about the complaints after being summoned by the mayor of Carmen de Patagones.Victoria Carrión, one of the complainants who attended the municipal school that bears the name of the reference (Pablo Leguizamón), At the same time that he recognized feeling remorseful for the way he acted with his father because today he does not have him alive, he admitted the possibility that something may have happened. The reflection arose from the testimonies brought by the witnesses, however, he denied the cases of the complainants. In response to this, Pinta's lawyer, Maximiliano De Mira, requested an impromptu statement, in which he asked the court to grant the nullity of the evidence request, considering that the accusation was not clear and that there were not enough evidence to continue with the trial. The appeal had already been presented during the hearing on Monday and, like in the first instance, it was rejected again. For this reason, the defense requested Pinta's acquittal, assuring that he had no way of knowing about the existence of the alleged abuses. After the judicial process was closed, judges Daniela Castaño, Eduardo DEmpaire, and Julián Saldías will have a week to take a decision regarding the facts for which Pinta was accused. The court will have three possible options: accept the prosecution's request, propose a sentence of their own, or grant the defense's request for acquittal.

Tragic reality of the minors victims of trafficking in Mexico. She seemed to be an adolescent like any other. She had two eyes, a mouth, two legs, and the charm that every woman, simply by being one, usually has. She was known for her beauty. She couldn't go out onto the street without receiving the accustomed catcalls from all the men who saw her. The other young women in the neighborhood envied her body, however, she was a girl of just 13 years old. One day, poverty led her to ask for work at a supposed modeling agency. As was logical, the entrepreneurs immediately hired her, because they saw that with that virgin body they could obtain many profits. They didn't even ask if she was of age, they only focused on her beauty, and once a contract of no legal value was signed, they ordered her to practice some steps, because that same night she had to dance and undress to please some gentlemen who would come to see her. It might interest you that pure vanity is what they sell us on TV. Time passed and she stopped being a common girl. She's no longer called by her old name, now they've temporarily named her Yesenia. Her beautiful black hair was dyed and now they promote her as the Gold Girl. And that's how her life has gone on. Between wine glasses, the lights of that dive, and the dirty desires of hundreds of men who night after night dream of being with her, the need robbed her of a piece of her life, robbed her of her innocence. The girl who was in her heart is now simply a woman forced to endure daily humiliation to eat, a woman who has lost her own name and is now called prostitute, harlot, courtesan, bitch, hetaira, streetwalker, or some people simply reduce her name to four cruel and offensive letters. You've heard stories like that of this young girl who, being very young, was defeated by hunger and was forced to sell her body for a few pesos. It's enough to examine the sad reality that our country offers when it comes to human trafficking. According to the Executive Secretariat of the National Public Security System, during the first half of 2024, 185 cases of victims of the crime of human trafficking were reported. During the two semesters of 2023, 382 cases were reported. Although cases decreased marginally, during the first half of 2024, more crimes against childhood and adolescence were registered than in previous years. Likewise, it was reported that 81.1% were women and 18.9% were men. Although human trafficking involves forced labor, prostitution, and others, the most common case of trafficking is for purposes of sexual exploitation. It is no secret to affirm that within organized crime groups, there are child traffickers who supply brothels across the country. Many of them were kidnapped or deceived by these individuals who threaten the victims of human trafficking with killing their family members if they try to escape. One of the reasons why I proudly call myself Coahuilense is because in our state, strip clubs and brothels are prohibited outside of the Tolerant Zone. I hope that President Claudia Sheinbaum, in her recent and obligatory crusade against narco-gang groups, does not only focus on attacking cartels that produce and traffic fentanyl. The simplest way for delinquents to launder money and enter is through establishments where abuse, insecurity, corruption, and lost innocence of children and girls abound.

data.text: A disturbing case unfolded when a young woman came forward as she reached adulthood to report her father and son for alleged sexual abuse. A father and his son were detained today in the Buenos Aires district of La Matanza for allegedly being the perpetrators of a sexual abuse against a young woman when she was a minor. A father and his son were detained today in the Buenos Aires district of La Matanza for allegedly being the perpetrators of a sexual abuse against a minor. Police sources reported that the case was initiated when the victim reached adulthood and filed a complaint in which she stated that she was abused during her childhood by her stepfather at the time. The alleged incidents occurred in the family home located in the town of Gregorio de Laferrere between 2010 and 2012, when the affected girl was 5 and 6 years old. According to her testimony, the sexual attacks occurred when the victim was under the care of the accused, who threatened her with death on multiple occasions and avoided any accusations against him. However, during a move made between 2016 and 2017, the victim was sexually assaulted again, but at that time, the perpetrator would have been the son of the main suspect. In this context, at the end of January, the Specialized Unit for Instruction and Trial in Family Violence and Gender Violence and Crimes Against Sexual Integrity Number One of the La Matanza Judicial Department convened the Division of Crimes Against Public Health of the Federal Police with the purpose of identifying and capturing the suspects. The officers apprehended the individuals involved on García Merou streets, in Laferrere's Gregorio, and Riglos in González Catán, respectively. Both detainees, one of them a Bolivian national, were placed at the disposal of the intervening judge for the crime of gravely outrageous sexual abuse, committed against a minor under 18 years old, taking advantage of the situation of cohabitation and committed by the person in charge of the guard, in ideal concurrence with aggravated corruption of a minor.

data.text: The authorities conducted a search warrant at a residence in the La Unión neighborhood of Itagüí, in the south of the Aburrá Valley, where they found and apprehended a 23-year-old man suspected of exercising sexual violence against a minor. According to the Metropolitan Police report, this man had allegedly had a sentimental relationship with the victim for three years. When she decided to end this relationship, the man, it seems, threatened and pressured her not to do so. It may interest you that an 11-year-old girl was a victim of sexual abuse in Manrique, and the community helped capture the alleged perpetrator. In view of the fact that the adolescent could no longer endure the situation and decided to maintain her decision to end the relationship, the now-accused man allegedly uploaded videos and photographs of the sexual abuses he committed against her to social media and digital platforms, according to Brigadier General William Castaño Ramos, commander of the Metropolitan Police. The commander added that during the raid at the residence, they found two cellphones on the man with evidence of the child sexual material he had distributed from them. Read also One more. "Go home" prevents another foreigner from entering Medellín due to alert as possible sex aggressor of minors. This investigation lasted around a month in which authorities collected evidence to request the operation in articulation with the General Prosecutor's Office, as well as the arrest warrant against the alleged sex abuser, who now faces a judicial process for the crimes of child pornography and abusive carnal access with a minor under 14 years old. In the dwelling, at the time of the operation, the uniformed officers also captured a 48-year-old woman, who would be the mother of the alleged perpetrator, to whom they found elements that were confiscated, such as a.38 caliber revolver, 12 cartridges, 54 grams of cocaine base, 150 paper sheets of cocaine base, and dosing equipment. In the official report, it was stated that the woman was captured in flagrante delicto, but it was not specified whether she was linked to the case of the sexual crimes against the minor or if she played any role in it. Both captured people were presented before the competent authorities for their judicialization. Regarding this, Commander Castaño Ramos stated that, after the preliminary hearings, the man was imposed a measure of private deprivation of liberty in a correctional center. The colonel also stated that in what has been run of 2025, the Police have captured nine people in the different municipalities of the Aburrá Valley for sex crimes against children, girls, and adolescents. Remember that these incidents must be reported immediately to any authority, on line 123 or on line 141 of the ICBF. It doesn't matter if it's about cases that are happening in homes, schools, community sites, hotels, or public places, citizens are co-responsible and must inform the authorities about them. In a joint operation between the Attorney General's Office and the National Police, a 23-year-old man was apprehended in the La Unión neighborhood of Itagüí municipality, Antioquia. The suspect is being investigated for the crimes of child pornography and statutory rape with a minor under 14 years old. The investigation revealed that the man had a three-year romantic relationship with a 16-year-old girl. After the breakup, the individual allegedly posted photos and videos of a sexual nature of the minor on social media, violating her intimacy and exposing her to a serious risk. During the search of the suspect's residence, authorities seized two mobile devices that had allegedly been used to disseminate the illicit material. The month-long investigation allowed for the collection of evidence that supported the arrest warrant issued by the Attorney General's Office. During the same operation, a 48-year-old woman, the mother of the perpetrator, was detained in flagrancy, and a.38 caliber revolver, 12 bullets, 54 grams of cocaine base, 150 cocaine base slips, and substances for dosing of narcotics were seized from her. Both the man and his mother were placed at the disposal of the competent authorities for their judicialization. In the preliminary hearings, the man was provisionally detained in a correctional center, while the woman's legal situation will be defined in the coming hours.

data.text: Narcotics trafficker arrested at an Ibiza nightclub in an unexpected turn of events during the trial The 23-year-old, arrested in Ibiza, was on the verge of sending two large trucks with 307 kilograms of narcotics Two large trucks intercepted at the port of Dover (United Kingdom) loaded with 307 kilograms of narcotics (heroin, cocaine, and ketamine) worth €24 million on the black market in the summer of 2022 initiated an investigation that ended with the arrest of Eddie Burton, 23 years old, a year later at the Pacha nightclub in Ibiza. His fingerprints and DNA on the trucks and narcotics led the British National Crime Agency (NCA) to the island, where he spent long periods, although he lived in Amsterdam. In this operation, his girlfriend, Sian Banks, 25 years old, was also detained for collaborating in this criminal enterprise. At the beginning of February, a trial commenced at the Court of the Crown of Canterbury against this young couple of narcotics traffickers, and both pleaded guilty to several charges of drug trafficking. Apparently, this criminal couple lived between Amsterdam and Ibiza, although he would often use various false names to avoid being intercepted by the police. Unexpected turn in the trial Yesterday, Wednesday, February 12, it was expected that Judge Simon Tylor would pass sentence on both. Surprisingly, young Eddie Burton is being saved from this for the moment. Just before the judicial session began in which the couple's sentence was to be revealed, Eddie Burton's lawyers handed a letter to the judge, in which the accused claimed that he participated in this criminal scheme because he was threatened with death, along with his family, if he did not, and because he had to settle an important debt. There are things I could have done differently, but there were threats of death against my family, explains Burton in his letter, according to the Liverpool Echo newspaper, from which the young man is native. Apparently, the letter is full of justifications for why he was forced to join a narcotics trafficking group. Judge Taylor, instead of issuing a sentence, explained that in the accused's explanation he saw modern slavery threats and couldn't ignore this matter. British journalists explain in their chronicles that Eddie's little boy face has also influenced this judicial decision. On the other hand, Burton's lawyer, Notu Hoon, explained that his client's stance was that, despite the accusations of modern slavery, he did not want to change his arguments. Hoon said that his client maintained he was coerced, but not in the sense of modern slavery. Judge Taylor added that this written statement explaining why someone pleads guilty to a crime suggests a lesser role in the scheme. At the same time, Burton refused to be re-questioned on this matter because, considering the threats he had suffered, he did not want to give the names of other individuals involved in this major drug trafficking shipment. Judge Taylor postponed Burton's sentence until next month, when a new basis for the argument will be presented to the court. However, it was not the same for his girlfriend, Sian Banks, who was sentenced by Judge Taylor to 5 years in prison.

According to a complaint filed in New York obtained by People, the anonymous plaintiff, a young musician from Chicago, claims that he was traveling in Los Angeles in 2022 when a Combs associate approached him and allegedly told him that the founder of Bad Boy Records was looking for new talent. The plaintiff says that he was then invited to Combs' birthday party and that a driver picked him up and took him to a private residence. At the party, the plaintiff claims to have met Diddy, who approached him saying, "My assistant told me you have a beautiful voice. Sit down, take a drink with me, and let's talk business." After being offered a drink, the plaintiff says that Combs promised him that he could get him a record deal and then asked him if he wanted to see his collection of jewelry. The plaintiff claims that he went with Combs to a private room and began to feel strange. The complaint alleges that the man was drugged. Later, Combs is accused of exposing his genitals to the plaintiff, asking him if he had ever performed oral sex on a man before and urging him to try it. The plaintiff claims that he then tried to leave, but Combs prevented him and told him that he would not receive a contract unless he complied. The complaint alleges that Combs lost his patience and forcibly inserted his penis into the plaintiff's mouth. The plaintiff also alleges that Combs stripped him naked and raped him before leaving him incapacitated in bed. The lawsuit is one of the dozen that accuses Combs of sexual misconduct, and the plaintiff is one of many being represented by Houston attorney Tony Buzbee. Combs has previously denied all allegations of sexual assault. Combs cannot respond to every new marketing maneuver, nor even to statements that are ridiculous or demonstrably false, said Combs' representative in a statement to PEOPLE. Mr. Combs and his legal team have full confidence in the facts and integrity of the judicial process. In court, the truth will prevail that Mr. Combs never sexually assaulted nor trafficked anyone, man or woman, adult or minor. Combs is also facing criminal charges after being accused of federal charges of sex trafficking, organized crime, and transporting for prostitution. He pleaded not guilty and is currently being held at the Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center while awaiting trial.

data.text: Federal authorities in the United States have charged eight Venezuelan nationals, allegedly in the country illegally, with operating a human trafficking ring across multiple states. This criminal organization is linked to the Aragua Train gang, known for its expansion in Latin America and involvement in crimes such as extortion and human trafficking.Victim recruitment and modus operandiAccording to the federal indictment, the arrested individuals lured women from South America with false promises of employment and a better quality of life in the US. However, once in US territory, the victims were subjected to sexual exploitation to pay off supposed debts accumulated during their illegal entry into the country. US Acting Attorney Robert McGuire detailed that these women, far from their homes and without support, were intimidated and threatened. In some cases, the traffickers would take away their children and migrant documents as a method of coercion to ensure their submission. Leaders of the network and links to the Aragua Train The investigation indicates that the human trafficking network was led by a mother and son. The individuals were identified as Yilibeth del Carmen Rivero del Caldero and Clebier Daniel MotaRivero. Both would have used their connection with the Aragua Train to intimidate the victims and force them to pay debts through sexual exploitation. Additionally, MotaRivero faces an additional charge for the illegal possession of a firearm, as he was found with a 9mm Glock pistol despite his irregular migrant status. Two other adult sons of Rivero del Caldero are among the eight arrested. Of these, five were captured in Tennessee and three in Texas. Commitment of authorities to curb organized crime The director of the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, David R. B. Rauch stated that the authorities are committed to dismantling these criminal organizations. We will not allow the Aragua Train nor any other criminal gang to establish operations in our state. We will pursue these delinquents and use all available legal tools to dismantle these networks and bring justice, Rauch declared. The case remains under development as the accused face federal charges for human trafficking and organized crime.

The Specialized Section on Gender Violence, Human Trafficking, and Illicit Migration Trafficking of the Judicial Investigation Body (OIJ) carried out six raids on Wednesday in various points of San José, specifically in Barrio Escalante, Curridabat, Rohmoser, Pavas, and La Veinticinco de Julio, with the aim of dismantling a criminal gang. The agents detained five women and one man as suspects of committing the crime of human trafficking for sexual exploitation, in an apparent massage parlor. The detained women are identified by the surnames Godínez, 29 years old, Ureña, 29 years old, Vargas, 19 years old, Barboza, 28 years old, Picado, 39 years old, and a male, Morales, 35 years old, who appears to be the leader of the gang. The authorities are still searching for the wife of the male, who also appears to have recruited women to force them to provide massage therapy services with explicit sexual content. During the operations, police seized 12 cell phones, a hard drive, four vehicles, three computers, five recorders, two tablets, and various documentation related to the investigation, in addition to one million colons in cash.

The judge of Tarija, Nelson Rocabado, issued a new warrant for apprehension and conduct against former President Evo Morales, charged with the crime of human trafficking with aggravating circumstances. The court also confirmed the declaration of rebellion against him for not appearing to testify on two occasions. The document, issued in Tarija on Tuesday, January 11, instructs the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime (Felcc) or any competent authority to execute the apprehension of Morales, identified with ID card number 2763595, and to conduct him to the corresponding instances. Yesterday, it was also known that the judicial authority rejected an appeal presented by Morales' legal defense against the previous warrant for apprehension. In this way, it was confirmed that Morales must be apprehended and that he exhausted the judicial instances for future appeals. In accordance with the invoked norms and subject to Article 51. .1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CCP), the First Criminal Chamber of the Tarija Departmental Court of Justice (TDJ) declared the incidental appeal filed by Juan Evo Morales Ayma's private attorney inadmissible, as read in the judicial resolution of January 27, according to DTV. RATIFY REBELLION Furthermore, the TDJ of Tarija ratified the declaration of rebellion against the coca leader after he failed to appear for the second time to declare in the case he faces for human trafficking with aggravating circumstances, a process initiated in November 2024, when it was revealed that he had a relationship with a 15-year-old minor while serving as President of the State, whom he allegedly impregnated. The impugned resolution, being a declaration of rebellion, is not susceptible to further appeal. This is due to the fact that defiance is considered a direct consequence of the defendant's procedural attitude, who does not present himself to the judicial summons without a valid justification, adds the cited judicial resolution by Brújula Digital. The Minister of Government, Eduardo Del Castillo, recently stated that the Police already have the operation order for Morales' capture, although they await the precise moment and location to avoid bloodshed, a statement that reveals the government's fear towards the figure of the former president, according to several opponents. POSITIONS In the words of the deputy from Comunidad Ciudadana, José Ormachea, nothing will happen with the new arrest warrant as the officialdom would be negotiating MAS (Movement to Socialism) candidacies with the alleged Evoist faction, supposedly led by the Senate President, Andrónico Rodríguez. I said it when the last order was issued and I say it now. The arcismo won't jail the counterpart with whom it is negotiating a unity candidacy of the MAS with Andrónico at the head, he stated in his X account. Meanwhile, representatives of the evismo denounced political persecution against their leader by putting him on trial a dozen times without legal or judicial basis, an action that, according to Senator Leonardo Loza, was orchestrated by former Justice Minister Iván Lima Magne.

Statement from Jesus Sánchez, 56 years old, was arrested by uniformed officers of the Bolivarian Police Corps of the state of Zulia (Cpbez), accused of continued sexual abuse against his stepdaughter, a 13-year-old girl, in an incident that occurred in the Servio Tulio Peña sector, Libertad parish, Machiques de Perijá municipality. The case was reported by the authorities of the educational institution where the minor studies, the young girl told her teacher that she was being subjected to her stepfather for intimacy with him, who forced her to practice orogenital sex, and gave her birth control pills. Upon receiving the complaint, the officials went to the location where the accused was found and arrested, he was taken to the Machiques Police Coordination Center, where he was placed at the disposal of the 20th Fiscalia of the Public Ministry. The minor was taken to the Nuestra Señora del Carmen Hospital, where she received professional attention.

Texas State Police and the U.S. Border Patrol arrested a suspected coyote, a human trafficker, in El Paso after a high-speed chase ended in a crash. The driver of a Chevrolet Tahoe in beige, who attempted to evade authorities, triggered a pursuit. The chase ended with a collision involving the SUV and elements of the U.S. Border Patrol and the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). According to the official report, the arrested man is accused of being a coyote, a person who smuggles migrants illegally from Mexico to the United States. Texas state police took him into custody pending charges for human trafficking facilitated by migrant smuggling.

Two men remain missing after a water accident in Limón. The incident occurred in Bananito Sur at the Esmeralda beach, where a motorboat went off course and suffered an accident. The Red Cross of Costa Rica confirmed that two men are still missing after a water accident in Limón. On this Wednesday, the Benemérita carried out search operations until 5 p.m. without obtaining any positive results. Searches were conducted both on the beach and in open water with the collaboration of Coast Guard services, said Tatiana Díaz, regional operational coordinator. Family members and some friends of the victims joined the search efforts. The Red Cross of Costa Rica will continue its search efforts tomorrow along with other institutions for these two young men who were declared missing on Tuesday night, added Díaz. According to authorities, the boat was traveling with 3 people, of whom only one managed to escape. By Max Vásquez redaccionlatinocc.com Various law enforcement agencies in Ventura County conducted a series of operations against human trafficking in January as part of a state-led effort called Operation Recover and Rebuild, coordinated by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department. The operation aimed to combat sex and labor trafficking, rescue victims, and bring traffickers to justice, where the Ventura County Human Trafficking Task Force (VCHTTF) led local efforts in collaboration with the police departments of Ventura, Camarillo, Thousand Oaks, Oxnard, and Simi Valley. Additionally, agencies such as the FBI, Ventura County District Attorney's Office, and Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Department participated. Agents and detectives from various cities also helped identify suspicious businesses allegedly involved in activities related to human trafficking. As part of the operation, detectives conducted raids at locations known for their connection to human trafficking, including motels and massage parlors. One of these operations, carried out on January 30 in Ventura, resulted in the arrest of a trafficker with an outstanding arrest warrant in Monterey County for child sex trafficking. Additionally, a client of sex services was arrested after attempting to engage in illegal activities. The task force also conducted inspections at 26 suspected businesses operating as illicit massage businesses (IMBs), which often serve as fronts for human trafficking. As a result, five massage parlors were closed due to multiple code infractions, and authorities issued administrative citations to several businesses. The Ventura County Sheriff's Department (VCSO) stated that they provided resources to approximately 52 individuals working at these locations, many of whom are believed to be victims of labor or sex trafficking. These operations are crucial in our ongoing fight against human trafficking. Our goal is not only to hold traffickers accountable, but also to provide victims with the support and services they need to escape exploitation, the VCSO stated in a press release. Authorities urge anyone who may be a victim of human trafficking or knows someone in danger to call 211 or contact local law enforcement to receive help. The Ventura County Task Force Against Human Trafficking remains committed to raising awareness and preventing human trafficking through law enforcement efforts and outreach programs.

The judge from Tarija, Nelson Rocabado, issued a new arrest and detention order against the former president, Evo Morales, who is accused of the crime of human trafficking with aggravating circumstances. The court also confirmed the declaration of rebellion against him for not appearing to testify on two occasions. The document, issued in Tarija on Tuesday, January 11, instructs the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime (Felcc) or any competent authority to execute the arrest of Morales, identified by ID number 2763595, and to conduct him to the corresponding instances. Yesterday, it was also known that the judicial authority rejected an appeal presented by Morales' legal defense against the previous arrest order. In this way, it was confirmed that Morales must be arrested and that he has exhausted the judicial instances for future appeals. In accordance with the invoked norms and in accordance with Article 51. Article 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CPP), the First Penal Chamber of the Departmental Court of Justice (TDJ) of Tarija declares the incidental appeal filed by the private attorney of Juan Evo Morales Ayma inadmissible, as read in the judicial resolution of January 27, according to DTV. REBELDIA CONFIRMED Furthermore, the TDJ of Tarija confirmed the declaration of rebellion against the coca leader after he failed to appear for the second time to testify in the case he faces for human trafficking with aggravating circumstances, a process initiated in November 2024, when it was revealed that he had a relationship with a 15-year-old girl, whom he allegedly impregnated while serving as President of the State. The impugned resolution, being a declaration of rebellion, is not susceptible to further appeal. This is due to the fact that rebellion is considered a direct consequence of the procedural attitude of the accused, who does not present himself to the judicial summons without a valid justification, adds the judicial resolution cited by Brújula Digital. Recently, the Minister of Government, Eduardo Del Castillo, stated that the Police already has the order of operations for the capture of Morales, although they await the precise moment and place to avoid bloodshed, a statement that for several opponents reveals the government's fear of the figure of the former president. POSITIONS In the words of the deputy of Comunidad Ciudadana, José Ormachea, nothing will happen with the new arrest warrant because the officialdom would be negotiating MAS Movement (MAS) candidacies with the evista faction, supposedly led by the President of the Senate, Andrónico Rodríguez. I said it when the last order was issued and I say it now. The arcismo is not going to jail its counterpart with whom it is negotiating a unity candidacy of the MAS with Andrónico at the helm, he noted on his X account. Meanwhile, representatives of the evismo denounced political persecution against their leader by subjecting him to a dozen trials without legal or judicial basis, an action that, according to Senator Leonardo Loza, was orchestrated by former Minister of Justice, Iván Lima Magne.

In a harsh blow against child sexual exploitation, detectives from the Sexual Crimes Investigation Brigade (Brisex) in Punta Arenas arrested a 33-year-old man, who had outstanding arrest orders for the crimes of statutory rape of a 14-year-old and simple theft. The investigation, carried out in 2023, allowed for the establishment that the defendant, taking advantage of the vulnerability of two 13-year-old girls, subjected them to sexual abuse in exchange for drugs and tattoos. This case highlights a dynamic of child sexual exploitation (ESNNA) in which the perpetrator uses their power and resources to manipulate the victims, said Subprefect Jéssica Fuentealba, head of the Brisex Punta Arenas. Thanks to the work of our detectives, we have managed to put an end to this situation and bring the perpetrator to justice. The arrested individual was detained in public and placed at the disposal of the court for their respective detention control.

In an operation carried out in the early hours of this Thursday, February 13, authorities dealt a blow to a network dedicated to the production and commercialization of child sexual abuse material. The intervention was carried out by the National Police, the General Prosecutor's Office of the State, and the US Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agency, achieving the disarticulation of this criminal organization.They killed me alive a month after the kidnapping of a young woman in Manta, her mother still has no answers. We affected a child pornography network with the arrest of four suspects, the police institution reported. Four people were detained in simultaneous raids in Quito and Esmeraldas, while five minors were rescued. The investigations revealed that the arrested individuals distributed illicit material to US citizens and that the suspects themselves used their minor children to produce the content. During the operations, security forces seized 13 mobile phones, a tablet, two phone chips, investigation-related documents, and two payment receipts that would evidence illicit transactions linked to this criminal activity. Authorities continue with the proceedings to identify other possible suspects and determine the scope of this criminal network. Meanwhile, the rescued minors have been placed under specialized protection to ensure their safety. According to Article 104 of the Organic Integral Penal Code (COIP), the perpetrator of the crime of commercializing child pornography using minors, children, or adolescents (MCA) is the person who publishes, buys, possesses, carries, transmits, downloads, stores, imports, exports, or sells, through any means, child pornography for personal use or for exchange, and will be sanctioned with a prison sentence of ten to thirteen years.

Ryan M. Newman, 33 años de edad, de Corning, Nueva York, se declaró culpable de producir pornografía infantil ante el juez de distrito estadounidense Meredith A. Vacca. Como un delincuente sexual condenado en el momento de sus crímenes, Newman enfrenta una penalización mínima mejorada de 25 años de prisión, una penalización máxima de 50 años y una multa de $250,000. El fiscal asistente de los Estados Unidos, Kyle P. Rossi, que maneja el caso, declaró que Newman fue condenado por delitos pornográficos infantiles por el estado de Nueva York en 2012, sentenciado a cumplir un plazo de prisión local y 10 años de libertad condicional, y requirió que se registre como un nivel 3 delincuente sexual, que es alguien considerado con un alto riesgo de reincidencia y una amenaza para la seguridad pública. In January 2021, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) received a report from Snapchat that a user had uploaded a video of child pornography. NCMEC forwarded the tip to the New York State Police, who executed a search warrant on Newman in 2022. The search determined that Newman had uploaded the child pornography video to Snapchat and possessed other child pornography on his electronic devices. Newman remained at large following the 2022 search warrant by state police. In April 2024, the FBI Corning received a tip that child pornography involving a child in the Corning area was distributed to an undercover agent in Illinois. The subsequent investigation found that Newman had sexually abused the child and produced the child pornography. Newman was apprehended by the FBI and Corning Police. Newman is also charged in Steuben County Court. The statement is the result of an investigation conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Corning Office, under the direction of Special Agent Matthew Miraglia, and the Corning Police Department, under the direction of Chief Kenzie Spaulding. The sentencing is scheduled for June 11, 2025, at 10:00 a.m. before Judge Vacca. 2025/02/13/005400/1739414503 West New York District Corning Sex Offense declares guilty on new charges of child pornography.
