The Navarre company Arena Comunicación will produce La revuelta de las putas, an animated documentary based on the autobiographical essay of the same title by activist Amelia Tiganus, who will also star in the film. The same will tell the story of this writer and feminist who suffered for years from exploitation by the mafia of prostitution. Her perpetrators have classified it as a contemporary epic. Tiganus, born in Romania and resident in the Basque Country since 2007, is known for her activism against human trafficking and her defense of feminism. In her work, she has recounted how she suffered a gang rape at 13 and later was sold for 300 euros to a prostitution ring at 17, being transferred to Spain. Already in our country, and after suffering a physical and psychological collapse after years of abuse, she managed to escape from sexual slavery and became an active denouncer and disseminator of these situations. The Uprising of the Prostitutes, which will tell its story in the context of current feminist theory, will be a co-production between Spain, the Czech Republic, and Romania, which has just received development aid from the Europa Creativa MEDIA program. The animated documentary has made its way in recent times in Spanish cinema, with titles such as Bidasoa (2018-2023) (2023), by Fermín Muguruza, or the recent Goya winner Mariposas negras (2024), by David Baute. The Uprising of the Prostitutes, a European co-production The Uprising of the Prostitutes will be a production of Arena Comunicación, Films Chips (Czech Republic) and Animashort (Romania). The development team is formed by Pablo Iraburu, Amaia Remírez, and Migueltxo Molina. Executive production is by Arantza González-Boza (Arena), Hana Blaha Šilarová, Marek Čermák, and Karolína Dvorská Fránková (Films and Chips, Czech Republic), Andreea Gurban, and Anton Octavian (Animashort, Romania). Beatriz Setuain will coordinate the international co-production. Pablo Iraburu has stated that he explains that Amelia's rebellious and fighting spirit has inspired this project from its inception. It inspires women and men from different countries, professionals in animation and documentary, united by the power that cinema has to tell transformative stories. Amaia Remírez adds that Amelia reveals to us through her story of descent into hell and fight to reborn the oldest form of slavery in the world, hidden in plain sight in our cities. She is a heroine with a unique voice and nuances, from absolute horror to total enjoyment and innocence, and we hope that this film will take the viewers by the hand to put themselves in her skin and, inevitably, admire her strength. After being awarded the Eurorregión Prize last year in the framework of the Cartoon Forum fair, and having received development aid from the Generazinema program of the Navarra Government, La Revuelta de las Putas continues its progress towards production, now with the support of MEDIA.

The legal defense of Evo Morales suffered a judicial setback. This follows yesterday's ruling in the highly publicized case of human trafficking activated against him, in which the 5th Penal Investigation Court against Corruption and Violence against Women in Tarija issued an order for his arrest. Thus, the arrest warrant and order for transportation, coded as N 010URL, signed on February 11 by Judge Nelson Alberto Rosales Rocabado, orders the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime (FELCC) to apprehend the former president. Morales, who has been sheltered by his loyalists in Lauca Ñ for more than 100 days, is under the microscope of Justice for the alleged commission of the crime of human trafficking, as a result of a complaint that reports he had a relationship with a minor when he was president. The authorities assert that Evo was not notified and classify the arrest order as illegal. ANOTHER BLOW TO THE EVISM APELACIÓN TO THE ARREST ORDER. And it is that the First Hall of the Departmental Justice Court (TDJ) of Tarija rejected and declared the appeal presented by the former president's legal team inadmissible. This, after on January 17, and for the second time, Morales did not appear to answer for the case in Tarija. From Sucre, the State Attorney General, Roger Mariaca, explained that Justice did not grant the appeal formulated by Evo's defense. He added that after this appeal demand was resolved, and in view of the existing declaration of rebellion issued on January 17, what remains is to execute the apprehension order. We are waiting for that to be determined by the judicial authority, and for the Bolivian Police to start their work, who are responsible for executing the said order, Mariaca noted. With this new ruling, Morales now has three warrants for his apprehension. The first date is October 16, 2024, the second is January 17, 2025, and the third is February 11. Case judge rejects Evo's appeal and ratifies his arrest order DEFENSE OF EVO In response, lawyer Cecilia Urquieta, part of the legal team of the former president, assured that the process is in an incidental stage and that the arrest order is illegal. To this, it is added that Morales was not notified with the ruling. It has been requested that the incidents that we have presented be considered. We are in an incidental stage because that arrest order and all those irregular and illegal acts that have been carried out, have not been officially notified to Mr. Evo Morales in Cochabamba, he sustained. The jurist demanded the presence of international observers to follow the case. From the ranks of the evism, his loyal followers qualified the action as part of a political persecution. Senator Leonardo Loza, one of the first to speak out, stated that this ruling responds to political and electoral decisions. He assured that they do not fear the detention of the former president. Any process, late or early, fabricated, organized, digitized, and managed politically by this government will eventually fall, he emphasized. On the other hand, the deputy aligned with the coca leader, Romina Gómez, labeled the order as illegal and political. Beforehand, the leader coca leader's legal defense pointed to the Luis Arce government for executing a black plan against him, which strengthened from September 26, 2024, and resulted in 11 processes and denunciations. In contrast, the vice-president of the Creemos bench, Efraín Suárez, assured that imprisoning Morales is something just since he committed many crimes, not only against minors but also electoral crimes. For the rector of the Autonomous Gabriel René Moreno University (UAGRM), Vicente Cuéllar, the judicial determination should not be surprising, since Justice must fulfill its role. However, he assured that the former president enjoys shielding from the Justice and the Government.

On January 20, during his speech at his oath as President of the United States, Donald Trump surprised both Americans and the rest of the world by mentioning the Aragua Train, a little-known issue until then outside of Latin America. In Europe, and particularly in Spain, this Venezuelan criminal organization was practically unknown, but Trump presented it as an example of the dangers associated with Nicolás Maduro's regime and its connection to international criminal networks. According to what had been previously denounced by former Colombian President Iván Duque, the Aragua Train operates as an extension of the Sol de Sol Cartel, a narcotics trafficking structure that directly links high-ranking officials of the Chavista regime, such as Nicolás Maduro and Diosdado Cabello. This major criminal gang, led by the Venezuelan criminal leader Héctor Niño Guerrero, originated in the Tocorón prison, located in the state of Aragua, about 100 kilometers from Caracas. Initially, the Aragua Train emerged as a prison-like structure seeking economic benefits through illicit activities, but over time, its reach expanded enormously. Among its activities, they stand out for narco-trafficking, robbery, hitman services, kidnapping, extortion, bribery, money laundering, arms trafficking, and human trafficking. Although its operations began in Venezuela, the influence of the Aragua Train has spread rapidly to other American continent countries and beyond. Originally, it established permanent cells in Chile, Peru, and Colombia, but more recently, its presence has been detected in Ecuador, Brazil, Mexico, Panama, Costa Rica, and even the United States. In Chile, for example, the gang has been linked to the kidnapping and murder of Venezuelan Lieutenant Ronald Ojeda. Chilean investigations point to the possibility that the tentacles of this crime could reach the Miraflores Palace in Caracas. It's not for nothing that Chilean prosecutor Mario Carrera considers the trial against the Tren de Aragua to be the most important in the history of organized crime in Chile, the first transnational criminal group that the Chilean justice system has faced. In Colombia, in 2022, the authorities in Bogotá attributed at least 23 murders to the Tren de Aragua. In the United States, the narco-trafficking group has also left its mark. The Department of the Treasury sanctioned the Tren de Aragua as a transnational criminal organization. Initially, activities were detected in Aurora, Colorado, and in the city of New York, but its scope has extended to other areas such as Denver or Chicago. Some members of this dangerous gang have been accused of serious crimes, ranging from shootouts to human trafficking, mainly affecting the Venezuelan community. In a recent case, Bernardo Raúl Castro, a 19-year-old Venezuelan immigrant, was charged with shooting at two police officers in New York. In another case in southern Florida, Yurwin Salazar, identified as a member of the Tren de Aragua, was charged with kidnapping and murder of a retired Venezuelan police officer. During the electoral campaign, Donald Trump accused the Chavist regime of deliberately exporting criminals to the United States and other countries as a regional destabilization strategy. He pointed out that the decline in crime rates within Venezuela was not the result of successful security policies, but rather the release and export of criminals abroad with passports in hand. According to the President of the United States and other Republican congressmen, this strategy constitutes a pressure and blackmail tool, designed to generate fear and intimidation both in neighboring countries and on American territory. A letter sent by Republican congressmen to President Joe Biden referred to the Tren de Aragua as a criminal invading army, warning of the dangers this organization poses to the national security of the United States. Federal authorities in the United States have detected sex trafficking networks linked to the Tren de Aragua in states such as Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Florida, and New Jersey. This criminal organization does not act independently. According to numerous investigations, this organization operates as the enforcement arm of the Sol de Soles Cartel, the narcotics trafficking network linked to the Chavista regime. This cartel, composed of high-ranking Venezuelan military and civilian officials, controls the international drug trade from Venezuelan territory. The Tren de Aragua gang facilitates many of these operations through its criminal network, which includes trafficking routes, bribes to authorities, and intimidation operations. The expansion of these dangerous narco-traffickers is not only a criminal problem, but also a geopolitical threat. Their presence in Latin American countries and the United States highlights the regime's ability to destabilize the region through criminal networks. Moreover, the lack of effective international cooperation to combat these organizations has allowed them to grow. On the other hand, the extension and growth of this type of narco-trafficking organizations, closely linked to Nicolás Maduro's regime, can turn international sanctions into almost laughable practices, soft scratches without the capacity to really hurt the Venezuelan leadership. They will affect the people but will never reach the Chavista nomenclature, which will always find alternative means of financing in this type of criminal gangs, whose ability to corrupt people, institutions, political parties, and organizations from other areas, both inside and outside Venezuela, is more than evident. The case of the Aragua Train highlights the need for a coordinated approach between the countries of the region and the United States to dismantle this dangerous structure. Trump's public denunciation and ongoing investigations have shed light on this organization, but the challenge persists, and its impact remains a central theme in regional security and U.S. policy towards Iberoamerica. The criminal regime of Nicolás Maduro is a hydra with multiple heads. The Aragua Train is one of them. Remember that name. Enrique Alvarado is a lawyer and diplomat.

The Public Prosecutor's Office reported on Wednesday that the recusal motion presented against the judges of the Third Collegiate Court of the National District responds to a dilatory strategy of the defense of María Paula Murillo Vargas and two other defendants in the human trafficking network dismantled in August 2022 through Operation Cattleya. The prosecutor Eduardo Velázquez explained that the recusal motion is based on an alleged impartiality claim after the court rejected a defense appeal, which sought to prevent the incorporation of hard drives with key evidence, such as photographs, conversations, and other documents related to sexual exploitation and human trafficking. As a result of that decision, the defenses resorted to the old dilatory tactic of recusal, with the sole purpose of delaying the process, since they know that the accusation against each of the accused is indestructible and that they will receive a certain conviction, Velázquez stated. The prosecutor added that the expert Ogando authenticated the expert reports, validating the information contained in the hard drives. However, the defense attempted to argue that they had not been notified of these evidence, despite being properly communicated in the intermediate phase of the process. As a consequence of the recusal, the hearing was recessed until the court decides on the request to remove the judges from the trial, which is in its final stage. Charges against the accused The Public Prosecutor accuses the accused of forming a criminal organization dedicated to human trafficking for sexual exploitation and the illicit trafficking of migrants. According to the investigation, they deceived foreign women with false promises of employment and subsequently subjected them to sexual exploitation. They also face charges of organized crime and, in some cases, money laundering due to the economic benefits obtained. The defendants in the case are José Miguel Michel Gurdis (alias Michel), Daniel Enrique Inirio Abreu, Cristina Virginia González Hernández, Cristina María Castillo Vargas, Robert Lee Eleuterio Paniagua Díaz, José Alberto Soriano Rosario (alias Cirujano), and Dionicio Mieses de la Cruz (alias Dionis). Also listed are Louis Marie Nephtalie, Engel Nefthali Vargas Soto (alias Ángel), Oliver Arnaud Lewinski and Timothy William Case Renee, Braulio Manuel Lugo, Marie Fokina Achille, Carlos Jhonatan Walwyn Campusano Díaz, Melvin José Valentín Peguero, Zafiro Nataly Sánchez González, Oscar Wicene, and Alejandro Arturo Batista Bustamante (alias Gato). Additionally, the indictment extends to the Caribe and Oscar hotels, located in the Gascue sector of the National District, as well as the Coco Real hotel in Bávaro, Punta Cana, La Altagracia province.

Brother of Judge Accused of Sexual Abuse Released from Prison On February 3, 2025, Wildo Machuca, brother of Judge Gloria Machuca, was released from Tacumbú Prison by decision of Judge Cynthia Lovera. The magistrate argued that Machuca suffered from boils on his skin that could put his life at risk. However, the victim's father questions whether a proper medical evaluation was conducted to justify this measure.Concern over the Accused's Proximity Although the judge ordered Machuca to undergo medical treatment, neighbors reported that he has been seen at his residence, located just two minutes from the victim's house. This situation generates fear in the affected family, which is trying to protect the child from any contact or news about the accused.Criticism of the Judicial System The victim's father expressed his indignation at what he considers an injustice and preferential treatment towards Machuca due to his familial connection with a judge. The family has faced significant emotional and economic wear and tear in their pursuit of justice, feeling abandoned by the judicial system. Background on the Wildo Machuca case Wildo Machuca was charged by the Public Ministry for child sexual abuse, accused of exploiting his closeness to the victim's family to commit the crime. Initially, he spent 40 days at the Sajonia police station before being transferred to Tacumbú under pressure from the family and their lawyer. Family commitment to seeking justice Despite the challenges, the victim's family remains determined to secure a conviction for Machuca. They have focused their efforts on providing emotional support to the child, involving her in sports and artistic activities to mitigate the impact of the trauma she has experienced.

Following the judge's measure, the defense of the victims, Juan Raúl Williman and Soledad Suárez, appealed the Justice's decision, which also allowed history professor Sebastián Mauvezín to wait for the trial at his home. Penadés and Mauvezín must serve their sentence under preventive detention until June 10, as stipulated. Both defendants will return to the prisons where they were previously held, Penadés to the one in Florida and Mauvezín to the one in Campanero, Lavalleja.

In 2004, the World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers was established, a commemoration promoted by the UN to make visible and combat the use of minors in armed conflicts. This day highlights the imperative need to protect childhood, ensure its comprehensive development, and prevent one of the most heinous violations of human rights. The recruitment of children and girls in armed conflicts constitutes one of the most serious forms of abuse against fundamental rights. Recognizing this problem, the United Nations established in 2004 the World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers, a date that is celebrated annually to denounce and raise awareness about the devastating impact of this practice on the lives of thousands of minors around the world. Every year, this day becomes a space for reflection and joint action between governments, international organizations, NGOs, and civil society. During the day, conferences, workshops, and information campaigns are organized in various regions, where human rights experts, UN representatives, and activists share statistics, testimonies, and experiences on the issue of child recruitment. According to UNICEF reports, it is estimated that hundreds of thousands of children have been forced to join armed groups, suffering irreparable physical, emotional, and social consequences. The celebration of World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers not only serves to remember the victims and denounce these practices, but also promotes the strengthening of public policies aimed at the demobilization, reintegration, and rehabilitation of affected minors. International authorities have advocated for the implementation of stricter legal frameworks and the commitment of states to eradicate any form of child exploitation in conflict zones. This coordinated effort aims to ensure that every child has the inalienable right to grow up in a safe environment, free from violence, and with access to education and healthcare. Additionally, the commemoration serves as a call to action for the global community to redouble its efforts in child protection. International cooperation is revealed to be essential in addressing a phenomenon that, despite progress, persists in numerous countries. The visibility of this issue through media campaigns and international events allows for maintaining the debate on the political and social agenda, motivating the implementation of strategies that guarantee the respect and dignity of childhood. The World Day Against the Use of Child Soldiers is an emblematic date that reinforces the UN's and the international community's commitment to fighting child abuse and exploitation in armed conflicts. It is a perpetual reminder that every child deserves a future without violence, in which their rights are protected and promoted. The annual celebration calls us to reflect on the injustices of the past and to build, with action and commitment, a present and a future in which childhood is truly safe. Source: Prensa.ec

data.text: Attorney General Austin Knudsen and Montana Department of Justice prosecutors and investigators testified today before the Senate Judiciary Committee in support of Senate Bill 261 sponsored by Senator Greg Hertz, which will protect children from deadly drugs like fentanyl. Under current state law, prosecutors can charge parents and other adults who cause or allow a child to inhale, be exposed to, come into contact with, or ingest methamphetamine, or come into contact with methamphetamine paraphernalia, but leaves other deadly drugs like fentanyl, heroin, and cocaine untouched. SB 261 will close that loophole and add all the listed Schedule I through V drugs, not prescribed by a doctor, to the statute. If passed, the bill will also make it a crime under the statute to cause or allow a child to inhale, ingest, or expose themselves to marijuana or THC products, such as edible foods or drinks. To assist or encourage a child to enter a location where human trafficking occurs. To assist, promote, or encourage a child to enter a location where dangerous drugs are produced or manufactured. This is a simple solution that will help keep Montana's children safe from dangerous drugs. We know that fentanyl is an extremely dangerous substance and should be treated as such in state law, said Attorney General Knudsen. I urge the Legislature to join me in supporting Senate Bill 261. Exposing children to dangerous drugs or insecure criminal environments is unconscionable. Adults are responsible for the safety and well-being of children, and SB 261 will hold them accountable for that, said Senator Hertz. data.text: As in all previous occasions when the National Police have struck the group led by El Faku, Salva, and Erik, all pseudonyms for the main leaders, in this latest police operation, announced exclusively by LevanteEMV on Wednesday, the victims of their extortion with a sexual background number in the dozens and are distributed throughout half of Spain. So far, more than half a dozen people have been detained in this major operation, according to various sources, which began at dawn on Tuesday in numerous homes in Valencia where most of the arrests took place in Pobla de Vallbona and, above all, Benissa. There, in a mansion in one of the multiple urbanizations of that municipality in the Marina Alta, is where the supposedly directed network of sextortion by Facundo B. S. H., 24 years old, who calls himself El Faku, Ismael B. O., alias Salva, and Massinissa F. M Erik had set up this time his command center in the form of a call center from where they made dozens of calls to cybersex workers until one of them fell into the provocation and ended up paying the revolutionary tax in exchange for not spreading their perversions or not physically attacking them. Both Faku and Salva, through whose mediation the former Levante UD footballer Toño was detained during the dismantling of the same network in 2019 (the player was fully exonerated), were detained in Benissa, as they personally supervised the work of those who answered the call center. The Highest Rung However, on this occasion, the specialists from the Kidnappings and Extortions Unit of the UDEV central headquarters in Madrid, who have taken the lead in the investigation, and those from Cybercrime of the Valencia Superior Police Headquarters, have taken a step further and have reached, according to sources of the highest solvency that this newspaper has been able to access, the highest level of the scheme, the one that manages and whitewashes the hundreds of thousands of euros that they have obtained from their victims over the years. According to those sources, dozens of bank accounts have been immobilized, and not just those opened by mules so that the sex workers could deposit the various amounts they were demanding under very serious threats, but above all, those of the genuine perpetrators of the scheme, which has been operational for more than six years. In that sense, investigators would have managed to immobilize a significant fortune with the assets acquired in the process of money laundering and with money held in those accounts, as well as in cryptocurrency credentials. Initially, the detainees will be handed over to the judge handling the case from its inception, the presiding judge of the Investigation Court number 20 of Valencia on the next Friday morning. The most media-covered detainee is undoubtedly the Uruguayan Facundo B. S. H., alias El Faku, detained for the first time at 21 years old and who three years later has escalated to become one of the leaders of the organization's part dedicated to setting up false prostitution contact scams and subsequent threats to sex workers who have called phones seeking out pages that promote sexual exploitation. As reported by the National Police in a statement following the detention of Facundo B. S. H. In the spring of 2021, in a town in Jaén where he was hiding, within the Girasol operation, exclusively reported by LevanteEMV, the alleged offender called himself the Messi of work (they called work his business and the method they used in sex trafficking, the same as any other similar scheme) on his Instagram account, where he defined himself with the term I'm a criminal (in English). With more than 20 police and judicial complaints against him and an undeniable criminal record, for now, this confessed criminal is back behind bars.

It appears that they made sales in Horquetas de Sarapiquí and the surroundings of a school in the San Bernardino locality, but also maintained two cultivation laboratories for the substance, providing them with proper maintenance. The searches were conducted in October 2022, during which a large quantity of materials and equipment for cultivation, as well as four packages containing marijuana buds weighing a total of approximately 35.15 grams, were collected as evidence. During this first day of trial, the indictment against them was read, in addition, one of the officers from the Narcotics Control Police explained the methodology used in the investigation of this case, and despite being asked if they wanted to testify, they refused. The suspects face sanctions ranging from four to eight years in prison for the crime of selling drugs. Authorities Arrest Over a Dozen People in Operation Against Child Exploitation in Georgia ATLANTA, Georgia (Telemundo Atlanta) More than a dozen people were arrested as part of a police operation against the sexual exploitation of children, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) reported on Wednesday. According to authorities, the suspects, including two Hispanics, were arrested in the Atlanta metropolitan area and northern Georgia. The Hispanics were identified as 30-year-old Ezequiel Ortiz and 25-year-old Elvis Beltrán Pineda, the police said. Operation Byte Down, the operation, identified 13 children living in households where they were allegedly exposed to online child sexual exploitation. The suspects face charges of child sexual exploitation and related offenses. Copyright 2025 WKTB. All rights reserved.

data.text: All is set at Federal Oral Court Two in Córdoba to begin the trial on Thursday, 20, regarding the disappearance and alleged femicide of 21-year-old Yamila Cuello. The events unfolded on October 25, 2009, at midday, when she left her grandmother's house in Coronel Olmedo neighborhood, in the southern part of the city, to meet friends for lunch. However, she never arrived at the gathering, and there was no further news of her, nor was her body found. This is a case with some similarities to that of teacher Anahí Bulnes, who was murdered by Santiago Campos Matos (perpetually convicted), who also took care of disposing of the victim's remains. In Yamila's case, those accused of aggravated human trafficking and qualified homicide are her ex-boyfriend and his friend, Néstor Simone and Horacio Palacios, who remain at large. Over 15 years after her disappearance, the strongest evidence comes from some testimonies, such as that of her grandmother Eulalia Contreras (who filed the complaint), who heard Yamila talking to a male voice on that day, saying "Don't treat me like that, don't threaten me, or else I won't go anywhere." It is also known that Simone had called Yamila eight times that morning and before noon, but not a single time after. Someone allegedly saw Simone cleaning bloodstains from his Renault 12 vehicle that day. Yamila's family has always believed that her ex-boyfriend tried to hand her over to a human trafficking network, with the complicity of Palacios. The trial will not be easy, and the tribunal will be composed of President Fabián Asís and vocal members Noel Costa and Carolina Prado, who will have to assess the consistency of the existing evidence when issuing a sentence. Prosecutor Carlos Gonella will lead the prosecution, which, if upheld, will result in the only possible sentence of life imprisonment. The truth is that the case is tremendous and too much time has passed. The hearings will be closely followed because, in addition, it is a very well-known case. The investigation suffered some twists but has finally reached its destination. We deserve to know what was done to Yamila Cuello.

The Public Prosecutor's Office charged the director of a school for not activating the protocol in the face of an incident of harassment and sexual abuse by a teacher towards students. Public Prosecutor Nilsa Marlene Torales, of the Penal Unit of the Caaguazú Zonal Prosecutor's Office, presented charges against the director of an educational institution, for the punishable acts of obstruction of prosecution and penal execution, violation of the duty of care and education. In the context of investigations into an incident of harassment and sexual abuse that a teenager allegedly suffered within an educational institution of the aforementioned locality. The representative of the Public Prosecutor's Office found sufficient evidence to convict the director of the aforementioned acts, as they were aware of the events, but did not report them or activate the protocol. The alleged harasser worked as a teacher at a school in this locality, who took advantage of recess to harass his students. The complainant's aunt personally informed the director about the incident, who failed to report or activate the protocol. On another occasion, the harassment occurred after an exam. In response to the situation, the teenager withdrew and told her grandmother, who went to the school to report the incident to the director, who, despite having direct knowledge, for the second time and repeatedly, omitted reporting the incident again. Source Diario Hoy

Willy Ochoa requested that in the US, the implications of granting asylum and diplomatic protection to Escandón be evaluated. Willy Ochoa, a former provisional governor of Chiapas from the PRI, sent a letter to Donald Trump, President of the United States, alerting him to alleged ties to narcotics trafficking by Rutilio Escandón Cadenas, designated as Consul in Miami, Florida. Ochoa accused the government of Rutilio Escandón, a Morena member, of being marked by negligence, omission, and disturbing ties to organized crime. Through the letter, made public by journalist Dolia Estévez, the PRI member stated that Escandón's possible appointment poses a real threat to the security of Chiapas, as well as the internal security of the United States. PRI member requests Trump evaluate appointment In light of this situation, Ochoa requested that Trump's administration carefully evaluate the implications of granting asylum and diplomatic protection to Rutilio Escandón in Miami. I am writing with the utmost respect to express my profound concern regarding the designation of Rutilio Escandón Cadenas as Consul of Mexico in Miami. This decision poses a real threat to the security of Chiapas and, consequently, to the internal security of the United States, particularly in Florida, a state that has prioritized the fight against organized crime and corruption. It is paradoxical that in Florida, a state led by distinguished figures such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Attorney General Pam Bondi, there now exists the possibility of granting immunity and diplomatic protection to a person whose tenure as governor was marked by negligence, omission, and disturbing ties to organized crime, as detailed in the letter. Photo taken from Facebook He added that it is alarming that a diplomatic position could become a reward for someone who, during their administration, was unable to implement the minimum measures to manage and control migration, thereby facilitating human trafficking by criminal networks that reached unprecedented levels in Chiapas between 2018 and 2024. These are the warnings launched by Trump The former acting governor of Chiapas pointed out that during Rutilio Escandón's administration, the state became a land without law, where massive migration overwhelmed state security, triggering an unprecedented humanitarian crisis. As a former governor of Chiapas and a committed citizen of security and transparency in public service, I have been a constant critic of the government's inaction in the face of criminal organizations. Despite the widely documented personal risks by various media in Mexico and the United States, I have defended the pacification of Chiapas, a state where freedom of expression and circulation has been systematically repressed by a complicit government with criminal groups. However, the cost of remaining silent is even greater, and therefore, I feel compelled to address the government of the United States publicly, he indicated. He also argued that there has been an increase in violence and criminality, as he points out that intentional homicides have increased significantly, in response to which he highlighted that this is demonstrated by investigations by the Grupo Imagen, Excélsior, and official data from the Executive Secretariat of the National Public Security System (SESNSP). In a kind of list, it highlighted the proliferation of armed criminal groups in the state, where it claims that Chiapas became a battleground for the evening news between the country's main cartels. Institutional collapse and corruptionDuring Escandón's administration, Chiapas was classified as the state with the highest perception of corruption in Mexico, reaching 88.3%, according to a study by the Mexican Institute for Competitiveness (IMCO). These are just a few examples of the severe security and governance crisis that Chiapas suffered under his mandate. The state became an uncontrollable corridor for drug trafficking, human trafficking, and the transit of individuals linked to extremist organizations such as Al Qaeda, Hezbollah, and the FARC, it pointed out. (POLITICO)

On Wednesday, a 51-year-old Bolivian man was arrested in the Esmeralda neighborhood sector, right in the heart of Iquique, after insulting and sexually assaulting a female police officer on duty. The police institution reported that the assault occurred when a man began insulting a female officer in a public street. The uniformed officer ordered him to leave, but the individual attacked her, making indecent advances. After this situation, a nearby police officer intervened and detained the 51-year-old Bolivian man. However, the individual resisted arrest and threatened to kill the police officers. Regarding this, Colonel Adrián Andrades detailed that the uniformed officer was performing her duties, conducting vehicle checks alongside her companion, a carabinero. Initially, she received constant insults from a subject, whom the officer ordered to leave. However, the subject went behind her and slapped her on the buttocks, she added. On the other hand, the presidential delegate of Tarapacá, Ivonne Donoso, stated that she addressed this situation with the Women's Secretary, Noemí Salinas, in order to provide support to the affected carabinera in this action. According to police information, the detained individual will be formalized for the crimes of sexual abuse and threats of murder against carabineros on duty. Meanwhile, Carabineros is conducting investigations to clarify the facts.VIDEO They detained a subject who sexually abused a carabinera conducting checks in the city center of Iquique, also threatening to kill another carabinero. data.text: A mixed rural transport driver identified as Camilo N was detained in the Pearl of the Gulf, in the municipality of Mecayapan, by agents of the Attorney General's Office (FGE), with the support of federal forces and agents from the Ministerial Police Chief's Office in Acayucan, dependent on the Zona Sur Coatzacoalcos delegation. He is accused of having sexually abused a minor, a friend of his daughter, and of having fled to avoid justice. According to the investigations, the 36-year-old man took advantage of the fact that the minor was visiting his daughter to commit the crime and then threatened her not to report it. After this, he escaped and spent almost a year as a fugitive, until he decided to return without knowing that there was already an arrest warrant against him. His capture was carried out in a difficult-to-access area, where on several occasions the residents have hindered the intervention of the authorities. However, with the support of the National Guard and the Mexican Army, law enforcement agents managed to locate and apprehend him. Camilo N was transferred to the Acayucan prison, where he will face a judicial process for the sexual abuse of minors, as per case file 115.

Project ESPERANZA Adoratrices warns of the multiple forms of violence that are perpetrated against women and girls, which often manifest themselves consecutively or simultaneously. Specifically, it draws attention to cases of women who were victims of female genital mutilation in their childhood or youth and who are subsequently victims of trafficking. The NGO launches the campaign "Sowing Equality and Rights" to raise awareness that female genital mutilation (FGM) constitutes a grave violation of human rights and a form of violence against women, with sanitary and psychosocial implications that violate the right of girls and women to physical integrity and directly affects their sexual and reproductive health, perpetuating gender inequalities and affecting many of the migrant women and trafficking victims who are found in Spain and who fled from gender violence and inequality in their countries. Human Trafficking, which mainly affects women and girls worldwide, is a global phenomenon considered a contemporary form of slavery and a severe violation of human rights. Human trafficking is also considered the third most lucrative illicit business, after the trafficking of arms and illegal drugs. February 6th is commemorated as International Zero Tolerance Day for Female Genital Mutilation, internationally recognized as a violation of the human rights of women and girls that includes all procedures involving the intentional alteration or damage of female genital organs for non-medical reasons. This practice affects more than 200 million girls and women worldwide. The MGF is a human rights violation that has its roots in gender inequality and the discrimination that women and girls suffer for being women, which can lead to severe lifelong health consequences, among others, it can produce severe bleeding and urinary problems, and later may cause cysts, infections, complications during childbirth, and an increased risk of the newborn's death. Geographically, most cases occur in the 30 countries of Africa, the Middle East, and Asia, where this practice is concentrated, and among migrants from those areas, although there are also cases of MGF in Europe, Latin America, North America, New Zealand, and Australia. Therefore, the MGF is a global problem. Human trafficking, on the other hand, disproportionately affects women and girls worldwide, which is why it is conceptualized today as a manifestation of gender-based violence. 71% of the victims of human trafficking worldwide are women (51%) and girls (20%), a direct consequence of their situation of greater vulnerability, resulting from inequality, discrimination, and violence to which they are exposed solely due to being women and girls. The various manifestations of gender-based violence are interconnected, and women and girls frequently suffer from multiple forms of gender-based violence simultaneously and consecutively. This is what happens, for example, to many women and girls from Sub-Saharan Africa, many of whom have been victims of child or adolescent marriage in their childhood or youth and, subsequently, while trying to escape violence, or deceived when seeking a better life, they fall into human trafficking networks that bring them to Europe to subject them mainly to sexual exploitation in prostitution. The Sembrar Igualdad y Derechos Proyecto ESPERANZA awareness campaign launches the Sembrar Igualdad y Derechos campaign with the goal of raising awareness about the urgency of working towards equality and access to rights for women and girls, and the need to prevent gender violence, specifically FGM (Female Genital Mutilation), by highlighting the way in which forms of gender violence often intersect and exacerbate one another. It aims to amplify a common message across different realities, including StopMGF, and to intensify the impact on the overall health of women. The awareness campaign uses the image of a cotton seed as an alternative concept to the brutality of the FGM knife, focusing on solutions that address the root cause of the problem, and overcoming the structures that perpetuate gender inequality and violence. That is why this campaign, which is primarily disseminated through social media, aims to make this reality visible, still unknown to certain sectors of the population, and to show long-term solutions based on education, social dialogue, and the empowerment of women to act collectively and put an end to this practice. Project ESPERANZA Integral Attention, Empowerment, and Prevention Project Esperanza Adoratrices has provided comprehensive care to more than 990 women victims of Trafficking, from 40 different nationalities, adopting a human rights perspective, intercultural, and gender-based, over the past 18 years. Sub-Saharan Africa stands out as the region of origin of the largest number of women victims of trafficking attended by the Project Esperanza in recent years. Women who have suffered human trafficking for exploitation have the right to be guaranteed access to comprehensive and specialized assistance and support that enables them to achieve effective physical, psychological, and social recovery, as well as the right to be recognized for international protection when they flee their countries due to violence or when they are unable to return to their countries due to fear of cruel, inhumane, or degrading treatment.The Project periodically conducts group workshops on gender violence prevention and empowerment for program beneficiaries, addressing, among other topics, self-esteem, prevention of violence within the couple, and prevention of Modern Slavery, to prevent this form of violence from being perpetuated and exercised against the daughters of these women. In this line, we work with specialized organizations in the prevention of female genital mutilation, such as UNAF and Save a Girl, Save a Generation, developing specific workshops centered on interculturality, in which women share and reflect on the positive and negative aspects of their cultures and address the different forms of violence they suffer, including forced marriage and FGM. Furthermore, Project Hope collaborates with Mundo Cooperante, an organization that has been fighting this brutal practice for years, working on projects with social organizations in Kenya and Tanzania and also raising awareness among the Spanish population about this reality.

The New York Times Photo While the Laken Riley Act is being discussed in the Senate (for approval), Republican lawmakers are pushing another immigration bill that will require DNA testing at the southern border. Following the news. Republican lawmakers are pushing the End Child Trafficking Act to address child trafficking and exploitation at the U.S.-Mexico border. Why this is important. The effort could reshape immigration policies by requiring DNA testing to verify family connections between undocumented immigrants and children. What the new immigration bill proposes, which requires DNA testing at the border The bill, reintroduced after previously lacking bipartisan support, coincides with the incoming administration's promise of stricter immigration reforms. Critics fear that the proposed bill could exacerbate the humanitarian challenges faced by migrant families seeking safety. In this regard, a coalition of 11 Republican senators, including Marsha Blackburn and Ted Cruz, announced the bill, which includes severe penalties for refusing DNA testing. You can read New anti-immigrant bill could transform federal and state powers in the US: What you need to know. Adult immigrants who resist DNA testing face deportation. Additionally, falsifying family relationships or participating in child recycling – a tactic where minors are used by unrelated adults to gain entry – could carry up to 10 years in prison. On the other hand, the provisions aim to combat child exploitation, a significant problem on the border. According to the U.S. Customs and Border Protection, nearly 110,000 unaccompanied minors crossed the southern border last fiscal year. Data supporting the bill reveals that around 30% of the examined minors were not biologically related to the adults claiming to be family members. The vulnerability of unaccompanied immigrant children Criticism also centers on the oversight by the Department of Homeland Security of unaccompanied children once they are transferred to the Department of Health and Human Services. An audit showed that, from 2019 to 2023, ICE struggled to maintain consistent tracking of over 448,000 unaccompanied minors placed in HHS care, with more than 32,000 failing to appear at their immigration hearings. Senators backing the legislation emphasize its necessity Senator Bill Cassidy has accused the current administration of exacerbating human trafficking issues by halting DNA family testing. Senator Blackburn is urging action against trafficker networks exploiting migration loopholes, a sentiment echoed by Senator Cruz.

Organization that operated massage parlors forced young women to have sex for $10,000. It is estimated that in each location, there would be 16 sexual encounters per day. The organization that operated massage parlors in San José forced women to have sexual encounters in exchange for $10,000. Located in high-value areas of San José, six massage parlors hid the illicit business of sexual services. One of them, for example, was located in the Escalante neighborhood, behind the Santa Teresita church, and surrounded by restaurants and other businesses. Agents from the specialized section on gender violence, human trafficking, and illicit migrant trafficking, along with the Prosecution, raided the six parlors in the afternoon on Wednesday. In the 25th of July City in Hatillo, they raided the home of the organization's leader, a 32-year-old man with the last name Morales, and in Escalante, they detained a 29-year-old woman with the last name Ureña, who was the administrator of that last location. According to the investigation, the criminal organization generated weekly earnings of 6 million colones. Each woman forced into sex work received a payment of 10,000 colones per encounter. It is estimated that there were 16 sexual encounters per day at each location. The group's leaders promoted massage parlors on the Telegram messaging app under the name Confort. Through catalogs, they offered young women access to the locations, and the victims were recruited through dates. Following the raids, five women were detained: Godínez, 29 years old, Vargas, 19 years old, Barboza, 28 years old, Picado, 39 years old, and Ugalde, 31 years old. The suspects had 1 million colones in cash, 12 cellphones, four vehicles, three computers, two tablets, and documentation related to the investigation seized. In addition, 15 women were rescued, who were being forced into sex work, and are now classified as victims.

Twenty-four years after the crime of Natalia Melmann, the young woman who was murdered in Miramar in February 2001, prosecutor Ana María Caro, who is investigating the case, requested that the DNA of a fifth suspect be analyzed. It is a 60-year-old former policeman who is currently residing in the Buenos Aires city of Trenque Lauquen. His identity has not been revealed yet. The analysis was conducted at the Expert Advisory Office in that city, due to the fact that the Scientific Police cannot intervene because some of the implicated individuals were part of the force. The prosecutor's office aims to match the DNA of the suspect with the genetic material found on the victim's body. The teenager was found dead days after her disappearance. (Photo courtesy of Nahuel Melmann) Twenty-four years have passed since the brutal murder of Natalia Melmann, which occurred on February 4. On the same date in 2001, a 15-year-old girl was returning home from dancing in the Miramar neighborhood. It was around 7 am when a group of police officers intercepted her, beat her, and forced her into a patrol car. Afterward, they took her to a house in the Copacabana neighborhood, on the outskirts of the city, where they tortured, raped, and hanged her with the cord of her own sneaker. For four days, there were no reports of Natalia's disappearance. Her family and friends searched for her alongside the security forces, unaware that the police had participated in the heinous act that would shock the entire country. Her body was found on February 8, buried under a pile of dry leaves in the Florentino Ameghino nursery. It is presumed that they discarded her body in that place on the same day of the crime. Natalia had bruises on her thighs, cigarette burns on her left hand, a broken nasal septum, and a severe head wound. Later, the autopsy revealed the presence of five different genetic profiles. Natalia's body was found on February 8, 2001. (Photo courtesy of Nahuel Melmann) In September 2002, the officers Oscar Echenique (61), Ricardo Anselmini (53), and Ricardo Suárez (58) were sentenced to life in prison. Gustavo Fernández, also known as El Gallo, was sentenced to 25 years in prison for being considered the person who delivered Melmann to her killers, but was acquitted of co-authoring the murder charges. However, his sentence was later reduced to 10 years. Finally, on November 13, 2019, Chamber III of the Bonaerense Court of Appeal annulled his acquittal and ordered a new trial to be held. This took place in 2023, and as a result, Panadero was found guilty of the crimes of aggravated illegal deprivation of liberty, aggravated sexual abuse, and double homicide aggravated by the premeditated intervention of several people and committed to ensure impunity. Thanks to timely work by the Barranquilla city hall under the leadership of Alejandro Char, it is recognized as the country's capital city with the lowest rate of begging and child labor. According to the DANE, the figure decreased from 1.6% to 0.8%. According to figures from the last quarter of 2024 provided by the DANE, Barranquilla leads with the lowest rate of begging and child labor. All of this is thanks to a coordinated effort between the Secretariat of District Social Management, the Atlántico Governor's Office, Family Commissions, the ICBF, the Juvenile and Adolescent Police, Colombian Migration, and the National Labor Ministry. It is worth noting that from the Barranquilla city hall, through the Trabajando por los niños program, it has been possible to impact on Barranquilla children and migrants, removing them from the streets and providing them with a better quality of life far from forced labor. From the district administration, the goal is to prevent children from suffering forced labor, as well as combat child hunger. The aim is to reach zero child begging in the city, continuing the comprehensive care of NNA, but this year we will intervene directly and forcefully in the cases of child exploitation detected in active searches. We will go to the homes of adults detected with children on the streets, together with the Police, Prosecution, ICBF, and Family Commissariat, to verify with neighbors if the child or adolescent is being exploited, stated Ismael Marín, district social management secretary. For 2024, Barranquilla benefited 190 families, which received home-based care and follow-up, of which 50 children, girls, and adolescents were linked to the district's educational system. With this, we are taking them off the streets and changing their lifestyle and that of their families, all through the Trabajando por los Niños program, led by First Lady Katia Nule. What we do from the Trabajando por los Niños program is to reclaim all those children who are on the streets, whether working or begging. It is a task that needs to be done every day with the support of everyone. A child you rescue from the street is a child who changes completely because those who are schooled, have their rights restored in health, recreation, and sports, with psychological help, the First Lady declared. For 2025, the municipality will implement the Barranquilla without child begging strategy, with prevention campaigns in shopping centers, health centers, hotels, at the airport, and in other critical areas, all to raise awareness of the importance of keeping minors away from the streets.

Washington, February 13 (EFE). Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi did not come to condemn the ways in which Indians have been deported from the United States to the Asian country, but said that they are children from ordinary families attracted by dreams and big promises. Many of them are brought without knowing why they are going to a country, and indeed, they are related to human trafficking, the Indian leader stated after being questioned in the White House following a meeting with US President Donald Trump. Modi added that he shares the opinion of the Republican leader to deport any citizen found in the US irregularly. We are completely prepared to bring them back to India, he said. The immigration policy of the US president has been harshly criticized by governments in Latin America, such as Colombia or Mexico, but not New Delhi, which has guaranteed its full cooperation regarding the deportation of Indian migrants to the US. US authorities have identified at least 18,000 undocumented immigrants from this Asian country.

Sean Diddy Combs has initiated legal action against NBCUniversal, Peacock TV, and Ample Entertainment, demanding a compensation of $100 million for defamation. According to the lawsuit filed in New York, the documentary "Diddy The Making of a Bad Boy" presented false and malicious accusations linking him to serious crimes, including serial murder and sex trafficking. The production, released on Peacock on January 14, addresses various allegations against the artist, suggesting that he could be linked to the death of his ex-partner, Kimberly Porter, as well as the deaths of entertainment figures such as Biggie, Andre Harrell, and Heavy D. It also mentions an alleged attempted murder against the singer Al B. Sure. Combs asserts that these accusations were disseminated without evidence and solely for the purpose of generating controversy and increasing the documentary's audience. Lawyer Erica Wolff for Combs has characterized the documentary as a deliberate attack on her client, pointing out that the defendants deliberately profited at the expense of the truth, decency, and basic principles of journalism. According to Wolff, they disseminated scandalous and damaging lies, accusing Combs of heinous crimes such as serial murder and child sex abuse, without providing evidence to support these claims. In the lawsuit, an interview with Ari Mark, co-founder of Ample Entertainment and executive producer of the documentary, is cited, in which he acknowledges that the project was rushed due to competition with similar productions, reinforcing the argument that information verification was insufficient. Jay-Z and Sean Combs are accused of violating a 13-year-old girl in an amended complaint The documentary also features testimonies from individuals close to Combs, such as Al B. Childhood friends and producers of Bad Boy Records, who recount their rise in the music industry and describe him as an abusive person surrounded by those who enabled him, share their stories. A former Bad Boy employee, speaking anonymously, claims that his job involved recruiting women for Combs' parties, some of whom were allegedly minors. However, Combs' defense argues that this accusation is based on a civil lawsuit filed by Rodney Lil Rod Jones, in which the supposed victims later denied being minors at the time of the incidents and denied witnessing any illicit acts. Peacock (peacock) January 2, 2025 This lawsuit follows a previous lawsuit filed by Combs in January for $50 million against NewsNation, after the news outlet aired an interview with Courtney Burgess, who claimed to have recordings showing Combs involved in sexual assaults on celebrities and minors. Combs has categorically denied the existence of such recordings and any involvement in the crimes attributed to him. For now, the legal battle of Combs continues, after being arrested and formally charged in September 2024 with conspiracy to commit a crime, sex trafficking, and transportation for prostitution. Although the producer has pleaded not guilty and denied all accusations, he remains detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn while awaiting his trial in May. In parallel, he faces more than 40 civil lawsuits for alleged sexual abuse. Check out the first trailer for the documentary The Fall of Diddy, about the case of Sean Combs

The Ecuadorian Police reported this Thursday that with the support of the United States, they dismantled a network of child pornography and arrested four people, including parents who used their children to produce this material. Operation Gran Fenix 7Pandora 1 was carried out in the Andean city of Quito and the coastal city of Esmeraldas, under the direction of the Attorney General's Office and in coordination with the Department of National Security of the United States of North America (HSI). The Police stated that, after investigative work and information exchange, they identified in Ecuador a criminal network dedicated to the production and commercialization of child sexual abuse material, audiovisual material that was produced by the same suspects using their minor children. The material was commercialized to Americans through live video calls or file transfers via instant messaging platforms, for which they received generous sums of money through international wire transfers from the United States, it was stated in a statement. In this context, in November 2024, an American was detained in the United States in possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), who was traveling continuously to Esmeraldas. Therefore, in December of last year, a preliminary investigation was opened in Ecuador for the alleged crime of commercializing child pornography, identifying four suspects and identifying two victims of these abuses. This Thursday, five minors were rescued from this criminal network and detained Nury Alexandra G.S., Kathiusca Maribel, George Miguel G.C., and Rosa Gissela S.O, who have no prior records. During the operation, the Police seized 13 mobile phones, a tablet, two chips, and various documents, among other items. Emeterio Vargas, Cindy Saraí's father, the presumed victim in the aggravated human trafficking case involving former Bolivian President Evo Morales, will be released from prison after the Investigating Magistrate's Court ordered the cessation of his preventive detention. Vargas's lawyer, Anibal Cabezas, confirmed to the medium El Deber that in a morning hearing to control the deadline held on Thursday, the judge determined the cessation of his detention at the Morros Blancos prison. According to Cabezas, now it remains the presentation of personal sureties and the personal bail process, among other requirements, to obtain his client's freedom in the coming days. The lawyer added that in the hearing, the Public Ministry tried to persuade the judge to extend his preventive detention by two more months, but in the end, the judicial decision prevailed. We recall that Vargas has been in Morros Blancos prison since October 2024, accused by the Departmental Prosecutor's Office of not reporting the fact of human trafficking in which his daughter had a relationship with President Morales. Mr. Vargas had nothing to do with this crime, he is a 67-year-old worker and was separated from his family during that time, Cabezas reaffirmed. In the case of human trafficking, his wife, Idelsa Pozo Saavedra, is also imputed, who was declared in rebellion, with an arrest order, for not appearing at the precautionary hearing last January.

The Attorney General's Office of the State of Puebla detained Brian N., alias el Chino, a native of the United States, who had an outstanding arrest warrant in his country for the crime of sexual abuse, against a minor. In compliance with a request made by The U.S. Marshals Services, through the Fugitive Task Forces program for the capture of the now-accused, the Attorney General's Office, with the support of federal, state, and municipal authorities, managed to locate and detain Brian N., in the municipality of Ajalpan. Because the fugitive entered Mexico illegally, a handover was carried out to personnel from the National Migration Institute (INM), the instance that will be responsible for transporting him to the border with the United States for his deportation and to be at the disposal of the corresponding authorities where he will have to respond to the facts that are imputed to him.

They prostituted women next to a daycare in Escalante They earned at least $20 per service Neighbors claim they reported the incidents in 2016 A massage parlor, where 15 women were being sexually exploited, operated next to a daycare in Escalante neighborhood, San José. This was confirmed by a team from Diario Extra, who visited the location to hear the opinions of the neighbors. However, upon arrival, it was observed that the local was located in a very commercial area, surrounded by a bar and a restaurant that serves seafood, a stem cell bank, and 150 meters from Parque Francia. Additionally, at least two rental rooms were located in the same street where the spa operated. This newspaper spoke with the owner of a residence, who rents two rooms, who preferred to remain anonymous and stated that a neighbor had reported this incident for several years. We saw the situation and complained, but it didn't go beyond that, because if the authorities didn't take action, we couldn't do anything. It was only after they intervened on Wednesday, despite the complaint being made since 2016, as explained. The source also mentioned that on several occasions, she was able to see how some women would stand in front of the establishment, which, given its structure, didn't seem to be a massage parlor but a normal house, to attract clients. Many people were seen entering and leaving the building daily, and they seemed to be rotating the women, as some days they were there and others weren't. They didn't make much of a scene, presumably to keep a low profile, but the man who owns the apartments nearby never stopped denouncing it, he added. Off the record, it was known that they were charging $20 per client, which is equivalent to 10,157 pesos, according to the exchange rate of February 13th. This gave a very bad image to this place, where we live people who believe in morality and repudiate these acts, he emphasized. Regarding the incident, the Director of the Judicial Investigation Agency, Randall Zúñiga, reported that six searches were conducted on Wednesday afternoon, February 12, in Pavas, Curridabat, Barrio Escalante, Rohrmoser, and Los Yoses, resulting in the capture of six suspects. Additionally, a 31-year-old woman, Ugalde, was apprehended on Thursday morning. The alleged criminal organization reportedly recruited women to offer what appeared to be therapeutic massages. However, upon the arrival of clients, it was not just about massages, but also explicit sexual services, as explained. It seems this situation occurred since September 2021, and this group allegedly committed the crimes in stores by offering this service. The case is being investigated under file number 230000451321PE. These women were forced to perform such acts, as they had to pay a fine or indemnification if they refused, added. This medium consulted Marcelo Solano, director of the Municipal Police of San José, if this establishment had a permit or license to operate legally. The raided location, which was a spa, had municipal and health permits, confirmed. The commercial license was issued by the Section of Permits and Licenses of the Municipality of San José in March 2019, as stated in a document in the possession of this newspaper. Regarding the health permit, which had expired and had to be renewed in February 2024, it indicated that its commercial activity was a beauty salon and spa. Cd. Victoria, Tamaulipas. Morning Conference, Tuesday, August 22, 2023. The then Undersecretary of Security LUIS RODRÍGUEZ BUCIO denounces cases of delinquents captured and then released by judges with a carefree attitude, across the country. For more details, the video is available on YouTube at the URL. To illustrate this, the man cited five examples: (1) EDUARDO OSORIO ROSADO, judge from Querétaro. The "angel" allegedly issued a total of 52 rulings in favor of suspected perpetrators of health-related crimes (i.e., narcotics traffickers) and illegal possession of firearms, from 2022 onwards. (2) JESÚS RODRÍGUEZ HERNÁNDEZ, from Nuevo León. He ordered the release of two individuals detained for illegal possession of a firearm and possession of amphetamines in the Linares region. (3) ÓSCAR ANTONIO MADERO, judge from Michoacán. He was criminally charged for issuing 15 rulings contrary to the investigator's request. (4) DANIEL RAMÍREZ PEÑA, judge from the State of Mexico Note: "Maleantes" translates to "delinquents" or "lawbreakers," and "sujetos" translates to "individuals" or "subjects." "Anfetaminas" translates to "amphetamines." A former magistrate was handed a acquittal sentence who received deposits of more than 12 million pesos. In his record, there are also seven resolutions contrary to the AMP's request. (5) JOSÉ LUIS HERNÁNDEZ HERNÁNDEZ, at that time judge of Coahuila, who has a criminal complaint and two complaints before the judiciary for not linking two detainees and suspected perpetrators of the deadly collapse in the El Pinabete mine in Sabinas, Coahuila, on August 3, 2022, to the trial process. The basic data indicate that 10 workers died and the Attorney General's Office (FGR) issued arrest orders against three suspected perpetrators. One of them fled, but the other two were released by the aforementioned judge HERNÁNDEZ, a figure in whose file there are 80 resolutions made against the AMP's requests. On another morning (September 10, 2024), the then Head of Security (now at SEGOB) ROSA ICELA RODRÍGUEZ denounced JOSÉ LUIS HERNÁNDEZ, who was also a judge in Coahuila, for releasing a member of the Fuerza AntiUnión Tepito cartel in less than 24 hours (note and video, in El Siglo de Torreón newspaper URL). NOW IN VICTORIA The latest scandal of this judge's behavior occurred in the Tamaulipas capital, where he released four individuals detained by the State Guard for carrying exclusive use military arms, such as two AR15 rifles and a 9-millimeter pistol. They were handed over to the federal AMP, but the same judge mentioned above (paragraph 5) JOSÉ LUIS HERNÁNDEZ, released them freely, as he did before with those responsible for the Sabinas mine collapse. In print media, the character is questioned for his mistakes in serious cases such as arms accumulation, health-related crimes, and organized crime. It is essential to highlight that the elements of the State Guard and Federal Guard, as well as the police officers of both levels, always risk their lives when executing capture orders or arresting dangerous criminals in flagrante delito. Therefore, it is a macabre mockery, a genuine slap in the face, that due to smiling decisions from complacent judges, the accused return to the street to resume their criminal activities. In this space, I have reported on that type of official who with astonishing ease grants amparos to families suspected of corruption, such as the CABEZA family from Reynosa or the GARCÍA family that governs Nuevo León. USELESS JUDICIARIES The punishment (when there is one) reminds me of that of pedophile priests who, instead of being in prison, are simply transferred to another parish. The same occurs with these judges who have as much breadth in their judicial decisions as in their bank accounts. The courts are always soft, they only relocate them to another city (or state), but the aforementioned individuals continue to do the same thing. As long as there is no exemplary punishment, impunity is a direct invitation to recidivism. In general, they will repeat the action every day with increasing frequency and gravity. Their audacity and hunger for gain, and (therefore) their danger, are superior. That's where the average citizen wonders if the Rule of Law still exists. There's a silly saying that used to be repeated by police reporters back in the 1990s. The police officer reaches an agreement with the detainee not to hand him over to the AMP, because he is very corrupt and, besides, it will cost him more. Although the AMP says the same thing, better take care of me, because that judge is very bad, he will strip you to the underwear. And the judge will repeat similar arguments pointing to the magistrate, state, or district judge. And if the crime is federal, the magistrate will tell the same story pointing to the Supreme Court. The higher up, the more expensive and complex it is. Of course, nothing guarantees that the doctors of the law emerging from the upcoming election will be better, more prepared, and (above all) honest. A word that sounds almost like a fable. For now, the most urgent thing is that the courts function and do not act as if they were bishops facing a abusing father. That instead of punishing with prison and compensation for the damage, they are satisfied with moving them to a different city (or church) so that they can continue their abuses. A clear example of the perverse process that feeds impunity. If the offender sees that nothing happens, they have a free field to become a serial offender.
