data.text: The Trafficking Networks of the Tren de Aragua: The Story of the Fines. Testimonies of Women Brought to Our Country to Integrate into the Sex Work Network Led by the Tren de Aragua. In this second installment of InSight Crime (see the first one here) on the forms of sexual exploitation practiced by the Tren de Aragua, we focus on the world of foreign women brought to our country with deceit. All of them are held by force and must pay a fee to the traffickers. Those who try to escape are tortured or murdered. By Lara LoaizaURLInSight CrimeWhen Isabel accepted the sales job in a commercial establishment that her cousin, Catalina, was offering outside of Venezuela, she never imagined that months later she would be lying on a Peruvian highway, pretending to be dead, with a bullet wound in her neck. Isabel was 22 years old and didn't want to let the opportunity slip away to work with her cousin at the establishment located in Mollendo, a city in the department of Arequipa, southwest of Peru. This offer was her ticket out of Venezuela's economic collapse. However, shortly after arriving in Peru, she discovered that the offer had been a scam and she was at the mercy of a human trafficking network. Isabel was one of the hundreds of Venezuelan women captured by human trafficking rings every year. Her story is intertwined in the pages of a judicial case with at least 43 people accused of belonging to the Tren de Aragua, a Venezuelan megaband that has expanded across South America. In various cities in Peru, the group has implemented a complex system of recruitment, transportation, and sexual exploitation of women, girls, and adolescents. The victims of this criminal scheme are known among sex workers as the "multadas", in reference to how trafficking victims must pay a debt to their captors for the cost of their trip and maintenance. The multadas, says Roxi, a Venezuelan sex worker living in Lima, are brought here, paid everything, and when they arrive, they are deceived, they come to be exploited. SEE PEOPLE TRAFFICKING The perverse crime that affects adults and minors is growing in the face of an indifferent state. The pink arm The victims' route to exploitation usually begins online. For Isabel, it all started with messages from her cousin, who acted as a recruiter. The recruiters, also known as captators, are the first link in the human trafficking chain and are responsible for identifying and deceiving victims to accept traveling abroad. Increasingly, human trafficking networks rely on other women for this process, as they inspire more trust in the victims. Peruvian authorities have referred to this figure as the "pink arm" of traffickers. Girls, often lured by other girls who are already in the situation of trafficking, arrive, that is to say, the mechanism of using victims to capture other victims, is explained by InSight Crime's Joel Jabiles Eskenazi, coordinator of the Protection Unit of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Peru. According to Isabel's testimony and information gathered by prosecutors, after Catalina convinced her to travel to Peru, she requested approval from a suspected leader of the Los Gallegos cell in Peru. Los Gallegos are a faction of the Aragua Train that arrived in the country in 2019, taking advantage of the migratory flows from Venezuela towards the Andean country to expand. Once with the leader's approval, Isabel, who by this time was still convinced that it was a real job, began her journey towards Peru. Catalina put her in contact with a supposed travel advisor, who was in charge of all the logistics of the trip and covered the costs, which, according to the case documents, vary depending on the country of origin. For women traveling from Venezuela, the travel advisors receive $500, and for those from Colombia, $300. The advisor took Isabel to Ecuador. Once in the country, the man contacted her with another operator, who bought her tickets to Lima, from where she would travel to Mollendo, where Catalina supposedly lived. Women who are released from their captors do not file complaints out of fear of reprisals. Photo Archive La República. Upon arriving in Mollendo, she did not find her cousin, but another woman, who bluntly informed her that the job they had promised her did not exist and that, instead, she would have to work in nightclubs or chongos, which in Peru are known as bars where sexual services are sold to pay off the debt for her trip. In an instant, Isabel realized she had been caught in a human trafficking network. Although she tried to contact her cousin to clarify the situation and escape the nightmare she was in, she never managed to do so. The documents from her case confirm that she lost all contact with Catalina, who left her Facebook and WhatsApp accounts abandoned. López Aliaga requests that the Aragua Train be declared a terrorist group to receive aid from the United States. The Exploitation The woman who received Isabel in Mollendo took her to a house where nine other women and a man lived, who was in charge of watching them so they wouldn't escape. There, they told her she had to pay a debt she owed Los Gallegos for the costs of her trip, as well as what they would charge her for housing and feeding her in Peru. The debts, or fines, vary according to the victim's nationality. If they came from Colombia, the fine was US$3,200, but if they had arrived from Venezuela, the sum was almost US$4,000, according to the documents. For Isabel, who had agreed to what she believed was a sales job at a commercial establishment, paying that amount of money was practically impossible. These fines are one of the forms of control that groups like Los Gallegos use to subject human trafficking victims. Any act of disobedience was punished with a fine increase of between US$250 and US$500. Others, to pay off their debt, recruited women like Isabel to take their place. As the woman who received her in Mollendo had sentenced her, Isabel was forced to work in a brothel, and at the end of the day, nothing was left for her. According to the case documents, the clients of the network paid around US$34 for half an hour, US$40 for an hour, and US$186 to spend the night with one of the women. All the money they earned had to be handed over to the man who watched them at the establishment and at the house where they slept as part of the payment for their debt. To keep the victims under their control, Los Gallegos did not only physically and intimidate them, but also exercised other forms of coercion. Their strategy included psychological manipulation accompanied by constant threats of harming their families, even in their countries of origin. It is because of the decentralized structure of the Tren de Aragua and their presence in several countries that allows them to find and threaten the families of their victims, even if they are abroad. They no longer leave, they no longer escape because they know what could happen to their children, and to their family in Venezuela, explains Ángela Villón, leader of Miluska Vida y Dignidad, an association of sex workers in Lima who has known cases of human trafficking firsthand. In addition, the women who are fined are constantly being watched. To prevent them from seeking help or forming connections, they are constantly transferred from street to street and city to city. They are taken here one week, taken there the next, and eventually, they are taken to provinces, says Liliana, another Venezuelan sex worker living in Lima. YOU CAN SEE Capturing members of the Aragua Train in Lima as part of an operation between Peru and the United States rescues 84 victims of human trafficking A maze with no exit Weeks after Isabel arrived in Mollendo, one of the women who lived with her managed to escape and reach the authorities. To avoid the police, Los Gallegos decided to move Isabel and the other women to the city of Arequipa. Once there, they were forced to work on the streets, while an armed man on a motorcycle kept watch from a distance. Isabel, on the other hand, attempted to escape twice. After the first failed attempt, they locked her in a room without allowing her to speak to anyone. In her second attempt, she got further, up to the transportation terminal, but again, they caught up to her. Under constant surveillance, it was not easy to escape. Moreover, even if she had managed to pay the fine with the group, it was almost impossible for them to let her go. There are cases where they pay and continue exploiting them, (...) they don't let them breathe for anything. They have to do what they say, Roxi maintains. The judicial documents echo her testimony. The women who had paid their debt had no other option but to continue working, and they had to pay 150 soles (US$40) per day to stay in the territory of Los Gallegos, as few of them had support networks that would allow them to escape the exploitation or return to their families. In interviews with InSight Crime, members of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the Human Trafficking Division of the Peruvian National Police (PNP) stated that the majority of women rescued during anti-human trafficking operations return to a situation of exploitation. Of the 2,500 people rescued in 2023, only 5% have open investigations, according to PNP data. This is because the Peruvian judicial system only initiates an investigation when a person files a formal complaint, something that very few victims do due to fear of reprisal. We have the limitation of being able to continue investigations because many times we have to search for other elements of evidence to lead us to determine that these are victims of human trafficking, because they do not accept it, explains General Aldo Ávila Novia, Head of the Human Trafficking Division of the PNP. It's quite difficult for them to accept that they are victims due to the circumstances of violence, he adds. The complaints are few. There are shortcomings in the investigations and operations against human trafficking, and, on occasion, sex workers are registered as victims of trafficking. And the reported cases continue to increase. In 2020, the PNP registered 372 complaints for human trafficking in the country, according to the National Institute of Statistics and Information of Peru. For 2022, the figure was 631, of which 85.3% were women (538), and 153 were Venezuelan. For 2024, only in the first six months of the year, the PNP registered 458 complaints, of which 78.7% of the presumed victims were women, and of them, 54 were between 13 and 17 years old. When Isabel tried to escape, the punishment did not take long to arrive. They made her put her hands on a table and hit her with the barrel of a gun, telling her she had to do it when they told her to, that she belonged to them, the judicial documents say. Since then, the threats increased. The criminals hit her constantly, took her phone to see her conversations with her family, and even told her they had sent people to Venezuela to look for her family members.You can see Aragua Mayor attacks Dina Boluarte over dismantling the Aragua train If that were true, there would be no extortions A light at the end of the tunnel One afternoon, around 2 p.m., two men arrived at Isabel's room. They told her to get up and gather her things, that she had to go with them. It had not been long since one of the group members was captured. Although the documents are not clear, it seems that the police also detained Isabel at that moment and then released her. They got into a car on a highway. They told her she had to be moved to a different location, one where she would be better off, and, stealthily, they asked her what she had told the police, to which she responded that she hadn't said anything. After about three hours of driving, they made her get out of the car. One of the men handed her a cell phone, while the other pulled out a gun and shot her. Isabel fell to the ground. The bullet had only grazed her. One of the men kicked her to make sure the job had been done well. She knew that if she moved, they would shoot her again, so she endured the pain. The last thing she heard them say was "get up, get up quickly, it's ready." Minutes later, she heard the car leave, and she began to seek help. Someone helped her get to the police station, where they took her statement and transferred her to the hospital. Although Isabel managed to escape her situation of exploitation and today the judicial case against her perpetrators is advancing in the courts of Arequipa, she is the exception to the rule.

Anahí Arizmendi, President of the Autonomous Institute National Council of Children's Rights (IDENNA), stated that the numbers of child sexual abuse cases have increased since 2020. The IDENNA representative reported that after the pandemic affected families worldwide, child sexual abuse cases significantly increased. She informed that they are providing training to those involved in the child protection system to ensure the comprehensive protection of children from the communities. She expressed that the major challenge is to advance in conflict resolution with prevention actions in a culture of peace, sports, and training to prevent more children and adolescents from being involved in acts of violence or a state of vulnerability.

Representative Celedón reports to the Child Protection Service on a child sex trafficking network in Talca Wednesday, January 22, 2025 11:08 hrs Screenshot of TVN news report. The recent report by Televisión Nacional de Chile (TVN) on the severe cases of abuse and aggression suffered by children, adolescents, and minors in Talca and the Maule region has caused a strong public impact. Among the reactions stands out that of Representative Roberto Celedón, who qualified the situation as extremely serious and announced that he has filed, through the Chamber of Deputies, with various related agencies, such as the Child Protection Service. The TVN report seemed serious and extremely worrying to me. After three years of investigation, three distinct individuals have been formalized. Three years is too long, the parliamentarian said, adding that efficiency must be a distinctive hallmark in public service, especially in the field of crimes against minors. Criticisms of delays in investigationsThe deputy highlighted that, according to the information exposed in the report, there would still be 40 additional cases to investigate, a situation he characterized as alarming. The Prosecutor's Office, the Investigations Police, and the Carabineros of Chile must be extraordinarily efficient. There can be no excuses on this matter, he emphasized.The legislator acknowledged having had a good initial impression of the Child Protection Service, but pointed out that the revelations in the report profoundly question the functioning and response of the institutions responsible for safeguarding the rights of minors. Finally, the parliamentarian reiterated his commitment to demanding clear and timely answers from the involved agencies to ensure that victims and their families receive justice. Three years is too long for a case as sensitive as this. It is imperative that measures are taken to prevent further delays in the future, he concluded.

data.text: Over a hundred days have passed since Morales' followers set up a vigil around the former president's residence and also control the surroundings of the facilities of the Six Federations of the Cochabamba Jungle. Armed supporters of Evo Morales. Photo: Unitel capture. After the ratification of the arrest order against former President Evo Morales in the case of human trafficking, the coca growers of the Cochabamba Jungle threatened to hang infiltrators. We want to be very clear. (If) we catch an infiltrator, we will hang him from a palo santo so he will know to respect the organizations and know with whom they're messing, said the leader of the Six Federations of the Cochabamba Jungle Vicente Choque. Morales' followers set up a vigil over a hundred days ago to prevent the former president's arrest. In Lauca Ñ, they set up earth mounds, as well as wooden fences. Senator Lucy Escobar was consulted about the threat and indicated that they hope people won't get involved or infiltrate because one reacts. Morales is being denounced for allegedly having a daughter with a minor in 2016, when he was in office. In the case, the father of the supposed victim received alternative measures. Learn more The personal thirst for revenge by Evo has led Bolivia to international shame This week, the Justice system also determined to reject Morales' appeal of his arrest order. In response, a new warrant was issued in the framework of the case of alleged human trafficking against the former president. Source Unitel

A 10-year prison sentence for abusing a minor in Ciudad Victoria, Tamaulipas. Joel E was sentenced to 10 years and 3 days in prison for the aggravated sexual abuse of a minor, which occurred in June 2022 in a neighborhood on the outskirts of Ciudad Victoria, reported the Attorney General's Office of Justice of Tamaulipas. The sentence was handed down by a Trial Court after the Public Prosecutor, assigned to the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for the Investigation of Crimes against Girls, Boys, and Adolescents and Crimes against Women due to Gender Reasons (FENNAM), presented evidence that demonstrated the defendant's responsibility. The Judge, in addition to the penalty of imprisonment, ordered a comprehensive repair of the damage to the victim, who suffered a severe attack on their sexual freedom. The National Police of Ecuador executed on February 13, 2025, the Operation Gran Fenix 7 Pandora 1, in Quito and Esmeraldas, under the direction of the General Prosecutor's Office and in coordination with the National Security Department of the United States of North America (HSI), through which a child pornography network was dismantled, and 4 people were apprehended. Background of the case Following investigative work and information exchange between HSI Frederick in Maryland (USA), In Ecuador, a joint operation between the National Police and the General Prosecutor's Office resulted in the identification of a criminal network dedicated to the production and commercialization of child sexual abuse material. The material, which was audiovisual in nature, was produced by the suspects themselves, using their minor children, and was sold to American citizens through live video calls or file transfers via instant messaging platforms. The suspects earned substantial sums of money through international wire transfers from the United States as a result of these illicit activities. A U.S. citizen was detained in possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), who had been repeatedly traveling to Esmeraldas, prompting an investigation in Ecuador in December 2024 for the alleged crime of child pornography trafficking. This investigation led to the identification of four suspects and the identification of two victims of these abuses. On February 13, 2025, five minors were rescued from this criminal network. The arrested individuals are Nury Alexandra G.S., Kathiusca Maribel, George Miguel G.C., and Rosa Gissela S.O., who have no prior records. Evidence includes 13 cellular phones, 2 payment receipts, 1 tablet, 2 SIM cards, and various documents. The National Police, in fulfillment of their constitutional mission, remains firm against networks that threaten the lives of minors.

data.text: A primary school teacher was sentenced to life in prison for the crime of sexual abuse of a minor and for the alleged commission of the crime of acts against modesty. William Luis Gómez Ulloa (57), a primary school teacher in the Marañón province, was investigated by the Marañón Provincial Penal Prosecutor's Office since 2014 for the alleged commission of the crime of sexual abuse of a minor and for the alleged commission of the crime of acts against modesty. The defendant was working as a classroom teacher at one of the primary educational institutions in the San Cristóbal annex, Huacrachuco district, Marañón province, from 2009 until 2014. HE ABUSED HIS POWER DURING RECESS During that time, in 2012, he sexually abused one of his 10-year-old students, who was in the third grade of primary school, during recess inside his classroom, after ordering her to close the door so he could review her homework. However, this has not been the only case, as there is also a second victim who was subjected to indecent touching by the perpetrator since 2013. This occurred inside his salon, in the presence of other students. In fact, this girl continued studying with the bad teacher until she completed sixth grade and endured constant harassment from the now-sentenced perpetrator. CONSTANT THREATSWilliam Gómez offered to promote them to the next grade without the need for them to study, and also threatened to fail them in their courses if they did not comply with his whims. One of the victims stated that when she avoided the teacher from approaching to kiss her, he would slap her. The prosecution was also able to have the perpetrator permanently barred from his professional practice and he must pay the indemnification to the victims for the commission of acts against their modesty in the sum of 9,000 soles for each, and for the crime of sexual violation, 25,000 soles in favor of the victim.

The alliance was formalized with a ceremonial signing of the memorandum of agreement on January 23, 2025. Dolly Rubia, IJM's national director of Post-Care Development, presented an overview and content of the memorandum, including the responsibilities and obligations of the signing organizations. Representatives from the associated organizations shared messages of commitment and encouragement to all who attended the ceremony. The owner of a bar accused of raping an employee claims that someone put something in his drink. The alleged rapist, who faces 7 years in prison, was recorded by another employee when he forced the 20-year-old victim while she was unconscious. A recording on a mobile phone, in which it is clearly observed how the alleged rapist moves over his unconscious victim on the co-pilot's seat of a car and inserts his hand under her dress, making repeated movements, has been key to the trial against the owner of a bar in Silla who was detained in August 2022 for sexually assaulting one of his employees. Despite this conclusive evidence, the accused, who faces 7 years in prison, claims that he does not remember anything and that someone must have put something in his drink. The world turned upside down, the alleged rapist claiming to be a victim of chemical submission. Honestly, I don't remember anything. I woke up in a car that wasn't mine, the defendant justified himself in the trial held yesterday at the Second Section of the Provincial Court of Valencia. That night, after finishing the work shift at his restaurant in Silla, the owner of the business and four of his employees went out to party at a well-known discotheque on Profesor López Piñero Avenue in Valencia. According to the defendant and the witnesses, they were in a reserved area of the club drinking liquor, gin, and shots. During the time they were at the discotheque, where the defendant invited his employees, he was making obscene comments and gestures to two of his employees, calling the victim "calientapollas". He touched her buttocks twice and told me he would make a Cuban with my breasts, one of the employees who testified yesterday reported. The colleagues who were working that night confirm that the victim was extremely drunk and that around 7:00 am, they had to accompany her to the vehicle, where they left her in the co-pilot's seat because she was falling asleep. She was very intoxicated, she was stumbling around like a blind person, remembers the witness.Due to alcohol consumption, the 20-year-old girl does not remember almost anything from those moments, when she was taken to her friend's car and fell asleep. She was like in a coma, she explained to the magistrates behind a screen. What she does remember is that she felt a discomfort in the vaginal area.It was later, on the way back to Silla in the car, that her colleagues woke her up and told her that they had to show her something. At that moment, they showed her the recording that one of them had taken with his mobile phone from the car window. The key piece of evidence that proved she had been raped while unconscious. In a car that was not hers, after leaving the nightclub, the victim's coworkers had left her asleep in the passenger seat due to her condition, as she was indisposed and seasick from drinking alcohol. The witnesses stepped away from the car and talked for a while, allowing the alcohol to wear off so they could drive back home. Meanwhile, her boss, the accused, got into the driver's seat of the victim's vehicle, with the false excuse of resting, despite having his own car just a few meters away. At a certain point, the witnesses noticed the car moving and approached it. Due to the sun's reflection, which was just rising, one of them approached to film with their phone, and it was then that they saw the scene that left no room for interpretation. She was extremely drunk, she was almost falling down because she was blind drunk. Witnesses claim that the accused realized what he had done and insisted on taking the victim home, but his companions refused. The same morning, the young woman filed a complaint with the Civil Guard and her companions provided the recording. The accused now faces a request for a seven-year prison sentence for a crime of sexual abuse with carnal access and payment of a €20,000 compensation for moral damages. In response, the defense denies that there was finger insertion and based their entire interrogation on proving that their client did not have stained hands, as the victim confesses to having her period. They also request an exemption due to alcohol consumption. However, the prosecutor dismantled the exculpatory thesis that the accused was especially drunk, by acknowledging that he drove to his home in Silla without any problems. . Barranquilla, the city with the lowest rates of begging and child labor among the major capitals. As a result of the great social bet of Mayor Alejandro Char, Barranquilla was the city that recorded the lowest index of begging and child labor among the four main cities of the country during the year 2024. This achievement, reported by the DANE in its 2024 report on child labor rates, is the result of the coordinated actions by the District Mayor's Office, through the Secretary of Social Management and its program Working for Children, which is accompanied by the First Lady, Katia Nule, the Secretary of Government, along with the Family Commissions of the ICBF, Child and Adolescent Police, Migration Colombia, and the Ministry of Labor. The DANE report indicates that for the year 2024, the record of children in a condition of begging in Barranquilla dropped to 0.8%, while in 2023 the figure stood at 1. 0.6%, which means a reduction of around 3,000 children, girls, and adolescents (CGA) who have escaped this cycle of begging. In March, the hearing against Nicolás Petro will continue for the narcopagos. To continue working towards this goal and continue with the forceful actions to face child begging in the city, the district administration reinforced the Barranquilla without child begging strategy in four fronts this 2025. The goal is to reach zero child begging in the city by continuing the comprehensive attention of CGA, but this year we will intervene directly and forcefully in the cases detected of child exploitation in the active searches that are carried out. We will go to the homes of the adults identified with children on the streets, together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, ICBF, and Family Commissary, to verify with neighbors if the child or girl is being instrumentalized, do a characterization, and evaluate if it merits comprehensive attention from the City Hall or judicial measures supported by Article 6 of Law 247 of 2002, said Ismael Marín, District Secretary of Social Management. All these priority actions for the defense and restitution of the rights of minors have the special accompaniment of the District's First Lady, Katia Nule, who highlights that this is an integral strategy that provides support to children in areas such as health, recreation, education, as well as to families. What we do from the Trabajando por los niños program is to demand all those children who are on the streets, whether working or begging. It's a job that needs to be done every day with everyone's support. A child you rescue from the street is a child who completely changes because we educate them, their health rights are restored, they are given opportunities for recreation and sports, and they receive psychological help. It's a beautiful, satisfying integral work in which we need the involvement of all actors involved so that Barranquilla continues to be a model city at the national level, said the first lady of the District, Katia Nule, highlighting that among the main cities, Barranquilla is the one that has most reduced child labor. The invitation is to continue working and to continue saying no to child labor. Indicators 2024 During the previous year, the Trabajando por los Niños program achieved the creation of a protective space located in the San Roque neighborhood. Additionally, it provided psychosocial support to 324 NNA (children and adolescents at risk) and benefited 190 families, to whom home-based care and follow-up were provided. 50 children, boys, and adolescents were linked to the educational system, and all beneficiary families received food security. Similarly, 140 active search days were carried out with an average of 10 to 12 coordinated interventions with the ICBF, Family Commissariat, Child and Adolescent Police, Colombian Migration, and Ministry of Labour. Sensitization days carried out in 12 points of the city, such as shopping centers, impacted approximately 10,000 people. 2025 Plan The Barranquilla Mayor's Office will strengthen in this 2025 the Barranquilla without child begging strategy in four fronts. The first action aims to continue prevention campaigns that include street dramas, sensitization in commercial centers, campaign points in city buildings, hotels, and the airport, special days for the commemoration of World Day Against Child Labor, and a strengthened Christmas Plan, said Leyla Yidios, director of the program. The second item points towards the constant reception of complaints through the enabled Denunciation Line, 3216976686, which operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The third area implies a greater presence of the entities committed to this work, such as ICBF, Family Commissariat, Children and Adolescence Police, Colombian Migration, and the Ministry of Labor, in critical points, increasing the number of active searches from 140 to 180 this year. These days will allow for the identification of cases and minimize the number of NNA exposed to begging and child labor. In this action, the Child and Adolescent Police will make available to these active search days 2 mobile CAI units delivered by the District Administration. The fourth point, called Contingent Actions, aims to identify cases through denunciation or active searches in critical points, attending to the NNA with referral to the ICBF zonal office or the UCJ for the restoration of their rights, which include preventive follow-ups of parents and family members so that minors are not repeatedly exploited by adults or responsible caregivers.

Bangkok, February 14 (EFE). An Argentine court issued an international arrest warrant against the leader of the Myanmar military junta, Min Aung Hlaing, for his alleged involvement in genocide and other crimes against humanity allegedly committed by the Army against the Rohingya Muslim minority, reports this Thursday the NGO that prompted the lawsuit. This is a historic step towards justice (...) It brings a ray of hope for the Rohingya who have suffered decades of genocide, watching how their families and culture were destroyed with impunity, said in a statement Tun Khin, president of the Rohingya Organization in the UK (ROUK). The NGO, which filed the lawsuit in November 2019 in the federal courts of Buenos Aires, indicated that the Argentine justice issued the order against Min Aung Hlaing and 22 other military commanders. They are accused of crimes that include genocide and other offenses listed in the Argentine Penal Code, such as aggravated murder, sexual abuse, and torture. This courageous decision sends a clear signal to Min Aung Hlaing and other military leaders that no one is above the law. In the end, they will have to be judged for the unbearable suffering they have caused not only to generations of Rohingya, but to all the victims of the military brutality in Myanmar, remarks Tun Khin. The case, regardless of the ones being studied at the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice, both in The Hague, was presented in Argentina based on the principle of universal jurisdiction for crimes such as genocide and crimes against humanity, recalls the BROUK. The brutal operation that the Myanmar Army launched in August 2017 against the Rohingya population in the north of the state of Rakhine, in this country and where this minority has been settled for centuries, motivated the exodus of more than 720,000 Rohingya. .000 refugees to neighboring Bangladesh, where thousands of Rohingya had been displaced in previous years. The UN estimates that during this campaign, which a report described as ethnic cleansing with genocidal marks, at least 10,000 people were killed, while hundreds of villages were razed by intentional fires. In November last year, the ICC prosecutor requested an arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing for the deportation and persecution of the Rohingya, among other crimes against humanity committed between August 25, 2017, and December 31, 2017, by Myanmar's armed forces and other authorities. While the ICC judges must still determine whether this request meets the necessary standard to approve the issuance of the requested arrest warrant against the Burmese general, the Argentine court's decision has triggered an automatic request for the prosecutor to issue the orders, according to the NGO. General Min Aung Hlaing led the February 1, 2021 military coup that ended a decade of democratic transition and opened a spiral of violence that has exacerbated the decades-long guerrilla war the country has been living, with thousands of young people joining new armed groups that fight against the Army.

data.text: Nashville, Tennessee. Two women managed to escape from their captor on February 10, when they called the police from a motel on Demonbreun Street. Both had arrived in Nashville on different dates, one by plane from Miami and the other in a rental car from El Paso, after being contacted through a website. According to judicial documents, 37-year-old Francisco Pascual Angulo promised them a luxurious lifestyle if they moved to Tennessee to organize parties and serve alcoholic beverages. However, upon arriving in the city, they were forced to engage in sexual relations with strangers, who paid in cash or through electronic transfer. Angulo housed them in a residence on Acklen Avenue, near Hillsboro Village, where he controlled their food and drinks, and demanded they share their location at all times. He threatened them and their families if they did not comply with his orders. After their escape and alerting the authorities, the police raided Angulo's property and seized cash, vehicles, and luxury goods. The suspect was arrested and taken to the Metro jail, where he faces two charges of human trafficking for commercial sexual purposes. His bail was set at $150,000.

The accused of sexually abusing his 8-year-old niece in Mallorca denies the allegations and claims it is a false accusation He claims that at one point he heard his sister tell the girl that if she told anyone about the abuse, she would buy her a video game console The man accused of sexually abusing his 8-year-old niece has denied the allegations on Friday and has assured that it was the second time he was falsely accused of similar incidents. During the trial held on Friday at the Provincial Court of Palma, the man has assured that at the time of the alleged incidents, he only entered the home where the victim was to change clothes and pick up something to wear, although he fell asleep. At the questions of the Public Prosecutor's Office, the accused explained that when he entered, his niece was watching TV, that he did not exchange any words with her, and that when he woke up, there was no one in the house. The man has denied the accusations of sexual abuse in this way and has added that it was the second time that his sister, the mother of the girl, had accused him of having touched her daughter, who has testified in private. According to what he added, he once heard his sister tell the girl that if she told about the abuse, she would buy her a video console. The prosecution is asking for a 12-year prison sentence and 10 years of supervised release for the defendant for acts that date back to May 2020 and took place in a locality in Mallorca. According to the indictment, on one occasion, taking advantage of being alone at home, the defendant made unwanted contact with the girl and even inserted his finger into her vagina. At another time, he also handled the girl's body and genitals.

The Spanish police investigation to locate an individual who allegedly downloaded several images of a sexual nature, both photos and videos, of minors, led the agents to an address in Sant Feliu where they identified the suspected pedophile, who also had regular contact with children. The teacher, who is currently free after his arrest and the seizure of several electronic devices found in his home, including his computer and mobile phone, was put at the disposal of the Investigating Judge's Court on duty, who released him on charges, as reported by SER Catalunya. Despite the severity of the events, they would have occurred outside the school setting and would not have affected any students of the school. The investigation continues to clarify all the details. On the other hand, from the Escola Pública lEstació educational center, where the accused used to work, they have decided to remove him from the classrooms, and the man has not returned to the school since his arrest, as explained by the Departament d'Educació to the mentioned medium. Additionally, they are studying the possibility of activating a protocol in the center in collaboration with the Serveis Territorials d'Educació de Girona.

The regulations include harsher penalties, restrictions on local officials and changes to migrant transportation in Miami (EFE) Florida Governor, Republican Ron DeSantis, signed two broad laws on Thursday that toughen the conditions for undocumented immigrants and facilitate in this state the implementation of President of the United States, Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda. The bills establish harsher penalties for undocumented immigrants who commit crimes, stricter application requirements for local officials and changes to the contentious state migrant transportation program (the governor will no longer have unilateral power to authorize them). One of the contentious aspects that are part of the laws signed today has to do with the automatic establishment of the death penalty for undocumented immigrants who are found guilty of a capital crime, such as murder or child sexual abuse. According to some experts, this aspect is likely to face legal complaints due to the fact that, as pointed out by some Democratic lawmakers in both chambers, the US Supreme Court ruled decades ago that mandatory and non-jury sentences were unconstitutional. The laws approved today in the framework of an extraordinary session of the State Legislature also contemplate the creation of a State Immigration Control Board, composed of the governor, the commissioner of agriculture, the attorney general, and the state's financial director. This board will coordinate legal and security actions with federal agencies and will have a $250 million fund to distribute among local law enforcement agencies that help federal efforts in this field, in order to stimulate cooperation with US Customs and Immigration Service (ICE). The texts establish the creation of new state crimes for the illegal entry or re-entry into Florida, elevating unlicensed driving to a serious crime for undocumented immigrants. In the same way, it criminalizes the entry into Florida of undocumented immigrants over 18 years old who enter the state after entering the United States, evading or avoiding inspection or examination by immigration agents, and will be subject to a nine-month prison sentence. The matriculation as residents of undocumented students in public universities of the state is eliminated, and all local sheriff's offices have until April to enroll in the federal 287(g) program, which grants authority to local agents to carry out tasks proper to federal immigration agencies. Today, the Florida Legislature has approved the strongest legislation to combat illegal immigration of any state in the country, DeSantis said in a press conference just before signing the bills, and in which he was accompanied by Senate President Ben Albritton and state House Speaker Daniel Pérez. The signing today marks the end of weeks of disagreements between DeSantis and state lawmakers, who have a Republican majority in both chambers, over immigration reforms, which merited calls for up to three special sessions.

Mass Operation Against Hawkers in Flores, Raids and Merchandise Seizure There are complaints about clandestine work and human trafficking in textile workshops. With over 550 officers, the City Police carried out a massive operation against illegal sales in Flores on Friday. The operation began near 4 am and covers the perimeter between Avellaneda and Nazca Avenues and Bogotá, Campana, Cuenca, Helguera, and Venancio Flores streets. In the early hours, they conducted around 50 raids on hawkers' warehouses with merchandise of illegal origin and spoiled food. They aim to evict 5,000 hawkers from 32 city blocks in the port district. Police sources reported that there are complaints about clandestine work and human trafficking in textile workshops. More than 550 inspectors, workers, and police officers from various divisions, including the Superintendent of Investigations, the Ministries of Security and Public Space, the Government Agency for Control, Transit, and the National Migration Directorate, participated. Aragua Train, the feared criminal organization of Latin America, continues in Peru and dares the PNP Here we are This criminal organization has released new videos in which it challenges the Peruvian National Police, while it assures having dismantled it in the country. In the recording, a member of the gang asserts, in a challenging manner, that they continue operating on the streets "Here we are," he says. The recording shows that, despite the efforts of the authorities, the group maintains its influence in the country, especially in activities such as extortion and human trafficking. "Here we are," he heard. "This is the Train, there's nothing about those crazy people. Here we are, the real tough guys. We have them working, my people." Everything is under control, my people, you can hear a suspected member of the criminal organization recording their firearm from a moving vehicle.  OPERATIVE in Challapalca prison cells are being raided and illegal antennas are being torn down. This type of statement is not new, since this criminal band has been a latent threat in several regions of Peru, and over the past few months, it has increased its presence in the country, where it has managed to establish several illegal networks. Although local authorities have made an effort to combat it, this criminal group seems to have found ways to remain operational and defiant. Disarticulation, according to the PNP However, the head of the PNP's Against Human Trafficking Directorate, Aldo Ávila Novoa, in an interview conducted on February 10, stated that the Peruvian National Police had completely disarticulated the Tren de Aragua networks in the country. In the same statement, he assured that several key members of the group had been detained and that part of their operational infrastructure had been dismantled, which was considered a significant blow to the criminal organization. As a criminal organization, the Aragua Train, in Peru, is completely dismantled. All the leaders have fallen (are serving their sentence in Challapalca), the police chief stated in RPP. According to the police chief, security forces have carried out multiple operations that have allowed them to reduce the capacity of this organization, preventing them from carrying out their criminal activities. In this context, he highlighted that both Peruvian and foreign authorities are working to combat the cells or factions of this organization, which include the Anti-Train and The Sons of God. The Aragua Train, a Constant Threat in Peru and Latin America The Aragua Train has been identified as one of the most influential criminal groups in Latin America, with presence in several countries. In Peru, their activity has been reported in various areas, particularly in human trafficking and extortion. The organization has been characterized by its ability to operate in different regions of the country. The Aragua Train US presents charges against eight Venezuelans, suspected members of the Aragua Train, for leading a human trafficking network that forced migrant women into prostitution. The US Department of Justice has presented a new legal effort to dismantle the transnational criminal organization known as the Aragua Train, which has expanded its operations in US territory. Judicial documents, reviewed by NTN24, reveal a four-count indictment involving the active participation of eight Venezuelan immigrants with the organization and leading a human trafficking network that forced migrant women to work in prostitution. According to authorities, the intention was for the victims to pay off their debts, acquired in their efforts to regularize their immigration status in the United States, through sexual favors. This formal accusation demonstrates our commitment to stopping human trafficking wherever we find it and holding those involved accountable. We're pursuing transnational organized crime groups like the Aragua Train, but this case shows we'll do what's necessary to stop those who traffic women and girls, no matter who's behind their suffering, said Robert McGuire, one of the prosecutors leading the investigation. According to authorities, the legal implications of these charges are severe, and the eight Venezuelan migrants would face sentences ranging from 15 to 20 years, with the possibility of life imprisonment, depending on the magnitude and circumstances of the crimes committed. This move by the United States Department of Justice marks, among other things, a critical front in the fight against human trafficking and the criminal structures that affect vulnerable communities.

International What is the Aragua Train, the criminal network expanding in America and which Trump seeks to declare a terrorist group Extortion, kidnappings, drug trafficking, and human trafficking. The dangerous gang born in Venezuela has expanded across the continent, sowing terror in several countries. Sandy Pineda February 13, 2025 12:03h The Government of Venezuela assured that it had put an end to the criminal structures that controlled prison centers, following a deployment in Tocorón, the birthplace of the transnational gang Tren de Aragua, last September 2024. (Photo Prensa Libre EFE) To talk about the Aragua Train is to go back to its origins in Venezuela and the figure of Héctor Guerrero Flores, better known as the Niño Guerrero, considered one of the most dangerous criminals in the country. This organization, which emerged within a prison, has grown to become one of the most feared in South America. Although their activities were already underway, the group gained notoriety in August 2012, when the Niño Guerrero escaped from Tocorón Prison in Aragua State. The name "Tren de Aragua" originated from a railway union linked to a project that never came to fruition. Its members began to engage in criminal activity, extorting contractors and selling jobs on construction sites. Over time, they gained recognition as the Tren de Aragua. Some of them ended up in Tocorón, where they came into contact with the Niño Guerrero. From prison, they began to coordinate their criminal operations outside, extending their control first to neighboring states and later to other countries such as Colombia, Peru, and Chile. Read also Massacre in Chiapas 4 data of the attack between narcos that would have left Guatemalans dead Expansion and consolidation One of the key factors in the expansion of the Tren de Aragua was the unofficial policy of the Venezuelan government, which, according to the Insight Crime analysis center, allowed certain criminal groups to take control of some prisons. Tocorón became the operations base of the Tren de Aragua, and the authorities' permissiveness was such that within the prison, a zoo, a pool, a park, a restaurant, and even a nightclub were built. Beyond the prison, the group consolidated its power by taking control of the San Vicente neighborhood and displacing other gangs in different states of the country. Their illicit activities include extortion, kidnapping, illegal mining, drug trafficking, and robberies. The Venezuelan migrant crisis also favored their expansion Capitalizing on the vulnerability of migrants, the gang implemented exploitation and extortion networks in other countries, infiltrating clandestine groups in Colombia. Today, the Aragua Train operates as a network of autonomous factions that adapt to local conditions and specialize in various criminal activities, including illegal loans (gota a gota), small-scale micro-trafficking of drugs, kidnappings, international small-scale drug trafficking, human trafficking, and robberies. The violence unleashed by the group in different countries has raised alarms in the region, leading to an increase in operations against them. In September 2023, the Venezuelan government regained control of Tocorón, dismantling their main stronghold. Read also Colombian lenders how the gota a gota loans work, the structure they are composed of and where they operate in Guatemala Since 2022, the security forces of Chile, Peru and Colombia have intensified their efforts to stop the expansion of the Aragua Train through large-scale operations. Aragua Train, target of Trump Although its presence in the United States is not known, there are suspicions that the Aragua Train already operates in the country. Its growing notoriety has generated concern in the government and Congress. In July 2024, the Department of the Treasury declared the Aragua Train as a Transnational Criminal Organization. However, President Donald Trump has sought to go further On his first day of his second term, he signed a series of decrees on immigration matters, among which was a recommendation for the State Department to initiate the process of designating the gang as a foreign terrorist organization. The corruption in Huánuco seems to have no end. On the contrary, each day new cases emerge that challenge the legality and morality of society. One of the most flagrant examples is the persistence of the brothel Villa Cariño, located in the lower part of the human settlement in Las Moras. Despite having been closed on multiple occasions, this establishment continues to operate, apparently with the complicity of certain authorities who, instead of enforcing the law, facilitate its reopening. This local is a constant focus of obscene acts, excessive drinking, and loud music, disturbing the peace of the community and giving a lamentable example to the children who grow up observing this scenario. Beyond the public scandal, the existence of Villa Cariño also reveals a structural problem of human trafficking and the exploitation of women in irregular conditions. The neighbors in the area, fed up with the situation, have filed complaints and, in some cases, have even managed to obtain court rulings in their favor. However, these efforts have proven to be useless, as the brothel continues to operate thanks to alleged bribes and corruption networks involving municipal officials, prosecutors, and judges. Here emerges a key question: what kind of justice is exercised in Huánuco when a judicial sentence can be ignored with total impunity? The complicity of certain sectors of the local government and the judicial system only reinforces public distrust in institutions. It is supposed that authorities should watch over the well-being of the community, but in this case, they seem more interested in protecting the interests of those who profit from the exploitation of women and social disorder. It is not a matter of condemning women who seek to earn a living, but of demanding dignified conditions for all. There are safer and more legitimate job alternatives, but as long as corruption allows these businesses to thrive in illegality, it's difficult to offer real options for those seeking a livelihood. It's time for the Ombudsman's Office and other competent authorities to take a firm stance on this issue. Simply closing down the brothel is not enough if its doors reopen soon under the same shadow of impunity. It's urgent to impose severe sanctions on those responsible, including those who, from their public positions, have allowed this den to continue operating.

The Penal Chamber considers that the proven facts clearly describe the accused's use of violence and intimidation. Original Author: Judicial Communication Power. The Civil and Penal Chamber of the Superior Court of Justice of Murcia (TSJMU) upholds the sentence of the Provincial Court of Murcia that sentenced a man to 13 years and 6 months in prison for a continued sex crime with carnal access to a 16-year-old minor, with the use of violence and intimidation. According to the verdict, the defendant took advantage of the minor, daughter of a friend of his, staying at his home after school to subject her to repeated sexual abuse, threatening her with harming her family if she revealed what had happened. The defendant would take her to the bathroom and force her to perform oral sex, making the girl insert his penis into her mouth, then grab her head, preventing her from retreating, threatening to tell her mother that she had misbehaved if she said anything, and telling her that he had a gun and would kill her, her family, and her cat if she said anything, adding that he had cameras set up throughout his house, as stated in the judicial resolution. And it is declared proven that the minor suffered repeated episodes of abuse over several months and has needed psychological treatment. The Court of Appeal dismisses the defense arguments, which initially claimed an error in the assessment of the evidence, questioning the credibility of the victim's testimony. According to the judges, the exploitation of the testimony of the minor presented as a victim has been carried out by the trial court in accordance with the general criteria or parameters of reliability indicated by the Jurisprudence. They add that there are no substantial contradictions in the minor's account, who has consistently maintained coherence in their statements, and highlight that the mother and brother have provided objective data that corroborate the circumstances in which the aggression occurred. The Tribunal also does not accept the accused's request to reduce the sentence to six years in prison due to the wrongful application of the violent or intimidating modality, and considers the imposed sentence justified by the Provincial Court of Murcia. In the present case, the proven facts describe with perfect clarity the accused's use of the minor in both physical (he grabbed her by the head and forced her to perform oral sex) and psychological (he threatened to kill her, her family, and her cat if she told anyone, and he had cameras set up throughout the house) ways, the sentence concludes. In addition to the prison sentence, he will be required to serve a seven-year period of supervised liberty after his release from prison, as well as a special disqualification from any profession or trade that involves contact with minors for a period of 17 years and 6 months. He will also be ordered to pay a €10,000 compensation to the victim in the form of moral damages, as well as a prohibition on approaching within a distance of less than 300 meters for 20 years and 6 months and one day. The decision is not final and can be appealed by way of cassation to the Supreme Court.

Former Judge Daniel Tobares, who used to work in the Second Circuit in Roca, will face a public oral trial in March next year in the case that is being prosecuted against him as a result of a complaint for sexual abuse. A public oral trial will be held from March 5 to 11 of this year, in extensive sessions scheduled from 9 to 1430. It will be a trial for the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access. If found guilty, the penalty for this crime ranges from 6 to 15 years in prison. Tobares arrives at this trial as a result of a complaint of abuse that occurred on April 5, 2021, and was labeled as a crime of sexual abuse with carnal access. In recent months, the investigation's progress, which included psychiatric and psychological expertise, determined that the accused is capable of facing a trial. The forensic tests were necessary because in March 2023, the defendant suffered two ACVs that left him in a critical state, which delayed the deadlines for the trial of the case. The same year, in August 2023, lawyers Oscar Pineda and Pablo Iribarren, who were the defendant's defenders at the time, resigned from the case without giving many explanations. Currently, the defender in charge is Juan Luis Vincenty. The fact that led to trial The complaint that initiated the case was filed by a young law student from Cipolletti, who presented it at the Third Police Station in Roca. The investigation was carried out by the prosecutors of the Fourth Circumscription, based in Cipolletti, to avoid any possible contamination due to the years of operation of the accused. The Public Ministry stated that on April 10, 2021, between 1:30 and 4 am, Tobares met the young woman at a central pastry shop. They spent some time together, and then he offered to take her to her home. However, he took her to his own residence and, taking advantage of the fact that the girl was not in a position to defend herself, he abused her. Among other pieces of evidence, the victim's clinical history from Hospital López Lima, planimetric data from the location where the alleged events took place, the psychological expertise conducted on the victim, as well as photos and telephone conversations obtained by the Office of Judicial Telephone Interceptions were incorporated.

The Chiapas Judiciary issued a historic sentence against Yudiel N for human trafficking and child pornography distribution, reaffirming its commitment to protecting minors. Here are the news staff. In a ruling that sets a precedent in the fight against crimes that threaten the integrity of girls, boys, and adolescents, the State of Chiapas Judiciary, led by Magistrate Juan Carlos Moreno Guillén, handed down a exemplary condemnatory sentence against Yudiel N. The accused was sentenced to 67 years and six months in prison, in addition to paying damages, for the crime of human trafficking in its mode of sexual exploitation through the distribution of child pornography. The investigation, initiated following a complaint from the Federal Bureau of Investigation of the United States (FBI), revealed that Yudiel N, under the alias RONALD FRANCO, used the TOR network to distribute child sexual abuse material since at least 2011. After a rigorous judicial process in Comitán de Domínguez district, the perpetrator was identified and sentenced, thus guaranteeing the protection of the victims, whose identities remain safeguarded. This sentence not only reflects the commitment of the Chiapas Judiciary to humanistic justice and a child-centered perspective, but it also sets a precedent in the fight against crimes that violate the rights of minors. With this decision, we reaffirm our commitment to ensuring a life free of violence for girls, boys, and adolescents in Chiapas, highlighted Magistrate Moreno Guillén.

The man, 49 years old, pretended to be a minor to lure the girl and has also been sentenced to two years in prison for creating child pornography.A father in Seville raped his seven-year-old neighbor's daughter who was at his house for a pajama party. Two years in prison and seven years without access to the WhatsApp messaging app is the sentence handed down by the Seville Court against a man who used this mobile application to trick a minor into sending him sexual images and videos.In the sentence, recorded by Europa Press, the First Section of the Seville Court declares as proven, as the accused admitted, that between March and May 2021, Javier Á.T.G., 49 years old, with no prior convictions computable for recidivism, used fake profiles created on the web page canalchat to lure a minor. The accused, who had no prior convictions, admitted that he created profiles on the web page canalchat between March and May 2021 to lure minors. He then used these profiles to obtain sexual images and videos from a 13-year-old girl. On fake profiles posing as a 15-year-old boy, he contacted a 13-year-old girl born on February 1, 2008, despite informing her of his age, and offered her his phone number to talk on WhatsApp with the intention of requesting her to send images and videos of a sexual nature to satisfy his lustful desires, as well as to send her sexual content. These images were also sent through the temporary photo website, which operates without records and anonymously, allowing the user to choose the amount of time the image remains visible, between one and 60 minutes for the option of viewing by time, or just five seconds if the express view option is selected, as stated in the sentencing judgment after the defendant admitted to the facts. Sexual Video Calls The sentence also reveals that, once the accused revealed his true age, he made video calls to the minor, during which she could be observed masturbating. These facts have caused the victim to have been in psychological treatment from May 2021 to June 2022, suffering significant emotional distress and presenting a depressed mood, frequent crying, floating anxiety accompanied by occasional episodes of greater intensity, feelings of guilt, and frequent tension headaches. The sentence also acknowledges that on the date when the facts occurred, the accused consumed cocaine, which caused a slight decrease in his volitional capacity. Additionally, the perpetrator paid 10,000 euros, corresponding to the amount claimed by the private prosecution in concept of civil liability. Before all these investigations, and after the agreement reached between the defense, the Public Prosecutor's Office, and the private prosecution, the court sentences Javier Á.T.G. to two years in prison for a crime of creating child pornography involving a minor under 16 years old and a crime of obscene exposure to minors, with the mitigating circumstances of damage repair and drug addiction, as well as a 1,800 euro fine, although his prison sentence is suspended as long as he does not reoffend for a period of time. Additionally, the Court of Appeals imposes seven years of prohibition on approaching the victim or communicating with her and seven years of prohibition on accessing WhatsApp and the canalchat.org website, eight years of special disqualification for a profession or job involving direct contact with minors, and five years of supervised liberty.

In the month of August 2024, a complaint was received by the Specialized Unit for Domestic Violence and Gender, where knowledge was taken of the facts of sexual abuse towards an 8-year-old child by his father, initiating the corresponding actions. The 2nd Turn Public Prosecutor's Office was duly notified, and existing protocols, forensic procedures, and other actions were applied. As a result, after the actions taken and the corresponding results having been elevated to Justice, and following an audience that took place recently, the Acting Magistrate decreed a sentence for the man identified by initials L.A.R.V, 30 years old, for the commission of repeated aggravated sexual abuse, with a sentence of 2 years of effective imprisonment, suspension of parental authority or guardianship, prohibition from holding public positions, among other measures.

This Friday, the first trial of the year of the Oral Court of Río Grande against a 37-year-old man accused of sexual abuse of his partner's child between 2012 and 2013 begins. In 2021, there was a judicial maneuver in which this man had been acquitted, which was later revoked, and the case finally reaches trial after years of process. Carlos Mallo will be taken to trial from this Friday by the Criminal Trial Court of the North District Judicial Court in the Campamento YPF courts. The hearings will begin with the accusation by the Chief Prosecutor Martín Bramatti in the absence of the Gender Prosecution Office, and the private defense of the accused will be handled by Drs. Sandra Arenas and Erica Soto. The trial is for the crime of severely outrageous sexual abuse aggravated against a minor, with whom Mallo was in a situation of cohabitation between 2012 and 2013, while maintaining a sentimental relationship with the minor's mother. A suggestive element is that the woman later took her own life. The defendant arrives at this trial in freedom after several years of judicial process in which he had numerous public shaming incidents by groups of mothers against Child Sexual Abuse, even the case became famous when it was publicly shamed on the occasion of attending court for his interrogation (photo), on which occasion Mallo's then-lawyer faced the protesters. The judicial process had the particularity that in 2021, Judge Daniel Cesari, with the consent of the prosecutor, dismissed the accusation against Mallo, and even attempted to leave his definitive discharge firm, denying an appeal presented by a querellant lawyer, the current president of the Concejo Deliberante, Dr. Guadalupe Zamora, as a private lawyer at the time. The Chamber of Appeals revoked Cesari's ruling and removed him from the case, in which this controversial judge attempted by all means to acquit the accused who now arrives at trial. A situation of absolute judicial insecurity of this Judiciary. The process that begins this Friday will have 19 witnesses.

During the hearing to control the detention and formalization, prosecutor Kelly Pérez reported that on February 11, 2025, at approximately 6:30 PM, at the intersection of Esmeralda Street and Juan Martinez Street in the city of Iquique, a group of Carabinero officers and officers were conducting inspections and controls in the area. At that moment, the accused began to insult a Carabinero who was inspecting another individual. Among the background information that was known were the statements of the victims, but also by a recording from municipal cameras that was analyzed by the Investigative Police and captured the entire incident, indicated the Prosecutor (f). The Public Ministry formalized the suspect for the crimes of surprise sexual abuse and threat to a Carabineros official and requested, along with the Carabineros' prosecutor, the precautionary measures of prohibition of approaching the victims, national custody, and monthly signature. Santiago, RD, February 13, 2025. The District Attorney's Office of Santiago obtained a three-month preventive detention order as a coercive measure against two men whom they accuse of kidnapping, retention, and sexual abuse of two adolescents in this city. The coercive measure was imposed following the request made by the investigating agency to the Permanent Attention Services Judicial Office of this judicial district, which, presided over today by Judge Yiberty Polanco Herrand, imposed the deprivation of liberty against Adrián Castillo Vargas (Vitico), 23 years old, and Ove Emmanuel González Rubén (Manuel), 20 years old. The District Attorney's Office of Santiago, through the Unit for Comprehensive Attention to Victims of Gender-Based Violence, Family Violence, and Sexual Crimes, was involved in the process, locating and recovering the 12- and 13-year-old victims, after which they were subjected to physical and psychological evaluations to determine the degree of impact they suffered. The teenage girls were reported missing after they left their respective residences in the La Otra Banda sector. The prosecution agency managed to locate and arrest the two suspects in the El Paraiso sector of the Esperanza municipality, in the Valverde province, where they are being held. The Public Prosecutor's Office describes in the request for measures, which was accepted by the court this Thursday, that the accused contacted the minors through a video game messaging or chat system, from which, under deceit, they made promises of gifts to create a false illusion and lure them. The Public Prosecutor's Office charges González Rubén with violating articles 3091, 330, and 355 of the Dominican Penal Code, modified by Law 2497 on Gender Violence, which defines gender violence, sexual abuse, and the illicit transfer of a minor. He also indicates transgression of Article 396, letters B and C, of the Code for the System of Protection and Fundamental Rights of Children, Girls, and Adolescents, Law 13603. In the meantime, Castillo Vargas is charged with violating Articles 3091, 354, 330, and 331 of the Dominican Penal Code, modified by Law 2497 on Gender Violence, for committing gender violence, sexual aggression, sexual assault, and illegal transfer against a minor. He is also charged with violating Article 396, letters B and C, of the Code for the Protection and Fundamental Rights of Children, Girls, and Adolescents (Law 13603). The court ordered the accused to serve preventive detention at the Mao Correction and Rehabilitation Center (CCR) in Valverde Province.

data.text: Suspected Abuse in Morillo They didn't want to take the complaint because there was no internet. Because of this, there are two people detained. A relative of the minor spoke on Que Pasa al Mediodía. A new case of suspected sexual abuse has shaken the locality of Morillo, a municipality that already had a history of scandals during the administration of former Intendant Atta Gerala. The case came to light when the minor's mother and brothers noticed changes in his behavior. After a conversation in which the young person burst into tears, he began to recount the events that had allegedly taken place in December. According to the testimony of a relative, the 15-year-old minor was a victim of a violent episode while returning from a meeting with friends. Everything started on Saturday night, or so the mother had been observing that the young person wasn't well, had strange behavior, looked sad, she reported in the program Que Pasa al Mediodía. The minor detailed that a white car intercepted him on the road and that he was forcibly taken into the car by four individuals, two of whom he recognized and are currently detained. When he was taken into the car, he doesn't know how it happened, but he fell asleep, explained the complainant, who added that the young man presented gaps in his memory. I imagine they gave him something because he doesn't remember anything else, she said. When he woke up, the minor found himself in Villa Las Rosas, at the home of one of the detained individuals. Two of the implicated individuals work in the municipality, one is a councilor, while the other was a secretary of government during Atta Gerala's administration. Yesterday, my relatives went to request that they be severed because they cannot continue to have people like those in the municipality, expressed the complainant, who also revealed that the minor received threats to keep silent. He woke up the next day with a man by his side who told him to go to the house and not to tell his parents what had happened. The family attempted to formalize the complaint, but they encountered obstacles due to technical problems in the online system. When we went to make the complaint, they didn't want to take it because there was no internet, because they told us that complaints are made online, explained. The authorities have initiated the corresponding investigations, while the minor's family claims justice and immediate disconnection of the implicated from their public positions.

The trial against a suspect accused of the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access began this Wednesday morning at the Criminal Court 1. The victim, a 9-year-old minor at the time, was abused in April 2023 in the neighborhood located at 96 and 67, where the defendant resided a few meters away from the victim's family home. The prosecution, led by Marcos Bendersky, accuses the defendant of forcibly taking the girl to a store. After throwing her to the ground and pulling down her pants, he committed vaginal penetration. This was confirmed by the medical reports made at the hospital on the child. This morning, the victim's mother and a sister testified, who the girl told that night about the abuse. According to her testimony, the girl was distressed and only managed to recount the abuse when she was at her sister's house for a slumber party with her nephew. In turn, the minor's father also testified before the court, composed of judges Luciana Irigoyen Testa, Ernesto Juliano, and Nicolás Lamberti, and stated that he found out about what happened when he returned home after work. He spoke directly with his daughter and begged her to try to remember any characteristic of her attacker. The girl assured him that her attacker was wearing a white Bermudas, a pink sweater, and tattoos on his face. The father, according to his account, was able to identify one of his neighbors, a 30-year-old man from Córdoba, as the alleged perpetrator of the abuse and acknowledged that, in that moment, he only wanted to take justice into his own hands. While the mother and sister were taking the minor to the hospital, the father and his brother-in-law went to the house of the person pointed out by the girl and began a fierce fight between the two. According to the father's statement, at one point the alleged perpetrator went to his room and grabbed a baby sleeping in a crib by the neck. It was his own child, and he told me to stop hitting him because I was going to kill him, he claimed, asserting that at that moment he threw the little one to the ground and as he bent down to pick him up, he took advantage to escape and take refuge in a neighbor's house. Later, the accused was arrested by the police and is currently housed in Batán prison. On Tuesday at 9 am, it will be the second day of the trial and the testimony of a large number of witnesses has been reviewed.

Crime and Justice Section Friday, February 14, 2025, 0949 The Civil and Penal Chamber of the Superior Justice Court of Murcia (TSJMU) confirmed the sentence of the Provincial Court of Murcia that convicted a man to 13 years and 6 months in prison for a continuous sex crime with carnal access to a 16-year-old minor, with the use of violence and intimidation. According to the sentence, the defendant took advantage of the minor, daughter of a friend, staying at his home after school to subject her to repeated sexual abuse, threatening her with harming her family if she revealed what happened. The defendant would take her to the bathroom and force her to perform oral sex, making the girl insert his penis into her mouth, then grabbing her head, preventing her from withdrawing, threatening to tell her mother she had misbehaved if she said anything, and telling her he had a gun and would kill her, her family, and her cat if she said anything, adding that he had cameras set up all over his house, as recorded in the judicial resolution. And it is declared proven that the minor suffered repeated episodes of abuse over the months and has needed psychological treatment. The Chamber dismisses the defense's arguments, which argued, first of all, an error in the appreciation of the evidence, questioning the credibility of the victim's testimony. According to the judges, the probative exploitation of the testimony of the minor presented as a victim has been carried out by the trial court in accordance with the general criteria or parameters of reliability indicated by the Jurisprudence. They add that there are no substantial contradictions in the minor's account, who has maintained coherence in her statements at all times, and emphasize that the mother and brother have provided objective data that corroborates the circumstances in which the aggression occurred. The Tribunal also does not accept the defendant's petition to reduce the sentence to six years of imprisonment due to the improper application of the violent or intimidating modality, and considers the imposed sentence justified by the Provincial Court of Murcia. In the present case, the proven facts describe with perfect clarity the accused's use of the minor both physically (he grabbed her by the head and forced her to perform oral sex) and psychologically (he threatened to kill her, her family, and her cat if she told anyone, and he had cameras set up throughout the house), concludes the sentence. In addition to the prison sentence, he will be required to serve a seven-year period of supervised release upon his release from prison, as well as a special incapacitation to engage in any profession or occupation involving contact with minors for a period of 17 years and 6 months. He is also ordered to pay an indemnification of 10,000 euros to the victim as compensation for moral damages, as well as a prohibition on approaching within 300 meters for 20 years and 6 months and one day. The decision is not final, and an appeal for cassation can be filed before the Supreme Court.
