Argentine Tribunal Issues International Arrest Warrant for Burmese Military Leader for Rohingya Genocide Bangkok, 14 Feb (EFE). An Argentine tribunal has issued an international arrest warrant for the leader of the Burmese military junta, Min Aung Hlaing, for his alleged involvement in the Rohingya genocide and other crimes against humanity allegedly committed by the Army against the Rohingya Muslim minority, reports this Thursday the NGO that prompted the lawsuit. It is a historic step towards justice that brings a ray of hope for the Rohingya who have suffered decades of genocide, seeing how their families and culture were destroyed with impunity, said in a statement Tun Khin, President of the Rohingya Organization in the UK (BROUK). The NGO, which filed the lawsuit in November 2019 in the federal courts of Buenos Aires, stated that the Argentine justice issued the order against Min Aung Hlaing and 22 other military commanders on Wednesday. Those accused face crimes that include genocide and others specified in the Argentine Penal Code, such as aggravated murder, sexual abuse, and torture. This brave decision sends a clear signal to Min Aung Hlaing and other military personnel that no one is above the law. Ultimately, they will have to be judged for the indescribable suffering they have caused not only to generations of Rohingya, but to all victims of military brutality in Myanmar, remarks Tun Khin. The case, independent of those being studied by the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice, both in The Hague, was presented in Argentina based on the principle of universal jurisdiction for crimes such as genocide and crimes against humanity, recalls the BROUK. The brutal military operation launched by the Burmese Army in August 2017 against the Rohingya population in the northern state of Rakhine, in this country and where this minority has been settled for centuries, motivated the exodus of more than 720,000 Rohingya. 0.000 refugees to neighboring Bangladesh, where thousands of Rohingya had been displaced in previous years. The UN estimates that during this campaign, which a report described as ethnic cleansing with genocidal marks, at least 10,000 people were killed, while hundreds of communities were destroyed by intentional fires. In November of last year, the ICC prosecutor requested an arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing for the deportation and persecution of the Rohingya, among other crimes against humanity committed between August 25, 2017, and December 31, 2017, by Myanmar's armed forces and other authorities. While the ICC judges still need to determine if this request meets the necessary standard to approve the issuance of the requested arrest warrant against the Burmese general, the Argentine court's decision has automatically triggered a request for the prosecutor to issue the orders, the NGO reports. General Min Aung Hlaing led the 2021 February 1 military coup that ended a decade of democratic transition and opened a spiral of violence that has exacerbated the decades-long insurgency, with thousands of young people joining new armed groups that fight against the Army.

A human trafficking ring dismantled in Zaragoza for sexual exploitation and drug trafficking. The victims were forced to work almost around the clock, every day of the week, with no choice of clients. Agents from the National Police have dismantled a criminal organization dedicated to human trafficking for sexual exploitation and drug trafficking in Zaragoza. Four people have been detained, accused of luring vulnerable women into prostitution under extreme conditions. The investigation began after a woman reported being lured from her country of origin with false promises of a job in Spain. Once in Zaragoza, she was forced into prostitution under the coercion of the detained individuals, with no possibility of escape from that situation. The victims were required to hand over a percentage of their earnings and pay an abusive rent where they lived in deplorable conditions. In some cases, they were also forced to supply narcotics to clients. Investigations carried out by the UCRIF of the Zaragoza Border and Foreigners Brigade led to the detention of three people in the Aragonese capital as suspected perpetrators of various crimes related to prostitution, drug trafficking, and human trafficking. On February 6, during the search of an apartment used as a brothel in the Delicias neighborhood, agents located and freed eight foreign women in an irregular situation, who were also engaged in prostitution in exploitative conditions. Additionally, substances intended for the consumption of the victims as well as for sale to clients were seized, along with key documentation, passports, accounting books, and activity control sheets. Subsequently, on February 10, in collaboration with the Provincial Brigade of Immigration and Borders of Seville, a fourth person was detained, suspected to be in charge of the brothel in Zaragoza.

On February 3, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele received U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, where they reaffirmed their commitments to strengthen relations between the two countries through the signing of a contentious agreement to send U.S. criminals to Salvadoran prisons in exchange for a per-inmate tariff. This unprecedented agreement explains how the needs of the United States and El Salvador, despite being very different, found a common solution. On one hand, the United States has a massive prison population, which becomes increasingly difficult to maintain. This difficulty is deepened by the rise in inflation over the past years, as well as the new policy of Donald Trump to reduce public spending. On the other hand, El Salvador has a top-notch penitentiary system with a large capacity to detain criminals, although the economic resources to maintain it are becoming increasingly scarce. Therefore, each tariff paid by the United States for each detainee is a significant economic aid to the Salvadoran penitentiary system. However, Bukele seems to be taking advantage of the opportunities presented by the new Trump Administration on one hand, the attempt to reduce costs from the US government is a clear advantage for El Salvador, as the United States, by sending its prisoners to the Central American country, would save thousands of dollars and reduce its prison population. On the other hand, this new agreement is a clear example of Trump's preference for strengthening US bilateral relations with its allies, rather than strengthening the US position in other international organizations or forums. U.S. inmates would be sent to the Center for Counter-Terrorism Detention (CECOT), the largest prison in all of Latin America, which is far from reaching its maximum capacity of inmates. CECOT houses criminals from MS13 and other gangs primarily, but with the arrival of U.S. inmates, a new criminal group gains prominence, the Aragua Train. The Venezuelan-born mega-crime syndicate has rapidly expanded throughout South America, with a presence in Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Bolivia, Chile, and Brazil. However, it has also expanded northward to various locations across the United States, with operatives of the Aragua Train arrested for building a criminal network of narcotics trafficking and human trafficking, concentrated in the states of Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Florida, and New Jersey. The presence of the Aragua Train in the United States should not come as a surprise with the start of the Venezuelan exodus in 2018, when more than a million migrants settled in the North American giant, becoming a window of opportunity for the mega-criminal organization to expand its operations northward. Consequently, former President Joe Biden declared the Aragua Train as a transnational criminal organization, while Trump declared the group as a terrorist organization. In this manner, the CECOT would harbor criminals from two major threats to international security, responsible for illicit activities such as human trafficking, narcotics trafficking, kidnapping, murder, and extortion. It appears that both the United States and El Salvador have assumed that, today, security is no longer a solely internal matter, but rather that there are transnational threats that deserve regional cooperation among states to combat them. Both countries have shown a unprecedented will to cooperate with each other, which could be the starting point for future agreements, whether in areas related to international security or other matters. President Bukele was categorical on social media X The most extraordinary migratory agreement in the world. Exactly, the impulse for cooperation did not take long to materialize, as both countries have signed another agreement in the nuclear energy field, with the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding on Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation (NCMOU). Another clear signal of Washington's initiatives to solidify strategic ties with its allies in vital areas, such as energy security. However, it is worth questioning whether this agreement between El Salvador and the United States aims to find solutions to each country's internal needs or rather responds to the search for a lasting bilateral relationship that seeks to strengthen itself with the arrival of Donald Trump at the White House.

Florida's Governor, Republican Ron DeSantis, signed two broad laws on Thursday that toughen conditions for undocumented immigrants and facilitate in this state the implementation of President of the US, Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda. The bills establish harsher penalties for undocumented immigrants who commit crimes, stricter application requirements for local officials, and changes to the contentious state migrant transport program (the governor will no longer have unilateral power to authorize them). One of the contentious aspects that form part of the laws signed today involves the automatic imposition of the death penalty for undocumented immigrants found guilty of capital offenses, such as murder or child sexual abuse. Read also Condemn Two Women to Rob and Kill Nicaraguan in Las Vegas According to some experts, this aspect will surely face legal complaints, because, as pointed out by some Democratic lawmakers in the plenary session of both chambers, the US Supreme Court ruled decades ago that mandatory and non-discretionary sentences of the jury were unconstitutional. The laws, approved this Thursday in the framework of an extraordinary session of the State Legislature, also contemplate the creation of a State Immigration Control Board, which will be composed of the governor, the commissioner of agriculture, the attorney general, and the state financial director This coordinating board will coordinate legal and security actions with federal agencies and will have a $250 million fund to distribute among local law enforcement agencies that assist federal efforts in this field, in order to stimulate cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). It may interest you that the U.S. Attorney is suing New York for allowing undocumented migrants to obtain driver's licenses. The texts establish the creation of new state crimes for illegal entry or re-entry into Florida, elevating unlicensed driving to a serious crime for undocumented immigrants. In the same way, it criminalizes as a crime the entry into Florida of undocumented migrants over 18 years old who enter the state after entering the United States evading or avoiding inspection or inspection by immigration agents, and will be subject to a nine-month prison sentence. The matriculations of undocumented students as residents are being removed from public universities in the state, and all local sheriff's offices have until April to enroll in the federal 287(g) program, which grants authority to local agents to perform tasks belonging to federal immigration agencies. Today, the Florida Legislature has approved the strongest legislation to combat illegal immigration in any state in the country, said DeSantis in a press conference shortly before signing the bills, accompanied by the president of the Senate, Ben Albritton, and the head of the state House of Representatives, Daniel Pérez. The Court of Appeal in Seville has sentenced a male for the crimes of creating child pornography involving a minor under 16 years old and exhibiting obscene behavior in the presence of minors after he lured a 13-year-old minor into exchanging sexual images and videos with them, imposing among other penalties seven years of prohibition on using the WhatsApp application and the website canalchat.org. In a judgment issued on February 6 of last year and recorded by Europa Press, the First Section of the Court of Appeal in Seville declares proven, by the explicit admission of the accused as a result of an agreement of concurrence between his defense, the Public Prosecutor's Office, and the private accuser, that between March and May 2021, this 49-year-old male identified as Javier Á.T.G., with no prior convictions computable for recidivism, used false profiles created on the canalchat.org website in which he pretended to be a 15-year-old youth. Through these false profiles, according to the account of proven facts recognized by the accused, he contacted a minor born on February 1, 2008, and, despite informing the minor that she was 13 years old, provided her with his phone number to contact her through WhatsApp with the intention of requesting that she send images and videos of a sexual nature to satisfy his lustful desires, as well as send him sexual content. The accused thus succeeded in having the minor send him explicit sexual images (...) that were sent through the temporary photo website, which operates without records and anonymously, allowing the selection of the desired image duration, between one and 60 minutes for the time-view option, or just five seconds if the express-view option to load the photo is selected, according to the condemnatory sentence after the defendant admitted to the incriminating facts. ADDITIONAL VIDEO CALLS According to the sentence, after revealing her true age, the accused even made video calls to the minor in which he could see her masturbating. The sentence adds that on May 27, 2021, with prior judicial authorization, a search was conducted at the accused's residence in Badajoz, where his mobile phone and computer used to commit the criminal acts were seized. The narrative of facts adds that as a consequence of these acts, the minor victim of them has been under psychological treatment from May 2021 to June 2022, suffering significant emotional distress and presenting a depressed mood, frequent crying, floating anxiety accompanied by occasional episodes of greater intensity, feelings of guilt, and frequent tension headaches. On the other hand, it is acknowledged that at the time of the events, the accused suffered from cocaine use disorder, which resulted in a slight impairment of his volitional capacity, as well as the fact that he has paid 10,000 euros corresponding to the total amount claimed by the private prosecution in concept of civil liability.PENALTIES IMPOSEDGiven the case, and by express agreement of the accused as a result of the agreement reached between his defense, the Public Prosecution and the private prosecution, the court sentences Javier Á.T.G. to two years in prison for a crime of child pornography creation involving a minor under 16 years old and a crime of obscene exhibition in front of minors, with the mitigating circumstances of damage repair and drug addiction, as well as 1,800 euros in fine. However, his prison sentence is suspended as long as he does not reoffend within a certain period of time. Additionally, the Court imposes seven years of prohibition on approaching the victim or communicating with her and seven years of prohibition on access to WhatsApp and the website canalchat.org, eight years of special incapacitation for a profession or trade that involves direct contact with minors, and five years of supervised freedom.

Arrested for Reckless Driving Near a School in Málaga The 26-year-old man, accelerated sharply near a pedestrian crossing, forcing several parents with children to step aside to avoid being run over. An 80-year-old grandfather from Fuengirola was sentenced to 10 years in prison for sexual abuse of his two granddaughters who were left paralyzed.The Local Police in Málaga have arrested a 26-year-old man as the suspected perpetrator of a traffic safety offense for driving with manifest recklessness. The incident occurred around 9:00 am on February 11, when a patrol was conducting surveillance and traffic regulation duties near a school in the Puerto de la Torre district. At that moment, one of the agents observed a dispute between a woman and the driver of a vehicle. Immediately, the individual stopped the vehicle and got out to approach the woman, yelling, as explained by the Local Police in a statement After these events, the officer regulating the traffic intervened with the parties, attempting to calm the situation and asking the man to park his vehicle correctly in order to avoid obstructing traffic and facilitating the passage of pedestrians heading to the city center. The individual took advantage of this and abruptly and unexpectedly started the vehicle at high speed, forcing most of the pedestrians, who were mostly parents with minor children crossing the pedestrian crossing, to stop in their tracks to avoid being run over. The driver, instead of slowing down, continued driving down the street at high speed, prompting a group of cyclists to get out of the way and stop to avoid being run over. The police officers in the area were unable to catch up to him, but they were able to provide a description of the individual and the vehicle's details. The day after the events occurred, the agents proceeded to their detention for a crime of reckless driving, putting road users in concrete danger. The crime of driving with manifest recklessness is punished with prison sentences of six months to two years and the deprivation of the right to drive motor vehicles and motorcycles for a period of more than one year and up to six years. Two detained for robbing a taxi driver's mobile phone and money. On the other hand, the Local Police recently reported the detention of two people aged 22 and 39 as suspected authors of a robbery with violence against a taxi driver's mobile phone and money. In the same statement, the police explained that these two individuals are also allegedly involved in another attempted robbery of a minor, a shoplifting in a supermarket, and possession of several objects of dubious origin.

Case against former judge Daniel Tobares for sexual abuse: when will the trial take placeFormer judge Daniel Tobares, who served in the Second Circuit in Roca, will face a public trial in March next year on a case filed against him as a result of a complaint for sexual abuse. See also the Case of Daniel Tobares: how the case against the judge accused of rape is advancing.The public oral debate will take place from March 5 to 11 of this year, in extensive sessions scheduled from 9 am to 2:30 pm. It will be a public oral trial for the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access. In the event of being found guilty, the penalty for this crime ranges from 6 to 15 years in prison. Tobares arrives at this trial as a result of a complaint filed on April 5, 2021, and labeled as a crime of sexual abuse with carnal access. In the last few months, the advances in the investigation, which included psychiatric and psychological evaluations, determined that the defendant is in a condition to face a trial. The evaluations were necessary because in March 2023, the defendant suffered two severe head injuries that left him in a critical state, which delayed the deadlines for the trial of the case. The lawyers of former Judge Daniel Tobares, accused of rape, also resigned from the case. The same year, in August 2023, lawyers Óscar Pineda and Pablo Iribarren, who were the defenders of the accused at the time, resigned from the case without providing many explanations. Currently, the defense attorney in charge is Juan Luis Vincenty. The fact that led to the trial The complaint that initiated the case was made by a young law student from Cipolletti, who filed it at the Third Police Station in Roca. The investigation was handled by the prosecutors of the Fourth Circuit, based in Cipolletti, to avoid any possible contamination due to the years of action of the accused. The Public Ministry stated that on April 10, 2021, between 1:30 am and 4 am, Tobares met the young woman at a central candy shop. There, they shared a moment and then offered to take her to her home. However, he took her to his own residence and, taking advantage of the fact that the young woman was not in a position to defend herself, he abused her. Among other evidence, the young woman's clinical history at the López Lima Hospital, planimetric data of the place where the alleged events took place, the psychological expertise carried out on the victim, as well as photos and telephone conversations collected by the Judicial Office of Telephone Interceptions were incorporated.

This regulation contains serious violations of human rights. Among its provisions, it includes the obligation to report to the immediate superior about intimate relationships with nationals or foreigners, residents or not in the country, or the prohibition of having relationships with anyone who assumes positions contrary to the Cuban Revolution, or the prohibition of driving any means of transportation, or the prohibition of participating in public social events, among other directives that the United Nations has considered to be constitutive of forced labor, indicating at the same time that forced labor is one of the forms of modern slavery. Also see the third United Nations complaint in 2024 about this modern slavery exercised by the Government of Cuba International condemnations on slavery and Resolution 368 of 2020 of the Mincex The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child (conclusion report of June 16, 2022, point 34c and 35c 1(_ftn1)), United Nations Human Rights Mandates (letter of November 16, 2019 2(_ftn2), letter of November 2, 2023 3(_ftn3)), Human Rights Watch (July 23, 2020 4(_ftn4)), Human Rights Foundation (August 22, 2022 5(_ftn5), June 16, 2020 6(_ftn6)), Prisoners Defenders (May 8, 2019 7(_ftn7), August 24, 2020 8(_ftn8), January 25, 2022 9(_ftn9) and January 4, 2024 10(_ftn10)), the European Parliament (resolutions of June 10, 2021 11(_ftn11), September 16, 2021 12(_ftn12), July 16, 2023 13(_ftn13) and February 2024 expected) and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (annual report 2020 14(_ftn14), annual report 202115(_ftn15) and annual report 202216(_ftn16)), among others, have issued condemnations for forced labor, modern slavery or servitude, on multiple occasions against the Cuban Government due to serious human rights violations in international missions of Cuban civilian workers, either by the State or Cuban companies (also by the State). Documented reports detail persecution, threats, confiscation of passports and academic diplomas at destination to prevent desertion, harassment, and sexual violence (43% of testimonies) directed towards professionals by Mission Chiefs, including doctors, nurses, artists, musicians, playwrights, athletes, architects, professors, and other Cuban civilians. These professionals are also subjected to the extraction of 85% of their salaries by their government and are prohibited from re-entering Cuba for 8 years in the event of leaving their job, or if they do not return to Cuba immediately upon completion. The fundamental laws that uphold forced labor are all in place in Cuba, in fact, through various laws. On one hand, there is Article 176 of the Cuban Penal Code, which has penalties of up to 8 years of deprivation of liberty for workers who leave their job or those who do not return to Cuba immediately upon its completion. On the other hand, there is the Official Regulation of Missions, which has the character of a law and has countless restrictions, unnumbered. It is Law Resolution 368 of 2020, which applies to these cooperators and professionals, and which obliges them, literally, to inform their immediate superior about their romantic relationships with nationals or foreigners, residents or not in the country, or prohibits participating in public social events without proper authorization or maintaining friendships or other types of relationships with people who assume positions contrary to the Cuban Revolution. It maliciously and unsubstantially concludes that Mr. Combs is a monster and an embodiment of Lucifer with many similarities to Jeffrey Epstein, the document shared by the medium Six Paige states. Value of the accusations The lawsuit is worth nothing more and nothing less than $100 million, and it emphasizes the statement made by the Los Angeles County Forensic Office in 2008, which declared that Kim died of natural causes. INTERPOL Washington and the National Central Bureau (NCB) of Ottawa signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Thursday to strengthen collaboration between the United States and Canada in the fight against the Aragua Train (TdA), a transnational criminal organization originating from Venezuela and increasingly present in North America. The signing of the agreement took place in the framework of the INTERPOL Central Bureau Chiefs Conference in Lyon, France. The agreement establishes a strengthened framework of cooperation, allowing for more agile exchange of criminal intelligence, joint investigation development, and strengthening of border security mechanisms to curb the illicit activities of the group in the United States and Canada. Today, we have taken a significant step in the fight to eradicate the TdA in the United States, declared Jeffrey A. Grimming, director of INTERPOL Washington. By pooling our law enforcement resources, the US and Canada are committed to ensuring that the Transnational Organized Crime (TdA) will not find a safe haven in any of our territories. Together, as partners, we will work coordinately to dismantle the organization and remove its criminal operatives from our communities. (Infobae URL Piarristeguy) On her part, Marie-Josée Homsy, director of the NCB Ottawa, highlighted the importance of international cooperation in combating organized crime. Confronting transnational criminal organizations such as the TdA requires international cooperation, she asserted. This agreement is an example of the solid daily collaboration between Canadian and US authorities, as well as INTERPOL's scope and capacity. Working together, we can dismantle criminal networks, protect our communities, and reaffirm our commitment to the rule of law. The agreement establishes concrete actions within the framework of INTERPOL, including the strengthening of operational data exchange and best practices, coordination of investigations and joint activities against TdA, and implementation of mechanisms to detect, prevent, and respond to its transnational illicit activities. In addition to signing the agreement, INTERPOL Washington participated in bilateral and multilateral meetings with strategic partners in the fight against TdA. Grimming also delivered a speech on the efforts of the United States to dismantle the organization, sharing strategies and best practices with representatives from more than 140 countries. Héctor Guerrero Flores, better known as the Niño Guerrero, is the number one of the Tren de Aragua and is currently being sought after across all of South America (Infobae Peru Composition). From its operational headquarters in Venezuela, the Tren de Aragua in just a few years transitioned from being a prison gang to a powerful criminal organization with tentacles in several countries across Latin America. In Peru, it was classified as the number one enemy. In Colombia, it has clashed with guerrilla groups and paramilitary groups for control of the borders. And in Chile, it has managed to establish itself in the north of the country and is considered a threat to national security. This gang has a wide-ranging portfolio of crimes, making its sources of financing multiple. Among the businesses it operates are human trafficking, migrant trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, robbery, and drug trafficking. According to InSight Crime, the prosperity of these criminal activities is partly due to the long periods of impunity that the regime of Nicolás Maduro has fostered in Venezuela.

Detectives from the Sexual Crimes Investigation Brigade (Brisex) in Chillán arrested a 42-year-old dentist of Colombian nationality for the crime of sexual abuse, which allegedly occurred against a 17-year-old girl inside a medical consultation in the San Carlos commune. Sub-commissar Elizabeth Pereira Rivas of Brisex Chillán stated that this case originated from a complaint filed last week at the San Carlos Criminal Investigation Brigade, which stated that the victim, a 17-year-old girl, while attending a dental consultation, was treated by a professional and repeatedly suffered the crime. According to the officer, following the complaint, the Public Prosecutor's Office issued an order to investigate this specialized brigade, so various investigative procedures were carried out, which allowed establishing the existence of the crime and the alleged participation of the accused, as an author. With all these precedents, the prosecution managed an arrest order against this man, which was executed by detectives from this specialized brigade. Therefore, he was placed at the disposal of the Guarantee Court for his respective detention control and formalization, said Subcomissary Pereira Rivas, who stated that the accused already has a penal record for similar acts. Investigative proceedings were carried out with personnel from the Sexual Crimes Brigade (BRISEX) of the Investigations Police of Chillán. A 90-day investigation period was set.

The bills establish harsher penalties for undocumented immigrants who commit crimes, stricter application requirements for local officials, and changes to the controversial state migrant transportation program (the governor will no longer have unilateral power to authorize them). The laws approved today in the framework of an extraordinary session of the state Legislature also contemplate the creation of a State Immigration Control Board, composed of the governor, the agriculture commissioner, the state attorney general, and the state financial director. Under Section 18-6-401 of the Colorado Revised Code, a person commits child abuse when they cause an injury to the life or health of a child, or allow a child to be placed in a situation that is unreasonable and poses a threat of injury to the life or health of the child, or are involved in a pattern of continuous conduct that results in malnutrition, inadequate medical care, cruel punishment, abuse, or an accumulation of injuries that ultimately results in the death of a child or severe bodily injury to a child. If there are no severe injuries as a result, child abuse is a misdemeanor offense that carries up to 364 days in prison and $1,000 in fines. Otherwise, child abuse is a felony offense that carries 2 to 16 years in prison and $2,000 to $750,000 in fines. In this article, our top Denver, Colorado criminal defense attorneys discuss the following topics on child abuse laws. I also listened to our informative podcast Learn about Colorado's Mandatory Reporting Laws for Child Abuse. Acts that constitute child abuse in Colorado The acts considered child abuse according to Colorado Revised Statutes 18-6-401 include (but are not limited to) Causing a life-threatening or health-threatening injury to a child, such as physical abuse or emotional abuse Permitting a child to be placed in a situation that poses a life-threatening or health-threatening risk to the child Engaging in a pattern of conduct that results in malnutrition, inadequate medical attention, cruel punishment, abuse, or a cumulative effect that ultimately results in a child's death or severe bodily harm Driving under the influence (DUI) or driving while ability impaired (DWAI) with a child in the vehicle Performing or permitting female genital mutilation (infibulation of a girl's labia, vulva, or clitoris or her labia majora) or Allowing a child to be present near controlled substance manufacturing or near certain drugs and precursors (such as phenylpropanolamine, pseudoephedrine, methamphetamine, and isomers) To be found guilty of child abuse in Colorado, prosecutors must prove any of the following elements of the offense beyond a reasonable doubt You caused a life-threatening or health-threatening injury to a child, You permitted a child to be placed in a situation that posed a life-threatening or health-threatening risk to the child, or You engaged in a pattern of conduct that resulted in malnutrition, inadequate medical attention, cruel punishment, abuse, or a cumulative effect that ultimately resulted in a child's death or severe bodily harm. 2. What are the penalties under Section 18-6-401 of the Colorado Revised Statutes?The consequences of child abuse in Colorado vary widely, depending on the victim's age, whether the perpetrator acted with knowledge, recklessness, or negligence, and whether the abuse resulted in injuries or death. The man confessed to the crime and said that he killed her after she hit him in the face. A brutal crime shocks Brazil. João das Graças Pachola, an evangelical pastor, confessed to the murder of Stefany Vitória Teixeira Ferreira, a 13-year-old girl who had been missing since Sunday. According to his statement to the Civil Police, the man killed the young girl after she hit him in the face. Stefany's body was found on Tuesday in the municipality of Ribeirão das Neves, the same day that Pachola was detained. The motivation, without a doubt, is cruelty and hatred. He said that he became nervous and hanged her immediately before burying her, said Police Chief Ingrid Estevam. The girl left her house on Sunday afternoon to visit a friend, but never arrived there. According to the police investigation, the pastor offered to drive her During the trip, he tried to do something with her, and we're waiting for the reports to determine what happened, Estevam explained. We're still waiting for the forensic results to determine if the victim suffered any sexual abuse. The case advanced thanks to the complaint of a couple who witnessed a suspicious scene on a rural road. As they reported, they saw a young girl jump out of an HB20 car before falling to the ground. The driver got out, grabbed her violently, and threw her back into the vehicle, the police chief explained. In the struggle, Stefany lost her shoes, which were key in the identification. From the car's license plate number, the agents identified Pachola and discovered that he had also been missing since Sunday. After a 24-hour search, they found him in a house in Contagem. During his detention, he confessed to the crime and revealed where he had left the minor's body. The pastor had a history of marital problems, although he had no prior criminal records. A year ago, he had closed his church, which his mother-in-law attended. She had asked for help for her daughter two years ago because she was having nightmares, but he refused, the police revealed. Pachola had a hearing this Wednesday at the 1st Penal and Jury Tribunal of Ribeirão das Neves, in which his preventive detention was confirmed. He is currently in the Antônio Dutra Ladeira prison. A total of 11 charges for sex crimes follow virtual approach to girls through social media platforms Discord, SnapChat and Instagram. INDIANAPOLIS, Indiana ( LMNDigital ) Are you one of the parents who constantly monitor your children's interactions on social media? If you haven't developed this habit yet, everything might change starting today. A 23-year-old man, who worked as a freelance lawyer in Marion County, faces 11 charges for sex crimes after a virtual approach to minors through social media platforms Discord, SnapChat and Instagram. His name is Guillermo Yanez and according to case 49D322502F4004925, which is currently in the Marion County Superior Court since February 12, 2025, allegedly disseminated lewd content, asked for photos without clothing, and indirectly bribed for sexual acts. The victims were between 11 and 15 years old. The first hearing took place on Thursday, February 13, 2025, and the trial has been scheduled for April 23 at 8:30 a.m. According to the records of the Indiana State Bar Association, the entity that accredits the exercise of the legal profession in this state, Guillermo Isaiah Yanez was admitted to practice law in Indiana on October 9, 2024. His license number 3907422 remains active and in good standing. According to the court's summary in the public registration document, the defendant was released on a $7,500 bond while awaiting trial. If found guilty, considering the charges brought against him in the state of Indiana's complaint, he could face more than 10 years in prison. Regarding crimes against minors through digital platforms, the U.S. Department of Justice's Criminal Division warns that both children and their parents must be aware that people are not always who they seem in virtual environments where identities can be easily fabricated. They also remind you that you can report a case of sexual exploitation or solicitation by calling 911 directly or through this link: report.cybertip.org. The agency shares the following recommendations for parents, guardians, caregivers, and educators to be proactive and prevent any sexual predator hidden behind a smartphone, tablet, or computer screen from harming children. Discuss online safety with the children and develop a plan with them before they participate in online interactive activities.Note: The translation aims to preserve the original meaning and tone of the text, using accurate and formal language to convey the seriousness of the issue. Establish clear guidelines, teach them to detect warning signs, and encourage open communication with you. Monitor children's internet use, including regularly reviewing their profiles and posts. Keep electronic devices in open and common areas of the home, setting time limits for their use. Review games, applications, and social media before children download or use them. Pay special attention to applications and websites with direct messaging, video chats, file uploads, and user anonymity, which are often favored by online child predators. Adjust privacy settings and use parental controls for online games, applications, social media, and electronic devices. Warn children to avoid sharing personal information, photos, and videos in public forums or with people they don't know in real life. Explain to your children that all published images will be permanently on the Internet. Teach your children about safety and the boundaries of their body, including the importance of saying NO to inappropriate requests both in the physical environment and in the virtual one. Be aware of possible signs of abuse, including changes in children's use of electronic devices, attempts to hide online activity, withdrawn behavior, outbursts of anger, anxiety, and depression. Encourage them to inform their parents, guardians, or another trusted adult if someone asks them to participate in sexual activities or other inappropriate behavior. Immediately report any suspicion of online grooming or child sexual exploitation by calling 911, contacting the FBI at fbi.gov, or filing a report with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) at 1-800-843-5678 or through this link report.cybertip.org.

Peruvian authorities announced the total dismantling of the Tren de Aragua, the Venezuelan-origin criminal organization that extended its illicit activities to several countries on the continent. The Peruvian National Police (PNP) confirmed that all leaders of the gang have been captured and are currently serving their sentence in Challapalca maximum-security prison. At this moment, we have the Tren de Aragua dismantled. As a criminal organization, in Peru, we have it totally dismantled. All leaders have fallen (are serving their sentence) in Challapalca, PNP General Aldo Ávila Novoa declared in an interview with RPP radio. The announcement followed a police operation in which 23 members of the group were detained, representing a significant blow to the organization's structure in the country. A non-traditional organized crime group Despite its dismantling in Peru, Ávila Novoa warned that the Aragua Train presents a very special behavior and an undefined structure. In collaboration with the Government of the United States, Peruvian authorities continue to analyze the internal organization of the gang, which, unlike other criminal groups, does not operate with a pyramidal or collegiate structure. The hypothesis that experts are handling is that the Aragua Train functions with differentiated levels of leadership, with leaders in different regions of the continent. Its presence has been detected in countries such as Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Spain, Brazil, Panama, the United States, and Costa Rica. A hard blow to crime in Peru The Aragua Train has been linked to various crimes in the region, including human trafficking, kidnappings, extortions, narcotics trafficking, and arms trafficking. The group's growth was fueled by the massive displacement of Venezuelan citizens due to the economic and political crisis in their country of origin. The capture of the leaders in Peru represents a significant advancement in the fight against this criminal network, although authorities remain vigilant about the possibility that other members may attempt to reorganize. We will continue working to ensure the country's security and prevent groups like this from operating on our territory again, concluded General Ávila Novoa. The Supreme Court has rejected the appeal filed by the defense of a man convicted of sexually abusing his two granddaughters in Fuengirola. In this way, the sentence imposed by the High Court of Justice of Andalusia, Ceuta, and Melilla (TSJA), is ratified, which set a penalty of 11 years and 6 months in prison for two consecutive crimes of sexual abuse of minors. Additionally, the aggressor must compensate each of the victims with 15,000 euros and will not be able to approach or communicate with them for 10 years. According to Málaga Hoy, the abuses began when the girls were 6 and 9 years old. According to the sentence, the grandfather took advantage of family trust to be alone with them, either when their parents left them in his house or when he visited them. The judicial resolution highlights that the aggressor took advantage of his status as a grandfather, driven by an evident desire to satisfy his sexual desires. The episodes of abuse included touching and sexual assaults that lasted for a decade. On some occasions, the eldest of the victims confronted her aggressor and told him to stop, but he threatened her that if she spoke out, something very bad would happen to her. Meanwhile, the younger sister tried to avoid being seen naked by the grandfather by locking herself in the bathroom with the lock. The victims kept silent for a decade, until the father of the young women decided to file a complaint about the incidents. The sentence describes how the abuses occurred at different times and locations, from the sofa while watching TV to the bedroom where they slept. In the case of the eldest sister, the abuses continued until she moved to study abroad. The court notes that the perpetrator sought moments to satisfy his sexual desires, especially taking advantage of the grandmother's absence when she went out to shop. Additionally, it points out that the victims, being so young, were unaware of what was happening to them and were manipulated by their grandfather, who asked them not to tell anyone because it was a secret between them.The Provincial Court of Málaga initially sentenced the perpetrator to four years in prison and five years of supervised freedom. However, both the prosecution and the private accuser appealed the sentence, requesting an increase in the penalty. The High Court of Justice of Andalusia partially upheld the appeal, increasing the sentence to five years and nine months in prison.Following a new review, the Supreme Court has ratified the sentence of 11 years and six months in prison, also confirming the prohibition on approaching or communicating with their victims for 10 years.

The abuse occurred on July 16, 2022, in the Las Aralias neighborhood, in Guácimo, Limón, when the girl was just 5 months old. The suspect was arrested on the same day, but after serving 6 months of preventive detention, he was released. I have felt indignation for months over what happened, and even more so now that they let him go free, knowing that he mocks us on the street, Mora said. The mother assures that the 3-year-old girl is currently doing well, but with injuries that could affect her as an adult. On the other hand, Mora fears for the safety of other children in the community, as she claims that the suspected abuser had problems with drugs. I am worried about other children who may be put in danger by him, he says. Mora expressed his dissatisfaction with the judicial system, stating that he feels the case of his daughter was not given the importance it deserved. I feel that the judges did not pay much attention to my daughter's case and it hurts me a lot because it was not a fair justice, since she was just an innocent and defenseless 5-month-old girl, he laments. Despite this and after appealing the case, the authorities rescheduled a trial for the end of this month, where it will be determined if new measures will be imposed on the suspect. The Attorney General's Office of Justice of the State of Mexico carried out the closure of 169 businesses of the type bars and snack bars, as well as apprehending 26 people, in 27 municipalities of the state as part of the Operation Atarraya. The results of this operation were carried out on the night of Friday, December 13, and Saturday, December 14, in joint actions with the National Guard, the Mexican Army, the Ministry of Security and Citizen Protection, the State Security Ministry, the National Anti-Kidnapping Coordination, and the Civil Protection. Operation Atarraya carried out simultaneous operations in Metepec, San Mateo Atenco, Toluca, Zinacantepec, in which 65 packages of cocaine, 20 packages of crystal, and 26 packages of marijuana were secured. The State Attorney's Office reported that business establishments were seized. On the other hand, it was detailed that victims of human trafficking, as well as minors who went to these establishments to consume alcoholic beverages, were identified and assisted.

A 73-year-old former pediatric surgeon is awaiting trial in prison in France, accused of sexually abusing 299 children between 1989 and 2014. According to the investigation, the majority of the victims were under 15 years old. The case is expected to be the largest child abuse trial in French history, aiming to convict Joël Le Scouarnec. The defendant had previously served a 15-year sentence for assaulting four children while working as a digestive surgeon. However, in the upcoming trial, nearly 300 additional victims will be added to the case. The first hearing is scheduled for February 24, where evidence of the hundreds of abuses will be examined. According to police information, among the items to be presented are a collection of dolls found hidden in the defendant's consulting room, as well as images of explicit sexual content on his computer. Another key piece of evidence is a notebook in which the abuser documented his victims. There, he would write the initials of their names and the crimes he committed with each of them. Victims, abused under anesthesia According to prosecutor Stéphane Kellenberger, many victims were in the hospital operating room under anesthesia, which prevented them from realizing what had been done to them. It is essential to note that Joël Le Scouarnec was accused of consuming child sexual abuse material by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation. In 2005, he was declared guilty, but he was not prohibited from working with children. Therefore, he continued his crimes until 2014. Finally, he was arrested in 2017, after a neighbor discovered him exposing himself to a child in the neighborhood. Among his victims are 158 men and 141 women, all from France. Of these, 256 were under 15 years old, but the average age of all was 11 years.

The National Police of Ecuador conducted an operation to dismantle a child pornography ring in which adult individuals were sexually exploiting their own children. The police deployment fulfilled judicial orders for detention and searches in Quito and the province of Esmeraldas, where four people linked to the ring were apprehended and five minors were rescued. According to the police, the criminal network operated in Ecuador and specialized in producing and marketing child sexual abuse material for U.S. citizens. The material, the agency adds, was produced by the same suspects using their minor children. During the operation, which was carried out in coordination with the Attorney General's Office (FGE) and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Investigations, (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, HSI, in English), uniformed officers seized 13 cell phones, two payment receipts, a tablet, two SIM cards, and various documents. The Prosecution Office stated that charges will be filed against the detainees within the next few hours. Agency

A document from the Prosecution Office proves the farce of the "menas" They are clearly over the age of majority The Annual Report of the Public Ministry states that for the Red Cross NGO, it was sufficient for the immigrant to declare or not declare their minority to be reported to the police In the midst of debate over the distribution of minors in autonomous communities, the State Prosecution Office has documented in its corresponding 2024 report the problem of Unaccompanied Minors, known popularly as "menas," who are often treated as minors despite their real age exceeding 18 years. According to the third section of the document related to human trafficking and foreign nationals, consulted by this medium, during the past year, proceedings have been initiated against people who were clearly over the age of majority, and who even stated so in the minors' centers. In the province of Tenerife, during the months of August to October, the location of the minor was carried out by members of the Red Cross, who were at the place of disembarkation of the canoe. According to the statement made by the Prosecution in the Memory, it was sufficient for the immigrant's minor age to be declared or not declared to be communicated to the police, who, without conducting any complementary evaluation work, communicated it to the Prosecution, which initiated the corresponding case file for age determination. In this situation, the Prosecution was able to verify that the location of the alleged minors was not being carried out correctly. Regarding the criteria for evaluating the birthdates listed in official documentation submitted to verify the disputed age of foreigners, which were already mentioned in provincial memories from 2022, it was observed that there were problems related to minors primarily from Gambia, given the system of document issuance maintained by these countries. It is noted in the official document that during 2023, this issue has spread to a large number of fiscal offices across the national territory.In particular, the delegated prosecutor of Almería highlights in the memory that when the submitted document is a passport, the date listed in it is taken into account. However, he points out the doubts raised regarding passports from certain countries regarding the authenticity of the data of the person listed in them in relation to the appearance of the supposed minor. This repeated situation over time has led to a meeting being held at the beginning of the current year between the Chief Prosecutor of the Civil Chamber of the TS, the Chief Prosecutor of the Technical Secretariat, the Minor's Unit, and the Chief Prosecutor of Human Trafficking and Immigration to draft an internal note that reflects common criteria, which is currently in the drafting phase, concludes the annual analysis of the General Prosecutor's Office.

In a recent operation, the Dominican Army has arrested three Dominican men, who are accused of transporting a total of 31 undocumented Haitian immigrants. This action is part of a broader effort to combat illegal migration in the Dominican Republic. One of the detainees, José Edilio Matías, was intercepted in the Valverde province while driving a vehicle with several Haitians on board. In another operation, Francis Mateo Rodríguez was arrested in Santiago after nine Haitian immigrants were found in his car. Janiel Montero Castillo was also detained in Bahoruco, where six Haitian immigrants were found. Local authorities have highlighted the gravity of the problem of undocumented migration, as evidenced by the fact that in the operations carried out, a total of 258 immigrants were intercepted in the provinces of Bahoruco and Dajabón. These individuals are being subjected to monitoring and supervision by the competent authorities. Following these arrests, the three Dominicans will be presented to the Public Ministry, where they will face the legal consequences of their actions. The Dominican Army reiterates its commitment to the fight against human trafficking and irregular migration, which represents a significant challenge in the region. The Army's actions aim not only to strengthen the country's border security, but also to protect the rights of migrants who, in many cases, are forced to travel under dangerous and insecure conditions in search of better life opportunities.

This Thursday, the New York Times reported that the Department of State (DOS in its English acronym) is preparing to designate eight organized crime groups operating in Latin America as terrorist groups, in compliance with one of the executive orders signed by President Donald Trump as soon as he returned to the White House on January 20. Among the organizations pointed out by the US government, five Mexican cartels stand out, accused of their power to bring large quantities of drugs and undocumented migrants into US territory. The Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG) and the Sinaloa Cartel, the two most powerful in Mexico, with international networks of operation, as well as La Familia Michoacana, the Northeast Cartel, and the United Cartels are included. Additionally, the list includes the Aragua Train, Venezuela's main criminal organization, the Mara Salvatrucha, or MS13, a group born in the United States from Salvadoran migrants that ravaged that country for years, and the Gulf Clan, Colombia's main criminal group. Although this list could be modified by the time of the official publication of this executive order, the document already explicitly referred to the Aragua Train and the MS13, considered to be among the most dangerous criminal organizations in the world. MADRID 6 Feb. (By Sevil Omer, World Vision USA Communication) Every year, millions of girls face a procedure that alters their lives and has its roots in harmful traditions. Female genital mutilation (FGM) is more than a practice, it's a violation of human rights. According to the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), around 200 million women and girls worldwide have been subjected to this practice. New estimates show a 15% increase in survivors since the last data was published in 2016, meaning 30 million more have been subjected to FGM. To put an end to this practice, the United Nations established International Zero Tolerance Day for FGM, which is celebrated annually on February 6. The United Nations' Sustainable Development Goal 5 (gender equality) also calls for intensified global efforts to end FGM by 2030. Here are the six data points about female genital mutilation (FGM) translated into English:1. Definition Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) consists of the partial or total removal of external female genitalia and may include other genital organ injuries for non-medical reasons. It is internationally recognized as a violation of human rights and a form of gender-based violence. The procedure is most frequently performed on girls between birth and 15 years old and is known in some areas as female circumcision or excision.2. The consequences of FGM for girls and women are painful and long-lasting for physical, psychological, sexual, and reproductive health. Often performed in unsanitary conditions and without anesthesia, it can cause intense pain, bleeding, and swelling that may obstruct urination or defecation. Long-term complications, such as chronic pelvic infections, urinary tract infections, and complications in childbirth for mothers and children, as well as emotional trauma and psychological suffering, including anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The procedure offers no health benefits and is not approved by the World Health Organization (WHO), most governments, or prestigious medical associations. Furthermore, the economic burden of treating complications caused by MGF is substantial, with the WHO estimating a cost of $1.4 billion per year for healthcare systems. 3. MGF is practiced worldwide and remains prevalent in at least 30 countries in Africa, the Middle East, Asia, and Latin America. It also persists among immigrant populations living in Western Europe, North America, Australia, and New Zealand. Why is the MGF still practiced? The MGF continues to be practiced due to deeply rooted cultural beliefs and gender inequality. Although most girls and women familiar with this practice would like it to end, they face immense social and cultural pressure to conform. In many countries, it symbolizes a girl's transition to adulthood and is considered essential for marriage. Mothers, fathers, extended family, and community leaders can coerce the practice to ensure acceptance.5. Medicalizing the MGF does not make it safe for girls or women. Even when performed by a healthcare professional, it is a violation of human rights and medical ethics. The UN, the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics, and many national medical associations have rejected this practice. The medicalization of the practice is leading to an alarming trend, with approximately 1 in 4 girls and women subjected to MGF by healthcare personnel. Medicalization is especially common in Egypt, where it is prohibited but remains widespread. 6. Eradicating MGF is possible. Most countries where it is still practiced have legislated against it. However, cultural and social norms must change. World Vision's child protection efforts focus on educating and empowering communities to reject MGF. In Kenya, programs such as alternative initiation rites, like a week-long coming-of-age celebration that includes training on the harmful practices of female genital mutilation and child marriage, have been implemented. Additionally, the boys learn to have a more positive perception of girls who have not suffered from MGF, opening a new path towards marriage and a change in attitudes. The goal of World Vision's child protection work is to keep all children safe from exploitation, abuse, and violence.

Florida Governor, Republican Ron DeSantis, signed two broad laws on Thursday that toughen the conditions for undocumented migrants and facilitate in this state the implementation of President of the US, Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda. The bills establish harsher penalties for undocumented immigrants who commit crimes, stricter application requirements for local officials, and changes to the state's contentious migrant transportation program (the governor will no longer have unilateral power to authorize them). One of the contentious aspects that are part of the laws signed today has to do with the automatic imposition of the death penalty for undocumented immigrants found guilty of a capital offense, such as murder or child sexual abuse. According to some experts, this aspect will certainly face legal complaints, as some Democratic lawmakers pointed out in the plenary session of both chambers, the US Supreme Court ruled decades ago that mandatory and non-discretionary jury sentences were unconstitutional. Also read: They sue Trump in New York for denying citizenship to children of undocumented immigrants The laws, approved today in the framework of an extraordinary session of the state Legislature, equally contemplate the creation of a State Immigration Control Board, which will be composed of the governor, the agriculture commissioner, the state attorney general, and the state financial director. This coordinating board will coordinate legal and security actions with federal agencies and have a $250 million fund to distribute among local law enforcement agencies that assist federal efforts in this field, in order to stimulate cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The texts establish the creation of new state crimes for illegal entry or re-entry into Florida, elevating unlicensed driving to a serious crime for undocumented immigrants. In the same way, it criminalizes as a crime the entry into Florida of undocumented immigrants over 18 years old who enter the state after entering the United States evading or avoiding inspection or examination by immigration agents, and they will be subject to a nine-month prison sentence. Se eliminan las matrículas como residentes de los estudiantes indocumentados en universidades públicas del estado, y todas las oficinas de los alguaciles locales tienen hasta abril para enrolarse en el programa federal 287(g) que concede autoridad a los agentes locales para realizar tareas propias de las agencias federales de inmigración. Hoy, la Legislatura de Florida ha aprobado la legislación más fuerte para combatir la inmigración ilegal de cualquier estado en todo el país, dijo DeSantis en una rueda de prensa poco antes de firmar los proyectos de ley, y en la que estuvo acompañado del presidente del senado, Ben Albritton, y el titular de la Cámara Baja estatal, Daniel Pérez. La firma de hoy supone el cierre de semanas de desacuerdos entre DeSantis y los legisladores estatales, con mayoría republicana en ambas cámaras, a raíz de las reformas migratorias, las cuales merecieron las convocatorias de hasta tres sesiones especiales. The TSJRM Confirms 13 and a Half Year Prison Sentence for a Man Who Sexually Assaulted the Daughter of a Friend The man took advantage of the 7-year-old girl staying at his home after school to force her to perform oral sex, threatening to tell her mother she was misbehaving if she spoke up Murcia The Civil and Penal Chamber of the Superior Court of Justice of Murcia (TSJMU) confirms the sentence of the Provincial Court of Murcia that sentenced a man to 13 years and 6 months in prison for a continued crime of sexual assault with carnal access to a 16-year-old minor, with use of violence and intimidation. According to the sentence, the accused took advantage of the minor, daughter of a friend, staying at his home after school to subject her to repeated sexual abuse, threatening to harm her family if she revealed what had happened. The defendant took her to the bathroom and forced her to perform oral sex, making the girl insert his penis into her mouth and then grabbing her head, preventing her from backing away, threatening to tell her mother that she had misbehaved if she told anyone, and saying he had a gun and would kill her, her family, and her cat if she told anyone, adding that he had cameras set up all over his house, as recorded in the judicial resolution. It is declared proven that the minor suffered repeated episodes of abuse over several months and has needed psychological treatment. The Court dismisses the defense arguments, which argued, first, an error in the appreciation of the evidence, questioning the credibility of the victim's testimony. According to the judges, the probative exploitation of the minor's testimony, presented as a victim, has been carried out by the trial court in accordance with the generally indicated criteria or parameters of reliability by the Jurisprudence. They add that there are no substantial contradictions in the minor's account, who has always maintained coherence in her statements, and emphasize that the mother and brother have provided objective data that corroborate the circumstances in which the aggression occurred. The Tribunal also does not accept the accused's request to reduce the sentence to six years in prison due to the improper application of the violent or intimidating modality, and considers the imposed sentence justified by the Provincial Court of Murcia. In the present case, the proven facts clearly describe the accused's use of the minor, both physically (he grabbed her by the head and forced her to perform oral sex) and psychologically (he threatened to kill her, her family, and her cat if she told anyone, and had cameras installed throughout the house), the sentence concludes. In addition to the prison sentence, he must serve a seven-year period of supervised liberty after his release from prison, as well as a special disqualification for any profession or occupation that involves contact with minors for a period of 17 years and 6 months. He is also ordered to pay a 10,000-euro compensation to the victim for moral damages, in addition to the prohibition of approaching within a distance of less than 300 meters for 20 years and 6 months and one day. Punish with Jail the Illegal Entry into the State Miami Agency Efe Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, a Republican, signed two broad laws that toughen the conditions of undocumented immigrants and facilitate in this state the implementation of President Donald Trump's massive deportation agenda. The projects establish harsher penalties for undocumented immigrants who commit crimes, stricter application requirements for local officials, and changes to the contentious state migrant transportation program. The governor lost unilateral power to authorize them. The laws automatically impose the death penalty on undocumented immigrants found guilty of capital crimes, such as murder or the sexual abuse of a child. According to some experts, this aspect will surely face legal complaints, as some Democratic lawmakers pointed out in the plenary session of both chambers, the US Supreme Court ruled decades ago that mandatory and non-jury sentences were unconstitutional. Penalties of up to nine months for illegal entry According to the new legislation, a State Immigration Control Board will be created, composed of the governor, the agriculture commissioner, the state attorney general, and the state finance director. This board will coordinate legal and security actions with federal agencies and have a $250 million fund to distribute among local law enforcement agencies that will help federal efforts in this field, in order to stimulate cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The texts establish the creation of new state crimes for the illegal entry or re-entry into Florida, elevating unlicensed driving to a serious crime for undocumented immigrants. Likewise, it criminalizes the entry into Florida of undocumented immigrants over 18 years old who enter the state after entering the United States, evading or avoiding inspection or examination by immigration agents, and they will be subject to a nine-month prison sentence. Undocumented immigrants lose their residency registration. Undocumented students lose their residency registration in public universities in the state, and all local sheriff's offices have until April to enroll in the federal program 287(g), which grants authority to local agents to perform tasks that are the responsibility of federal immigration agencies. The Florida Legislature has approved the strongest legislation to combat illegal immigration in any state in the country, said DeSantis. The signing marks the end of weeks of disagreements between DeSantis and state lawmakers, both with Republican majorities in both chambers. The approval of these immigration reforms warranted three special sessions in the Florida Legislature.

Last year, Barcelona registered more crimes against women. According to data presented at the Local Security Board meeting held this Friday, both domestic abuse and habitual violence in homes increased, as well as sexual assaults and abuses. The Mossos d'Esquadra units and the Barcelona Urban Guard attended to more victims and referred more high-risk situations to municipal social services. Although threats in gender violence decreased by 10% and domestic violence decreased by 9.3%, physical abuse increased by 17.33% and habitual violence in the home increased by 16% when comparing 2024 crime data to 2023 data. Crimes related to gender violence increased by 2.2% in the city and domestic violence crimes increased by 6.4%. According to Spanish legislation, gender violence always involves a male aggressor and a female victim, who are or have been linked by a romantic relationship, with or without cohabitation. Domestic violence, on the other hand, involves aggressor and victim within the family nucleus, although the majority of cases involve female victims.Regarding sexual violence in Barcelona, the crimes have increased by 3.9% and one in five cases occur within the family environment. Representatives from the Departament d'Interior and the Barcelona City Council have emphasized that these data indicate a stabilization of this type of crime after several years of high growth in sexual assaults in the city.Increased police activityIn this sense, they have highlighted the increase in police patrol hours by 21%, mainly in entertainment areas, and the number of identified suspects by 34%, which has resulted in a resolution rate of over 80% for these crimes in the city. The Mossos and Guardia Urbana agents maintain coordination to ensure the safety of potential victims with safe routes to public transportation upon leaving nightclubs. Last year, the Mossos d'Esquadra in Barcelona attended to 7,463 victims, a 5.9% increase from 2023. All are related to domestic, gender-based, and sexual violence, hate crimes and discrimination, forced marriages or female genital mutilation, which are later incorporated into the comprehensive victim support system. The Guardia Urbana also has the Te acompañamos project to prevent, detect, and act against machismo violence. Last year, there were 676 cases, 73% of which were linked to social services. In 163 cases, there was suspicion of risk, and 21 of them ended in a criminal complaint. Within this plan, a pioneering guide for alert indicators is being developed, which facilitates the work of agents when observing signs of possible cases of abuse. These indicators serve to make reports evaluating the risk and to attend to women from different municipal services specifically for these cases. In 2024, 100 women were detected who were suffering situations of violence. The Urban Guard also has attention points for victims of macho violence and their children. Last year, 539 statements were made to women, 16% of whom were accompanied by minors, 113 protection orders were granted, and 79 emergency housing referrals were made to services. Crime rates are down. The Local Security Board of Barcelona has analyzed the city's crime data from last year as well as the challenges to reduce the sense of insecurity that citizens feel. The meeting was presided over by the Mayor of Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, alongside the Minister of Interior and Public Security, Núria Parlon, the Deputy Mayor for Prevention, Security, Coexistence, and Internal Regime, Albert Batlle, the Director General of the Police, Josep Lluís Trapero, the Government Delegate in Catalonia, Carlos Prieto, the Chief Commissioner of the Mossos, Miquel Esquius, the Chief of the Barcelona Urban Guard, Pedro Velázquez, the Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police Region of Barcelona, Montserrat Estruch, the Director of the Civil Protection Service, Prevention, Fire Extinction, and Rescue, Sebastià Massagué, as well as representatives from the National Police, Civil Guard, Prosecution, and judiciary. As reported by EL PERIÓDICO, crimes in the city decreased by 4.7% over the past year, while police activity increased by 4.5% (1,230 more) to reach a total of 28,485 detentions. Additionally, the number of people investigated has risen by 6.3% to 61,386 (3,630 more). The security forces have planned 6,258 operations, a 9% increase from last year, mainly related to strategic plans such as preventing home robberies, crimes in public transportation or at night, or against repeat offenders. Mossos and the Urban Guard have also carried out specific operations that have allowed for a 19.6% increase in identifications (346,494 in total), requiring a 29.3% increase in the number of seized knives (3,371 in absolute numbers), over 750 kilograms of different types of drugs, and over 150 electric scooters used by repeat offenders to commit the crime or ensure their escape.

By Arturo Molina Morelia, Mich., February 13, 2025. The Civil Registry of Michoacán prevented at least 3 child marriages in 2024. Couples with at least one minor under 16 approached authorities to request union. The cases were mainly reported in the Michoacán Bajío region, between the municipalities of La Piedad and others bordering the state of Jalisco. According to Noé García Cancino, the three cases stood out due to the insistence of families, who even resorted to legal amparos that were dismissed. In Michoacán, the law is very clear and cannot have child marriages under any circumstances. They wanted to bring amparos but we did not allow them, stated the state official. Although these cases stood out due to judicial conflict issues, they are not the only ones. The officials of the Civil Registry in indigenous regions also reported requests with minors. All would have been rejected. The law in Michoacán says that to get married, you have to force the delivery of the INE, and that can only be obtained at 18 years old. In some way, it's a gap that has allowed us to contain this phenomenon, he explained. In Mexico, child marriage is prohibited in all states, and no minor can legally get married in the Civil Registry. However, informal unions persist, especially in indigenous and rural communities where cultural practices and customs prevail. According to data from the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI), in 2022, 32 marriages were registered in which at least one of the contracting parties was under the age of 18. This number is the second lowest observed in the period 2013-2022, only higher than the 26 registered in 2020. In 2024, the Mexican Senate approved a reform to Article 2 of the Constitution to prohibit child marriages in indigenous communities, seeking to harmonize cultural practices with the human rights of girls and boys. Despite legal advances, informal unions of minors continue in some regions, especially in indigenous and rural communities, where cultural and economic practices perpetuate this situation. These unions are not always officially registered, making it difficult to obtain precise figures on their prevalence. In summary, although legal reforms aim to eradicate child marriage in Mexico, informal unions of minors persist in certain communities, and the lack of official records hinders the collection of precise data on their prevalence in 2024.

PALMA 14 Feb. (EUROPA PRESS) A man accused of sexually abusing his 8-year-old niece has denied the allegations on Friday and claimed that it was the second time false accusations of similar nature had been made against him. During the trial held on Friday at the Provincial Court of Palma, the man claimed that at the time of the alleged incidents, he only entered the home where the victim was to change clothes and pick up something to wear, although he fell asleep. Upon questioning by the Public Prosecutor's Office, the accused explained that when he entered, his niece was watching TV, that he did not exchange any words with her, and that when he woke up, no one was in the house. The man thus denied the allegations of sexual abuse and added that it was the second time his sister, the mother of the girl, had accused him of touching her daughter, who testified in private. According to what she added, her sister once told the girl that if she told about the abuse, she would buy her a video game console. The prosecution is asking for a 12-year prison sentence and 10 years of supervised release for the defendant for incidents that date back to May 2020 and took place in a locality in Mallorca. According to the accusation document, on one occasion, taking advantage of being alone at home, the defendant committed sexual contact with the girl and even inserted his finger into her vagina.
