A 47-year-old man in Seville is sentenced to seven years in prison for extorting intimate images of a minor via WhatsApp. SEVILLE, February 14. The Provincial Court of Seville has issued a ruling convicting a man to prison for creating child pornography and indecent exposure to a minor. This verdict follows the discovery that the defendant manipulated a 13-year-old girl into exchanging sexual images and videos, leading to various restrictive measures, including a seven-year ban on using messaging apps like WhatsApp and accessing the canalchat.org webpage. On February 6, the First Section of the Seville Court of Appeal issued the ruling, which states that Javier Á.T.G., a 49-year-old man with no relevant prior convictions, acknowledged his guilt in a plea agreement between his defense, the prosecution, and the private accuser. According to the established facts, the defendant used fake profiles on the canalchat.org platform posing as a 15-year-old minor between March and May 2021. The man contacted the minor, born in February 2008, and after she clearly stated her age, he persuaded her to send him explicit sexual content through WhatsApp, seeking to satisfy his sexual impulses. As a result, the minor ended up sending him explicit images through a temporary photo-sharing website designed to maintain anonymity. The judicial resolution also reveals that, after discovering his true identity, the defendant conducted video calls in which he observed the minor in explicit situations. Following the issuance of a court order, the police searched his residence in Badajoz on May 27, 2021, seizing devices used in the crimes. The effects of this case on the victim have been devastating. From May 2021 to June 2022, the minor received psychological treatment due to significant emotional distress, which included anxiety, feelings of guilt, and episodes of deep sadness. The sentence also mentions that the accused had a cocaine consumption disorder at the time of the events, which could have affected their ability to control their impulses. It is acknowledged that the accused has economically compensated the victim by paying 10,000 euros for the damages caused. Finally, Javier Á.T.G. has been sentenced to two years in prison, although his sentence will be suspended if he does not reoffend. In addition, he must comply with several restrictions, including avoiding any contact with the victim and prohibitions related to the use of messaging applications and contact with minors for several years, as well as supervised liberty and a special disqualification to occupy positions that involve interaction with children.

Services Highlights The brutal murder of Tatiana Coinac, a 44-year-old Moldovan escort found dead in her apartment on Amsterdam Street in Oviedo in March 2023, will not go to trial. Lieutenant Adán Feito, 35 years old at the time of the crime, has admitted to the facts via video conference at the Second Section of the Provincial Court this Friday morning and accepted a sentence of 42 years in prison. Thirty years for the crime of murder and twelve more for sexual assault. The Asturias Public Prosecution Office, the victim's family, represented by attorney José Manuel Fernández González, and the defendant's defense team have reached an agreement in this way, which has been ratified by the accused. The trial, in which the former soldier from Mieres faced a possible sentence of permanent imprisonment revisable plus an additional fifteen years for sexually assaulting the Moldovan woman before murdering her, was scheduled for next April before a popular jury. Now, the matter has been closed and the sentence is expected for the beginning of the week. Furthermore, Feito, in preventive detention since May two years ago, will have to compensate the victim's family with 200,000 euros in civil liability. The murder of the Moldovan escort, which will be two years old next month, shocked Oviedo with its brutality and the intense investigation that followed for two months after the discovery of the body in the bathtub of the 3rd floor of number 1 on Amsterdam Street. The account begins at the start of February 2023, when the corporal met Tatiana Coinac through different contact web pages where the victim offered her sexual services as an escort and erotic masseuse. After a first meeting around those dates, nearly a month later, the man contacted her again by phone and they agreed on a new appointment for March 9 The military man, who had been discharged but intended to return to the Army at some point due to other cases of sexual violence against a former comrade, went to Oviedo from Pola de Lena after making various phone and WhatsApp contacts with the woman who would soon become his victim. Once at the building entrance, she let him in and allowed him to enter, under the belief that it would be a professional meeting, as defined by the Public Prosecutor's Office. The horror unfolded inside. In the bedroom, with a clear intention of satisfying his sexual desire, Feito picked up two pillowcases that were on the bed and gagged the Moldovan woman with a strong knot, preventing her from seeking help. Additionally, using another item, he tied her wrists tightly, rendering her defenseless. He then violently raped her, without her being able to do anything to stop it. He taken a cylindrical lubricant container and repeatedly inserted it into her anus, causing multiple lacerations. But that wasn't the end of it. With the sole intention of ending the woman's life and causing her the maximum possible suffering (beyond what was strictly necessary to cause her death), the prosecutor's account of the accused's actions, recognized this Friday, reveals that the man placed himself behind the woman and strangled her using the "mataleón" technique. She, with her back turned, was unable to anticipate the attack. Given his military training, Sergeant Adán was well-versed in this technique. He grasped the woman's neck tightly between his arms and fell onto the bed with her on top. He remained in this position for seven to ten minutes, holding his arms with great force and a tremendous amount of violence, until Tatiana stopped breathing. Aware that he had succeeded in ending her life, he placed her in a lateral position to transport her to the bathroom and left the corpse inside the bathtub. From there, he took his time. He went to the kitchen, grabbed a pair of scissors from a drawer, and returned to the bathroom, where he tore the woman's clothes into shreds. He threw them into a trash can along with the two pillowcases he had used as a gag, stripped her completely naked, and turned on the faucet. While the bathtub filled with water, he went back to the kitchen to leave the scissors and returned shortly after. He waited a few minutes, turned off the faucet once the bathtub was full of water, and left the building. In total, 57 minutes of terror on Ámsterdam Street. It was the time it took him to enter and exit, as witnessed by the surveillance cameras in the area. He returned to Pola de Lena with his wife and son. The National Police, following an alert call from Tatiana's mother from Benicarló after failing to contact her daughter for days, found the body on Sunday morning, March 12. After two months of intense investigations, coordinated by the General Commissariat of Madrid, the corporal was arrested on May 29. There were more than enough indications of his DNA on the pillowcases he used to gag the escort and on the wig he used, which was listed in the appointment calendar without his contact information, indicating that he was the last client to access the apartment, as well as his footprints and the same shoe he was wearing when the agents intercepted him in Pola de Lena. He confessed the facts at the headquarters, although in his first appearance in court, he chose not to declare, and later stated that the facts he is accused of are not true, he has now fully acknowledged them before the Second Section of the Provincial Audience and accepted the 42-year prison sentence. Shortly after the first details of the crime were known, as EL COMERCIO had previously reported, the Ministry of Defense initiated the procedures to expel Captain Adán Feito from the Army of the Land, not for the brutal crime, but for his last known episodes of sexual violence. Two, in particular, which took place between September 2020 and November 2021, when he was still stationed at the barracks of the Galicia Infantry Regiment number 64, in Jaca (Huesca), and for which he remained suspended and temporarily disqualified until May 2024, as it was a very serious offense. He had sexually abused a fellow soldier on at least two occasions. This earned him a two-year prison sentence for the crimes of abuse of authority and sexual abuse without carnal access. The sentence of the Third Military Territorial Court is from May 5, 2022. It took four days for the first voices of condemnation and rejection of the crime by the political authorities to be heard after the discovery of the Moldovan escort's body. On Wednesday, March 15 (the body had been found on Sunday), the Government of the Principality issued a brief press release expressing condolences to the family and calling for this type of crime to be included in the statistics on gender-based violence as soon as possible, which currently only record homicides committed by partners or ex-partners of the victims. At the time, the then-Director General of Equality, Nuria Varela, advocated for the creation of a register that includes all women murdered by any type of machismo violence. The women who did come out onto the street that same day were the Women of the Scandal for a concentration against machismo, to which, however, neither local nor autonomous authorities attended. The mayor, Alfredo Canteli, condemned the crime the following morning and criticized that the concern of some parties and some feminists is that the victim appears on the list of fatalities.

The Bizkaia Provincial Court has sentenced a man to 9 years in prison for sexually abusing a semi-conscious woman and allowing the sex sequence to be recorded. The court considers the defendant to be the perpetrator of a sex abuse crime and another against intimacy and the right to one's own image, as he consented to the recording of the sex sequence by another person who was not tried due to being in a state of rebellion. The Provincial Court of Bizkaia has sentenced a man to a total of 9 years in prison for sexually abusing a woman who was in a state of semi-consciousness and allowing the entire sex sequence to be recorded by another person who was not tried due to being in a state of rebellion. The court imposes 7 years in prison for a sex abuse crime under article 181, 1, 2, and 4 of the applicable Penal Code in effect at the time of the facts (2019) and an additional 2 years in prison and a fine of 10 euros per day for 14 months for a crime against intimacy and the right to one's own image. Furthermore, it is established that the victim must be compensated with 4,900 euros for the injuries and 10,000 euros for the moral damage caused, among other measures and penalties. The proven facts took place in June 2019 in a Bilbao residence that the victim attended accompanied by the accused, the boyfriend of a friend (not being judged in this process as they were in rebellion). At a certain moment, the victim lost consciousness, entering a lethargic state, possibly due to some substance (not identified) that the accused and his girlfriend administered to her. Therefore, the defendant, taking advantage of her state of unconsciousness and with the intention of satisfying his sexual desire, abused her, while the woman in a state of rebellion recorded the entire sequence. These recordings were shown to third parties by the person who recorded them. The court recalls that the accused refused to testify during the trial but had the testimonies of the victim and several friends, as well as the video of the facts. In it, the complainant is seen in a state of deep sleep or unconsciousness and it is seen that during a sequence that lasts several minutes, she is subjected to various sexual acts without her ever waking up at any moment, nor did she make any movement (she is completely inert). It is evident to any observer that the accuser did not give consent to any of the acts to which she was subjected, since she was not in a state to do so (she was in a state of semi-consciousness or deep sleep), the Vizcayan Audiencia affirms. As for the crime against intimacy, the court states that the images clearly show that the accused was fully aware that he was being recorded throughout the entire sexual sequence. Furthermore, in several instances, he speaks with the person recording, precisely about what they were recording, the Provincial Audiencia of Bizkaia concludes, indicating that the accused's participation in this crime, which was clearly affecting the victim's intimacy, leaves no doubt. Deep personal, social, and reputational harm suffered by the victim. At the time of imposing the penalties, the court considers that there are two aggravating circumstances in this case: the facts occur in a context of trust for the victim (there was a friendship relationship) and the variety of sexual acts to which the accused subjected the woman. On moral damage, the Provincial Court of Bizkaia highlights the deep personal harm suffered by the victim upon learning of the facts (which are undoubtedly serious) and, alongside it, the social and reputational harm suffered in her closest environment, which forced her to leave Bilbao.Testimony deduction. The court agrees to deduce testimony from private individuals for remission to the Chief Investigating Magistrate if the accused had committed a crime of threats against the victim in this procedure, given the statements made by her in the trial. This sentence is not final and is subject to appeal before the High Court of Justice of the Basque Country.

Detectives from the Sexual Crimes Investigative Brigade in Chillán managed to apprehend a 42-year-old dentist of Colombian nationality for the crime of sexual abuse, which allegedly occurred within his dental clinic in the San Carlos commune. According to the officer, following the complaint, the Public Ministry issued an order for this specialized brigade to investigate, which allowed for various proceedings to be carried out that established the existence of the crime and the alleged participation of the accused as the perpetrator. With these background, the prosecutor managed an arrest warrant against this man, which was executed by detectives from this brigade. Therefore, he was placed at the disposal of the Guarantee Court for his respective detention control and formalization, said Subcomissary Pereira Rivas, adding that the defendant already has a penal record for similar facts. The Local Prosecutor's Office of San Carlos formalized him this Thursday, pointing out that the dentist already had a previous conviction under the same modus operandi. During the hearing, the Public Ministry requested the preventive imprisonment of the accused, however, the measure was not granted by the Guarantee Court, a decision that was later confirmed by the Court of Appeals. The court set a 90-day deadline for the investigation.

data.text: Three men accused of sex crimes in Villavicencio. At the request of the Prosecutor's Office, judges of control of guarantees imposed a measure of guarantee in a correctional center against three men, who, it appears, sexually assaulted three minors and one woman, in different incidents that occurred between 2023 and 2024, in Villavicencio (Meta). Prosecutors from the Center for Integral Attention to Victims of Sexual Abuse (CAIVAS) charged them, according to their individual responsibilities, with the crimes of abusive sexual acts with a minor under 14 years old, violent sexual act, and violent carnal access, all aggravated behaviors. Charges that were not accepted by any of the defendants. The first of the incidents occurred between January and October 2023 in Villavicencio (Meta). Where a man, taking advantage of the trust he had, because he was the partner of the mother of the victim, a 13-year-old, allegedly, sexually assaulted her on several occasions, while they were alone in the family residence. In another case, the defendant is John Henry Cruz Moreno, who as a music teacher, on August 31, 2024, summoned his students to rehearse on a Saturday at the school where he worked. According to the investigation, it appears that he made sexual advances to two of the students, aged 13 and 15. Finally, on the early morning of May 18, 2024, Oscar Ferney Parrado Rincón allegedly sexually assaulted a 32-year-old woman who had taken a taxi driven by him to go home to the east of the city. It appears that this man changed the route and threatened his victim with a sharp object, in order to proceed to sexually assault her.

The Mother of God is the only place on Earth where the Blessed Virgin builds a Nazareth Home. Former Military Chaplain, Father Ignacio María Doñoro de los Ríos, known worldwide for his bold courage in the face of organ traffickers and human traffickers, rescuing children in El Salvador, shares with Aleteia how the Blessed Virgin's shelter heals and empowers the little ones rescued in his current mission in Peru. Nazareth Home is a work of God (as Father Doroño points out) that has rescued for 14 years girls, children, and adolescents living in extreme moral, emotional, and material poverty in Peru, in one of the most inaccessible regions of the Amazon jungle. It has two home shelters, one for girls and young women, and another for boys and young men. They also have two schools and a rural agricultural and livestock technology center, linked to the autonomous farm of more than 70 hectares, which, in addition to consolidating the daily nutrition of the children at home, ensures their labor life upon completing high school. It is María who, amidst the difficulties and obstacles, carries the children in her arms and presents them to Jesus, teaching them that in Him lies true joy and strength. The Virgin consoles them, wipes away their tears, and is their strength in weakness, shares the former chaplain. Hogar Nazaret has various projects that help hundreds of small children and impact thousands of others. From providing medical attention to children arriving in precarious situations, to providing them with adequate nutrition and education. But they also care about safeguarding the well-being of the most vulnerable. Despite the great hardships that the region faces, where not even roads exist for travel, Father Ignacio has strived so that the children find the beauty of God through the Virgin and dignify the house and all the spaces where they live. Through beauty, God tells these little ones that they are unique, irreproducible, and necessary, and that this is what their Mother has dreamed for them. Jesus said, "I thank you, Father, because you have revealed these things to the simple, to the humble, and you have hidden them from the great." In the small is the Lord, who leaves an infinite eternity of his mark. It's as if he takes their hand and says, "Look, all of this is for you." Now begins a new story. Now begins my eternal promise of love for you, share. The father has one thing clear: everything is little for them, who have suffered the most. Here is the translation:Therefore, everything they do and build is done with the purpose of being like a bridge that will lead them to God, who says, "Do not be afraid, I am with you. I love you, and I love you in an eternal way." What I wanted to show with all of this is that there is a story of love between God and each one of the children of Hogar Nazaret, explains Father Ignacio. Prayer to protect the children from any harm The Virgin of the Rocio The first thing one finds at Hogar Nazaret in the middle of the Amazon is an exact replica of the Rocio in Andalusia, Spain. In the Amazon jungle, the Virgin of the Rocio is welcomed in a special way because, despite their circumstances or habits, and despite so much pain, in a land where nothing has ever grown, that dew that falls that are also the tears of God, because the passion of Christ continues in the crucified of the earth, produces precious fruits of flowers of love that heal, forgive, and liberate. When they ask me why the Virgin of the Rocio, when there are so many advocations, I respond that I have always seen in Her the consolation of the afflicted. The Virgin of the Rocio is the Mother of the humble, she has an essential characteristic: the light that illuminates the paths, especially the darkest ones. That is why, in this isolated place, where perhaps the difficulties are greater, she is the star that guides the poorest children towards hope. The Virgin of the Rocio is a whisper of love, it is a look of Mother. And remember, it is contundently stated that Mary is not only the Mother of a people or a nation, but Mother of all humanity. Therefore, and taking into account her maternal work, Mary does not discriminate. She welcomes each one of her children with a unique tenderness and dedication. Each child is special, regardless of their origin, language, or culture. She is a Mother who comes out to meet everyone, searching for those who need the most consolation and protection. All of us can be the outstretched arms of the Virgin in Nazareth's Home. For Father Doñoro, the most beautiful thing about this mission is that the Lord, from the very beginning, wanted this work to live from absolute Providence. We have no diocese, religious order, or foundation. We live on charity. That's why he invites you to be part of it by visiting the following link. A 36-year-old man was arrested in Santa Fe as a suspect in the rape of his 13-year-old stepdaughter, who gave birth after years of abuse. The investigation, initiated in Rosario, was transferred to Río Tercero (Cordoba) after it was confirmed that several attacks occurred there. Prosecutor Paula Bruera obtained an indictment for qualified sexual abuse and aggravated corruption, highlighting the manipulation exercised over the victim in a forced cohabitation environment. SEE ALSO Cutting the projection of soybean and corn harvest due to drought According to the Cordoba Public Prosecutor's Office, the accused allegedly abused the minor from the age of 11, taking advantage of her vulnerability. The teenager, after giving birth, attempted to flee with her baby to rural areas to escape the aggressor, prompting complaints from her biological mother in Santa Fe. Authorities confirmed that the defendant had already been questioned and remains incarcerated at the Bouwer Penitentiary Service. The victim, her newborn daughter, and her mother were transferred to judicial facilities in Río Tercero for psychological evaluations, a Gesell camera, and DNA tests. These exams aim to reconstruct the timeline of events and ensure solid evidence for the trial. There are also reports of deflation under Milei, celebrating INDEC data. The case exposes failures in the protection of minors, as the victim lived years of abuse without any warning signs being detected. Authorities insist that the investigation remains open and do not rule out further charges. Meanwhile, human rights organizations demand urgent policies to prevent intrafamilial sexual crimes. Source: Noticias Argentinas. Illustrative archive image.

The Child and Adolescent Prosecutor in Valverde, Carmen Estefanía Rodríguez, delivered a lecture titled Dangers in Social Networks at the Sacred Heart of Jesus College, on the occasion of International Internet Safety Day. During the event, she highlighted the growing number of minors affected by cybercrimes in the country and the need to strengthen the prevention and persecution of these digital crimes. By Juan Pablo Bourdierd. Mao, RD. The Child and Adolescent Prosecutor in Valverde, Carmen Estefanía Rodríguez, gave the lecture titled Dangers in Social Networks on the occasion of International Internet Safety Day. The activity took place at the Sacred Heart of Jesus College and was directed at students and TIC Facilitators of Regional 09 in Mao. Representatives from the Educational District 0903 of Sabaneta and the Marino Almonte High School in Las Caobas also participated. Carmen Estefanía Rodríguez and educational authorities accompanied students from Marino Almonte High School in Las Caobas. During her intervention, prosecutor Rodríguez emphasized the growing number of children and adolescents who are victims of sexual harassment and cyberbullying through social media. Citing data from the National Office of Statistics (ONE, 2022), she noted that 22.9% of the Dominican population aged 10 or older who used the internet that year was a victim of some type of cybercrime, including cyberbullying, social network hacking, or identity theft. Additionally, the Special Prosecutor's Office Against Crimes and High-Tech Crimes (PEDATEC) reported, through a request made to the Unique Portal for Public Information Access (SAIP), that from 2019 to June 2023, 591 online crimes against minors had been reported in the country. However, only 24 of these cases have been judicialized or resulted in conviction. Rodríguez highlighted that Law 5307 on High-Tech Crimes and Cyber Delinquencies is the regulatory framework governing the investigation, prevention, prosecution, and punishment of electronic crimes in the Dominican Republic. Among the main crimes in this area, child pornography and sexual harassment through digital means stand out. The magistrate also explained that the production, dissemination, sale, and any form of commercialization of content with pornographic material involving children, girls, or adolescents is a crime, as stipulated in Law 5307. The penalties for this crime range from two to four years in prison, in addition to fines ranging from ten to five hundred times the minimum wage. The event was also attended by Félix Rodríguez, director of the Educational District 0904 in Monción, Cristian Torres, regional subdirector of Education, Edizabeth Durán, regional IT technician, and Carmen Díaz, director of the Educational District 0906 in Villa Los Almácigos. Also representing the Ministry of Education, Damián Morales, in charge of Educational Robotics, was present. The event reaffirmed the authorities' commitment to raising awareness about digital security, promoting responsible internet use, and protecting minors from online dangers.

On Wednesday afternoon, February 12, the discovery of Jennifer Fernanda, a 15-year-old girl who had been reported missing since January 29 in Tijuana, was confirmed alive. The minor was found in the municipality of Teziutlán, in the state of Puebla, accompanied by a 33-year-old man. Her rescue was made possible thanks to a coordinated operation between the authorities of Baja California and Puebla, through the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Disappearance. The man found with the minor has been identified as Óscar N, and it is presumed that he had manipulated Jennifer to leave her home and travel with him. Up to this point, preliminary information indicates that the suspect was detained, although no further information has been released yet. Jennifer Fernanda was last seen on January 29 in the city of Tijuana. Her disappearance generated an intense mobilization of relatives, friends, and feminist collectives that demanded her immediate location. Among the organizations that raised their voices on this case, the Colectiva Nacional 501 issued a public statement in which they denounced a presumed case of manipulation. According to this group, the teenager would have been deceived to leave her home by an adult man, who contacted her through the WhatsApp messaging application. The case generated concern over the growing incidence of crimes related to digital violence and the exploitation of minors in online platforms. The Colectiva Nacional 501 emphasized the urgency of strengthening protection measures for girls, boys, and adolescents in the digital sphere and of strengthening surveillance over the environments in which they interact. How was she rescued Jennifer Fernanda's discovery in Teziutlán was the result of a joint work between Baja California and Puebla authorities. The Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Disappearance was in charge of the operation that led to their location and protection. Subsequently, the minor was placed under protection to evaluate her physical and emotional health. Regarding Óscar N, the authorities are managing the hypothesis that he manipulated the adolescent to induce her to leave her home. Although his detention has not been officially confirmed, it is expected that in the next few hours, a statement will be issued by the Attorney General's Office of the State of Puebla or Baja California to clarify her legal situation. The case of Jennifer Fernanda has once again put the vulnerability of minors in digital environments at the center of the discussion and the need for greater efforts to prevent similar cases. Feminist and human rights collectives have reiterated the urgency of strengthening digital education and online security strategies to protect children and adolescents from potential aggressors. In turn, authorities have urged parents and guardians to maintain constant communication with minors and supervise the digital platforms on which they interact. They have also reminded the importance of reporting any suspicious activity to the corresponding instances to avoid risk situations. As details of the case are clarified and Oscar N's legal situation is confirmed, users on social media have expressed relief over Jennifer Fernanda's safe recovery, waiting for justice to be served and for measures to be strengthened to prevent digital violence and child exploitation in Mexico.

A 13-year-old girl was a mother, and her stepfather was arrested for rape. A 36-year-old man was detained, accused of raping and impregnating his partner's daughter. This case began in Santa Fe and was transferred to Córdoba because several of the abuses occurred in that province.The stepfather of a 13-year-old girl who was a mother was arrested for rape, as part of a case that began in Santa Fe and was transferred to Río Tercero, Córdoba, due to several of the abuses having taken place in that locality.The Special Unit for Sexual Integrity Crimes in Rosario initiated an investigation in January 2025, involving a 36-year-old man accused of raping and impregnating his partner's daughter. Prosecutor Paula Bruera made the request for imputation, capture, and detention of the suspect, who was finally apprehended in Santa Fe. The man was accused by the Public Prosecutor's Office of Córdoba for the crime of sexual abuse with carnal access qualified by the pre-existing cohabitation situation and corruption of minors aggravated by custody. In this sense, the judicial document states that the investigation determined that, under conditions of extreme vulnerability, the accused would have manipulated and sexually abused his stepdaughter from the age of 11, who, at 13, gave birth to a girl. Additionally, it states that the accused would have manipulated her to the point that on repeated occasions, the victim left the home she shared with her mother to live secretly in a rural area. In the face of this situation, the mother of the girl and ex-partner of the accused made the complaints in the province with the objective of knowing the whereabouts of her daughter. The authorities reported that the investigation continues, and that the accused has already been questioned and is being held in the Bouwer Penitentiary Service facilities. In the meantime, the minor, her daughter, and her mother were transferred to the Courts of the Jurisdiction of Río Tercero and to the Judicial Police facilities in Córdoba, where the procedural acts related to the case will be carried out, such as the psychological expertise, the Gesell camera, and DNA tests.

The 15-year-old girl is being physically and psychologically attended to. 02.13.2025. Puebla, Pue. Authorities in Puebla located 15-year-old Jennifer Fernanda alive, and detained Oscar Avalino N after allegedly abducting her through a secret relationship in Tijuana, Baja California. 15-year-old Jennifer Fernanda Camacho Osobampo was located alive in the Lomas Verdes neighborhood, Chignautla in Teziutlán, Puebla, according to state authorities in the afternoon of this Wednesday, February 12. After her location, Oscar Avelino Márquez attempted to pass Jennifer off as his sister, as Jennifer had allegedly been a victim of grooming, a type of pederastic deception committed by adults to emotionally manipulate minors for abuse purposes. The teenager had gone missing since January 29 in Tijuana, Baja California, and it was inferred that a close friend of her father, identified as Oscar Avalino N, had taken her away with deception. When the family realized that the minor was not at her residence, authorities initiated an intense search, even tracking Jennifer Fernanda's conversations to locate her whereabouts. The case gained national attention when the family pleaded for help on social media to find her. They discovered conversations between the teenager on social media with Óscar Avalino N, a 33-year-old man who had a close relationship with the family and even lived in the same house. The ministerial authorities reported that the father had provided him with lodging in one of the rooms, as they trusted him. After the minor's disappearance, it was known that the man allegedly convinced Jennifer to go to the Central Camionera de Tijuana to leave with him. Thanks to the collaboration between the Baja California Attorney General's Office and the Puebla Attorney General's Office, the authorities were able to locate the minor in the latter state. During the operation, security agents detained Oscar Avalino N, who was with Jennifer at a residence. The individual was put at the disposal of the authorities to determine his legal situation, while the minor received attention from child protection specialists and is waiting to be handed over to Tijuana authorities to be transferred to her family. The authorities continue to investigate since Puebla is part of the human trafficking route that involves minors being taken by deception.

Former Legislator Palina Sentenced for Sexual Abuse of Niece Roberto Palina, who was a provincial legislator on several occasions, was sentenced to three years of suspended prison on Thursday as a result of a shortened trial that reached an agreement in court. The former general secretary of the Federation of Sugar Industry Workers (FOTIA) was found guilty of simple sexual abuse, aggravated by the victim's age. Article 119 of the Penal Code dictates that whoever sexually abuses a person will be punished with imprisonment or prison for six months to four years, when the victim is under 13 years old or when there is violence, threat, coercive or intimidating behavior in a relationship of dependence, authority, or power, or when taking advantage of the victim's inability to give free consent due to any reason. According to the victim's complaint filed with prosecutor Mariano Fernández, who is the niece of the former legislator, the attack occurred on a night between November 22 and 26, 2021 at 9:00 p.m. in an apartment in the Sur neighborhood of San Miguel de Tucumán. How the attack occurred: At that location, the accused Palina, his partner, and the victim's aunt lived together. The victim stated that she was violently assaulted by the former parliamentarian. According to her account, taking advantage of the fact that they were alone in the apartment, he entered the victim's room, got into bed beside her, grabbed her hands, pulled off the blanket she was covering herself with, and without the victim's consent, began touching her, pulled down her pants, and touched her breasts and buttocks with his hands, both above and below her underwear. He then removed her underwear and his own as well. The victim also stated that the man attempted to rape her but that she managed to escape by locking herself in the bathroom. After the complaint was formalized, statements were taken and there was a judicial battle between prosecutors and judges in the middle. For this Thursday, a hearing on the accusation control was planned, conducted by Judge Alejandro Tomás, but both the assistant prosecutor Osvaldo Martínez Terán and the defender Macario Santamarina communicated that they had reached an agreement for a shortened trial to which the judge gave place. Thus, the penalty of three years of conditional imprisonment against Palina was determined, a decision that remained firm immediately.

A man was sentenced to 18 months in prison for admitting to sexually assaulting a friend of his son who was a minor at the time. The first of the proven incidents occurred in April 2022, when the accused took advantage of the presence of several friends and friends of his son at his home to touch the victim and tell her phrases like affection, my baby, and my princess. The Provincial Court of Murcia has sentenced a man to a year and a half in prison and five years of supervised liberty for admitting in court to having committed two instances of unwanted touching against a friend of his son, who was a minor at the time of the incidents in 2022. The sentence, in accordance with the verdict, convicts the defendant of a continued offense of sexual abuse, today considered as sexual assault, and imposes a 150-meter restraining order against the victim for three years and a five-year prohibition on engaging in any profession or job that involves contact with minors. In addition, the minor will be indemnified with two thousand euros for moral damages, an amount that was paid in advance before the trial, so the atonement for repairing the damage will be applied. The first of the proven facts occurred in April 2022, when the accused took advantage of the presence in his home of several friends and girlfriends of his son to make her touchings and tell her expressions like affection, my baby, and my princess. Just two days later, when the minor returned with the group of friends to the accused's residence, he gave her a kiss on the mouth as she was saying goodbye. The sentence has left the effective fulfillment of the penalty of deprivation of liberty suspended for two years, on condition that during that time he does not commit any new crimes.

Despite the victim's denial, the now convicted man subjected her to sexual abuse and kept her locked in the room until he managed to consummate the act. The interim penal prosecutor 4 at the Unit for Sexual Integrity Crimes (UDIS), Carolina Mateo Bellini, represented the Public Prosecution Office in front of Chamber 7 of the District Center Court of Judgment, in the hearing in which a 20-year-old man was sentenced to 6 years of effective imprisonment for the crimes of sexual abuse with carnal access, in ideal concurrence with illegal deprivation of liberty. The prosecution's action began from the complaint filed by a woman, who stated that on October 1, 2023, she attended a gathering along with her partner and a friend, staying there until approximately 7 am. Upon leaving, the complainant had a disagreement with her partner, so she decided to leave with the accused and two other friends to his home, who, up to that moment, was a trusted friend. Upon arriving at the accused's residence, the woman stated that she preferred to sleep in a separate room. However, both of them lay down on a bed, back to back. At a certain point, the subject began to insist that they maintain sexual relations by touching. Despite the woman's refusal, the accused restrained her against her will and subjected her to a sexual act, only allowing her to leave the dwelling afterwards. In the request for trial, the prosecution maintained that the facts have foundation, mainly, in the complaint filed by the victim, which is corroborated by the various testimonies incorporated into the case. Judge Francisco Mascarello sentenced the defendant to 6 years of effective imprisonment and, in the same ruling, ordered the extraction of genetic material from the convicted person, by the Molecular Biology Service of the Technical Department of the Fiscal Investigations Body (CIF), after assigning the Unique Genetic Identification Data (DUIG), for its incorporation into the Genetic Data Bank.

Federico Esteban N., a 45 years old, the subject who pursued, harassed, and bit the buttocks of a young woman from Málaga, was detained on Wednesday in Celaya by the Guanajuato Attorney General's Office, for the alleged crime of sexual abuse. This aggressor was identified and detained after attacking a young woman on the past Sunday, February 2, in Celaya. Now, he has been placed at the disposal of a judge to face justice. In Guanajuato, there is no room for impunity. Violence against women will be punished with the full weight of the law. The Attorney General's Office reiterates its unbreakable commitment to justice and the protection of victims. We will not give quarter to criminals, said the Guanajuato Attorney General's Office, which initially refused to receive the complaint from the victim, arguing that there was no crime to pursue. However, as the video of the attack went viral and the case became media attention, the Attorney General's Office acted quickly and captured the sex abuser. How the assault on the young woman in Celaya occurred. It happened through social media, where several videos were disseminated and went viral, showing a young woman being harassed in public. This incident occurred in the municipality of Celaya, around 6:00 p.m. on Sunday, February 2, when the young woman was attempting to enter a residence located in the Zona de Oro neighborhood. According to security camera footage, the young woman was walking down Avenida 12 de octubre, near the Zona de Oro neighborhood, before turning onto a side street to enter her home. During her journey down Avenida 12 de octubre, a white Tsuru-type vehicle is observed parking nearby. A man gets out of the vehicle and walks towards the young woman. As the young woman tries to enter her house, the man, dressed in gray, quickly approaches her from behind, grabs her from behind, and bends down to bite her buttock. Once the sexual abuse had taken place, the individual ran to their vehicle and left. Moments later, the young woman quickly entered her home. Hours later, a video of the assault went viral on social media, exposing yet another case of street harassment. On Monday, February 3rd, the young woman appeared before the State Prosecutor's Office to report the sexual abuse she suffered, but told the media that they refused to accept her complaint, citing that there was no crime to pursue. The young woman appeared in the media again on Tuesday, February 4th, to report the assault she suffered. Her case became a media sensation. They told me there was no crime as such, she said the young woman Khaterine Michel. On the morning of this Wednesday, the Prosecutor's Office reported that the State Attorney General's Office of Guanajuato had approached the young woman from Celaya who on Sunday, February 2nd, 2025, was a victim of sexual abuse. Our Attorney General, Dr. Gerardo Vázquez Alatriste, has personally attended to the victim and provided comprehensive care. In this context, we commit to thoroughly integrating and attending to the investigation file, with the objective of clarifying the facts and seeking justice. We will conduct a thorough investigation into the actions of the public officials involved, in order to ensure that their actions meet the highest standards of service to citizens. By this Wednesday afternoon, the Guanajuato Prosecutor's Office reported that they had apprehended the sexual abuser.

The defendant allowed the entire sex sequence to be recorded by another person who was not judged as she was in a state of rebellion. BILBAO, 14 (EUROPA PRESS) The Provincial Court of Bizkaia has sentenced a man to a total of 9 years in prison for sexually abusing a woman who was in a state of semi-consciousness and allowing the entire sex sequence to be recorded by another person who was not judged as she was in a state of rebellion. The court imposes 7 years in prison for a sex abuse offense under Article 181, 1, 2, and 4 of the applicable Penal Code (2019) and an additional 2 years in prison and a fine of 10 euros per day for 14 months, totaling 4,200 euros, for a crime against intimacy and the right to one's own image. Furthermore, it orders the defendant to compensate the victim with 4,900 euros for injuries and 10,000 euros for moral damage caused, among other penalties and measures. The facts that have been proven had taken place in June 2019 at a residence in Bilbao, where the victim went accompanied by the accused, the boyfriend of a friend of hers (not being judged in this process as she was in rebellion). At a certain moment, the victim lost consciousness, entering a lethargic state, possibly due to some substance that had been administered to her by the accused and his girlfriend, which has not been identified. Then, the defendant, taking advantage of her state of unconsciousness and with the intention of satisfying his sexual desire, abused her, while the woman in a state of rebellion recorded the entire sequence. Those recordings were shown to third parties by the person who recorded them. The court recalls that the accused refused to testify during the trial, but they had the testimony of the victim and various friends, as well as the video of the facts. The footage shows the complainant in a state of deep sleep or unconsciousness and it is clear that during a sequence lasting several minutes, she is subjected to various sexual acts without ever waking up or moving at all (she is completely inert), according to the resolution. It is, of course, obvious to any observer that the complainant did not give consent to any of the acts she was subjected to because she was not in a condition to do so (she was in a state of semi-unconsciousness or deep sleep), the Vizcayan Audiencia adds.As for the crime against intimacy, the court affirms that the images clearly show that the accused was fully aware that he was being recorded throughout the entire sexual sequence. Additionally, on several occasions, he speaks with the person recording, precisely about what they were recording, which the Bizkaia Provincial Court concludes, finding that the accused's participation in this crime, which was affecting the victim's intimacy in an evident manner, leaves no room for doubt. DEEP PERSONAL, SOCIAL, AND REPUTATIONAL HARM When determining the penalties, the court considers two circumstances that aggravate the behavior in this case: the facts occur in a context of trust for the victim (there was a friendship relationship) and the variety of sexual acts to which the accused subjected the woman. Regarding moral damage, the Bizkaia Provincial Court highlights the deep personal harm suffered by the victim upon learning of the facts (which are undoubtedly grave) and, alongside this, the social and reputational harm suffered in their immediate environment, which forced them to leave Bilbao. In conclusion, the court decides to take testimony from private individuals for referral to the Dean's Court of Instruction if the accused has committed a crime of threats against the victim in this procedure, given the statements made by the victim in court. This sentence is not final and can be appealed to the Basque Country High Court of Justice.

Visit website More than 260 foreign nationals, who were forced to work in online scam centers in Myanmar, have been released and handed over to Thai authorities. The operation is part of a larger crackdown on human trafficking and cybercrime along the border between the two countries. On February 12, the Myanmar rebel group DKBA (Democratic Karen Buddhist Army), which had recently attacked scam centers in the area, handed over the victims to Thai authorities People brought to Thailand worked at a center in Kyauk Khet, a village in the Karen state of Myanmar, near the border between the two countries, according to the DKBA, which controls the area. They were transported by boat across the border river and disembarked 30 km south of the Thai side in Phop Phra, according to an AFP journalist. There are currently 261 people, but the final number has not yet been confirmed, said Natthakorn Rueantip, a Thai army officer, to Mae Sot. Foreigners must be interrogated before being sent back to their countries of origin with the coordination of their embassies, the Thai authorities specified, wanting to verify their backgrounds. As in previous cases, it is expected that authorities will discover that some have been victims of human trafficking, while others have taken up these jobs voluntarily. The commander of the DKBA contacted a Thai parliament member on Tuesday to arrange the release of the 260 workers. The latest information speaks of 221 men and 39 women, mostly from Africa and Asia. Now, we are releasing all those we find, but the process is difficult. The Immigration Department of the junta is making demands and the terrain is difficult, said DKBA Chief of Staff, Saw San Aung, to Voice of America (VOA). Cyber-Slavery Built as fortresses and managed by criminal networks, the scam centers employ by force thousands of people of various nationalities, who are forced to scam their fellow nationals by phone or internet. A cybercrime industry estimated to be worth billions of dollars, whose true size is difficult to assess due to its clandestine nature and authorities' response shortcomings. Scammers recruit workers with language skills for the languages targeted by cyberfraud, typically English and Chinese. Locals are lured with promises of well-paying jobs, but are then coerced into committing crimes, including romantic scams, cryptocurrency fraud, credit card scams, money laundering, and illegal online gambling. These workers become what some media outlets and NGOs refer to as cyber slaves. A witness who requested anonymity for security reasons spoke to VOA in a phone interview on Wednesday, stating that gangs force victims of human trafficking to meet monthly income targets of up to $50,000. If they failed, they were tortured. They were only allowed to sleep for two or three hours a day and worked non-stop. They were locked in dark cells and subjected to continuous abuse. The UN estimates that several hundred thousand people are now working in these clandestine call centers. While Chinese and Southeast Asian citizens still make up the majority in these networks, freed victims mention the presence of many African citizens. Among the nationalities of the released victims on February 12, there were citizens of Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Burundi, Ghana, and Uganda. The rapidly escalating phenomenon that is causing concern The problem of call centers and the explosion of crime in Myanmar, which is sinking into a civil war, is a major concern for Southeast Asian authorities, as the phenomenon seems to be completely out of control in recent years. Under the combined effect of China and Cambodia's toughening of laws and, especially, the collapse of the rule of law in Myanmar since the February 2021 coup, criminal networks are flourishing in the country. The trafficking of drugs and people is skyrocketing, driven by institutional vacuum and the lack of regulation and enforcement of laws in these areas. In response to the phenomenon, the Thai government cut off electricity access in several neighboring Myanmar regions in early February, known for hosting a vast criminal network of scams and human trafficking. Thailand's Defense Minister, Phumtham Wechayachai, justified the measure by saying it was a matter of national security for the kingdom. Banking and visa regulations have also been tightened in an attempt to prevent con artists from using Thailand as a transit country to move workers and money. The Government has deployed additional security forces along the border to face any possible influx of people released from call centers, said Phumtham. He also said that Thailand would ease sanctions on internet service provision, fuel, and electricity if Burmese authorities prove that they were not involved in the networks. This is a source of tension not only with Thailand, but also with China, for which the dismantling of these organizations has become a priority. Beijing has pressured both the ruling junta and the armed groups active in the north of the country. China, one of the main suppliers of arms to the Burmese junta, but also with ties to local rebel groups, has repeatedly asked Burmese authorities to put an end to this market. Taking advantage of the pandemic, these networks have exploited the COVID-19 pandemic, as explained in a 2023 UN report. The measures put in place to respond to the health crisis have had a significant impact on certain activities, leading in particular to the closure of casinos in many countries. These activities have been transferred to less regulated areas, such as conflict-affected border zones. At the same time, the pandemic has increased the vulnerability of many migrants, who have found themselves stranded overnight in foreign countries without work. While generalized lockdowns have increased the number of people online who are likely to be scammed. Experts from the United States Institute of Peace believe that the profits generated by this clandestine industry are mainly laundered through the real estate sector worldwide. However, they are also used to finance certain regional political elites in Laos, Cambodia, and Myanmar, for example, in exchange for their implicit cooperation.

The Office for Children, Girls and Family (PRONNIF) has reported that in the state of Coahuila, at least 6,000 cases related to child neglect have been registered, of which 1,200 correspond to the La Laguna region. It is estimated that this type of case could increase by up to 50% in 2025, mainly due to the consumption of drugs by parents. To strengthen attention for children, girls, and adolescents in a vulnerable situation, the integration of fifteen specialized agents from the Public Ministry was announced, who specialize in crimes such as physical aggression, sexual abuse, and neglect by direct family members. María Teresa Araiza, PRONNIF prosecutor in Coahuila, explained that the lack of family cohesion and the absence of support networks significantly contribute to children being victims of aggression or becoming involved in high-risk situations. Although cases of adolescent homicide are rare in the state, family disintegration has led to many young people being influenced by criminal figures due to the lack of paternal guidance or responsible authority. Many of these minors grow up in unfavorable environments where neglect and violence are normalized. It is essential to work on prevention and creating safe spaces for them, Araiza noted.Inter-institutional coordination for child protection In Torreón, the installation of the State and Municipal Executive Secretaries Commission was held, with the presence of representatives from the municipal DIF systems of the Lagunera region. The objective of the meeting was to homologate criteria in the attention of children, girls, and adolescents at risk. During the meeting, Araiza emphasized the importance of joint work between PRONNIF, specialized public prosecutors, and the Integral Protection System for Girls, Boys, and Adolescents (SIPINNA) to strengthen investigations and prevent crimes against minors. It is essential that society, institutions, and the media promote a culture of child protection. Prevention and urgent measures One of PRONNIF's main approaches is the prevention of the criminalization of adolescents. Araiza noted that early attention and positive parenting education can reduce the incidence of violence among minors. It is crucial that young people have spaces to express themselves and be given the opportunity to rechannel their behavior with timely interventions, he stated. In the La Laguna region, recent cases of minors bringing guns to school have raised concern among authorities. However, the prosecutor assured that these cases must be approached with a protection-focused approach and respect for the rights of children and adolescents, avoiding their criminalization without a proper analysis of their environment. The solution is not in severely punishing the young people, but in strengthening prevention programs, early detection, and support for families, concluded Araiza.

A man has been sentenced to 13 years and six months in prison for sexually abusing a 7-year-old girl in Murcia. The sentence was upheld by the Civil and Penal Chamber of the Superior Justice Court of the region, who supported the decision of the Provincial Court. The perpetrator, who knew the victim's family, took advantage of the fact that the girl would stay at his home after classes. According to the judicial resolution, the aggressor subjected the minor to repeated acts of sexual abuse, threatening to harm her loved ones if she dared to report what had happened. The details of the case are chilling. It is reported that the man would take the girl to the bathroom, where he would subject her to assaults, manipulating her fear by telling her that he had a gun and could kill her, her family, and even her pet, if she said anything. This situation lasted for months and required the minor to receive psychological treatment as a result of the trauma suffered. Despite the defense's attempts to question the validity of the girl's testimony and suggest that there was an error in the evaluation of the evidence, the court dismissed these allegations. The magistrates emphasized that the girl's account was coherent, and that the mother and brother of the victim provided objective information that supported the version of events. Additionally, the Court did not consider it relevant to grant the defendant's request to reduce their sentence, as the evident acts of physical and psychological violence exercised against the girl were clear and unequivocal. The sentence highlights the seriousness of the threats made by the aggressor, which involved not only the girl, but also her family and her pet. As part of the sentence, the individual will face a period of supervised release of seven years after their release, and will be prohibited from accessing any profession that would allow them to interact with minors for a total of 17 years and six months. He will also have to pay 10,000 euros to the victim for moral damages and will be subject to a restraining order that will prohibit him from approaching her within 300 meters for 20 years and six months. It is essential to highlight that this decision is not definitive, as the possibility of appealing to the Supreme Court is foreseen.
